english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Information Technology runs a 72-unit, three-year structure split cleanly into thirds: 27 core units, a 27-unit major, and 18 units of free electives. The major choice does most of the work differentiating graduates: Software Development, Networking and Cyber Security, and Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning are the most commonly taken.

Compared to the Bachelor of Computer Science, the IT degree leans more applied in its core, with less emphasis on algorithmic complexity and formal computation theory and more on systems integration, project delivery, and IT service management. It's aimed at graduates headed toward corporate IT departments and consultancies rather than pure software development houses.

Career paths the university lists include IT consultant, network administrator, cybersecurity analyst, systems analyst, and software developer. February and July intake, delivered mainly at Adelaide City Campus.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Introduction to Programming; IT Systems Fundamentals; Business Analysis (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Database Systems; Networking Fundamentals; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Systems Analysis and Design; 1 major course; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — IT Project Management; 1 major course; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — 2 major courses; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — IT Capstone Project; 1 major course; 1 elective (24 units).
admission_requirements: SACE (or equivalent) completion with an ATAR of approximately 75.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.0, with 6.0 minimum in each band.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology: Data Analytics
description:
The data analytics specialisation of Adelaide University's Bachelor of Information Technology: a three-year degree (144 units) with a 66-unit IT core and a common first year that lets students change major, then a specialisation in turning data into decisions, covering data management, analysis, visualisation and the tools used across industry.

The degree is provisionally accredited at professional level by the Australian Computer Society, and it includes an industry capstone project with a real client. Study is split across the Adelaide city and Mawson Lakes campuses. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits students aiming at data analyst, business intelligence or analytics-focused IT roles rather than software engineering.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Problem Solving and Programming (6 units); Structured Data (6 units); Computing Innovations in the Modern World (6 units); Information Technology Systems (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — System Requirements (6 units); Security Foundations (6 units); Discipline courses.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Cloud Platforms (6 units); Unstructured Data (6 units); Discipline courses; Discipline courses.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Professional Communication and Teamwork (6 units); Agile Development and User Experience (6 units); Discipline courses; Discipline courses.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Discipline courses; Discipline courses; Discipline courses.
Year 3, Semester 2 — Business for IT Professionals (6 units); ICT Capstone Project 1 (6 units); ICT Internship 1 (6 units); ICT Internship 2 (12 units); ICT Internship 3 (18 units); ICT Internship 4 (24 units); ICT Capstone Project 2 (6 units); ICT Internship 1 (6 units); ICT Internship 2 (12 units); ICT Internship 3 (18 units); ICT Internship 4 (24 units).
admission_requirements: Guaranteed entry ATAR 70 (or equivalent secondary qualification); no prerequisite subjects; IELTS 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each band for international applicants.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Information Technology: Games Development
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Information Technology, games development specialisation, is a three-year degree (144 units). It keeps the IT core and common first year, then focuses on game engines, mobile game development and entertainment software built on object-oriented programming, with an industry capstone project for a real client.

The degree is provisionally accredited at professional level by the Australian Computer Society, taught across the city and Mawson Lakes campuses. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits students who want to build games and interactive media and keep general IT employability, since the shared core still covers programming, systems and networking.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Problem Solving and Programming (6 units); Structured Data (6 units); Computing Innovations in the Modern World (6 units); Information Technology Systems (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — System Requirements (6 units); Security Foundations (6 units); Discipline courses.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Cloud Platforms (6 units); Unstructured Data (6 units); Discipline courses; Discipline courses.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Professional Communication and Teamwork (6 units); Agile Development and User Experience (6 units); Discipline courses; Discipline courses.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Discipline courses; Discipline courses; Discipline courses.
Year 3, Semester 2 — Business for IT Professionals (6 units); ICT Capstone Project 1 (6 units); ICT Internship 1 (6 units); ICT Internship 2 (12 units); ICT Internship 3 (18 units); ICT Internship 4 (24 units); ICT Capstone Project 2 (6 units); ICT Internship 1 (6 units); ICT Internship 2 (12 units); ICT Internship 3 (18 units); ICT Internship 4 (24 units).
admission_requirements: Guaranteed entry ATAR 70 (or equivalent secondary qualification); no prerequisite subjects; IELTS 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each band for international applicants.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Information Technology: Networking and Cyber Security
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Information Technology, networking and cyber security specialisation, is a three-year degree (144 units). On top of the shared IT core it covers network infrastructure, security operations, and both defensive and offensive security practice, with an industry capstone project.

The degree is provisionally accredited at professional level by the Australian Computer Society and taught across the city and Mawson Lakes campuses. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits students heading into network administration, security operations or cyber security analyst roles, in a sector with a well-documented shortage of graduates in Australia.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Problem Solving and Programming (6 units); Structured Data (6 units); Computing Innovations in the Modern World (6 units); Information Technology Systems (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — System Requirements (6 units); Security Foundations (6 units); Discipline courses.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Cloud Platforms (6 units); Unstructured Data (6 units); Discipline courses; Discipline courses.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Professional Communication and Teamwork (6 units); Agile Development and User Experience (6 units); Discipline courses; Discipline courses.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Discipline courses; Discipline courses; Discipline courses.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology: Software Development
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Information Technology (Software Development) is a three-year degree (February and July intakes) with a 66-unit IT core covering problem solving, programming, structured and unstructured data, IT systems, security, cloud platforms, agile development, and business for IT professionals. The 48-unit software development major adds object-oriented programming, web and mobile development, concurrent and cloud programming, system design, design patterns, and an introduction to DevOps.

Work-integrated learning is 12 to 24 units, taken as an ICT capstone project with a real client or an ICT internship of 6 to 24 units. The degree is provisionally accredited at professional level by the Australian Computer Society and recognised internationally through the Seoul Accord. Indicative international fee is around A$52,500 per year.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Problem Solving and Programming (6 units); Structured Data (6 units); Computing Innovations in the Modern World (6 units); Information Technology Systems (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — System Requirements (6 units); Security Foundations (6 units); Object-Oriented Programming (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Cloud Platforms (6 units); Unstructured Data (6 units); System Design (6 units); Software Development Practice (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Professional Communication and Teamwork (6 units); Agile Development and User Experience (6 units); Cloud and Concurrent Programming (6 units); Web Technology (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Mobile Application Development (6 units); Design Patterns (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Business for IT Professionals (6 units); Introduction to DevOps (6 units); ICT Capstone Project 1 (6 units); ICT Internship 1 (6 units); ICT Internship 2 (12 units); ICT Internship 3 (18 units); ICT Internship 4 (24 units).
admission_requirements: Guaranteed entry ATAR 70 (or equivalent secondary qualification); no prerequisite subjects; IELTS 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each band for international applicants.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Interior Architecture (Honours)
description: A four-year, 192 unit design degree in interior architecture with integrated honours, taught on the Adelaide city campus and built around progressive design studios: Foundation, Materials, Detail, Inclusion and Workplace. Alongside the studios, students take history, construction, digital documentation, professional practice, sustainability and research methods. The structure is 162 core units, 12 work-integrated learning units and 18 electives. The degree aligns with the four-year standards of the International Federation of Interior Architects/Designers and the Interior Design/Interior Architecture Educators Association. Entry requires a secondary qualification equivalent to SACE and IELTS 6.5. Graduates work as interior designers and design managers, and in adaptive reuse, sustainability consulting and placemaking, with postgraduate research a further option. It suits students who want a professionally aligned interior design degree with a strong studio focus.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Common core.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Digital Interior Practices (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Digital Interior Documentation (6 units); Common core.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Interior Architecture Studio (Detail) (6 units).
admission_requirements: ATAR 75 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of International Relations
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of International Relations is a three-year degree (144 units) built around a 66-unit core plus one 48-unit major chosen from options that include international security, international development, politics, population and migration studies, environmental management, and seven language streams from Chinese to Spanish.

Students complete a 15-day internship or an international exchange, with study tours and semester exchange also available, and teaching leans on simulations, case studies and seminars with visiting scholars. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits students aiming at diplomacy, foreign affairs, international organisations, policy analysis or development work.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Common core; Elective; Introduction to Comparative Politics (6 units); Australia’s Foreign Policy in the Indo-Pacific (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Introduction to Global Politics (6 units); The State of the World: Post Covid-19 (6 units); Majors; Majors.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Common core; Approaches in International Relations (6 units); Professional Pathways and Destinations 2 (6 units); Majors.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Elective; Global Environmental Politics (6 units); Majors; Majors.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Common core; Elective.
admission_requirements: Guaranteed entry ATAR 75 (or equivalent secondary qualification); no prerequisite subjects; IELTS 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each band for international applicants.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Journalism
description: The Bachelor of Journalism at Adelaide University is a three-year degree that develops expertise in telling impactful stories across multiple media platforms. Students build skills in news gathering, writing and multimedia production, learn to record and edit audio and video content, write for online audiences, and create immersive journalism using the latest technologies, alongside media law and ethics and a long-form journalism project. Hands-on experience is a cornerstone, with real-world projects such as producing a news segment. Graduates work as journalists, reporters, producers and editors across print, broadcast, online and multimedia news, and in communication-focused roles.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Journalism Foundations (6 units); News Writing (6 units); Introduction to Broadcast (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Audio Journalism (6 units); Multimedia Journalism (6 units); Common core.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Media Law, Policy and Ethics (6 units); Feature Writing (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Journalism Theory and Practice (6 units); Television and Video Journalism (6 units); Common core.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Constructive Journalism (6 units); Investigative Journalism (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Journalism Production (6 units).
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 70 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Bachelor of Laboratory Medicine (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Laboratory Medicine (Honours) at Adelaide University prepares students to work as accredited medical laboratory scientists in diagnostic pathology or research. Students develop core knowledge of the natural and biomedical sciences and their application in diagnostic pathology, learning to perform diagnostic tests including cross-matching for blood transfusions, identifying infection-causing organisms, screening for cancer cells and detecting genes responsible for disease. Medical laboratory scientists support clinicians in diagnosing, managing and treating disease, and help shape public health initiatives such as disease prevention and the development of new diagnostic tests. Graduates work in diagnostic pathology laboratories across Australia.

Year 1, Semester 1 — Chemistry 100 (6 units); Human Physiology 100 (6 units); Mathematics for Laboratory Sciences (6 units); Health, Society and Systems (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Chemistry 101 (6 units); Human Physiology 101 (6 units); Professional Issues in Laboratory Medicine (6 units); Data Skills for Scientists (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Biochemistry (6 units); Histology (6 units); Genetics (6 units); Microbiology (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Genomics and Bioinformatics (6 units); Immunology (6 units); Pathophysiology (6 units); Essential Haematology (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Histotechnology (6 units); Infectious Diseases (6 units); Chemical and Molecular Pathology (6 units); Transfusion and Haemostasis (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Clinical Practice A (12 units); Clinical Practice B (12 units).
Year 4, Semester 1 — Advanced Clinical Practice A (12 units); Experimental Research Practice A (12 units).
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 80 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.5.

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
Adelaide University's single Bachelor of Laws is a 96-unit, four-year AQF Level 7 degree: half core, half elective, but with real constraints on when students can take the elective half. No more than 9 units can be taken at Level I, and a minimum of 12 units is reserved for Level III, so students can't front-load easy electives early and coast.

Of the 48 elective units, 36 must be law electives, leaving 12 units as genuinely broadening electives students can take from outside the law school, such as a language, a science course, or a business elective, depending on interest. That's a deliberate design choice distinguishing the single LLB from Adelaide's various double-degree law combinations (Arts, Business, International Relations), which restructure the unit split differently and run longer.

The degree meets the requirements set by the Legal Practitioners Education and Admission Council of South Australia for admission to legal practice, subject to completing Practical Legal Training after graduation. Career paths span solicitor, barrister, in-house counsel, and policy roles, and a meaningful share of graduates go on to further postgraduate study rather than practising law directly.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Legal Method and Reasoning; Criminal Law; Torts; 1 broadening elective (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Contracts; Constitutional Law; 1 law elective; 1 broadening elective (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Property Law; Equity and Trusts; 2 law electives (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Administrative Law; Evidence; 2 law electives (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Corporations Law; Civil Procedure; 2 law electives (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Professional Conduct and Ethics; 3 law electives (24 units).
Year 4, Semester 1 — Level III law electives; clinical legal education component (24 units).
Year 4, Semester 2 — Level III law electives; research elective (24 units).
admission_requirements: SACE (or equivalent) completion with an ATAR of approximately 90.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with 6.0 minimum in each band.

name: Bachelor of Mathematical and Computer Sciences
Bachelor of Mathematics
description: Adelaide University's Bachelor of Mathematics is a three-year undergraduate degree in Adelaide covering the theory and technical skills of the mathematical sciences, including statistical modelling. Students work on real business problems in the university's Maths Clinic and on industry projects, and can add an honours year for research training. Graduates work as analysts, modellers and statisticians across finance, technology, health, environmental management and research.

Year 1, Semester 2 — Calculus 2 (6 units); Linear Algebra (6 units); Common core.

Year 2, Semester 2 — Statistical Practice (6 units); Discipline courses; Discipline electives Level 2; Common core.

name: Bachelor of Media and Communication
description: The Bachelor of Media and Communication at Adelaide University is a flexible three-year degree that teaches students to create impactful media and communications content for any career context. Students understand the issues, trends and technologies shaping how we interact, and learn to produce well-informed and targeted media and communication strategies for a range of organisations, audiences and platforms, using words, images and sound to tell powerful stories. Graduates work in public relations, social media, design, immersive media, film, gaming and entertainment, and communication roles across industries.

Year 1, Semester 2 — Media and Communication Professional Identities (6 units); Discipline courses.

name: Bachelor of Medical Studies
description: Adelaide University's Bachelor of Medical Studies is a three-year undergraduate degree in Adelaide and the first stage of the university's six-year integrated medicine program. Teaching is scenario-based, covering individual, community, Indigenous and global health, with clinical skills developed in simulation facilities and early exposure to practice. On successful completion students gain direct entry into the three-year Doctor of Medicine.

Year 1, Semester 2 — Medical Studies 1 (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Medical Studies 2A (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Medical Studies 2B (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Medical Studies 3 (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Transition to Clinical Studies (18 units); Research Skills Development (6 units).

name: Bachelor of Midwifery
description: The Bachelor of Midwifery at Adelaide University is a three-year degree that equips students for a career in maternity care, emphasising women's and family-centred care. Students develop the skills to meet the social, emotional, physical and cultural needs of women and their families through pregnancy, birth and the postnatal period, with supervised clinical practice. International students study primarily on campus with a February start. The degree leads to registration as a midwife. Graduates work as midwives in hospitals, birth centres, community and continuity-of-care models, and rural and remote health.

Year 1, Semester 2 — Healthy Mothers and Babies (6 units); Midwifery Practice Experience 1 (6 units); Human Biology 2 (6 units); Aboriginal Health (6 units).

Year 3, Semester 2 — Midwifery Project (6 units); Becoming a Midwife (6 units); Midwifery Practice Experience 5 (12 units).

name: Bachelor of Music
description: Adelaide University's Bachelor of Music is a three-year performance-focused degree with a single structure and a choice of major: Classical Performance, Jazz Performance, Creative Practice, or Music Education. Core musicianship study runs alongside weekly one-on-one instrumental or vocal tuition and required ensemble work in orchestras, chamber groups, big bands and choirs, plus electives. Entry is by competitive audition, in person or by recording. An integrated four-year pathway combines the degree with the Master of Teaching (Secondary) for those aiming at classroom music teaching. Graduates work as performers, session and ensemble musicians, music directors, composers, private teachers and arts workers, often piecing together portfolio careers. It suits students with the instrumental or vocal standard to pass the audition who want conservatorium-style training inside a university.

Year 1, Semester 2 — Elective; Musicianship 1B (6 units); Classical Performance 1B (6 units); Music Professional Development 1B (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Musicianship 2A (6 units); Classical Performance 2A (6 units); Music Professional Development 2A (6 units); Elective.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Musicianship 2B (6 units); Classical Performance 2B (6 units); Music Professional Development 2B (6 units); Elective.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Classical Performance 3A (6 units); Music Professional Development 3A (6 units); Elective; Elective.
Year 3, Semester 2 — Classical Performance 3B (6 units); Music Professional Development 3B (6 units); Elective.

name: Bachelor of Music Theatre
description: Adelaide University's Bachelor of Music Theatre is a three-year undergraduate degree in Adelaide with individualised training across performance, musicianship and production. Students take advanced classes in ballet, jazz, tap, voice and acting, perform regularly, and finish with a graduation musical, an industry showcase and a professional portfolio. Graduates work as music theatre performers and in related creative and teaching roles.

Year 2, Semester 1 — Music Theatre Musicianship 2A (6 units); Music Theatre Performance 2A (6 units); Music Theatre Production 2A (6 units).

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Nursing packs 880 hours of clinical placement into its 144-unit, three-year structure, delivered as five credit-bearing Professional Experience Placement courses worth 42 units in total, starting in first year rather than being held back until students have finished the theory-heavy component.

Placements run across metropolitan, regional, and rural South Australian health services, and the degree is offered not just at Adelaide City Campus but also at Mount Gambier and Whyalla, meaning some students train in genuinely regional clinical settings rather than only large metropolitan teaching hospitals, a point of difference for students planning to work rurally after graduation, where SA has persistent nursing workforce shortages.

The degree qualifies graduates to apply for registration as a nurse with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. Career paths include registered nurse across acute, aged, mental health, and community care settings, with many graduates staying within the SA Health system given the placement relationships built during the degree.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Foundations of Nursing Practice; Anatomy and Physiology 1; Health Assessment; Professional Experience Placement 1 (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Anatomy and Physiology 2; Pharmacology for Nursing; Mental Health Nursing Foundations; Professional Experience Placement 2 (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Acute Care Nursing; Pathophysiology; Nursing Research and Evidence; Professional Experience Placement 3 (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Chronic and Complex Care; Aged Care Nursing; 1 elective; Professional Experience Placement 4 (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Child and Family Health Nursing; Leadership in Nursing Practice; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Transition to Professional Practice; Complex Care Capstone; Professional Experience Placement 5 (24 units).
admission_requirements: SACE (or equivalent) completion with an ATAR of approximately 80; current National Police Certificate and immunisation compliance required prior to placement.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, with a minimum of 7.0 in each band (registration/AHPRA English requirement).

name: Bachelor of Occupational Therapy (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Occupational Therapy (Honours) at Adelaide University teaches students to help people overcome constraints caused by injury or illness so they can do everyday tasks that are often taken for granted. Students build knowledge across key areas of health, integrating psychology, anatomy and sociology, and complete occupational therapy courses focused on diverse areas of practice. Hands-on experience comes through placements, workshops and regional experiences, where students practise solving real problems faced by working occupational therapists and learn about assistive technology, adaptation techniques and rehabilitation. Graduates work with clients across the lifespan to improve quality of life.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Human Anatomy 100 (6 units); Physiology Essentials 100 (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Lifespan Development for Occupational Therapy Practice (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — The Individual in Society (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Occupational Therapy Practice Education (6 units); Therapeutic Communication and Group Work (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Occupational Therapy Practice and Mental Health (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Advanced Evidence Based Practice (6 units); Health Science Honours Preparation (6 units).
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 90 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 7.0, with no band below 7.0.

name: Bachelor of Oral Health
description: Adelaide University's Bachelor of Oral Health is a three-year, evidence-based undergraduate degree in Adelaide. Students study the anatomy and physiology of the teeth, gums and oral tissues and their links to general health, train in a dental simulation clinic, and complete extensive clinical placements including a community dental outreach program. Graduates work in oral health therapy, dental hygiene and health promotion.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Dental and Health Science IOH Part 1 (6 units); Clinical Practice IOH Part 1 (8 units); Human Biology IOH Part 1 (6 units); Population Health & Professional Practice IOH Part 1 (4 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Dental & Health Science IIOH Part 1 (4 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Dental & Health Science IIOH Part 2 (4 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Oral Health Elective IIIOH Part 1 (4 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Oral Health Elective IIIOH Part 2 (4 units).
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 70 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 7.0, with no band below 7.0.

name: Bachelor of Outdoor and Environmental Leadership
description: Adelaide University's Bachelor of Outdoor and Environmental Leadership is a three-year undergraduate degree in Adelaide, shaped by the university's environmental science and management research. It combines health and wellbeing, environmental leadership and sustainability with practical field experience, and students lead outdoor programs and self-guided expeditions. Graduates work in outdoor education, environmental programs, sustainability and community roles.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Science of People, Society and the Future Planet (6 units); Biology 1B: Evolution and Diversity of Organisms (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Ecological Issues 1 (6 units); Physical Geography and Human Environmental Impacts (6 units); Outdoor Leadership Theory and Practice (6 units); Coastal Environments (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Environmental Interpretation and Community Engagement (6 units); Elective.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Plant Identification 2 (6 units); Animal Identification in Wildlife Conservation 2 (6 units); Park and Ecotourism Management (6 units); Elective.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Fire and Culture (6 units).
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 70 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Bachelor of Pharmaceutical Science
description: Adelaide University's Bachelor of Pharmaceutical Science is a three-year undergraduate degree in Adelaide and the only degree of its kind in South Australia. It covers how medicines are discovered, formulated, tested and manufactured, with a workplace placement and teaching from active researchers. It is a pharmaceutical science degree rather than a pharmacy qualification, so it does not by itself lead to registration as a pharmacist. Graduates work across the pharmaceutical and biotechnology sectors in research, formulation, analysis and quality roles.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Human Physiology 100 (6 units); Health, Society and Systems (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Elective.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Pharmacology B (6 units); Pharmacology C (6 units); Elective.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Elective.
Year 3, Semester 2 — Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Industry Experience (6 units); Elective.
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 75 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours) at Adelaide University prepares students to become pharmacists who help people get the best outcomes from their medicines. Students step into clinical practice and learn in a dedicated pharmacy teaching laboratory, gaining 12 weeks of practical experience in community pharmacies and hospitals. The degree teaches students to dispense medicines, counsel patients, analyse drug interactions and deliver quality care, building the skills needed for contemporary pharmacy practice. Students work alongside experienced clinicians and researchers and benefit from strong links with clinical practice and the community, graduating ready to join one of the world's most trusted professions.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Human Physiology 100 (6 units); Chemistry 100 (6 units); Health, Society and Systems (6 units); Health Professional Essentials (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Human Physiology 101 (6 units); Chemistry 101 (6 units); Pharmacy Practice 1 (6 units); Data Skills for Scientists (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Pharmacology A (12 units); Dosage Form Design 1 (6 units); Pharmacokinetics and Biopharmaceutics (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Pharmacology B (6 units); Pharmacology C (6 units); Dosage Form Design 2 (6 units); Pharmacy Practice 2 (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Pharmacotherapeutics Practice 1A (6 units); Pharmacotherapeutics Theory 1 (6 units); Dosage Form Design 3 (6 units); Quality Use of Medicines (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Pharmacotherapeutics Practice 1B (6 units); Pharmacotherapeutics Theory 2 (6 units); Pharmacy Practice Health Services Provision (6 units).
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 85 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Bachelor of Philosophy, Politics and Economics
description: Adelaide University's Bachelor of Philosophy, Politics and Economics is a three-year undergraduate degree in Adelaide. Students study theory and applied questions across all three disciplines, from morality and social justice to markets and policy, and complete an industry internship in third year. Graduates leave with analytical, communication and presentation skills and move into government, policy, research, consulting and analysis roles.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Philosophy: Big Questions (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Data Analytics (6 units); Philosophy: Key Thinkers (6 units); Introduction to Australian Politics (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Intermediate Macroeconomics (6 units); Ethical Theories: Their Foundations and Practical Applications (6 units); Common core.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Principles of Social Policy (6 units); Passions and Interests: The History of Greed (6 units); Program electives; Program electives.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Common core.
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 70 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours) at Adelaide University is a four-year honours degree that teaches students to assess, treat and prevent health conditions across the full lifespan. Supported by practising physiotherapists and award-winning researchers, students gain hands-on experience from day one, advancing both technical and communication skills. The contemporary, culturally informed curriculum covers human anatomy and physiology, biomechanics, muscle assessment, pharmacology and pain science, as well as the social and psychological factors that affect health and wellbeing. Students learn to apply these principles in real-world scenarios, graduating ready for an active, people-focused profession that helps clients lead healthy, functional lives.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Human Anatomy 100 (6 units); Human Physiology 100 (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Human Anatomy 200 (6 units); Physiotherapy Exercise Prescription and Activity (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Biopsychosocial Practice (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Applied Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy (12 units); Core selective courses.
Year 3, Semester 2 — Acute Care (12 units); Rehabilitation (12 units).
Year 4, Semester 1 — Clinical Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy (12 units).
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 90 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 7.0, with no band below 7.0.

name: Bachelor of Podiatry (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Podiatry (Honours) at Adelaide University teaches students to treat a range of lower limb issues and enhance quality of life for people with painful feet and legs, including those managing chronic conditions such as diabetes and arthritis. Through a blend of theory, practical experience and clinical placements, students develop the skills to diagnose, manage and treat disorders affecting the foot, ankle and lower limb. The degree builds core knowledge of human anatomy, physiology, biomechanics and disease groups, and teaches clinical practice skills in surgery, pharmacology, orthopaedic management, wound management and high-risk and chronic condition care. Graduates enter allied health careers as podiatrists.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Human Anatomy 100 (6 units); Podiatry Studies 100 (6 units); Human Physiology 100 (6 units); Aboriginal Health: Culture, Community and Country (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Podiatry Studies 101 (6 units); Lower Limb Anatomy and Biomechanics 101 (6 units); Introduction to Evidence Based Practice and Research in Health Sciences (6 units); Human Physiology 101 (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Pharmacology A (12 units); Podiatry Professional Studies 200 (6 units); Clinical Podiatry Practice 200 (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Pharmacology B (6 units); Pharmacology C (6 units); Podiatry Studies 201 (6 units); Clinical Podiatry Practice 201 (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Health Science Honours Preparation (6 units); Podiatry Studies 300 (6 units); Applied Podiatry Studies 300 (6 units); Clinical Podiatry Practice 300 (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Pain Sciences (6 units); Podiatry Studies 301 (6 units); Applied Podiatry Studies 301 (6 units).
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 85 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 7.0, with no band below 7.0.

name: Bachelor of Property
description:
Adelaide University delivers property as a major within the Bachelor of Commerce rather than as a standalone Bachelor of Property. It is a three-year degree (144 units) combining a commerce core in accounting, finance, economics and management with property-specific courses in property economics, investment, development and statutory and advanced valuation.

The university is working with the Australian Property Institute on accreditation, so the formal valuer registration pathway is still being finalised. The degree includes work-integrated learning through a business practicum and business clinic. Entry is an ATAR of about 80. It suits students heading into valuation, property investment, development or asset management.
admission_requirements: Guaranteed entry ATAR 80 (or equivalent secondary qualification); no prerequisite subjects; IELTS 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each band for international applicants.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Psychology
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Psychology builds on twelve core psychology courses common to every specialisation in the suite (Cognitive Neuroscience, Counselling and Interpersonal Skills, and the general stream), meaning students can defer choosing a specialisation without falling behind, since the differentiation mostly happens in fourth-year honours options.

From 2026, progression to the fourth (honours) year requires a GPA of at least 6.0 across all psychology core courses completed in years one to three. That's a real bar, not a formality, and the university is explicit that not everyone clears it. Students who don't can still graduate with the three-year Bachelor of Psychology, or apply separately for the one-year stand-alone Bachelor of Psychology (Honours) or the Graduate Diploma in Psychology (Advanced) as alternate routes.

The degree is accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council, a prerequisite for eventually registering as a psychologist in Australia. Career paths before further study include research assistant, human resources, and community services roles; full registration as a psychologist requires completing honours plus supervised postgraduate training or a further accredited program.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Introduction to Psychology A; Biological Bases of Behaviour; Research Methods in Psychology 1 (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Introduction to Psychology B; Social Psychology; Research Methods in Psychology 2 (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Cognitive Psychology; Developmental Psychology; Statistics for Psychology (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Abnormal Psychology; Personality and Individual Differences; Research Methods in Psychology 3 (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Psychological Assessment; Health Psychology; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Applied Psychology Capstone; Ethics in Psychological Practice; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 4 (Honours, GPA-gated) — Advanced Research Methods; Honours Thesis; specialised electives (Cognitive Neuroscience or Counselling and Interpersonal Skills stream).
admission_requirements: SACE (or equivalent) completion with an ATAR of approximately 85.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with 6.0 minimum in each band.

name: Bachelor of Public Health
description: The Bachelor of Public Health at Adelaide University is a three-year degree that gives students the skills to shape healthier futures using an information-driven, people-first approach. Students explore the social, cultural, commercial and environmental factors that influence wellbeing, use research techniques and practice-based skills to investigate current health issues, and learn to assess evidence critically and develop and deliver health policy and promotion initiatives. Graduates work in health promotion, epidemiology and surveillance, policy and program roles across government, non-government organisations and research.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Health, Society and Systems (6 units); Selective Group 1; Common core.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Selective Group 1.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Selective Group 2; Common core.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Public Health Evaluation (6 units); Selective Group 2.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Designing and Managing Public Health Programs (6 units); Science, Evidence and Politics: Building Healthy Public Policy (6 units); Selective Group 3; Common core.
Year 3, Semester 2 — Work Integrated Learning (Public Health) (6 units).
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 75 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Science is a three-year degree (144 units) with February and July intakes, built from a common core, a science program core, one major or a discipline-course block, a required work-integrated learning component, and electives. The work-integrated learning is mandatory and ranges from research projects to fieldwork to industry placements depending on the major.

There are more than 30 majors across animal and veterinary sciences, chemistry, molecular and biomedical sciences, earth sciences, physics, ecology and evolution, environmental and plant sciences, and food science. Students can extend to a four-year Bachelor of Science (Honours) for research training, or fast-track into a Master of Research with about one further year.
curriculum: No fixed course sequence; students choose electives across areas including: Animal Behaviour; Animal Science; Food Science and Technology; Analytical Chemistry; Chemistry; Medicinal and Biological Chemistry; Nuclear Chemistry; Pure and Applied Chemistry; Biochemistry; Biotechnology; Genetics; Microbiology and Immunology; Geology.
admission_requirements: Guaranteed entry ATAR 70 (or equivalent secondary qualification); no prerequisite subjects; IELTS 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each band for international applicants.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Social Work
description: The Bachelor of Social Work at Adelaide University is a four-year degree that prepares students to support individuals, families and communities to address life challenges, enhance wellbeing and bring about social change. Social workers can work in private practice or as part of an interprofessional team across clinical, community and organisational settings, and the degree blends intellectual challenge with practical placements. International students study primarily on campus. Graduates work in child protection and family services, health and hospital social work, mental health, community development, and policy and advocacy.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Human Service Provision (6 units); Communication Skills in Social Work and Human Services (6 units); Child Development (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Introduction to Australian Politics (6 units); Group Work (6 units); Making Sense of Societies: Sociology in Practice (6 units); Working with Community (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Human Service Intervention (6 units); Social Research Methods (6 units); Interviewing Skills in Social Work and Human Services (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Mental Health and Mental Wellbeing (6 units); Preparation for Field Placement (6 units); Human Service Workers and the Law (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Aboriginal Australians and the Human Services (6 units); Social Work Field Education 1 (18 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Advanced Social Work Theory and Practice (6 units); Working with Human Service Organisations (6 units); Policy Practice (6 units).
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 75 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 7.0, with no band below 7.0.

name: Bachelor of Software Engineering (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Software Engineering (Honours) at Adelaide University equips students with the specialist knowledge, technical skills and software development practices to work professionally as software engineers. Students are exposed to a blend of theoretical knowledge and applied practical skills, developing a deep understanding of how software solutions are designed and built. They learn the knowledge, principles and systematic practices of software requirements, design, development and testing to produce reliable, maintainable and scalable solutions to complex problems. Students become proficient in programming and in producing quality software artefacts, graduating with a versatile and sought-after skillset for the software innovation sector.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Professional Engineering Practice (6 units); Problem Solving and Programming (6 units); Structured Data (6 units); Information Technology Systems (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Security Foundations (6 units); Object-Oriented Programming (6 units); System Requirements (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Engineering Project Management (6 units); Cloud Platforms (6 units); System Design (6 units); Software Development Practice (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Unstructured Data (6 units); Agile Development and User Experience (6 units); Data Structures and Algorithms (6 units); Web Technology (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Secure Software Development (6 units); Systems Engineering and Professional Practice (6 units); Design Patterns (6 units).
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 80 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Bachelor of Speech Pathology (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Speech Pathology (Honours) at Adelaide University equips students to diagnose and treat conditions across the full scope of speech pathology practice, including speech and language, swallowing, fluency, voice and cognition. Students explore core anatomy, physiology, public health and health research concepts and learn how these are applied in the speech pathology field. Professional and technical skills are sharpened in simulation suites and purpose-built training facilities, and through clinical placements. Speech pathologists help people of all ages who experience difficulties with communication or with eating and drinking safely, and graduates work across health, education and community settings.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Common core; Human Anatomy and Physiology A (6 units); Introduction to Speech Pathology Practice (UoA) (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Psychological Foundations for Allied Health (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Linguistics for Speech Pathology B (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Speech Pathology Clinical Skills and Practice (6 units); Program electives.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Preparing for Speech Pathology Practice (6 units).
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 90 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 8.0, with no band below 8.0.

name: Bachelor of Sustainability and Climate Change
description: Adelaide University's Bachelor of Sustainability and Climate Change is a three-year undergraduate degree in Adelaide. It examines the environmental and political forces shaping climate policy and adaptation, and students choose interest areas including global politics, environmental management and sociology. Graduates work in sustainability, environmental policy, advocacy and program roles across government, business and non-government organisations.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Common core; Humanity in a Changing Climate (6 units); Fundamentals of Climate Change (6 units); Elective.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Global Environmental Politics (6 units); Culture, Society and Climate Change (6 units); Majors; Majors.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Common core; Professional Pathways and Destinations 2 (6 units); Communicating Climate Change (6 units); Majors.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Majors; Majors; Responding to Climate Change (6 units); Elective.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Common core.
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 75 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Bachelor of Teaching
description: A four-year honours degree that qualifies graduates to teach primary school, Reception to Year 6. It is a standalone undergraduate route into teaching, not a graduate-entry program. Placement is substantial and starts in first year, building to 640 hours of supervised professional experience across the degree. Before the final placement, students must pass the national LANTITE literacy and numeracy test and complete child protection training, and a Working with Children Check is required. Entry requires IELTS 7.0 with no band below 7.0 for international students. On graduation students are eligible to apply for registration with the Teachers Registration Board of South Australia. Adelaide also offers early childhood and secondary teaching routes, with secondary teaching taken as a graduate-entry master's. It suits students committed to primary teaching from the start of their undergraduate study.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Learning About Language (6 units); Languages Education (6 units); Technologies Education (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — The Brain and Learning (6 units); Discipline courses; Health and Physical Education (6 units); Professional Experience 1: Professional Identity and the Role of the Teacher (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Digital Literacy and Artificial Intelligence for Learning and Societal Change (6 units); Science Education (6 units); Discipline courses; Humanities and Social Science Education (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Learning About Reading (6 units); Mathematics Education 1 (6 units); Classroom Management in Primary Contexts (6 units); Professional Experience 2: Curriculum, Pedagogy and Assessment (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Effective Pedagogical Practices for Primary Contexts; Professional Experience 3: Planning, Teaching and Assessing for Diversity (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Learning about Literacies and Text Production (6 units).
admission_requirements: ATAR 75; personal-capacity interview typical for teaching entry (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, no band below 7.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL), required for health/education placements

name: Bachelor of Veterinary Bioscience
description:
A three-year science degree that is the first half of Adelaide University's six-year veterinary pathway: graduates move into the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine, and only the two together lead to registration as a vet.

Year one covers foundational biology and chemistry, with later years moving into veterinary anatomy and physiology, animal nutrition, genetics, microbiology, parasitology and epidemiology, and hands-on animal work from first semester. It includes a 12-week animal husbandry placement on farms with cattle, sheep and horses, taught at purpose-built facilities including a teaching hospital. Entry is competitive: an ATAR of about 90, SACE Stage 2 biology, chemistry or mathematical methods, plus a questionnaire and the Casper assessment. It suits students committed to the full veterinary pathway.
admission_requirements: ATAR-equivalent selection rank of 90.00 or higher (adjusted) (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, no band below 7.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL), required for health/education placements

name: Bachelor of Veterinary Technology
description: Adelaide University's Bachelor of Veterinary Technology is a three-year, clinically focused undergraduate degree in Adelaide with access to the university's $37 million veterinary health centre. Students build advanced skills in the nursing care of companion animals, horses, farm animals, wildlife and exotic pets, and graduate with substantial hands-on experience. They work as veterinary technicians and nurses across clinical practice, industry and animal welfare.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Animal Handling and Husbandry (6 units); Foundations of Science for Veterinary Technologists (6 units); Anatomy for Veterinary Technologists (6 units); Veterinary Team Foundations (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Principles of Animal Behaviour, Welfare and Ethics (6 units); Introduction to Mechanisms of Health (6 units); Physiology for Veterinary Technologists (6 units); Evidence-based Veterinary Technology (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Animal Microbiology, Virology and Immunology 2 (6 units); Introduction to Workplace Skills 2 (6 units); Pathology for Veterinary Technologists 2 (6 units); Clinical Studies A (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Pharmacology, Pharmacy and Therapeutics 2 (6 units); Biosecurity, Epidemiology and Food Safety for Veterinary Technologists (6 units); Clinical Studies B (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Clinical Skills in Veterinary Technology 3 (12 units); Transition to the Veterinary Technology Profession 3 (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Clinical Practice in Veterinary Technology 3 (12 units); Program electives.
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 75 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Bachelor of Visual Effects
description: Adelaide University's Bachelor of Visual Effects is a three-year undergraduate degree in Adelaide focused on the visual effects work behind film, television and streaming content. Students develop technical and creative skills in areas such as 3D, compositing, simulation and lighting, working on production-style projects with industry input. Graduates work as VFX artists, compositors and technical artists in the screen and games industries.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Cinematic Design (6 units); Digital Compositing (6 units); Introduction to 3D (6 units); Introduction to Film and Television (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Cinematography and Editing (6 units); Character Performance (6 units); Look Development (6 units); Common core.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Common core; Common core; Dynamic Effects (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Work Integrated Learning.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Work Integrated Learning.
Year 3, Semester 2 — Work Integrated Learning.
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 70 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Bachelor of Viticulture and Oenology
description: The Bachelor of Viticulture and Oenology at Adelaide University is a four-year degree that teaches best-practice techniques for growing wine grapes and making wine, taught at the Waite Campus where a large share of Australia's wine research takes place. Students learn hands-on, from growing grapes in the on-campus vineyard to making wine in the commercial-scale campus winery, within one of the largest agricultural and viticultural teaching and research precincts in the Southern Hemisphere. Graduates work as winemakers and viticulturists, managing vineyards, developing new technologies and focusing on sustainable winemaking.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Biology 1B: Evolution and Diversity of Organisms (6 units); Program core selective courses; Program core selective courses.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Soils and Landscapes (6 units); Biology 1A: Molecules, Genes and Cells (6 units); Program core selective courses.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Soil and Water Resources (6 units); Agricultural Biochemistry (6 units); Foundations in Plant Science (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Agricultural Genetics (6 units); Viticultural Science 2 (6 units); Sensory Studies 2 (6 units); Introductory Winemaking 2 (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Plant Health (6 units); Viticultural Science 3 (6 units); Winemaking at Vintage 3 (6 units).

Graduates move into management consulting, human resource management, supply chain roles and general leadership positions across business, not-for-profits and government. name: Master of Accounting
description:
Adelaide University's Master of Accounting is a two-year conversion degree accredited by both Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand and CPA Australia, so graduates are eligible for membership of both and can enter their professional programs.

No accounting background is required: the curriculum runs from financial and management accounting, business law, economics and business mathematics through auditing, taxation and financial statement analysis, ending with an accounting industry project in the final semester. Entry is a completed bachelor's degree or equivalent. It suits career changers and mid-career professionals heading into audit, tax, management accounting or forensic accounting roles.

Year 1, Semester 1 — Accounting Concepts and Methods (6 units); Principles of Finance (6 units); Business Statistics (6 units); Economic Principles (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Accounting Information Production and Analytics (6 units); Commercial and Business Law (6 units); Intermediate Financial Reporting (6 units); Management Accounting Concepts and Techniques (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Taxation Law and Policy (6 units); Auditing and Assurance Services (6 units); Advanced Financial Accounting (6 units); Financial Statement Analysis (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Accounting Industry Project 1 (6 units); Program electives; Program electives; Program electives.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); no prior accounting study required. GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; cognate graduates receive advanced standing.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Accounting and Business Analytics
description: Adelaide University's Master of Accounting and Business Analytics is a two-year degree in Adelaide that combines a professional accounting grounding with data analytics skills, so graduates can both prepare and interpret financial information and analyse the data behind business decisions. It suits graduates from other fields moving into accounting and analytics roles across industry, government and professional services.

Year 1, Semester 1 — Business Statistics (6 units); Economic Principles (6 units); Accounting Concepts and Methods (6 units); Principles of Finance (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Accounting Information Production and Analytics (6 units); Intermediate Financial Reporting (6 units); Fundamentals of Business Analytics (6 units); Customer Analytics (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Predictive and Visual Analytics (6 units); Commercial and Business Law (6 units); Management Accounting Concepts and Techniques (6 units); Auditing and Assurance Services (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Program electives; Advanced Financial Accounting (6 units); Managing with Big Data Analytics (6 units); Business Analytics Project 1 (6 units).
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; OR A completed nested or related graduate certificate (AQF level 8) or higher or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution. This degree requires a Grade Point Average (GPA) equivalent to an Adelaide University 4.5 on a 7-point scale for entry.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Accounting and Finance
description:
A two-year master's (96 units) that sits between the Master of Accounting and the Master of Finance, giving both a professional accounting qualification and genuine finance depth. It is accredited by Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand and CPA Australia, so graduates can join both professional programs.

The accounting side covers financial and management accounting, auditing and taxation; the finance side adds investment, derivatives and corporate finance, with access to simulated trading environments. A graduate certificate or diploma exit is available. Entry needs a bachelor's degree with a GPA equivalent to 4.5 on Adelaide's 7-point scale, no accounting background required. It suits people who want both the CA or CPA pathway and finance skills for a broader commercial or leadership role.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Accounting Concepts and Methods (6 units); Economic Principles (6 units); Principles of Finance (6 units); Business Statistics (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Accounting Information Production and Analytics (6 units); Intermediate Financial Reporting (6 units); Fixed Income Securities (6 units); Equity Valuation and Analysis (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Derivatives (6 units); Ethical Principles in Finance and Accounting (6 units); Commercial and Business Law (6 units); Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Advanced Investment Management (6 units); Management Accounting Concepts and Techniques (6 units); Advanced Financial Accounting (6 units); Program electives.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in any discipline (cognate discipline preferred)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Applied Finance
description:
A shorter, more applied companion to the Master of Finance: 1.5 years full-time (72 units, 54 core plus 18 electives), with a graduate certificate or diploma exit point. The core runs through accounting concepts, principles of finance, economics, equity valuation, fixed income, derivatives and advanced investment management, plus an ethics course, and electives include financial modelling, behavioural finance, fintech, blockchain and international finance.

The emphasis is on applied courses and real-world problem solving rather than finance theory, and the finance courses align with major professional bodies. Entry needs a bachelor's degree with a GPA equivalent to 4.5 on Adelaide's 7-point scale. It suits people who want a faster route into financial analyst, investment or corporate finance roles.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Business Statistics (6 units); Economic Principles (6 units); Accounting Concepts and Methods (6 units); Principles of Finance (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Equity Valuation and Analysis (6 units); Fixed Income Securities (6 units); Ethical Principles in Finance and Accounting (6 units); Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Derivatives (6 units); Advanced Investment Management (6 units); Program electives; Program electives.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in any discipline (cognate discipline preferred)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Architecture
description:
Adelaide University's Master of Architecture is a two-year graduate-entry degree for people who hold a Bachelor of Architectural Design or an equivalent three-year pre-professional architecture degree; international applicants may be considered on portfolio. It is accredited by the Architectural Practice Board of South Australia and meets the National Standard of Competency for Architects, so after supervised experience and the registration exams graduates can register as architects in Australia and New Zealand.

Learning is studio-based in dedicated design studios and workshops, with real projects and industry input across sustainable design, heritage conservation and construction technology. It suits architecture graduates who need the accredited master's to register and want to develop a specialisation.

Year 2, Semester 1 — Reflective Practices (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Advanced Architectural Design Research Studio (Graduate Project) (12 units); Professional Practice in Architecture (6 units); Architectural Professional Experience (6 units).

name: Master of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
description:
Adelaide University's Master of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning is a two-year degree (66 core units) covering AI ethics, privacy and security, programming for AI and ML, statistical foundations, machine learning algorithms, applied AI, advanced topics, deep learning applications, and generative AI, ending in a two-semester industry capstone project. Students also take 18 elective units in areas such as computer vision and multimodal ML, data-driven decision-making, and prediction.

Entry requires a bachelor's degree in computer science, computer systems engineering, or software engineering (or a graduate certificate in computing), a GPA around 4.5 on a 7-point scale, and IELTS 6.5. It is not a conversion degree for people without a computing background. Part-time study is not available to international students.

Year 2, Semester 1 — Applied Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (6 units); Advanced Topics in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (6 units); Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Generative Artificial Intelligence (6 units); Applied Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning 2 (6 units); ICT Master Capstone Project 1 (6 units); ICT Master Capstone Project 2 (6 units).

english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

Master of Biotechnology

Adelaide University offers biotechnology at master's level as the Master of Science specialising in Biotechnology: a two-year degree (96 units) combining advanced research platforms and techniques with a strong commercialisation focus, including a science commercialisation and innovation course covering intellectual property and taking discoveries to market.

Electives include animal biotechnology, genomics applications, good manufacturing practice and risk assessment, and academically strong students can take a year-long independent research project. Entry needs a bachelor's or honours degree in a related field such as genetics, biochemistry or molecular biology with a GPA equivalent to 5.0 on Adelaide's 7-point scale. It suits science graduates heading into research, product development or commercialisation roles in pharmaceuticals, healthcare, agriculture or biotech startups.

name: Master of Business Administration (MBA)
description:
Adelaide University's MBA is a compact 36-unit program designed to run 1.5 years full-time, aimed at people who already have several years of management experience rather than a direct pathway from undergraduate study.

The core is 27 units including a capstone course, with 3 units set aside for an applied research component and 6 units of electives students can draw from any postgraduate coursework the university offers, which in practice lets students informally lean the degree toward finance, marketing, or entrepreneurship without committing to a named specialisation. A dedicated specialisation track (Human Resource Management is one option) restructures this into seven core courses plus three specialisation courses and two electives.

Intake runs three times a year (March, June, and August), unusually frequent for an MBA and suited to working professionals who can't always start in February. Graduates typically move into senior management, consulting, or start their own ventures, and the degree leans on case-study teaching and industry guest input rather than a purely lecture-based format.
curriculum:
Term 1 — Managing People and Organisations; Financial Management for Decision Making; Strategic Marketing; 1 elective.
Term 2 — Business Analytics; Managerial Economics; Operations and Supply Chain Management.
Term 3 — Leadership and Change; Corporate Strategy; Applied Business Research Project (part 1).
Term 4 — MBA Capstone: Integrative Business Strategy; Applied Business Research Project (part 2); 1 elective.
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree plus a minimum of 3 years' relevant professional work experience (or approved equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with 6.0 minimum in each band.

name: Master of Business Analytics
description:
Adelaide University's Master of Business Analytics is a two-year degree (96 units) with February and July intakes. The core covers accounting concepts, principles of finance, business statistics, economic principles, predictive and visual analytics, chatbots and text analytics, and managing with big data. Discipline courses add analytics fundamentals, customer analytics, and two Business Analytics Projects in the final semester that act as the capstone.

Electives range across financial modelling, blockchain and smart contracts, fintech, people analytics, and advanced marketing analytics. A maths background is recommended but not required; entry is a bachelor's degree with a GPA around 4.5 on a 7-point scale and IELTS 6.5. Indicative international fee is around A$57,100 per year.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Accounting Concepts and Methods (6 units); Principles of Finance (6 units); Business Statistics (6 units); Economic Principles (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Entrepreneurial Thinking (6 units); Project Management Fundamentals (6 units); Fundamentals of Business Analytics (6 units); Customer Analytics (6 units); Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Predictive and Visual Analytics (6 units); Chatbots and Text Analytics for Business (6 units); Managing with Big Data Analytics (6 units); Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Business Analytics Project 2 (6 units); Business Analytics Project 1 (6 units); Program electives; Program electives.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in any discipline (cognate discipline preferred)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Computer Science
description:
A two-year, 96-unit degree (66 core + 30 elective units) at Adelaide City Campus with February and July intakes, weighted heavily toward artificial intelligence and machine learning alongside cybersecurity.

The 30 elective units (five 6-unit courses) can be drawn from options including generative AI, applied AI and machine learning, deep learning applications, data in IT systems, requirements and user experience, and an ICT internship.

Provisionally accredited at the Professional level by the Australian Computer Society (ACS) and recognised internationally through the Seoul Accord. Adelaide University lists graduate career paths including computer scientist, AI specialist, defence scientist, IT manager, and systems programmer.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — ARTI5006 Ethics, Privacy and Security in AI and ML; COMP5004 Programming for AI and ML; INFO6004 Cloud Security; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — ARTI6003 Machine Learning Algorithms; COMP5050 Event Driven Computing (PG); COMP5800 Industry Research Project; PROJ5001 Project Management for IT Professionals (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — ARTI6000 Advanced Topics in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning; INFO6003 Security Architecture and Engineering; 2 electives (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — COMP6024 ICT Master Capstone Project 1; COMP6000 ICT Master Capstone Project 2; 2 electives (24 units).
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (AQF7) or bachelor honours (AQF8) in computer science, computer systems engineering, or software engineering (or a graduate diploma AQF8+ in computer science), with a GPA equivalent to 4.5/7.0.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with 6.0 minimum in each of reading, listening, speaking, writing.

name: Master of Construction Management
description: Adelaide University's Master of Construction Management is a two-year degree in Adelaide that prepares students to oversee projects from start to finish, on time, on budget and to quality. It emphasises sustainability, modern construction techniques and construction technology, with multidisciplinary coursework and opportunities for industry placements and research. Graduates work across residential, commercial and infrastructure construction.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Construction Management Research Methods (6 units); Cost Planning and Management (6 units); Construction Management and Technology 2 (6 units); Building Services and Environment (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Construction Management and Technology 1 (6 units); Measurement (6 units); Building Materials and Structures (6 units); Construction Contract Management (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Advanced Construction Technologies (6 units); Construction Management Research Dissertation A (6 units); Program electives; Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Digital Design and Construction (6 units); Advanced Construction Contract Management (6 units); Construction Management Research Dissertation B (6 units); Program electives.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; OR A completed nested or related graduate certificate (AQF level 8) or higher or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution. This degree requires a Grade Point Average (GPA) equivalent to an Adelaide University 4.5 on a 7-point scale for entry.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Counselling and Psychotherapy
description: Adelaide University's Master of Counselling and Psychotherapy is a two-year degree in Adelaide that builds clinically proficient counsellors grounded in ethics and evidence-based practice. Students study contemporary theories and therapeutic approaches and develop skills through experiential learning, including simulated sessions with actors playing clients. Graduates work as counsellors and psychotherapists across health, education and community services.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Counselling Skills 1 (6 units); Attachment Processes in the Therapeutic Relationship (6 units); Counselling and Psychotherapy Theories (6 units); Mindfulness-based Counselling Applications (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Ethics in the Counselling Workplace (6 units); Counselling Skills 2 (6 units); Nature of Grief (6 units); Discipline courses.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Discipline courses; Discipline courses; Discipline courses.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Discipline courses; Discipline courses; Program electives.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; AND; OR Undertake the Casper Situational Judgement Test (CSJT); AND; OR Attend an interview, if invited.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 7.0, with no band below 7.0.

name: Master of Curatorial and Museum Studies
description: Adelaide University's Master of Curatorial and Museum Studies is a two-year degree in Adelaide delivered in partnership with cultural institutions including the South Australian Museum and the History Trust of South Australia. It challenges existing museum theory and practice, with a focus on ethical collection and exhibition development, First Nations truth-telling, and international cultural exchange. Graduates work as curators and museum professionals.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Making a museum (6 units); Program electives; Program electives.
Year 1, Semester 2 — The Secret Life of Objects: Museums in Practice (6 units); Program electives; Program electives.
