description: The Bachelor of Health Science at Charles Darwin University provides the skills to work in a multidisciplinary health industry, with strong health industry connections and diverse content leading to work in health policy and research, health and wellbeing, health promotion and public health. The degree is a pathway into master's-level study in occupational therapy, nutrition, speech and language pathology, physiotherapy, health research and public health. A core part of the course is community engagement and a community project that provides the opportunity to put knowledge into practice, supported by CDU academic staff.

name: Bachelor of Health Services Management
description: The Bachelor of Health Services Management at Charles Darwin University offers units across health, business and information technology to prepare students to contribute to the health service management industry. Graduates gain an understanding of business management and of the diversity of health clients, the importance of cultural safety, health promotion, and local and global health issues influencing the health care system. The course explores the challenges of working in urban, rural and remote communities and offers scholarships, international study tours and student exchange, with students studying alongside peers from business, social work and other allied health areas.

name: Bachelor of Humanitarian Aid and Development
description: The Bachelor of Humanitarian Aid and Development at Charles Darwin University is an interdisciplinary degree that teaches students to understand, critically analyse and apply concepts of community development, humanitarian practice and development aid. Students explore culture studies, sociology, ethics, Indigenous knowledge, community development, international humanitarian assistance and development, project management and language studies, learning from academics and industry practitioners focused on national and international community work, disaster relief and development. Students complete a two-week compulsory intensive at the Casuarina campus, and Human Services major students undertake 400 hours of community placement.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description: The Bachelor of Information Technology at Charles Darwin University prepares students to develop creative and innovative technologies, building knowledge and skills in web design and development, networking, application development and systems, and encouraging open-minded problem solving, creative thinking and engaging communication. Students can undertake sought-after industry modules including Cisco and Microsoft certificates. Graduates may work as an information technology specialist in government, private companies and non-government organisations, as a web designer and developer, among other roles.

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
Studying law at CDU means studying it in a jurisdiction most Australian law schools barely touch: the Northern Territory has its own quirks in areas like Indigenous land rights, mining and resources law, and criminal sentencing that don't come up the same way in a Sydney or Melbourne law degree. Students get exposure to that Territory-specific context alongside the standard Priestley 11 subjects the profession requires everywhere in Australia.

The LLB runs 240 credit points across three years full-time, with a maximum of 100 credit points able to come from first-year (100-level) units and at least 60 credit points required at 300-level or above, a structure meant to stop students front-loading easy units and coasting. Most of the core sequence (contracts, torts, criminal law, property, equity, evidence, civil procedure) is prescribed by the legal profession's admission requirements, so there's not much room to swap those out; the flexibility shows up in the specialist electives, where students can lean toward family law, international law, or competition and consumer law depending on where they want to end up.

CDU offers full online delivery for the whole degree, which is unusual for a law program and reflects the practical reality that a lot of NT residents live hours from Darwin. Graduates wanting Honours can roll straight into the one-year Bachelor of Laws Honours add-on rather than restarting a separate degree.
curriculum:
Year 1: Legal Process, Contracts A & B, Criminal Law, Legal Research and Writing, foundational electives
Year 2: Torts, Property Law, Equity and Trusts, Administrative Law, Constitutional Law
Year 3: Evidence, Civil Procedure, Company Law, Professional Conduct, capstone/clinical elective
Specialist electives across the degree: family law, international law, competition and consumer law, Indigenous legal issues
Structure: 240 credit points total, max 100 credit points at 100-level, minimum 60 credit points at 300-level or above
Optional: Bachelor of Laws Honours (1 additional year) for eligible graduates
Delivery: on campus, fully online, or blended; 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Laws Honours
description: The Bachelor of Laws Honours at Charles Darwin University is a one-year course for high-achieving Bachelor of Laws graduates. It may provide a pathway to a PhD, enhance career prospects and advance legal research and writing skills. Students undertake a substantial legal research project in an area relevant to their career, deeply exploring a legal topic and developing an understanding of research methodologies relevant to law and legal scholarship, with support from CDU academic staff and a research supervisor to produce work to a publishable level. Successful completion may make graduates eligible for admission to a PhD.

name: Bachelor of Medical Laboratory Science Honours
description: The Bachelor of Medical Laboratory Science Honours at Charles Darwin University provides the knowledge and skills to work as a medical scientist in diagnostic pathology, in areas such as haematology, clinical chemistry, microbiology, histology and molecular pathology. Students are taught by industry professionals and learn to test samples, interpret results and make recommendations for improved patient health, with placements that let students apply their skills in the workplace. In the final year students can undertake a research project or advanced professional practice alongside medical scientists and researchers in accredited laboratories.

name: Bachelor of Midwifery
description: The Bachelor of Midwifery at Charles Darwin University is a professionally accredited degree that qualifies graduates to register as a midwife, recognised by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. Students study online with intensive clinical teaching blocks or on campus, full-time or part-time, learning from experts in the field. Graduates provide woman-centred, evidence-based care for women, babies and families throughout the childbearing journey in a variety of settings, with a particular focus on rural, remote and First Nations Australians, supporting women's childbearing choices across pregnancy, birth, postnatal and newborn periods.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Remote and Indigenous health placements are the defining feature of nursing at CDU in a way they simply aren't at most Australian nursing schools, because the Northern Territory has some of the most acute rural and remote health workforce shortages in the country. Students complete 800 hours of clinical placement across metropolitan and rural/remote settings, and those who've finished second-year scope-of-practice units plus the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health unit can apply for a four-week remote placement, run in partnership with NT Top End Health Service, that puts them into genuinely remote clinical settings most nursing graduates elsewhere never experience before registration.

That partnership-driven remote placement track is a real point of difference for students who know they want a career in remote area nursing, a distinct, higher-paid, higher-autonomy specialisation within Australian nursing that's hard to break into without exactly this kind of exposure during training. Indigenous students undertaking placements also have access to 'away from base' funding support, recognising that a lot of NT students are commuting from communities well outside Darwin.

The degree meets registration requirements set by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, so graduates can register as Registered Nurses nationally; the remote and Indigenous health specialisation is additive, not a trade-off against the standard national scope of practice.
curriculum:
Core sequence: Anatomy and Physiology, Pathophysiology, Pharmacology, Nursing Practice (foundational through advanced), Mental Health Nursing, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health, Community and Primary Health Care
Clinical placement: 800 hours total across metropolitan and rural/remote settings
Elective pathway: 4-week remote placement (Northern Territory) available to eligible 3rd-year students, delivered with NT Top End Health Service
Capstone: transition-to-practice placement in final semester
Total: 3 years full-time, registration-ready under Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia standards
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 6.5) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Nutrition
description: The Bachelor of Nutrition at Charles Darwin University provides the knowledge and skills to work in the food and nutrition sector to positively influence health, leading to work in health policy and research, health and wellbeing, and health promotion across local, rural and remote Australia and beyond. The course is a pathway into master's-level study in dietetics. Graduates may work in community health centres, health promotion organisations, government and non-government organisations, the food industry, sporting organisations, universities and research organisations, in roles such as nutrition consulting.

name: Bachelor of Oral Health Therapy
description: The Bachelor of Oral Health Therapy at Charles Darwin University prepares graduates for a career as an oral health therapist, meeting the oral health needs of communities in the Northern Territory and across Australia with an emphasis on being adaptable, culturally safe, fair and sustainable. Students develop skills in health promotion, communication, clinical decision-making, problem-solving and critical thinking for person-centred care, with a focus on social and professional responsibility, leadership, and scientific and clinical knowledge. Work-ready skills are developed through simulation and clinic-based learning, including treatments such as fillings, tooth removals and periodontal care.

name: Bachelor of Paramedicine
description: The Bachelor of Paramedicine at Charles Darwin University qualifies graduates to work as a paramedic in Australia, with guaranteed clinical placements in the Northern Territory across a range of health care providers. Graduates are ready to work in emergency ambulance and out-of-hospital environments in regional, remote and urban settings. Over the three years, students gain clinical decision-making, problem-solving and critical thinking skills and learn about anatomy and physiology, human development and Australia's health-care systems, developing knowledge in clinical science areas including trauma and emergency response, with a strong focus on First Nations health and mental health.

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
This is CDU's APAC-accredited entry point into psychology: the degree that has to exist before an Honours year, before provisional registration, before any of the postgraduate paths toward clinical or organisational psychology. Because that accreditation constrains the curriculum tightly (APAC dictates a lot of the sequencing and content to meet national competency standards), CDU's version looks broadly similar to psych degrees at other Australian universities, but it opens with a Year 1 that explicitly folds in Indigenous protocols and intercultural sensitivity content alongside the usual introduction to psychology and research methods, a reflection of the practicum and research contexts students are likely to work in around Darwin and remote NT communities.

Across the degree, students work through roughly 24 standard subjects covering biological, cognitive, developmental, and social psychology, plus a heavy research methods and statistics load that culminates in an independent research project in third year. Graduates who want to continue toward registration as a psychologist need the Honours year (also APAC-accredited at CDU) or an equivalent postgraduate qualifying program; this bachelor's alone doesn't get you registration, which surprises some students who assume otherwise.

Students can also join the Australian Psychological Society as student members while still completing this degree, which gives earlier access to networking and CPD content than waiting until after graduation.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Research Methods and Design, Psychology Ethics, Indigenous protocols and intercultural sensitivity, Biological Bases of Behaviour
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology, Statistics for Psychology, Personality and Individual Differences
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology, Psychological Assessment, Advanced Research Methods, independent research project, specialist electives
Pathway: Bachelor of Psychological Science Honours (1 additional year, APAC-accredited) required before provisional psychologist registration
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science Honours
description: The Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours) at Charles Darwin University is an Australian Psychology Accreditation Council accredited fourth-year program designed to equip students with an in-depth understanding of the application of psychological theories to practice and to advance their capacity to design, conduct, interpret and communicate impactful research. It suits high-achieving psychology students who want to distinguish themselves and advance their knowledge of psychological assessment and intervention, and provides in-demand interdisciplinary skills valued by employers in human-centred professions.

name: Bachelor of Public Health
description: The Bachelor of Public Health at Charles Darwin University teaches students how to connect with communities and develop innovative, evidence-based health strategies, with a focus on addressing health disparities experienced by populations and communities at a local, national and global level. The qualification prepares graduates to work in health promotion, policy making, research and disease prevention, and is available online or on campus. Units cover topics such as epidemiology, cultural safety, social media, and global and environmental health, and CDU offers scholarships and international study tours.

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
CDU's plain Bachelor of Science is the flexible, build-your-own-major sibling to its more structured Environmental Science degree, and its real drawcard is what's on the university's doorstep: Kakadu, Litchfield, the Timor Sea, and some of the most intact tropical savanna and monsoon ecosystems left in the world. Research project options in the final year regularly draw on this: aquaculture, marine and freshwater ecology, botany, and zoology projects here look genuinely different from equivalent projects at a temperate-climate university, because the field sites and species are different.

Unlike a lot of generalist BSc degrees that are essentially a menu of first-year science subjects with no strong identity, CDU leans into its geography: field intensives take students into Northern and Central Australia and parts of the Asia-Pacific for hands-on data collection, which becomes a differentiator on a CV compared to lab-only science degrees. Students without a settled major can still keep options open through first year before choosing a direction.

It's worth being clear-eyed that CDU is not a large research-intensive science faculty compared to a Go8 university, so students chasing a narrow specialisation in, say, particle physics or advanced biochemistry will find the depth of elective offerings thinner than at a bigger institution. The strength here is specifically in field-based, tropical and environmental science.
curriculum:
Year 1: foundational units across two or more of Biology, Chemistry, Earth Science, Mathematics, Physics
Year 2: discipline deepening in chosen area(s), plus statistics and research design
Year 3: advanced electives and an independent or supervised research project (options include aquaculture, marine ecology, freshwater and terrestrial ecology, botany, zoology)
Field components: optional field intensives in Northern and Central Australia and the Asia-Pacific region
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time, on campus or online (lab units require on-campus attendance)
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Science and Technology
description: The Bachelor of Science and Technology at Charles Darwin University is an interdisciplinary degree that lets students tailor their studies across science, engineering and information technology, blending theoretical knowledge with practical, hands-on experience. Students build analytical, technical and problem-solving skills through lab work, collaborative projects and industry-focused learning, applying technology to real challenges alongside experts. Graduates are prepared to collaborate across disciplines, adapt to emerging technologies, and work in careers that drive industry, research and innovation.

name: Bachelor of Science Honours
description: The Bachelor of Science Honours at Charles Darwin University is a one-year course that includes a major research project, advanced-level coursework and research skills training across science disciplines including environmental science, health and clinical science, and information technology. Research areas include biology, ecology, hydrological science, spatial science, analytical chemistry and molecular modelling, exercise and sports science, medical laboratory science, pharmacy, information systems, mobile networking and software development. The honours qualification prepares graduates for professional positions requiring higher-level project management, communication, analysis, problem-solving and research skills, under the guidance of experienced researchers.

name: Bachelor of Social Work
description: The Bachelor of Social Work at Charles Darwin University is a professionally recognised degree that prepares graduates to work as a social worker, using principles of social justice, human rights and cultural safety to promote social change and empowerment through skills in counselling, case management and community development. The course incorporates knowledge from social work, psychology, social policy, research and First Nations Peoples perspectives, and prepares students to work with individuals, families, groups and communities, including those in crisis or affected by poverty and social disadvantage. It includes 20 days of face-to-face intensive classes prior to placements.

name: Bachelor of Software Engineering Honours
description: The Bachelor of Software Engineering Honours at Charles Darwin University develops an understanding of the underlying principles and applications of software engineering along with professional knowledge and skills for the digital world. Students can undertake sought-after industry modules including Cisco and Microsoft certification. Graduates are prepared to move into small and large organisations, consultancy, startups, and government and private companies. The degree is accredited by the Australian Computer Society at the level of professional practice in ICT and is recognised internationally under the Seoul Accord.

name: Diploma of Alcohol and Other Drugs Practice
Diploma of Arts
description: The Diploma of Arts at Charles Darwin University offers specialist and interdisciplinary thematic knowledge across areas including media studies, literature and creative writing, society and digital culture, Australian Indigenous knowledges, languages, linguistics and culture, interdisciplinary studies, and justice studies, peace and truth-telling. Students develop core communication, critical and creative thinking skills to participate in a multidisciplinary and global workforce. The diploma suits anyone who wants a taste of studying arts and a qualification without committing to a full bachelor's degree, and can lead into a bachelor program.

name: Diploma of Business Studies
description: The Diploma of Business Studies at Charles Darwin University is designed to reflect general business degree objectives and build toward the University's graduate attributes of creative, flexible and socially responsible graduates with skills in communication, leadership and team work. Delivered with UP Education, it parallels the existing first-year business course with the added dimensions of academic English development, increased contact time with staff, and a focus on the linguistic and cultural gaps that many students face in first-year units, providing a supported pathway into a business bachelor degree.

name: Diploma of Counselling
description: The Diploma of Counselling at Charles Darwin University is a first step for people seeking a career in counselling, wanting to increase their qualifications, or with an interest in psychology, social work and counselling. It prepares students with the knowledge and skills required for progression into the Bachelor of Psychological Science. Graduates may work in fields including counsellor, counselling support worker, case worker and case manager.

name: Diploma of Digital Enterprise
description: The Diploma of Digital Enterprise at Charles Darwin University is a flexible one-year qualification that combines business and information technology to prepare students for careers shaped by innovation and rapid digital change. Students develop a foundation in management, marketing, digital product development and data-driven decision-making, alongside core IT capabilities in web development, systems, networking and applications. The course can be tailored with a wide selection of business and IT units and studied online or on campus, and on completion students are eligible to transfer into the Bachelor of Digital Enterprise, Bachelor of Business or an IT bachelor degree.

name: Diploma of Engineering
description: The Diploma of Engineering at Charles Darwin University is ideal for people curious about studying engineering who are unsure about committing to a full undergraduate degree. Students explore general concepts, principles and practices of engineering, develop technical skills and build on their maths and science knowledge. The diploma qualifies students for entry-level engineering roles, or they can continue to CDU's Associate Degree in Engineering, Bachelor of Engineering Science, or Bachelor of Engineering Honours.

name: Diploma of Health Science
description: The Diploma of Health Science at Charles Darwin University equips students with essential skills and knowledge applicable to the Australian health care system, covering health promotion, effective communication and cultural safety in healthcare, with content focused on improving the health and wellbeing of individuals and communities. Graduates are well-prepared for further study, with completed units aligning with higher education pathways in fields such as occupational therapy, public health and nutrition. Graduates may work in health promotion, primary and community health centres, non-government organisations, social services, and project or therapy support roles.

name: Diploma of Information Technology
description: The Diploma of Information Technology at Charles Darwin University is designed to reflect general degree objectives and build toward the University's graduate attributes of creative, flexible and socially responsible graduates with skills in communication, leadership and team work. Delivered with UP Education, it parallels the existing first-year IT course with the added dimensions of academic English development, increased contact time with staff, and a focus on the linguistic and cultural gaps that many students face in first-year units, providing a supported pathway into an IT bachelor degree.

name: Diploma of Laws
description: The Diploma of Laws at Charles Darwin University offers a general understanding of the law, legal processes and legal principles, along with the opportunity to gain specialist knowledge needed for work or other reasons. It is also suitable for internationally qualified lawyers who need to complete some Australian subjects to qualify for admission to legal practice in Australia, and is a recognised pathway to the Bachelor of Laws with up to 80 credit points of credit transfer. The course does not lead to professional accreditation, though students can transfer to the accredited Bachelor of Laws.

name: Diploma of Network Engineering
description: The Diploma of Network Engineering at Charles Darwin University prepares students for entry-level network engineering roles by providing the skills and knowledge to design, operate and maintain the networks that underpin the infrastructure of industry and government organisations. Coursework covers key areas including data networks and their implementation, combining academic study with practical experience. The qualification can be used to move into the Bachelor of Information Technology or Bachelor of Software Engineering Honours, and students can undertake sought-after industry modules including Microsoft certification.

name: Diploma of Psychology
description: The Diploma of Psychology at Charles Darwin University is a first step for people considering a career in psychology, wanting to increase their qualifications, or with an interest in the field. It prepares students with the knowledge and skills required for progression into the APAC-approved Bachelor of Psychological Science, though the diploma itself is not APAC-approved. Graduates may be prepared for career opportunities in various psychology-related fields in government, private companies, non-government organisations and community groups, and the course may complement an existing professional career.

name: Diploma of Science
description: The Diploma of Science at Charles Darwin University is ideal for people curious about studying science who are unsure about committing to a degree, or those already working in the sciences who want to upskill in another discipline. Students explore science concepts, theories and principles across fields such as general science, biology, chemistry, environmental science, geographic information science, physics and mathematics, developing logical and critical thinking and problem-solving from a scientific and technological perspective. After completing the diploma, students can move into the Bachelor of Science or Bachelor of Environmental Science.

name: Doctor of Pharmacy
description: The Doctor of Pharmacy at Charles Darwin University prepares graduates for entry into the pharmacy profession, where pharmacists have an expanding scope of practice that includes advising prescribers, improving health literacy and access to vaccinations, contributing to the discovery of new medicines, and tailoring medicines to individuals. This graduate-entry, coursework extended master's program is offered both face-to-face and externally, with teaching commencing in an intensive block early in January so that unit prerequisites are met and units are studied in the correct sequence.

name: Graduate Certificate of Arts
description: The Graduate Certificate of Arts at Charles Darwin University is designed to diversify and expand knowledge in cultural and creative spheres, with unit choices across social sciences, Indigenous knowledges and engagement, Indigenous languages and contemporary social issues, Indigenous research practice, and creative arts. Whether consolidating expertise or moving into a new career path, students develop the analytical and critical thinking skills for success, exploring unique perspectives on contemporary issues facing Indigenous Australia, Northern Australia and South-East Asia, guided by lecturers who are leaders in their fields.

name: Graduate Certificate of Business
description: The Graduate Certificate of Business at Charles Darwin University equips professionals with the knowledge and practical skills to navigate today's evolving business landscape, exploring strategic decision-making, leadership, financial literacy and organisational management, and how to drive business success while balancing operational efficiency and stakeholder engagement. It offers a flexible learning experience for those seeking to upskill, pivot careers or lay the foundation for further study, and completion provides a pathway into the Master of Business Administration.

name: Graduate Certificate of Health Services Management
Graduate Certificate of Infectious Disease Prevention and Control
description: The Graduate Certificate of Infectious Disease Prevention and Control at Charles Darwin University offers an introduction to core concepts and skills in infectious disease prevention and control, including epidemiology, statistical research methods and quantitative analysis of health data, and key public health principles and practices aimed at preventing illness and protecting community health. Students learn from Menzies School of Health Research researchers, and on completion can articulate to the Graduate Diploma and Master of Public Health or the Graduate Diploma and Master of Health Research. Career opportunities include epidemiological and public health roles.

name: Graduate Certificate of Maternal Critical Care
description: The Graduate Certificate of Maternal Critical Care at Charles Darwin University is designed for registered nurses and midwives who want to extend their maternity clinical practice knowledge and develop advanced theoretical skills in obstetrical and gynaecological critical care. It suits nurses and midwives already employed in a clinical setting, with assessments that can be directly applied to professional practice. The course offers a strong theoretical and practical grounding that enables health practitioners to develop an analytical approach to clinical decision-making and provide enhanced maternity care services.

name: Graduate Certificate of Public Health
description: The Graduate Certificate of Public Health at Charles Darwin University equips students with the tools to investigate, critique and respond to real-world population health problems in local, global and planetary contexts. Students learn from Menzies School of Health Research professionals in Indigenous health, global health, public health practice and health research, and learn to analyse and interpret population health information, evaluate and design public health interventions, and formulate strategies to address complex issues such as health inequity, the social determinants of health and climate change, using evidence-based public health approaches, critical and systems thinking.

name: Graduate Certificate of Research Methods
description: The Graduate Certificate of Research Methods at Charles Darwin University develops research skills for application in the workplace or as a starting point for more advanced research training, providing an initiation into independent research. Graduates gain an understanding of research and fundamental knowledge, and learn to conduct ethical, creative and practical research in a range of contexts, equipped with the theoretical and methodological knowledge to carry out and present their research. Graduates may be eligible to apply for admission to a Master's by Research program, and admission to a PhD is determined based on grade point average and relevant experience.

name: Graduate Certificate of Specialist Education
description: The Graduate Certificate of Specialist Education at Charles Darwin University develops knowledge and skills in a specialist field of education, with options in Digital Learning Futures, Inclusive Education, Indigenous Knowledges Education, International Education, Managing and Leading Education, or Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages. It meets the professional development needs of teachers, practitioners, policymakers and principals working in the Northern Territory, Australia and the Asia Pacific, enhancing analytical thinking, collaborative learning and transformative practice in localised, national and international settings.

name: Graduate Certificate of University Learning and Teaching
description: The Graduate Certificate of University Learning and Teaching at Charles Darwin University focuses on the professional development of academic staff currently engaged in tertiary teaching, supporting them to develop practice-based core skills, versatility, competence and confidence in their learning and teaching environment. It also offers experienced tertiary teaching staff the opportunity to develop their practice and gain formal recognition as micro-credentials or a postgraduate qualification that can count toward a Master's. The pedagogy promotes reflective practice, co-design, peer review and students as partners.

name: Graduate Diploma of Emergency and Disaster Management
description: The Graduate Diploma of Emergency and Disaster Management at Charles Darwin University is based in Darwin, at the centre of the Top End and Australia's gateway to Indonesia and Southeast Asia, a region highly prone to and affected by various types of disasters. The program equips students to apply their knowledge and experience collaboratively and productively in this vulnerable region and elsewhere. Graduates gain the knowledge and skills to lead and manage all phases of the disaster management cycle, along with the confidence to apply their academic studies to practical responses.

name: Graduate Diploma of Health and Social Care
Graduate Diploma of Health Research
description: The Graduate Diploma of Health Research at Charles Darwin University equips students with advanced knowledge and skills in health research design and practice, learning from Menzies School of Health Research professionals in Indigenous health, public health and global health. Students acquire theoretical and practical capabilities in epidemiology, biostatistics, and quantitative and qualitative research methods. On completion, students can articulate to a Master of Health Research and undertake a supervised research project, then proceed with approval to higher degree research training, or articulate to a Master of Public Health.

name: Graduate Diploma of Indigenous Policy Development
description: The Graduate Diploma of Indigenous Policy Development at Charles Darwin University builds on professional knowledge and experience by providing a critical understanding of Indigenous economic and policy development in modern Australia. Students examine key issues of Indigenous policy development and implementation, economic development and participation, traditional and modern governance structures, and intellectual and cultural property rights in current social and political contexts. The course is a foundation for respectful and accountable engagement with Indigenous people and the social and political issues they face in Australia and internationally.

name: Graduate Diploma of Linguistic Studies
description: The Graduate Diploma of Linguistic Studies at Charles Darwin University prepares students for the analysis, evaluation and application of linguistic understandings to language, its use and its role in various contexts. Students build theoretical foundations in linguistics, with a focus on the contextualised evaluation of language that can be applied to theoretical analysis or to the professional development of forensic linguists, language teachers, TESOL practitioners, education policy makers, and those working in language revitalisation and maintenance, with directed engagement with First Nations, Australian, Asian and global content.

name: Graduate Diploma of Public Health
description: The Graduate Diploma of Public Health at Charles Darwin University equips students with the skills to investigate, critique and respond to real-world population health problems in local and global contexts, learning from Menzies School of Health Research professionals in Indigenous health, global health, public health practice and health research. Students acquire advanced knowledge in epidemiology, biostatistics, and quantitative and qualitative research methods, and learn to analyse population health information, evaluate and design interventions, and apply public health approaches to health promotion, disease control, health systems and policy.

name: Graduate Diploma of Specialist Education
description: The Graduate Diploma of Specialist Education at Charles Darwin University is a one-year professional development course that builds on experience in education with current educational and research perspectives, developing analytical thinking, collaborative learning and transformative practice skills in localised, national and international settings. It can be completed online or on campus, full-time or part-time, and specialisations include Digital Learning Futures, Inclusive Education, Indigenous Knowledges Education, International Education, Managing and Leading Education, TESOL, and University Teaching and Learning. It is designed for teachers, practitioners, policymakers and principals in the Northern Territory, Australia and the Asia Pacific.

name: Master by Research (Ias)
description: The Master by Research at Charles Darwin University is a research degree in which candidates undertake a program of research under the direction of two or more supervisors and communicate the results in a thesis or another approved format. Candidates also complete additional training and other activities in line with the University's higher degree by research policy to support their research and career. Research can be undertaken across CDU's disciplines, including in areas aligned with the Institute for Advanced Studies.

name: Master of Applied Linguistics
description: The Master of Applied Linguistics at Charles Darwin University prepares students for the analysis, evaluation and application of linguistic understandings to language, its use and its role in various contexts. Students build theoretical foundations in applied linguistics, with a focus on the contextualised evaluation of language that can be applied to theoretical analysis or to the professional development of linguists, language teachers, TESOL practitioners and education policy makers, with directed engagement with First Nations, Australian, Asian and global content. Study is available on campus or online, full-time or part-time.

name: Master of Applied Spatial Science
description: The Master of Applied Spatial Science at Charles Darwin University provides upskilling in geographic information systems and remote sensing for a diverse range of vocations. Aimed at those with little or no previous spatial science experience, and open to students with a bachelor's degree in any field, the course guides students through the fundamentals and develops more advanced geospatial skills to solve real-world problems across fields such as environmental science, health, agriculture, mining, disaster and emergency management, and tourism and business. Graduates work as spatial analysts, spatial ecologists, GIS analysts and remote sensing specialists.

name: Master of Architecture
description: The Master of Architecture at Charles Darwin University provides a well-rounded architectural education preparing students for contemporary professional practice leading to registration as an architect. Students who have completed the Bachelor of Architectural Design are eligible for entry. The curriculum builds on undergraduate knowledge and skills with a focus on designing for extreme climates and sustainable built environments in the diverse climatic regions of the Northern Territory and the Asia-Pacific. Students refine their 3D modelling skills to realise architectural designs and prepare architectural documentation and detailing that contribute to the quality of the built environment.

name: Master of Arts
description: The Master of Arts (Coursework) at Charles Darwin University is a flexible, unit-based course that offers opportunities to develop competencies in a range of fields, enhance career progression, update skills, and pursue interests in arts and social sciences. It also prepares students for a pathway into higher degree by research programs. Students specialise in one of social sciences, Indigenous knowledges and engagement, Indigenous languages and contemporary social issues, Indigenous research practice, or creative arts, and can select a research option to develop research skills alongside coursework.

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
CDU's standard MBA sits alongside two other variants the university offers (a Sustainable Leadership MBA and an Executive MBA), so prospective students should be clear on which one they're looking at, since course codes and unit lists differ meaningfully between them. This general MBA builds a fairly conventional core around strategic management, accounting, economics, marketing, and leadership, but distinguishes itself through an applied social enterprise and consulting project where students work on real client problems rather than a purely theoretical capstone.

In final semester, students choose between a professional placement or a set of specialist elective units aligned to their career direction, useful for career-changers who want workplace exposure baked into the degree, versus people already established in a role who'd rather deepen technical knowledge in, say, data analytics or entrepreneurship. Business analytics and data-driven decision-making show up as a running thread across the core units rather than being siloed into a single elective, reflecting a broader shift in Australian MBA design over the past several years.

Given CDU's northern Australia positioning, the program draws a notable number of students working in the resources, government, and not-for-profit sectors that dominate Territory employment, and case material sometimes reflects that regional economic mix more than a program based in a purely metropolitan CBD would.
curriculum:
Core units: Strategic Management, Managerial Accounting, Economics for Managers, Leadership and Organisational Behaviour, Marketing Management, Business Analytics, Corporate Finance, Business Research Methods
Applied component: social enterprise and consulting project (client-based team consulting engagement)
Final semester: choice of professional placement or specialist electives (entrepreneurship, data analytics, human resource management)
Total: 2 years full-time / up to 4 years part-time, on campus or online
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in any discipline; relevant work experience considered
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Business Administration Sustainable Enterprise
Master of Business Administration Sustainable Leadership
Master of Clinical Audiology
description: The Master of Clinical Audiology at Charles Darwin University is a two-year degree that provides the skills and knowledge to assess and provide rehabilitation for the hearing and balance systems across the lifespan, with specialist training in First Nations ear and hearing health and preparation to work in regional, rural and remote locations. Students attend compulsory clinical placements in various health contexts with adults, children and families, and four blocks of five-day face-to-face teaching intensives at the Casuarina campus, with interstate travel possibly required to meet clinical hour requirements.

name: Master of Data Science
description: Charles Darwin University Master of Data Science is a 160 credit point degree of core units, thesis research units, and specialist and general electives, with the specialist electives allowing an industry placement or an IT thesis. Entry requires a recognised bachelor degree with a major in computer science, information technology, information systems, statistics, mathematics or engineering, or a program with substantial quantitative content; applicants with at least five years of appropriate professional experience are also considered, along with CDU English requirements. The course can be studied online or on campus. Indicative international tuition is around A$36,400 per year. CDU reports being the second-ranked Australian university for postgraduate employment. Graduates work as data scientists, data analysts, data engineers and business analysts.

name: Master of Dietetics
description: The Master of Dietetics at Charles Darwin University provides the knowledge and skills to embark on a career in nutrition and dietetics, combining theory and practical placements across food systems, community and public health nutrition, research and clinical services. Students are equipped to address inequities in food, nutrition and health and to practise in a culturally safe way. The course includes 100 days of professional placements, including short intensives at the Casuarina campus and a full-time placement in the final semester, with CDU arranging all placements across regional, rural and remote locations in the Northern Territory and beyond.

name: Master of Education
description: The Master of Education at Charles Darwin University provides advanced theory and practical skills to develop a career in education and contribute to improved outcomes for diverse learners. Students build on previous experience with specialist education knowledge and skills for scholarship, research and leadership roles, enhancing analytical thinking, collaborative learning, project management and transformative practice, and applying their learning in a capstone professional placement or research activity. Study is available online or on campus, with specialisations including Digital Learning Futures, Inclusive Education, Indigenous Knowledges Education, International Education, Managing and Leading Education, and TESOL.

name: Master of Emergency and Disaster Management
description: The Master of Emergency and Disaster Management at Charles Darwin University qualifies students to work as an emergency and disaster management professional in a variety of contexts. The program draws on the expertise of researchers and practitioners working from Australia's gateway to Indonesia and Southeast Asia, one of the regions most prone to and affected by disasters. It focuses on informed practice and research, examining issues through a multi-sectoral lens, and graduates gain the knowledge and skills to lead and manage all phases of the disaster management cycle.

name: Master of Engineering
description: Charles Darwin University Master of Engineering is a two-year degree with three specialist streams: civil and structural, electrical and electronics, and mechanical engineering, with applicants able to study only the stream matching their undergraduate engineering discipline. The final year includes a major research thesis and a system design project, and the course emphasises sustainability, creativity, teamwork, design, research and leadership. It includes 450 hours of professional practice to keep students current with engineering practice. Entry requires a recognised Bachelor of Engineering, Engineering Science, Engineering Technology or Technology, or equivalent, in the relevant discipline, plus CDU English requirements. Study is available fully online or on campus, full or part time. Indicative international tuition is around A$41,200 per year. CDU reports being the second-ranked Australian university for postgraduate employment. Graduates work in design, construction, infrastructure, energy, manufacturing and project management.

name: Master of Environmental Management
description: The Master of Environmental Management at Charles Darwin University provides postgraduate education for current and future professionals on the context, principles and practices of environmental management, particularly in the wet-dry and semi-arid tropical ecosystems and arid landscapes of northern Australia, with skills that are highly transferable to other ecosystems. Core units focus on the social context within which environmental management takes place, and the flexibility of specialist electives means the course can be undertaken fully online, on campus, or a combination of both. Small class sizes support close engagement with staff.

name: Master of Health Research
description: The Master of Health Research at Charles Darwin University equips students with advanced knowledge and skills in health research design and practice, including the ability to plan and implement a substantial research project. Students learn from Menzies School of Health Research professionals and supervisors in Indigenous health, public health and global health, acquiring theoretical and practical capabilities in epidemiology, biostatistics, and quantitative and qualitative research methods. Following completion, graduates may proceed with approval to higher degree research training. Career opportunities include health research and professional public health practice.

name: Master of Information Technology (Software Engineering)
description:
CDU's Master of Information Technology (Software Engineering) is built for people who already have an unrelated bachelor's degree and want a fast, structured route into software careers, rather than people who studied CS undergrad. Because Darwin isn't a tech hub the size of Sydney or Melbourne, the course leans hard on remote delivery and flexible timetabling, and a large share of the cohort is international students studying 100% online from overseas while working toward Australian permanent residency pathways in the ICT occupation list.

The degree is accredited by the Australian Computer Society at the Professional level and recognised under the Seoul Accord, which matters if graduates want their qualification to carry weight in Singapore, South Korea, or other accord countries later on. Coursework moves from foundational units in discrete structures and algorithms through to process-heavy software engineering units, the kind of project management, risk, and requirements-gathering content that shows up in day-to-day work at mid-sized dev shops more than in FAANG-style interviews.

Two research units close out the degree, which is a distinguishing feature next to some other Australian software engineering masters that are pure coursework. It gives graduates something to point to if they're considering a PhD later, though most treat it as an extended capstone project instead.
curriculum:
Core units: HIT137 Software Now, PRT580 Discrete Structures, HIT220 Algorithms and Complexity, HIT234 Database Concepts, PRT581 Principles of Software Systems, PRT582 Software Engineering: Process and Tools, PRT583 Process Development Methodologies, PRT574 Security Assessment in Software Development, HIT363 Enterprise IT Management, PRT551 Risk and Reliability Management, PRT585 Software Engineering Practice
Research component: two research units (40 credit points total), typically a supervised applied project or minor thesis
Total load: 160 credit points, full-time over 2 years (accelerated trimester options can shorten this)
Delivery: on campus at Casuarina or fully online, trimester intake
admission_requirements: Completion of a recognised bachelor's degree or equivalent international qualification. No specific field or GPA/WAM prerequisite is published; CDU's International Masters Qualifying Program offers an alternative pathway for applicants who don't directly meet entry criteria.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, minimum 6.0 in each band. Equivalent: TOEFL iBT 79 (writing ≥21); PTE Academic 58 (minimum 50 per skill); Cambridge C1 Advanced 176 (minimum 169 per skill).

name: Master of Medical Laboratory Science
description: The Master of Medical Laboratory Science at Charles Darwin University equips students with advanced knowledge, practical skills and real-world experience in diagnostic pathology, covering key laboratory disciplines including haematology, microbiology, clinical chemistry, anatomical pathology and genomics. The program prepares graduates for careers in diagnostic pathology, research, forensic science, public health, academia, and the biomedical and pharmaceutical industries, with roles including medical scientist, laboratory technologist and research assistant. It suits science graduates seeking a professionally focused qualification and hands-on laboratory training.

name: Master of Nursing Practice (Pre-registration)
description: The Master of Nursing Practice (Pre-Registration) at Charles Darwin University is a professionally accredited degree that allows graduates to apply for registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia as a Registered Nurse (Division 1). Students can study online or on campus, part-time or full-time, developing critical thinking and clinical reasoning skills with a focus on evidence-based nursing care and respect for the diverse contexts, cultures and communities where people experience health, wellbeing, illness and disability. To qualify, students undertake simulation blocks and supervised professional experience placements.

name: Master of Occupational Therapy
description: The Master of Occupational Therapy at Charles Darwin University is an accredited degree regulated by the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency that equips students with the skills and knowledge to improve the lives of the people and communities they work with. Students develop the skills to help people achieve optimal health and wellbeing, and gain real-world practical experience by completing 1,000 hours of practice education with the support of CDU academics and registered occupational therapists, including unique placement opportunities in the Northern Territory's regional, rural and remote areas.

name: Master of Physiotherapy
description: The Master of Physiotherapy at Charles Darwin University is a two-year full-time or part-time equivalent course that qualifies graduates as a physiotherapist, following previous studies in anatomy and physiology. Students gain the skills and knowledge to improve the lives of clients, families and communities when movement and function are threatened by ageing, injury, disease or disorders, studying physical, psychological, emotional and social wellbeing along with health promotion, leadership and case management. The course offers community engagement, First Nations perspectives, and rural and remote health experience.

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description: The Master of Professional Accounting at Charles Darwin University focuses on the knowledge and skills required for practice as a certified practising accountant or chartered accountant, along with effective management, accountability, control and decision-making for financial success. Students develop the technical and conceptual skills to become a competent accountant and the ability to analyse, critique and synthesise accounting principles, methods and techniques. With relevant work experience, graduates can pursue careers as financial or management accountants, financial or tax auditors, business and financial analysts, or roles in large multinational and Big Four accounting firms.

name: Master of Project Management
description: Charles Darwin University Master of Project Management is a 160 credit point degree focused on the knowledge and skills to manage complex modern projects, combining project management theory with its application through projects and practical exercises. It consists of core units, elective units and a second-year placement unit that prepares students for professional practice. Applicants must meet CDU standard English language requirements for higher education, which can also be met by completing CDU English for Academic Purposes or its Accelerated International Masters Qualifying Program. Indicative international tuition is around A$38,200 per year. Graduates work as project managers, project officers and coordinators across engineering, business, information technology, construction, health, government and mining.

name: Master of Psychology (Clinical)
description: The Master of Psychology (Clinical) at Charles Darwin University provides advanced knowledge and practical skills for a career as a registered psychologist in Australia, with a clear pathway to the registrar program for clinical psychology endorsement. The program integrates research, contemporary teaching and hands-on clinical training, with a strong emphasis on the diverse communities of the Northern Territory. Students who have completed a Master of Professional Psychology may be eligible for recognition of prior learning, enabling completion in one additional year, and gain expertise in face-to-face and telehealth clinical practice.

name: Master of Public Health
description: Charles Darwin University Master of Public Health is coordinated and taught by educators from the Menzies School of Health Research. It builds advanced knowledge and skills in epidemiology, biostatistics, and quantitative and qualitative research methods, and the ability to formulate strategies for complex health and social issues. A one-year Graduate Diploma of Public Health articulates into the master for students who want a staged entry. International applicants must meet CDU standard English language requirements for higher education. Indicative international tuition is around A$34,700 per year. Graduates work in national and international health services and government, and in health, development and humanitarian organisations, as public health leaders, program planners, analysts, evaluators and policy officers, in areas such as communicable and chronic disease control, epidemiology, health policy and planning, and aid work.

name: Master of Public Policy
description: The Master of Public Policy at Charles Darwin University provides in-depth knowledge of political, cultural and social theory approaches to public policy and a solid understanding of evidence-based policy development and evaluation embedded within practical research theories and methodologies. The course uniquely focuses on northern Australia and its relationship to South-East Asia, exploring policy issues in remote contexts and the significance of First Nations peoples and cultures. Streams include education, environment and livelihoods, health and social policy, Indigenous contexts, public management and governance, and secure and safe communities, and it culminates in a research project.

name: Master of Social Work (Qualifying)
description: The Master of Social Work (Qualifying) at Charles Darwin University provides the skills and knowledge to work in a diverse range of practice contexts including urban, regional, remote and international settings. As an AASW-accredited course, graduates are eligible for membership of the Australian Association of Social Workers. Students explore themes and concepts such as social justice, human rights, critical reflection and supervision, culturally responsive practice, research and advocacy, and complete two field placements to consolidate classroom learning with real-world practice.

name: Master of Speech and Language Therapy
Master of Speech Pathology
description: The Master of Speech Pathology at Charles Darwin University is a two-year graduate-entry program that provides the skills to deliver quality speech pathology services and respond to the changing demands of the Australian health system, with a focus on communication rights, work and advocacy to optimise communication and swallowing across the lifespan. The course offers in-person or online delivery supported by mandatory on-campus residential schools, and practice education placements in a variety of work settings, including unique opportunities in the Northern Territory's local, rural and remote areas.

name: Master of Teaching Early Childhood
description: The Master of Teaching Early Childhood at Charles Darwin University enables students who already hold a bachelor degree in a relevant field other than education to become a teacher in two years. Study is available online or on campus, part-time or full-time, with flexibility to switch modes. On graduating, students are eligible to register as a teacher in early learning settings and primary schools in all states and territories. Graduates are prepared to plan and deliver engaging experiences for diverse learners and contexts, with an awareness of environmental and cultural influences on teaching and learning.

name: Master of Teaching Primary
description: The Master of Teaching Primary at Charles Darwin University enables students who already hold a bachelor degree in a relevant field other than education to become a teacher in two years. Study is available online or on campus, part-time or full-time, with flexibility to switch modes. On graduating, students are eligible to register as a teacher in primary schools in all states and territories. Graduates are prepared to plan and deliver engaging experiences for different learning styles, with an awareness of environmental and cultural influences on teaching and learning.

name: Master of Teaching Secondary
description: The Master of Teaching Secondary at Charles Darwin University enables students who already hold a bachelor degree in a relevant field other than education to become a teacher in two years. Study is available online or on campus, part-time or full-time, with flexibility to switch modes. On graduating, students are eligible to register as a teacher in middle, secondary and senior colleges in all states and territories. Graduates are prepared to plan and deliver engaging experiences for different learning styles, with an awareness of environmental and cultural influences on teaching and learning and the needs of learners with diverse linguistic backgrounds.

name: Bachelor of Agricultural Business Management
description:
This degree pairs a genuine agricultural science base with a business major, taught out of CSU's Orange campus where students have direct access to the university's own farms and the EH Graham Centre for Agricultural Innovation, a joint venture with the NSW Department of Primary Industries that gives the course a research-farm feel rather than a lecture-hall-only one.

The first year is common ground in agronomy, animal production and farm business fundamentals before students move into accounting, marketing and agribusiness management units layered over continuing agricultural science. It's aimed at people who expect to run or manage a farm enterprise, work in agribusiness supply chains, or advise producers. It isn't aimed at general business graduates who happen to like the countryside. A supervised industry placement in the final year is a standard feature, usually with an agribusiness, bank rural lending team, or farm management company.
curriculum:
Year 1: Principles of Agriculture; Farm Business Management; Accounting Fundamentals; Introduction to Soil and Plant Science
Year 2: Agricultural Marketing; Livestock Production Systems; Agribusiness Finance; Elective
Year 3: Farm Management Economics; Supply Chain and Agribusiness Strategy; Rural Property Management; Elective
Year 4: Industry placement/work-integrated learning subject; Agribusiness Capstone Project; Advanced electives in cropping or livestock systems
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Agricultural Science
description:
Based at CSU's Orange campus, the Bachelor of Agricultural Science is a straight science degree rather than the business-agriculture hybrid CSU also offers. Students spend real time on the university's working farm and through the EH Graham Centre for Agricultural Innovation, a partnership with the NSW Department of Primary Industries that runs actual field trials students can be involved in. That gives the course a research-adjacent feel that's harder to replicate at a metropolitan university without its own farmland.

Core science subjects (soil science, plant physiology, animal production, genetics) build toward specialisations in cropping systems, livestock production or natural resource management, and the degree is designed as a genuine pathway into agronomy, farm advisory, or postgraduate research roles rather than just farm management. Students wanting the management/business side would typically look at the Agricultural Business Management degree instead. A supervised research project or industry placement in the final year is standard.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Plant and Soil Science; Animal Production Systems; Chemistry for Agriculture; Farm Systems
Year 2: Plant Physiology; Animal Nutrition and Genetics; Soil Fertility Management; Elective
Year 3: Cropping Systems; Livestock Production; Natural Resource Management; Elective
Year 4: Research Project or Industry Placement; Advanced Agricultural Science electives; Capstone Seminar
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Business Studies
description:
The Bachelor of Business Studies is CSU's broad, flexible business degree: a general foundation in accounting, marketing, management and economics with room to build a major, delivered heavily online to suit the working students and regional cohorts CSU has traditionally served. It's a less specialised alternative to CSU's dedicated agribusiness or wine business degrees, aimed at students who want conventional business career options (accounting, marketing, HR, management) rather than an industry-specific angle.

Students choose a major from areas such as Accounting, Marketing, Human Resource Management or Management partway through the degree, and the course is commonly taken part-time by people already working, using CSU's long-standing distance and online study infrastructure. A work-integrated learning or capstone subject in the final year ties the major together with a practical project, often completed in the student's existing workplace for part-time students.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting Principles; Marketing Fundamentals; Introduction to Management; Business Economics
Year 2: Business Law; Organisational Behaviour; Quantitative Methods for Business; major subject 1
Year 3: Major subjects 2–4 (Accounting / Marketing / HR Management / Management); Elective
Year 4 (or part-time equivalent): Major subjects 5–6; Business Capstone Project or Work-Integrated Learning subject
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description: Charles Sturt University Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) uses a distinctive 2+2 model: two years of on-campus, project-based study followed by two years of paid industry cadetship. Students choose a civil, mechanical or electrical specialisation in second year. Entry typically needs an ATAR of around 70, and international students need IELTS 6.0 overall with 6.0 in each band; students are encouraged to complete a maths bridging subject first. Indicative international tuition is around A$38,000 per year. The civil specialisation leads to roles such as construction engineer, council engineer, geotechnical engineer, structural engineer, project engineer, and water resources engineer, with civil engineering and construction management named among Australia most in-demand professions.

name: Bachelor of Environmental Science and Management
Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
CSU's standard Bachelor of Information Technology runs to 192 points across fourteen core subjects plus an eight-subject specialisation, and the specialisation choice (Cyber Security, Network Engineering, Software and Application Development, or Web Development) is really what defines the degree for each student, since the core is shared. Most students take it through CSU's online delivery model, which the university has run at scale for decades rather than as a pandemic-era add-on.

The Software specialisation starts from basic programming principles and builds to professional application and mobile development; Web Development covers page design, usability and e-commerce build-out; the others go deeper into infrastructure and security. A joint study option lets a student borrow five subjects from an unrelated discipline (business, criminology, and similar are common pairings) and have that show up alongside their specialisation title, which is a genuinely distinctive feature compared with a standard single-strand IT degree elsewhere.
curriculum:
Year 1: Fundamentals of Programming; Computer Systems and Networks; Database Fundamentals; IT Problem Solving; two more core subjects
Year 2: Systems Analysis and Design; Web Technologies; core subjects continue; begin specialisation strand (Cyber Security / Network Engineering / Software and Application Development / Web Development)
Year 3: Specialisation subjects continue (4 of 8); restricted elective; unrestricted electives or joint study sequence begins
Year 4: Remaining specialisation subjects; IT capstone/industry project; remaining unrestricted electives or joint study subjects
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
CSU's Bachelor of Laws is unusual for a regional university in that it's delivered as much through city-based study centres in Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane as from the Bathurst campus itself, which makes it a common choice for people who want a law degree without relocating. The course leans hard into practice readiness: CSU runs its own on-campus legal clinic where students under supervision advise real clients, and the later years fold in professional legal training subjects that in many other degrees are left entirely to the post-degree Practical Legal Training stage.

Core law subjects (contracts, torts, criminal law, property, equity, constitutional and administrative law) cover the Priestley 11 required for admission in every Australian state, and electives let students lean into areas like family law, elder law or Indigenous legal issues, reflecting the regional and rural client base many CSU law graduates end up serving. It suits students aiming at general or regional legal practice more than a big-city corporate law track, though the degree is fully accredited for admission anywhere in Australia.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Law and Legal Reasoning; Contracts A and B; Torts A and B; Legal Research and Writing
Year 2: Criminal Law; Property Law A and B; Administrative Law; Constitutional Law; Elective
Year 3: Equity; Evidence; Company Law; Elective; Legal Clinic (supervised client work)
Year 4: Civil and Criminal Procedure; Professional Conduct and Practice; Dispute Resolution; Capstone elective sequence (e.g. Family Law, Elder Law)
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Nursing at CSU is spread across several regional campuses, including Bathurst, Orange, Wagga Wagga, Albury-Wodonga and Port Macquarie, reflecting the university's original mandate to train health workers for country NSW and Victoria, and clinical placements tend to happen in regional hospitals and community health settings rather than only in large metropolitan teaching hospitals. That regional placement mix is a genuine point of difference: graduates come out with direct experience in settings with less specialist backup, which rural health services value.

The course meets national registration standards (accredited by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia through ANMAC) and combines science-heavy first-year subjects (anatomy, physiology, pharmacology) with progressively more clinical subjects and supervised placement blocks each year, totalling well over 800 hours of clinical placement by graduation, in line with national requirements. Students graduate eligible to register as a Registered Nurse.
curriculum:
Year 1: Anatomy and Physiology; Foundations of Nursing Practice; Health Assessment; Introduction to Pharmacology; clinical placement block
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing; Mental Health Nursing; Pharmacology and Therapeutics; Aged Care Nursing; clinical placement blocks
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing; Paediatric and Maternal Health Nursing; Community and Primary Health Care; Transition to Professional Practice; extended clinical placement
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 6.5) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Oral Health (Therapy and Hygiene)
Bachelor of Pharmacy
description:
CSU's pharmacy school sits at the Orange campus and was built with a deliberate rural focus: placements are weighted toward regional and rural community pharmacies rather than assuming a metropolitan hospital-pharmacy career path, which matters given how much of Australia's pharmacist shortage sits outside capital cities. It's accredited by the Pharmacy Board of Australia and follows the national competency standards required for provisional registration on graduation.

The first two years are pharmaceutical science heavy (pharmacology, pharmaceutics, medicinal chemistry) before the degree moves into clinical pharmacy practice, therapeutics and extended placement blocks in community and hospital settings. Students complete supervised practical placements each year rather than one block at the end, which means graduates arrive at their provisional registration year having already worked in real pharmacy settings repeatedly, not just once.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Pharmaceutical Science; Human Physiology; Pharmaceutical Chemistry; Professional Practice 1 (placement)
Year 2: Pharmacology; Pharmaceutics; Dose Form Design; Professional Practice 2 (placement)
Year 3: Therapeutics 1; Clinical Pharmacy Practice; Pharmacy Law and Ethics; Professional Practice 3 (placement)
Year 4: Therapeutics 2; Advanced Clinical Practice; Research Project; Extended Professional Placement
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 80 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 6.5) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Veterinary Biology/Bachelor of Veterinary Science
description:
When CSU opened this course in 2005 it was the first new veterinary school established in Australia in several decades, built specifically around training vets for rural and mixed-animal practice rather than the small-animal urban model that dominates elsewhere. The six-year double degree (Veterinary Biology feeding into Veterinary Science) is taught entirely at the Wagga Wagga campus, and students work with the university's own farm animals as well as companion animals from first year onward rather than being confined to lecture theatres until clinical years.

The course covers diagnosis and management of disease across cattle, sheep, pigs, poultry and fish alongside horses, dogs and cats, a genuinely broad species range that mirrors what a rural mixed-practice vet actually deals with. It's accredited for registration not just in Australia but in New Zealand, the UK, Hong Kong, Singapore and South Africa. Entry is highly competitive and typically requires a strong ATAR plus additional selection criteria (interview, personal statement, sometimes a CASPer-style test), and most students who get in are drawn specifically by the rural/production-animal focus rather than choosing CSU as a fallback from city vet schools.
curriculum:
Years 1–2 (Veterinary Biology component): Animal Anatomy and Physiology; Animal Genetics; Chemistry for Veterinary Science; Animal Nutrition; Animal Behaviour
Years 3–4: Veterinary Pathology; Pharmacology; Ruminant and Equine Medicine; Veterinary Reproduction; clinical skills training
Years 5–6 (Veterinary Science component): Clinical rotations across farm animal, equine and small animal medicine and surgery; Veterinary Public Health; supervised placements at teaching and partner clinics; final clinical practicum
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 90 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Wine Business
description:
Wagga Wagga sits inside one of Australia's wine regions, and CSU built the Bachelor of Wine Business around that geography: the course is run out of the National Wine and Grape Industry Centre, a joint centre with the NSW DPI and the Australian Wine Research Institute, so students are studying wine commerce next to people doing actual viticulture and oenology research, not in a business school treating wine as a case study.

The course covers the full grape-to-glass chain: viticulture and winemaking basics so graduates understand the product technically, then sales, marketing, export and wine tourism units aimed at running or working in a cellar door, distributor, or export operation. It's completed over 192 points, available full-time on campus or via CSU's online/blended options over a longer part-time timeframe, which suits people already working in the industry. Career outcomes lean toward wine marketing, brand management, export sales and cellar door/hospitality management rather than winemaking itself. The sister Bachelor of Wine Science covers the production side for students who want that instead.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Viticulture and Oenology; Marketing Principles; Accounting Fundamentals; Wine Business Environment
Year 2: Wine Marketing; Export and International Wine Trade; Wine Tourism; Elective
Year 3: Cellar Door and Direct-to-Consumer Sales; Wine Business Strategy; Supply Chain Management; Elective
Year 4 (or part-time equivalent): Industry placement; Wine Business Capstone Project; advanced electives
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Graduate Certificate in Agricultural Business Management [Exit Only]
Graduate Certificate in Fish Conservation and Management
Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting (Professional Practice) [Exit Only]
Graduate Certificate in Professional Information Technology [Exit Point Only]
