Graduate Diploma in Professional Accounting (Professional Practice)
Graduate Diploma of Business Data Analytics
Graduate Diploma of Professional Information Technology
Graduate Diploma of Project Management and Leadership
Master of Education (with specialisations)
description:
CSU is one of the largest producers of teaching graduates in Australia, and its Master of Education is built for people already in the classroom rather than as an entry qualification. Most students are practising teachers upgrading their credentials or repositioning into leadership, special education, TESOL or curriculum roles while still working. It's delivered predominantly online with intensive residential schools for some specialisations, a model CSU has run for teacher education longer than most competitors.

Students pick a specialisation stream (options typically include Educational Leadership, TESOL, Inclusive and Special Education, and Literacy) after a shared core of research and pedagogy subjects, and the course culminates in either a research project or an extended professional inquiry tied to the student's own school context, which makes the degree noticeably more workplace-embedded than a purely theoretical education master's.
curriculum:
Core (all students): Educational Research Methods; Contemporary Issues in Education; Leading Learning and Change
Specialisation stream (choose one): Educational Leadership; TESOL; Inclusive and Special Education; Literacy and Numeracy — four subjects per stream
Final subjects: Professional Inquiry Project or Research Dissertation; Elective from a second specialisation area
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in education or a related discipline, or teaching qualification
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 6.5) or equivalent

name: Master of Health Professional Practice (with specialisations)
Master of Professional Information Technology
description:
Charles Sturt built its IT postgraduate offering around distance and online delivery long before it was standard practice, and the Master of Professional Information Technology still carries that DNA: most students study while working, often changing careers into IT from a completely unrelated first degree. The course doesn't assume a computing background: early subjects cover programming fundamentals, systems analysis and database design before moving into higher-level electives, so a former teacher or accountant can genuinely finish job-ready rather than half-converted.

What sets it apart from a generic IT master's is the flexibility to specialise late rather than early. Students pick up strands in areas like cyber security, data analytics or enterprise systems once they've got the grounding, and CSU's long history running IT via its regional study centres means the online cohort experience is mature rather than an afterthought. Discussion forums, recorded lectures and academic support are built for people juggling full-time work, not bolted onto an on-campus model.

Graduates tend to land in business analyst, systems administrator or junior developer roles, with a meaningful share moving into government IT given CSU's strong ties to NSW public sector employers through its Wagga Wagga and Bathurst campuses.
curriculum:
Year 1, Session 1: Fundamentals of Programming; Database Design; IT Project Management; Systems Analysis and Design
Year 1, Session 2: Network Design and Administration; Enterprise Architecture; IT Governance and Risk; Elective
Year 2, Session 1: Specialisation subject 1 (choose one strand: Cyber Security, Data Analytics, Enterprise Systems); Specialisation subject 2; Research Methods in IT; Elective
Year 2, Session 2: Specialisation subject 3; Specialisation subject 4; IT Capstone Project; Elective
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant or any discipline (typical Australian postgrad IT/CS entry bar used as approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Master of Project Management and Leadership (Professional Practice)
Bachelor of Arts
description:
CQU's Bachelor of Arts covers Creative Writing, Literary Studies, Journalism and a Psychology major with a broader, less statistics-heavy approach than the dedicated Bachelor of Psychological Science, a genuine option for students who want psychological literacy without the accreditation-driven statistics load. Each major runs 8 units, generally weighted toward advanced-level content in the second half (Creative Writing runs its own six-unit structure with two double-weighted units, a slightly different shape from the rest).

Work-integrated learning is built in as a placement loosely tied to a student's major discipline rather than a rigid single-track internship, giving CQU's largely regional and online cohort some flexibility about where that placement actually happens, a meaningful accommodation for students who aren't based near a major media or publishing hub but still want the Journalism or Creative Writing major.
curriculum:
Major (8 units, typically 2 Level 1 + 6 advanced) chosen from Creative Writing, Literary Studies, Journalism, or Psychology (broad, non-accredited stream)
Second major or minor from the same or a related humanities discipline
Work-integrated learning placement, matched to the student's major discipline
Research and academic writing foundation units in Year 1
Elective units to complete the degree
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR/selection rank as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
CQUniversity's Bachelor of Business is unusually broad on majors for a regional university: Accounting, Digital Business, Financial Planning, Hospitality Management, HR Management, Management, Marketing and Property are all on the list, though not every major runs at every campus, so the actual mix a student gets depends heavily on whether they're at Rockhampton, Bundaberg, Cairns, Mackay, Townsville, Brisbane or Sydney, or studying online.

Property and Financial Planning majors stand out as less commonly offered at other Australian business schools; the Financial Planning major in particular is designed against the education standards required for financial adviser registration, giving graduates a direct professional pathway that a generic business degree wouldn't provide. Most students take a double major (two 8-unit blocks) rather than a single major with electives, reflecting CQU's emphasis on giving regional and online students broad employability across multiple functions rather than narrow specialisation.
curriculum:
Business core units: Accounting Principles, Economics, Marketing Fundamentals, Business Law, Management Principles, Business Statistics
Major 1 (8 units) chosen from Accounting, Digital Business, Financial Planning, Hospitality Management, HR Management, Management, Marketing, Property
Major 2 (8 units) or two 4-unit minors from the same list
Work-integrated learning or internship unit (major-dependent)
Capstone: Strategic Management or Business Consultancy Project
Electives to complete the total credit point load
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR/selection rank as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
CQU's engineering degree leans hard into dual-major combinations that most Australian engineering schools don't offer as standard: Electrical with Data Analytics, Electrical with Information Processing, and Civil with Humanitarian Engineering sit alongside the conventional Civil, Electrical and Mechanical majors, plus standalone Mechatronic and Resource Systems Engineering majors that run to 23 units rather than the standard load.

First year is structured around problem-solving, teamwork and professional practice before the major-specific technical content ramps up, and sustainability runs as an explicit overarching theme rather than a single elective, a reflection of CQU's regional footprint across mining, agriculture and resources-heavy parts of Queensland, where its engineering graduates most often end up working. The Humanitarian Engineering strand within Civil is a genuine point of difference, aimed at students interested in disaster response and development-sector infrastructure work rather than conventional civil contracting.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Foundations, Engineering Mathematics, Engineering Mechanics, Professional Practice and Teamwork
Major (choose one): Civil, Civil with Humanitarian Engineering, Electrical, Electrical with Data Analytics, Electrical with Information Processing, Mechanical, or 23-unit Mechatronic/Resource Systems Engineering
Sustainable development principles integrated across major units
Industry-based capstone design project in final year
Work-integrated learning/industry placement component
Accredited pathway to Engineers Australia professional recognition
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion with strong mathematics; ATAR/selection rank as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) and Diploma of Professional Practice (Co-Op Engineering)
Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Sciences
Bachelor of Health and Rehabilitation Science
Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
The Bachelor of IT at CQUniversity runs core IT units through the first term before splitting students into Application Development, Business Analysis, or Cyber Security majors from term two onward. Cyber security in particular has become the major CQU pushes hardest in its marketing given the national skills shortage, and it's ACS-accredited at the professional level like the rest of the degree.

What sets the final-year structure apart is the explicit choice between an internship stream and a project stream for the capstone. Students on the internship track spend roughly 32 hours a week for ten consecutive weeks embedded with a host organisation, which is a substantial placement compared to a single-unit industry project elsewhere. For students who can't commit to that block (a real constraint for CQU's large regional and mature-age cohort juggling existing jobs), the project stream delivers an equivalent capstone experience without leaving paid work.
curriculum:
Term 1 core: Introduction to Programming, Computer Systems and Networks, Database Fundamentals, ICT Professional Practice
Major (from Term 2): Application Development, Business Analysis, or Cyber Security
Minor or elective units in a second ICT area, digital media, entrepreneurship, or marketing
Capstone (final term, choice of stream): Internship (32 hrs/week for 10 weeks with a host organisation) or Project
ACS-accredited at professional level on completion
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR/selection rank as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
CQU's Bachelor of Nursing is designed around the reality that most of its students are studying regionally or fully online, with campus-based support available in Brisbane, Bundaberg, Cairns, Mackay, Rockhampton and Townsville. Before any of the 800 required placement hours happen, students complete simulated clinical training at a nominated Clinical Learning Centre, a practical necessity given how spread out CQU's delivery footprint is across Queensland.

The placement structure is genuinely demanding for regional and online students in a way a metropolitan-campus student might not experience: CQU is upfront that placements are sourced as locally as possible but aren't guaranteed to be, and students may need to relocate temporarily and cover the associated costs themselves. That trade-off, flexibility to study from almost anywhere in regional Queensland against the possibility of having to travel for clinical blocks, is a defining feature of the course rather than an edge case.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing, Anatomy and Physiology, Introduction to Primary Health Care, first of six professional practice placements (following simulated Clinical Learning Centre training)
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Pharmacology, Pathophysiology, Research and Evidence-Based Practice, continued placement blocks
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing, Maternal and Child Health, Aged and Chronic Care, Emergency Nursing, final capstone placement and Transition to Professional Practice
800 hours of professional practice placement across 6 blocks, commencing in first year
Eligible for AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse on completion
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR/selection rank as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
The Bachelor of Psychological Science is CQU's APAC-accredited foundation degree: 16 core psychology units plus a minor (either one 8-unit minor or two 4-unit minors) meet the Level 1 competencies needed to progress into the university's own one-year Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours) and, from there, into provisional registration pathways toward becoming a psychologist.

The capstone is a supervised applied project tackling a genuine real-world problem rather than a purely theoretical thesis, and the course is offered both online and on-campus, a meaningful distinction for CQU given how much of its psychology cohort studies from regional Queensland towns without ready access to a psychology department. Compared to CQU's separate Bachelor of Science (Psychology), this is the more direct route into the accredited registration pipeline.
curriculum:
16 core psychology units covering: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Psychology, Cognitive Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology, Research Methods and Statistics I & II, Personality and Individual Differences, Abnormal Psychology, Psychological Assessment
Minor: one 8-unit minor or two 4-unit minors from outside psychology
Capstone: supervised applied research project on a real-world issue
APAC-accredited, satisfying Level 1 competencies for 3-year undergraduate psychology
Pathway: Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours), 1 year full-time
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR/selection rank as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Diploma of Information and Communications Technology
Graduate Certificate in Emergency and Disaster Management
Graduate Certificate in First Nations Public Health
Graduate Diploma of Human Resource Management
Graduate Diploma of Leading Organisational Change
Master of Arts
description:
This is CQUniversity's coursework Master of Arts, built specifically as the next step for graduates of its own Bachelor of Arts, Digital Media, Music or Theatre degrees: it accelerates from the nominal 18 months down to a single full-time year if the incoming student already holds relevant CQU undergraduate credit, which is a fairly generous articulation compared to most postgraduate arts programs elsewhere.

The degree is explicitly research-oriented rather than a coursework grab-bag: candidates work with an academic advisor to scope a specific topic within the humanities or arts, produce a literature review, and build toward an independent dissertation-style project, which makes it a genuine bridge into PhD study for students who didn't do an honours year at undergraduate level.
curriculum:
Advanced coursework units in the chosen specialisation (drawn from Arts, Digital Media, Music, or Theatre disciplines)
Research Methods and Literature Review unit
Dissertation planning and academic advisor consultation
Independent research project/dissertation in final stage
Audition or interview required at entry for creative-practice specialisations
Accelerated 1-year pathway available for CQU Bachelor of Arts graduates with relevant credit; 18 months standard
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Business Management
description:
Master of Business Management sits as CQU's discipline-based alternative to a full MBA. Core units in applied business research, accounting, finance, HR, marketing and business communication feed into a specific major (Marketing, International Business, HR Management, Leading Organisational Change, or the less common Emergency and Health Services Management), rather than the generalist case-study approach an MBA takes.

The Emergency and Health Services Management major is a genuine point of difference nationally: CQU has strong regional ties to emergency services and health administration in Queensland, and this major reflects that connection directly. Every major offers an optional internship, and a professional practice and career development unit runs through the degree asking students to self-assess their own leadership and management competencies rather than treating that reflection as incidental to the coursework.
curriculum:
Core units: Applied Business Research, Accounting for Managers, Finance, Human Resource Management, Marketing Management, Business Communication, Professional Practice and Career Development
Major (choose one): Marketing, International Business, Human Resource Management, Leading Organisational Change, or Emergency and Health Services Management
Optional internship within the chosen major
Elective units, including options for an overseas study tour
Capstone: applied management project or professional practicum
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Data Analytics
description: CQUniversity Master of Data Analytics is the successor to its Master of Information Systems, with the first intake from Term 1 2027 and an updated structure. It is a 12-unit master, up to two years full-time or four years part-time, of core, specialist and elective units, with core units including ICT Project Preparation and Industry Engagement and a Postgraduate ICT Capstone Project, and electives such as Artificial Intelligence Integrated Internet of Things. The course builds sought-after skills in data analytics and business intelligence for professionals extending their expertise or moving into the data field. Indicative international tuition is around A$39,800 per year. Updated unit details are published progressively ahead of the 2027 launch.

name: Master of Engineering
description: CQUniversity Master of Engineering opens with a unit on Australian engineering practice and three project units that apply discipline knowledge in authentic projects, sometimes with an industry mentor, followed by 24 credit points of electives in areas such as sustainability, mining, project management and rail, and a two-term major research project. Students without prior industry experience complete an internship. To meet Engineers Australia accreditation requirements, students demonstrate 480 hours of engineering practice, with a further 180 hours gained through industry seminars, guest lectures and workshops. On completion graduates are recognised as graduate professional engineers in Australia. Indicative international tuition is around A$41,500 per year. Graduates work across the energy, infrastructure and resources industries.

name: Master of Information Systems
description: CQUniversity Master of Information Systems is being replaced by the Master of Data Analytics from Term 1 2027, with the final intake for the Master of Information Systems in Term 3 2026. It is a 12-unit master, up to two years full-time or four years part-time, of core, specialist and often elective units designed to extend professional understanding or support a move into a new direction in information systems. CQUniversity teaches this course online and on campus, with credit available for relevant prior study or work experience. Prospective students starting in 2027 or later should apply for the Master of Data Analytics, which carries an updated structure focused on data analytics and business intelligence. Indicative international tuition is around A$39,700 per year.

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
CQUniversity's Master of IT opens with a shared first term (project management, introductory programming, ICT services management, and information systems analysis and design) before splitting students into a major-plus-minor structure across networks and information security, mobile application development, or software design and development. That structure is deliberate: CQU expects a chunk of its IT postgrad intake to be career-changers rather than CS graduates, so the common term functions as a leveller before the specialised units start.

Because the degree is delivered across three terms a year rather than two semesters, students who front-load their study can complete faster than the nominal 24 months, and there are built-in exit points at 4 units (Graduate Certificate) and 8 units (Graduate Diploma) if circumstances change. ACS accreditation means graduates can pursue Australian Computer Society membership on the way to a Skills Assessment for skilled migration, which is a genuine driver of enrolment for CQU's substantial international IT cohort.
curriculum:
Term 1 (common core): Project Management, Introduction to Programming, ICT Services Management, Information Systems Analysis and Design
Major (choose one): Networks and Information Security, Mobile Application Development, or Software Design and Development
Minor: second major area selected from the remaining two options
Elective units to complete the 24-month, three-term-a-year structure
Exit points: Graduate Certificate in IT (4 units), Graduate Diploma in IT (8 units)
Capstone project or industry-based unit in final term
ACS-accredited at completion of the full Masters
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant or any discipline (typical Australian postgrad IT/CS entry bar used as approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Master of Management for Engineers
description:
The Master of Management for Engineers is built for practising engineers who want the management credential without doing a generalist MBA. Nine core units cover organisational behaviour, project management, operations, accounting for management and organisational governance, framed throughout with engineering contexts rather than generic case studies, and up to seven elective units let students pull from business analytics, HR, marketing or digital communications depending on where their career is heading.

Sustainable business development and globalisation run as a connecting theme across the core units rather than a single bolt-on subject, which lines up with CQU's broader engineering faculty emphasis on sustainability. An internship stream is available for students who want direct industry exposure rather than filling the elective load purely with coursework, useful for engineers moving from a technical role into their first management position.
curriculum:
Core units (9): People and Organisations, Organisational Governance and Leadership, Operations Management, Innovation and Sustainable Business Development, Project Management Concepts, Accounting for Management, Human Resource Management, Marketing and Digital Communications, Business Analytics
Elective units (up to 7), selectable from across the university's business and management offerings
Optional internship stream in place of some electives
Capstone unit applying management theory to an engineering-sector case or workplace project
24-month nominal duration
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in engineering or related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Project Management
description: CQUniversity Master of Project Management develops advanced knowledge and skills to lead and manage projects in diverse settings, covering both the technical and the human side of project management through coursework and research as used in large commercial and public organisations. Students can add a minor in Hospital and Health Services Management, Information Systems, Information Technology or Management, and in the final year choose a research, practicum or internship stream; the practicum develops a project in a simulated company environment. The degree is fully accredited by the Project Management Institute Global Accreditation Centre, and graduates accrue professional development units. Indicative international tuition is around A$38,600 per year. Graduates work across engineering, business, information technology, construction, health, government, mining and transport.

name: Master of Public Health
description: CQUniversity Master of Public Health is built around the social-ecological model of health that underpins community-based and community-led public health, and is designed around innovative interventions for social change. Across its 12 units students study the origins and evolution of public health, complex adaptive systems thinking, social and environmental determinants of health, epidemiology and statistics, communicable diseases, social justice and partnership development. The indicative first-year fee covers a full-time year of eight units over two terms. Credit and recognition of prior learning can reduce the study load for students with relevant experience or prior study. Indicative international tuition is around A$35,800 per year. Graduates work in public health practice, health policy and planning, epidemiology, disease control, health research and community development.

name: Associate Degree in Agribusiness
description: The Associate Degree in Agribusiness at Curtin University is a two-year qualification, delivered through the Bachelor of Agribusiness, that builds skills to address agricultural concerns such as food security, farming systems, climate challenges and changing markets. It provides a pathway into the bachelor degree. Graduates work in agribusiness support, farm management and agricultural supply chain roles. Indicative international tuition is around 63,000 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Actuarial Science
description: The Bachelor of Actuarial Science at Curtin University is a three-year full-time degree that provides a foundation in actuarial science, applied statistics and quantitative finance, setting graduates on the pathway to a career as an actuary. Graduates work in insurance, superannuation, investment, banking and risk. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 42,300 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Advanced Biomedical Sciences (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Advanced Biomedical Sciences (Honours) at Curtin University is a four-year full-time degree for students who want to contribute to the advancement of health and scientific discovery through an honours degree in biomedical research. Students combine advanced coursework with a supervised research project. Graduates pursue research careers, further study and roles in diagnostics and biotechnology. Indicative international tuition is around 48,300 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Advanced Commerce (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Advanced Commerce (Honours) at Curtin University is a four-year full-time degree that gives a commerce career a head start while also developing research skills. Students study across commerce disciplines with an added research component. Graduates work across business, finance, economics and consulting, or continue to higher research degrees. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 41,400 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Advanced Science (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Advanced Science (Honours) at Curtin University is a four-year full-time degree for students who want to be STEM leaders applying advanced, multidisciplinary knowledge to major science challenges. Students combine advanced coursework across science disciplines with a supervised research project. Graduates pursue research careers, further study and STEM leadership roles. Indicative international tuition is around 49,100 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Agribusiness
description: The Bachelor of Agribusiness at Curtin University is a three-year full-time degree that builds skills to address agricultural concerns such as food security, farming systems, climate challenges and changing markets. Study combines agricultural science with business and economics. Graduates work in agribusiness management, agricultural supply chains, policy and consulting. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 43,100 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Applied Geology
description: The Bachelor of Applied Geology at Curtin University is a three-year full-time degree in which students learn about the Earth's geological processes and how they affect the environment, climate and resources. Study includes fieldwork and applied projects. Graduates work as geologists across the minerals, energy, environmental and geotechnical sectors. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus, with strong links to the Western Australian resources industry. Indicative international tuition is around 49,300 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Applied Science (Architectural Science)
description: The Bachelor of Applied Science (Architectural Science) at Curtin University is a three-year full-time degree covering the design of buildings and spaces, from houses and parks to hospitals and shopping centres, responding to the growing need for infrastructure. Graduates work in architectural science, building design and construction support roles, and can continue to the Master of Architecture. Indicative international tuition is around 43,000 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description: The Bachelor of Arts at Curtin University is a three-year full-time degree designed for imaginative students, developing creativity and critical thinking across a range of humanities and creative arts majors. Students tailor the degree to their interests. Graduates work across media, communications, community services, government, education and the creative industries. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 41,500 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Biomedical Sciences
description: The Bachelor of Biomedical Sciences at Curtin University is a three-year full-time degree that combines biology with medicine for a career in health science and research. Students study human biology, disease and laboratory science. Graduates work in medical research, diagnostics, biotechnology and health, or continue to graduate-entry health programs. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 47,500 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Business Administration
description: The Bachelor of Business Administration at Curtin University is a three-year full-time degree that provides broad career options and wide-ranging skills in marketing, finance, project management, human resources and strategic management. Graduates work in management, operations and business roles across sectors. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 41,500 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description:
Curtin's Bachelor of Commerce runs on a build-it-yourself model: a major is a fixed set of eight units, and students choose the first one in their opening semester with guidance from an advisor rather than being locked in at application. A second major can come from the rest of the Commerce list or, less obviously, from the Arts or Creative Arts major lists, which is how a Curtin commerce student ends up graduating with, say, Marketing paired with Screen Arts rather than a strictly business-only transcript.

The final-year capstone is framed around international business exposure specifically, applying entrepreneurial and critical-thinking skills to something closer to a live workplace problem than a standard assessed group project, which reflects Curtin's broader push to make its business degrees read as job-ready to Perth's resources, logistics, and professional services employers rather than purely theoretical.

Given Curtin's business school accreditation (AACSB) and its physical size, one of the largest commerce cohorts in Western Australia, the major combinations available (Accounting, Banking and Finance, Economics, Human Resource Management, International Business, Management, Marketing, among others) are broader than most WA competitors offer inside a single degree.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introductory business units across accounting, economics, and management, first major selection, foundational quantitative unit
Year 2: Core major units (four of eight), second major or minor units, electives
Year 3: Remaining major units, capstone experience (international business focus, applied workplace-style project), electives
Structure: one major minimum (8 units), optional second major from Commerce, Arts, or Creative Arts lists
admission_requirements: WACE/Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Communications
description: The Bachelor of Communications at Curtin University is a three-year full-time degree that provides training and professional skills for traditional and emerging media and communication careers. Students study across areas such as journalism, public relations, digital media and strategic communication. Graduates work in communications, content, public relations and media roles. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 39,700 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Computing
description: The Bachelor of Computing at Curtin University is a three-year full-time degree with options in computer science, cybersecurity and software engineering. Students build programming, systems and problem-solving skills through project-based learning. Graduates work as software developers, security analysts and systems specialists across industry. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 45,800 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Creative Arts
description:
Curtin's Bachelor of Creative Arts narrows the choice to three majors (Fine Art, Screen Arts, or Theatre Arts) rather than the sprawling major list attached to the Bachelor of Arts, which makes it a more deliberately practice-focused degree from day one. Students build a thorough grounding in both the theory and the practice of their chosen discipline, then layer on a specialisation drawn from a different Creative Arts area or effectively any other field they meet the prerequisites for, so a Theatre Arts major might specialise in Screen Arts, or step entirely outside Creative Arts for something like marketing or writing.

The capstone unit is where the degree's practical bent shows most clearly: Fine Art students mount an exhibition, Theatre Arts students stage a performance, Screen Arts students complete a screen project, all functioning as a public-facing portfolio piece rather than a written exam or essay.

Curtin's location gives Screen Arts students in particular a practical edge. Perth's screen production sector has grown considerably with state government screen incentives drawing international productions to WA, and Curtin has leaned into that with industry-facing production units.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introductory major units (theory and practice foundations), specialisation exploration units, electives
Year 2: Core major units, specialisation units (Fine Art, Screen Arts, or Theatre Arts, or another discipline), electives
Year 3: Advanced major units, capstone project (exhibition, performance, or screen project depending on major), remaining electives
Majors offered: Fine Art, Screen Arts, Theatre Arts
admission_requirements: WACE/Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Design
description: The Bachelor of Design at Curtin University is a three-year full-time degree in which students learn to design through project-based activities using industry-standard equipment, technologies and media platforms. Students choose a design major and build a professional portfolio. Graduates work across communication, digital, spatial and product design. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 38,000 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Digital Creative Industries
description: The Bachelor of Digital Creative Industries at Curtin University is a three-year full-time degree for students who want to channel their creativity into a profession that brings experiences and stories to life. Study spans digital media, games, screen and creative content. Graduates work in digital content, games, screen and creative production roles. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 41,500 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood Education)
description: The Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood Education) at Curtin University is a four-year full-time initial teacher education degree in which students prepare to play an integral role in shaping the social and cognitive development of young children. The program combines coursework with supervised professional experience placements. Graduates are prepared for registration and work as early childhood teachers. Indicative international tuition is around 40,300 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Educational Studies
description: The Bachelor of Educational Studies at Curtin University is a three-year full-time degree that builds workplace skills in education, with comprehensive knowledge of education curricula, leadership and research. It does not lead to teacher registration on its own. Graduates work in education support, training, learning design and policy roles. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 38,900 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
Curtin runs its engineering degree through a common Engineering Foundation Year before anyone commits to a discipline. First-year students cover fundamentals shared across all engineering areas and only choose their major (from Chemical, Petroleum, Electrical and Electronic, Mechanical, Mechatronic, Civil and Construction, Metallurgical, Mining, Industrial and Systems, or Environmental Engineering) heading into second year, which gives students who arrive unsure between, say, mechanical and mechatronic engineering a genuine trial period rather than forcing a decision at enrolment.

The major list itself is a tell for what Curtin is known for regionally: Metallurgical, Mining, and Petroleum Engineering majors sit alongside the more universally-offered options, a direct reflection of Perth's position as headquarters city for most of Australia's mining and resources companies, and Curtin's engineering graduates in those majors tend to move directly into WA's resources sector rather than needing to relocate.

Final year is a genuine honours research project done independently within the chosen major, and students can add a four-unit specialisation or minor on top of their major to sharpen the degree toward a specific career direction, pairing Mechanical Engineering with a renewable energy specialisation, for instance.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Foundation Year — common units across all disciplines (engineering mathematics, mechanics, computer-aided design, introductory programming)
Year 2: Major-specific core units (Chemical, Petroleum, Electrical and Electronic, Mechanical, Mechatronic, Civil and Construction, Metallurgical, Mining, Industrial and Systems, or Environmental Engineering)
Year 3: Advanced major units, specialisation or minor units (four units), professional practice exposure
Year 4: Honours-level independent research project, remaining advanced major units
Structure: pre-major foundation year, one Engineering major, optional four-unit specialisation or minor
admission_requirements: WACE/Year 12 completion with strong mathematics/physics; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Health Sciences
description: The Bachelor of Health Sciences at Curtin University is a three-year full-time degree with two distinct majors. The health promotion major is designed for students interested in improving health and wellbeing at a population level, alongside a second health-focused major. Graduates work in health promotion, community health, policy and program roles. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 46,200 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description: Curtin University Bachelor of Information Technology prepares students for high-demand areas of computing, covering fundamental programming and security skills and the workings of modern computers and computer networks, with a focus on distributed computing and room to specialise around personal interests. The course is accredited by the Australian Computer Society. Curtin works with industry partners to shape course content and to provide final-year placement opportunities so graduates leave career-ready. Entry is available through several pathways: senior secondary results and ATAR with adjustment factors applied automatically, an AQF Certificate IV, Diploma or Advanced Diploma with the subject prerequisite met, or a bridging or enabling course. International students must also meet Curtin English language requirements. Indicative international tuition is around A$45,800 per year.

name: Bachelor of Innovation
description: The Bachelor of Innovation at Curtin University is a three-year full-time degree that future-proofs a business career by building the expertise to solve tough problems and the confidence to put solutions into practice. Students work on applied projects and ventures. Graduates work in innovation, product, business development and entrepreneurial roles. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 44,200 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Laws
description: The Bachelor of Laws at Curtin University is a three-year full-time degree and the first qualification needed to begin a career as a legal practitioner. Students study core areas of law with practical legal skills built in. Graduates progress toward admission to practise and work in legal practice, government, policy and business. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 69,200 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Medical Sciences (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Medical Sciences (Honours) at Curtin University is a one-year full-time intercalated course that allows Curtin Medical School students in the medical degree to gain experience in research. Students complete a supervised research project alongside advanced coursework. Graduates return to the medical program with strengthened research skills and are prepared for clinician-researcher careers. Indicative international tuition is around 99,700 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Mine and Engineering Surveying
description: The Bachelor of Mine and Engineering Surveying at Curtin University is a three-year full-time degree that trains specialist surveyors with expertise in advanced software and equipment, including GPS and drones, to acquire and process land and satellite data. Graduates work as mine and engineering surveyors across the resources and construction sectors. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 45,600 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Multidisciplinary Science
description: The Bachelor of Multidisciplinary Science at Curtin University is a three-year full-time degree that builds expertise across multiple science disciplines increasingly important for addressing environmental and industry issues. Students combine study areas to suit their interests and career goals. Graduates work across scientific, environmental and technical roles that require breadth. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 48,000 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours) at Curtin University is a program of around three years and nine months full-time, described by the university as the only undergraduate pharmacy program in Western Australia. It offers practical experience alongside a theoretical grounding in pharmacy. Graduates progress toward registration and work as pharmacists across community, hospital and clinical settings. Indicative international tuition is around 46,600 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Psychology (Honours)
description:
Curtin's Bachelor of Psychology (Honours) is APAC-accredited and runs as a combined four-year sequence rather than a standard three-year degree with honours bolted on afterward. The honours stream is embedded as an expected continuation for students who hit the mark, not a separate application most students won't get into. That said, entry to the honours stream itself is competitive: a minimum 70% average across the 14 core second- and third-year psychology units is required, and offers go out by invitation rather than automatic progression.

The APAC accreditation is the whole point structurally: it's what makes graduates eligible for associate membership of the Australian Psychological Society and sets up the standard Australian pathway toward provisional registration and eventual practice, which distinguishes this from a psychological-science degree that stops short of the accredited sequence.

Because the honours year functions as a genuine research year within the four-year structure rather than an optional fifth year, students plan their thesis topic and supervisor arrangements earlier than they would in a bolt-on honours model, and Curtin's psychology school covers a fairly broad research spread from clinical and health psychology through to forensic and organisational applications.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introductory Psychology (Level One sequence), foundational science or statistics unit, electives
Year 2: Core psychology units (part of the 14-unit core sequence) — social, developmental, biological psychology
Year 3: Remaining core units — cognition, research methods, psychopathology, personality; honours stream invitation based on 70% average across core units
Year 4 (Honours): independent research thesis, advanced seminars
APAC accredited; graduates eligible for APS associate membership
admission_requirements: WACE/Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Science (Nursing)
description:
Curtin's undergraduate nursing degree runs 840 hours of clinical placement across the course (hospitals, private practices, aged care, rural health settings, and mental health services), which starts as early as second semester of first year, meaning students are shadowing real clinical environments well before most other health degrees would send them out. Placements can involve shift work including night duty and weekends by design, since the point is exposure to how hospitals actually run rather than a sanitised nine-to-five version of nursing.

The course structure leans heavily on simulation before fieldwork: Curtin's simulated practice labs are used to build competency in a controlled setting first, so that clinical placement time is spent applying skills rather than learning them cold in front of a patient. Given Curtin's status as WA's largest nursing school by intake, the simulation infrastructure (mock wards, standardised patients) is a genuine scale advantage over smaller providers.

Students are pushed toward interprofessional learning throughout, working alongside pharmacy, physiotherapy, and medical students in shared units rather than training in a nursing-only bubble, which mirrors how WA Health actually staffs its wards and is meant to make the transition into a graduate nurse year less of a culture shock.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Introduction to Professional Nursing, simulated practice units; clinical placement begins second semester
Year 2: Adult Health Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Pharmacology for Nursing, interprofessional learning units, clinical placements (hospital and community settings)
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing, Rural and Remote Health placement option, Aged Care Nursing, capstone clinical placement block, Transition to Professional Practice
Total: 840 hours clinical placement, 216 hours simulated practice across the course; registration pathway with Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia
admission_requirements: WACE/Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Science (Science)
description:
Curtin's Bachelor of Science (Science) covers an unusually wide net of majors for one degree title: Agricultural Science, Earth Sciences, Environmental Biology and Ecology, Environmental Science, Food Science and Technology, ICT, Marine Science, Mineral Processing, Software Development, and Space and Planetary Science all sit under it, which reflects Curtin's identity as a resources-and-industry-adjacent university rather than a pure research-science school. Mineral Processing and Space and Planetary Science in particular are majors you won't find at most Australian universities, tied respectively to WA's mining sector and Curtin's own astronomy research group (home to some of the country's radio astronomy and remote sensing work).

Students pick at least one science major and can double up, with extension specialisations layered on for those wanting to go deeper into a sub-area without adding a whole second major, plus minors that don't carry first-year prerequisites for students who want breadth without planning it out from day one.

Honours is a genuine one-year add-on rather than an embedded final-year component, which means students finishing the standard three years and wanting a research-track future need to apply separately and typically need a strong average across their major units.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundational science units (two areas typically), mathematics or statistics service unit, introductory major unit(s)
Year 2: Core major units, laboratory or fieldwork components, extension specialisation or minor units
Year 3: Advanced major units, capstone or research-methods unit within major, remaining minor or elective units
Optional Year 4 (Honours): independent research thesis, separate application required, competitive entry
admission_requirements: WACE/Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Social Work
description: The Bachelor of Social Work at Curtin University is a four-year full-time degree that develops the comprehensive skills to help individuals and groups and promote positive relationships, equality, human rights and social change. The program includes substantial supervised field education. Graduates are eligible for professional recognition and work as social workers across community, health and government settings. Indicative international tuition is around 43,300 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Surveying
description: The Bachelor of Surveying at Curtin University, offered as the Bachelor of Surveying (Honours), is a four-year full-time degree in a highly specialised professional discipline that involves measuring the surface of the Earth and its features. Students learn advanced surveying methods, instrumentation and data processing. Graduates progress toward licensing and work as land and engineering surveyors. Indicative international tuition is around 39,400 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Surveying Technology
description: The Bachelor of Surveying Technology at Curtin University, delivered through the Bachelor of Surveying (Honours), is a four-year full-time degree in the specialised discipline of measuring the surface of the Earth and its features. Students focus on surveying technology, instrumentation and spatial data processing. Graduates work as surveying technologists and technicians across the resources, construction and spatial sectors. Indicative international tuition is around 37,500 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Technology (Computer Systems and Networking)
description:
This Bachelor of Technology sits in the more hands-on end of Curtin's ICT offerings: hardware, networking (LANs and WANs specifically), network management, and Internet of Things content, with Python and Linux taught progressively from basics through to advanced application rather than assumed as prior knowledge. It's a more infrastructure-and-systems-focused degree than a standard software-development-flavoured IT degree, aimed at students who want to end up managing networks and infrastructure rather than writing application code full-time.

The course is explicit about industry certification alignment: Cisco and Amazon Web Services certifications are named targets the curriculum is built to prepare graduates for, which matters in a job market where certifications often carry as much weight as the degree title itself for network engineering and cloud infrastructure roles.

The professional practice requirement (minimum 8 weeks, logged formally) pushes students into real workplace exposure before graduation, and Curtin frequently pairs this degree with a Bachelor of Information Technology as a double degree for students who want both the networking depth and the broader IT/software coverage on one transcript.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Programming (Python), Computer Systems Fundamentals, Networking Fundamentals, Linux Systems Administration (introductory)
Year 2: Network Programming and Distributed Computing, Security Fundamentals, LAN/WAN Design and Management, Linux Systems Administration (advanced)
Year 3: Internet of Things Systems, Network Management and Cloud Infrastructure, professional practice placement (minimum 8 weeks, logged), capstone networking project
Certification alignment: prepares students for industry certifications including Cisco and AWS
admission_requirements: WACE/Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Urban and Regional Planning
description: The Bachelor of Urban and Regional Planning at Curtin University is a four-year full-time degree in which students learn to improve the ways cities and regions respond to current and future challenges. Study spans planning theory, statutory planning, urban design and sustainability. Graduates work as urban and regional planners in government and consulting. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 38,500 Australian dollars per year.

name: Doctor of Business Administration
description: The Doctor of Business Administration at Curtin University is a professional doctorate for experienced managers who want to combine advanced business knowledge with research skills, structured around coursework and a substantial applied research thesis. Graduates take on senior leadership, consulting and applied research roles. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus, with flexible options for working professionals. Indicative international tuition is around 30,400 Australian dollars per year.

name: Doctor of Education
description: The Doctor of Education at Curtin University is a professional doctorate, typically four years full-time, for educators seeking doctoral-level study with a view to becoming leaders in classroom teaching, curriculum development and educational leadership. It combines coursework with a supervised research thesis. Graduates take on senior leadership, policy and research roles in education. Indicative international tuition is around 27,900 Australian dollars per year.

name: Doctor of Pharmacy
description: The Doctor of Pharmacy at Curtin University is a program of around fifteen months that provides graduates with advanced knowledge in pharmacy applicable across a range of practice settings, including recent developments across the full scope of practice. Graduates are prepared for advanced and specialist pharmacy practice. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 116,700 Australian dollars per year.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Agriculture and Food Science
description: The Doctor of Philosophy - Agriculture and Food Science at Curtin University is the university's research doctorate, the standard prerequisite for a career in research or academia. Candidates undertake an original, supervised research program culminating in a thesis. Graduates pursue research careers in agriculture, food science, government and industry. Courses at Curtin are primarily based at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 42,100 Australian dollars per year.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Business and Management
description: The Doctor of Philosophy - Business and Management at Curtin University is a research doctorate in which candidates develop a systematic and critical understanding of a complex field of learning and specialised research skills to advance knowledge. Candidates complete an original supervised research thesis. Graduates pursue academic, research and senior advisory careers. Courses at Curtin are primarily based at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 40,400 Australian dollars per year.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Environmental Science
description: The Doctor of Philosophy - Environmental Science at Curtin University is the university's research doctorate, the standard prerequisite for a career in research or academia. Candidates undertake an original, supervised research program culminating in a thesis. Graduates pursue research careers in environmental science across universities, government and industry. Courses at Curtin are primarily based at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 42,100 Australian dollars per year.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Exercise, Sports and Rehabilitation Science
description: The Doctor of Philosophy - Exercise, Sports and Rehabilitation Science at Curtin University is a research-based higher degree that develops research skills and advances knowledge in the field. Candidates undertake a supervised original research project, and non-physiotherapists may be accepted where the research area fits. Graduates pursue research careers in exercise, sport and rehabilitation science. Indicative international tuition is around 45,200 Australian dollars per year.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Medical Radiation Science
description: The Doctor of Philosophy - Medical Radiation Science at Curtin University is a research doctorate in which candidates develop a systematic and critical understanding of the field and specialised research skills to advance knowledge, completing an original supervised research thesis. Graduates pursue research and academic careers in medical radiation science and imaging. Courses at Curtin are primarily based at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 42,100 Australian dollars per year.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Medicine
description: The Doctor of Philosophy - Medicine at Curtin University is a research-based higher degree that develops research skills and advances knowledge in medicine and health. Candidates undertake an original, supervised research project culminating in a thesis. Graduates pursue clinician-researcher and academic careers, and research roles in health services and industry. Courses at Curtin are primarily based at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 34,600 Australian dollars per year.

name: Doctor of Philosophy (Media, Culture and Creative Arts)
description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Media, Culture and Creative Arts) at Curtin University is a research doctorate in which candidates use an in-depth understanding of theories and concepts to develop practical solutions for real-world problems, completing an original supervised research thesis. Graduates pursue academic, research and creative practice careers. Courses at Curtin are primarily based at the Bentley Perth campus. name: Doctor of Philosophy (Spatial Sciences) Research

description: The Master of Clinical Psychology at Curtin University is a full-time degree that provides the final qualification and supervised clinical practice for a professional career in psychology. Students combine advanced coursework, research training and supervised placements across clinical settings. Graduates progress toward registration and endorsement as clinical psychologists. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 47,600 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Commerce
description: The Master of Commerce at Curtin University is a two-year full-time degree that, through credit for recognised learning, enables business professionals to upskill quickly in a choice of seven specialist areas including finance, marketing, human resource management and supply chain management. Students build core commerce knowledge alongside a chosen specialisation. Graduates advance into business, finance and management roles. Indicative international tuition is around 50,600 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Computing
description:
Curtin's Master of Computing is built for career-changers rather than CS undergrads looking to specialise further. The entry requirements assume a bachelor's degree plus some demonstrated programming, operating systems, and computing maths background, and the first stretch of the course deliberately re-teaches fundamentals before splitting into the three available majors: Computer Science, Cyber Security, or Artificial Intelligence.

What distinguishes it from a lot of one-size-fits-all computing conversion masters is the credit arrangement for Curtin's own graduates. Someone who already did a Bachelor of Technology or Bachelor of Computing at Curtin can be granted up to a full semester of credit, effectively turning this into an 18-month top-up for internal students while still running as a full two-year program for outsiders.

The major project in the final stage is where the specialisation actually gets tested. Students in the Cyber Security stream, for instance, end up doing something closer to an applied security research piece than a generic capstone, which matters given Perth's growing resources-sector demand for industrial cyber security skills specifically, an angle Curtin leans into given its mining and energy industry connections.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Programming Fundamentals, Computer Systems Fundamentals, Computing Mathematics, Database Systems
Semester 2: Data Structures and Algorithms, Networks and Security Fundamentals, major-track foundation unit, elective
Semester 3: Major units (Computer Science, Cyber Security, or Artificial Intelligence stream) x3, elective
Semester 4: Advanced major units, Major Project (capstone, specialisation-specific)
Credit: up to one semester's credit available for Curtin Bachelor of Technology or Bachelor of Computing graduates
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree with demonstrated knowledge/skills in programming, operating systems, and computing mathematics (or equivalent); Master Qualifying Program pathway available for those who don't meet direct entry.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall.

name: Master of Cyber Security
description: Curtin University Master of Cyber Security is a one-year, project-based degree that adds cyber security to an existing background in information technology, computational science or engineering. Students learn to design and implement secure information infrastructure and systems, working through industry-inspired projects that build both blue-team and red-team skills alongside governance knowledge. Entry requires a three-year bachelor degree in information technology, computational science or engineering plus at least two years of relevant work experience, or a four-year degree in one of those fields. Indicative international tuition is around A$43,800 per year. Curtin cites a median Australian cyber security salary of about A$110,000 and strong projected job growth, with graduate roles including security administrator, junior penetration tester and security analyst.

name: Master of Design
description: The Master of Design at Curtin University is a two-year full-time degree that advances knowledge of contemporary design practice and develops students as innovative design leaders. Students work through studio-based projects and design research. Graduates work in design leadership, strategy and practice roles across industry. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 41,400 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Dietetics
description: The Master of Dietetics at Curtin University is a two-year full-time degree in which students learn to educate individuals and groups in medical nutrition therapy and public health nutrition programs. The program combines coursework with supervised professional placements. Graduates are prepared for accreditation and work as dietitians across clinical, community and food service settings. Indicative international tuition is around 48,800 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Digital and Social Media
description: The Master of Digital and Social Media at Curtin University is delivered through the Master of Multimedia Journalism, an eighteen-month masters for people seeking specialist journalism and digital media skills to complement a prior degree or graduate qualification. Students build multimedia storytelling, digital content and social media skills. Graduates work in digital content, social media and communications roles. Indicative international tuition is around 39,900 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Education
description: The Master of Education at Curtin University is a one-year full-time degree that furthers knowledge and skills to inspire and lead educational improvement and transformation. Students study contemporary education theory, leadership and practice. Graduates advance in teaching, education leadership, curriculum and policy roles. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus, with online options available. Indicative international tuition is around 40,700 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Engineering Management
description:
Curtin's Master of Engineering Management is a genuinely fast program: 12 months full-time across three trimesters rather than the standard two years, jointly delivered by the Faculty of Science and Engineering and the Faculty of Business and Law, which shows up directly in the unit split: 125 credits of engineering units (choose five from six options) plus 125 credits of business units (four core plus one elective) plus a 50-credit engineering project capstone.

The business content isn't generic MBA filler bolted onto an engineering degree: strategic management, finance, projects and operations management, and human factors units are chosen specifically because they map onto what an engineer moving into a management or project-lead role actually needs, rather than a broad business-generalist curriculum. That combination is aimed at engineers already in the workforce who want to move from individual-contributor technical roles into managing engineering teams or projects, not new graduates.

Evening class availability is a deliberate accommodation for that same audience: working engineers studying part-time over a minimum 24 months rather than pausing a career for full-time study, which is a genuinely different student profile than most of Curtin's other engineering postgraduate offerings attract.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Engineering units (two of five chosen options), Strategic Management
Trimester 2: Engineering units (remaining chosen options), Finance for Engineers, Projects and Operations Management
Trimester 3: Human Factors in Engineering Management, business elective, Engineering Project (capstone, 50 credits)
Full-time: 12 months across three trimesters; part-time minimum 24 months, two units per trimester; evening classes available
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Environment and Climate Emergency
Master of Finance
description: The Master of Finance at Curtin University is offered as a specialisation within the Master of Commerce, a two-year full-time degree that lets business professionals upskill quickly through credit for recognised learning in a choice of seven specialist areas. Students build finance capability alongside core commerce knowledge. Graduates work in financial analysis, investment and corporate finance roles. Indicative international tuition is around 43,000 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Geoscience
description: The Master of Geoscience at Curtin University is a two-year full-time degree that advances knowledge of geology or geophysics, or lets students explore a new branch of geoscience. Study combines advanced coursework with applied and field-based learning. Graduates work as geoscientists across the resources, environmental and energy sectors. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 49,100 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Geospatial Intelligence
description: The Master of Geospatial Intelligence at Curtin University is a two-year full-time degree that increases knowledge of geospatial science and strengthens skills in location-allocation, dataset integration and modelling. Graduates work as geospatial analysts and intelligence specialists across defence, government and industry. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 49,100 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Global Engagement (MC-GLOBL)
description: The Master of Global Engagement at Curtin University is delivered through the Master of Human Rights and Global Engagement, a two-year full-time degree that develops advanced practical expertise and intercultural skills to engage in human rights and social justice issues on a global scale. Graduates work in international organisations, government, advocacy and the not-for-profit sector. Indicative international tuition is around 40,900 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Health Administration
description: The Master of Health Administration at Curtin University is a two-year full-time degree that develops the skills and knowledge to navigate the complexities of leading and managing the delivery of services in a modern healthcare environment. Graduates work in health service management, planning and administration roles. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 46,300 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Human Resources
description: The Master of Human Resources at Curtin University is offered as a specialisation within the Master of Commerce, a two-year full-time degree that lets business professionals upskill quickly through credit for recognised learning in a choice of seven specialist areas. Students build human resource management capability alongside core commerce knowledge. Graduates work in HR advisory, business partnering and people management roles. Indicative international tuition is around 51,100 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Human Rights
description: The Master of Human Rights at Curtin University is an eighteen-month full-time degree in which students put human rights learning into practice and pursue their areas of interest in greater depth. Study spans human rights theory, philosophy and applied practice. Graduates work in advocacy, policy, research and humanitarian roles. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 41,600 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Human Rights and Global Engagement
description: The Master of Human Rights and Global Engagement at Curtin University is a two-year full-time degree that develops advanced practical expertise and intercultural skills to engage in human rights and social justice issues on a global scale. Graduates work in international organisations, government, advocacy and the not-for-profit sector. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 41,500 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Indigenous Australian Cultural Studies
description: The Master of Indigenous Australian Cultural Studies at Curtin University is a one-year full-time postgraduate program informed by environmental issues and Native Title, Indigenous research methodology, and Indigenous knowledges. Students build deep understanding of Indigenous Australian cultures, communities and organisations. Graduates apply this knowledge across education, health, community services, policy and research roles. Indicative international tuition is around 39,900 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Information Systems and Technology
description: The Master of Information Systems and Technology at Curtin University is a two-year full-time degree that meets the demand for digital experts and the potential of new technology to enhance business productivity. Students study systems analysis, data, and the strategic use of technology in organisations. Graduates work as business analysts, systems analysts and information systems consultants. Indicative international tuition is around 31,500 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Innovation and Entrepreneurship
description: The Master of Innovation and Entrepreneurship at Curtin University is a two-year full-time degree that develops the skills to innovate, lead and make an impact through entrepreneurship, intrapreneurship and international marketing. Students work on applied projects and ventures. Graduates start businesses or move into innovation, product and business development roles. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 42,400 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of International Business
description: The Master of International Business at Curtin University is offered as a specialisation within the Master of Commerce, a two-year full-time degree that lets business professionals upskill quickly through credit for recognised learning in a choice of seven specialist areas. Students build international business capability alongside core commerce knowledge. Graduates work in international trade, global operations and business development roles. Indicative international tuition is around 30,800 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of International Business and Entrepreneurship
description: The Master of International Business and Entrepreneurship at Curtin University is offered through the Master of Commerce, a two-year full-time degree that lets business professionals upskill quickly through credit for recognised learning in a choice of seven specialist areas. Students combine international business with entrepreneurship and innovation. Graduates work in international trade, global operations and venture development roles. Indicative international tuition is around 30,800 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of International Relations
description: The Master of International Relations at Curtin University is a two-year full-time degree that equips students to shape global policy and lead meaningful change. Study spans international politics, security, diplomacy and global governance. Graduates work in government, international organisations, diplomacy, policy and research. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 36,600 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of International Relations and National Security
description: The Master of International Relations and National Security at Curtin University, delivered through the Master of International Relations, is a two-year full-time degree that equips students to shape global policy and respond to national and international security challenges. Graduates work in government, security and intelligence agencies, international organisations and policy roles. Indicative international tuition is around 41,800 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of International Security
description: The Master of International Security at Curtin University is an eighteen-month full-time degree that equips students to respond to 21st century security challenges in Australia and globally. Study spans transnational threats, security policy and strategy. Graduates work in security, intelligence, defence, policy and international affairs roles. Courses at Curtin are primarily taught on campus at the Bentley Perth campus. Indicative international tuition is around 55,500 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Management
