Students explore the relationship between diet and disease and develop evidence-based treatments for conditions such as obesity, diabetes, allergies and malnutrition, applying their learning through supervised professional placements. Graduates work as dietitians in hospitals, community health, private practice, food industry and public health roles.

name: Master of Engineering
description:
Deakin's Master of Engineering is aimed at engineering graduates looking to deepen technical specialisation or pivot into a growth area. Offerings have included streams in areas like advanced manufacturing, renewable energy, and civil/structural engineering, reflecting the university's Waurn Ponds research strengths (including the Carbon Nexus carbon-fibre facility and Deakin's broader materials and manufacturing research groups). It's a coursework master's rather than a research degree, though most streams include a substantial engineering project unit.

Entry generally expects a relevant engineering bachelor's degree; students without one may be directed toward a longer pathway with additional foundation units. The degree suits engineers wanting formal postgraduate specialisation for career progression, plus a share of international students using it as a bridge toward Engineers Australia's Chartered status requirements.
curriculum:
Part A – Foundation (if required): bridging units in core engineering mathematics and systems
Part B – Core postgraduate engineering studies: Advanced Engineering Analysis, Engineering Project Management, Research Methods for Engineering
Part C – Specialisation stream (e.g. Advanced Manufacturing, Renewable Energy, Structural Engineering): 3–4 units
Part D – Capstone Engineering Project
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a related engineering discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Film and Television
description: The Master of Film and Television at Deakin University is an experience-rich course taught by industry-active academics in industry-grade facilities at Deakin Studios, a virtual production, TV and film studio on the Melbourne Burwood Campus. Students grow transferable skills for media industries including collaboration, problem solving and personal organisation, work in a writers' room on a digital short series, and learn to write with the camera. Graduates work across screen production, writing, directing, producing and post-production in the film, television and digital content industries.

name: Master of Finance
description: The Master of Finance at Deakin University is a postgraduate degree from a business school ranked in the world's top 200 for accounting and finance. Students develop expertise across financial markets, corporate finance, derivatives, portfolio management and international finance, alongside capabilities in fintech, financial data analytics and sustainable finance. Learning takes place in Deakin's industry-standard Trading Room, where students work with live trading data on decision making and risk management strategies. Graduates work in investment, corporate finance, banking, funds management and risk roles.

name: Master of Fine Arts
description: The Master of Fine Arts at Deakin University is built around studio practice, creative research and a major final project, helping students refine their creative voice and graduate with a standout portfolio. Students are supported by discipline experts in areas such as dance, theatre, new media, photography, visual arts and visual communication design, and build transferable skills valued across the creative industries including imaginative thinking, problem solving, collaboration and research. The multidisciplinary structure encourages cross-disciplinary work. Graduates pursue practice, teaching and leadership roles across the arts.

name: Master of Health and Human Services Management
Master of Health Economics
description: The Master of Health Economics at Deakin University develops advanced skills in economic evaluation, resource allocation and modelling to inform policy and improve health outcomes. The course offers a flexible study experience, letting students complete a major or minor research project or focus on coursework through a wide range of electives, and build expertise in areas such as health technology assessment and policy analysis. Graduates work as health economists and analysts in government, research institutes, consulting and the pharmaceutical sector.

name: Master of Health Management
description: The Master of Health Management at Deakin University prepares students for a career in the health sector by developing skills in leadership, planning and health service management. Students learn to manage people, resources and programs while contributing to better health outcomes, and to apply business and management principles in a health context with a patient and community-focused approach. The degree can be tailored through specialisations including public health, health economics and business administration. Graduates work in management and executive roles across hospitals, community health, aged care and government.

name: Master of Health Promotion
description: The Master of Health Promotion at Deakin University builds the expertise to improve health and wellbeing at a population level. Students develop skills in program planning, communication, policy, advocacy and research to address the social and structural determinants of health, grounded in principles of equity, social justice and empowerment. The course is accredited by the International Union for Health Promotion and Education and enables graduates to register as a health promotion practitioner. Graduates work across government, non-government and community organisations in program, policy and advocacy roles.

name: Master of Humanitarian, Development and Disaster Studies
description: The Master of Humanitarian, Development and Disaster Studies at Deakin University builds a deeper understanding of the crises shaping the world and the community-led responses working to address them. Students explore international development, humanitarian action, disaster and crisis response, and community development, and examine the causes and impacts of challenges such as climate change, poverty, forced migration and inequality. Through critical analysis of real issues, students learn how communities create practical and just solutions. Graduates work with aid agencies, NGOs, government and international organisations.

name: Master of Information Systems
description: Deakin University Master of Information Systems teaches students to solve real business problems by connecting people, data and technology, building expertise across digital business analysis, data management, cyber security strategy, project management and the ethics of digital transformation. It requires 8, 12 or 16 credit points depending on entry point and recognition of prior learning; full-time students study four credit points per trimester across two trimesters a year, so it takes two years and can be fast-tracked to 1.5. The course connects the strategic role of technology with the practical work of managing knowledge and information in modern organisations. Indicative international tuition is around A$45,100 per year. Graduates work in business analysis, information management, digital strategy and project delivery.

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
Deakin's Master of IT is organised into four deliberate stages rather than a loose bundle of electives: a foundation block for students without a strong computing background, a fundamentals block, a mastery block, and a final specialisation or elective block: two people can graduate with quite different course transcripts depending on how much catching-up they needed early on. That staged structure is one reason the course accepts graduates from non-IT bachelor's degrees, not just computer science.

Specialisation options run through Deakin's SIT/MIS-coded units and typically cover areas like data science, cyber security, and enterprise systems, taught out of Deakin's Cloud Campus infrastructure. Deakin was an early mover into fully online postgraduate IT delivery in Australia and still runs a large online cohort alongside on-campus students at Burwood. Work-integrated learning options (industry-based capstone projects with real client organisations) are a recurring feature of the specialisation stage, giving graduates a portfolio project rather than just coursework to point to.
curriculum:
Part A – Foundation IT Studies (for students needing a computing bridge): Programming, Systems Fundamentals, Database Fundamentals, Networking Fundamentals
Part B – Fundamental IT Studies: Software Engineering, IT Architecture, Data Modelling, Professional and Research Practice in IT
Part C – Mastery IT Studies: Advanced units in software development and systems, capstone-adjacent project subject
Part D – Specialisation or electives: four Level 7 SIT/MIS units (e.g. Cyber Security, Data Science, Enterprise Systems) or an industry-based capstone project
admission_requirements: Full (16cp) entry: bachelor's degree in any discipline. Reduced-credit pathways for a bachelor's/honours in a related IT discipline, or a bachelor's (any discipline) plus 2+ years relevant work experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Master of Infrastructure Engineering and Management (Professional)
Master of International Relations (Professional)
description: The Master of International Relations at Deakin University explores geopolitical issues, climate change, poverty, pandemics and human rights, examining the nature of these problems and current responses. Students develop skills in policy analysis and gain a systematic understanding of the threats to peace and security, and learn about the global forces shaping political, social and economic life. Electives and optional focus areas such as conflict and security, diplomacy and activism, or human rights and international law let students define their direction. Graduates work in government, diplomacy, international organisations, NGOs and research.

name: Master of Nursing
description: Deakin University Master of Nursing is a postgraduate qualification for registered nurses who want to move into senior clinical, leadership, education or research roles. It requires 12 credit points, with core specialisation units taught in first year on a semester basis, and students choose a coursework stream, which can be tailored with course-specific or general electives, or a thesis stream. Full-time students study four credit points per trimester across two trimesters a year. Entry requires registration as a registered nurse in the country of practice and a Bachelor of Nursing or equivalent. Indicative international tuition is around A$35,300 per year. Graduates are prepared for advanced practice and for leadership, teaching and research positions across healthcare settings.

name: Master of Nutrition and Population Health
description: The Master of Nutrition and Population Health at Deakin University builds knowledge and skills to work across clinical, community and policy settings. This multidisciplinary course integrates nutrition science, public health, epidemiology, behavioural science and policy to help students address complex health challenges at individual and population levels. Students explore how nutrition influences health across the lifespan, from biological processes to the social and environmental factors that determine food choice, and develop skills in research design and data analysis. Graduates work in public health nutrition, policy, program and research roles.

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description: Deakin University Master of Professional Accounting is designed for both accounting and non-accounting graduates who want an accredited accounting qualification. Completing the appropriate units grants eligibility for associate membership of CPA Australia and meets the educational requirements for the CA program of Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, the Institute of Public Accountants, and the Professional Accounting Program. The degree requires 8, 12 or 16 credit points depending on entry point and recognition of prior learning; full-time students study four credit points per trimester across two trimesters a year, so it runs two years and can be fast-tracked to 1.5 or, with enough credit, one year. International students meet the English requirement with a bachelor degree from a recognised English-speaking country, IELTS 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0, or equivalent. Indicative international tuition is around A$49,000 per year.

name: Master of Professional Psychology
description: The Master of Professional Psychology at Deakin University is a fifth-year course accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council that prepares students for supervised practice and the pathway to general registration as a psychologist with the Psychology Board of Australia. Through applied learning, students develop capabilities in ethical and culturally responsive psychological assessment, diagnosis and evidence-based interventions, and explore professional practice across the lifespan and with diverse populations. Graduates complete supervised practice toward registration and work as psychologists across clinical, organisational and community settings.

name: Master of Public Health
description: Deakin University Master of Public Health requires 16 credit points and normally takes two years full-time at four credit points per trimester across two trimesters a year, with a fast-track to 1.5 years for applicants with relevant qualifications or experience. Students tailor the degree by choosing electives from eight fields of study, including health promotion, public health nutrition, humanitarian assistance, and disability and inclusion. All students receive a two-year membership of the Public Health Association of Australia while studying. Recognition of prior learning can grant credit. Indicative international tuition is around A$44,500 per year. Graduates move into senior public health roles, work with international organisations such as UNICEF and with NGOs focused on cancer, tobacco, drugs, reproductive health, obesity, food security and violence, or continue to a PhD.

name: Master of Sustainability (Professional)
description: The Master of Sustainability at Deakin University gives students the skills to address national and global sustainability issues and to implement strategies that balance environmental, social and economic considerations. Students apply their learning through projects or practical experience that reflect current industry needs, and graduate well positioned to develop and deliver practical solutions to complex sustainability challenges. With the sustainability sector projected to grow strongly, demand for skilled professionals is rising. Graduates work in sustainability, environmental management, strategy and policy roles across business, government and consulting.

name: Master of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
Master of Technology and Innovation Leadership
Advanced Diploma in Criminology and Justice
Bachelor of Arts
description:
ECU's Bachelor of Arts covers a fairly focused set of four disciplines (Visual Arts, Creative and Professional Writing, English, and Historical and Political Studies) rather than the sprawling nine-or-more-major menu some other Australian BAs offer, which keeps the degree tighter but means students wanting, say, a straight sociology or anthropology major would need to look elsewhere. The Creative and Professional Writing major sits alongside ECU's newer standalone Bachelor of Creative Writing (launched 2025), so students who want writing as one part of a broader arts education rather than the sole focus of their degree take this route instead.

Historical and Political Studies pairs history with political science content rather than treating them as fully separate majors, giving students a combined lens on how historical events shape contemporary policy and politics, useful preparation for students eyeing government, policy, or journalism careers as much as academic history. Visual Arts, meanwhile, benefits from ECU's studio facilities and connections into WA's contemporary art scene, including opportunities tied to Perth galleries and public art commissions.

Combined degree options exist too, most notably Bachelor of Arts/Bachelor of Media and Communication, for students who want to pair a humanities major with a more vocationally-oriented communications qualification rather than choosing one over the other.
curriculum:
Foundation units: critical thinking and academic writing, introduction to research in the humanities
Majors (choose one): Visual Arts, Creative and Professional Writing, English, Historical and Political Studies
Years 2-3: major-specific unit sequence plus free electives across the university
Capstone: major project, exhibition, portfolio, or extended essay depending on major
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time, on campus or online
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Aviation
description: The Bachelor of Aviation at Edith Cowan University provides a focused, professional education for people seeking to enter the aviation industry or already working in aviation who aspire to managerial roles or want qualifications recognised in countries that require them. Studies cover the underlying science and technology of aircraft systems, navigation, law, meteorology, human factors, aerodynamics and performance. The course suits those wishing to fly for a living or to work as a paraprofessional in an airline or aviation-oriented industry.

name: Bachelor of Biomedical Science
description: The Bachelor of Biomedical Science at Edith Cowan University prepares students for a field with long-term career prospects, including roles in management, research, education and specialised laboratory work. Biomedical scientists focus on how cells, organs and systems function in the human body, and their work is central to understanding and treating human disease. The course introduces a broad range of theory including anatomy, physiology, microbiology, immunology and genetics, and develops the practical laboratory skills needed for the profession.

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
The distinguishing feature of ECU's Bachelor of Business is the sports business major, which draws on the university's genuinely strong sport science research reputation (ECU runs one of Australia's better-known exercise and sport science schools) and pairs it with the standard business core, a combination that's harder to find with equal depth elsewhere. Other majors on offer include accounting, human resource management, management, marketing, and tourism, so the degree functions as a fairly conventional broad business qualification with one specific area of genuine differentiation.

Students who want to go deeper into the sport side specifically can also look at ECU's dedicated Bachelor of Global Sport Business Management or a Sport Business/Exercise Science double degree, which suggests the university has deliberately built out a cluster of related offerings rather than treating sport business as a single elective bolt-on. For students choosing the plain Bachelor of Business, the sports major functions as a genuine specialisation with its own unit sequence, not just a marketing label on generic management content.

Perth's business environment leans on mining services, government, and increasingly sport and tourism given WA's growing events calendar, and case studies and guest lecturer content in the degree tend to reflect that regional mix rather than a generic east-coast corporate framing.
curriculum:
Core units: Principles of Management, Marketing Fundamentals, Financial Accounting, Business Economics, Business Law, Business Analytics, Organisational Behaviour
Majors (choose one): Accounting, Human Resource Management, Management, Marketing, Sports Business, Tourism
Capstone: industry project or internship in final year
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time, on campus (Joondalup) or online
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Business Analytics
description: The Bachelor of Business Analytics at Edith Cowan University is designed to meet the increasing demand for skilled professionals in business analytics and artificial intelligence. The program has a strong industry focus, giving students hands-on experience through industry partnerships and innovative initiatives, and connecting them directly with industry to position graduates for success in a dynamic job market. Students learn to analyse complex data, apply AI methods and support evidence-based business decisions.

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description: The Bachelor of Commerce at Edith Cowan University equips students with business knowledge, skills and personal development to set them up for career success. Students are supported to develop practical business capability across core commerce disciplines, choosing areas of focus that align with their career goals. The degree combines theory with applied learning and employability skills, preparing graduates for roles across accounting, finance, management, marketing and related fields.

name: Bachelor of Communication
description: The Bachelor of Communication at Edith Cowan University prepares students for an ever-changing communication sector where the challenge is to help organisations build credibility, trust and brand awareness with their target audiences. Students develop knowledge and skills across advertising, public relations, digital communication, public affairs and community relations and engagement, and gain an awareness of strategic communication. Graduates work across the communication and media industries in a crowded, fast-moving media landscape.

name: Bachelor of Community and Human Services
description: The Bachelor of Community and Human Services at Edith Cowan University gives students the skills, knowledge and capacity to make a difference in the lives of individuals and diverse communities. Through a social science and human rights lens, students study how communities work, develop and change over time, and explore concepts of wellbeing and vulnerability. The degree suits people with a deep understanding of others and a passion for supporting people and communities, preparing graduates for roles across community services.

name: Bachelor of Computer Science
description: The Bachelor of Computer Science at Edith Cowan University introduces programming principles, systems analysis and computer security in the first year, then moves into advanced topics such as artificial intelligence, with a major in cyber security or software engineering in the final two years. Students undertake complex computer science projects both independently and in teams, graduating with in-demand technical skills for careers across the computing and technology industries.

name: Bachelor of Counselling
description: The Bachelor of Counselling at Edith Cowan University is a long-standing program that equips aspiring counsellors with a theoretical foundation in the allied health and counselling field. The course is underpinned by ideas about the human condition and the ways childhood experiences shape who we are. Students learn from experienced clinicians, gaining expertise while exploring the issues faced by individuals, couples and families, and graduate ready for a meaningful career in the helping professions.

name: Bachelor of Counter Terrorism Security and Intelligence
description: The Bachelor of Counter Terrorism, Security and Intelligence at Edith Cowan University offers a choice of eight major subjects and covers terrorism and international security, intelligence foundations and more. Students learn how to use technology to secure assets, protect critical and national infrastructure, and employ security management techniques. After the first year, students specialise in countering terrorism threats, graduating ready for careers in national security, intelligence and protective security.

name: Bachelor of Creative and Performing Arts Honours
description: The Bachelor of Creative and Performing Arts (Honours) at Edith Cowan University gives students the opportunity to focus in depth on a research topic of their choice while receiving further research training at fourth-year Honours level. Students can concentrate on their chosen discipline, including Creative Arts, Dance or Performance Making, and are guided through refining a research topic and undertaking research that synthesises practical, theoretical and historical understanding, preparing them for postgraduate study or professional practice.

name: Bachelor of Creative Writing
description: The Bachelor of Creative Writing at Edith Cowan University places storytelling at the heart of the course, developing students' awareness of and attention to voice, style, character, dialogue, empathy and influence. Students are introduced to writing techniques across a variety of forms including fiction, non-fiction and poetry, and learn how stories help us make sense of ourselves and the world. Graduates pursue careers in writing, publishing, editing and communication.

name: Bachelor of Criminology and Justice
description:
This degree treats the criminal justice system as a single connected pipeline rather than teaching law, policing, courts, and corrections as separate silos. Students trace how a case moves from lawmaking through policing, prosecution, courts, and corrections, and examine how "justice" gets defined differently by different groups along the way. It draws explicitly on political science, psychology, sociology, and law as contributing disciplines rather than being housed purely within a law school framework, which shapes it toward a more social-science-flavoured criminology than a pre-law degree.

Two named majors, policing and youth work, let students specialise fairly early, and the degree's signature applied component is the Criminal Justice Review Project, a work-integrated learning unit where students conduct real review work connected to a justice agency rather than a simulated case study. Placements and industry-based projects with WA criminal justice agencies (police, courts, corrections, youth services) run alongside the 11 core units that anchor the degree regardless of major.

Graduates commonly move into policing, youth justice, corrections, community corrections, court administration, or policy roles within WA's justice and human services sector, and the degree can also combine with a Bachelor of Laws for students who want law and criminology credentials together.
curriculum:
Core units (11 total): Introduction to Criminology, Criminal Law and Justice, Policing and Society, Courts and Sentencing, Corrections and Community Justice, Youth Justice, Research Methods in Criminology, Justice Ethics
Majors (choose one): Policing, Youth Work
Applied learning: Criminal Justice Review Project (work-integrated learning), optional practicum or industry-based placement
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time, on campus or online
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Design
description: The Bachelor of Design at Edith Cowan University is an integrated degree that introduces the core design disciplines of graphic, spatial and digital interaction design. Students develop expertise through hands-on design projects, exploring the areas of design they are most passionate about and working alongside designers with complementary skills. Studio-based learning prepares graduates for in-demand roles as traditional industries transform and designers take a central role in that change.

name: Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description:
ECU's Bachelor of Education (Primary) leans on the university's placement network of more than 1,000 partner schools and early learning centres across Western Australia, spanning metro, regional, rural, and remote settings. It's a scale that gives students genuine choice in where they complete professional practice rather than being funnelled into a handful of nearby Perth schools by default.

Where the degree differentiates itself from a purely generalist primary teaching qualification is the option to add a formal specialisation in mathematics, music, science, or languages, layered on top of the generalist primary knowledge base. That's useful for graduates who want to be the designated specialist teacher in one of those areas at their eventual school, rather than a generalist competing for those roles without formal backing. The degree is nationally accredited and specifically meets Teacher Registration Board of Western Australia requirements, including the literacy and numeracy proficiency standards graduates must clear before registration.

Because WA has significant regional and remote school staffing need, a meaningful share of practicum placements and eventual graduate employment happens outside the Perth metro area, and the placement network is explicitly built to expose students to that range of school contexts before they're deciding where to apply for their first teaching job.
curriculum:
Core sequence: Child and Adolescent Development, Curriculum Studies (English, Mathematics, Science, HASS, Health and PE), Inclusive Education, Classroom Management, Aboriginal Education and Perspectives
Optional specialisation (choose one): Mathematics, Music, Science, Languages
Professional practice: staged placements across metro, regional, rural, and remote WA schools through all four years
Capstone: extended final-year professional practice placement with formal teaching standards assessment
Total: 4 years full-time, TRBWA-accredited
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Engineering Honours
description:
ECU offers an unusually wide spread of engineering specialisations for a mid-sized Australian university: civil, civil and environmental, chemical, mechanical, mechatronics, computer systems, electrical power, electrical and renewable energy, electronics and communications, and instrumentation control and automation are all separate accredited streams rather than a generic engineering degree with late-stage electives. The renewable energy and electrical power streams in particular line up with Western Australia's expanding renewables and grid infrastructure sector, which has grown substantially as WA moves away from its historical reliance on gas peaking plants.

The degree is delivered from the purpose-built Joondalup campus, which houses dedicated engineering labs and equipment for each specialisation rather than shared generalist facilities, meaningful for hands-on disciplines like mechatronics or instrumentation control where lab access shapes how much practical skill students actually build before graduating. It's a four-year Honours-embedded structure (Engineers Australia accredited), so students don't need to apply separately or add an extra year to graduate with Honours standing, unlike some universities that treat Honours as a bolt-on fifth year.

Given WA's resources sector dominance, civil, electrical power, and instrumentation control graduates in particular find a strong local employment pipeline into mining, oil and gas, and utilities work, while the computer systems and mechatronics streams connect more to Perth's smaller but growing tech and automation employers.
curriculum:
Years 1-2: Engineering Mathematics, Engineering Mechanics, Materials Science, Circuit Theory, Thermodynamics, Engineering Design and Professional Practice
Specialisation streams (choose one): Chemical, Civil, Civil and Environmental, Computer Systems, Electrical Power, Electrical and Renewable Energy, Electronics and Communications, Instrumentation Control and Automation, Mechanical, Mechatronics
Year 3: stream-specific core units, industry-linked design project
Year 4 (Honours): capstone engineering project, advanced electives, professional experience placement
Total: 4 years full-time, Engineers Australia accredited, delivered at Joondalup
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 70-85 for competitive entry (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Environmental Science
description: The Bachelor of Environmental Science at Edith Cowan University is an international dual degree in which students study two and a half years at ECU and one year at the University of Portsmouth in the UK, graduating with a Bachelor of Environmental Science from ECU and a BSc (Hons) Environmental Science and Management from Portsmouth. Students gain a grounding in the biological, chemical, physical and social aspects of the environment and the knowledge and skills used in its management.

name: Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science
description:
Exercise and sport science is one of ECU's strongest-regarded programs nationally, and the degree sits inside a cluster of closely related offerings (a separate Exercise Science and Rehabilitation degree, a Sports Science and Football degree, and combined degrees pairing exercise science with sport business), which lets students self-select toward performance, rehabilitation, or management-adjacent career paths from the outset rather than treating "sport science" as one undifferentiated qualification.

Delivery mixes on-campus weekly labs and lectures with a blended format for some units (online content through the semester punctuated by two intensive on-campus lab/seminar blocks), which suits students balancing study with elite sport commitments, coaching work, or jobs in the fitness industry while completing the degree. ESSA (Exercise and Sports Science Australia) accreditation is built into the course design, so graduates come out eligible for ESSA credentialing without needing to complete bridging requirements afterward.

Career outcomes cited by the university span further than gym-floor exercise science roles: sports administration, teaching, coaching, strength and conditioning, corporate and workplace health, sports development, and performance analysis all show up as genuine graduate destinations, reflecting how broad the "sport science" label has become as an industry.
curriculum:
Core units: Functional Anatomy, Exercise Physiology, Biomechanics, Motor Control and Learning, Sport and Exercise Psychology, Nutrition and Performance, Strength and Conditioning, Research Methods in Sport Science
Practical components: on-campus laboratory sessions weekly (or intensive blocks for blended-format units)
Capstone: supervised placement or applied research project in an exercise, sport, or corporate health setting
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time, ESSA-accredited, on campus with some blended-delivery units
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Global Media and Communication
description: The Bachelor of Global Media and Communication at Edith Cowan University is an international dual degree in which graduates receive a Bachelor of Global Media and Communication from ECU and a BA (Hons) Global Communications and Media from the University of Portsmouth in the UK. Students undertake studies across journalism, broadcasting, screen production and strategic communication, gaining valuable international experience alongside the skills needed for careers in the global media and communication industries.

name: Bachelor of Global Sport Business Management (International)
description: The Bachelor of Global Sport Business Management at Edith Cowan University prepares students for a career in the globalised sport industry, including the growth area of event management. Students learn about sport delivery systems, event management, leadership and programming, business environments and markets, sport and recreation facilities and services management, strategic and human resource management, marketing in global sport business, and funding and finance, graduating ready for management roles across sport organisations and events.

name: Bachelor of Health Science
description: The Bachelor of Health Science at Edith Cowan University is about enhancing the health of communities and tackling health-related societal challenges such as obesity, harmful alcohol and drug use, and pandemics. Students develop skills to assess and monitor health situations and to design intervention strategies that make a difference to the lives and health of others, and gain valuable industry experience through a work placement in the final year.

name: Bachelor of Hospitality and Tourism Management
description: The Bachelor of Hospitality and Tourism Management at Edith Cowan University equips students for a career in one of the world's fastest growing and in-demand industries. Students gain an understanding of food and beverage management, sustainable tourism development, managing the service and guest experience, business identity and protocols, the business environment, and data analytics. Students can specialise by choosing a major in marketing, human resource management, international business or events management.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description: The Bachelor of Information Technology at Edith Cowan University prepares students for careers in information technology, IT management and cyber security. The first year introduces programming, mathematics, networking, databases and computer security, and students then develop advanced skills in web development, data management and visualisation in an enterprise context, IT security management and project management, and tackle complex IT projects with industry.

name: Bachelor of Journalism and Broadcast Media
description: The Bachelor of Journalism and Broadcast Media at Edith Cowan University builds hands-on skills that extend beyond traditional reporting, teaching students to engage audiences on issues that matter, including social justice, climate change, diversity and inclusivity, across all media channels. The course focuses on news, entertainment and sports content across television, radio, online and social platforms, preparing graduates for a range of roles in the media industry and beyond.

name: Bachelor of Laws
description: The Bachelor of Laws at Edith Cowan University is a fully accredited law degree available both on campus and online, designed to fit around students' other commitments. It builds the practical skills needed in the courtroom and beyond, opening doors to careers in legal practice, business, government and social justice. Students gain hands-on advocacy experience through the university's practical programs, graduating with more than legal theory.

name: Bachelor of Marketing, Advertising and Public Relations
description: The Bachelor of Marketing, Advertising and Public Relations at Edith Cowan University is unique to ECU, blending three related disciplines to give students a suite of skills for work in any creative industry. Students hone their marketing skills alongside strategic business management knowledge and build employability skills including critical thinking, teamwork, communication and problem-solving. Students may also undertake a work placement in their area of interest to gain advanced experience.

name: Bachelor of Music
description: The Bachelor of Music at Edith Cowan University, taught at the Western Australian Academy of Performing Arts, gives students the skills to succeed in the music industry. Students can pursue specialist training in areas inside and outside their chosen major, with a focus on practical skills in classical, contemporary, jazz, composition and sonic arts. The course is taught by working practitioners whose expertise spans the breadth of the music world today.

name: Bachelor of Music Honours
description: The Bachelor of Music (Honours) at Edith Cowan University provides outstanding music students with an introduction to research while focusing on advanced professional and practical skills. The course prepares students for entry into the music profession as highly skilled elite performers with a deep understanding of their art form, and offers a stepping stone to further postgraduate study. Specialisations include classical performance, jazz performance, contemporary music, composition and screen composition.

name: Bachelor of Osteopathy Honours
description: The Bachelor of Osteopathy (Honours) at Edith Cowan University trains qualified allied health professionals who use direct manual therapy interventions to improve movement, reduce pain, and manage or treat a range of physical conditions including acute pain and sports injuries. ECU is the first and only university in Western Australia to offer a degree in osteopathy, and the course is designed to prepare students for modern healthcare systems and a growing registered health profession.

name: Bachelor of Performing Arts
description: The Bachelor of Performing Arts at Edith Cowan University, taught at the Western Australian Academy of Performing Arts, explores original, self-devised and collaborative approaches to researching, creating, producing and presenting contemporary arts practice. The course combines theoretical and technical knowledge of performance and seeks to unlock limitations through practical inquiry, examining the evolving nature of contemporary practice and new approaches to presentation and production.

name: Bachelor of Preclinical Foundations of Imaging Science
description: The Bachelor of Preclinical Foundations of Imaging Science at Edith Cowan University prepares students towards a career as a sonographer, a highly skilled medical imaging professional who operates an ultrasound machine to perform diagnostic examinations. Demand for ultrasound as a first-line investigation has increased across all care settings, creating a shortage of sonographers in Australia. Students acquire knowledge and skills in applied anatomy, physiology and pathophysiology, and the operation of ultrasound imaging systems and image reporting.

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description: The Bachelor of Psychological Science at Edith Cowan University is an international dual degree that lets students learn about psychology while gaining valuable international experience, with three years of study at ECU and one at a partner institution. Students learn how to analyse and research behaviour and to explain interactions between people and their environment, building a bridge to employment in fields including mental health, human resources, and child and family services.

name: Bachelor of Psychology (Honours)
description:
ECU folds Honours directly into its Bachelor of Psychology as a four-year combined structure rather than making students apply separately for a bolt-on fifth year, which is a genuine timeline advantage for students who already know they want the full APAC-accredited pathway toward provisional psychologist registration. Twelve core psychology units run through the degree, and one unit worth flagging specifically is Cross Cultural and Indigenous Psychology: not a universal fixture of Australian psych degrees, and it reflects a broader push across WA psychology programs to build cultural competency content directly into core curriculum rather than treating it as optional.

Students aren't locked into a single-track psychology-only degree either; ECU allows combining a psychology major with a second major or minor from elsewhere in the university, or choosing electives freely, which suits students who want breadth (say, criminology, business, or a language) alongside their psychology core. Entry into the Honours component specifically requires a Weighted Average Mark of 70+ with a credit average across second and third year units and the majority of psychology units, so it's a genuine academic gate rather than an automatic progression.

The degree is offered both online and on campus, and graduates with the completed Honours year are positioned for provisional registration with the Psychology Board of Australia or entry into further postgraduate training (clinical, counselling, organisational, forensic) depending on which specialisation they pursue after this degree.
curriculum:
Years 1-3: 12 core psychology units including Introduction to Psychology, Research Methods and Statistics, Cross Cultural and Indigenous Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Cognition and Learning, Social Psychology, Abnormal Psychology, Biological Psychology
Elective structure: combine with a second major/minor or free electives across the university
Year 4 (Honours): supervised empirical research thesis, advanced seminars in psychological research and practice
Entry to Honours year: minimum 70 WAM with credit average in 2nd/3rd year and majority of psychology units
Total: 4 years full-time, APAC-accredited, on campus or online
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 70-85 for competitive entry (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Psychology and Counselling
description: The Bachelor of Psychology and Counselling at Edith Cowan University introduces students to the professional practice of counselling while preparing them for advanced psychology training. Students acquire skills to analyse and research behaviour and to explain interactions between people and their environment. The course is a springboard to postgraduate studies in psychology and counselling, and provides a pathway towards Honours and registration as a psychologist.

name: Bachelor of Psychology, Criminology and Justice
description: The Bachelor of Psychology, Criminology and Justice at Edith Cowan University suits students interested in the human mind, particularly the kind that turns to crime. It is more focused on psychology than ECU's Bachelor of Criminology and Justice, and suits students thinking of further study in psychology or criminology, or employment within the criminal justice system. Graduates have a pathway to Honours and postgraduate studies leading to registration as a psychologist.

name: Bachelor of Science (Nursing)
description:
ECU's nursing degree runs on partnership-model placements rather than scattering students across many disparate providers for short rotations. Students can complete the bulk of their practical hours within one health service partner, among them Sir Charles Gairdner Osborne Park Health Care Group, North Metropolitan Health Service Mental Health, Ramsay Health Care, and Western Australian Country Health Service. That continuity model means students build depth with one clinical environment and its staff over multiple placement blocks rather than restarting orientation at a new site every rotation, which several graduates report as easing the transition into graduate-year employment at the same health service.

The WA Country Health Service partnership specifically opens placement pathways into regional and rural WA, which matters given the acute nursing workforce shortages outside Perth metro. Students interested in rural or remote nursing practice have a structured route into that experience during training rather than having to seek it out independently after registration.

As a Bachelor of Science rather than a Bachelor of Nursing by name, the degree still meets all Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia registration requirements for Registered Nurse practice; the science framing reflects ECU's faculty structure rather than a different scope of practice or accreditation pathway.
curriculum:
Core sequence: Anatomy and Physiology, Pathophysiology, Pharmacology and Therapeutics, Nursing Practice (progressive units through all years), Mental Health Nursing, Aboriginal Health, Primary Health Care and Community Nursing
Clinical placement: staged practical placements through partner health services (Sir Charles Gairdner Osborne Park Health Care Group, North Metropolitan Health Service Mental Health, Ramsay Health Care, WA Country Health Service)
Capstone: final-year transition-to-practice clinical placement
Total: 3 years full-time, registration-ready under Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia standards
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, plus health/immunisation checks and (for clinical placements) police check (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0 (typical registration-body bar for nursing/health programs, approximate)

name: Bachelor of Science (Occupational Therapy) Honours
description: The Bachelor of Science (Occupational Therapy) Honours at Edith Cowan University is for students enrolled in ECU's Bachelor of Occupational Therapy, with applications by invitation based on academic performance in the first three years. The Honours year lets students develop an understanding of the factors that affect occupational performance in self-care, education, work, social participation, play and leisure for individuals, groups and populations, alongside a supervised research project.

name: Bachelor of Screen Production
description: The Bachelor of Screen Production at Edith Cowan University, taught at the Western Australian Academy of Performing Arts, teaches students to use screen storytelling to bring critical issues to the forefront, challenge societal norms and highlight diverse perspectives. Students engage in collaborative projects with fellow students on industry ventures, developing practical skills across the screen production process for careers in film, television and digital media.

name: Bachelor of Social Work
description: The Bachelor of Social Work at Edith Cowan University prepares students for a career grounded in eco-social justice, equality and human rights, working alongside individuals and communities to improve society's overall wellbeing and support the most vulnerable populations. Students develop professional and relational skills that can take them into mental health, community development, child protection or social research, and the accredited degree leads to eligibility for professional social work practice.

name: Bachelor of Speech Pathology
description: The Bachelor of Speech Pathology at Edith Cowan University trains speech pathologists who provide diagnostic assessment and management of communication and swallowing disorders for people of all ages, from babies to older populations. Students learn to support people through direct therapy interventions, education, consultancy and advocacy, and the course suits people passionate about communication and helping people across the lifespan.

name: Bachelor of Speech Pathology Honours
description: The Bachelor of Speech Pathology (Honours) at Edith Cowan University is for students enrolled in ECU's Bachelor of Speech Pathology, with applications by invitation only based on academic performance in the first three years. The Honours year provides the skills necessary to assess, plan and treat people with communication and swallowing disorders in a range of contexts, and is closely aligned with areas such as speech science, psychology and audiology.

name: Bachelor of Visual Arts
description: The Bachelor of Visual Arts at Edith Cowan University, taught at the Western Australian Academy of Performing Arts, develops students' ability to use the tools and techniques of visual art, from drawing to photography and printmaking to digital art. Students use these skills to make work that addresses matters of social importance and influences how audiences think about issues of local and global significance, building a practice for careers in the visual arts.

name: Bachelor of Youth Work
description: The Bachelor of Youth Work at Edith Cowan University trains youth workers who provide guidance, support and resources to help young people aged 12 to 26 navigate the challenges they face while fostering personal growth and empowerment. Students learn interpersonal and helping skills, inclusive practice, and how to create social change with and for young people, studying specialist youth work units alongside complementary areas that support their practice.

name: Diploma in Aviation
description: The Diploma in Aviation at Edith Cowan University is an entry point to studying aviation for people working in the industry or flying as a hobby. It provides a pathway into the Bachelor of Aviation, where students can graduate with the bachelor degree after two additional years of study using credit for units already completed. This on-campus course provides a focused, professional education and graduate status for those seeking to enter the aviation industry.

name: Doctor of Philosophy
description: The Doctor of Philosophy at Edith Cowan University is an opportunity to pursue a topic in depth at the highest academic level. A PhD is an independent, supervised research project that develops the candidate's capacity to conduct high-quality, original research, and is assessed on the submission of a thesis, or a creative work with an accompanying exegesis, together with an oral examination. It may be undertaken in any school within ECU.

name: Graduate Certificate in Creative Arts Entrepreneurship and Cultural Innovation
description: The Graduate Certificate in Creative Arts Entrepreneurship and Cultural Innovation at Edith Cowan University has students explore and conceptualise a creative venture, such as a performance, event or small enterprise, while building a foundation in critical theory and entrepreneurial practice. The course explores ideation, strategic framing, value proposition design, and the cultural, economic and ethical dimensions of creative entrepreneurship, with specialist pathways in Creative Producing, Creative Technologies and Social Innovation.

name: Graduate Certificate in Data Science
description: The Graduate Certificate in Data Science at Edith Cowan University establishes a solid foundation in the mathematics, statistics and computer science methods and tools central to data science. Data science is an interdisciplinary field that uses scientific methods, processes, algorithms and systems to extract knowledge and insights from structured and unstructured data. The certificate suits people seeking to enter the field or build a base for further postgraduate data science study.

name: Graduate Certificate in Design Thinking
description: The Graduate Certificate in Design Thinking at Edith Cowan University responds to the expansion of the design industry into emerging fields such as design thinking, service design and human-centred design, which are in high demand in areas including business management, communications, public health and health sciences. The course develops design thinking competencies that open new employment opportunities for graduates across a range of sectors.

name: Graduate Certificate in Environmental Assessment and Management
description: The Graduate Certificate in Environmental Assessment and Management at Edith Cowan University is for professionals who want to extend their knowledge in environmental assessment and management. It is designed for people who need the skills to integrate environmental planning, conservation and monitoring into the broader decision-making of their organisations, covering environmental impact assessment and environmental management, and can serve as a pathway into the graduate diploma or master degree.

name: Graduate Certificate of Applied Digital Marketing
description: The Graduate Certificate of Applied Digital Marketing at Edith Cowan University is designed in consultation with industry to create graduates proficient in the knowledge and application of digital marketing. Confidence and competence in digital and social media are crucial for marketing professionals and for those who own or manage a small to medium business. Students critique topical, current practice and apply digital marketing skills in real contexts.

name: Graduate Certificate of Business
description: The Graduate Certificate of Business at Edith Cowan University suits professionals with no formal qualifications who want to enhance their knowledge in business and management. It also serves as an introduction to the Graduate Diploma of Business and, in turn, the Master of Business Administration. The certificate covers the management of people and organisations, along with marketing and integrated principles relating to economics and finance.

name: Graduate Certificate of Counselling and Psychotherapy
Graduate Certificate of Cyber Security
description: The Graduate Certificate of Cyber Security at Edith Cowan University is designed to meet the demand for cyber security professionals in government, law enforcement and industry. The course engages with, and provides a pathway for, information technology professionals seeking to start or progress a career in cyber security, and is also relevant to those seeking to enter the IT profession with no previous experience in the discipline.

name: Graduate Certificate of Hospitality Management
description: The Graduate Certificate of Hospitality Management at Edith Cowan University is designed for people already working or intending to work in the hospitality industry, aimed at graduates and professionals with work experience but no formal university qualifications. The course develops a foundation of business and management principles, including the management of people and organisations, hospitality operations, marketing and strategic planning.

name: Graduate Diploma in Creative Arts Entrepreneurship and Cultural Innovation
description: The Graduate Diploma in Creative Arts Entrepreneurship and Cultural Innovation at Edith Cowan University combines advanced theory with hands-on learning through industry collaboration, equipping students to lead, innovate and create impactful artistic and cultural ventures. Building on prior ideation and strategic framing, students develop and test a creative venture such as a performance, event or small enterprise that demonstrates originality, audience awareness and sustainable innovation, with specialist pathways in the field.

name: Graduate Diploma in Early Childhood Teaching
description: The Graduate Diploma in Early Childhood Teaching at Edith Cowan University equips aspiring early childhood teachers who hold an existing degree to teach in early childhood settings after one year of full-time study. Focusing on children from birth to five years of age, the course centres on the care and education of children in this age group in partnership with families and communities, building on the strengths students bring to the program.

name: Graduate Diploma in Environmental Science
description: The Graduate Diploma in Environmental Science at Edith Cowan University is designed for professionals who need the skills and knowledge to integrate environmental planning, conservation and monitoring into their organisations' decision-making. The course covers environmental impact assessment, planning and monitoring in the context of major ecosystems, emphasises the global, regional and local nature of environmental issues, and covers environmental management, providing a pathway to the master degree.

name: Graduate Diploma in Teaching (Secondary)
description: The Graduate Diploma in Teaching (Secondary) at Edith Cowan University equips aspiring high school teachers who hold an existing degree in another field to teach with provisional registration in Western Australian secondary schools after one year of full-time study. A key feature is 50 days of professional experience, which allows students to connect theory and practice while building professional and generic skills in real teaching environments.

name: Graduate Diploma of Business
description: The Graduate Diploma of Business at Edith Cowan University can lead into the Master of Business Administration and is designed to give students the skills and knowledge needed to manage successfully in contemporary organisations. With flexible study options, the diploma builds on knowledge including people management, marketing, professional development and value creation, and graduates are able to make independent judgements and provide sustainable business solutions.

name: Graduate Diploma of Counselling and Psychotherapy
Graduate Diploma of Medical Sonography
description: The Graduate Diploma of Medical Sonography at Edith Cowan University prepares students to work as sonographers, highly skilled medical imaging professionals who operate ultrasound machines to perform diagnostic examinations. Demand for ultrasound as a first-line investigation has increased across all care settings, creating a shortage of sonographers in Australia. Students acquire knowledge and skills in applied anatomy, physiology and pathophysiology and the operation of ultrasound imaging systems.

name: Graduate Diploma of Public Health
description: The Graduate Diploma of Public Health at Edith Cowan University prepares students for a career improving and protecting the health and wellbeing of the general population. Public health practitioners help individuals and communities take greater control over their health and wellbeing and influence organisational and political environments in ways that lead to better health outcomes. The diploma builds knowledge and skills for practice across local, national and international communities.

name: Graduate Diploma of Supply Chain and Logistics Management
Master of Arts (Performing Arts)
description: The Master of Arts (Performing Arts) at Edith Cowan University, offered through the Western Australian Academy of Performing Arts, is aimed at researchers, critics and practitioners from across the arts community who want to extend their independent capacity to operate in an increasingly multi-art-form and technologically based profession. Students may research, devise and produce new works of art, or develop new approaches to arts practice and its critical and social contexts.

name: Master of Aviation Management
description: The Master of Aviation Management at Edith Cowan University develops future-ready aviation leaders equipped to navigate the complexities of a global, technology-driven and highly regulated industry. The course blends strategic management, organisational capability, safety and risk governance, sustainability and applied research to prepare graduates for senior roles across airlines, airports, government agencies and aviation service providers. Students engage in applied research and industry projects, graduating ready to lead in a fast-changing aviation sector.

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
ECU's School of Business and Law is ranked WA's top business school for quality and sits in the top two nationally on the AFR BOSS Best Business Schools list, and the MBA is AACSB-accredited, putting it in a global tier most Australian business schools outside the Group of Eight don't reach. Within the program, students choose from a genuinely large bank of 14 specialisation areas rather than a handful of generic tracks, which lets working professionals steer the degree toward whatever function or industry they're actually trying to move into.

Curriculum design has been updated to fold in ethical AI use directly into core content rather than treating it as an add-on module, which reflects how quickly generative AI has changed expectations for MBA graduates in strategy, marketing, and operations roles over the past couple of years. Cohorts skew toward working professionals studying part-time or online, so the teaching model relies heavily on case discussion and applied assignments tied to students' own workplaces rather than an on-campus-immersion residential model.

WA's economy is still heavily resources-and-services weighted, and a fair share of the cohort comes from mining services, government, and healthcare administration, which shapes case study content and networking opportunities differently than an MBA cohort concentrated in Sydney financial services.
curriculum:
Core units: Strategic Management, Managerial Economics, Financial Management, Marketing Management, Leadership and Organisational Behaviour, Business Analytics and Ethical AI, Operations Management, Business Research Project
Specialisations: choose from 14 areas including international business, human resource management, marketing, project management, finance, and entrepreneurship
Capstone: applied strategy project or business research report
Total: 2 years full-time / up to 4 years part-time, on campus or online, AACSB-accredited
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Master of Business Administration Global
description: The Master of Business Administration Global at Edith Cowan University develops highly skilled global managers and leaders who can contribute to organisations effectively and responsibly in an international business context. In a globally competitive environment, the course focuses on building organisational capability by creating a climate and culture conducive to innovation, and gives students the ability to understand and strategically navigate the complexities of international business.

name: Master of Business Analytics
description: The Master of Business Analytics at Edith Cowan University develops a conceptual and practical understanding of data analytics. Students are exposed to a range of business areas including accounting and finance, human resource management, marketing, supply chain management and the information systems that support them, and work with business analytics tools to identify patterns and trends in complex data sets and visualise them in meaningful ways.

name: Master of Business by Research
description: The Master of Business by Research at Edith Cowan University provides advanced, research-based study in theoretical and applied areas of business. Students may choose from disciplines including accounting, economics, event management, finance, hospitality management, management, marketing, management information systems, planning, recreation management, sport management and tourism management. The course extends understanding of knowledge in the discipline alongside research methods, culminating in a thesis.

name: Master of Business Psychology
description: The Master of Business Psychology at Edith Cowan University develops professionals who understand human behaviour and how to leverage this knowledge in business contexts, skills in demand across corporate, government and not-for-profit sectors. The course takes a contemporary evidence-based perspective and is designed for professionals who want to lead change in the workplace, equipping graduates to apply psychological frameworks to complex business settings and empower people and organisations.

name: Master of Clinical Psychology
description: The Master of Clinical Psychology at Edith Cowan University prepares students for professional practice in clinical psychology, especially the assessment and treatment of psychological disorders, in response to strong demand for clinical psychology graduates in government and the not-for-profit and private sectors. Students learn skills for working with clients across the lifespan, including infants and families, children, adolescents, adults, groups and couples, and people from diverse backgrounds.

name: Master of Communication
description: The Master of Communication at Edith Cowan University equips students with the professional and theoretical knowledge to meet constant digital disruption in the communication sector with confidence. As companies grapple with protecting their reputation and behaving ethically under intense scrutiny from many stakeholders, communication professionals need to provide counsel at the highest level, and the course prepares graduates for senior strategic communication roles.

name: Master of Computer Science
description:
ECU's Master of Computer Science is a conversion-friendly degree: it's designed to take graduates from unrelated bachelor's disciplines and get them industry-ready in computing, which is why the first-year units look like a compressed CS undergrad (data structures, algorithms, systems, databases) before the program moves into more advanced electives in the second year. It's accredited by the Australian Computer Society, and ECU folds in its considerable cyber security research strength as an elective pathway rather than keeping the two programs walled off from each other.

That cyber security connection is worth noting specifically because ECU is one of only two Australian universities recognised by the federal government as an Academic Centre of Cyber Security Excellence, and the only one in Western Australia. Students in the computer science degree who want a security-adjacent skill set can pull electives from that research base without needing to enrol in the separate Master of Cyber Security. Beyond security, elective streams commonly run toward data science, machine learning, and software engineering practice.

Perth's tech employment market is smaller and more resources-and-mining-services-oriented than Sydney or Melbourne's, so ECU's industry placements and capstone project partners often skew toward that sector along with WA government IT roles, rather than the startup-heavy scene more associated with the east coast.
curriculum:
Foundational units: Programming Fundamentals, Data Structures and Algorithms, Database Systems, Computer Systems and Networks, Software Engineering Principles
Advanced units: choose electives across cyber security, data science and analytics, artificial intelligence, or advanced software engineering
Capstone: industry-linked project or research-based minor thesis
Total: 2 years full-time (shorter with credit for a relevant undergraduate background), accredited by the Australian Computer Society

name: Master of Computing and Security by Research
description: The Master of Computing and Security by Research at Edith Cowan University provides advanced, research-based study in theoretical and applied areas of computing or security science. The course extends knowledge in the discipline alongside knowledge of research methods, and students undertake a significant independent research investigation resulting in a thesis relevant to computing or security. The degree develops advanced technical and analytical capability and prepares graduates for research careers or for progression to a PhD.

name: Master of Counselling
description: The Master of Counselling at Edith Cowan University equips students with the knowledge, skills and experience to work effectively as a professional counsellor across diverse settings. Students learn to engage clients through a person-centred approach while exploring a range of counselling theories and techniques including psychodynamic, cognitive-behavioural and humanistic approaches, graduating ready to support people to navigate life's challenges and improve their wellbeing.

name: Master of Creative Arts Entrepreneurship and Cultural Innovation
description: The Master of Creative Arts Entrepreneurship and Cultural Innovation at Edith Cowan University is a first-of-its-kind program in Australia for artists, producers and cultural innovators who want to transform ideas into impactful ventures. The course equips students with the skills to lead, innovate and thrive in a rapidly evolving global creative economy, combining advanced theory with hands-on practice through industry collaboration.

name: Master of Cyber Security
description:
ECU is one of only two universities the Australian federal government has recognised as an Academic Centre of Cyber Security Excellence, and the sole one in Western Australia, a designation that reflects the size of ECU's cyber security research and teaching group, described by the university as the largest in Australia and ranked among the top ten globally. The Master of Cyber Security draws directly on that research base rather than being a generically branded security add-on to a computing degree, and it's built specifically to serve government, law enforcement, and industry demand for security specialists rather than general IT professionals.

Entry pathways are unusually flexible: applicants can come in with a related bachelor's degree, or with a bachelor's in any discipline paired with five years of relevant work experience, which opens the program to career-changers already working in IT operations, law enforcement, or defence-adjacent roles without a computing degree on paper. Course length can also compress for students with relevant prior qualifications or experience, rather than everyone doing a fixed two years regardless of background.

Perth hosts a meaningful concentration of defence, mining-sector, and government security roles, and ECU's placement and industry connections in cyber security lean into that local demand alongside the more geographically distributed remote/online cohort the program attracts nationally and internationally.
curriculum:
Core units: Cyber Security Fundamentals, Network Security, Digital Forensics, Security Risk Management, Cryptography, Incident Response and Threat Intelligence, Governance Risk and Compliance
Electives: penetration testing, cloud security, industrial control systems security, security research methods
Capstone: applied security project or research minor thesis, often linked to industry or government partners
Total: 2 years full-time / 4 years part-time (reduced duration available with relevant background), on campus or online
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Master of Data Science
description: The Master of Data Science at Edith Cowan University builds the foundations in mathematics, statistics and computer science that underpin data science, an interdisciplinary field that uses scientific methods, processes, algorithms and systems to extract knowledge and insights from structured and unstructured data. Students develop knowledge and skills in key data science tools and techniques, preparing graduates for analytics and data science roles across industries.

name: Master of Education
description:
Rather than one generic Master of Education, ECU structures the degree around named specialisations: Behaviour and Wellbeing, Early Childhood Education, Learning Difficulties, Literacy Education, Special Education, and Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL). Each is built from the same four core units plus four specialisation-specific units, so the degree can serve very different practitioners (an early childhood educator and a TESOL specialist, for instance) without pretending one curriculum fits both.

The related Master of Education (Advanced) extends this into a two-year structure that lets students graduate with two specialisations rather than one, aimed particularly at international students who want both the additional academic communication development time and broader specialisation coverage before returning to their home education systems or seeking WA teaching roles. Both versions target practising teachers and education professionals wanting formal postgraduate standing rather than beginning teachers, since the units assume classroom experience as a base.

Given ECU's strong existing footprint in initial teacher education across Western Australia, a lot of the postgraduate cohort are ECU-trained teachers returning for career progression into specialist, leadership, or coordinator roles, though the program draws students from other teacher-training backgrounds and overseas as well.
curriculum:
Core units (4): Educational Research Methods, Contemporary Issues in Education, Leadership in Educational Contexts, Reflective Practice in Education
Specialisation units (4, choose one specialisation): Behaviour and Wellbeing, Early Childhood Education, Learning Difficulties, Literacy Education, Special Education, or TESOL
Extended option: Master of Education (Advanced) allows two specialisations over 2 years
Total: 1.5-2 years full-time equivalent depending on pathway, on campus or online
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Master of Engineering
description: Edith Cowan University Master of Engineering is for graduates who hold a non-professionally-accredited engineering or technology degree and want to upgrade to an accredited engineering qualification, or to move into a new specialisation such as civil and environmental or mechanical engineering. Students complete five core units, 11 specialisation units and a practicum unit, and must gain at least 12 weeks of full-time-equivalent practical work experience before graduating. ECU admission and English language requirements apply. Indicative international tuition is around A$45,400 per year. Graduates work as civil, environmental, structural and water resource engineers and as construction managers, in the development, design, improvement and construction of infrastructure and civil engineering systems.

name: Master of Engineering Science
description: The Master of Engineering Science at Edith Cowan University is a research program providing advanced-level research in engineering disciplines including chemical, civil, electrical, renewable energy, environmental, mechanical, mechatronic and petroleum engineering. Students undertake a supervised research project that makes a contribution to knowledge in their chosen engineering field, developing high-level research and analytical skills for careers in research and advanced engineering practice.

name: Master of Environmental Science
