description: The Master of Environmental Science at Edith Cowan University provides skills and experience in environmental science, focusing on project management, occupational health and safety, sustainability, monitoring and reporting. Students gain work experience in relevant industry organisations, developing an understanding of how environmental projects are managed, and build skills for the environmental, engineering and sustainability sectors. Graduates are equipped for roles in environmental consulting, government, sustainability and resource management across Western Australia and beyond.

name: Master of Environmental Studies
description: The Master of Environmental Studies at Edith Cowan University is a joint degree with Tokyo City University in Japan that prepares students to explore global environmental problems and contribute to a sustainable society. Students complete one semester of study on location at Tokyo City University and can undertake a two-week internship in Japan, completing a substantial project in the final semester.

name: Master of Finance
description: The Master of Finance at Edith Cowan University is a coursework degree for students seeking comprehensive postgraduate skills in applied finance, financial management, financial analysis and investment strategy. The course prepares students to work in the dynamic financial services industry, focusing on how individuals, financial institutions, businesses and governments make financial and investment decisions, and teaching students to identify, analyse and manage financial risk.

name: Master of Horticultural Science
description: The Master of Horticultural Science at Edith Cowan University delivers theoretical and practical knowledge for the production, postharvest handling and supply chain of horticultural produce, along with the management and sustainability issues surrounding how produce is gathered, stored and used. Students are instilled with principles of advanced production technologies and practices to address key national and global challenges in horticulture.

name: Master of Human Resource Management
description: The Master of Human Resource Management at Edith Cowan University develops excellence in people management to enhance the ability of leaders and managers to contribute to organisational success. Students learn to respond to people management challenges within contemporary organisations and develop skills in communication, teamwork, critical thinking and problem-solving, graduating as business-driven HR professionals. Graduates are prepared for careers in strategic human resource management, employment relations and organisational consulting across sectors.

name: Master of International Hospitality Management
description: The Master of International Hospitality Management at Edith Cowan University is a unique course in Western Australia that brings together business and management principles in relation to the hospitality industry. Students are equipped with the knowledge and skills for a career in senior management in the international hospitality industry, and undertake a four-month internship in their final semester. Students learn strategic management, revenue and operations management, and service leadership, graduating ready for senior roles in the global hospitality industry.

name: Master of Laws (Research)
description: The Master of Laws (Research) at Edith Cowan University offers candidates the opportunity to undertake research in a specialised area of law. Students complete compulsory research support units and a supervised thesis that makes a substantial contribution to legal knowledge, developing high-level skills in research and analysis that equip graduates for careers in advanced research, tertiary education and specialised legal practice.

name: Master of Management Information Systems
description: The Master of Management Information Systems at Edith Cowan University is relevant to both IT and non-IT professionals who want to develop their skills in information and communications technology and its application to business. Management information systems describe the broad opportunities for supporting the application of technologies to business, and the course addresses the business and technology issues arising from enterprise systems.

name: Master of Marketing and Innovation Management
description: The Master of Marketing and Innovation Management at Edith Cowan University is a unique course in Western Australia that develops marketing managers capable of managing complex business cases in national and international contexts. Students learn to create value for an organisation, its customers, its partners and society at large, and are equipped with the skills and knowledge required for a career in customer, product and innovation management.

name: Master of Medical and Health Science by Research
description: The Master of Medical and Health Science by Research at Edith Cowan University builds on specialised undergraduate degrees to provide advanced-level study in medical, biomedical, paramedical, allied health and exercise sciences. The award comprises coursework, which provides instruction in research skills, methods and statistics, and the production of a research thesis, preparing graduates for research careers in health and medicine.

name: Master of Midwifery (Research)
description: The Master of Midwifery (Research) at Edith Cowan University is for people with experience in midwifery practice and a relevant undergraduate degree or equivalent qualification who are interested in a research career. Students explore an area of particular interest and learn how to be an independent researcher under the supervision of leaders in midwifery, developing high-level research skills for academic, clinical and policy roles.

name: Master of News and Entertainment Media
description: The Master of News and Entertainment Media at Edith Cowan University prepares students for a range of roles in the media industry and beyond, teaching the basics of journalism through to the practicalities of reporting and presenting news, entertainment and other content across television, radio, streaming, online and digital storytelling platforms. Specialist studio units replicate professional environments so students graduate industry-ready.

name: Master of Nursing (Graduate Entry)
description: The Master of Nursing (Graduate Entry) at Edith Cowan University is for people who hold a degree in a discipline other than nursing and are now considering a career in the profession. The course has a strong focus on clinical nursing practice and research and includes work practicums in Perth hospitals to prepare students for the healthcare industry. On graduation students are eligible to register with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia.

name: Master of Nursing Studies
description: The Master of Nursing Studies at Edith Cowan University is designed primarily for internationally registered nurses, and also enables Australian registered nurses to gain and update skills to further their careers. The course develops in-depth knowledge of contemporary health care and the skills to apply it to practice, covering topics such as clinical leadership, health equity and social justice. Students complete supervised clinical placements in Perth health settings, applying their learning to real patient care before entering the workforce.

name: Master of Nutrition and Dietetics
description: The Master of Nutrition and Dietetics at Edith Cowan University is a pathway to the profession of dietetics, integrating theoretical and practical components across clinical dietetics, food service, community and public health, and research. Students are trained to understand and interpret nutrition science, assess nutritional needs, conduct research and give dietary advice for general health and specialised requirements, including medical conditions and improved performance.

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description: The Master of Professional Accounting at Edith Cowan University provides an opportunity for graduates whose first degree is in a discipline other than accounting to undertake major studies in accounting and law. The course leads to the acquisition of accounting skills and knowledge and helps fulfil the requirements for membership of the professional accounting bodies, preparing graduates for careers in accounting and finance.

name: Master of Project Management
description: Edith Cowan University Master of Project Management is a 12-unit degree in the School of Business and Law that equips students to design, implement and lead projects in almost any industry. It can be completed in as little as 24 months part-time, and a fast-track option of nine units and about 18 months is available to applicants with a relevant bachelor degree in project management, engineering or information technology, a project management major, any bachelor degree plus two years of project management experience, or a current professional certification such as PMP, CAPM, PMI-ACP or Chartered Project Professional. A graduate certificate or graduate diploma can also reduce the study load. Indicative international tuition is around A$40,100 per year. Graduates work as project managers across sectors.

name: Master of Public Health
description: The Master of Public Health at Edith Cowan University prepares students for a career improving and protecting the health and wellbeing of the general population. Public health practitioners help individuals and communities take greater control over their health and influence organisational and political environments in ways that lead to better health outcomes. The course builds advanced knowledge and skills for practice across local, national and international communities.

name: Master of Science by Research
description: The Master of Science by Research at Edith Cowan University provides advanced, research-based study in theoretical and applied areas of biological science, environmental science, environmental management, sustainability, horticulture, bioinformatics, analytical chemistry, physics, data science or mathematics. Students undertake a significant independent research investigation resulting in a thesis, extending knowledge in the discipline alongside knowledge of research methods. The course develops high-level skills in research design, methods and analysis, and prepares graduates for a PhD or research-focused roles in industry and government.

name: Master of Screen Production
description: The Master of Screen Production at Edith Cowan University, taught at the Western Australian Academy of Performing Arts, teaches the art and craft of storytelling, exploring the global environment for screen production and the ethics, dynamics, opportunities and challenges of a professional career as a screen storyteller. Students work in professional environments on short dramas, documentaries and episodic web series in roles including producing, directing, screenwriting, cinematography and editing.

name: Master of Supply Chain and Logistics Management
description: The Master of Supply Chain and Logistics Management at Edith Cowan University is a unique course designed to advance careers in logistics, transportation, distribution, operations and production management. Students study the procurement, warehousing, inventory management and transportation of goods, with an option to specialise in either information systems or cyber security for supply chain, preparing graduates for management roles across many businesses.

name: Master of Teaching (Early Childhood)
description: The Master of Teaching (Early Childhood) at Edith Cowan University provides a nationally accredited initial teaching qualification for students who already hold a bachelor degree or equivalent in an area other than education. The course is dedicated to producing quality graduates ready for employment across the early childhood education sector, including teaching children from birth to eight years of age, with a focus on the care and education of young children.

name: Master of Technology
description: The Master of Technology at Edith Cowan University offers a postgraduate pathway to an engineering qualification at the technologist grade for applicants with a non-engineering or non-technology first degree who wish to transition to an engineering career. Graduates can seek engineering technologist roles in industry, or can upgrade to an accredited professional engineering qualification by articulating into a further course.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
Federation's Arts degree was rebuilt fairly recently after facing internal pressure to be cut, and the version that survived is noticeably more focused than a generic humanities degree: a new History and Heritage Studies major sits alongside a strengthened Indigenous Studies major, plus options in Literature, Media and Screen Studies, Sociology and Writing. The History and Heritage Studies major in particular leans into regional and local heritage and tourism content, a reasonable fit for a university whose home city, Ballarat, built its identity around goldfields heritage and has an active heritage-tourism industry on its doorstep.

The Indigenous Studies major covers identity, reconciliation, human rights and Aboriginal health and visual arts, taught across Federation's Mt Helen, Berwick and Gippsland campuses, all locations with meaningful Aboriginal community presence and partnerships the university draws on for guest teaching and placement opportunities.

Like Federation's other undergraduate degrees, the Arts program builds in a work placement component through the university's cooperative education model: a genuine point of difference from Arts degrees at universities where a humanities student might graduate without ever setting foot in a workplace tied to their study.
curriculum:
Year 1: Critical and Ethical Thinking; Introduction to chosen major area; foundational units across two elective majors; Academic and Professional Writing
Year 2: Major units (History and Heritage Studies, Indigenous Studies, Literature, Media and Screen Studies, Sociology, or Writing); minor/elective units; Work Placement preparation
Year 3: Advanced major units; capstone research or creative project; Work Placement (cooperative education model)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
The Bachelor of Business at Federation runs a genuinely common first year across Management, Marketing, Creativity and Innovation, Accounting and Finance, Economics, Statistics and Law before students commit to a major, a deliberately soft entry that lets students who arrive unsure what kind of business career they want switch direction without losing credit. From second year, the major choice narrows to Management, Marketing, or Banking and Finance, each with its own progression of discipline units.

What's distinctive is how open the elective slots are: students can pull interdisciplinary electives from IT, Psychology, Sociology, Environmental Science or Outdoor Studies, so a business student with an interest in, say, environmental policy can build a genuinely hybrid transcript rather than one confined to a business faculty silo. The degree also runs on Federation's co-operative education model, which folds a supervised industry placement or industry-based project directly into the award rather than leaving work experience to student initiative.

It's a broader, more exploratory degree than a specialised single-major commerce program, which suits students who want optionality more than early specialisation, though students set on chartered accounting or a specific finance career path may find Federation's separate accounting-specific degrees a tighter fit.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Management; Marketing Principles; Accounting Fundamentals; Economics for Business; Business Statistics; Business Law; Creativity and Innovation
Year 2: Major units begin (Management, Marketing, or Banking and Finance stream); interdisciplinary elective 1; interdisciplinary elective 2
Year 3: Advanced major units; Strategic Management; Industry Placement / Industry-Based Project; capstone elective in chosen major
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Community and Human Services
Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice
Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description:
This is Federation's direct entry pathway into primary teaching, run out of Ballarat, Berwick and Gippsland campuses with a strong regional-and-outer-suburban placement network, a practical advantage for graduates, since Victorian country and growth-corridor schools are chronically short of primary teachers and often recruit straight out of prac. Students pick a specialisation partway through: English, Mathematics, Science, or an Inclusive Education stream focused on supporting kids with additional learning needs, and that choice shapes a chunk of the later-year electives.

The degree is built around supervised professional experience placements that increase in length and responsibility each year, culminating in a full-time final-year placement where students effectively run a classroom under a mentor teacher's supervision. Federation also builds in explicit test preparation for LANTITE, the national literacy and numeracy test that every intending teacher in Australia has to pass before their final placement. That hurdle trips up a meaningful number of otherwise capable education students, so having it addressed inside the curriculum rather than left to self-study is a real point in the course's favour.

Graduates come out with provisional registration eligibility with the Victorian Institute of Teaching, and the degree counts toward accreditation nationally through AITSL standards, so the qualification travels reasonably well if a graduate later moves interstate.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Primary Teaching; Child and Adolescent Development; Language and Literacy 1; Mathematics Education 1; Professional Experience Placement 1
Year 2: Curriculum specialisation units (English, Mathematics, Science or Inclusive Education stream); Assessment and Reporting; Behaviour Management; Professional Experience Placement 2
Year 3: Inclusive Education and Diverse Learners; Digital Technologies in the Classroom; Indigenous Perspectives in Education; Professional Experience Placement 3; LANTITE preparation
Year 4: Curriculum and Pedagogy capstone units; Ethics and Professional Practice; Extended Professional Experience Placement (full-time block)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
Federation's engineering degree runs through its Gippsland campus and lets students choose between Civil, Mechanical, Mining or Electrical and Information Engineering streams, all under a single Engineers Australia-accredited honours degree. The Mining specialisation is worth noting specifically: Gippsland's location near Victoria's brown coal region and the university's long history training engineers for the Latrobe Valley power stations gives that stream an industry pipeline that's harder to replicate at a metro university.

What sets the course structure apart from a lot of engineering degrees is the compulsory 450-hour, 60-day paid industry placement built directly into the credit points rather than treated as an optional add-on students have to hunt down themselves. Federation's careers team has existing relationships with regional engineering firms and utilities, so placement isn't left entirely to the student's own networking.

Core content in the first two years is common across the specialisations (mechanics, materials, thermodynamics, engineering mathematics) before students split into their chosen stream for design-heavy, discipline-specific units. The honours year centres on an independent capstone research or design project, usually tackling a real problem sourced from a regional industry partner rather than a purely academic brief.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Mathematics 1 and 2; Engineering Mechanics; Materials Science; Introduction to Engineering Design; Programming for Engineers
Year 2: Thermodynamics; Fluid Mechanics; Circuit Theory; Engineering Statistics; stream selection (Civil, Mechanical, Mining or Electrical and Information)
Year 3: Discipline-specific design and analysis units (e.g. Structural Analysis for Civil, Machine Design for Mechanical, Mine Ventilation for Mining, Power Systems for Electrical); Paid Industry Placement (60 days / 450 hours)
Year 4 (Honours): Capstone Engineering Project (industry-sourced brief); Engineering Management; Professional Practice and Ethics; advanced electives in chosen stream
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 70-85 for competitive entry (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Environmental and Conservation Science
Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science
Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
Federation doesn't run one generic IT degree; the Bachelor of Information Technology branches into named specialisations (Cybersecurity, Artificial Intelligence and Data Science, and Networking and Security among them) under the same core award, so the actual content a student studies looks quite different depending on which stream they pick after the shared first year of programming, systems fundamentals and networking basics. The Cybersecurity stream in particular has grown quickly given Australia's ongoing skills shortage in the area, and Federation ties it to Federation Co-op, its paid industry placement scheme, which guarantees 60 days of paid work experience built into the degree rather than something students compete for informally.

That paid placement is a genuine differentiator against IT degrees at larger universities where 'industry experience' often means an unpaid capstone project rather than an actual job. Career development units run alongside the technical content across all years, aimed at making sure graduates leave with a portfolio and interview-ready skills, not just transcript knowledge.

Students heading into data-heavy careers gravitate to the AI and Data Science stream, while those interested in the corporate security and incident-response side tend to pick Cybersecurity or Networking and Security. Federation's careers pages promote graduate outcomes including data scientist, cybersecurity analyst, network specialist and software engineer roles.
curriculum:
Year 1: Programming Fundamentals; Introduction to Networks; Database Systems; IT Systems Analysis; Career Development 1
Year 2: Stream specialisation begins (Cybersecurity, AI and Data Science, or Networking and Security core units); Cloud Computing; Software Development Methods; Career Development 2
Year 3: Advanced stream units (e.g. Threat Intelligence and Incident Response for Cybersecurity; Machine Learning for AI/Data Science; Network Security Architecture for Networking); Federation Co-op Paid Industry Placement (60 days); Capstone IT Project
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Federation's nursing degree structures its first year on the standard national calendar but shifts second and third year to start four weeks early, a scheduling quirk that exists specifically so each semester can be cleanly divided into a coursework block followed by a dedicated placement block, rather than trying to run classes and clinical shifts concurrently. It's a small structural detail, but it's the kind of thing that actually shows up in how manageable students find the degree compared to nursing programs that squeeze placement in around a normal teaching timetable.

Students complete 800 hours of supervised clinical placement across roughly 100 days, rotating through acute medical and surgical wards, mental health, aged care and community nursing settings, with placements arranged through Federation's partnerships with Victorian health services (and occasionally placements taken overseas). The university offers both a fully on-campus mode and a blended mode with compulsory on-campus intensive weeks each semester, which has made the course reasonably popular with regional and mature-age students who can't relocate for a fully residential program.

Graduates are eligible to apply for registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, and the degree carries ANMAC accreditation as is standard for Australian nursing programs.
curriculum:
Year 1: Anatomy and Physiology; Foundations of Nursing Practice; Health Assessment; Introduction to Pharmacology; Professional Nursing Practice 1 (early clinical exposure)
Year 2 (early start): Medical-Surgical Nursing 1 and 2; Mental Health Nursing; Pathophysiology; Clinical Placement Block 1 and 2
Year 3 (early start): Aged Care Nursing; Community and Primary Health Nursing; Complex Care Nursing; Leadership in Nursing Practice; Clinical Placement Block 3 and 4 (culminating in a transition-to-practice placement)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, plus health/immunisation checks and (for clinical placements) police check (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0 (typical registration-body bar for nursing/health programs, approximate)

name: Bachelor of Outdoor and Environmental Education
Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
This is Federation's APAC-accredited undergraduate entry point into psychology, available both on-campus and fully online, a mode flexibility that matters because a lot of accredited psychology sequences are campus-only, which shuts out regional and working students who still want the registration pathway. Federation counts 15 core units alongside eight elective units across the degree, with first year covering biological and cognitive psychology, research methods and statistics, the unglamorous but non-negotiable groundwork every accredited psych degree has to include.

What gets covered across the three years spans developmental, cognitive, social, abnormal and personality psychology, giving graduates a genuinely broad base rather than an early narrow specialisation, which fits the reality that Australian psychology training pushes specialisation into postgraduate study rather than undergraduate level. Graduates who want to become registered psychologists need to continue on to an accredited fourth year (Honours or Graduate Diploma) and then either two years of supervised practice or two years of postgraduate study. Federation is explicit about this pathway rather than implying the bachelor's degree alone is a practising qualification, which is a distinction some students don't fully grasp before enrolling.

The online version runs at roughly 10+ hours of study per week, aimed at students balancing work or family commitments who can't attend on campus.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology; Biological Psychology; Cognitive Psychology; Research Methods 1; Statistics for Psychology
Year 2: Developmental Psychology; Social Psychology; Personality Theories; Research Methods 2; elective units
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology; Psychological Assessment; Applied Psychology topics; Research Project; elective units (eight electives total across the degree)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Social Work
description:
Federation's social work degree is one of the newer additions to its Institute portfolio, delivered from Mt Helen and Berwick and built around what the university calls an eco-systems and empowerment approach: framing social problems as sitting across natural, built and social environments rather than treating client issues in isolation. It carries provisional accreditation with the Australian Association of Social Workers, the professional body that ultimately gates registration for graduates wanting to practise.

The standout feature is the sheer volume of placement: 140 days spread across the four years, putting students into real agency settings working with child protection, youth services, mental health, palliative care, and family violence response, under supervision from practising social workers rather than university staff alone. That's a heavier placement load than many comparable degrees and reflects the profession's own accreditation requirements more than a Federation-specific choice, but it does mean graduates arrive at their first job with substantially more direct client-contact hours than a typical undergraduate.

Academically the course threads casework and counselling skills alongside a critical social policy lens: students spend real time on structural causes of disadvantage (housing, income support, colonisation and its ongoing effects on Aboriginal communities) rather than treating social work purely as an individual helping profession.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Social Work; Human Growth and Development; Sociology of Australian Society; Communication Skills for Practice
Year 2: Social Policy and the Welfare State; Case Management and Casework Skills; Working with Diversity and Difference; Field Education Placement 1
Year 3: Mental Health and Social Work Practice; Child, Youth and Family Practice; Research Methods for Social Work; Field Education Placement 2
Year 4: Advanced Practice with Groups and Communities; Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Perspectives; Ethics and Professional Regulation; Field Education Placement 3 (extended block)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Sport, Physical and Outdoor Education
Bachelor of Veterinary and Wildlife Science
Diploma of Business and Sports Management (Higher Education)
Graduate Certificate in Community Energy and Micro-Grid
Graduate Certificate in Social and Community Services
Graduate Certificate of Applied Cyber Security
Graduate Diploma of Applied Cyber Security
Master of Business Administration
description:
Federation's MBA runs out of its Business School with a Ballarat home base but a large international cohort studying the equivalent through Brisbane and offshore partners, and it's built as a 16-unit program rather than the leaner 12-unit MBAs some competitor universities now offer, meaning more coverage but also a longer runway, typically 24 months full-time for international students. Core content covers the standard MBA spine of accounting, finance, HR and marketing, but Federation lets students cross-pick electives from its other postgraduate business degrees (strategic marketing, business economics, entrepreneurship units), so two students can graduate with meaningfully different elective profiles.

The program doesn't chase the case-study prestige model of a G08 MBA; it's positioned more practically, aimed at working professionals and international students looking to build a generalist management credential with a manageable price point relative to Melbourne or Sydney options. A capstone strategy project in the final trimester asks students to work through a real organisational problem, often sourced from a regional Victorian business or the student's own employer.

There's also an MBA (International Business) variant that swaps some electives for trade and cross-cultural management content, reflecting the large proportion of international students who go through the Ballarat and Brisbane campuses.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Managing People and Organisations; Accounting for Managers; Economics for Business Decision Making; Marketing Management
Trimester 2: Corporate Finance; Strategic Management; Business Research Methods; elective (chosen from postgraduate business school offerings)
Trimester 3: Operations and Supply Chain Management; Leadership and Change; elective; elective
Trimester 4: International Business Environment; Entrepreneurship and Innovation; elective
Trimester 5: Capstone Strategy Project; final elective
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Master of Engineering Technology (Renewable Energy and Electrical Power Systems)
Master of Nursing
description:
Federation actually runs several distinct programs under the Master of Nursing banner rather than one single course, and which one a given student ends up in depends heavily on their career goal: a Nurse Practitioner stream built for registered nurses already working clinically who study part-time over two years while continuing in practice, and a Research stream aimed at nurses wanting to complete a substantial thesis (around 40,000 words) under supervision into a nursing-specific problem. The Nurse Practitioner variant was developed with practising nurse practitioners and industry partners, and its content leans heavily into advanced health assessment, diagnostic reasoning and independent prescribing, skills that sit above standard RN scope of practice and require separate endorsement from the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia after graduation.

A standard full-time load is 120 credit points a year, usually four 15-credit units per semester, though the part-time clinical-practitioner cohort typically spreads that over double the calendar time given most are working full-time RN shifts alongside study. Federation also offers a related Master of Health (Advanced Nursing) aimed more at nurse educators than clinicians, which is worth distinguishing from the clinical Master of Nursing pathway for anyone comparing options.

Graduates of the Nurse Practitioner stream come out eligible to apply for NP endorsement, while the research stream is aimed more at academic or policy career paths than direct clinical advancement.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Advanced Health Assessment; Pathophysiology for Advanced Practice; Research Methods in Nursing
Semester 2: Pharmacology and Prescribing; Diagnostic Reasoning; Leadership in Health Systems
Semester 3: Clinical Practicum 1 (supervised, part-time cohort); Evidence-Based Practice
Semester 4: Clinical Practicum 2; Thesis or Major Project (Research stream: approx. 40,000-word thesis; Nurse Practitioner stream: capstone clinical portfolio)
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0 (typical registration-body bar for nursing/health programs, approximate)

name: Master of Technology (Enterprise Systems and Business Analytics)
description:
Federation built this master's for people already working in IT or business who want to move into the systems side of enterprise operations rather than pure software development. The degree leans on real vendor platforms (SAP modules feature heavily, alongside tools from IBM, SAS and Teradata), so assignments involve configuring an actual ERP instance rather than reading about one in a textbook. That vendor exposure is a genuine point of difference: a lot of competing business analytics masters teach the theory of ERP and CRM systems without giving students hands-on time inside them.

The program sits in Federation's School of Engineering, IT and Physical Sciences and is accredited by the Australian Computer Society, which matters for the 485 post-study work visa pathway that many students are here for. Content runs from data warehousing and business intelligence through to supply chain operations and IT project leadership, with a strong emphasis on the 'why' behind enterprise system failures (change management, business process re-engineering, organisational resistance), not just the technical build.

Most students take it over two years full-time, often at Federation's Brisbane campus, and a chunk of the cohort arrives with an unrelated undergraduate degree, since the first-year units are built to bring people up to speed on programming and networking fundamentals before the specialist content starts. The masters project in the final trimester is where most people end up building a portfolio piece for job applications: a working analytics dashboard or a small ERP configuration case study.
curriculum:
Year 1, Trimester 1: Understanding the Digital Revolution; Foundations of Programming; Networking and Security
Year 1, Trimester 2: Enterprise Systems; Big Data and Analytics; Professional Research and Communication
Year 1, Trimester 3: Business Process Analytics and Change; Business Intelligence and Data Warehousing; IT Service Management and Professional Culture
Year 2, Trimester 1: Leadership in IT Project Management; Real-Time Analytics; Supply Chain Operations and Management
Year 2, Trimester 2: IT Professional Engagement (industry-facing capstone unit)
Year 2, Trimester 3: Masters Project
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline, AU or equivalent overseas), approximate default, not program-specific verified.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall (per aggregator cross-check; approximate, not directly page-verified).

name: Associate Degree in Medical Science (Laboratory Medicine)
description: The Associate Degree in Medical Science (Laboratory Medicine) at Flinders University is a two-year full-time qualification that provides practical knowledge and skills for a career in diagnostic pathology as a medical laboratory technician. The program gives accelerated entry into the workforce after two years of study, with laboratory-based teaching and practical experience built in. Students who continue can articulate into the related bachelor degree. Graduates work in diagnostic pathology laboratories across hospital and private settings. Indicative international tuition is around 39,200 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Accounting
description: The Bachelor of Accounting at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree that prepares students for a professional career in accounting. It builds knowledge across financial accounting, management accounting, taxation, audit and business law, and is accredited toward membership of the major Australian professional accounting bodies. Students can study at Bedford Park or the City campus, or online, and have access to practical experience. Graduates work as accountants and financial professionals in public practice, industry and government. Indicative international tuition is around 35,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 058295A.

name: Bachelor of Archaeology
description:
Flinders makes a specific claim worth checking against reality: more field schools in more locations than any other archaeology department in Australia, spanning maritime sites, desert environments and tropical jungle contexts in the same undergraduate program. That's not a small thing for an archaeology degree, where fieldwork access usually depends heavily on which region a university happens to be near - Flinders instead runs students through Indigenous, historical, maritime and world archaeology field survey and excavation as standard parts of the major.

The teaching staff angle is real too - the department includes archaeologists with active international research programs from the Mediterranean to Southeast Asia to Australia's arid interior, so undergraduate teaching draws on current fieldwork rather than textbook case studies alone. Intensive short-course-style topics in human osteology, stone artefact analysis and maritime archaeology lab methods sit alongside the standard lecture/seminar units, giving students specific technical skills that show up directly on a CV.

This is squarely a vocational-leaning humanities degree - the fieldwork intensity is there because employment in archaeology (cultural heritage consultancies, government heritage bodies, museums) runs on demonstrated practical competency more than most humanities fields, and Flinders structures the degree around proving that competency rather than just describing it.
curriculum:
Year 1: introduction to archaeology, world prehistory, foundations of Indigenous archaeology in Australia
Year 2: field survey and excavation methods, historical archaeology, maritime archaeology foundations
Year 3: specialised field schools (choice of Indigenous, historical, maritime or international sites), advanced topics in cultural heritage and the law
Throughout: optional intensive short courses in human osteology, stone artefact analysis, maritime archaeology lab methods
Field schools run across multiple environments - coastal/underwater, arid interior, and international sites
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Arts
description: The Bachelor of Arts at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree that students design around more than twenty majors spanning the humanities and social sciences. Areas of study include history, politics, languages, philosophy, sociology, criminology, English and creative writing, with the flexibility to combine two majors or add a minor. The first year can be studied fully online. The degree develops research, communication, analysis and critical thinking skills valued across the public sector, media, education, community organisations and business. Indicative international tuition is around 31,900 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 002633F.

name: Bachelor of Arts and Science
description: The Bachelor of Arts and Science at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree that lets students study across the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences in a single flexible program. Students combine creative and analytical inquiry, choosing majors and topics from both faculties to build a broad, versatile skill set. The degree suits students with interests that cross traditional discipline boundaries and prepares graduates for careers that value both scientific literacy and strong communication and reasoning. Indicative international tuition is around 38,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 088518J.

name: Bachelor of Behavioural Science (Psychology) (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Behavioural Science (Psychology) (Honours) at Flinders University is a one-year full-time fourth-year program for students who have completed an accredited psychology sequence. Students undertake advanced coursework and a supervised research thesis, developing the research and analytical skills that form part of the path toward registration as a psychologist. Honours also opens entry to higher degree research and to fifth-year professional programs. Graduates work in research, mental health, human resources and policy, or continue toward clinical training. Indicative international tuition is around 33,500 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 017912J.

name: Bachelor of Business (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Business (Honours) at Flinders University is a one-year full-time program for students who have completed a relevant bachelor degree. Students deepen their knowledge in a chosen area of business strategy, leadership and innovation and complete a substantial independent research project, building research design, project management and academic writing skills. Honours opens the pathway to a higher degree by research or PhD and signals to employers the ability to lead a project independently. Graduates move into analyst, strategy and management roles or continue to postgraduate research. Indicative international tuition is around 33,700 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 031353G.

name: Bachelor of Business Analytics
description: The Bachelor of Business Analytics at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree that equips students with artificial intelligence and analytical tools to support business decision making. Through industry-engaged projects and hands-on work with real business data, students build the strategic insight to turn analysis into action. The skills apply across finance, healthcare, IT, government and education in a sector projected to grow strongly over the coming years. Graduates work as business analysts and in related data and insight roles, bridging technical teams and business decision makers. Indicative international tuition is around 38,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 116920G.

name: Bachelor of Clinical Sciences
description: The Bachelor of Clinical Sciences at Flinders University is the first stage of an assured pathway into the Doctor of Medicine, taught over three years full-time. Students build foundational knowledge in the biomedical and clinical sciences alongside early clinical exposure, preparing for graduate-entry medical study. The school-leaver pathway is competitive and leads, on successful completion and meeting progression requirements, into the postgraduate Doctor of Medicine. Graduates continue into medical training toward registration as a medical practitioner. Indicative international tuition is around 58,800 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 080922F.

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description: The Bachelor of Commerce at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree that builds a broad set of work-ready skills for a professional career in private and public enterprise. Students study across areas such as accounting, finance, economics, management and marketing, with the option to specialise, and can study at Bedford Park, the City campus or online. Practical experience is available during the degree. Graduates work across business, finance, government and consulting. Indicative international tuition is around 35,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 002627D.

name: Bachelor of Computer Science
description: The Bachelor of Computer Science at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree that builds skills in programming, data analysis, algorithms and problem solving. Taught at the Tonsley and City campuses, the program combines computing fundamentals with applied project work and the option of practical industry experience. Graduates work as software developers, systems analysts and in related technology roles across industry and government. Indicative international tuition is around 37,600 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 064064K.

name: Bachelor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences (Honours) - 1 Year
description: The Bachelor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences (Honours) at Flinders University is a one-year full-time program for students who have completed a relevant computing, IT or mathematics degree. Students undertake advanced coursework and a hands-on research project, learning to plan, execute and communicate a major thesis while developing data-driven modelling, coding and experimentation skills. The year prepares graduates for PhD study, research and development careers, or technical leadership roles in industry. Indicative international tuition is around 43,600 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 118384K.

name: Bachelor of Creative Arts (Fashion) VET Entry
description: This is the VET-entry pathway into the Bachelor of Creative Arts (Fashion) at Flinders University, for applicants who have completed an Advanced Diploma in applied fashion design, fashion and textiles merchandising or a related field. With advanced standing, students complete the degree in around one and a half years, studying core topics in the Adelaide CBD across the Adelaide College of the Arts, TAFE SA and the Flinders City campus. Graduates are prepared for professional roles across fashion design, production and related industries. Indicative international tuition is around 63,700 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 091846M.

name: Bachelor of Creative Arts (Honours) 1 year
description: The Bachelor of Creative Arts (Honours) at Flinders University is a one-year full-time program in which students undertake a major creative project or creative research project of their choice under the guidance of accomplished practitioners. Study programs are available for writers, dancers, digital and visual effects designers, fashion designers, filmmakers, producers, directors, actors, photographers and visual artists. The honours year develops critical analysis, research and presentation skills that help graduates take their artistic practice further or continue to postgraduate research. Indicative international tuition is around 30,500 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Creative Writing
description: The Bachelor of Creative Writing at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree taught at the Bedford Park campus for students who want to write across fiction, non-fiction, poetry, screen and other forms. The program combines workshops, craft study and practical experience, and shares pathways with the Bachelor of Arts and the Diploma in Arts. Graduates prepare for work as authors, editors, researchers, writers and publishers, and for further study. Indicative international tuition is around 37,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 119232G.

name: Bachelor of Criminology
description: The Bachelor of Criminology at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree covering crime prevention, law enforcement, criminal justice, and the social and policy context of crime. Taught at Bedford Park and the City campus, the program combines criminological theory with applied study and access to practical experience. Graduates work in policing, corrections, courts, policy, community services and research. Indicative international tuition is around 31,900 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 092879E.

name: Bachelor of Criminology (Honours) - 4 year direct entry
description: The Bachelor of Criminology (Honours) at Flinders University is a four-year full-time direct-entry degree that combines the criminology major with an honours research year. Students examine the causes and consequences of crime and the operation of justice systems, and develop advanced analytical, research and project management skills. In the final year students complete a major research thesis with an expert supervisor. Graduates work in justice, policy, research and social change roles. Indicative international tuition is around 32,600 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 096843G.

name: Bachelor of Cybersecurity
description: The Bachelor of Cybersecurity at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree that builds a strong foundation in computing, networking and information security, then lets students specialise in areas such as cloud security and applied cryptography. Students can complete an industry placement before finishing, and the degree is part of Flinders' degree-based apprenticeship program, allowing some students to earn while they learn. Graduates work protecting the digital systems that businesses and communities rely on. Indicative international tuition is around 46,700 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 121084G.

name: Bachelor of Disability and Community Inclusion
description: The Bachelor of Disability and Community Inclusion at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree that prepares graduates to work as skilled practitioners supporting people with disability and promoting inclusion in the community. Students study across Bedford Park and the City campus, with pathways available from related diplomas and associate degrees, and options to specialise further in postgraduate study. Graduates work in disability services, community organisations, advocacy and the National Disability Insurance Scheme sector. Indicative international tuition is around 40,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 102685F.

name: Bachelor of Disability and Developmental Education
description: The Bachelor of Disability and Developmental Education at Flinders University is a four-year full-time accredited degree that prepares graduates to work as developmental educators supporting people with disability across the lifespan. The program combines coursework in inclusive practice, health and human development with substantial supervised placements. Pathways are available from related diplomas and associate degrees, and the degree can be studied at Bedford Park or online. Graduates work as developmental educators in disability, health and community services. Indicative international tuition is around 41,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 058482J.

name: Bachelor of Early Childhood Education - Birth to 5
description: The Bachelor of Early Childhood Education (Birth to 5) at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree that qualifies graduates to teach in early childhood settings for children from birth to five years. Students study child development, curriculum and pedagogy alongside supervised professional experience in centres and preschools. Entry requires a strong academic record and an IELTS overall score of 7.0. Graduates work as early childhood teachers in long day care, kindergarten and preschool settings. Indicative international tuition is around 35,600 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 116862A.

name: Bachelor of Early Childhood Education - Birth to 8
description: The Bachelor of Early Childhood Education (Birth to 8) at Flinders University is a four-year full-time initial teacher education degree that qualifies graduates to teach across early childhood and the early primary years. Students study curriculum, child development and pedagogy with hands-on professional experience placements, graduating career-ready. Entry requires a strong academic record and an IELTS overall score of 7.0. Graduates work as registered teachers in early childhood settings and the early years of primary school. Indicative international tuition is around 33,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 107184J.

name: Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description:
A minimum of 80 days of professional experience placement across four years is the load-bearing feature of this degree, structured as escalating blocks - a Year 1 placement, then Year 2A and 2B placements, then a final assessment placement in the fourth year - each one building toward the classroom competencies the Teachers Registration Board actually checks for. Students need a Child-Related Employment Screening cleared before their very first placement in first semester, which tells you how early the practical component starts relative to the classroom coursework.

Before the professional experience topics can be undertaken, students also have to clear the national Literacy and Numeracy Test for Initial Teacher Education Students (LANTITE) - a requirement that trips up a nontrivial number of otherwise strong students each year, so it's factored into the course structure rather than left as an afterthought. At 144 units over four years, this is a longer undergraduate degree than most, reflecting both the academic content and the placement hours needed for teacher registration.

The R-7 (Reception to Year 7) scope means graduates are prepared specifically for primary schooling rather than a K-12 generalist qualification, and Flinders positions the placements across a genuine variety of primary school settings rather than concentrating them at one or two partner schools.
curriculum:
Year 1: foundations of primary education, child development, curriculum studies, Professional Experience Year 1 placement
Year 2: literacy and numeracy pedagogy, inclusive education, Professional Experience Year 2A and 2B placements
Year 3: curriculum specialisation units (science, humanities, arts education), LANTITE requirement to be cleared before continuing to placements
Year 4: advanced pedagogy and assessment, Professional Experience Final Assessment placement
144 units total; minimum 80 days of professional experience across the degree; Child-Related Employment Screening required before first placement
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
Anyone unsure which branch of engineering suits them can start the Flexible Entry version of this degree and pick a specialisation after a shared first year of core engineering fundamentals - materials, mechanics, programming, mathematics, design and electronics. That's a genuine hedge against the common problem of 18-year-olds locking into Civil or Mechanical before they've had any real exposure to either.

Flinders offers accredited engineering across an unusually wide spread for a mid-sized Australian university - Biomedical, Civil, Electrical and Electronic, Environmental, Maritime, Mechanical, Nuclear, Robotics and Software - and the Mechanical stream in particular lets students specialise further into areas like Electro Mechanical Systems, Materials Engineering, Maritime Engineering or Advanced Manufacturing and Digital Design. Civil students similarly choose among Civil Infrastructure, Environmental Engineering, Structural Engineering or Transport Systems Engineering majors.

The honours designation isn't a bolt-on extra year here - it's built into the four-year degree from the start, which lines up with Engineers Australia accreditation requirements and means graduates don't need to complete a separate honours program to hit the professional threshold most employers and further study pathways expect.
curriculum:
Year 1: shared engineering core - engineering mathematics, mechanics, materials, introductory programming, engineering design, electronics fundamentals
Year 2: specialisation begins - discipline-specific core units (e.g. thermodynamics and fluid mechanics for Mechanical; structures and geotechnics for Civil)
Year 3: advanced discipline units, major selection within specialisation (e.g. Transport Systems Engineering major within Civil, or Advanced Manufacturing within Mechanical)
Year 4: capstone engineering project/thesis, professional practice topics, industry-based project work
Four-year integrated honours structure, Engineers Australia accredited across all specialisations
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 70-85 for competitive entry (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) Flexible Entry
description: The Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) Flexible Entry at Flinders University lets students start a four-year accredited engineering degree without committing to a specialisation in first year. Students build core engineering skills and choose their major later from areas including civil, mechanical, electrical and electronic, biomedical, robotics, software and environmental engineering. Teaching is at the Tonsley and City campuses with access to practical experience. Graduates are prepared for professional engineering practice and eligible for professional accreditation. Indicative international tuition is around 41,700 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 093042J.

name: Bachelor of Engineering Science
description: The Bachelor of Engineering Science at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree that builds foundations in mathematics, physics, programming and design before students specialise in a major such as biomedical, civil, electrical and electronic, mechanical, sustainability, or design and user experience. Taught at the Tonsley and City campuses, it prepares graduates for entry-level technical roles and provides a transfer pathway into an accredited Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) program. Indicative international tuition is around 40,800 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Engineering Technology (Advanced Manufacturing and Digital Design)
description: The Bachelor of Engineering Technology (Advanced Manufacturing and Digital Design) at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree built with substantial industry input. Students learn the fundamentals and practical application of advanced manufacturing, digital design and Industry 4.0 techniques, and can specialise in advanced manufacturing with mechanical, electrical and electronic, or robotics engineering. The degree targets skills used in automated industrial production and smart factory settings. Graduates work in manufacturing, automation and digital design roles. Indicative international tuition is around 42,800 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 110754J.

name: Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science
description: The Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree focused on improving health and human performance through evidence-based practice. Students combine study of exercise physiology, biomechanics, motor control and strength and conditioning with hands-on learning and industry placements. The degree provides a pathway into the Master of Clinical Exercise Physiology. Graduates work in sport, fitness, corporate health and community programs, and can continue toward accreditation as exercise physiologists. Indicative international tuition is around 40,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 091862M.

name: Bachelor of Film and Television (Screen Industries)
description: The Bachelor of Film and Television (Screen Industries) at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree in which students create a television pilot, build hands-on production skills and graduate with a professional portfolio. The program covers screen production across development, production and post-production, taught at the Bedford Park campus with access to practical experience. Graduates work across the screen industries in production, post-production and content roles. Indicative international tuition is around 37,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 119233F.

name: Bachelor of Finance and Business Economics
Bachelor of Game Design
description: The Bachelor of Game Design at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree for students who want to build a career making games. Taught at the City campus, it combines game design, production and technical skills with portfolio development, and entry includes a portfolio, CV and written statement. Pathways are available from the Bachelor of Information Technology (Game Development) and from arts diplomas. Graduates work as game designers and in related roles across the games and interactive media industry. Indicative international tuition is around 37,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 118383M.

name: Bachelor of Geospatial Information Systems
description: The Bachelor of Geospatial Information Systems at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree that blends science, technology and spatial analysis. Students learn to capture and analyse geographic data from drones, satellites and mapping software and apply it to challenges in environment, urban growth, defence and disaster response, with hands-on projects and fieldwork. Graduates work as GIS analysts and spatial scientists across government, environmental, planning and defence sectors. Indicative international tuition is around 37,600 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 110618F.

name: Bachelor of Health Sciences
description:
The pitch for Flinders University's Bachelor of Health Sciences is flexibility: pick a full major in one health discipline, or split your electives across a major and two minors, choosing from areas as varied as Ageing, Health Management, Health Promotion, Digital Health, Physiology and Neuroscience, Psychology, and Therapy Studies. First year is common across the degree, so the actual specialisation decision doesn't have to be made until students have had a semester or two of exposure to the different areas.

That breadth suits people aiming at health system roles that aren't clinical practice itself - health promotion officers, program coordinators, policy and management roles - rather than students who already know they want to be a nurse or physiotherapist and would be better served by a direct-entry professional degree. At 108 units it's a standard three-year Bachelor of Science-equivalent load, with an optional fourth honours year available for students who want to build research skills before going on to postgraduate study.

Because the major/minor combination is genuinely open, the degree ends up serving two different student populations under one name: those using it as a stepping stone into postgraduate clinical training (nutrition, psychology, public health), and those treating the combination itself as the career-ready qualification, particularly in health promotion and management.
curriculum:
Year 1: common health sciences core - human biology, health systems, introduction to health promotion, foundations of research methods
Year 2: major/minor selection begins - discipline-specific units in chosen area(s) such as Health Promotion, Health Management, Ageing, or Physiology & Neuroscience
Year 3: advanced major units, applied project or work-integrated learning placement relevant to chosen specialisation
Optional Year 4 (Honours): independent research thesis plus advanced seminars
108 units for the pass degree; major-and-two-minors or single specialisation structure available
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Human Nutrition
description: The Bachelor of Human Nutrition at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree that explores the links between diet, health and disease prevention through evidence-based practice. Students study nutrition science, public health nutrition and food across the lifespan, with access to practical experience. It provides a pathway toward the Master of Nutrition and Dietetics for students who want to become accredited practising dietitians. Graduates work in community and public health nutrition, food industry and health promotion roles. Indicative international tuition is around 39,700 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 069219M.

name: Bachelor of Inclusive and Specialised Education (Early Childhood)
description: The Bachelor of Inclusive and Specialised Education (Early Childhood) at Flinders University is a four-year full-time initial teacher education degree that prepares graduates to teach students with diverse learning needs, while also qualifying them to teach in general early childhood and primary settings. Students study inclusive pedagogy, child development and curriculum alongside supervised professional experience. Inclusive education is a recognised growth area with teacher shortages across early childhood and primary. Graduates work as registered teachers with a specialist inclusive education focus. Indicative international tuition is around 33,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 117254F.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description: The Bachelor of Information Technology at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree designed with industry, so graduates leave with practical project experience and industry certifications. Students build skills across software development, cybersecurity, cloud and enterprise systems, with strong demand for IT graduates nationally. The degree prepares students for public and private sector technology roles or to launch their own venture. Graduates work as software developers, systems analysts and in related technology roles. Indicative international tuition is around 37,600 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 020067D.

name: Bachelor of International Relations and Political Science
description: The Bachelor of International Relations and Political Science at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree covering global political challenges from climate diplomacy and national security to human rights, inequality and modern warfare. Students develop the skills to analyse and influence complex issues in Australia and internationally, with access to internships including placements in Washington, Vienna and the South Australian Parliament. Graduates work in policy, advocacy, government, diplomacy and international organisations. Indicative international tuition is around 31,900 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of International Relations and Political Science (Honours) - 4 year direct entry
description: The Bachelor of International Relations and Political Science (Honours) at Flinders University is a four-year full-time direct-entry degree that combines the standard major with an honours research year. Students deepen their analysis of international systems, public policy and political theory and develop advanced research, communication and project management skills. In the fourth year students complete a major research thesis with an expert supervisor. Graduates are positioned for leadership, academic and policy-focused roles in Australia and internationally. Indicative international tuition is around 32,600 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 102682J.

name: Bachelor of International Relations and Political Science (Honours) 1 year
description: The Bachelor of International Relations and Political Science (Honours) at Flinders University is a one-year full-time program for students who have completed a relevant bachelor degree. Students undertake advanced coursework in their area of specialisation and complete a substantial independent research thesis, building research design, project management and academic writing skills. Honours opens the pathway to a higher degree by research or PhD and signals to employers the ability to work independently on a complex project. Graduates work in government, policy, research and international organisations. Indicative international tuition is around 30,500 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Languages
description: The Bachelor of Languages at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree taught at the Bedford Park campus for students preparing for a global career. Students develop advanced proficiency in one or more languages alongside study of culture, translation and intercultural communication, with study abroad opportunities available. Graduates work in translation and interpreting, international business, diplomacy, education and community services. Indicative international tuition is around 31,900 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 069017K.

name: Bachelor of Laws (Honours)
description:
Fourth year is where this degree earns its "Honours" label - a dissertation plus three option topics, at least half of which have to be taken at honours or masters level, which is a meaningfully heavier research load than a standard three-year law degree tacks on. The option list itself skews toward areas Flinders' law school has built genuine research strength in: health law and medical negligence, technology law covering AI and data protection, plus the usual family, IP, insolvency and human rights options.

Clinical legal education runs through the Flinders Legal Advice Clinic, which gives students actual client-facing experience rather than purely simulated advocacy exercises, and there are separate work-integrated learning placements available for students who want supervised time in a legal practice setting before graduating. That combination - real clinic work plus optional practice placements - matters for graduates aiming at admission to practice, since it builds practical competency alongside the required units.

At 90 compulsory units plus the honours dissertation and options, this is a substantial four-year commitment, and the health law and technology law strands in particular reflect where Flinders has positioned its research and teaching focus relative to other South Australian law schools.
curriculum:
Years 1-3: 90 units of compulsory law topics - contracts, torts, criminal law, constitutional law, property, equity, evidence, civil and criminal procedure
Year 3-4: clinical legal education through the Flinders Legal Advice Clinic; optional work-integrated learning placement
Year 4: honours dissertation (13.5 units) plus three option topics (22.5 units minimum at honours/masters level) chosen from areas including Health Law, Technology Law, Family Law, Intellectual Property, International Human Rights, Insolvency Law
Total: 90 compulsory units + dissertation + 40.5 units of options
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 70-85 for competitive entry (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Laws and Legal Practice
description: The Bachelor of Laws and Legal Practice at Flinders University is a law degree with a future-focused curriculum and hands-on legal experience built in from first year. Students can graduate in three and a half years with direct entry into the Graduate Diploma in Legal Practice, and can combine law with criminology, international relations and political science, or business. International placement opportunities include Mongolia, Washington, Vienna and Parliament. Graduates are prepared for admission to practise and for careers in areas such as human rights, environmental law and family law. Indicative international tuition is around 38,000 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Mathematical Sciences
description: The Bachelor of Mathematical Sciences at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree with majors in mathematics, data science or physics, complemented by minors such as coding, climate change or water resources. Students gain hands-on experience through projects and work-integrated learning placements, and high-achieving students can continue with honours in computing and mathematical sciences. Graduates work in data, finance, research, modelling and analytics roles. Indicative international tuition is around 38,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 075594D.

name: Bachelor of Media and Communication
description: The Bachelor of Media and Communication at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree designed with industry input and a digital focus. Students study across areas such as digital content, journalism, public relations, screen and strategic communication, with access to practical experience and study abroad. Teaching is at the City and Bedford Park campuses. Graduates work in content production, communications, public relations, journalism and marketing roles. Indicative international tuition is around 31,900 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 098433J.

name: Bachelor of Medical Science
description: The Bachelor of Medical Science at Flinders University is a three-year full-time degree exploring the human body through biochemistry, molecular biology, physiology and related fields, with an emphasis on evidence-based knowledge and laboratory skills. It prepares graduates for careers in health research, diagnostics and industry, and provides a pathway toward graduate-entry health and medical programs. Graduates work as medical scientists in research institutes, government, diagnostic laboratories and the pharmaceutical sector. Indicative international tuition is around 38,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 028940C.

name: Bachelor of Medical Science (Honours) - 4 years
description: The Bachelor of Medical Science (Honours) at Flinders University is a four-year full-time degree that combines the medical science curriculum with a substantial individual research project bridging theory and practice. Over four years students deepen their scientific understanding and analytical skills and complete a supervised thesis. Graduates find opportunities in medical research at universities and government and industry-funded organisations, in the pharmaceutical sector, and in diagnostics, or continue to PhD study. Indicative international tuition is around 41,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 113274A.

name: Bachelor of Midwifery
description: The Bachelor of Midwifery at Flinders University is a three-year full-time pre-registration degree with hands-on clinical experience and modern simulation facilities. Students study across Bedford Park and the City campus, with an IELTS overall requirement of 7.0. Supervised clinical placement is a central part of the program, preparing graduates for registration as midwives. Graduates work as registered midwives in hospital and community maternity settings. Indicative international tuition is around 38,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 039814G.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Eight hundred hours of clinical placement is the number that defines this degree - it's the minimum required for graduates to register as a nurse, and Flinders builds it in across hospitals, community health centres and specialised care units rather than front-loading or back-loading it into one block. The university guarantees placements within South Australia, which removes one of the bigger logistical headaches nursing students elsewhere sometimes face.
