Graduates work as electronics engineers, network and systems engineers, robotics engineers and telecommunications engineers across communications, defence, medical technology and public administration. Indicative international tuition is around A$48,200 per year.

name: Master of Engineering (by Research) Computer Systems, Biomedical
Master of Engineering Management
description: La Trobe's Master of Engineering Management is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree that adds commercial and leadership capability to an engineering qualification. Students take management, innovation and sustainability subjects designed for engineers, plus a business foundation in marketing, finance, organisational behaviour and business data analysis. The second year moves into risk and cost management, project management, strategic management and computer-aided engineering, and students deepen one engineering specialisation chosen from twelve disciplines. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Graduates move into engineering project management and technical leadership roles across manufacturing, technology, telecommunications, geotechnical, government and construction. Indicative international tuition is around A$50,000 per year; confirm the current figure on the La Trobe course page.

name: Master of Health Administration
description: La Trobe's Master of Health Administration is a 240-credit-point degree, two years full-time, taught at the City campus in Melbourne, with a 1.5-year pathway for graduates who hold a health bachelor and are eligible for AHPRA registration. It builds the skills to lead and manage health agencies, services and programs, in general management and in specialist areas such as project management and quality management, and students choose one of seven specialisations including health strategy and policy, digital health, health promotion and public health. The teaching staff hold clinical qualifications and have worked in senior healthcare management roles in Australia and overseas. The degree is accredited by the Australasian College of Health Service Management. Entry is a three-year bachelor degree, with IELTS 6.5 and no band below 6.0. Graduates take senior management roles across public and private healthcare, at organisations such as Northern Health, Western Health and Cancer Council Victoria. Indicative international tuition is around A$44,200 per year.

name: Master of Health Information Management
description: The Master of Health Information Management at La Trobe University combines the clinical and business sides of healthcare, using data to improve the quality of patient care. Students hone skills in clinical classification, data analytics, health informatics, health systems and workforce management, and complete placements in healthcare agencies. The program covers implementing and managing health information systems in the context of cybersecurity, identifier and interoperability requirements, and analysing health data for safety and quality reporting. Graduates step into senior roles across hospitals, health insurers, health technology companies and government agencies.

name: Master of Information and Communication Technology
Master of Information Technology
description:
La Trobe's Master of IT runs on a 240 credit point, two-year structure by default, but drops to 180 points and 18 months for anyone entering with a cognate Australian bachelor's degree in computer science, IT or information systems, a meaningful shortcut that a lot of applicants coming from a non-technical undergraduate background don't get. Foundational subjects in database logic, programming, network engineering and cybersecurity run early, with entrepreneurship and project management folded in as transferable skills rather than treated as an afterthought elective.

Where the degree earns its ACS accreditation is in the specialisation list, which reaches further than a typical Australian IT masters: artificial intelligence, cloud analytics, cybersecurity, Internet of Things, networking, software engineering, and, less commonly offered, quantum information technology. That last one reflects La Trobe's investment in quantum computing research at its Bundoora campus rather than being a token addition to a course list.
curriculum:
Foundational subjects: Database Logic and Data Structures, Programming, Network Engineering, Cybersecurity Fundamentals
Professional skills subjects: Professional Practice, Project Management, Entrepreneurship in IT
Specialisation (choose one): Artificial Intelligence, Cloud Analytics, Cybersecurity, Internet of Things, Networking, Quantum Information Technology, or Software Engineering
Elective subjects to complete the credit point total
Capstone project or industry-based subject in final year
240 credit points over 2 years standard; 180 credit points/18 months for cognate-entry applicants
ACS-accredited
admission_requirements: Australian bachelor's degree (or equivalent), 240cp/2yr pathway (any discipline), or 180cp/1.5yr pathway (cognate: computer science, IT, or information systems).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Logistics and Supply Chain Management
description: La Trobe's Master of Logistics and Supply Chain Management is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree, designed with industry, that reduces to 1.5 years with recognised prior study. Students get direct exposure to the sector through field trips to ports and distribution centres, guest lectures and optional industry placements, and study emerging technology in the field including AI, blockchain, the Internet of Things, cybersecurity governance and applied data analytics, alongside circular economy and carbon accountability practices. Entry is a bachelor degree in any discipline, or completion of La Trobe's Postgraduate Qualifying Program. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Graduates work as procurement, supply chain and operations managers and as logistics consultants across transport, government, manufacturing and not-for-profit organisations. Indicative international tuition is around A$49,000 per year.

name: Master of Manufacturing Engineering
description: La Trobe's Master of Manufacturing Engineering is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree, accredited by Engineers Australia and designed with industry leaders, that blends engineering knowledge with business skills. Students build proficiency in system design, materials processing and sustainable engineering while working with AI, robotics and machine learning, and add enterprise skills in consultation, negotiation, and risk and project management. An 800-hour work-integrated learning placement is available. Entry is a four-year bachelor degree in manufacturing engineering or a related field, or a Sydney Accord accredited three-year Bachelor of Technology. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Graduates work as manufacturing, design and process engineers, product designers, defence contractors and supply chain managers, in research, design development, quality assurance and logistics. Indicative international tuition is around A$48,200 per year.

name: Master of Nursing
description: La Trobe's Master of Nursing is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree for people who are already registered nurses. Clinical specialisations, done in hospital settings with health partners, include acute care, critical care, cardiac care, perioperative practice, neonatal care and medical imaging; non-clinical specialisations build research, leadership and health management expertise. Delivery is blended, with face-to-face or fully online options. Entry is a recognised nursing degree equivalent to an Australian bachelor; clinical specialisations require current registration, and international applicants are not held to the Australian practising-certificate requirement for the non-clinical pathway. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Graduates work as clinical nurse specialists and managers, nurse educators, nurse researchers and directors of nursing. Indicative international tuition is around A$41,600 per year.

name: Master of Nursing Practice
description: La Trobe's Master of Nursing Practice is a two-year, 240-credit-point pre-registration degree that qualifies people with a bachelor degree in any discipline to become registered nurses, whether upskilling or changing careers. It is taught through the La Trobe Rural Health School, with theory from clinicians and academics and 800 hours of clinical placement in regional and rural hospitals and health services. Study covers primary care, acute care, chronic illness, Indigenous health and mental health. The degree is accredited by the Australian Nursing and Midwifery Accreditation Council, and graduates may be eligible for registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. IELTS 7.0 with no band below 7.0. Graduates work as registered nurses across acute, subacute, primary and community health and aged care. Indicative international tuition is around A$47,600 per year.

name: Master of Nursing Science
description:
The Master of Nursing Science is La Trobe's postgraduate pathway for registered nurses seeking a specialist clinical qualification rather than a management-focused credential. Students typically move into specialisations like perioperative nursing, primary health care, or mental health nursing, drawing on La Trobe's clinical partnerships including its affiliated clinical school arrangement with Austin Health in Melbourne's north-east.

Because candidates already hold RN registration, the degree assumes a working clinical base and builds advanced practice knowledge and research skills on top of it, rather than repeating undergraduate nursing content. Part-time study while continuing to work clinically is the norm rather than the exception, and the course structure accommodates that with a mix of online coursework and clinically-oriented practicum or advanced placement components tied to the chosen specialisation.
curriculum:
Core subjects: Advanced Nursing Practice, Research Methods in Health Sciences, Evidence-Based Practice, Health Care Ethics and Policy
Specialisation stream (choose one): Perioperative Nursing, Primary Health Care, or Mental Health Nursing
Advanced clinical/practicum component tied to chosen specialisation
Elective subjects to complete the degree
Research project or minor thesis in final stage
Delivered via clinical partner network including La Trobe's affiliation with Austin Health
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a health-related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Occupational Therapy Practice
description: La Trobe's Master of Occupational Therapy Practice is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree open to graduates from any undergraduate discipline, with a weighted average mark of at least 65 percent. It combines coursework in assessment and intervention, the therapeutic use of occupation and the adaptation of environments with 1000 hours of placement, structured as a six-week block in the first year and two eight-week blocks plus a ten-week project-based placement in the second. The degree is accredited by the Occupational Therapy Council of Australia and approved by the Occupational Therapy Board of Australia and the World Federation of Occupational Therapists. Graduates work in general hospitals, private practice, rehabilitation centres, and community and mental health services. Indicative international tuition is around A$53,000 per year.

name: Master of Philosophy (High Cost)
description: The Master of Philosophy at La Trobe University is an internationally recognised master's by research degree designed for students to develop advanced skills in independent and sustained research. Each candidate undertakes a supervised research project on a topic in their discipline, culminating in a thesis of up to 50,000 words or its practice-based equivalent that makes an independent contribution to existing scholarship. The qualification is recognised at Australian Qualifications Framework Level 9. Some research areas attract a higher fee and require a different course code. Graduates are prepared for a PhD or research-focused employment.

name: Master of Physiotherapy Practice
description: La Trobe's Master of Physiotherapy Practice is a two-year, 255-credit-point degree that qualifies graduates to work as physiotherapists, assessing and treating movement disorders and musculoskeletal, neurological and cardiorespiratory conditions using exercise prescription, manual therapy and patient education. It is accredited by the Australian Physiotherapy Council. Entry is a bachelor degree completed in the last five years that includes tertiary subjects in musculoskeletal anatomy and human physiology, and international applicants submit a prerequisite information form. Graduates work in private practice, hospitals, rehabilitation and community health centres, industrial and specialist clinics, and in ergonomics and clinical research. Indicative international tuition is around A$60,400 per year for a full-time year.

name: Master of Professional Engineering
description: La Trobe's Master of Professional Engineering is a one-year, 120-credit-point degree that offers a fast track to an Australian engineering career for people who already hold an accredited engineering bachelor degree. Co-designed with industry partners including Siemens, John Holland and Acciona, it blends on-campus and online learning with hands-on experience at engineering companies, and covers sustainable engineering practice in Australia alongside project management and leadership. Entry is a Washington Accord accredited four-year Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) or an equivalent assessed by Engineers Australia. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Graduates move into engineering management, project leadership and strategic planning roles across energy and resources, construction, infrastructure, manufacturing and transport. Indicative international tuition is around A$49,200 per year.

name: Master of Psychological Science
description: La Trobe's Master of Psychological Science, now titled Master of Psychological Science (Research), is a two-year full-time degree by research rather than a coursework program. Students complete an independent research project supervised within the School of Psychology and Public Health, in areas that include autism spectrum disorders, clinical and health psychology, behavioural neuroscience and neuropsychology, cognitive and developmental psychology, and social and intercultural psychology. It is a masters degree by research at AQF level 9 and can serve as a pathway toward a PhD. Entry is a Bachelor of Psychological Science with honours completed within the last ten years, with a weighted average mark of 70 or above, and the school must be able to supervise the chosen research area. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Indicative international tuition is around A$46,200 per full-time year. Note that this is a research training program, not a professional or registration qualification.

name: Master of Public Health
description: La Trobe's Master of Public Health is a 240-credit-point degree, two years full-time, taught at the City campus in Melbourne, online, or in Sydney, with a 1.5-year pathway for graduates who hold a cognate health bachelor plus two years of relevant work experience. No health background is required for the standard entry. Core study builds foundations in systems thinking, epidemiology, health policy and research methods, and how to gather, interpret and use health data, and students choose one of seven specialisations including health promotion, health management, health strategy and policy, digital health, and ageing strategy and policy. Entry is a three-year bachelor degree, with IELTS 6.5 and no band below 6.0. Graduates work as policy officers, health project managers, and in health promotion and epidemiology roles across government, the private sector and community organisations. Indicative international tuition is around A$44,200 per year.

name: Master of Rehabilitation Counselling and Mental Health
Master of Science
description: The Master of Science at La Trobe University is a master's by research degree that requires students to deepen their knowledge of their discipline and develop advanced skills in independent and sustained research. Candidates undertake a supervised research project that culminates in the submission of a thesis for examination, demonstrating an advanced and integrated understanding of a complex body of knowledge in one or more disciplines. The qualification is recognised at Australian Qualifications Framework Level 9, and graduates pursue careers across the technology, public health and pharmaceutical sectors or continue to a PhD.

name: Master of Social Work (Research)
description: The Master of Social Work (Research) at La Trobe University requires students to complete a research program in social work, attend research seminars and submit a thesis on an approved subject. Areas of study include social work practice, social policy, intellectual disability, ageing, child and family welfare, health and mental health. The qualification is recognised at Australian Qualifications Framework Level 9. The degree prepares graduates for a professional career in industry, academic research or higher education, and can serve as a pathway into a PhD.

name: Master of Speech Pathology
description: La Trobe's Master of Speech Pathology is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree that qualifies graduates to work as speech pathologists, supporting people with communication and swallowing needs. Study covers observation in everyday settings, assessment, interpreting clinical data and developing interventions, taught through clinical workshops, guided demonstrations, simulation and supervised work with clients. The degree is accredited by Speech Pathology Australia, and graduates may apply for membership. Entry is a completed bachelor degree, with IELTS 7.5 overall and no band below 7.0. Graduates work in hospitals, community health centres, private practice, schools, rehabilitation and aged care, and in health promotion, teaching and consulting. Indicative international tuition is around A$54,600 per year.

name: Master of Sport Analytics
description: La Trobe's Master of Sport Analytics is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree that applies data, statistics and artificial intelligence to performance and decision-making in sport. Students build foundations in probability, statistics and analytical methods, then apply machine learning, large language models and generative AI to performance analysis, talent identification, injury management and fan engagement, working with industry-standard tools including R, Python and SQL. Entry is a bachelor degree in any discipline, with relevant work experience also considered. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Graduates work as sport analysts, performance analysts, game analysts and data scientists with clubs, sporting bodies and analytics providers. Indicative international tuition is around A$43,400 per year.

name: Master of Teaching (Primary)
description: La Trobe's Master of Teaching (Primary) is a two-year, 240-credit-point initial teacher education degree, with a 1.5-year accelerated option, that qualifies graduates to teach in primary schools. It combines practical and evidence-based coursework with extensive supervised in-school placement, and is accredited by the Victorian Institute of Teaching across most campuses. Entry is a completed bachelor degree with relevant content; applicants from countries where English is not the main language of instruction need IELTS 7.0 overall with no band below 7.0 and at least 7.5 in speaking and listening. Graduates work as primary school teachers in Australia and overseas, and in community education and non-traditional learning settings. Indicative international tuition is around A$41,600 per year.

name: Bachelor of Actuarial Studies
description:
Actuarial studies at Macquarie is built directly against the Actuaries Institute's exemption framework rather than as a general quantitative degree that happens to touch on actuarial topics. Strong performance in the relevant units can earn exemptions from the Institute's Foundation Program subjects (CM1, CM2, CS1, CS2, CB1, CB2) and the Actuary Program's ACC and DSP subjects, which shortens the professional qualification path students face after graduation, a meaningful head start given how long the full actuarial credentialing process typically takes on top of any degree.

The department has also been recognised as a Center of Actuarial Excellence by the US-based Society of Actuaries, a status held by a limited number of programs globally, which gives the degree standing for students who might end up working in US, UK or Asian insurance and superannuation markets rather than only the Australian one. Macquarie Business School's AACSB accreditation applies here too, on top of the actuarial-specific recognition.

Students completing the degree as part of a double degree, paired with Applied Finance, Science, or Information Technology, and achieving credit or higher in the relevant units become eligible for exemptions from both the Foundation and Actuary Program subjects, which is one reason the actuarial-plus-finance or actuarial-plus-IT combination shows up so often among Macquarie's actuarial cohort rather than students taking the single degree alone.
curriculum:
Core sequence: mathematics for actuarial studies, probability and statistics, life contingencies, financial mathematics, actuarial modelling, economics for actuaries, actuarial statistics
Advanced units: risk theory, general insurance, financial risk management, investment and asset modelling
Accreditation: recognised by the Actuaries Institute, with exemption eligibility for Foundation Program subjects CM1, CM2, CS1, CS2, CB1, CB2 and Actuary Program subjects ACC, DSP
Recognition: Department of Actuarial Studies and Business Analytics holds Center of Actuarial Excellence status from the Society of Actuaries (US)
Structure: 3 years full-time; frequently combined as a double degree with Applied Finance, Science or Information Technology
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion with strong mathematics; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Advanced Information Technology
description: The Bachelor of Advanced Information Technology provides graduates with the necessary skills to pursue a career in Information Technology. A foundation of programming, data, networking and cyber security provides a solid base for later study. The majors focus on important current areas of Information Technology. Any pair of majors can be taken as a double major combination. Electives and flexible unit choice allow the majors to be complemented by more Information Technology study or by units from other disciplines. The emphasis in all majors is on concepts, insights and skills that enable graduates to use current technologies and to also evaluate and adapt to new technologies as they emerge. Central to the learning of the conceptual material is extensive practical experience where non-trivial problems are analysed, solutions designed and developed, both individually and in groups. A final-year industry-based group project in the PACE/capstone unit brings everything together to solve a real world problem. This is a Macquarie University (Sydney) course. This award is part of Macquarie's Bachelor of Information Technology course family, listed and administered together with the Bachelor of Information Technology on the university's official course page.

name: Bachelor of Ancient History
description: The Bachelor of Ancient History at Macquarie University is a bachelor's degree. The Bachelor of History offers a dynamic and comprehensive exploration of the human past, from ancient civilisations to contemporary global developments. Students gain critical thinking, research, synthesis, and communication skills through engagement with primary sources, material culture, textual evidence and historical scholarship. The degree includes four majors: Ancient History, Archaeology, Modern History, and Public History and Heritage, enabling specialisation while maintaining a strong multidisciplinary core. Through analytical inquiry, debate, and evidence-based argument, students develop the ability to interpret fragmentary or conflicting sources and communicate effectively in academic and professional contexts. The potential for digital and field-based learning opportunities further enhances practical skills and real-world application.

name: Bachelor of Applied Finance
description: Macquarie's Bachelor of Applied Finance equips students with corporate finance and investment management skills for navigating markets, banks and financial regulation. Graduates learn to help individuals and organisations create value, invest wisely and control risk, skills in demand across the global finance industry. The course runs full-time in 3 years. The course is CRICOS-registered and open to international students studying in Australia.
curriculum: Course structure: Full time: 3 years. See the official Macquarie course page for the full unit-by-unit structure.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
Macquarie's Bachelor of Arts is genuinely broad rather than a single-discipline degree with a generic label. Majors span history, philosophy, international studies, media, English, politics, ancient history, linguistics and a long list of languages, and students commonly combine two majors rather than committing to one, similar to how the Commerce degree is structured. The Faculty of Arts is one of the university's larger faculties and its ancient history and Egyptology programs in particular have a reputation that draws students from well outside Sydney specifically for that specialisation, a genuine point of distinction few other Australian BA programs can match.

Like every Macquarie undergraduate degree, the BA carries a compulsory PACE unit, so arts students end up with a documented placement or community-engagement project on their transcript rather than the degree being purely classroom-based, which matters for a cohort often steered (fairly or not) toward assumptions about limited direct career pathways. Students planning postgraduate study in a specific humanities discipline, or aiming at teaching, law, journalism or public service career tracks, typically use the major and elective combination to build toward those follow-on qualifications rather than treating the BA as a terminal generalist credential.

The degree also functions as the entry point for language study leading toward Macquarie's translation and interpreting postgraduate programs, since a number of the languages taught at undergraduate level (Chinese, French, Japanese, Korean, Spanish) map directly onto the postgraduate NAATI-accredited pathway.
curriculum:
Structure: choose one or two majors from a wide list including History, Philosophy, International Studies, Media, Communication and Cultural Studies, English, Politics and International Relations, Ancient History, Linguistics, and languages (Chinese, French, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, and others)
Foundational units: discipline-specific first-year sequences depending on chosen major(s)
PACE unit: compulsory work-integrated or community engagement placement
Electives: free choice across faculties
Structure: 3 years full-time, 24 units total; can be combined with Laws, Commerce, Education or other degrees
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Arts - Media
description: The Bachelor of Arts - Media at Macquarie University is a bachelor's degree. The Bachelor of Media and Communications is an undergraduate degree focused on the analysis, critique, and production of media. This degree can be completed in three years in a full-time study mode. Media permeates all aspects of the everyday life. In this course students learn to critically engage with media, and how to produce media forms, including: podcasts; radio broadcasts; journalism; web-based media; social media content and public relations campaigns, and screen media. The course offers a sophisticated blend of media theory and production to ensure graduates are critical, enquiring, innovative, and engaged. Taught by a staff of active researchers and media producers, students learn and develop industry skills using the on-site professional production facilities, ensuring that students are equipped with current production expertise and theoretical approaches.

name: Bachelor of Arts - Psychology
description: The Bachelor of Arts - Psychology at Macquarie University is a bachelor's degree. Psychology is a discipline characterised by both scientific research and applied professional practice. This degree is concerned with providing students with a scientific understanding in the psychological processes that underlie behaviour including perception, cognition, learning, motivation, neuroscience, psychopathology, personality, emotion, developmental psychology, health psychology, counselling and social relationships, as well as training in the analysis of data and research methodologies. This course allows students to complete an accredited Psychology degree across three years, or part-time equivalent. Students in this course will also have the option to apply for the Bachelor of Psychological Sciences (Honours) course to complete an additional fourth year of honours in Psychology, conditional on meeting the admission requirements.

name: Bachelor of Business
description: The Bachelor of Business develops skills in business, ethics, sustainability, critical thinking, problem solving, teamwork, managerial agility, strategy and communication, the core competencies Macquarie identifies as needed to lead in a globalised, competitive business environment. The degree suits students who want a broad grounding across business disciplines rather than a single specialised commerce major. The course runs full-time in 3 years. Entry is based on: Selection Rank 75. The selection rank considers a student's Australian Tertiary Admissions Rank (ATAR) or equivalent rank plus any adjustment factors they are eligible for.

name: Bachelor of Business Analytics
description: The Bachelor of Business Analytics at Macquarie University was developed with industry and offers a blend of business and computing. Students gain technical depth in computing, business and statistics through units co-taught by the Faculty of Science and Engineering, work on industry-defined projects delivering solutions and insights to partners, and study industry-focused units covering teamwork, leadership and job readiness. Graduates work as business and data analysts, insights specialists and analytics consultants.

name: Bachelor of Business Leadership and Commerce
Bachelor of Chiropractic Science
description: The Bachelor of Chiropractic Science at Macquarie University is a bachelor's degree. Chiropractic is a healthcare profession focused on diagnosing, treating, managing, and preventing musculoskeletal disorders, conditions that affect the muscles, bones, joints, and nerves. Chiropractors are dedicated to understanding how these disorders can impact overall health and well-being. With a deep knowledge of the connection between the body’s structure and function, chiropractors take a holistic approach to care. In this course, students explore a variety of non-invasive treatment approaches used by chiropractors, including manual therapy, rehabilitation exercises, patient education, lifestyle advice, and self-care strategies. Students also explore the role of chiropractic in delivering integrated care as part of a multi-disciplinary healthcare team. The goal is to empower individuals of all ages to live healthier, more active lives by preventing and managing musculoskeletal issues.

name: Bachelor of Clinical Science
description: The Bachelor of Clinical Science at Macquarie University is a fast track into further study in medicine, physiotherapy, audiology, speech and language pathology, and public health. Students build skills through professional practice training and a local, regional, rural or international placement, study ethics, health disparities and Indigenous health, and connect essential concepts by studying subjects such as physiology and anatomy together. Graduates continue to postgraduate health study or work in health science, research and allied health support roles.

name: Bachelor of Cognitive and Brain Sciences
Bachelor of Commerce
description:
The Bachelor of Commerce at Macquarie starts everyone on the same broad foundation year across accounting, economics, business law and quantitative methods before students pick one or two majors from a list running through accounting, finance, marketing, management, business analytics, actuarial studies, economics and international business, among others. Combining two majors rather than one is common here, and the degree is explicitly built to make that pairing work rather than treating a second major as an awkward add-on, which is one reason it draws students who aren't sure yet whether they want to end up in finance, marketing or something more analytical.

What distinguishes it structurally from a lot of other commerce degrees is the compulsory PACE unit, Professional and Community Engagement, a Macquarie-wide requirement that places students with a real organisation to work on an actual problem for course credit rather than a simulated case study. For commerce students that typically lands as a capstone-adjacent internship experience, so most graduates leave with at least one documented piece of workplace experience already on the resume before they've applied for a graduate role.

Macquarie Business School carries AACSB accreditation, held by a minority of business schools worldwide, which matters for students weighing this degree against a less internationally recognised commerce program when they're thinking about working or studying further afield after graduation.
curriculum:
Foundation units: financial and management accounting basics, microeconomics and macroeconomics, business law, quantitative methods and statistics for business, business communication
Majors (choose one or two): Accounting, Finance, Marketing, Management, Business Analytics, Actuarial Studies, Economics, International Business, Human Resource Management, and others
PACE unit: compulsory work-integrated internship or community engagement placement, typically embedded as a capstone experience
Electives: free choice across the Business School and other faculties
Structure: 3 years full-time, 24 units total
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Commerce - Professional Accounting
description: This accounting degree equips students with the knowledge and skills to pursue a professional career in accounting, building a foundation in core accounting principles alongside business capabilities in information technology, blockchain and data analytics, economics, commercial law, taxation, forensics and financial management. The program is accredited by CPA Australia, Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, the Institute of Public Accountants, and the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants, preparing graduates for professional recognition and global industry standards. This is a Macquarie University (Sydney) course. This award is part of Macquarie's Bachelor of Professional Accounting course family, listed and administered together with the Bachelor of Professional Accounting on the university's official course page.

name: Bachelor of Criminology
description: The Bachelor of Criminology at Macquarie University builds comprehension of crime and injustice, covering the key institutions of criminal justice: the police, courts and prisons. Students study crime and criminal behaviour from legal, political, sociological and psychological perspectives, explore the causes and consequences of crime and alternatives to conventional crime control, and undertake internships with government or industry partners. Graduates work in policy and research, crime prevention, corrections, community justice and government agencies.

name: Bachelor of Cyber Security
description: The Bachelor of Cyber Security at Macquarie University equips students to tackle current and emerging cybercrime challenges, with a degree co-designed by organisations including Amazon, EY, CSIRO, Data61, IBM and Microsoft. Students expand their skillset with units on policy, crime prevention, ethics and governance, and work on real-world, industry-based projects developing practical solutions. Graduates work as security analysts and engineers, penetration testers, and security consultants across technology, finance and government.

name: Bachelor of Economics
description: The Bachelor of Economics aims to provide students with an understanding of the way contemporary economies work. This course focuses on the skills and issues that are likely to be focal in future economic professions, both in the private and in the public and government sector. Units such as health economics, ecological economics, economic development and public economics are specifically designed to address important economic and societal challenges of our time. This is a Macquarie University (Sydney) course.

name: Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood Education) (Birth to 12)
description: This award provides an early childhood teaching qualification completed as a double degree with Bachelor of Arts. The course combines an academic major in discipline studies or in Education with the equivalent of two years full time professional study. In these professional requirements students are engaged in an exploration of evidence-based practice in educational theory, curriculum and pedagogy. The integrated professional experience program allows students to apply, in primary classroom contexts, the pedagogical knowledge and skills they develop in their academic and curriculum-based methodology units. This degree qualifies graduates to teach children aged birth to five years in a broad range of prior to school settings. The course focuses on developing specialist knowledge of young children's learning and development and to plan, implement and evaluate curriculum and learning experiences in prior to school settings. Teacher Education Students explore a range of philosophical, theoretical and practical aspects of learning and teaching which equips them with the professional capacity to respond to the complexity and diversity of children, families and communities in Australian society. A key component of this program is focused on the development of leadership and advocacy skills with an emphasis on working collaboratively with families and communities to achieve the best learning outcomes for young children. This is a Macquarie University (Sydney) course. This award is part of Macquarie's Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood) course family, listed and administered together with the Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood) on the university's official course page.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
Macquarie's engineering honours degree runs on five accredited specialisations (Mechanical, Mechatronic, Software, Civil, and Electrical and Electronic Engineering), all recognised by Engineers Australia, with the Software Engineering stream carrying additional accreditation from the Australian Computer Society. That Engineers Australia stamp is what makes the qualification recognised across North America, and much of Asia and Europe through mutual recognition agreements, which matters for a cohort that includes a substantial number of international students planning careers outside Australia.

What sets the degree apart in practice is Macquarie's PACE program, which the university treats as a genuine point of differentiation rather than a token add-on: engineering students get placed with real firms to work on live technical problems, and Macquarie Park's cluster of engineering, tech and infrastructure employers sitting a short walk from campus makes those placements more accessible here than at universities without an equivalent employment precinct next door. The honours component isn't a bolt-on fourth year either. It's integrated through the degree, culminating in a substantial final-year design or research project specific to the chosen specialisation.

Students can also combine the engineering degree with Commerce or Science as a double degree, which is common enough at Macquarie that dedicated combined-degree pages exist for those pairings, aimed at students who want engineering credentials alongside a business or science major rather than choosing between them.
curriculum:
Common engineering core (early years): engineering mathematics, mechanics, materials, engineering design, programming for engineers, professional engineering practice
Specialisation (choose one, accredited by Engineers Australia): Mechanical Engineering; Mechatronic Engineering; Software Engineering (also accredited by the Australian Computer Society); Civil Engineering; Electrical and Electronic Engineering
Work-integrated learning: PACE placement units with industry partners
Final year: capstone engineering design/research project specific to specialisation
Structure: 4 years full-time honours degree; combinable as a double degree with Commerce or Science
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion with strong mathematics/physics; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Environment
description: The Bachelor of Environment and Conservation at Macquarie University examines how people interact with the natural world, the environmental processes that sustain life on Earth, and the pressures that threaten planetary health. It provides an interdisciplinary foundation in environmental sciences, management and biological conservation, with depth in a chosen major in Environmental Sciences and Management or Biodiversity and Conservation. Research-led learning in ecology, conservation and environmental processes is paired with hands-on laboratory and field training, equipping graduates with the scientific knowledge and analytical capability to confront complex environmental issues.

name: Bachelor of Environment and Conservation
description: The Bachelor of Environment and Conservation at Macquarie University is a bachelor's degree. The Bachelor of Environment and Conservation examines how people interact with the natural world, the environmental processes that sustain life on Earth, and the pressures that threaten planetary health. It provides a comprehensive, interdisciplinary foundation in environmental sciences, management, and biological conservation. Students develop broad capability across environmental systems and sustainability, alongside depth in a chosen major in Environmental Sciences and Management or Biodiversity and Conservation. This degree will equip students with the scientific knowledge, analytical capability, and practical experience needed to confront and solve complex environmental issues. Strong research-led learning in ecology, conservation, and environmental processes is paired with hands-on laboratory and field training.

name: Bachelor of Exercise and Sports Science
description: The Bachelor of Exercise and Sports Science at Macquarie University prepares students to apply evidence-based practice across sport, health and performance-focused careers. Students gain experience in settings from private clinics and schools to professional sporting organisations, use facilities including an indoor synthetic track, strength and conditioning areas and anatomy labs, and hear from experts linked to elite sport, the fitness industry and rehabilitation. Graduates work in exercise science, strength and conditioning, sports performance, rehabilitation and health promotion.

name: Bachelor of Game Design and Development
description: The Bachelor of Games Design and Development program aims to provide graduates with the necessary skills to be a successful video game designer, developer and producer. Recognising that the video games industry in Australia is small and jobs are hard to come by, we also intend to give graduates a wider variety of career options in software development and user experience design. The BGDD program comprises three streams, addressing three different skill areas important for the field: 1. Software development. Video games are complex pieces of software and their development requires all the skills of other software development projects, including programming, version control, and quality assurance testing. This stream also develops understanding and skills related to the production of computer graphics and technical art. 2. User experience (UX) design. Designing a video game requires a strong understanding of how interaction with game systems and representations motivate and shape player behaviours and experiences. This requires an understanding of theories for system and UX design, as well critical user testing and communication skills, to measure and shape how people engage with software and its psychological effects. 3. Software production. Video games are massive worldwide industry and game production is one of the most complex and multidisciplinary crafts. An informed producer of entertainment software needs to know best practices for effectively managing a diverse team as well as the cultural and market contexts within which their software will be produced and released.

name: Bachelor of Health Sciences
description: The Bachelor of Health Sciences at Macquarie University is a versatile degree in which students build foundational skills before choosing one of four interdisciplinary majors: Digital Health, Health Administration, Health Coaching, or Mental Health and Counselling. Students sharpen problem-solving, teamwork, communication and ethical skills on real challenges from industry partners, and develop transferable decision-making skills. Graduates work in health administration and management, digital health, health promotion and community health roles.

name: Bachelor of History
description: The Bachelor of History at Macquarie University offers a dynamic exploration of the human experience from ancient civilisations to contemporary global societies, with majors in Ancient History, Archaeology, Modern History, and Public History and Heritage. Students choose from more than 40 units, go behind the scenes of public displays such as major museum exhibitions, and explore 3D scanning, photogrammetry, remote sensing and the use of AI to interpret evidence. Graduates work in research, museums and heritage, education, archives, policy and writing.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description: Macquarie University Bachelor of Information Technology is built from a core zone in the chosen field and a flexible zone for depth or breadth, with one or two majors drawn from more than 20 options including artificial intelligence, data science, cyber security, information systems and business analysis, software development, web development, and games design and development. The data science major uses computational and statistical techniques, machine learning and data mining to work with big data. The degree is co-designed with industry partners including Microsoft, IBM, Amazon, CSIRO Data61 and DSTG, and connects students with more than 300 companies through projects and internships. It is accredited by the Australian Computer Society. Year 12 applicants apply through UAC, with entry based on selection rank or the Subject Advantage scheme. Indicative international tuition is around A$48,200 per year.

name: Bachelor of International Studies
description: The Bachelor of International Studies at Macquarie University has students collaborate with experts and global communities to co-create practical responses to emerging global needs, with majors including Global Leadership and Communication, Humans and Emerging Technologies, International Relations and Government, and Modern Languages. Students graduate with tangible outcomes such as case studies and stakeholder maps, apply their learning through internships, study tours and virtual exchanges, and use human-centred thinking and ethical analysis. Graduates work in foreign affairs, development, non-government organisations, global business and research.

name: Bachelor of Laws (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Laws (Honours) at Macquarie University is built around real experience and connection with industry, with opportunities to complete an internship at a leading firm. The degree is informed by a board of top-tier firms and legal innovators, students gain insight from specialists across human rights, climate and energy, criminal justice, trade and property, and join an alumni community of judges, barristers and law partners. Graduates complete practical legal training toward admission and work in legal practice, policy and business.

Bachelor of Marketing and Media

This three-year degree, offered both on-campus and online, has an interdisciplinary focus integrating social and environmental domains in the planning and design of sustainable cities and regions. Students develop depth in social and environmental sustainability, health and wellbeing, housing and governance, and technology, AI and Geographic Information Systems, graduating with knowledge of planning theory, policy and governance alongside practical skills in plan-making, urban design, impact assessment and research. description: The Bachelor of Psychological Sciences (Honours) at Macquarie University is typically a one-year course for high-achieving students aiming for a professional career in psychology. It builds on the foundational training of an accredited Level 1 psychology qualification, which covers the psychological processes underlying behaviour including perception, cognition, learning, motivation, neuroscience, psychopathology, personality, emotion, and developmental, health and social psychology, alongside research methods and data analysis. In the Honours year, students plan and carry out an independent, sustained critical investigation of a chosen research topic, completing an accredited fourth year of psychology study.

name: Bachelor of Psychology
description:
This is Macquarie's APAC-accredited undergraduate psychology sequence, and the accreditation detail matters more than it might for other degrees: without a program recognised by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council, graduates can't progress toward provisional or general registration as a psychologist in Australia at all. The three-year degree covers the discipline broadly, from cognitive and biological psychology through developmental, social and abnormal psychology, before students who want to continue toward registration move into the honours year.

That honours year isn't automatic. Admission requires a weighted average grade of 70 across all psychology units and 75 across 300-level psychology units specifically, with a minimum of 72 credit points completed, and it only starts in first semester, running two semesters as an intensive research year built around an individually supervised thesis. For students who don't clear that bar or don't want to pursue registration, the base three-year degree still stands on its own as a psychology qualification, just not one that leads directly into professional practice.

Given how competitive honours entry is nationally in psychology (the accreditation bottleneck limits places at every Australian university, not just Macquarie), students aiming for registration are generally advised to treat the 300-level grade threshold as a first-year planning consideration rather than something to worry about only in third year.
curriculum:
Core sequence: introduction to psychology, biological psychology, cognitive psychology, developmental psychology, social psychology, abnormal psychology, research methods and statistics I-III
300-level advanced units: personality, health psychology, forensic psychology, neuropsychology (options vary by year)
Honours year (separate admission, weighted average 70 overall / 75 at 300-level required): advanced research methods, supervised empirical thesis, specialist seminars
Accreditation: Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC) — required pathway toward provisional psychologist registration
Structure: 3-year bachelor's degree; honours year (2 semesters, February entry only) as a separate accredited add-on

description: The Bachelor of Science at Macquarie University is co-designed with CSIRO, Johnson & Johnson and ResMed, equipping students with the professional and technical skills employers value through built-in employability units and tailored career support. Students learn from teachers with expertise in areas such as the changing environment, future materials and fuels, and biotechnology, and experience applied and immersive learning that hones analytical thinking, teamwork and project management. Graduates work in laboratory and field science, data and research roles, and further study.

The course integrates Indigenous knowledge and sustainability considerations into core units, and includes work-integrated learning in collaboration with industry organisations. Two quantitative first-year units are matched to major groupings: FOSE1025 for Biology, Biotechnology, Chemistry, Human Biology, Earth and Environmental Sciences and Physiological Sciences majors, and FOSE1030 for Astronomy, Applied Physics, Mathematics or Statistical Data Science majors. This is a Macquarie University (Sydney) course. name: Bachelor of Science - Psychology
description: The Bachelor of Science - Psychology at Macquarie University is a bachelor's degree. Psychology is a discipline characterised by both scientific research and applied professional practice. This degree is concerned with providing students with a scientific understanding in the psychological processes that underlie behaviour including perception, cognition, learning, motivation, neuroscience, psychopathology, personality, emotion, developmental psychology, health psychology, counselling and social relationships, as well as training in the analysis of data and research methodologies. This course allows students to complete an accredited Psychology degree across three years, or part-time equivalent. Students in this course will also have the option to apply for the Bachelor of Psychological Sciences (Honours) course to complete an additional fourth year of honours in Psychology, conditional on meeting the admission requirements.

name: Bachelor of Security Studies
description: The Bachelor of Security Studies at Macquarie University equips students to navigate complex, interconnected and evolving challenges. Students learn to analyse security data, assess threats and apply intelligence techniques, connect with experts through guest lectures by Australian ambassadors, UN officials and NATO representatives, and tackle issues such as online extremism through scenario exercises and security challenge games. Graduates work in national security, defence, intelligence, risk analysis and government agencies.

name: Bachelor of Social Science
description: The Bachelor of Social Science at Macquarie University is a bachelor's degree. The Bachelor of Social Sciences at Macquarie University is a distinctive course that equips graduates with knowledge and skills to create change in the world. Alongside a deep grounding of key social concepts, debates and methodologies, students learn to design, manage and execute projects, collaborate with diverse stakeholders and develop leadership and organisational skills. Students learn the technical and transferable skills to work with data and construct meaningful narratives that address real world and contemporary social problems. Students select an interdisciplinary major focused on a ‘grand challenge’, on topics including health, wellbeing, climate change, sustainability, security, work and technology. Students be taught by active researchers, leading academics and award-winning teachers and students be given the opportunity to connect with employers and communities via a range of work-integrated learning opportunities embedded throughout the course.

name: Bachelor of Social Sciences
description: The Bachelor of Social Sciences at Macquarie University is designed for people who want to create purposeful change, with majors including Health, Wellbeing and Society, Media, Culture and Communications, and Sociology. Students use skills in data analysis, interviewing, survey design and policy evaluation to disentangle complex problems, design and execute projects with diverse stakeholders under active researchers, and develop ethical, evidence-based solutions to real-world challenges. Graduates work in social research and policy, community services, communications and advocacy.

name: Bachelor of Speech and Hearing Sciences
description: The Bachelor of Speech and Hearing Sciences at Macquarie University is described as Australia's only integrated undergraduate speech and hearing sciences degree. Students use a world-leading phonetics lab, an anechoic chamber and the Australian Hearing Hub, gain insights from clinically active lecturers, connect with industry leaders such as Cochlear and NextSense, and apply their knowledge during a 50-hour placement. Graduates continue to postgraduate study in speech pathology or audiology, or work in research, hearing services and community organisations.

name: Bachelor of Teaching (Early Childhood Education)
description: This award provides an early childhood teaching qualification completed as a double degree with Bachelor of Arts. The course combines an academic major in discipline studies or in Education with the equivalent of two years full time professional study. In these professional requirements students are engaged in an exploration of evidence-based practice in educational theory, curriculum and pedagogy. The integrated professional experience program allows students to apply, in primary classroom contexts, the pedagogical knowledge and skills they develop in their academic and curriculum-based methodology units. This degree qualifies graduates to teach children aged birth to five years in a broad range of prior to school settings. The course focuses on developing specialist knowledge of young children's learning and development and to plan, implement and evaluate curriculum and learning experiences in prior to school settings. Teacher Education Students explore a range of philosophical, theoretical and practical aspects of learning and teaching which equips them with the professional capacity to respond to the complexity and diversity of children, families and communities in Australian society. A key component of this program is focused on the development of leadership and advocacy skills with an emphasis on working collaboratively with families and communities to achieve the best learning outcomes for young children. This is a Macquarie University (Sydney) course. This award is part of Macquarie's Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood) course family, listed and administered together with the Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood) on the university's official course page.

name: Doctor of Medicine
description: The Overview and Aims of the course have been defined in terms of a Vision statement and associated Mission and Design statements, as provided below. Vision To create a medical course which provides a truly transnational quality assured medical education experience for local and international students. While embedded in learning within the Australian health care context, a strong emphasis on the comparison of health care systems and on emerging technologies in medical practice will ensure that our students master the cultural awareness and communication skills required for positive patient-centred care in any setting. Macquarie University graduates will be doctors who capably practice quality medicine in diverse local and global communities, and effectively connect with patients and inter-professional teams across cultures. Mission The primary mission of the Medical course is to graduate doctors with the scientific, clinical, social and professional capabilities that will serve as the basis for medical practice across the world. By collaborating with domestic and international partners who share similar value sets, we will provide an outstanding clinical and educational experience locally and globally. Our primary mission will be realised through our commitment to: Comparative and reflective approach to learning. We will use a comparative approach to the varied clinical, cultural and health system experiences of the course's diverse group of students. By encouraging reflection on these experiences, we will foster the achievement of an international perspective and a global capability set for our graduates. Patient-centred Care.

A Minimum Score of 50 overall and 50 in each section (domestic applicants and international applicants residing in Australia or New Zealand) OR Medical College Admission Test (MCAT) A minimum overall score of 500 (international applicants residing outside Australia) Satisfactory Multiple Mini-Interview Performance Qualifications considered for admission must have been completed within 10 years of intended enrolment. GAMSAT and MCAT scores submitted must be within four, and three years, respectively of intended enrolment. Interview opportunity and offers are competitive, meeting minimum requirements does not guarantee offer of admission Comprehensive admissions information is provided on the Macquarie MD website , including details about alternative admission pathways for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants.

name: Doctor of Physiotherapy
description: The Doctor of Physiotherapy is a 3 year Masters (Extended) course. The DPT offers an extended curriculum with advanced clinical knowledge and skills as well as business, leadership and advocacy skills. Students undertake an extensive and innovative integrated clinical education program, and a substantial research project. The Doctor of Physiotherapy aims to ensure graduates have the following capabilities: Capability 1 Scientist and Scholar: Graduates will be scientists and scholars with advanced knowledge and skills to deliver science and evidence-based physiotherapy practice. Capability 2 Clinical Practitioner: Graduates will be effective communicators and highly skilled physiotherapists delivering person-centred healthcare. Capability 3 Engaged Global Citizen: Graduates will be socially and culturally safe adaptive practitioners with awareness of local and global public health issues, able to operate effectively in a range of health systems and advocate for innovations to enhance health. Capability 4 Professional: Graduates will be ethical and reflective physiotherapy practitioners able to lead and work collaboratively within teams. This is a Macquarie University (Sydney) course.

name: Master of Applied Finance
description:
Applied Finance at Macquarie runs through a five-unit core covering corporate finance, financial instruments, financial risk management, investments and a professional practice unit, then branches into one of four specialisations: Funds Management, Risk Management, Corporate Finance, or Instruments and Valuation, drawing on a pool of more than 30 elective units. That elective depth is unusually large for a finance master's and reflects the program's history as much as anything: it grew out of what's now the Macquarie Applied Finance Centre, a specialist unit within the Business School built specifically around finance practitioner education rather than finance being one specialisation inside a general MBA.

The degree is recognised by the CFA Institute, which for a program this finance-specific matters more directly than it would for a general MBA, since CFA recognition speaks to how closely the curriculum tracks the CFA's own body of knowledge in valuation, portfolio management and financial analysis. Less common electives in sustainable finance and resources, infrastructure and energy finance sit alongside the four core specialisations, which reflects Sydney's position as a hub for both green finance and natural resources project financing, giving students in those tracks a genuinely local industry pipeline rather than an imported curriculum.

Given Macquarie's own history and its association with Macquarie Group (one of the world's largest specialist investment banks, no formal ownership link but a strong professional and reputational connection through name and alumni networks), the degree draws heavily on finance industry practitioners as guest lecturers and adjunct staff, which shapes it toward practitioner-oriented, market-relevant content over purely academic finance theory.
curriculum:
Core units (5): Corporate Finance; Financial Instruments; Financial Risk Management; Investments; Professional Practice
Specialisation (choose one, from 30+ elective units): Funds Management; Risk Management; Corporate Finance; Instruments and Valuation
Additional elective areas: Sustainable Finance; Resources, Infrastructure and Energy Finance
Recognition: CFA Institute recognised program
Structure: full-time or part-time; typically 1.5-2 years full-time equivalent
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Macquarie's MBA sits inside a business school carrying AACSB accreditation, a marker held by roughly the top 6 percent of business schools globally, and the degree draws heavily on the school's applied finance and actuarial research strength, meaning the finance and analytics electives here tend to have more genuine quantitative depth than the equivalent electives at a generalist MBA program. Sydney's Macquarie Park location also puts the cohort within easy reach of the corporate campuses of Optus, Canon, Cochlear and a string of other multinationals headquartered in the same business park, and networking events and guest lectures lean on those neighbours more than a CBD-based MBA program typically can.

The program follows the standard MBA architecture of a core management and leadership sequence, covering strategy, finance, marketing and organisational behaviour, layered with electives that let students angle the degree toward general management, finance or a more analytics-heavy track depending on career direction. As with Macquarie's undergraduate degrees, PACE-style industry engagement is woven into the postgraduate experience through consulting projects and industry-based capstone work rather than confined to a single elective.

Students coming from a non-business undergraduate background (engineering, science, health) are a substantial share of the intake, which shapes classroom discussion toward translating technical or clinical expertise into management responsibility rather than assuming everyone arrives with a commerce background already.
curriculum:
Core units: managerial economics, financial management, strategic management, marketing management, organisational behaviour and leadership, business analytics for decision making
Electives: chosen to build a general management, finance, or analytics-focused profile — options include corporate finance, digital marketing, supply chain management, entrepreneurship
Capstone: applied strategy or consulting project, often with an industry partner
Accreditation: Macquarie Business School holds AACSB accreditation
Structure: full-time or part-time options; typically 1.5-2 years full-time equivalent

name: Master of Chiropractic
description: Chiropractic is an allied health profession that focuses on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of musculoskeletal disorders, and the effects of these disorders on health and wellbeing. Chiropractors have a deep understanding of the relationship between body structure and function and adopt a holistic approach to healthcare. Chiropractors apply a variety of non-invasive treatment approaches, including manual therapy, therapeutic exercise, patient education, lifestyle recommendations, and self-management interventions to help people of all ages live full, active, and healthy lives. The Master of Chiropractic will develop your clinical, professional practice, and research appraisal skills so you can confidently assess, diagnose, and manage a wide variety of musculoskeletal disorders. As a graduate, you will be eligible to apply for registration as a chiropractor in Australia and New Zealand and be equipped with the knowledge and skills to work in clinical practice and other non-clinical health-related roles. On successful completion of the Master of Chiropractic you will achieve the following graduate capabilities: Capability 1 Scientist and Scholar: Graduates will be applied scientists and research-informed scholars with the advanced knowledge and skills required to deliver evidence-based chiropractic care. Capability 2 Clinical Practitioner: Graduates will be effective communicators and highly skilled, competent chiropractors able to apply a person-centred approach to practice. Capability 3 Engaged Global Citizen: Graduates will be socially and culturally inclusive chiropractors with an awareness of local and global public health issues. Capability 4 Professional: Graduates will be ethical and reflective chiropractors ready to lead and work collaboratively within teams within their scope of practice. This is a Macquarie University (Sydney) course.

name: Master of Clinical Audiology
description: The Master of Clinical Audiology (MClinAudiology) is a two year postgraduate course located within the Department of Linguistics at Macquarie University. It is a unique offering in NSW with only six other professionally accredited programs existing in Australia (Victoria, Queensland, South Australia, Western Australia and the Northern Territory). Our location, within the Australian Hearing Hub offers our students the unique ability to interact with a wide variety of hearing researchers (Cochlear and National Acoustics Laboratories), hearing care service providers like the Next Sense, Shepherd Centre and other allied health partners (such as speech pathologists, teachers of the Deaf, and early intervention specialists). The Macquarie University Master of Clinical Audiology course aims to provide our students with the skills, knowledge and training they need to practice as a qualified clinical audiologist. The course prepares students for the assessment, rehabilitation, and habilitation of populations with hearing impairment, as well as training in research studies' design. Our Macquarie University audiology graduates will be competent practitioners with strong scholarly, social, and professional abilities and highly employable, capable of engaging across disciplines, with diverse local and global communities. The Master of Clinical Audiology program is two years in duration. The first-year focusses on diagnostic and knowledge-based and skill-based outcomes, while the second-year centres on clinical management of clients, their families, and clinical practice more broadly, including understanding the hearing healthcare system and how it fits within the healthcare system more broadly. The structure is designed so that it systematically segues to ensure progression and development of competencies throughout the two years.

description: The Master of Clinical Neuropsychology course includes units which contain a blend of theory and practice together with 1,000 hours of supervised practice and a research project. Students completing this course typically work as clinical neuropsychologists in public or private hospitals and/or in private practice. Hospital/clinic settings encompass neurological, psychiatric, geriatric, paediatric, drug/alcohol, forensic, and rehabilitation disciplines, where the neuropsychologist may engage in assessment and contribute to therapeutic/management programs. On completion of this course, students will be qualified to be eligible for registration as a psychologist with the Psychology Board of Australia and eligible to commence the pathway to be endorsed as a clinical neuropsychologist. The course aims are to develop graduates who have the following capabilities: Capability 1. Scientist and Scholar: Graduates will be evidence-based practitioners and scholars with advanced knowledge and skills in clinical neuropsychology able to deliver services across the lifespan. Capability 2. Psychologist Practitioner: Graduates will be effective communicators and highly skilled, competent psychologists delivering safe, client-centred neuropsychological assessment and intervention. Capability 3. Engaged Global Citizen: Graduates will be socially and culturally responsive psychologists with awareness of the issues affecting behaviour and cognition, and who are ready to operate effectively in a range of health settings. Capability 4. Professional: Graduates will be ethical and reflective psychologist practitioners ready to lead and work collaboratively within teams. This is a Macquarie University (Sydney) course.

name: Master of Data Science
description:
The Master of Data Science covers the standard core of the field, statistical and machine learning methods, data management, programming and data visualisation, but the structural detail worth knowing is Macquarie's zone system: a core zone of compulsory units everyone completes, and a capstone unit specifically flagged in the handbook (units carrying a C designation) that requires students to apply the degree's technical content to a substantial project rather than close out with another taught unit. That capstone is where the degree earns its applied reputation, typically built around a dataset and problem sourced from industry or a research partner rather than a synthetic classroom exercise.

As a two-year full-time degree it runs longer than some competitor data science master's programs, which reflects Macquarie positioning it partly as an entry pathway for students without a quantitative undergraduate background (commerce, life sciences, humanities graduates retraining into data roles) rather than purely as an advanced technical top-up for computer science graduates. Students entering with a stronger quantitative or programming background can typically move through the foundational content faster and spend proportionally more time on the machine learning and advanced statistical modelling units toward the end of the degree.

Macquarie Business School's Department of Actuarial Studies and Business Analytics has a hand in aspects of the analytics curriculum here, which shows up in a stronger-than-average statistical modelling and risk-analytics flavour compared with data science programs housed purely in a computer science faculty.
curriculum:
Core zone: programming for data science, statistical methods, data management and databases, data visualisation, machine learning fundamentals, applied research methods
Advanced units: predictive modelling, big data technologies, natural language processing or deep learning (options vary by intake)
Capstone unit (C-coded): applied data science project, typically with an industry or research partner
Electives: drawn from business analytics, computing, or statistics depending on background and interest
Structure: full-time, typically 2 years; shorter with recognised prior study in a quantitative discipline
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree with quantitative background
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
Macquarie compresses what would be a three-year undergraduate IT degree into the first year of this master's, then spends the second year on advanced, specialised content, which is how the university frames it for the large share of students entering from an unrelated bachelor's degree, commerce or the humanities, say, without prior computing study. That two-speed structure only really works because of the zone system: a foundation zone for students who need to pick up programming and systems fundamentals from scratch, a core zone shared by everyone, and a flexible zone where the specialisation and electives sit.

Three specialisations are on offer: Artificial Intelligence, Cyber Security and Information Systems. The AI stream goes into machine learning, natural language processing and the ethical and legal questions that come with deploying AI systems in production rather than treating those as an afterthought unit. Cyber Security covers digital forensics, ethical hacking and information security operations, aimed at students heading toward SOC analyst, penetration testing or security engineering roles rather than pure compliance work. Information Systems sits closer to enterprise IT strategy and systems management for students aiming at business-facing technology roles.

Students finishing the degree can choose between a supervised research project and an industry internship as their final applied component, a genuinely different choice depending on whether the plan is a PhD application or a fast track into an employer's graduate program. Given Macquarie's location next to the Macquarie Park tech and business precinct (home to a dense cluster of multinational tech and engineering firms), the internship route in particular tends to draw on placements that wouldn't be as accessible from a campus further from Sydney's northern tech corridor.
curriculum:
Year 1 (accelerated foundation, for students without an IT background): programming fundamentals, data structures and algorithms, systems analysis and design, database systems, networking fundamentals
Year 2 core: advanced software engineering, cloud computing, applied research methods in IT
Specialisation (choose one): Artificial Intelligence (machine learning, natural language understanding, AI ethics and law); Cyber Security (information security, digital forensics, ethical hacking, data privacy); Information Systems (enterprise systems, IT strategy and governance)
Flexible zone: electives within or outside the IT discipline
Final component: supervised research project or industry internship
Structure: full-time, typically 2 years (1.5 years with recognised prior study)
