name: Bachelor of Data Analytics
description:
This degree sits at the intersection of statistics, programming and business decision-making rather than treating data analytics as a pure computer science offshoot: students build up R and Python skills for analysis alongside database design and visualisation tools like Tableau and Power BI, but the course frames all of it around organisational and business problem-solving rather than algorithmic theory for its own sake.

Students choose a specialisation track, most commonly Data Science or Business Intelligence, and the course requires an industry internship or applied project as part of the structure rather than offering it as an optional extra. Murdoch runs this partly through its IT Innovation Hub, which houses a data centre reported at roughly $2 million in infrastructure investment, a relatively serious facility for an undergraduate-focused analytics degree at a mid-sized Australian university.

Scholarship pathways like the Westpac Young Technologists Program give some students early industry contact before graduation, which matters in a field where employers weight practical project experience heavily against a still-developing formal discipline. Graduates commonly move into business intelligence analyst, data analyst or junior data scientist roles depending on which specialisation track they followed.
curriculum:
Year 1: introduction to programming (Python/R), statistics for data analysis, database fundamentals, business and organisational context units
Year 2: data visualisation and reporting (Tableau, Power BI), database design and management, applied statistical modelling, specialisation choice (Data Science or Business Intelligence)
Year 3: advanced analytics/machine learning fundamentals (Data Science track) or business intelligence systems (Business Intelligence track), industry internship or capstone analytics project, research and communication skills
Total: 3 years full-time; industry internship or applied project embedded in final year

description:
Murdoch's engineering degree is genuinely small in scope compared to the sprawling multi-discipline programs at the larger Group of Eight universities. It offers three specialisations (Electrical and Renewable Energy Engineering, Environmental Engineering, and Industrial Control and Automation Engineering) rather than a dozen, and leans into that focus with a facility the school describes as the only one of its kind at a Western Australian university: a real-world engineering plant with a dedicated control room, used for hands-on training rather than simulation alone.

Every student completes 450 hours of professional work placement as part of the degree, and honours is embedded rather than a separate bolt-on year students apply for separately. Everyone finishes with an individual research or industry project in year four, applying material from the first three years to a genuine open-ended problem. That focus on renewable energy and industrial automation tracks reasonably well with Western Australia's resources and energy sector employment base, which is a different emphasis than engineering programs oriented toward software or biomedical applications.

Given the specialisation is fixed early relative to some universities' common-first-year models, students choosing this course should have a reasonably clear sense already of whether they want electrical/renewables, environmental, or automation/control work.
curriculum:
Years 1–2: engineering mathematics, engineering mechanics and materials, electrical circuits and systems fundamentals, programming for engineers, specialisation core units begin
Year 3: specialisation deepening (Electrical and Renewable Energy, Environmental, or Industrial Control and Automation), control systems, sustainability and infrastructure units, 450 hours professional work placement (completed across the course)
Year 4 (Honours, embedded): advanced specialisation electives, individual research or industry-based honours project, professional practice and ethics
Total: 4 years full-time (Honours embedded, not a separate application); access to Murdoch's dedicated engineering plant and control room facility
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 75-80 (or equivalent); completion of WACE Mathematics Methods and Chemistry or Physics recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Engineering Technology
description:
A three-year degree accredited by Engineers Australia at engineering technologist level, with a major in electrical and renewable energy engineering, environmental engineering, or industrial control and automation engineering.

Murdoch runs a real engineering plant on campus, the Bayer pilot plant with its own control room, described as the only facility of its kind in WA, so students train on industrial equipment rather than simulations. Entry is an ATAR of about 70 with VET and mature-age pathways. It suits students who want an applied, hands-on engineering career, and it articulates into the two-year Master of Engineering Practice for those who want to reach professional engineer level.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 75-80 (or equivalent); completion of WACE Mathematics Methods and Physics recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Food Science and Nutrition
description:
A three-year degree covering food composition, processing and preservation alongside human nutrition, including how diet, the gut microbiome and nutrients affect health and disease. Students work in laboratories and food production settings with industry-standard equipment, and use Murdoch's living labs including Whitby Falls Farm.

There is no single professional accreditation attached to the degree. Entry is an ATAR of about 70 with alternative pathways available. It suits students aiming at food manufacturing, product development, quality assurance, food safety regulation or public health nutrition roles, and it can be paired with a Master of Food Science for a longer research-oriented path.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of WACE Chemistry recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Forensic Science
description:
A three-year science degree with a major in forensic biology or forensic chemistry and toxicology, and an optional second major in forensic investigation. Students run simulated crime scenes and analyse biological and chemical evidence in the labs of the Murdoch Health and Knowledge Precinct.

The distinctive element is the Cold Case Review initiative, where students contribute to real unsolved homicide and missing-persons cases under supervision. Entry is an ATAR of about 70. It suits students who want a laboratory and investigation career applying science to the justice system, working toward roles as forensic scientists, toxicologists, crime scene officers or laboratory analysts, with postgraduate study in forensic science or research as a next step.

name: Bachelor of Global Security
description:
A three-year degree focused on terrorism, intelligence, conflict and international affairs, with a choice of major: cyberspace policy and security, environment conflict and security, politics and international studies, or terrorism and counterterrorism studies.

Internships and placements with government agencies and other organisations are built in. Murdoch reports the degree ranks first in Western Australia for full-time employment among humanities and social science graduates. Entry is an ATAR of about 70, with online, on-campus and mixed-mode study available. It suits students aiming at intelligence and security analysis, policy work, defence, law enforcement or roles in international organisations.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
Murdoch's IT degree is built around named majors rather than a single generalist stream, and Cyber Security and Forensics is the one the school markets hardest: it covers network security, software security, computer forensics and penetration testing, and it carries Australian Computer Society accreditation at the Professional level, which is a recognised bar for graduates entering security roles in Australia.

Students aren't locked to a single major either; the course structure explicitly supports a double major within IT, or pairing an IT major with a major from another Murdoch degree, which lets students build combinations like cyber security plus data science or IT plus criminology that a single-major degree wouldn't allow. Delivery mixes on-campus lectures with lab-based practical work and industry placement opportunities, which matters in a discipline where a lot of the actual skill (network configuration, exploit analysis) doesn't transfer well from lecture slides alone.

Career outcomes cited by the school for cyber-focused graduates include security consultant, forensic investigator and database administrator roles: a broader spread than "penetration tester" alone, reflecting that most entry-level security jobs in Australia are still generalist information-security roles rather than narrow specialisations.
curriculum:
Year 1: programming fundamentals, computer systems and networks, database fundamentals, introduction to information security
Year 2: network security, systems administration, software security principles, major-specific units (e.g. Cyber Security and Forensics, Data Science, Web and Mobile Development)
Year 3: computer forensics, penetration testing and vulnerability assessment, advanced major electives, industry placement or capstone project
Total: 3 years full-time; Cyber Security and Forensics major accredited by the Australian Computer Society at Professional level; double-major and cross-degree combinations available
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of WACE or equivalent secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Information Technology and Business
description:
A three-year degree that deliberately sits between IT and business rather than training programmers. Students learn programming, networking and data management alongside management, communication and entrepreneurship, with the aim of designing and managing technology solutions that serve business goals.

Learning is project-based, with real-world challenges and time in Murdoch's IT Innovation Hub, and industry partners shaped the course. Entry is an ATAR of about 70. It targets roles such as business analyst, IT consultant, systems analyst, project coordinator and digital transformation specialist, and suits students who are more interested in how organisations use technology and make decisions than in software development.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of WACE or equivalent secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Laboratory Medicine
description:
A four-year degree in diagnostic pathology science, covering biochemistry, haematology, immunology, microbiology, histopathology, diagnostic genomics and transfusion science, with practical laboratory training and placements in diagnostic pathology labs.

It is professionally accredited by the Australian Institute of Medical and Clinical Scientists, and Murdoch says accredited graduates are preferentially employed by the pathology sector. Study is based in the Murdoch Health and Knowledge Precinct alongside hospitals and research centres. Entry is an ATAR of about 70. It suits students who want a laboratory-based health career diagnosing disease from patient samples, rather than patient-facing clinical work.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 75-80 (or equivalent); completion of WACE Chemistry and Human Biology recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
The distinguishing feature of Murdoch's law degree is SCALES, its award-winning student law clinic: students earn academic credit working actual client matters in areas like human rights law, family law and community legal issues, under supervision, rather than working through hypothetical case studies for the whole degree. That's a genuine point of difference from law schools where "clinical experience" is a mooting exercise dressed up in different language.

The school also foregrounds a social-justice orientation more explicitly than many Australian law programs: human rights and access-to-justice framing shows up across the marketing and, by the school's account, in elective offerings, which shapes who tends to be drawn to Murdoch Law over a more corporate-commercial-focused program. Mooting runs through a purpose-built courtroom facility and is positioned as building advocacy and courtroom presence alongside the clinic work rather than replacing it.

Beyond the clinic, Murdoch's Work Integrated Learning internship program places law students with law firms, government agencies and not-for-profits, which is a fairly standard offering across Australian law schools but is run here with the same WIL infrastructure Murdoch uses for its business and other professional degrees.
curriculum:
Year 1: introduction to law and legal system, legal research and writing, contracts, torts
Year 2: property law, criminal law, constitutional law, equity, SCALES law clinic (credit-bearing clinical placement) or mooting unit
Year 3: evidence, administrative law, dispute resolution, WIL internship (law firms, government, not-for-profit), advanced electives (e.g. human rights law, family law)
Total: 3 years full-time (as a single degree) or extended when combined with another Murdoch degree; SCALES clinical placement credit-bearing and available to eligible students
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 80+ (or equivalent); completion of WACE or equivalent secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Bachelor of Laws (LLB) - Graduate Entry
description:

It is accredited by the Legal Practice Board of Western Australia, so completion satisfies the academic requirement for admission to legal practice in WA (the practical legal training component is completed separately after graduation).

Practical experience is built in through the SCALES community law clinic, where students work with real clients, a mooting program in a purpose-built courtroom, and work-integrated learning placements with firms, government and community legal centres. Recognition of prior learning may give advanced standing. It suits graduates from science, health, criminology, business or arts backgrounds who want to practise law or pair legal skills with their existing field.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Murdoch's nursing degree puts 20 weeks of supervised work experience into the course, spread across hospitals, aged care and community health settings rather than concentrated in a single block. Students typically encounter several different care contexts before they graduate rather than specialising in one setting by default. The School of Nursing's placement partners span both metropolitan Perth hospitals and rural WA services, so students can end up doing a rotation somewhere quite different from where they studied.

Before students reach a real ward, the course leans on simulated clinical environments and case-based learning to build competence and confidence, a fairly standard approach in Australian nursing education now, but one Murdoch runs with dedicated simulation labs on its Perth campus. Specialty placement areas mentioned by the school include gerontology, mental health, paediatrics and critical care, giving students exposure to sub-specialties they might not otherwise encounter until postgraduate study.

On graduation, students are eligible to register with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia through AHPRA, and the degree is commonly used as a springboard into postgraduate specialisation: critical care, mental health nursing or midwifery graduate-entry programs are the usual next step for those who want to sub-specialise.
curriculum:
Year 1: foundations of nursing practice, anatomy and physiology, health assessment, introduction to professional communication and ethics
Year 2: pathophysiology and pharmacology, mental health nursing, chronic disease and complex care, clinical placement blocks in hospital and community settings
Year 3: acute and critical care nursing, aged care and rehabilitation, leadership and transition to practice, specialty placement rotations (e.g. paediatrics, mental health, critical care)
Total placement across the course: approximately 20 weeks of work experience in hospitals, aged care and community settings
Total: 3 years full-time; graduates eligible for AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); satisfactory National Police Certificate and immunisation compliance required prior to clinical placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements for nursing.

name: Bachelor of Psychology
description:
This is Murdoch's APAC-accredited undergraduate psychology sequence: three years that lead, for eligible students, into a fourth Honours year rather than being accredited as a stand-alone terminal qualification. Students who complete both years exit eligible for provisional registration with the Psychology Board of Australia, which is the credential that actually matters for anyone planning to practise.

The Honours year is where the degree's research emphasis becomes explicit: students negotiate an original empirical research topic with a supervisor, and the year culminates in both a written thesis and a poster presented at a research conference, a dual output that mirrors how psychology researchers actually communicate findings, rather than a thesis alone. Advanced coursework alongside the research project balances theoretical grounding with the practical and professional issues graduates will face applying psychology in clinical, organisational or community settings.

Because Honours places are typically limited relative to the number of students completing the pass degree, students planning to progress need to maintain competitive grades through years one to three, a standard feature of Australian psychology accreditation nationwide, not unique to Murdoch, but one that shapes how seriously students need to take GPA management from first year.
curriculum:
Year 1: introduction to psychology, biological psychology, cognitive psychology, introductory statistics and research methods
Year 2: developmental psychology, social psychology, personality and individual differences, intermediate research methods
Year 3: abnormal psychology, psychological assessment, advanced statistics, discipline electives
Year 4 (Honours, separate accredited course): advanced seminars in applied psychology, supervised original empirical research project, thesis and conference-style poster presentation
Total: 3 years full-time (pass degree); Honours (4th year) APAC-accredited and required for provisional psychologist registration eligibility
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 70-75 (or equivalent); completion of WACE or equivalent secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Psychology Honours
description: The APAC-accredited fourth year of psychology study at Murdoch, taken after a three-year accredited psychology sequence. It combines advanced coursework with a supervised empirical research thesis, and completing it is a required step toward registration as a psychologist: graduates go on to a professional master's or doctorate, or the 5+1 internship pathway. Entry is competitive and based mainly on the grade average across core psychology units. The result is classified, and a higher classification improves access to the limited places in professional postgraduate programs. It suits psychology graduates committed to the professional pathway, and it also supports research and applied roles on its own.

name: Bachelor of Science / Doctor of Veterinary Medicine
description:
Murdoch runs the only veterinary school in Western Australia, and this is its flagship pathway: a three-year Bachelor of Science (Veterinary Biology) that transitions directly into a two-year Doctor of Veterinary Medicine, with the DVM itself run across trimesters rather than standard semesters to compress five years of content into the combined structure. Students don't apply separately into the DVM. The two qualifications are integrated by design, though academic progression standards still apply at the transition point.

The degree gives access to genuinely rare undergraduate infrastructure for an Australian veterinary program: a working teaching hospital treating companion animals, exotics, farm animals and horses, plus an operational farm, all on the same Perth campus rather than split across satellite sites. Species-group electives ("streaming") let students start weighting their final years toward large animal, equine or small animal practice depending on where they see their career heading, and the final year is largely spent immersed in the teaching hospital rather than in lecture theatres.

Because the DVM sits at AQF level 9, a master's-equivalent qualification, this is one of the longer and more structured pathways in the Murdoch catalogue, and the tuition reflects the cost of running live-animal clinical training rather than being comparable to a standard science degree.
curriculum:
Years 1–3 (Bachelor of Science, Veterinary Biology): animal biology and physiology, biochemistry, animal husbandry, foundational veterinary science units, six semesters total
Years 4–5 (Doctor of Veterinary Medicine, trimester-based): clinical veterinary training, species-group elective streaming (large animal, equine, small animal), professional and business skills for veterinary practice, six trimesters total
Final year: primarily hands-on clinical rotations through the on-campus veterinary teaching hospital and farm
Total: 5 years full-time, integrated BSc + DVM (AQF level 9 for the DVM component)
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 90+ (or equivalent), plus completion of Murdoch's veterinary science aptitude assessment and/or interview; highly competitive limited-entry program.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Bachelor of Science Honours
description: A one-year science honours year following a Bachelor of Science or a related degree at Murdoch, in a discipline such as biological science, chemistry, environmental science, physics, mathematics, or one of Murdoch's strengths in veterinary and animal science, agriculture and food science. It combines advanced research-methods coursework with a supervised research project and thesis. Entry requires a completed bachelor's degree with a strong grade average, usually a credit average or better, in the relevant field. The honours result is classified, and a first or upper second class is the standard requirement for PhD entry and research scholarships. It suits science graduates who want a research year before a doctorate or a research career.

Facilities include a dedicated exercise physiology lab, strength and conditioning and rehabilitation labs, and a performance lab with 3D motion capture and a 50-metre running track. Entry is an ATAR of about 70 with several alternative pathways. It suits students who want an applied sport science career, and it is the standard entry point to Murdoch's Master of Clinical Exercise Physiology for those going on to clinical practice.

There is no ATAR requirement: Year 12 graduates need a completed Australian Year 12 or equivalent, and others need post-secondary study or at least six months of work experience. On completion, students receive up to a year of credit toward Murdoch degrees including the Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Science and the Bachelor of Business. name: Doctor of Business Administration
description: Murdoch University's Doctor of Business Administration is a professional doctorate, about three years full-time equivalent, combining coursework with an applied research thesis. It differs from a PhD by targeting experienced professionals who want to investigate a practical problem and advance professional practice rather than pursue purely theoretical research. Candidates work within a core business discipline such as accounting, finance, management or marketing. Entry requires honours-level results, or a coursework master's with a distinction average plus at least three years of management experience, along with a research proposal and a nominated supervisor. Delivery is part-time or full-time with mixed-mode and face-to-face options at the Perth campus. Graduates move into consultancy, senior advisory and specialist leadership roles across industry, government and the not-for-profit sector.
admission_requirements: A master's degree in business (or equivalent) plus significant relevant professional experience (typically 5+ years).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Doctor of Education
description: Murdoch University's Doctor of Education is a professional doctorate, about three years full-time, combining coursework in research methods and education research topics with an applied research dissertation. It differs from a PhD by being built for practising education leaders who want to research a problem in their own context while staying in work. Supervision is available on campus or remotely to support working professionals. Research areas include school leadership, teacher development, Aboriginal education, educational technology and curriculum design. Entry requires an honours degree, a master's, or a bachelor's plus scholarly or professional achievement judged equivalent. Graduates are school principals, program and curriculum designers, university teachers and government advisers who want a doctoral qualification grounded in practice.
admission_requirements: A master's degree in education (or equivalent) plus significant relevant professional experience (typically 5+ years).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Doctor of Information Technology
description: A professional doctorate in information technology, combining coursework with an applied research thesis, aimed at experienced IT professionals who want to research a practical problem and advance professional practice rather than pursue purely theoretical work. Study areas reflect Murdoch's IT and computing research, such as cybersecurity, data science, networks and information systems. Entry normally requires honours-level results or a coursework master's with strong grades plus relevant professional experience, along with a research proposal and a nominated supervisor. Graduates move into senior technical, consulting and leadership roles, or academic positions. It suits senior IT practitioners who want a doctorate grounded in industry practice.
admission_requirements: A master's degree in IT/computing (or equivalent) plus significant relevant professional experience (typically 5+ years).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Doctor of Philosophy
description: Murdoch's research doctorate, normally four years of full-time candidature, ending in a thesis of no more than 100,000 words that makes an original contribution to knowledge. Admission requires a bachelor's degree with at least upper second class honours or equivalent postgraduate research preparation, plus a written proposal and a nominated supervisor. Candidature is offered across all disciplines, and Murdoch particularly encourages interdisciplinary work. Its recognised research strengths include veterinary and animal science, agriculture, food and environmental science, supported by facilities such as Whitby Falls Farm and the Nambeelup food research centre, alongside energy, health and social sciences. It suits people with a strong research background aiming at academic, industry or government research careers.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor honours degree (first or upper-second class) or a master's degree with a research component, or equivalent research experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Agriculture, Environmental and Related Studies
Doctor of Philosophy - Management and Commerce
Doctor of Psychology in Clinical Psychology
description: An intensive professional research doctorate in clinical psychology, about 3.5 years full-time, combining coursework, at least three supervised clinical placements through Murdoch's on-campus psychology clinic and external providers, and a major research project that makes an original contribution to knowledge in the context of practice. It is accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council as a packaged Level 3 to Level 4 course, so graduates are eligible to apply for registration with the Psychology Board of Australia with clinical endorsement. Entry is by transfer from the Master of Applied Psychology (Clinical Psychology) or direct entry with equivalent qualifications and current registration. It goes further than the clinical master's by adding a substantial doctoral research thesis. It suits people who want to practise as clinical psychologists and lead research.
admission_requirements: An honours degree (or equivalent GPA) in psychology accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council, plus a competitive selection interview.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Doctor of Veterinary Medical Science
description: A combined coursework and research doctorate in veterinary medical science, which Murdoch says is the only program of its kind in Western Australia. Candidates undertake advanced coursework and a substantial research project across veterinary disciplines such as epidemiology and public health, parasitology and clinical specialties, using Murdoch's veterinary facilities and the 203-hectare Whitby Falls Farm. Entry normally requires a veterinary science degree with at least upper second class honours, or a veterinary degree plus evidence of significant scholarly or professional achievement. Graduates move into senior research, clinical, industry and academic roles. It suits veterinarians who want an internationally recognised research qualification and advanced specialist training.
admission_requirements: A veterinary science degree (BVMS or equivalent) plus current veterinary registration and an approved research proposal.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: FlexiTrack High
description: A pathway at Murdoch for high-achieving Year 12 students who want an alternative route into a university degree. Rather than relying only on an ATAR, students take Murdoch study while still at school and, on meeting the requirements, receive a selection rank equivalent to 70 for entry to most Murdoch undergraduate degrees. It suits current secondary students who want to start building university credit and secure a pathway before they finish school.
admission_requirements: An in-school enabling pathway for Year 11/12 students not guaranteed a Selection Rank; delivered in partnership with participating high schools.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.5 (no band below 5.0), or equivalent, typical bar for enabling/pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Advanced Wound Care
description: Murdoch University's Graduate Certificate in Advanced Wound Care is a 12 credit point qualification for nurses and allied health clinicians, covering wound assessment, healing physiology, chronic and complex wounds and evidence-based management. It builds specialist skills that are in demand across acute, aged care and community settings, and can contribute credit toward further postgraduate nursing study. It suits practising clinicians who regularly manage wounds and want formal advanced training.
admission_requirements: A registered nursing qualification and current registration, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Asian Language
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in an Asian language, offered in languages such as Indonesian, covering language skills plus the cultural and regional context. It can be paired with an in-country study component and articulates toward Murdoch's graduate diploma in Asian language. It suits professionals and graduates who need working proficiency in an Asian language for work in trade, diplomacy, development or education.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; some prior language study preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Business Administration
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate covering the core of general management, the entry stage of Murdoch's MBA pathway. The units introduce leadership, finance, marketing and strategy and transfer in full toward the Graduate Diploma in Business Administration and then the MBA. Entry is open to graduates from any field, with professional experience considered. It suits people who want a short management credential, or a low-commitment start on the MBA with the option to continue in stages.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree plus at least 2-3 years of relevant professional work experience (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Cancer Nursing
description: Murdoch University's Graduate Certificate in Cancer Nursing is a 12 credit point course for registered nurses, covering the biology of cancer, treatment modalities, symptom and side-effect management and supportive and palliative care. It develops the specialist knowledge needed to work in oncology and haematology settings and can contribute credit toward further postgraduate nursing study. It suits registered nurses moving into or already working in cancer care who want a recognised specialty qualification.
admission_requirements: A registered nursing qualification and current registration, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Contemporary Mental Health
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate focused on contemporary mental health practice, one of the specialisation streams within Murdoch's Master of Health Care Management. It covers current models of mental health care, recovery-oriented practice and the service context, and the units transfer in full toward the graduate diploma and master's in this area. It suits health and community-sector staff who want a short, focused mental health qualification or a staged route into the master's.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in health/nursing/psychology, or equivalent clinical experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Counselling
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate introducing counselling theory and foundational skills, the entry stage of Murdoch's counselling pathway. The units transfer toward Murdoch's graduate diploma and master's in counselling. On its own it is an introductory qualification and not a route to practise as a counsellor. It suits people considering a move into counselling who want to test the field before committing to a longer program.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; some helping-profession experience preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Criminology
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate drawn from the early units of Murdoch's Master of Criminology, covering areas such as crime and criminal justice, policing, and research and analysis. It is open to graduates from outside criminology as well as people working in justice or policy, and the units transfer in full toward the Graduate Diploma and Master of Criminology. It suits people who want a short criminology credential for work, or a way to test the field before committing to the master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree (or equivalent); open to graduates from other fields and to people working in the justice sector.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Design Thinking
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in human-centred design, covering user research, empathy mapping, customer insight and prototyping for products and services, including a real client project. It is aimed at updating the skills of people across business, community development, engineering, design, health, IT, marketing and communication. The units transfer in full toward Murdoch's Graduate Diploma in Design Thinking and Service Innovation. It suits professionals who want to add structured design-thinking methods to their work.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent professional experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Education
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in education for people already working in education, covering learning theory, curriculum and evidence-informed practice. It is not an initial teaching qualification. The units transfer toward Murdoch's graduate diploma and master's in education. It suits practising teachers and education staff who want a short qualification to support progression, or a first step toward a master's.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; teaching or workplace-training experience preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Energy and Carbon Studies
Graduate Certificate in Environmental Assessment and Management
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in environmental assessment and management, covering environmental impact assessment, regulation, monitoring and management planning, drawing on Murdoch's environmental science staff and facilities. The units transfer toward Murdoch's graduate diploma and master's in environmental science. It suits people working in or moving into environmental roles in consulting, industry or government who want a short, applied qualification or a staged path to a master's.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in science, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Food Science
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in food science, covering food chemistry and microbiology, processing, safety and quality, drawing on Murdoch's agricultural and food science strengths. The units transfer toward Murdoch's graduate diploma and master's in food science, including its industry-practice master's. It suits people working in food manufacturing, quality or product development who want a formal food science qualification or a staged route into a master's.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in science, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Food Security
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in food security, drawing on Murdoch's Master of Food Security and its agricultural science base. It covers food production systems, resource constraints and the policy and social dimensions of securing food supply. The units transfer toward the graduate diploma and master's in food security. It suits science graduates and practitioners working on agriculture, food policy or development who want a short qualification or a staged route into the master's.
admission_requirements: An AQF Level 7 qualification in the plant, food, ecological, environmental or animal sciences, or an equivalent field.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Gerontological Healthcare
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in gerontological healthcare, one of the specialisation streams within Murdoch's Master of Health Care Management. It covers ageing, aged care models, and the clinical and service issues specific to older people, with units that transfer in full toward the graduate diploma and master's. It suits nurses, allied health staff and aged care managers who want a short qualification in older-person care or a staged path to the master's.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in health/nursing, or equivalent clinical experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Health Administration, Policy and Leadership
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate drawn from Murdoch's Master of Health Administration, Policy and Leadership, covering health policy, leadership and management and how they shape the health system. The units transfer in full toward the graduate diploma and master's, which is accredited by the Australasian College of Health Service Management. It suits clinicians and health staff moving into administration or policy who want a short qualification or a staged route into the master's.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; healthcare-sector experience preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Health Care Management
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate drawn from Murdoch's Master of Health Care Management, covering leadership and management for the health sector with an emphasis on patient safety, quality and clinical governance. The units transfer in full toward the graduate diploma and master's, and students can later specialise in gerontological healthcare or contemporary mental health. It suits health professionals moving into management who want a short qualification or a staged path to the master's.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; healthcare-sector experience preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in High Performance Sport
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate drawn from Murdoch's Master of High Performance Sport, covering applied testing and training practice, data analysis and evidence-based decision-making in elite sport. The units transfer in full toward the master's. Entry normally requires a bachelor's degree in a cognate area. It suits sport and exercise science graduates and practitioners who want a short high-performance qualification or a staged route into the master's.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in sport/exercise science, or equivalent; coaching or high-performance sport experience preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Human Resources Management
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in human resource management, covering recruitment and selection, employee relations, workforce planning and HR strategy. The units transfer toward Murdoch's graduate diploma and master's in human resource management, and the certificate aligns with the knowledge base recognised by the Australian HR Institute. It suits people moving into HR from another role, or HR staff who want a formal qualification and a staged path to a master's.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; some professional experience preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Infectious Disease
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in infectious disease, the entry stage of Murdoch's postgraduate infectious disease offering, covering the biology, surveillance and control of communicable disease, taught by researchers with laboratory facilities on the Perth campus. The units transfer in full toward the Graduate Diploma and the Master of Infectious Disease Surveillance and Control. Entry normally requires a science background. It suits science and health graduates who want a short qualification in infectious disease or a staged path to the master's.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in health/biomedical science, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Information Technology
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in information technology for graduates from any field, covering programming, systems, databases and networks, with no prior IT study assumed. The units transfer in full toward Murdoch's graduate diploma and master's in information technology, which offer specialisations in areas such as cybersecurity and data science. It suits career changers who want a short IT qualification, or a staged, lower-commitment route into a master's that lets them confirm the field suits them before committing.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; no prior IT background required for the standard entry stream.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in One Health
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in One Health, the interdisciplinary approach that connects human, animal and environmental health. It draws on Murdoch's combined strengths in veterinary science, public health and environmental science, covering zoonotic disease, antimicrobial resistance and cross-sector collaboration. It can lead into related postgraduate study in biosecurity and infectious disease. It suits people working across the human, animal and environment health interface who want a formal grounding in the One Health framework.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in health, veterinary, or environmental science, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Plant Biosecurity
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in plant biosecurity, drawing on Murdoch's strength in agricultural science and its Master of Biosecurity. It covers plant pest and disease identification, risk assessment and biosecurity policy and procedure, with flexible delivery designed for people working while they study. Units transfer toward Murdoch's biosecurity graduate diploma and master's. It suits people in agriculture, horticulture or plant health roles who want a formal plant biosecurity qualification.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in science/agriculture, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Policy and Development
Graduate Certificate in Project Management
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in project management, covering project planning and scheduling, risk and cost management, procurement and stakeholder engagement, with an emphasis on applying the methods to a real project context. The units transfer in full toward Murdoch's graduate diploma and master's in project management. It suits people moving into project coordination or management roles who want a short formal qualification, or a staged, lower-commitment route into the master's.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; some professional experience preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Protected Area Administration
Graduate Certificate in Public Administration
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in public administration, covering how government works: policy processes, public sector management, budgeting, governance and accountability. The units transfer in full toward Murdoch's graduate diploma and master's in public policy and administration. It suits public servants and people entering the sector who want a formal qualification to support progression, or a short, lower-commitment step toward the master's while they decide whether to continue.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; relevant public-sector experience preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Public Policy
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in public policy, covering the policy cycle, policy analysis and evaluation, and the political and institutional context of policymaking in Australia. The units transfer in full toward Murdoch's graduate diploma and master's in the field. It suits people working in or moving into policy and program roles across government and the community sector who want a formal grounding, or a short first step toward the master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree (or equivalent); open to graduates from any field and to people working in government.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Tertiary and Adult Education
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in tertiary and adult education, for people who teach or train in universities, vocational education, workplaces and community settings. It covers adult learning principles, course and session design, assessment and facilitation. The units transfer toward Murdoch's graduate diploma in education for tertiary and workplace contexts. It suits lecturers, trainers, clinical educators and workplace learning staff who want a formal teaching qualification for adult learners.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; teaching or workplace-training experience preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate of Forensic Science (Professional Practice)
Graduate Diploma in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science
Graduate Diploma in Asian Language (In-country)
description: Murdoch University's Graduate Diploma in Asian Language (In-country) is a 24 credit point course: students spend a period studying the language in a country where it is spoken, alongside coursework in language and regional studies. It builds on the graduate certificate in Asian language. It suits people who want to reach a strong working level in an Asian language and gain the immersion experience that supports it.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; some prior language study preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Australian Migration Law and Practice
description: Murdoch University's Graduate Diploma in Australian Migration Law and Practice is a 24 credit point course and the OMARA-recognised entry qualification for becoming a registered migration agent in Australia. It covers migration law, visa categories, the practice and ethics of migration advice and case management, taught by academics and practitioners, with an optional internship in a law firm, government agency or not-for-profit. A law degree is not required and the course is open to all backgrounds, though it is also useful for lawyers adding migration work. Completing the diploma and passing the OMARA Capstone assessment makes a graduate eligible to register as a migration agent. It suits people entering migration advice work and lawyers expanding into the area.
admission_requirements: A Bachelor of Laws (or equivalent), and current or eligible registration as a migration agent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Clinical Exercise Physiology
Graduate Diploma in Community Development
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in community development, sitting between Murdoch's graduate certificate and the Master of Community Development. It covers community development ideas and practice through work with real, active community projects, from remote-area cultural projects to urban sustainability and grassroots arts. All units transfer in full toward the master's. Entry is open to graduates and practitioners from a range of backgrounds. It suits community-sector workers who want a substantial qualification with the option to complete the master's later.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; community-sector experience preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Counselling
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in counselling, sitting between Murdoch's graduate certificate and master's in counselling. It extends the certificate with further theory, skills practice and the beginnings of supervised work. All units transfer in full toward the master's, which carries the substantial supervised placement and professional recognition. The diploma is an intermediate qualification and not a route to independent practice on its own. It suits people moving into counselling who want a substantial qualification and a staged path to the master's.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; some helping-profession experience preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Creative Arts Therapies
description: The 24 credit point first year of Murdoch's Master of Creative Arts Therapies, which Murdoch says is the only program of its kind in Western Australia. Study is highly experiential, taught in purpose-built creative arts therapies spaces through workshops and supervised practice, and covers arts psychotherapy theory and foundational practice. Completing the diploma is the entry point to the master's year, where students build toward professional membership with ANZACATA and Level 2 membership with the Australian Counselling Association. Entry involves a creative practice portfolio and an interview. It suits people committed to training as creative arts therapists.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in arts, health, or a related discipline, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Criminology
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in criminology, sitting between Murdoch's Graduate Certificate and Master of Criminology. It extends the certificate with further study in crime, justice, policing and research methods. All units transfer in full toward the master's. It is open to graduates from other fields and to people working in the justice sector. It suits people who want a substantial criminology qualification with the option to complete the master's later.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree (or equivalent); open to graduates from other fields and to people working in the justice sector.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Cyber Security and Networking
Graduate Diploma in Design Thinking and Service Innovation
description: Murdoch University's Graduate Diploma in Design Thinking and Service Innovation is a 24 credit point course that takes a human-centred approach to innovation, rethinking product and service experiences around the customer. Developed with industry, it launches students into a real project problem with a local industry partner, working in a project team across connected units, plus two electives in areas such as web strategy, community development or organisational change. It builds on the Graduate Certificate in Design Thinking, whose units transfer in. It suits people who want to lead service and product innovation and work directly with industry on live problems.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent professional experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Education (Tertiary and Workplace)
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in education for tertiary and workplace settings, sitting above the graduate certificate in tertiary and adult education. It covers adult learning, curriculum and program design, assessment, and evaluating teaching, for people who teach in universities, vocational education, workplaces and professional training. All units transfer toward Murdoch's master's in this area. It suits lecturers, trainers and workplace educators who want a substantial teaching qualification for adult and post-school learners.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; teaching or workplace-training experience preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Energy and Carbon Studies
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in energy and carbon studies, part of Murdoch's long-running energy studies program. It covers renewable and sustainable energy technologies, energy policy and markets, and carbon measurement and management. It articulates toward Murdoch's Master of Renewable and Sustainable Energy. It suits engineers, scientists and policy professionals who want a substantial qualification in the energy transition with the option to continue to the master's.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in science/engineering, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Energy and the Environment
Graduate Diploma in Environmental Science
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in environmental science, sitting between a graduate certificate and Murdoch's master's in the field. It covers ecosystem and conservation science, environmental assessment and management, and research skills, using Murdoch's field sites and laboratories. All units transfer toward the master's. It suits science graduates and environment-sector professionals who want a substantial qualification with the option to continue to the master's.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in science, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Extractive Metallurgy
description: Murdoch University's Graduate Diploma in Extractive Metallurgy is a 24 credit point course for people working in or entering the minerals industry, covering mineral processing and comminution, hydrometallurgy and pyrometallurgy, process metallurgy and the economics of mineral resources. Teaching is by staff with industry and research backgrounds, and while much of the course is available online, on-campus laboratory sessions are required for the practicum unit. It also prepares students for higher degree study in extractive metallurgy. It suits minerals-industry professionals who need specialist metallurgical knowledge or a step toward a master's or PhD.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in engineering/science, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Food Science
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in food science, sitting between a graduate certificate and Murdoch's master's in the field. It extends the certificate with further study in food processing, safety, quality systems and product development. All units transfer toward the master's, including its industry-practice version. It suits food-industry professionals who want a substantial qualification with the option to complete the master's later.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in science, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Forensic Science (Professional Practice)
Graduate Diploma in Gerontological Healthcare
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in gerontological healthcare, sitting between the graduate certificate and Murdoch's Master of Health Care Management with a gerontological specialisation. It extends the certificate with further study in ageing, aged care services and leadership in the sector. All units transfer in full toward the master's. It suits aged care clinicians and managers who want a substantial qualification with the option to finish the master's later.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in health/nursing, or equivalent clinical experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Human Resources Management
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in human resource management, sitting between the graduate certificate and Murdoch's master's in the field. It extends the certificate with further study in employment law, remuneration, learning and development and strategic HR. All units transfer toward the master's. It suits HR practitioners who want a substantial qualification with the option to complete the master's later.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; some professional experience preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Infectious Disease
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in infectious disease, sitting between Murdoch's graduate certificate and the Master of Infectious Disease Surveillance and Control. It extends the certificate with further study in outbreak investigation, surveillance systems and laboratory methods. All units transfer in full toward the master's. It suits science and health graduates who want a substantial infectious disease qualification with the option to complete the master's later.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in health/biomedical science, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Information Technology
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in information technology, sitting between Murdoch's graduate certificate and master's in the field. It covers programming, databases, networks, cybersecurity fundamentals and a project component, with no prior IT degree assumed. All units transfer toward the master's. It suits career changers who want a substantial IT qualification with the option to complete the master's later.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; no prior IT background required for the standard entry stream.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Information Technology Management
Graduate Diploma in Internetworking and Security
Graduate Diploma in Psychology (Advanced)
description: Murdoch University's Graduate Diploma in Psychology (Advanced) is an APAC-accredited fourth-year psychology qualification, one year full-time or part-time equivalent, for graduates who have completed an accredited three-year psychology sequence. It combines advanced coursework with a group research project written up as an individual thesis, and is offered at the Perth and Singapore campuses. Entry normally requires a credit average or better across undergraduate psychology units. On completion, graduates are eligible for provisional registration with the Psychology Board of Australia and can apply for a professional master's such as the Master of Applied Psychology (Clinical) or (Professional). It suits psychology graduates continuing on the path toward registration as a psychologist.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in psychology (or equivalent) meeting APAC pre-registration requirements.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Veterinary Clinical Studies
Graduate Diploma in Web Communication
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in web communication, covering web strategy and planning, content development, user experience, analytics and the management of digital communication projects. It sits within Murdoch's media and communication postgraduate offering, is taught with practical project work, and can articulate toward a related master's. It suits communication, marketing and content staff who want substantial, current skills in digital and web communication, or a qualification to move into a digital-focused role.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree (or equivalent); relevant work experience may be considered.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: K-Track
description: A fee-free 15-week enabling program at Murdoch's Perth campus for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students who want to move into an undergraduate degree without the usual prerequisites, starting from around Year 10 level. Study is on campus, full-time over four days a week or part-time across two semesters, in classes capped at 30 for close support. The curriculum covers academic writing, referencing, essay structure, scientific method and study skills such as time management and critical thinking. Because it is classed as full-time study, students may be eligible for Centrelink payments. On completion at the required standard, students qualify to apply for entry to a Murdoch undergraduate degree. It suits First Nations students, including mature-age applicants, returning to or entering formal study.
admission_requirements: Available to Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander students who have not received an ATAR or completed Year 12; no academic prerequisites.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.5 (no band below 5.0), or equivalent, typical bar for enabling/pathway programs.

name: Law Honours
description: The honours year in law at Murdoch, taken alongside or after the later years of the Bachelor of Laws for students who meet the grade threshold. It involves a supervised research thesis on a legal question, in areas that reflect Murdoch's strengths such as public and constitutional law, resources and environmental law, and law and society, together with legal research training. Selection is based on grade average in law subjects. The honours result is classified, and a first or upper second class supports entry to a PhD, associateships with judges, and competitive graduate roles. It suits law students aiming at research, the judiciary or academically demanding practice areas.
admission_requirements: Completion of the corresponding pass degree (or equivalent) with a minimum GPA of approximately 5.5/7.0, or direct entry with an ATAR of approximately 80+ for high-achieving Year 12 entrants.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Applied Psychology
description: Murdoch's professional psychology master's, offered in two streams: a Clinical Psychology stream and a Professional stream, both APAC-accredited as packaged Level 3 to Level 4 courses. They form the fifth and sixth year of the psychology training pathway, combining advanced coursework, supervised placements through the on-campus psychology clinic and external services, and a research project. Entry requires an accredited fourth year of psychology, usually with a credit average or better, or equivalent qualifications with current registration. Graduates are eligible to apply for registration with the Psychology Board of Australia, with clinical endorsement available through the clinical stream. It suits psychology graduates completing the path to practise as a registered psychologist.
admission_requirements: An honours degree (or equivalent GPA) in psychology accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Applied Psychology in Clinical Psychology
Master of Applied Psychology in Organisational Psychology
Master of Biosecurity
description: A postgraduate degree in biosecurity, which Murdoch says was the first master's of its kind in Australia. The content was developed with input from Australia, New Zealand, Canada and the United States, so it covers international biosecurity requirements as well as domestic ones, and teaches students to identify, assess and mitigate biosecurity risks and to develop, implement and evaluate biosecurity policy and procedure. Delivery is flexible: full-time or part-time, and designed so students can study from another country while working. Graduates work in technical, research and administrative roles in quarantine and pest and disease management with state agriculture departments, state and federal biosecurity agencies, Plant Health Australia, Animal Health Australia, private industry and international equivalents. It suits people already working in agriculture, environment or border roles who want a formal biosecurity qualification.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in science/agriculture, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Murdoch's MBA is a comparatively compact program by design, aimed at working professionals rather than career-switchers straight out of undergrad, and the course leans on Perth's business environment (mining and resources, agribusiness and government) for its case material and guest-lecturer network more than trying to compete with the east-coast MBAs on global brand recognition alone.

Coursework covers the standard MBA core (strategy, finance, leadership, marketing) but Murdoch places a specific emphasis on practical applied projects tied to real organisations, consistent with the university's broader Work Integrated Learning approach that shows up across its business degrees. Students without an undergraduate business background typically complete foundation units before the core MBA content, which widens entry beyond commerce graduates to professionals moving into management from technical or clinical careers.

The program is positioned as a flexible, often part-time-friendly qualification for working Western Australians rather than a full-time residential cohort experience, which shapes its delivery mode and scheduling more than curriculum content.
curriculum:
Foundation units (if required): accounting and finance fundamentals, economics for managers, quantitative methods
Core: strategic management, organisational leadership, corporate finance, marketing management, operations and supply chain management
Applied learning: business consulting project or work-based capstone tied to a real organisation
Electives: choice from areas such as international business, human resource management, or project management
Total: typically 1.5–2 years part-time (accelerated full-time options available)
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree plus at least 2-3 years of relevant professional work experience (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Business Administration (Global)
description:
Murdoch University's Master of Business Administration (Global) is a two-year MBA (48 credit points) that, unlike most Australian MBAs, requires no prior work experience, so it is built for early-career graduates and international students as much as for established managers. The core covers management, marketing, accounting, finance, strategy, and professional ethics, and students then choose a focus area such as business finance, people management, sustainability, health management, or international marketing.

A work-integrated learning component places students with local businesses and government departments for a professional placement or applied research project. It runs face-to-face and online with three intakes a year (trimesters). Entry is a bachelor's degree, or a portfolio route with a CV, a GMAT or GRE score, and an 800-word statement. It suits people using the MBA to change career direction or to build a general management base early rather than to convert existing seniority into a formal qualification.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree plus at least 2-3 years of relevant professional work experience (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Business Administration / Master of Health Care Management
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree plus at least 2-3 years of relevant professional work experience (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Business Administration / Master of Human Resources Management
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree plus at least 2-3 years of relevant professional work experience (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Clinical Chiropractic
description:
A two-year graduate-entry master's that, combined with an approved bachelor's degree, completes the qualification needed to practise as a chiropractor. Entry requires a cognate bachelor's degree with a GPA of at least 2.0 and completed tertiary units in human anatomy and human physiology within the last ten years; at Murdoch the usual feeder is the Bachelor of Health Science.

The program is accredited by the Council on Chiropractic Education Australasia, so graduates are eligible for registration with the Chiropractic Board of Australia and in New Zealand, with pathways to recognition in several other countries. Clinical training runs in Murdoch's teaching clinic. It suits health science graduates committed to a manual, primary-contact allied health career.
admission_requirements: Completion of the corresponding Bachelor of Health Science (Chiropractic) or equivalent pre-clinical qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Clinical Exercise Physiology
description:
Murdoch University's Master of Clinical Exercise Physiology is a one-year degree (three trimesters) that builds on an exercise science background to qualify graduates as clinical exercise physiologists. It covers exercise prescription, clinical assessment and behaviour change for chronic disease management, and includes a year-long industry placement working alongside Accredited Exercise Physiologists and other health professionals.

The program is accredited by Exercise and Sports Science Australia at exercise physiology level, so graduates are eligible to apply to register with ESSA as an Accredited Exercise Physiologist. Entry requires a weighted average of at least 60 in prior study plus current ESSA Exercise Scientist registration, a recent ESSA-accredited exercise science degree, or completion of a graduate entry assessment. Facilities include physiology laboratories and a performance centre with 3D motion capture. It suits exercise science graduates moving into clinical practice with chronic and complex conditions.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in exercise/sport science, or equivalent, meeting ESSA accreditation prerequisites.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Communication
description:
Murdoch University's Master of Communication is a two-year degree (48 credit points) covering strategic communication and planning, social media and digital strategy, global communication, cultural and media studies, and the ethical side of communication and public relations, with a coursework or research-thesis route and a possible 18-month completion with prior credit.

Students work with real clients through MESH, an on-campus communication consultancy, and a work-integrated learning placement is part of the program. Entry is a communication or related bachelor's degree, or substantial industry experience (about ten years in media and communication, or five in a management role), which opens it to career changers. It suits people moving toward senior roles in communication, PR, digital strategy or media.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in communication or a related field, or substantial industry experience (about ten years in media and communication, or five in a management role).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Community Development
description: Murdoch University's Master of Community Development is a postgraduate degree covering the ideas and practices used to support community-led change in Australia and internationally. Students work with real, active community projects, ranging from cultural-strength projects in remote areas to urban agriculture, sustainability and grassroots creative arts initiatives. Entry requires a recognised bachelor's degree or higher, or equivalent training and experience, and it does not need to be in a directly related field. Graduates work in community and social services, local government, humanitarian organisations and NGOs, aid work, social and economic planning, sustainable development and Indigenous governance. It suits community-sector practitioners who want to deepen their practice and move into planning, coordination and leadership roles, as well as graduates entering the field.
