Students explore the evolving media landscape from traditional newsrooms to digital platforms, develop practical skills in writing, reporting and multimedia production across print, broadcast and online, and engage in real-world learning through internships, newsroom simulations and live media projects. Graduates work as journalists, reporters, editors and producers, and in communication roles.

name: Bachelor of Justice
description: The Bachelor of Justice at QUT draws on criminology, policing, policy, governance, intelligence, investigations, sociology, law, psychology and ethics, with three majors: Criminology and Violence Prevention, Investigations and Intelligence, and Policy, Politics and Social Reform. Students build real-world experience through industry projects and justice work placements, including options in First Nations justice sectors. Graduates work in criminology, violence prevention, advocacy, government, law enforcement and policing, corrections, and intelligence and security roles.

name: Bachelor of Laws (Honours)
description:
QUT's law degree is a Queensland-facing professional qualification first and a general humanities degree second. The course is built to satisfy the academic requirements for admission as a lawyer in Queensland, which means the compulsory Priestley 11 subjects (contracts, torts, property, criminal law, evidence, equity, and the rest) anchor the structure regardless of which electives students choose around them. The Honours component is built into the four-year degree rather than bolted on, reflecting a fairly common structure among Queensland law schools.

QUT Business School and Law sit close to Brisbane's legal and government precinct, and the faculty runs clinical legal education options: supervised work on real client matters through a legal practice clinic, which is a more hands-on alternative to purely theoretical electives for students wanting practice experience before graduate positions. Moot court and advocacy training are also a visible part of the elective offering.

Most QUT law graduates go on to complete Practical Legal Training (PLT) before admission, since the LLB itself covers the academic but not the practical-skills admission requirement, a distinction worth knowing going in, since the degree alone doesn't make you an admitted lawyer.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Law and Legal Reasoning, Contract Law A and B, Torts Law, foundational elective units
Year 2: Property Law, Criminal Law, Administrative Law, Equity and Trusts
Year 3: Evidence, Civil Procedure, Company Law, elective law units (commercial, criminal justice or public law strands)
Year 4: Legal Ethics and Professional Responsibility, an Honours research or clinical legal education unit, remaining electives, capstone units
Throughout: option to undertake clinical legal education working on real client matters; moot court and advocacy electives available
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12, ATAR approx. 85-90
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Mathematics
description: QUT's Bachelor of Mathematics is a three-year undergraduate degree in the Faculty of Science, taught at the Brisbane campuses. Students choose from three majors and apply mathematical and statistical methods to real problems in finance, logistics, health, environmental management and technology. QUT ranks tenth in Australia for statistics and operational research in the QS subject rankings. Graduates work as analysts, statisticians and modellers across industry, government and research.

name: Bachelor of Media and Communication
description: Media and communication at QUT is offered through the Bachelor of Communication with a Media and Communication Industries major, taught at Australia's number one ranked university for communication and media studies. Students master digital trends, audience analysis, media and data analytics, then specialise with in-demand skills, with real-world learning through industry expert teachers, real client briefs and the world-leading Digital Media Research Centre. Graduates work across media, entertainment, digital content, communications and creative industries.

name: Bachelor of Medical Imaging (Honours)
description: QUT's Bachelor of Medical Imaging (Honours) is a four-year undergraduate degree in the Faculty of Health, taught at the Brisbane campuses with clinical placements. It trains diagnostic radiographers in imaging techniques, anatomy and patient care, with an embedded honours research component. Graduates are eligible to apply for registration as diagnostic radiographers and work in hospitals, private imaging practices and research.

name: Bachelor of Medical Laboratory Science
description: QUT's Bachelor of Medical Laboratory Science is a four-year undergraduate degree in the Faculty of Health, taught at the Brisbane campuses with laboratory and placement components. It trains medical scientists in the diagnostic testing that underpins clinical decisions, across disciplines such as haematology, microbiology, histopathology and clinical biochemistry. Graduates work in hospital and private pathology laboratories and in research.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
The QUT nursing degree is built to the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia's registration standard, so a fixed number of clinical placement hours (roughly 800 to 840 depending on the placement mix in a given year) sit alongside the classroom and simulation content. This isn't optional or supplementary; it's what makes the degree a registration pathway rather than a health-science degree with a nursing flavour. QUT runs its own clinical simulation labs at Kelvin Grove that mimic hospital ward environments, which is where students first practise procedures before moving into real clinical placements across Brisbane's public and private hospital network.

The course structure moves from foundational anatomy, physiology and pharmacology in first year through medical-surgical nursing, mental health nursing and maternal/child health in the middle years, to more specialised and leadership-oriented content by final year, including a period of near-graduate-level practice placement intended to smooth the transition into a graduate nurse program.

Queensland's public hospital system is the main employer destination for most graduates, and QUT's placement partnerships with Metro North and Metro South health services give students a reasonably direct line into graduate program applications at those services.
curriculum:
Year 1: Anatomy and Physiology, Foundations of Nursing Practice, Pharmacology basics, first clinical placement block
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing I and II, Mental Health Nursing, Pathophysiology, ongoing clinical placements
Year 3: Maternal and Child Health Nursing, Complex Care Nursing, Leadership in Nursing Practice, extended clinical placement block including a transition-to-practice rotation
Throughout: approximately 800+ hours of NMBA-mandated clinical placement across Brisbane public and private health services; simulation lab training precedes most placement blocks
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12, ATAR approx. 70-75; open to domestic students only
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 6.5

name: Bachelor of Nutrition Science
description: QUT's Bachelor of Nutrition Science is a three-year undergraduate degree in the Faculty of Health, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It covers the science of nutrition and its application to individual and population health, and is a nutrition science rather than a dietetics qualification, so it does not by itself lead to dietitian registration. Graduates work as nutritionists, community and public health nutrition officers and health educators, or continue to a dietetics master's.

name: Bachelor of Paramedic Science
description: QUT's Bachelor of Paramedic Science is a three-year undergraduate degree in the Faculty of Health, taught at the Brisbane campuses with clinical and ambulance placements. It trains students in out-of-hospital emergency care, clinical assessment and patient management, with course content reviewed with industry to reflect current practice. Graduates are eligible to apply for registration as paramedics and work in ambulance services, retrieval and event health.

name: Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours)
description: QUT's Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours) is a four-year undergraduate degree in the Faculty of Health, taught at the Brisbane campuses with placements in community and hospital pharmacies. It combines pharmaceutical science, clinical practice and an honours research component, and makes graduates eligible for the supervised internship year that leads to registration as a pharmacist. Graduates work as community and hospital pharmacists and in pharmaceutical research.

name: Bachelor of Podiatry
description: QUT's Bachelor of Podiatry is a four-year undergraduate degree in the Faculty of Health, taught at the Brisbane campuses with extensive clinical placements. It trains students to assess and treat conditions of the foot, ankle and lower limb across the lifespan, and graduates are eligible to apply for registration with the Podiatry Board of Australia. They work in private practice, public health services and multidisciplinary clinics.

name: Bachelor of Property Economics
description: QUT's Bachelor of Property Economics is a three-year undergraduate degree in the Faculty of Business and Law, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It covers property valuation, investment, finance, development and the law and economics of real estate, with industry-connected projects, and is aligned to the professional pathways in the property industry. Graduates work in valuation, property investment and analysis, development and property consulting.

name: Bachelor of Science (Environmental Science)
description:
Set against Queensland's own environmental pressure points (the Great Barrier Reef, coastal development, bushfire risk, water catchment management), QUT's environmental science major has a fairly local flavour compared to a generic environmental degree, with field trips and research projects that draw on southeast Queensland ecosystems and QUT researchers' active work in reef and catchment science. The degree sits inside the broader Bachelor of Science framework, so students get a solid grounding in chemistry, biology and earth systems before specialising.

Field work is a real component rather than an occasional add-on: students can expect sampling trips, ecological survey work and lab analysis built into core units, not just theoretical coverage of environmental monitoring techniques. The later years let students lean toward conservation biology, environmental management, or more policy-and-planning-adjacent content depending on career direction.

Career outcomes split fairly evenly between government environmental agencies (state Department of Environment roles, local council sustainability positions) and private environmental consulting firms doing impact assessments for development and infrastructure projects. QUT's Brisbane location puts it close to both sectors.
curriculum:
Year 1: Chemistry I, Biology of Organisms, Earth Systems Science, Introduction to Environmental Science
Year 2: Ecology, Environmental Chemistry, Geographic Information Systems, field-based sampling and survey units
Year 3: Conservation Biology, Environmental Management and Policy, Water and Catchment Science, a research project unit
Throughout: field trips and ecological survey work built into core units; research projects often connect to QUT's applied reef and catchment research groups
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12, ATAR approx. 70-75
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Science Advanced (Honours)
description: QUT's Bachelor of Science Advanced (Honours) is a four-year undergraduate degree in the Faculty of Science, built for high-achieving students heading toward research. Students choose from five majors and take an embedded honours year, working with research groups on original projects. Teaching is at the Brisbane campuses, and students with a strong ATAR may be eligible for QUT Excellence Scholarships. Graduates work as research scientists, chemists and biologists, or continue to a PhD.

name: Bachelor of Social Work
description: The Bachelor of Social Work at QUT prepares students to promote social justice and facilitate progressive change with individuals, families, groups and communities. Core units cover trauma and addictions, mental health, mediation, gender and diversity, community development, Indigenous rights and perspectives, child protection, youth and family practice, disability, social policy and climate action, with 1,000 hours of supervised professional placement. Graduates receive international recognition and are eligible for Australian Association of Social Workers membership, working in child protection, health, mental health, community development and policy.

name: Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Science
description: QUT's Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Science is a three-year undergraduate degree in the Faculty of Health, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It provides a pathway to accreditation as an Accredited Exercise Scientist or Accredited Sports Scientist, covering exercise physiology, biomechanics, motor control and performance analysis with practical placements. Graduates work in strength and conditioning, performance analysis, corporate health and community fitness, and often continue to clinical exercise physiology study.

name: Bachelor of Vision Science
description: QUT's Bachelor of Vision Science is a three-year undergraduate degree in the Faculty of Health, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It is the first stage of QUT's five-year optometry pathway: graduates continue to the Master of Optometry and are then eligible to register with the Optometry Board of Australia. The degree covers ocular anatomy, optics, visual science and clinical skills. Graduates who complete the master's practise as optometrists.

name: Diploma in Architectural Studies
description: QUT's Diploma in Architectural Studies is a one-year pathway program offered through QUT College at the Brisbane campuses. It gives students the foundation knowledge and English-language preparation to enter QUT's architecture and built environment degrees with advanced standing. Graduates progress into the Bachelor of Design (Architecture) and related programs.

name: Diploma in Creative Industries
description: The Diploma in Creative Industries at Queensland University of Technology is a one-year diploma. It is offered through the Faculty of Creative Industries, Education and Social Justice. The course provides a pathway into QUT's Bachelor of Communication, Bachelor of Design, Bachelor of Design, International, or Bachelor of Creative Arts (excluding acting). Successful graduates will receive up to 1 year of credit for prior learning (advanced standing) towards their chosen Bachelor degree. The course sits within QUT's creative arts and english and pathway programs study areas. Graduates pursue roles such as arts administrator, communication specialist, creative director and creative entrepreneur. Indicative international tuition is $28,200 per course for 2027 entry. The course holds CRICOS registration 081617G.

name: Diploma in Engineering
description: The Diploma in Engineering at Queensland University of Technology is a one-year diploma. It is offered through the Faculty of Engineering. The Diploma in Engineering offers a supportive pathway into the Bachelor of Engineering (Honours), helping students develop the knowledge, confidence and practical skills to succeed. Graduates pursue roles such as aerospace avionics engineer, biomechanical engineer, biomedical engineer and chemical engineer.

name: Diploma in Information Technology
description: The Diploma in Information Technology at Queensland University of Technology is a one-year diploma. It is offered through the Faculty of Science. The course provides a pathway into QUT's Bachelor of Information Technology. Successful graduates will receive 1 year of credit for prior learning (advanced standing) towards the Bachelor of Information Technology. Graduates pursue roles such as computer game programmer, computer scientist, computer-aided designer and database manager.

name: Graduate Certificate in Business and Communication
Graduate Certificate in Business Process Management
description: The Graduate Certificate in Business Process Management at Queensland University of Technology is a six-month graduate certificate. It is offered through the Faculty of Science. This course offers Commonwealth Supported Places, making it more than 60% more affordable. Graduates pursue roles such as business analyst, consultant, operations manager and systems analyst.

name: Graduate Certificate in Communication for Engineering
Graduate Certificate in Communication for Health
Graduate Certificate in Communication for Information Technology
Graduate Certificate in Cyber Security and Networks
Graduate Certificate in Data Science
description: The Graduate Certificate in Data Science at Queensland University of Technology is a six-month graduate certificate. It is offered through the Faculty of Science. Graduates pursue roles such as data analyst, data scientist, data systems developer and data-driven decision maker.

name: Graduate Certificate in Digital Business and Innovation
description: The Graduate Certificate in Digital Business and Innovation at Queensland University of Technology is a six-month graduate certificate. It is offered through the Faculty of Business and Law.

name: Graduate Certificate in Digital Communication
description: The Graduate Certificate in Digital Communication at Queensland University of Technology is a six-month graduate certificate. It is offered through the Faculty of Creative Industries, Education and Social Justice. Graduates pursue roles such as digital content producer, digital journalist, digital performance analyst and social media entrepreneur.

name: Graduate Certificate in Education
description: The Graduate Certificate in Education at Queensland University of Technology is a six-month graduate certificate. It is offered through the Faculty of Creative Industries, Education and Social Justice. This course is one of many Commonwealth Supported Places that QUT has secured to make postgraduate study more affordable and accessible. The Graduate Certificate in Education does not lead to teacher registration. Students select from 7 available majors.

name: Graduate Certificate in Information Technology
description: The Graduate Certificate in Information Technology at Queensland University of Technology is a six-month graduate certificate. It is offered through the Faculty of Science. Graduates pursue roles such as computer scientist, computer systems engineer, computer-aided designer and data communications specialist.

name: Graduate Certificate in Project Management
description: The Graduate Certificate in Project Management at Queensland University of Technology is a six-month graduate certificate. It is offered through the Faculty of Engineering. Graduates pursue roles such as change management specialist, portfolio manager, program manager and project contract manager.

name: Graduate Certificate in Strategic Design
description: The Graduate Certificate in Strategic Design at Queensland University of Technology is a six-month graduate certificate. It is offered through the Faculty of Creative Industries, Education and Social Justice. Graduates pursue roles such as business analyst, design strategist, design thinking facilitator and entrepreneur.

name: Graduate Diploma in Digital Communication
description: The Graduate Diploma in Digital Communication at Queensland University of Technology is a one-year graduate diploma. It is offered through the Faculty of Creative Industries, Education and Social Justice. QUT is ranked number 33 in the world and number 1 in Queensland for media and communications studies at university (QS World Rankings, 2025). Graduates pursue roles such as digital content producer, digital journalist, digital performance analyst and social media entrepreneur.

name: Graduate Diploma in Environmental Health
description: The Graduate Diploma in Environmental Health at Queensland University of Technology is a one-year graduate diploma. It is offered through the Faculty of Health. Graduates pursue roles such as environmental health officer, government officer, policy officer and public health officer.

name: Graduate Diploma in Health Management and Leadership
description: QUT's Graduate Diploma in Health Management and Leadership is a one-year qualification in the Faculty of Health, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It builds the skills to manage health services and lead teams, covering health systems, quality, finance and workforce, and can articulate into the master's. Graduates work as managers and program leads across hospitals, primary care and government.

name: Graduate Diploma in Information Technology
description: The Graduate Diploma in Information Technology at Queensland University of Technology is a one-year graduate diploma. It is offered through the Faculty of Science. This course offers Commonwealth Supported Places which makes it over 60% more affordable. Cyber security roles alone are projected to grow by 38 percent by 2030, reflecting urgent national skills needs (AustCyber). Graduates pursue roles such as computer scientist, computer systems engineer, computer-aided designer and data communications specialist.

name: Graduate Diploma in Legal Practice
description: The Graduate Diploma in Legal Practice at Queensland University of Technology is a six-month graduate diploma. It is offered through the Faculty of Business and Law. Graduates pursue roles such as barrister, crown law officer, in-house lawyer and solicitor.

name: Graduate Diploma in Occupational Health and Safety
description: The Graduate Diploma in Occupational Health and Safety at Queensland University of Technology is a one-year graduate diploma. It is offered through the Faculty of Health. The course is accredited by the Australian OHS Education Accreditation Board. Graduates pursue roles such as occupational health and safety adviser, occupational health and safety coordinator, occupational health and safety manager and senior adviser (health and safety).

name: Graduate Diploma in Public Health
description: The Graduate Diploma in Public Health at Queensland University of Technology is a one-year graduate diploma. It is offered through the Faculty of Health. Graduates pursue roles such as community health officer, health promotion officer, policy officer and project manager.

name: Graduate Diploma in Strategic Design
description: The Graduate Diploma in Strategic Design at Queensland University of Technology is a one-year graduate diploma. It is offered through the Faculty of Creative Industries, Education and Social Justice. This course is a career-focused learning experience that is a solid pathway to further studies such as the Master of Design (Strategic Design) or research-based careers. Graduates pursue roles such as business analyst, design strategist, design thinking facilitator and entrepreneur.

name: Master of Advanced Manufacturing
description: QUT's Master of Advanced Manufacturing is an 18-month degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It builds engineering skills in automation, additive manufacturing, robotics and digital production for a sector the Federal Government is backing through the National Reconstruction Fund. Domestic full-time students are offered Commonwealth Supported Places. Graduates work as automation, industrial, operations and process engineers.

name: Master of Advanced Manufacturing with Data Analytics
description: QUT's Master of Advanced Manufacturing with Data Analytics is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It pairs the advanced manufacturing curriculum, covering automation, robotics and digital production, with data analytics, so graduates can both design modern production systems and use the data they generate. Graduates work as automation, industrial, operations and process engineers with an analytics focus.

name: Master of Advanced Manufacturing with Project Management
description: QUT's Master of Advanced Manufacturing with Project Management is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It pairs the advanced manufacturing curriculum, covering automation, robotics and digital production, with project management, preparing graduates to lead manufacturing and automation projects. Graduates work as automation, industrial, operations and process engineers moving into project and delivery roles.

name: Master of Advanced Robotics and Artificial Intelligence
description: QUT's Master of Advanced Robotics and Artificial Intelligence is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. Students work on perception, control, machine learning and autonomous systems in a school home to robotics researchers Michael Milford and Peter Corke, and QUT ranks first in Australia for data mining and analysis. Graduates work as robotics and AI engineers, computer vision engineers and machine learning specialists.

name: Master of Architecture
description: The Master of Architecture at QUT is a two-year degree that builds on undergraduate study to provide advanced understanding of architectural design and research, with a focus on people-focused, climate-responsive design for sub-tropical conditions. Students work in architectural practice while honing their skills in the classroom, learning from internationally recognised experts, and prepare to sit registration exams to become an architect. Graduates work in architectural practice, urban design, and the wider built environment.

name: Master of Artificial Intelligence
description: The Master of Artificial Intelligence at QUT develops specialised AI knowledge to respond to industry demand, building confidence with AI and machine learning models, methods, processes and software applications. Students apply advanced critical thinking and creative problem-solving to complex AI and ML problems, with a choice of project or research stream and a significant industry project or research experience. QUT ranks in the top 13 in Australia for data science and artificial intelligence, and the degree has a strong focus on ethical and responsible AI. Graduates work as AI and machine learning engineers, data scientists, and AI strategy and governance specialists.

name: Master of Biomedical Systems and Technology
description: QUT's Master of Biomedical Systems and Technology is an 18-month degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It brings engineering to healthcare problems, covering medical devices, biomechanics, imaging and bioinstrumentation, and QUT places in the world's top 75 for biomedical engineering in the ShanghaiRanking subject list. Graduates work as biomedical and design engineers, in medical device development and regulatory assessment.

name: Master of Business
description: The Master of Business at QUT is taught at a business school in the global top 1 percent, one of only three Australian business schools with triple international accreditation. Students choose a major from Financial Analytics and Technology, Global Business, Human Resource Management, Management, Innovation and Analytics, or Marketing Strategy, with a curriculum that prioritises hands-on learning, real industry projects and work-integrated learning. Graduates work in specialist and leadership roles across finance, human resources, management, marketing and analytics.

name: Master of Business Administration (Digital MBA)
description:
QUT markets this specifically as a Digital MBA, and the distinguishing feature is real: the degree is delivered flexibly with a strong online component and folds digital transformation, data-driven decision making and technology strategy into what would otherwise be a fairly standard MBA core (strategy, finance, marketing, leadership). It's aimed squarely at working professionals rather than a full-time cohort straight out of undergrad. QUT's MBA intake skews toward people already in mid-career roles looking to move into more senior leadership or to pivot into a digitally-oriented function.

The core units cover the traditional MBA ground, but electives let students go deeper into areas like digital strategy, innovation management or data analytics for business, which is where the Digital branding earns its keep rather than being a marketing label over an unchanged program. Group-based case work and a capstone strategy project (often tied to a real organisation) are the assessment backbone in the later stages.

QUT Business School's connections to Brisbane's corporate and government sector feed guest speakers and capstone project partners, though as with most Australian MBAs the value is heavily networking-and-credential driven rather than purely content-driven.
curriculum:
Core units: Strategic Management, Managerial Finance, Marketing Strategy, Leading People and Organisations, Digital Business Strategy
Elective strands: Data Analytics for Managers, Innovation and Entrepreneurship, Digital Transformation, International Business
Capstone: an applied strategy project conducted with a real host organisation, presented to faculty and industry assessors
Delivery: flexible/blended format aimed at working professionals, with intensive block and online components
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree plus at least 3 years professional work experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Clinical Psychology
description: QUT's Master of Clinical Psychology is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Health, taught at the Brisbane campuses with supervised clinical placements. It is an accredited postgraduate program that prepares provisionally registered psychologists for clinical practice across the lifespan, using an integrative approach to assessment and therapy. Graduates work as clinical psychologists in public and private mental health services and in health research.

name: Master of Counselling
description: The Master of Counselling at QUT is designed for professionals from a variety of settings who want to develop advanced knowledge and skills in counselling and professional supervision. It takes an applied, transformational and experiential focus, with an emphasis on solution-focused and narrative therapies, family therapy, group work and supervision, and students work with real clients under supervision at QUT Health Clinics. The course is accredited by the Australian Counselling Association. Graduates work as counsellors and clinical supervisors across health, community, education and private practice settings.

name: Master of Cyber Security
description: QUT Master of Cyber Security runs across three semesters, about 1.5 years full-time. It starts with programming fundamentals and web development with databases, moves to identifying vulnerabilities in computer systems, then advances into cyber security governance, the software development life cycle, human-centred design, computer networks and security, and human factors in cyber security. Work-integrated learning includes a significant industry project or industry research experience. English language requirements apply, with recognised qualifications from approved English-speaking countries considered. Indicative international tuition is around A$45,500 per year. Graduates work as cyber security specialists, information security analysts and penetration testers, and in security strategy and network design roles.

name: Master of Data Analytics
description: QUT Master of Data Analytics is a 192 credit point degree, two years full-time or four years part-time, made up of 108 credit points of core units including a 36 credit point capstone, plus 84 credit points of specialisation units. Specialisations are biomedical data science, computational data science, statistical data science, and information systems analytics. Entry requires a recognised bachelor degree in information technology, mathematics or biomedical science with a GPA of at least 4.0 on the QUT 7-point scale, plus QUT English language requirements, and an early exit with a Graduate Certificate in Data Science is available. Graduates build skills in programming, data processing, statistical modelling, data systems and data-driven decision-making, and work across banking and finance, media, health, education, information technology, engineering, agriculture and mining. Indicative international tuition is around A$45,200 per year.

name: Master of Data Science
description:
Run out of QUT's Centre for Data Science, this master's leans on staff who do applied analytics work with government and industry partners rather than a purely theoretical statistics faculty, and that shows up most in the final capstone, where students take on an industry project or industry research placement working with a real dataset and stakeholder rather than a simulated one. The course covers computational data science, statistical modelling, machine learning and information systems analytics as named specialisation strands, letting students lean the degree toward whichever of those areas matches their prior background and career target.

It's designed as a conversion-friendly degree: QUT accepts students from a range of quantitative undergraduate backgrounds, not just computer science or statistics, provided they can pick up the programming and stats foundations in the early units. Python, R and SQL are the working tools throughout, with dedicated units on big data infrastructure and data visualisation alongside the modelling content.

Graduates go into data analyst, data scientist and data engineering roles across finance, government and increasingly health-sector employers in Brisbane and beyond, with QUT's teaching staff research connections in finance and public-sector data work feeding directly into the kinds of case studies used in class.
curriculum:
Foundational units: Programming for Data Science, Statistical Methods, Databases and Big Data Technologies
Core units: Machine Learning, Data Visualisation and Communication, Information Systems Analytics
Specialisation strands: Computational Data Science, Statistical Data Science, or Biomedical Data Science (choose one focus for advanced electives)
Capstone: an industry project or industry-based research placement, working with a real organisation's data and presenting findings to stakeholders
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree in a quantitative discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Design (Strategic Design)
description: QUT's Master of Design (Strategic Design) is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Creative Industries, Education and Social Justice, taught at the Kelvin Grove campus in Brisbane. It applies design thinking to business, service and systems problems rather than product craft, and graduates can qualify for entry to a research PhD. They work as design strategists, design directors, researchers and design thinking facilitators.

name: Master of Digital Communication
description: QUT's Master of Digital Communication is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Creative Industries, Education and Social Justice, taught at the Kelvin Grove campus in Brisbane. It covers content strategy, social and digital media, branding and audience analytics, with applied client projects. Graduates work as digital communication and content specialists, brand and social media managers and digital marketing managers.

name: Master of Education (Educational Leadership)
description:
Aimed at practising teachers and school staff already eyeing (or already in) leadership roles, such as deputy principal, head of department, or curriculum coordinator, rather than at people entering education from scratch, this QUT master's is built around real school-leadership problems: staff management, school improvement planning, change leadership, and the policy environment Queensland schools operate in. Most units assume some teaching or school-based experience, and assessment tasks frequently ask students to apply frameworks to their own school context rather than a hypothetical one.

QUT's education faculty has close relationships with Queensland state and Catholic education systems, and the degree's content reflects current Queensland Department of Education priorities (school improvement frameworks, workforce planning, wellbeing-focused leadership) more than a generic international leadership-theory course would. Students can typically study part-time alongside full-time school roles, which is how most of the cohort completes it.

It functions as much as a credentialing step for principal-track career progression as it does a theoretical qualification, a fairly explicit trade-off for anyone weighing it against a more research-focused education master's.
curriculum:
Core units: Leading School Improvement, Educational Policy and Governance, Managing Change in Schools, Leading Teaching and Learning
Elective units: Workforce and Staff Leadership, Data-Informed Decision Making, Wellbeing-Centred Leadership
Capstone: an applied leadership project set within the student's own school context, supervised by faculty
Delivery: typically part-time, structured for practising teachers and school leaders studying alongside full-time work
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree and teaching qualification/experience preferred
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 6.5

name: Master of Engineering Management
description: QUT Master of Engineering Management is designed for practising engineers who want the specialist skills and advanced knowledge for leadership and management roles across engineering fields. As a standalone degree it takes one year; it can also be combined with the Master of Project Management or the Master of Engineering Technology to complete two master degrees in two years. Study areas include quality control, organisational infrastructure management and the development of decision support systems, giving graduates the analytical tools to improve operational efficiency, typically in manufacturing and service organisations. Indicative international tuition is around A$48,000 per year. Graduates become specialist engineering managers and leaders of engineering processes within their professional field.

name: Master of Engineering Technology
description: The Master of Engineering Technology at Queensland University of Technology is a one-year master's degree. It is offered through the Faculty of Engineering. Graduates pursue roles such as ai specialist, power engineer, robotics engineer and sustainability engineer.

name: Master of Health Management and Leadership
description: QUT's Master of Health Management and Leadership is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Health, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It is built for clinicians and health staff moving into management, covering health systems, financing, quality, workforce and change leadership. Graduates work as service and department managers, program leads and health executives across hospitals, primary care and government.

name: Master of Health, Safety and Environment
description: QUT's Master of Health, Safety and Environment is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Health, available on campus in Brisbane or online. It covers occupational health and safety, environmental health, risk management and legislation, and holders of a related graduate diploma can complete it in one year full-time. Graduates work as health and safety and environmental managers, advisers and consultants across industry and government.

name: Master of Information Technology (Computer Science)
description:
This is QUT's conversion and advanced-standing pathway into computer science at postgraduate level: it takes students with an IT-adjacent or quantitative background (sometimes without a CS-specific undergraduate degree) and builds them up through core computing fundamentals before letting them specialise in the computer science stream, which covers algorithms, software engineering practice and more advanced topics like machine learning or systems programming depending on electives chosen.

QUT's IT faculty sits close to Brisbane's growing tech and games sector, and the program includes an industry project unit in most specialisations, connecting students with real companies for a semester-length applied piece of work rather than a purely academic thesis. This industry-facing structure is a deliberate differentiator from more research-oriented computer science master's programs at other universities.

International students using the degree as a skilled-migration pathway make up a substantial share of the cohort, and the computer science specialisation specifically targets the kind of software development and systems roles that align with Australia's skilled occupation lists, though the degree's actual content is solid computing education rather than a migration-only credential.
curriculum:
Foundation units (for students without a CS background): Programming Fundamentals, Data Structures and Algorithms, Systems Analysis and Design
Core units: Software Engineering Practice, Advanced Algorithms, Database Systems
Specialisation electives: Machine Learning, Distributed Systems, Cybersecurity Fundamentals, Mobile Application Development
Capstone: an industry-based project unit or, alternatively, a research-based project for students intending further postgraduate study
admission_requirements: 2-year program: bachelor's degree (any discipline) with GPA 4.0/7.0. 1.5-year program: bachelor's in IT with GPA 4.0/7.0, or bachelor's (any discipline) GPA 4.0/7.0 plus 3 years FTE professional IT experience, or a Graduate Certificate in IT (GPA 4.0/7.0).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (QUT standard postgraduate requirement).

name: Master of Nursing (Entry to Practice)
description: QUT's Master of Nursing (Entry to Practice) is a two-year graduate-entry degree that prepares people who are not already nurses to apply for registration as a registered nurse with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. One year of advanced standing is built in, so it runs two years rather than three. Students complete 800 hours of clinical placement plus simulation practice, and a bioscience unit in first semester grounds them in anatomy and physiology. Entry for applicants without a nursing background is a recognised bachelor degree in another field completed within the past ten years with a grade point average of at least 4.0 on a 7-point scale. Graduates begin practice as registered nurses across acute, community, aged care and mental health settings.

name: Master of Nutrition and Dietetics
description: QUT's Master of Nutrition and Dietetics is an 18-month degree in the Faculty of Health, taught at the Brisbane campuses with clinical, community and food-service placements. It is a graduate-entry qualification that leads to eligibility for accreditation as a practising dietitian. Graduates work as dietitians in hospitals, community health and private practice, and in public health nutrition and the food industry.

name: Master of Optometry
description: QUT's Master of Optometry is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Health and the second half of QUT's five-year optometry pathway, following the Bachelor of Vision Science; there is no direct entry. It provides the clinical training and supervised practice needed to diagnose and manage eye conditions and prescribe corrective and therapeutic treatment. Graduates are eligible to register with the Optometry Board of Australia and practise as optometrists.

name: Master of Philosophy (Law)
description:
An MPhil is a research degree, not coursework. Students admitted into QUT's Master of Philosophy (Law) are essentially doing a scaled-down PhD, working under a single or small team of academic supervisors on an original legal research thesis over roughly one to two years, rather than sitting through lectures and exams. It suits people who already have a strong law or related honours-level qualification and want to test whether they're suited to (or want to build a track record for) doctoral-level legal research, an academic career, or specialist policy/research roles.

QUT's law faculty has active research strengths in areas like technology and law, health law, and Indigenous legal issues, and MPhil candidates typically align their thesis topic with an existing supervisor's research area to get meaningful guidance rather than working in isolation. There's no fixed curriculum in the conventional sense; progress is marked by milestones (research proposal, confirmation of candidature, periodic progress review) rather than semester-based units.

Graduates either progress to a PhD (the MPhil can function as a stepping stone with credit transfer in some cases), move into specialist legal research or policy roles, or use the qualification alongside existing legal practice experience for academic or think-tank positions.
curriculum:
Milestone-based structure rather than semester units: research proposal and literature review, confirmation of candidature seminar, periodic progress review, thesis submission and oral examination
Supervision: one primary and one associate supervisor aligned with the candidate's research area
Coursework component: a small number of research methods and academic writing units, varying by candidate's prior qualifications
Typical areas of supervision available: technology and law, health law, Indigenous legal issues, commercial and corporate law
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree in law with a research proposal
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description: QUT Master of Business (Professional Accounting) can be completed in 1.5 to 2 years full-time. Graduates with a bachelor degree in business or a related field and a GPA of at least 4.0 on the QUT 7-point scale take 144 credit points and finish in 1.5 years; graduates from any other discipline take 192 credit points starting with foundation studies. The course is built in three blocks: foundation studies (48 credit points), discipline studies (96 credit points) and complementary studies (48 credit points). Subject to core unit selection, graduates hold a degree recognised by CPA Australia, Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand and the Institute of Public Accountants, meeting the academic requirements to enrol in their professional programs. Indicative international tuition is around A$40,100 per year. It suits graduates aiming for higher-level accounting roles or their own practice.

name: Master of Professional Engineering
description: QUT's Master of Professional Engineering is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It is a graduate-entry qualification for people with a related bachelor's degree, with seven majors all accredited by Engineers Australia at professional engineer level, which supports international recognition. Graduates work as professional engineers in fields including electrical, computer, control systems and signal processing.

name: Master of Project Management
description: The Master of Project Management at QUT is a transdisciplinary qualification accredited by the Australian Institute of Project Management and aligned with the Project Management Body of Knowledge. Students engage with industry practitioners and academics who are experts in their field, and the curriculum uses real-life case studies and scenarios. Professionals use it to advance their career, change sectors or improve their employability. Graduates work as project and program managers across construction, engineering, IT, infrastructure, health, events and government.

name: Master of Psychology (Educational and Developmental)
description: QUT's Master of Psychology (Educational and Developmental) is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Health, taught at the Brisbane campuses with supervised placements. It is an accredited postgraduate program preparing psychologists to work with learning, development and wellbeing across childhood, adolescence and adulthood. Graduates work as educational and developmental psychologists, and in counselling, research and education policy.

name: Master of Public Health
description: QUT's Master of Public Health is a 192-credit-point degree, two years full-time or 1.5 years for graduates with a recognised health bachelor degree. It combines eight core units with a 48-credit-point major and a research component, taken as a dissertation or a shorter research project plus electives. Majors are emergency and disaster management, epidemiology and research methods, health promotion, and health, safety and environment, and students can also mix units across majors. Core units and most electives can be studied on campus or online. Graduates work in government health agencies, non-government organisations, community health, workplace health and safety, and research. Indicative international tuition is around A$41,300 per year.

name: Master of Renewable Energy
description: QUT's Master of Renewable Energy is an 18-month degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It covers solar, wind and storage technologies, grid integration and energy systems for the shift away from fossil fuels, and domestic full-time students are offered Commonwealth Supported Places. Graduates work as electrical and energy engineers, energy analysts, consultants and policy officers.

name: Master of Renewable Energy with Data Analytics
description: QUT's Master of Renewable Energy with Data Analytics is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It combines renewable energy engineering with data analytics as the city rebuilds infrastructure for the 2032 Olympic Games, and QUT ranks first in Australia for data mining and analysis. Graduates work as electrical and power engineers, energy analysts and consultants with an analytics focus.

name: Master of Renewable Energy with Project Management
description: QUT's Master of Renewable Energy with Project Management is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It pairs renewable energy engineering, covering solar, wind, storage and grid integration, with project management as Brisbane rebuilds infrastructure ahead of the 2032 Olympic Games. Graduates work as electrical and power engineers, energy analysts and consultants moving into project and delivery roles.

name: Master of Robotics and Artificial Intelligence
description: QUT's Master of Robotics and Artificial Intelligence is an 18-month degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. Students work on perception, control, machine learning and autonomous systems in a school home to robotics researchers Michael Milford and Peter Corke, and domestic full-time students are offered Commonwealth Supported Places. Graduates work as robotics and AI engineers, computer vision engineers and machine learning specialists.

name: Master of Social Work Qualifying
description: QUT's Master of Social Work (Qualifying) is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Health, taught at the Brisbane campuses with two supervised field placements totalling 1,000 hours. It is a graduate-entry qualifying degree for people with a related bachelor's degree, and is accredited by the Australian Association of Social Workers so graduates are eligible for AASW membership. They work in health, child and family services, mental health and community organisations.

name: Master of Sustainable Infrastructure
description: QUT's Master of Sustainable Infrastructure is an 18-month degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It covers the planning, delivery and operation of transport, water and civil infrastructure with a sustainability focus, and domestic full-time students are offered Commonwealth Supported Places. Graduates work as civil and transport engineers, and in logistics, supply chain and infrastructure planning.

name: Master of Sustainable Infrastructure with Data Analytics
description: QUT's Master of Sustainable Infrastructure with Data Analytics is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It combines sustainable infrastructure engineering with data analytics as Brisbane rebuilds its transport and civil networks for the 2032 Olympic Games, drawing on QUT's top-ranked data mining research. Graduates work as civil and transport engineers and infrastructure analysts.

name: Master of Sustainable Infrastructure with Project Management
description: QUT's Master of Sustainable Infrastructure with Project Management is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It pairs sustainable infrastructure engineering, covering transport, water and civil works, with project management as Brisbane prepares its networks for the 2032 Olympic Games. Graduates work as civil and transport engineers and infrastructure project managers.

name: Master of Teaching (Early Childhood)
description: QUT's Master of Teaching (Early Childhood) is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Creative Industries, Education and Social Justice, taught at the Kelvin Grove campus in Brisbane. It is a graduate-entry teaching qualification for the early years, combining coursework in child development and pedagogy with supervised placements in early learning and school settings. Graduates are eligible for teacher registration and work as early childhood teachers.

name: Advanced Diploma of Accounting
description: The Advanced Diploma of Accounting at RMIT University prepares students for a career as a tax agent or for further accounting study. Students apply skills in accounting systems and internal controls, undertake a work placement with an accounting entity, and develop the theoretical and technical skills for specialised work in the accounting and financial services industries. Skills covered include implementing and maintaining accounting systems, internal control and audit, preparing financial statements for corporate reporting entities, business performance reporting, and preparing tax returns and providing tax advice for legal entities. Study options include full-time and part-time blended delivery in Melbourne.

name: Advanced Diploma of Building Design (Architectural)
description: The Advanced Diploma of Building Design (Architectural) at RMIT University prepares students to work as architectural technicians in building design offices and architectural practices, focusing on the practical and technical application of design skills to create innovative, sustainable designs for domestic and commercial-scale building projects. Topics include sustainable design, industry digital applications, problem-solving through drawing, construction technology and processes, project documentation, architectural project administration, materials technology, building services, and planning and building regulation codes and standards. It is based in Melbourne.

name: Advanced Diploma of Electronics and Communications Engineering
description: The Advanced Diploma of Electronics and Communications Engineering at RMIT University develops skills to design, validate and evaluate electronics and communication equipment and systems, along with risk management, project estimating and management, and technical and sales advice. Students learn industry-standard software and skills in programmable gate array technologies, circuit simulation, printed circuit board design, digital and analogue systems, amplifiers, analogue integrated circuit design, communication systems, mobile phones and global positioning. An advisory committee of industry representatives keeps the curriculum current. It is taught in Melbourne.

name: Advanced Diploma of Engineering Technology - Electrical
Advanced Diploma of Screen and Media
Advanced Diploma of Visual Arts
description: The Advanced Diploma of Visual Arts at RMIT University helps students further develop their artistic practice and creative skills across a range of industry contexts, including drawing, painting, installation, printmaking, digital media, sculpture, web design, photography, business and exhibition. Students learn to communicate ideas and concepts, interpret assignment briefs, work collaboratively and independently, select appropriate mediums, work sustainably from studios and workshops, and use traditional, contemporary and emergent technologies. Graduates leave with a sound theoretical and practical knowledge base and the skills to plan, execute and evaluate an artistic career. It is taught in Melbourne.

name: Associate Degree in Applied Science
description: The Associate Degree in Applied Science at RMIT University provides an entry point to the biomedical science and biotechnology industries. This hands-on program involves significant time in laboratory classes, with students working in small practical groups that support interaction with teachers and classmates. The lab is fitted with equipment used in biotechnology and biomedical applications, and graduates qualify for membership of the Australian Society for Microbiology and the Australian Institute of Medical Scientists. Before beginning, students choose a pathway in science, biomedicine or pharmacy. It is taught in Melbourne.

name: Associate Degree in Aviation (Professional Pilots)
description: The Associate Degree in Aviation (Professional Pilots) at RMIT University, designed in collaboration with industry, equips students with the skills and knowledge to pursue a career as a pilot. Blending aviation theory with practical flying lessons, the program prepares students to undertake the Civil Aviation Safety Authority Commercial Pilot Licence theory and flight tests, and students may also undertake subjects in instrument and instructor ratings. Flight training takes place at RMIT's Point Cook campus.

name: Associate Degree in Business
description: The Associate Degree in Business at RMIT University develops professional skills across all aspects of the modern business environment, with subjects spanning marketing, human resources, accountancy and management. Blending the academic and the practical, students explore how these areas work together to enable effective management of a contemporary business, and graduate able to analyse and solve problems, work collaboratively and understand core business concepts, for immediate employment or as a basis for further study. Students work with partner companies on group projects and gain mentorship from senior industry figures. It is taught in Melbourne.

name: Associate Degree in Design (Furniture)
description: The award-winning Associate Degree in Design (Furniture) at RMIT University teaches students to create original furniture designs with a strong grounding in design methods, manufacturing technologies and processes informed by cultural and social factors. Students combine real-life industry projects and design theory with a hands-on focus on production to create sustainable contemporary furniture products, and investigate the contemporary, cultural and environmental aspects of professional furniture design practice. Assignments are live industry briefs, and students can participate in global design and trade exhibitions. It is taught in Melbourne.

name: Associate Degree in Digital Technologies (Advanced Manufacturing)
Associate Degree in Engineering Technology
description: The Associate Degree in Engineering Technology at RMIT University, accredited by Engineers Australia, provides a flexible pathway to an engineering degree. Students gain broad theoretical and technical knowledge of the underlying principles of engineering, learning to analyse and interpret complex problems, communicate with a range of stakeholders, and find effective solutions to industry issues. Five majors are offered: mechanical, aerospace, advanced manufacturing and mechatronics, electrical and electronics, and civil engineering. RMIT is ranked ninth in Australia and in the top 150 globally for engineering and technology in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026.

name: Associate Degree in Fashion
description: The Associate Degree in Fashion at RMIT University is a stepping stone into the fashion industry, blending technical expertise with business knowledge. Students learn fundamental techniques such as design concepts, pattern development, construction and garment fitting, and develop business acumen in marketing communication strategies, trend forecasting, buying methodologies and supply chain management. A common first semester helps students choose between a Design and Technology or a Business and Retail option, and the course spotlights the circular economy and sustainability. RMIT is ranked number one in Australia and 19th in the world for art and design in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026.

name: Associate Degree in Fashion and Textile Merchandising
Associate Degree in Fashion Design and Technology
Associate Degree in Graphic Design
description: The Associate Degree in Graphic Design at RMIT University builds industry knowledge and specialist skills for a career in graphic design. Students may work across fields including corporate identity, book and magazine layout, advertising, branding, packaging, web design, wayfinding and exhibition design, combining communication, design, technology and business. The program provides strong skills in finished art and design concept development and in-depth knowledge of the design process, with rigorous research and learning experiences that develop critical thinking and innovative design solutions. Students work with industry-standard software such as InDesign, Illustrator and Photoshop. It is taught in Melbourne.

name: Associate Degree in Health Sciences
description: The Associate Degree in Health Sciences at RMIT University provides an introduction to health sciences, exploring both the individual and public view of health in Australia. It suits students undecided about their career options in the health sector, giving them a better understanding of different health professions. Through the lens of the health industry, students learn about psychology, project management and exercise for health conditions, with a focus on health promotion, and engage with an industry partner on a real-world health promotion project and work placement. It is taught in Melbourne.

name: Associate Degree in Information Technology
description: The Associate Degree in Information Technology at RMIT University is project-based and linked to current industry requirements, building foundational knowledge in cyber security, artificial intelligence, programming and data handling. Through theoretical subjects and hands-on training, students learn operating systems, IT support and systems administration, network infrastructure design and security using CISCO technologies, hardware, software and network troubleshooting, virtualised and cloud-based systems, software application development, and user-centred design. Graduates can enter the workforce with current IT skills or continue to a bachelor degree. It is taught in Melbourne.

name: Associate Degree in Interior Decoration and Design
description: The Associate Degree in Interior Decoration and Design at RMIT University explores practical and theoretical decoration and design frameworks for creating innovative interior concepts and proposals. Underpinned by sustainable practices in the planning and specification of interior structures, there is a strong focus on materials and surface treatments, furnishings, and colour and lighting solutions to create aesthetic and functional spaces in residential and commercial environments. Projects give students the opportunity to work directly with industry. Assignments are live industry briefs. It is taught in Melbourne.

name: Associate Degree in Professional Writing and Editing
description: The Associate Degree in Professional Writing and Editing at RMIT University is a practical, industry-focused program that builds the skills, expertise and versatility needed to become a professional writer or editor. Students work alongside peers passionate about reading and writing and learn from teachers and mentors who are leading practitioners, gaining a broad base of skills in fiction, creative nonfiction, professional communication, digital content, grammar and editing before specialising, with a focus on building a writing portfolio and engaging with industry and readers. RMIT is ranked fifth in Australia and in the top 100 in the world for media and communication in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026.

name: Associate Degree in Screen and Media Production
description: The Associate Degree in Screen and Media Production at RMIT University teaches screen industry skills and knowledge in concept development, storytelling, pre-production, production and post-production for single and multi-camera productions. Students gain extensive experience on industry-standard cameras and video editing software, work on actual film and television projects to build connections, and learn from practitioners with knowledge of emerging production trends. There is a strong emphasis on industry knowledge, collaboration, team building and professionalism. It is taught in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Accounting
description: The RMIT Bachelor of Accounting builds theoretical and technical accounting knowledge through core studies in accounting and law, developing the skills to analyse and evaluate data and information across the discipline. Students also explore business and future technology, digital literacy, social impact, economics and sustainability, and build an e-portfolio through industry engagement. Graduates work as accountants, auditors, financial analysts and advisers, and can progress toward professional accreditation.

name: Bachelor of Accounting Professional Practice
description: The Bachelor of Accounting Professional Practice at RMIT University provides a strong theoretical and technical foundation in accounting and business, preparing students for professional practice and evolving industry demands. The curriculum focuses on core accounting principles and law, developing in-depth discipline knowledge and practical skills alongside professional skills such as critical thinking, problem-solving and communication, and combines technical expertise with real-world application through professional practice. RMIT is ranked ninth in Australia and in the top 100 globally for accounting and finance in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026.

name: Bachelor of Applied Mathematics and Statistics
Bachelor of Applied Science (Aviation)
description: The Bachelor of Applied Science (Aviation) at RMIT University is designed for aspiring aviation professionals interested in operational, managerial and planning roles. Students develop a comprehensive understanding of the aviation industry along with leadership, analytical, business and problem-solving skills to ensure the smooth operation of airlines, airports and aviation businesses. Studies can be tailored across airline and airport operations, aviation management, aircraft maintenance, human factors, aviation safety and security, and business analytics, and the degree includes a capstone industry project addressing a real-world aviation problem. It is taught in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Architectural Design
description:
Design studio work starts in the very first semester here rather than being held back until students have "earned" it through a year of theory - RMIT runs the studios like a working architecture practice from day one, and they typically make up half of each semester's workload. Groups stay small, and from second semester onward students actually choose which studio project and theme to follow rather than being assigned one, so the degree lets people specialise in interests (housing, urban design, materials experimentation) earlier than most architecture programs allow.

The supporting subjects - technology, communication, history - fill out the rest of the degree and are there specifically to give studio work real technical and historical grounding, not to function as separate academic silos. It's explicitly a pathway degree: this bachelor's alone isn't the endpoint, it feeds into RMIT's Master of Architecture and the accreditation that comes with it, so most students here already know they're in for five-plus years of study total before registration.

The appeal for prospective students is usually the intensity of the studio culture and the small-group, project-based teaching model over the sheer volume of design work produced by third year.
curriculum:
Year 1: Design Studio 1 and 2 (foundations), Architectural Communication, Introduction to Building Technology, History of Architecture
Year 2: Design Studio 3 and 4 (student-selected themes), Structures, Environmental Systems, Architectural Communication (advanced)
Year 3: Design Studio 5 and 6 (student-selected themes), Professional Practice, Digital Design Technology, capstone design project
Pathway continuation into Master of Architecture for professional accreditation
admission_requirements: ATAR ~75+ (or equivalent Year 12); folio/selection task may apply
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Aviation (Pilot Training)
description: The Bachelor of Aviation (Pilot Training) at RMIT University offers a blend of flight training and industry-relevant theory, preparing students for a career as a pilot or in operational management and planning roles. Students develop the critical skills to assess and manage all aspects of the aviation industry and to work independently and in teams to solve real industry issues in aviation operations. The degree prepares students to gain their Recreational, Private and Commercial Pilot Licence, which enables commercial flying within Australia, with flight training at RMIT's approved airfields.

name: Bachelor of Biomedical Science
description: The RMIT Bachelor of Biomedical Science lets students study the human body in health and disease, with a Biomedical Science option that includes a specialist minor in medical biotechnology or clinical health and disease, and an Osteopathy pathway option that combines with the Master of Clinical Osteopathy. The degree offers flexibility to study across the biomedical sciences. Graduates work in medical and health research, laboratory and diagnostic science, biotechnology and pharmaceuticals, or continue to postgraduate study.

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
RMIT restructured its Bachelor of Business around what it calls an agile, non-traditional model, built to layer more hands-on industry work into a normally quite theoretical degree. Students choose from fourteen majors - Entrepreneurship, Finance, Global Business, Logistics and Supply Chain, Management and Change, Marketing, People and Organisation, Business Information Systems, Economics, Financial Planning and several others - plus an optional minor, or can leave without declaring a major at all if they want maximum flexibility.

That range of majors is genuinely wide for an undergraduate business degree; a lot of universities offer four or five majors and expect students to fit their interests into one of them, whereas here a student interested in blockchain-enabled business or social impact work has an actual named pathway rather than a generic elective. Programs run three years full-time or six part-time, with February, July and October intakes, giving mid-year starters and people restarting study after a break more entry points than the standard once-a-year model.

Industry integration runs through most majors via partnerships with named organisations rather than generic "real-world case studies," and RMIT frames the whole degree around solving actual problems for those partners as part of coursework.
curriculum:
Year 1: Business foundation courses - Accounting Fundamentals, Economic Principles, Marketing Foundations, Business Statistics, Business Communication
Year 2: major courses begin (from 14 available majors - e.g. Finance, Marketing, Business Information Systems, Logistics and Supply Chain), optional minor
Year 3: advanced major courses, industry-partnered capstone project, electives
admission_requirements: ATAR ~70+ (or equivalent Year 12); no prerequisite subjects
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Business Professional Practice
description: The Bachelor of Business Professional Practice at RMIT University immerses students in real-world experiences with an agile, non-traditional course structure that includes greater hands-on learning, industry engagement and a year dedicated to professional practice studies. Students can pursue an entrepreneurial path, management roles, or a focus on economics and finance, business information systems, or people and organisational change, choosing from a range of business majors. RMIT is ranked tenth in Australia and in the top 150 globally for business and management studies in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026.

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description: The RMIT Bachelor of Commerce focuses on the technology aspects of business and how emerging technologies affect the exchange of goods and services. With five majors on offer, students explore the complexities of law, policy development, market dynamics and technological innovation that shape today's commerce, staying up to date with technology, business theory and market trends. Graduates work in business analysis, finance, economics, marketing and management across industries.

name: Bachelor of Computer Science
description: The RMIT Bachelor of Computer Science provides in-depth knowledge of systems infrastructure, software methods and technologies, and application technologies, from theoretical and practical angles. Students gain a fundamental understanding of computer hardware, operating systems, computer networks, data structures and algorithms, and database systems, and can specialise in different fields of computer science. Graduates work as software engineers and developers, systems and data specialists, and IT consultants.

name: Bachelor of Construction Management (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Construction Management (Honours) at RMIT University develops the theoretical knowledge and technical skills to work as a construction management professional. Students critically evaluate and apply construction management concepts and methodologies, extending their knowledge in building design, building services, construction methods and processes, procurement and supply chains, sustainability, economics and resource management, and build confidence in managing projects from start to finish. RMIT is ranked number one in Australia and in the top 15 globally for architecture and built environment in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026. Course material is designed with industry.

name: Bachelor of Creative Writing
description: The RMIT Bachelor of Creative Writing is designed to make students confident, skilled and adaptable in contemporary creative industries, where writing and editing sit alongside creativity, communication and critical thinking. Students work across genres including fiction, screen and digital writing, spend deep time with their creative work, run experiments and build industry connections with passionate writers. Graduates work as writers, editors, content creators, and in publishing and communications.

name: Bachelor of Criminal Justice
description: The Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice at RMIT University teaches students how crime is defined and measured, how law and human rights intersect, and how factors such as Indigeneity, race, gender, class and disability shape experiences of crime and justice. Learning is practical and connected to the real world, including working with real wrongful conviction cases, completing a 50-day placement, and learning alongside prisoners. Students build skills in research, policy analysis, critical thinking and communication, and can major in criminology, justice systems or legal studies, graduating ready to work across policing, courts, corrections, policy, advocacy, community services or further study.

name: Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice
description: The RMIT Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice explores how justice systems interact with law enforcement, human rights and global crime, with students working on real cases as part of their study. Students learn how crime is defined and measured, how law and human rights intersect, and how factors such as Indigeneity, race, gender, class and disability shape experiences of crime and justice, building skills in research, policy analysis and critical thinking. Graduates work in policy and research, corrections, crime prevention, community justice and government agencies.

name: Bachelor of Criminology and Psychology
description: The RMIT Bachelor of Criminology and Psychology combines the two disciplines to get beneath the surface of crime. Students examine real cases, unpack crime trends, and learn how laws, policies and institutions affect people's lives, building practical skills including basic forensic interviewing, risk assessment, complex case management and communicating with offenders, victims and clients from diverse backgrounds. Graduates work in justice and corrections, community services, research and policy, and support roles.

name: Bachelor of Cyber Security (Professional)
description: The RMIT Bachelor of Cyber Security equips students with the specialist knowledge to troubleshoot, analyse, design, support and provide cyber security solutions. The hands-on degree is modelled on the Australian Signals Directorate framework, covering areas from computer forensics and cyber security testing to blockchain and AI, preparing students for current and emerging threats. Graduates work as security analysts and engineers, penetration testers, incident responders and security consultants.

name: Bachelor of Data Science
description: The RMIT Bachelor of Data Science develops skills in data analytics, statistics, computer science, machine learning, programming, mathematics and data wrangling, positioning students to contribute to business decision-making, corporate strategy and government planning. Students gain strong problem-solving skills and learn to communicate their work to technical and non-technical audiences and to consider relevant standards. Graduates work as data scientists and analysts, machine learning and analytics engineers, and research analysts.

name: Bachelor of Design (Communication Design)
description:
