RMIT's data science master's spends its first year deliberately narrow - solid computer science and statistics foundations - before opening into advanced electives and an industry or research project in year two. That sequencing is a response to a common complaint about data science master's programs elsewhere: students arriving from non-CS backgrounds (commerce, biology, social science) who get thrown into advanced machine learning units without the linear algebra or programming grounding to keep up. RMIT's structure front-loads that grounding instead.

The 192-credit-point, two-year full-time program includes a Graduate Diploma exit point at 96 credit points for students who need to leave partway through with something to show for it - a genuine safety net rather than a marketing line, since a lot of comparable programs offer no formal mid-point qualification at all. Case studies threaded through the coursework bring in practising data scientists to walk through legal, ethical and policy questions - algorithmic bias, data privacy law - alongside the purely technical content, which matters given how much scrutiny data science work now attracts.

Delivery mixes lectures, tutorials, and heavy practical lab time, with the year-two project functioning as the main portfolio piece graduates take into job interviews.
curriculum:
Year 1: Programming for Data Science, Statistics for Data Science, Database Systems, Data Preprocessing and Wrangling, Introduction to Machine Learning, Data Visualisation
Graduate Diploma exit point available at 96 credit points
Year 2: Advanced Machine Learning, Big Data Processing, electives (e.g. Natural Language Processing, Deep Learning), Data Ethics and Policy, capstone industry or research project
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a quantitative or IT-related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
description: The RMIT Master of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence is a conversion degree for graduates from any discipline who want a career in data science and AI. Whether their background is in business, science, engineering, health, economics or social sciences, students follow a structured pathway to build the technical, analytical and strategic capabilities to create, deploy and govern AI-enabled, data-driven solutions for industry challenges. Graduates work as data scientists, AI engineers and analytics specialists.

name: Master of Design (Architecture & Design)
description: The Master of Design (Architecture and Design) at RMIT University is a research degree based on the idea that research is conducted through designing, with the process of designing paralleling research in other fields. Research candidates are supported within communities of design practice, and the program may be undertaken in project or thesis mode in consultation with a supervisor. On completion, students have a body of knowledge that includes recent developments in one or more disciplines, advanced knowledge of research principles and methods, and the ability to reflect critically on theory and its application. RMIT is ranked number one in Australia and in the top 15 globally for architecture and built environment in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026.

name: Master of Design Innovation and Technology
description: The RMIT Master of Design Innovation and Technology sits at the intersection of architecture, interior, industrial and experience design, letting students address issues from a wide variety of professions including engineering, landscape architecture, service design, graphic design, animation, interaction, lighting and sound design. Students gain practical experience collaborating with industry partners and through global intensive design studios. Graduates work as design innovators, service and experience designers, and design strategists across sectors.

name: Master of Energy Efficient and Sustainable Building
description: The RMIT Master of Energy Efficient and Sustainable Building responds to industry demand for skilled professionals in sustainable building practices. It provides the skills and theory to design, develop and implement solutions for new and retrofitted buildings and the sustainable built environment, addressing shifting environmental priorities in an increasingly urbanised world. Graduates work in sustainable building design and assessment, energy and facilities management, and green building consulting.

name: Master of Engineering (Electrical and Electronic Engineering)
Master of Environmental Science and Technology
Master of Fashion (Design)
description: The Master of Fashion (Design) at RMIT University helps students define their position in the world of fashion and pitch their work to industry through an innovative body of publicly showcased work. The program imagines future fashion design contexts, creates ethical design propositions, and uses cross-disciplinary design strategies to drive competitive creative practice. Students establish their design, communication and presentation methods for fashion garments, products, accessories, materials, spaces and experiences, and choose electives that customise their studies, culminating in a collection or design outcome. RMIT is ranked number one in Australia and 19th in the world for art and design in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026.

name: Master of Finance
description: The RMIT Master of Finance keeps pace with the latest trends in the finance industry, from sustainable finance to fintech, with a curriculum covering finance, financial modelling, econometrics, trading and research. Students may be eligible for advanced standing or recognition of prior learning based on previous study. Graduates work in banking, investment and portfolio management, corporate finance, risk and fintech roles.

name: Master of Fine Art
description: The RMIT Master of Fine Art is designed for people with emerging art practices looking to focus their work, and for those extending existing practices, with a structure that allows room for experimentation. Students are mentored by academic staff who are professional artists, performers, writers, historians and curators, exploring multiple media and conceptual tools to develop the core of what they want to create as an artist. RMIT is highly ranked internationally for art and design. Graduates work as practising artists, and in curatorial, education and creative industry roles.

name: Master of Food Science and Technology
description: The RMIT Master of Food Science and Technology develops skills and knowledge in food processing and preservation, the chemical properties of food materials, food safety, packaging and labelling, and food product and process innovation, plus subjects supporting the technical positions the food industry requires. It suits graduates with a background in science, engineering, agriculture or related disciplines. Graduates work as food technologists and scientists in product development, quality and safety, processing and regulation.

name: Master of Geospatial Science
description: The RMIT Master of Geospatial Science makes students experts in geographic information systems, mapping, satellite positioning and remote sensing, with professional-level expertise in the analysis, management, capture and visualisation of spatial information using the latest technologies. RMIT has taught geospatial science for more than 50 years and its graduates are sought after by industry. Graduates work as GIS analysts and developers, surveyors, remote sensing specialists and spatial data scientists.

name: Master of Global Studies
description: The RMIT Master of Global Studies prepares students to make a global impact in international development, security, humanitarian emergencies and sustainability. Engaging with organisations, communities and thought leaders from diverse backgrounds, students build advanced skills in analysis and critical thinking, communication, leadership, ethical engagement and research, oriented toward emerging and future challenges. Graduates work in international development and aid, humanitarian organisations, diplomacy, policy and research.

name: Master of Human Resource Management
description: The RMIT Master of Human Resource Management updates knowledge and builds skills for a global HR practice, examining people and culture issues in the context of global changes affecting workplaces. Graduates understand how HR practice applies within small and medium enterprises, start-ups, entrepreneurial firms, multinationals, and the public and not-for-profit sectors, with advanced standing available for previous study. Graduates work in human resources, people and culture, talent and organisational development roles.

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
RMIT's Master of IT gives students seven specialisations to choose from - big data analytics, cloud infrastructure, AI in systems and applications, mobile and IoT computing, security and blockchain, software systems architecture, and web systems and search technology - which is an unusually wide spread for a two-year master's. Most competitor programs pick two or three tracks and call it done; RMIT built this one with industry partners specifically so students could chase whichever corner of tech was actually hiring that year.

Teaching mixes pre-recorded short lectures with lectorials, hands-on lab classes and project work, which suits the many students juggling part-time work in Melbourne's CBD-adjacent tech scene - RMIT's city campus location isn't incidental to that. The 192-credit-point load (full load for someone without recent related study) runs across roughly two years, with a research or industry project toward the end that's meant to function as a portfolio piece for job applications, not just an assessment box to tick.

Because the specialisations map fairly directly onto ANZSCO-recognised IT occupations, it's a common choice for students building toward a skills assessment for Australian permanent residency, alongside those simply wanting a technical master's from a university with a strong industry reputation in tech.
curriculum:
Year 1: Programming Fundamentals, Data Structures and Algorithms, Database Concepts, IT Research Methods, Software Engineering Fundamentals, Networking
Year 2: chosen specialisation core courses (e.g. Big Data Analytics, Cloud Computing Architecture, Applied Machine Learning, IoT Systems, Cyber Security Fundamentals, depending on stream) plus electives
Final semester: Capstone Project or Industry-Based Learning placement
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline, AU or equivalent overseas) with GPA 2.0/4.0, or 5+ years relevant IT work experience (programming, software engineering, systems/business analysis, ICT management, etc.) in lieu of a degree.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or TOEFL iBT 79+).

name: Master of Interior Design
description: The RMIT Master of Interior Design emphasises ideas and a design-led approach to research and experimentation, enabling students to work across a range of practices and to engage interior design as an agent of social and cultural change. Students develop strong communication and technical skills and learn to contribute to collective responses to real industry briefs, engaging with clients. Graduates work as interior designers, spatial designers, and in workplace, retail, hospitality and exhibition design.

name: Master of International Business
description: The RMIT Master of International Business is aimed at students seeking global careers in private, public or not-for-profit organisations. Designed with the oversight of an Industry Advisory Board, it provides real-world experiences and the skills to succeed in local and international business environments, with advanced standing available for previous study. Graduates work in international trade and operations, global business development, consulting and management roles.

name: Master of Justice and Criminology
description: The RMIT Master of Justice and Criminology is designed for students wishing to enter a career in the justice system and for people already working in the industry who want to update and extend their knowledge. Some subjects are offered online for flexibility, and students gain practical skills and connections through RMIT's strong justice sector links. Graduates enhance their careers in policing, customs, corrections, the courts, policy and research.

name: Master of Laboratory Medicine
description: The RMIT Master of Laboratory Medicine, taught in central Melbourne, builds the knowledge to perform and oversee a range of diagnostic procedures in a clinical pathology laboratory, alongside problem-solving and critical thinking skills. It is designed for graduates of general science or biomedical science degrees interested in a career in diagnostic pathology or medical research who lack experience in the diagnostic laboratory disciplines. Graduates work as medical laboratory scientists in pathology, diagnostics and research.

name: Master of Landscape Architecture
description: The RMIT Master of Landscape Architecture is an award-winning degree accredited by the Australian Institute of Landscape Architects, recognised for fostering design knowledge, critical thinking and design advocacy through innovative teaching and research. RMIT is highly ranked internationally for architecture and built environment. Graduates become leaders and innovators in landscape architectural practice, working in design studios, government and multidisciplinary firms.

name: Master of Marketing
description: The RMIT Master of Marketing develops the expertise to direct and implement an organisation's marketing strategy, shaped around real-world marketing projects and challenges. Students gain hands-on experience in planning, directing, implementing and monitoring an organisation's marketing efforts, blending theory with practice, with advanced standing available for previous study. Graduates work as marketing managers and directors, brand and digital strategists, and market research and insights leaders.

name: Master of Media
description: The RMIT Master of Media prepares students to be strategic leaders in an evolving media industry. The first year introduces video, audio and internet media production; the second year explores complex cross-media projects and develops the strategic and leadership skills to lead in the industry, with a global focus and hands-on projects in well-equipped facilities. Graduates work in media production and strategy, content leadership, communications and digital media roles.

name: Master of Medical Physics
description: The RMIT Master of Medical Physics applies physical sciences such as radiation physics to improve diagnostic medical imaging and cancer treatment. Studying in central Melbourne, students develop the skills to evaluate and optimise the performance of medical equipment and procedures, analyse outputs, diagnose problems and provide quality assurance for patient treatments, applying specialist knowledge in instrumentation and quantitative measurement. Graduates work as medical physicists and radiation safety specialists in hospitals, cancer centres and research.

name: Master of Occupational Health and Safety
description: The RMIT Master of Occupational Health and Safety provides specialisations in a multidisciplinary profession with applications across all industries. As community expectation and government legislation demand higher levels of protection for employees and the community, demand for qualified OHS professionals is growing. Students can pursue a research stream to deepen their expertise. Graduates work as OHS managers, advisers and consultants across industry, government and consultancies.

name: Master of Photography
description: The RMIT Master of Photography prioritises students' professional photographic practice, centring on image-making and its role in shaping contemporary visual culture. Students are encouraged to challenge the medium technically, conceptually and theoretically, experimenting and creating within studio-based group learning and independent projects, and exploring traditional, experimental and expanded forms. Graduates work as professional photographers and artists, and in visual media, curatorial and education roles.

name: Master of Physiotherapy
description: The RMIT Master of Physiotherapy, based in Bundoora in Melbourne, produces agile, evidence-informed health professionals. Students learn therapeutic communication skills, business and enterprise acumen, technology and digital health skills, and knowledge of healthcare across the lifespan, with simulated and clinical experiences embedded in the curriculum. The degree leads to eligibility for registration as a physiotherapist. Graduates work as physiotherapists in hospitals, private and sports practice, aged and community care and rehabilitation.

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description: RMIT University Master of Professional Accounting is a two-year, 192 credit point degree of 16 courses for graduates from any discipline who want a qualification recognised by CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand; it satisfies the academic requirements for entry to the CA Program and graduates can enrol in the CPA Australia program. A defining feature is work-integrated learning, with projects run alongside industry and community organisations. Entry requires an Australian bachelor degree or equivalent in any discipline; applicants with an unrelated degree may also need two years of relevant work experience. Indicative international tuition is around A$51,800 per year. Graduates move into professional accounting, audit, tax and advisory roles.

name: Master of Project Management
description: The RMIT Master of Project Management is designed for professionals working or looking to work in project management, emphasising the practical application of theory to respond to current and emerging trends. Students critically engage with project management theory and best practice, and evaluate and implement strategies using real-world, project-based cases, learning to run complex projects with a range of stakeholders. Graduates work as project and program managers across engineering, IT, construction, events and government.

name: Master of Property
description: The RMIT Master of Property is an industry-connected degree that develops the skills for high-level and senior management roles in the property sector. Graduates gain sound knowledge of property as an asset class in local and global contexts, the ability to independently conduct research and analyse industry trends, and the teamwork and management skills to formulate industry solutions and make evidence-based decisions. Graduates work in property development, investment, asset management and valuation.

name: Master of Public Policy
description: The RMIT Master of Public Policy deepens understanding of critical societal issues and engagement in policy development, taught by leading policy academics and industry professionals and reflecting the latest debates and approaches to global, national and local policymaking. Graduates work as policymakers, advocates and managers in human services, government and non-government organisations, and increasingly in the private and corporate sectors.

name: Master of Science (Applied Physics)
description: The Master of Science (Applied Physics) at RMIT University develops advanced research skills and lets students contribute to new developments in applied physics. Under expert supervision, students join researchers active in areas including advanced imaging and nanoscale characterisation, fibre optics and optical spectroscopy, materials physics, medical physics and bioimaging, neutron and X-ray imaging and scattering, quantum computing and quantum information, quantum materials, optics and sensing, radiation physics and dosimetry, and soft matter and biological physics. It is a masters by research undertaken in Melbourne.

name: Master of Social Science (Global, Urban & Social Studies)
description: The Master of Social Science (Global, Urban and Social Studies) at RMIT University is a research degree that develops advanced research principles, methods and mastery of a body of knowledge in the social sciences through a thesis or research project. Individually supervised programs are available across three areas: the social, the urban and the global. RMIT has particular expertise in urban planning and housing studies, sustainability, criminology, globalisation and cultures studies, applied linguistics, translating and interpreting, sociology, international development and relations, community development, social and public policy, and social work. Students nurture industry partnerships and collaborate with other researchers.

name: Master of Social Work
description: The RMIT Master of Social Work is a postgraduate qualifying program from a school that has taught social work for over 40 years, with programs that reflect contemporary ideas about social work in a changing world. Field education forms a large component, with students undertaking 140 days of work placements in human and community service organisations. Graduates practise as social workers in health, child and family services, mental health, community development and policy.

name: Master of Statistics and Operations Research
description: The RMIT Master of Statistics and Operations Research combines a theoretical foundation with practical applications of the current techniques used by engineers, scientists and other professionals in industry, research, consulting, teaching and business, using statistical software alongside an in-depth understanding of the statistical processes involved. Graduates work as statisticians, operations research analysts, data scientists and quantitative consultants. Students graduate knowledgeable, creative and critical in how they interpret and analyse data.

name: Master of Supply Chain and Logistics Management
description: The RMIT Master of Supply Chain and Logistics Management teaches students to negotiate contracts, resolve conflicts, design efficient processes and solve complex logistical problems, preparing them to design and scale supply chains globally. Students benefit from project work and interactions with leading global companies, and develop project management and negotiation skills, with advanced standing available for previous study. Graduates work in supply chain strategy, procurement, logistics and operations roles.

name: Master of Technology (Fashion & Textiles)
description: The Master of Technology (Fashion and Textiles) by Research at RMIT University enables students to develop an advanced body of knowledge applied to real-life research contexts. Individually supervised programs align with the school's Centre for Materials Innovation and Future Fashion or its research streams, reflecting supervisors' expertise and collaborative relationships with industry. The program is undertaken by thesis mode and suits candidates taking a scientific approach to advanced textiles and material science, such as protective, medical and forensic textiles and performance apparel, or a social science approach to an aspect of the fashion and textiles system. RMIT is ranked number one in Australia and 19th in the world for art and design in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026.

name: Master of Translating and Interpreting
description: The RMIT Master of Translating and Interpreting, taught in the heart of Melbourne, develops expertise and a deeper understanding of language and communication. Students learn to use communication media to support translating and interpreting and gain insight into the intersection of theory and practice, with options to study interpreting for community health, medical, police and legal contexts and conferences, linking technology, ethics and theory to practical issues. Graduates work as translators and interpreters across government, health, legal and community settings.

name: Master of Urban Design
description: The RMIT Master of Urban Design confronts critical issues affecting cities, such as climate change, population growth, shifting workplaces and transformations in industry, technology and infrastructure. In a studio-based, multidisciplinary environment, students engage these issues through project-based study, learning to creatively integrate expertise from related urban disciplines into design proposals that promote alternative models for future city-building. Graduates work as urban designers in design studios, planning consultancies and government.

name: Master of Urban Planning and Environment
description: The RMIT Master of Urban Planning and Environment prepares students to create sustainable, liveable and equitable urban places. Students develop skills in critical analysis, engage in professionally relevant projects and research, and promote effective policy outcomes, with practical and experiential learning working on planning problems in the field and consulting with industry. The degree is widely supported by industry, with the majority of urban planners in Victoria being RMIT alumni. Graduates work as urban and environmental planners in government, consultancies and property organisations.

name: Master of Writing and Publishing
description: The RMIT Master of Writing and Publishing explores the publishing process from manuscript to marketplace, with the opportunity to intern at Bowen Street Press, a student-led independent publishing house on RMIT's city campus. Students learn in small classes from acclaimed academics and industry experts, and gain real-world experience through connected studios that pose specific industry challenges. Graduates work in book and digital publishing, editing, writing and content roles.

name: PhD (Biomedical Engineering)
description: The PhD (Biomedical Engineering) at RMIT University is a higher degree by research in which candidates develop the advanced knowledge and skills to create engineering solutions to health and medical conditions for patients, professionals and healthcare workers. Candidates have access to leading researchers and facilities in biomaterials, biomechanics, medical electronics, signal processing and tissue engineering, and to 3D-printing facilities including the Digital Manufacturing Facility, the MicroNano Research Facility and the Aikenhead Centre for Medical Discovery. RMIT is ranked ninth in Australia and in the top 150 globally for engineering and technology in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026.

name: Advanced Diploma of Accounting
description:
This qualification (FNS60222) sits above the standard Diploma of Accounting as the next rung for people already working in accounting or bookkeeping roles who want to move into more senior positions without doing a full university degree. There's no work placement requirement built in, which reflects that most students taking this at South Metro TAFE are already employed in the industry and studying around their job rather than starting from zero.

Delivery leans heavily online with mandatory on-campus attendance for assessments, and the college is upfront that students should budget 10-15 hours a week of study outside class time: assignment prep, private study and research on top of scheduled contact hours. That's a meaningful time commitment for people who are often studying part-time while working full-time, which is the more common profile for this level of qualification than a straight-from-school student.

The practical payoff is Tax Practitioners Board recognition: complete the prescribed taxation units and pass them, and graduates become eligible to pursue registration as a Registered Tax Agent, a credential that opens up self-employed tax practice or more senior roles in accounting firms handling client tax affairs.
curriculum:
Core units: complex corporate reporting requirements, financial reports for corporate entities, management accounting systems, budgets and forecasts, tax documentation for legal entities
Elective units: audit and assurance practice, financial risk management, specialised tax practices (prescribed units required for Tax Practitioners Board pathway)
Delivery: predominantly online with mandatory on-campus attendance for scheduled assessments
No mandatory work placement; approximately 10-15 hours per week of self-directed study expected outside class
Pathway: eligible graduates (with prescribed taxation units) can pursue Registered Tax Agent recognition through the Tax Practitioners Board
admission_requirements: Diploma of Accounting or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 (no band below 5.0)

name: Advanced Diploma of Apparel, Fashion and Textiles
Advanced Diploma of Civil and Structural Engineering
Advanced Diploma of Civil Construction Design
Advanced Diploma of Creative Product Development
Advanced Diploma of Engineering Technology - Electrical
Advanced Diploma of Maritime Operations (Master Unlimited)
Advanced Diploma of Screen and Media
Diploma of Accounting
description:
The standard-level Diploma of Accounting (FNS50222) is the more common entry point into professional accounting study at South Metro TAFE, sitting below the Advanced Diploma and typically taken by people who haven't yet worked in the field rather than those already employed and upskilling. It shares the same no-mandatory-placement structure as the Advanced Diploma: the assumption is that competency is demonstrated through simulated business scenarios and assessment tasks rather than a supervised workplace stint.

Like its advanced counterpart, delivery is mostly online with scheduled on-campus attendance for assessments, and the college flags 10-15 hours a week of expected self-directed study on top of scheduled contact. Accounting coursework tends to be assignment-heavy and cumulative, so falling behind on one unit's calculations makes the next unit noticeably harder.

Graduates commonly move into bookkeeping, accounts assistant or accounts payable/receivable roles, and the diploma functions as a credit-bearing pathway into further study, either the Advanced Diploma for those wanting Tax Agent registration eligibility, or articulation into a related university accounting degree for students who decide partway through that they want the fuller qualification.
curriculum:
Core units: financial reports preparation for reporting entities, management accounting systems, tax documentation for individual and business clients, budgeting and forecasting
Elective units: selected in consultation with industry (options may include payroll systems, business software applications, workplace financial systems)
Delivery: predominantly online with mandatory on-campus attendance for scheduled assessments
No mandatory work placement; approximately 10-15 hours per week of self-directed study expected outside class
Pathway: articulation into Advanced Diploma of Accounting or related university accounting/commerce degrees
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 (no band below 5.0)

name: Diploma of Apparel, Fashion and Textiles
Diploma of Business
description:
The Diploma of Business at South Metro TAFE is the deliberately broad option in the college's business suite. Where the Diploma of Accounting and Diploma of Hospitality Management lock students into a named discipline from the start, this qualification builds general business administration, project coordination and leadership competencies that apply across office environments regardless of sector.

That breadth is the point rather than a shortcoming: students who aren't sure yet whether they want to specialise into accounting, marketing, HR or operations get a year to build transferable skills and figure out direction, and the qualification is commonly used as a stepping stone into supervisory or team-leader roles in whatever industry a student happens to already be working in, rather than requiring a career change to make use of it.

As with the other business-suite diplomas at the college, there's no mandatory industry placement; assessment relies on workplace simulations and, where students are already employed, real workplace projects and evidence drawn from their existing job.
curriculum:
Core units: business innovation and improvement processes, workplace health and safety systems, business risk management, project scope and objectives, team leadership and workplace communication
Elective units: selected in consultation with industry (options may include human resources fundamentals, marketing principles, business technology and systems)
No mandatory work placement; assessment via workplace simulation and, for employed students, real workplace project evidence
Study load: approximately 10-15 hours per week of self-directed study expected outside scheduled class time
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 (no band below 5.0)

name: Diploma of Civil and Structural Engineering
Diploma of Community Services
description:
Entry into South Metropolitan TAFE's Diploma of Community Services (CHC52021) generally expects a Certificate IV in Community Services already completed, or equivalent industry experience: it's pitched at people who've already had some exposure to the sector rather than a first qualification for someone entirely new to community work. The approximately 240 hours of mandatory work placement is arranged by the college itself rather than left to students to source, and comes with its own logbook system that both the student and the host workplace need to complete.

Because placements put students into direct contact with vulnerable community members, the compliance requirements are more involved than for most other diplomas at this level: a Working With Children Check and National Police Clearance are required before placement starts, and students must be 18 or over to go on placement at all, an industry-wide requirement rather than something specific to this college.

Graduates typically move into case work, community support, disability services or youth work roles, and the diploma level is often the practical ceiling for direct-service roles before further specialisation (such as a related degree) becomes necessary for case management or supervisory positions.
curriculum:
Prerequisite: Certificate IV in Community Services (or equivalent industry experience)
Core units: case management, community services context and practice, client advocacy, work within a legal and ethical framework, trauma-informed practice
Elective units: selected in consultation with industry (options may include disability support, youth work, family and domestic violence response)
Mandatory work placement: approximately 240 hours, arranged/negotiated by South Metropolitan TAFE, documented via vocational placement logbook
Compliance requirements: Working With Children Check and National Police Clearance required before placement; students must be 18+
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 (no band below 5.0)

name: Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care
description:
This diploma only opens up once a student already holds the Certificate III in Early Childhood Education and Care. It's a deliberate two-stage pathway rather than a standalone entry qualification, which means every student arrives with at least some paid or supervised experience already in a childcare setting. The diploma itself runs across two stages, each carrying 360 hours of mandatory work placement, for a combined 720 hours of supervised field experience across the qualification, a substantial practical component relative to the classroom time.

South Metro TAFE structures the course to work around people already employed in the sector: full-time study runs at roughly two days a week (or one evening at the Rockingham campus for students working in a regulated childcare service), and those students can count their paid work hours toward the placement requirement rather than needing to find separate unpaid placement time on top of a job.

Graduates typically move into lead educator or room leader roles in long day care, and the diploma is also the recognised qualification level for meeting the "diploma-qualified educator" ratio requirements under the National Quality Framework, which is what makes it valuable to centres beyond just the individual's own skill development.
curriculum:
Prerequisite: Certificate III in Early Childhood Education and Care (CHC30121 or equivalent)
Stage 1: children's health, safety and wellbeing, curriculum planning for early learning, working with families and communities, 360 hours supervised work placement
Stage 2: leadership and program development, inclusive practice for children with additional needs, legal and ethical frameworks in ECEC, further 360 hours supervised work placement
Total placement: 720 hours across the diploma (working students may count paid hours in a regulated service)
Study load: approximately 2 days per week full-time (or evening delivery at Rockingham for employed students)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, Working with Children Check required
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 5.5)

name: Diploma of Electronics and Communications Engineering
Diploma of Engineering - Technical
description:
This diploma (MEM50222) sits in the engineering trades pathway rather than the professional engineering pathway: it's the technical-officer-level qualification that follows on from trade or apprenticeship training, not a route toward becoming a registered engineer, which is an important distinction for students weighing this against a university engineering degree. Full-time study runs at roughly three to four days a week.

South Metro TAFE also runs this as a traineeship option, meaning eligible students can be employed under a formal training contract with an engineering or manufacturing employer and earn a wage while working through the qualification. That's a genuinely different funding and career model from full-time classroom study, and one that suits people already in the trades workforce wanting to move up without stopping work entirely.

The qualification targets specific technical roles rather than a generic "engineering" outcome: the college names CAD operator, hydraulic fitter, mechanical technician and robotics technician as typical destinations, which gives a fairly concrete sense of the mechanical/automation trades employers actually hire this diploma's graduates into.
curriculum:
Core units: engineering drawing and CAD interpretation, materials science for engineering trades, mechanical systems and components, quality and testing procedures, workplace health and safety in engineering environments
Elective units: selected in consultation with industry (options may include hydraulics and pneumatics, robotics and automation systems, CNC machining)
Delivery: full-time equivalent to 3-4 days per week; also available as a traineeship for students employed under a training contract
Typical outcomes: CAD operator, hydraulic fitter, mechanical technician, robotics technician
Pathway: foundation for further study toward Advanced Diploma of Engineering (Mechanical/Electrical)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent with Mathematics
english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 (no band below 5.0)

name: Diploma of Environmental Monitoring and Technology
Diploma of Hospitality Management
description:
This diploma requires 28 units of competency (13 core plus 15 electives chosen in consultation with industry), and its most distinctive feature is where the practical training actually happens: South Metro TAFE runs students through the Bentley Pines Restaurant and Bar, a real, publicly dining venue on campus where students take on management responsibilities and serve actual paying customers rather than simulated ones. That's a genuinely different practical experience from hospitality courses that rely purely on mock service exercises.

There's no external work placement requirement, which is a little unusual for a hospitality qualification: the college's position is that the Bentley Pines operation already delivers the equivalent supervised, real-world management experience without students needing to source an outside venue and juggle two sets of rostering and assessment expectations.

Career outcomes the college points to include function manager, restaurant manager and front office manager roles, all management-track positions rather than entry-level service jobs, reflecting that this is the "management" diploma rather than the operational Certificate III/IV level that precedes it in the hospitality qualification ladder.
curriculum:
Core units (13): financial management for hospitality venues, staff rostering and workforce planning, WHS management in hospitality, quality customer service, licensing and compliance for hospitality operations
Elective units (15, industry-consulted): food and beverage service management, event and function coordination, revenue and yield management, front office operations
Practical component: face-to-face management practice in the Bentley Pines Restaurant and Bar (on-campus, open to the public)
No external work placement requirement
Total: 28 units of competency; typical outcomes include function manager, restaurant manager, front office manager
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 (no band below 5.0)

name: Diploma of Information Technology (Advanced Networking)
description:
This diploma assumes students already have hands-on networking competence before day one: the college is explicit that applicants should already be comfortable deploying and configuring virtual machines, subnetting, and configuring switches and routers, and points people without that background toward the Certificate IV in IT (Networking) first. That's a more practical entry bar than a generic "must have completed Year 12" requirement, and it keeps the diploma cohort at a more consistent skill level than open-entry courses often achieve.

Every SM TAFE diploma-level IT unit set folds in cyber security awareness, client management and professional ethics regardless of specialisation, so networking students aren't learning switch configuration in isolation from the security and client-facing skills that actual network administrator jobs require day to day.

The course is squarely vocational rather than theoretical. The training is built around current industry equipment and standards rather than networking theory divorced from what employers are actually running, which suits students aiming directly at network administrator, IT support or junior systems engineer roles rather than further academic study.
curriculum:
Prerequisite skills (or Certificate IV in IT - Networking): VM deployment and configuration, subnetting, switch and router configuration
Core units: advanced network design and implementation, network security and threat management, server administration, cloud infrastructure fundamentals
Cross-diploma units (all SM TAFE IT diplomas): cyber security awareness, working in teams, client management skills, ethics and privacy in IT
Elective units: selected in consultation with industry, aligned to current networking equipment and standards
No formal industry placement; hands-on lab-based assessment using current networking hardware
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 (no band below 5.0)

name: Diploma of Nursing
description:
This is the qualification that produces Enrolled Nurses in Western Australia: a genuinely different clinical scope from the Registered Nurse pathway that runs through university, and South Metro TAFE builds the course around human biology, medical terminology, pharmacology and person-centred care rather than the broader theory base of a nursing degree. Placement here is not optional or arranged loosely: it's mandatory for completion, and the college organises it directly rather than leaving students to find their own healthcare facility.

The placement conditions are worth being upfront about because they surprise some students: shifts run across the full week including public holidays, in week-long blocks, and can be rostered morning, afternoon or night, a genuine simulation of shift-work nursing rather than a business-hours internship. Facilities used for placement can be up to a 45-minute drive from campus, and transport and parking costs during placement are the student's own responsibility, which matters for people budgeting around a full-time study load.

Every student is issued a clinical placement handbook to document progress and works under the direct supervision of a nominated registered nurse throughout, a structured, closely supervised model reflecting how much is genuinely at stake in nursing placements compared with most other vocational diplomas.
curriculum:
Core units: human biosciences for nursing, medication administration and pharmacology, person-centred nursing care, mental health nursing, chronic and complex care, professional and legal requirements for enrolled nurses
Elective units: selected in consultation with industry (may include palliative care, perioperative nursing, or maternal and child health)
Mandatory clinical placement: arranged directly by South Metropolitan TAFE, week-long shift blocks including weekends/public holidays and morning/afternoon/night shifts, supervised by a registered nurse, documented via clinical placement handbook
Compliance and logistics: placement facilities may be up to 45 minutes from campus; transport/parking costs are the student's responsibility
On completion: eligible for registration as an Enrolled Nurse with AHPRA
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, National Police Check and Working with Children Check required
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 6.5)

name: Diploma of Photography and Digital Imaging
Diploma of Screen and Media
description:
This diploma runs with named specialisation streams rather than a single generalist screen production pathway. Options at South Metro TAFE have included animation, gaming, visual effects and immersive media production on one hand, and specialist make-up services for film, television and live theatre events on the other, which is a wider spread than most screen diplomas offer under one course code. Students effectively pick a lane early rather than sampling broadly across all of screen and media production.

Full-time study runs at roughly three days a week of scheduled attendance, but the college is explicit that students should expect an additional 25% of self-directed work on top of that: portfolio pieces, render time for animation and VFX work, or practice sessions for make-up students, none of which fits neatly into scheduled class hours the way theory-based subjects do.

The training environment is built around industry-standard software and equipment rather than education-only tools, which matters in a field where employers screening entry-level hires often look directly at a demo reel or portfolio rather than a transcript. The diploma's value is largely in what students can show, not just what units they completed.
curriculum:
Core units: screen and media industry practice, pre-production and concept development, digital production techniques, project management for screen and media
Specialisation stream (varies by intake): Animation, Gaming and Visual Effects — 3D modelling, animation principles, compositing and visual effects, game asset development
OR Specialist Make-Up Services — character and creature make-up, prosthetics, make-up for film/TV and live theatre production
Capstone: portfolio or showreel project demonstrating specialisation competencies
Study load: approximately 3 days/week scheduled attendance plus an additional 25% self-directed work (portfolio development, render/practice time)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 (no band below 5.0)

name: Diploma of Travel and Tourism Management
Associate Degree of Business and Enterprise
Associate Degree of Global Hotel Management
Associate Degree of International Hotel and Tourism Management
Bachelor of Business
description:
The Bachelor of Business at Southern Cross gives students a choice most business degrees don't: take one major plus a run of electives and a double internship, or pair the major with a full second major (a "shared major") pulled from another discipline entirely. That second path is the more distinctive one: a marketing major paired with a psychology shared major, say, produces a different graduate than the standard single-major business degree most competitors offer.

Majors on offer include business and data analytics, entrepreneurship and innovation, international business, marketing, and tourism and event management, plus professionally accredited specialisations in accounting and financial services for students chasing CPA or CA pathways later. The internship option is double-weighted, meaning it counts for more credit than a standard elective, and gives students actual workplace hours to point to at graduation rather than just coursework.

Given SCU's footprint on the NSW north coast and Gold Coast, the tourism and event management major in particular draws on genuine regional industry connections rather than being a bolt-on to a generic commerce curriculum.
curriculum:
8 core units: Accounting for Decision Making, Economics for Business, Business Statistics, Marketing Principles, Managing People and Organisations, Business Law, Business Ethics and Sustainability, Strategic Management
Major (choose one, 96 credit points): Accounting / Business and Data Analytics / Entrepreneurship and Innovation / Financial Services / International Business / Marketing / Tourism and Event Management / Aviation Management
Either: 4 option units + 2 double-weighted Internship or Industry Project units
Or: a second Shared Major (96 credit points) from another SCU discipline in place of options and internship
Capstone integrated into the major's final units
admission_requirements: ATAR ~60+ (or equivalent Year 12); no prerequisite subjects
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Business and Enterprise (Aviation Management)
Bachelor of Business in Hotel Management
Bachelor of Business in Tourism and Hospitality Management
Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description:
SCU's Bachelor of Education (Primary) is a 32-unit, four-year degree that front-loads professional experience earlier and more frequently than a lot of comparable teaching degrees: four separate professional experience placements are built into the structure rather than one long final-year practicum. Like the university's other degrees, it runs on six-week teaching blocks, which changes the rhythm of assignment deadlines and exam periods compared to a standard semester system.

For students who decide partway through that primary teaching isn't the right fit, or who need to pause for financial or personal reasons, SCU built in staged exit qualifications: complete 24 units and you can leave with a Bachelor of Educational Studies, 16 units gets an Associate Degree of Educational Studies, and 8 units gets a Diploma of Education. That's an unusually explicit safety net compared to most teaching degrees, which tend to treat any early departure as a dropout rather than a credentialed off-ramp.

Graduates are eligible for registration as primary school teachers through NESA (or the equivalent body interstate), and the degree can also be taken combined with a Bachelor of Arts for students who want breadth alongside the teaching qualification.
curriculum:
Core education units across four years: Child Development and Learning, Curriculum Studies (Literacy, Numeracy, Science, HASS, The Arts, Health and PE), Educational Psychology, Inclusive Education, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Education, Classroom Management
Four Professional Experience placements distributed across the degree, increasing in duration and responsibility
Exit points: Diploma of Education (8 units) / Associate Degree of Educational Studies (16 units) / Bachelor of Educational Studies (24 units) / full Bachelor of Education, Primary specialisation (32 units)
Final-year capstone professional experience placement and portfolio for NESA-aligned graduate teacher standards
admission_requirements: ATAR ~65+ (or equivalent Year 12), plus Working with Children Check
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 overall, no band below 7.0 (teaching registration requirement)

name: Bachelor of Environmental Science
description:
The environmental science degree at SCU is inseparable from its geography: first and second-year units run at the Lismore campus, but students move to the National Marine Science Centre in Coffs Harbour for specialist third-year units delivered in intensive mode, covering oceanography, marine ecology, coral reef ecology and marine pollution. That's a genuinely unusual arrangement (a dedicated marine science facility used for intensive block teaching rather than folded into a generic on-campus environmental science curriculum), and it means students get hands-on field and lab time at a research centre most environmental science degrees can't offer.

The degree sits within a broader Bachelor of Science framework at SCU that also covers agriculture and earth systems specialisations, so environmental science students share early coursework (ecology, ecosystem regeneration, resource management, environmental modelling) with peers heading into agricultural or marine-specific tracks before diverging in later years.

Graduates come out with a mix of terrestrial and coastal environmental competencies: useful for roles spanning land management, regional council environmental planning, and marine or coastal conservation work along the NSW north coast and beyond.
curriculum:
Year 1 (Lismore): Introduction to Environmental Science, Ecology, Chemistry for Environmental Science, Earth Systems, Statistics for Science
Year 2 (Lismore, some Coffs Harbour intensives): Ecosystem Regeneration, Environmental Modelling, Soil and Water Science, Resource Management
Year 3 (intensive blocks at the National Marine Science Centre, Coffs Harbour): Oceanography, Marine Ecology, Marine Pollution, Coral Reef Ecology, Marine Ecosystem Management
Capstone: independent research project or industry-linked environmental project in final year
admission_requirements: ATAR ~60+ (or equivalent Year 12)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Exercise Science and Psychological Science
Bachelor of Global Hotel and Tourism Management
Bachelor of Health Science (Health and Lifestyle)
Bachelor of Laws
description:
The LLB at Southern Cross is accredited by the NSW Legal Profession Admission Board, which means graduates can seek admission to practice anywhere in Australia after completing Practical Legal Training (PLT). The degree itself doesn't confer admission, and students need to budget for a PLT course afterward on top of the LLB. Core units cover the expected ground (Civil Litigation and Procedure, Evidence, Australian Criminal Law, Professional Conduct) plus a Philosophy of Law unit that pushes students toward legal theory rather than pure black-letter law.

One genuinely distinctive feature: the elective Mediation Practice and Procedure unit meets the training and assessment threshold under the National Mediator Accreditation System, so a law student can graduate with a mediation credential recognised outside the courtroom, not just a law degree. Environmental Law also sits among the core rather than elective units, which lines up with SCU's broader environmental science strength and gives the degree a slight regional/environmental-law lean compared to a purely commercial-law-focused LLB elsewhere.

The degree is also offered as a combined program with a Bachelor of Arts or Bachelor of Legal and Justice Studies for students wanting breadth before specialising.
curriculum:
Core units: Legal Research and Writing, Australian Legal System, Contracts, Torts, Property Law, Civil Litigation and Procedure, Evidence, Australian Criminal Law, Constitutional Law, Environmental Law, Professional Conduct, The Philosophy of Law
Electives include Mediation Practice and Procedure (meets National Mediator Accreditation System threshold requirements)
Final-year capstone unit integrating advocacy and legal ethics
Graduates require separately completed Practical Legal Training (PLT) before admission to legal practice
admission_requirements: ATAR ~70+ (or equivalent Year 12)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Legal and Justice Studies
Bachelor of Nursing
description:
SCU's Bachelor of Nursing is built around 840 hours of supervised clinical placement, the threshold AHPRA sets for registration eligibility, spread across residential aged care, GP practices, community health settings and hospital wards in regional and sometimes remote New South Wales. Placements run two to six weeks at a stretch, and because SCU's campuses sit outside the major capitals (Lismore, Coffs Harbour, Gold Coast), students frequently end up placed in rural and under-served facilities that metro university cohorts rarely see, a genuine point of difference for anyone weighing a nursing career outside the big cities.

The degree is structured as a three-year progression where clinical exposure escalates each year rather than being backloaded into a single capstone placement block, which the university describes as scaffolding cognitive, emotional and clinical capability development in parallel. Coursework covers pathophysiology, pharmacology, mental health nursing and aged care alongside the practical placement rotations.

Graduates are eligible to apply for registration as a Registered Nurse with AHPRA, and the regional placement footprint means many students end up with employment leads in the same communities where they trained.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Health Assessment, Introduction to Professional Nursing, first clinical placement block
Year 2: Pathophysiology and Pharmacology, Mental Health Nursing, Nursing Older People, Acute Care Nursing, expanding placement rotations across aged care and community settings
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing, Child and Family Health, Leadership in Nursing Practice, Transition to Professional Practice, final capstone clinical placement
Total supervised Work Integrated Learning across the degree: approximately 840 hours, required for AHPRA registration eligibility
admission_requirements: ATAR ~60+ (or equivalent Year 12), plus health/immunisation and police checks
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0 (nursing registration requirement)

name: Bachelor of Nursing - Enrolled Nurse to Registered Nurse Pathway
Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
This is the accreditation-pathway degree for students who actually want to become psychologists rather than just study psychology as a general interest. It's conditionally accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC) as the first rung (the 3+1 model still requires a fourth-year Honours or equivalent afterward). SCU also offers the Honours year as a direct follow-on, which is the fully APAC-accredited stage that unlocks provisional registration and postgraduate clinical training.

Students can pursue the Psychology Extension Major for the most direct route toward the accredited sequence, or take a shared major or open electives if they want psychology alongside another discipline without committing to the registration pathway from day one, useful for students still deciding whether clinical psychology, forensic work, or something adjacent like HR or research is the actual goal.

Coursework covers the core APAC knowledge areas: biological bases of behaviour, cognition, developmental psychology, social psychology, and research methods and statistics, with statistics weighted more heavily than in most humanities degrees given how much of professional psychology training downstream depends on quantitative research literacy.
curriculum:
Core units: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Psychology, Cognition and Learning, Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology, Research Methods in Psychology I and II, Psychological Testing and Assessment, Abnormal Psychology, Personality and Individual Differences
Major options: Psychology Extension Major (APAC-aligned sequence) OR a Shared Major from another discipline OR 8 elective units
Statistics and research methods sequence runs across multiple years rather than a single unit
Exit into Bachelor of Psychological Science with Honours (separate, fully APAC-accredited fourth year) for students pursuing provisional psychologist registration
admission_requirements: ATAR ~65+ (or equivalent Year 12)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science with Honours
Bachelor of Social Work
description:
Two supervised field placements, in two different human service organisations, totalling 1,000 hours, sit at the centre of this degree: that's the Australian Association of Social Workers' (AASW) accreditation requirement, and SCU structures the whole course around building toward those placements rather than treating them as an add-on at the end. Placement I runs 500 hours in one organisation, Placement II runs 600 hours in a second, deliberately different setting, so graduates leave having practiced in two distinct parts of the human services sector rather than specialising narrowly before they've even started work.

Because SCU's placement network draws on regional NSW and Gold Coast community organisations, students often end up placed in settings that a metro-based social work degree's placement pool wouldn't typically reach, such as remote community health, regional Aboriginal community-controlled organisations, or rural family services. Before placement starts, students need to clear Working with Children and National Police Certificate checks, and local placement isn't guaranteed even for students who live nearby.

Graduates are eligible for AASW accreditation, the qualification employers actually check for when hiring into social work positions across health, child protection, and community services.
curriculum:
Core units: Introduction to Social Work Practice, Human Behaviour and the Social Environment, Social Policy and Social Justice, Social Work Theory and Methods, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Perspectives on Social Work, Research for Social Work Practice, Mental Health and Social Work, Working with Families and Groups
Social Work Placement I — 500 hours supervised WIL in a human service organisation
Social Work Placement II — 600 hours supervised WIL in a second, different organisation
Mandatory compliance checks (Working with Children, National Police Certificate) required before each placement
Total WIL across the degree: 1,000 hours, meeting AASW accreditation standards
admission_requirements: ATAR ~65+ (or equivalent Year 12), plus Working with Children Check
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 6.5

name: Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Science
Diploma of Clinical and Allied Health
Diploma of Health and Human Sciences
Graduate Certificate in Early Childhood Education Leadership
Graduate Certificate in Social Sciences for Social Work
Graduate Certificate of Business in Global Hotel Leadership
Graduate Diploma of Business in Global Hotel Leadership
Master of Business Administration
description:
SCU's MBA is built around a single specialisation choice rather than a menu of electives: most students take Business Analytics and Artificial Intelligence, reflecting where the university has clearly decided to place its bet on what differentiates the degree from a generic MBA. Students who'd rather keep things broad can swap the specialisation for two additional elective units instead, trading depth in one area for a wider spread across leadership and management topics.

The capstone is an industry research project tied to the student's own workplace or a career direction they're moving toward, rather than a generic case-study exam, which means the final deliverable doubles as a portfolio piece for job applications or internal promotion cases. Like the rest of SCU's postgraduate suite, the MBA runs on six-week study blocks, letting full-time-equivalent students who study continuously finish faster than the traditional two-year MBA timeline.

An online-only Managing and Leading People variant exists as a separate, more HR-focused version of the degree for students who know upfront that people management rather than analytics is their priority.
curriculum:
Core units: Leadership and Organisational Behaviour, Strategic Management, Managerial Finance, Marketing Management, Operations and Supply Chain Management, Economics for Managers, Business Ethics and Governance, plus foundation units for non-business-background entrants
Specialisation: Business Analytics and Artificial Intelligence (or 2 elective units in place of the specialisation)
Capstone: Industry Research Project, tied to the student's current or target workplace
Delivered in six-week teaching blocks; full course length varies with prior credit and specialisation choice
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree plus professional work experience preferred
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Business in Global Hotel Leadership
Master of Engineering Management
description: Southern Cross University Master of Engineering Management uses a focused six-week unit model and requires the equivalent of eight units (96 credit points), which a full-time student completes in about a year. Learning is active and discussion-based, delivered on campus or fully online with workshops, virtual classes and online forums. Entry requires a four-year undergraduate degree in engineering or a cognate discipline, or a three-year degree in engineering or a cognate discipline plus at least two years of documented relevant work experience, or equivalent recognised prior learning and industry experience; international applicants and those who studied in another language meet English requirements. Indicative international tuition is around A$52,000 per year. Graduates step into engineering leadership and management roles across the sector.

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
Southern Cross runs its Master of Information Technology on the university's six-week unit calendar rather than the standard 12-week semester, so students who want to accelerate can push through the 16 units required for the full degree in a little over a year instead of two. That compressed cadence suits the cohort it tends to attract: IT professionals switching tracks, or international graduates using the degree as a fast, structured entry point into an Australian tech career.

The course leans specifically toward data science and cyber security rather than trying to cover the entire IT waterfront, and Microsoft certification content is folded directly into coursework so graduates leave with credentials alongside the testamur. Students choose one specialisation from a list that includes advanced cyber security, big data analysis, computational intelligence and machine learning, computer forensics, and mobile and cloud systems, which means two students finishing the same degree in the same year can walk away with genuinely different skill sets.

A notable design choice is the exit fork at the end: instead of a single final-year project, students pick between a research project and an industry-based learning placement. The latter puts SCU's regional industry partnerships to direct use, useful for anyone building an Australian work history rather than just a transcript.
curriculum:
9 core units (data science, cyber security, software development, user experience, and systems foundations) — 48 credit points
One specialisation stream, choose one: Advanced Cyber Security / Big Data Analysis / Computational Intelligence and Machine Learning / Computer Forensics / Internet Engineering / Pervasive and Immersive User Experience / Programming for the Internet of Things / Mobile and Cloud Systems — 48 credit points
1 option unit — 24 credit points
Capstone: Research Project OR Industry-Based Learning placement
Delivered across six-week teaching blocks rather than standard 12-week semesters; 16 units (192 credit points) total for students without recognised prior learning
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant or any discipline (typical Australian postgrad IT/CS entry bar used as approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Master of Social Work (Qualifying)
description:
This is SCU's graduate-entry route into professional social work practice for students who already hold a bachelor's degree in an unrelated field and want to requalify rather than start an undergraduate degree from scratch. It carries the same AASW-mandated 1,000 hours of supervised placement as the undergraduate program, but compressed into a postgraduate timeframe: Field Placement I runs 400 hours (57 days) across sessions two and three of first year, and Field Placement II runs 600 hours (86 days) across sessions two and three of second year, each in a different human service organisation.

Both on-campus and online students complete the same two placements in two different fields of practice, which the university frames as deliberately building breadth of experience rather than letting students stay in one comfortable setting for the whole degree. Coursework compresses the theoretical foundations of social work (human behaviour, social policy, practice methods) into a shorter timeframe than the undergraduate degree, on the assumption that students bring existing academic maturity and often relevant life or work experience from their first degree.

Graduates qualify for AASW accreditation and can move directly into social work roles in health, child protection, mental health, and community services.
curriculum:
Foundational units: Social Work Theory and Practice, Human Behaviour and the Social Environment, Social Policy and Advocacy, Research Methods for Social Work, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Perspectives
Field Placement I — 400 hours (57 days) across Sessions 2–3, Year 1, minimum three days per week
Field Placement II — 600 hours (86 days) across Sessions 2–3, Year 2, in a different organisation to Placement I
Mandatory Working with Children and National Police Certificate checks before each placement
Total WIL: 1,000 hours, meeting AASW accreditation requirements for the qualifying degree
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in any discipline (non-social work background)
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 6.5

name: Advanced Diploma of Engineering Technology - Electrical
Associate Degree of Applied Artificial Intelligence
description: The Associate Degree of Applied Artificial Intelligence at Swinburne University of Technology is a two-year full-time degree that equips students to apply artificial intelligence within cyber security or game development industries. Through industry-immersed projects, students gain practical skills, knowledge and a strong sense of the ethical use of AI. Graduates work in applied AI roles and can pathway into a bachelor degree. Indicative international tuition is around 39,700 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 119239M.

name: Associate Degree of Aviation
description: The Associate Degree of Aviation at Swinburne University of Technology is an eighteen-month degree designed for students accepted into an airline cadet training program. It prepares students for a professional pilot career with training delivered through CAE Melbourne Flight Training that goes beyond the minimum licensing requirements set by the Civil Aviation Safety Authority. Graduates progress toward airline pilot careers. The course holds CRICOS registration 119364F.

name: Associate Degree of Computing Technologies
description: The Associate Degree of Computing Technologies at Swinburne University of Technology, delivered through the Associate Degree in Applied Technologies, is a two-year full-time degree that equips students with engineering and digital technology skills to deploy Industry 4.0 technologies. Students work through industry-based projects and practical workshops and can choose a major such as civil engineering or mechanical systems. Graduates work in technical and para-professional technology roles or pathway into a bachelor degree.

name: Associate Degree of Engineering
description: The Associate Degree of Engineering at Swinburne University of Technology is a two-year full-time degree that provides the technical skills and qualification to work as an associate engineer, or a pathway into the Bachelor of Engineering. It includes eight industry projects and majors in areas such as civil, electrical and electronics, and mechanical engineering. Graduates work as engineering associates and technicians. Indicative international tuition is around 41,100 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 108893E.

name: Associate Degree of Science
description: The Associate Degree of Science at Swinburne University of Technology is a two-year full-time degree covering key scientific skills and knowledge, delivered through the university's science offering with majors such as applied mathematics and astronomy and astrophysics. It provides a pathway into the Bachelor of Science. Graduates work in scientific and technical support roles or continue to a bachelor degree.

name: Bachelor of Accounting
description: The Bachelor of Accounting at Swinburne University of Technology is an accredited three-year full-time degree with a choice of two majors, accounting or accounting and financial planning, and guaranteed work-integrated learning. Students develop technical accounting skills alongside an understanding of how finance affects businesses and people. Graduates work as accountants and financial professionals and are on a pathway to professional accreditation. Indicative international tuition is around 46,700 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 088381K.

name: Bachelor of Accounting and Business Information Technology (Professional)
Bachelor of Animation
description: The Bachelor of Animation at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree that develops advanced skills in producing 2D, 3D and stop-motion animation for film, television, visual effects and games. Students access a purpose-built animation studio, interactive pen displays, high-end cameras and render farms. Graduates work as animators and visual effects artists across screen and games. Indicative international tuition is around 47,400 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 092511D.

name: Bachelor of Applied Innovation
description: The Bachelor of Applied Innovation at Swinburne University of Technology is offered as the second degree in a combined program alongside a discipline degree such as engineering, design, business, science or computer science. Students build innovative thinking to complement their main field, learning through multidisciplinary innovation labs, hackathons, industry projects and innovation sprints. Graduates enter their chosen profession with an added innovation and entrepreneurship edge. Indicative international tuition is around 53,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 108362K.

name: Bachelor of Artificial Intelligence
description: The Bachelor of Artificial Intelligence at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree teaching future-focused skills in AI solution design and implementation, machine learning and statistical modelling. Students combine computer science and mathematics with specialised training in machine learning and natural language processing, learning through industry-engaged, project-based coursework with an emphasis on ethical AI use. Graduates design and deploy intelligent systems across industries. Indicative international tuition is around 44,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 121174E.

name: Bachelor of Artificial Intelligence in Business
description: The Bachelor of Artificial Intelligence in Business at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree, described by the university as Australia's first business AI degree of its kind. Through project-based industry learning, students gain an understanding of business practices alongside proficiency in emerging AI technology, graduating ready to tailor AI-driven solutions to business problems. Graduates work in AI strategy, analytics and business innovation roles. Indicative international tuition is around 43,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 118260M.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description: The Bachelor of Arts at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree that develops critical thinking and communication skills across majors including criminology, cyber and society, environment and sustainability, and media and communication. Students explore the social impacts of contemporary issues and shape a meaningful career direction. Graduates work across community, media, policy, research and business roles. Indicative international tuition is around 37,800 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 088388C.

name: Bachelor of Aviation
description:
Students in this degree start flying in week three, not after a year of ground school. Swinburne's flight training partner CAE Melbourne Flight Training operates out of Moorabbin Airport, one of the busiest general aviation airports in the country, giving students frequent, high-volume flight hours on a large modern fleet plus simulators rather than sporadic, weather-dependent bookings at a smaller school. The commercial flying component is built to Air Transport Pilot Licence (ATPL) theory standard as set by the Civil Aviation Safety Authority, and students exit holding a Commercial Pilot Licence with multi-crew jet aircraft operating experience.

The degree isn't just flight training wrapped in a university label: a genuine piloting major sits alongside ten aviation core units and six units of minor/elective study, covering aviation human factors, aviation management and aviation technology, so graduates come out understanding the operational and regulatory side of the industry, not just stick-and-rudder skills.
