Given how capital-intensive flight training is, the structure of paying for a fixed number of core aviation units plus a piloting major (rather than open-ended hour-building) gives students a clearer cost and time expectation than pursuing a CPL independently through a standalone flight school.
curriculum:
10 aviation core units (125 credit points): aviation human factors, aviation management, aviation technology, aviation law and regulation, meteorology, navigation
Piloting major (8 units, 100 credit points): flight training through CAE Melbourne Flight Training at Moorabbin Airport, theory to ATPL (CASA) standard, culminating in a Commercial Pilot Licence
6 units (75 credit points) of minor and/or elective study
Flight training begins from week three of the course
Total: 300 credit points across three years
admission_requirements: ATAR ~65+ (or equivalent Year 12), plus medical fitness (CASA Class 1) for flight-training stream
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Aviation and Piloting
description: The Bachelor of Aviation and Piloting at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree that packages commercial piloting qualifications with study of aviation human factors, management and technology. Flight training takes place at CAE Melbourne Flight Training at Moorabbin, with students flying from week three. Graduates progress toward commercial and airline pilot careers. Indicative international tuition is around 83,400 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 093354D.

name: Bachelor of Aviation Management
description: The Bachelor of Aviation Management at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree for non-piloting careers in the aviation industry, with majors in aviation operations or uncrewed aircraft systems and guaranteed industry projects. The uncrewed aircraft systems major includes a remote pilot licence and skills in UAV design, navigation and data analysis. Graduates work in airline and airport operations, aviation regulation and uncrewed aircraft roles. Indicative international tuition is around 47,500 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 093355C.

name: Bachelor of Biomedical Science
description: The Bachelor of Biomedical Science at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree that builds skills in human health, disease, digital anatomy, medical science and industry-based research. Students learn using technology and facilities including virtual reality and digital dissection, with industry placement opportunities. Graduates work in medical research, laboratories, health and biotechnology, or continue to graduate-entry health programs. Indicative international tuition is around 43,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 116519E.

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
Swinburne's Bachelor of Business gives students a wide bench of majors (Business Administration, Business Analytics and Analysis, Entrepreneurship, Finance, Human Resource Management, Logistics and Supply Chain Management, Management, Marketing, Sports Management, plus a heavier Accounting major and an even heavier Accounting and Finance double major), and then leaves a genuinely large chunk of the degree, up to eight units, open for a second major, co-major, minor or straight electives. That flexibility means two Bachelor of Business graduates from the same cohort can leave with quite different profiles: one stacking marketing with a psychology minor, another pairing accounting with a data analytics co-major.

A Professional variant of the degree exists for students who want a placement built into the structure rather than left as an optional add-on, mirroring the model Swinburne uses across its engineering and IT degrees. Industry-integrated learning is something of a house style here rather than a one-off feature bolted onto a single program.

The Sports Management major stands out as a less common offering compared to typical Australian business degrees, useful given Melbourne's concentration of major sporting codes, venues and sports-industry employers.
curriculum:
Major (choose one): Accounting (9 units) / Accounting and Finance (16 units) / Business Administration / Business Analytics and Analysis / Entrepreneurship / Finance / Human Resource Management / Logistics and Supply Chain Management / Management / Marketing / Sports Management (8 units each unless noted)
Up to 8 units of further study: second major, co-major, advanced minor, minor(s), or electives
Professional stream available with an integrated industry placement co-major
Capstone unit integrated into the chosen major's final units
Total: 300 credit points across four years (300 credit points, standard full-time load 8 units/year)
admission_requirements: ATAR ~60+ (or equivalent Year 12); no prerequisite subjects
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Business (Professional) - Accounting and Financial Planning
description: The Bachelor of Business (Professional) at Swinburne University of Technology is a four-year full-time degree, offered here with an accounting and financial planning focus, that includes a 12-month paid work placement. Students develop core business capability across operations, organisational behaviour and workplace relations alongside specialist study, combining business innovation with social impact. Graduates enter accounting, financial planning and business roles with a year of professional experience. Indicative international tuition is around 35,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 095883G.

name: Bachelor of Business Analytics
description: The Bachelor of Business Analytics at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree that teaches students to harness data and understand the AI and technology transforming industries. Students learn to interpret both business and technical languages, identify operational challenges and use data to predict opportunities and create solutions, with study in cybersecurity, law and ethics. Graduates work as business and data analysts. Indicative international tuition is around 46,700 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 118264G.

name: Bachelor of Business Analytics and Analysis
description: The Bachelor of Business Analytics and Analysis at Swinburne University of Technology, delivered through the Bachelor of Business Analytics, is a three-year full-time degree that teaches students to solve big data, process and technology challenges, with the option of a six or twelve-month professional placement. Students learn to interpret business and technical languages and use data to create solutions. Graduates work as business and data analysts. Indicative international tuition is around 43,400 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 118264G.

name: Bachelor of Business Information Technology (Professional)
description: The Bachelor of Business Information Technology (Professional) at Swinburne University of Technology, delivered through the Bachelor of Information and Communication Technology (Professional), is a four-year full-time degree teaching network configuration, web and app programming and database design, with a guaranteed 12-month paid work placement. Graduates work in software, systems and IT roles with a year of professional experience. Indicative international tuition is around 45,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 095881J.

name: Bachelor of Computer Science
description: The Bachelor of Computer Science at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree that combines software development and machine learning application with a specialist major such as cyber security, data science or software development. It includes six industry projects. Graduates work as software developers, machine learning engineers and computing specialists. Indicative international tuition is around 33,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 088400A.

name: Bachelor of Construction Management
description: The Bachelor of Construction Management at Swinburne University of Technology, offered as the Bachelor of Construction Management (Honours), is a three to four-year degree teaching people, process and resource management for construction projects with guaranteed industry projects. It focuses on digital technologies such as Building Information Modelling, extended reality and AI, from residential developments to large-scale infrastructure. Graduates work as construction and project managers. Indicative international tuition is around 43,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 118324M.

name: Bachelor of Criminal Justice and Criminology
description: The Bachelor of Criminal Justice and Criminology at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree that develops the skills and understanding to work within the criminal justice system. It covers local and global criminality, traditional and emerging responses to crime, the international dimensions of criminal justice, and the technological advances affecting the sector. Graduates work in policing, corrections, courts, policy and community services. Indicative international tuition is around 38,400 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 098002K.

name: Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice
description: The Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree examining how crime is predicted, prevented, investigated and addressed in a rapidly evolving digital world. Drawing on criminology, law and forensic psychology, students explore the causes of crime, criminal behaviour, the justice system and the impact of emerging technologies. Graduates work in policing, corrections, policy, research and community services. Indicative international tuition is around 36,900 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 121201G.

name: Bachelor of Cyber Security
description: The Bachelor of Cyber Security at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree that teaches students to protect networks, prevent cybercrime and defend online data. Study covers encryption systems, access control, network architecture and the fundamentals of cyber defence. Graduates work as security analysts, engineers and consultants across defence, media, health and other industries. Indicative international tuition is around 46,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 109148H.

name: Bachelor of Data Science
description: The Bachelor of Data Science at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree that builds big data management and visualisation skills, with industry experience through projects and work placements. Students learn the tools used to manage big data sets and how data is used to solve and anticipate problems. Graduates work in data-driven decision making, forecasting and analytics roles across business. Indicative international tuition is around 46,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 109149G.

name: Bachelor of Design (Industrial Design)
description:
Industrial Design at Swinburne runs on a studio model where the coursework builds toward two named capstone units, Capstone: Industrial Design Major Project 1 and 2, rather than a single undifferentiated final-year project, giving students a full year to develop, refine and present one substantial body of design work instead of squeezing it into one semester. Studio units like the Socially Responsible Design Studio push students toward designing for real constraints (accessibility, sustainability, manufacturing limitations) rather than purely conceptual or aesthetic exercises.

Fourth-year students choose between elective streams, one of which routes through Design Factory Melbourne, Swinburne's industry-facing innovation space that runs live projects with external companies, giving students who take that path a materially different final year than classmates who stay in a more traditional industrial design studio track.

The curriculum deliberately layers business studies, materials and manufacturing technology, and design psychology on top of the studio work, reflecting an assumption that a working industrial designer needs to understand cost, consumer behaviour and production constraints as much as form.
curriculum:
Early studio units: design fundamentals, sketching and visualisation, materials and manufacturing processes, design history and theory
Mid-course studio units: Socially Responsible Design Studio, human-centred design, design psychology and consumer research, business studies for designers
Fourth-year elective stream (choose one): Industrial Design specialisation OR Design Factory Melbourne Projects stream
Capstone: Industrial Design Major Project 1 (DID40001) and Major Project 2 (DID40002)
Total: 400 credit points across four years
admission_requirements: ATAR plus folio/selection task submission
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Digital Construction Management
description: The Bachelor of Digital Construction Management at Swinburne University of Technology, delivered through the Bachelor of Construction Management (Honours), is a three-year full-time degree focused on managing construction projects from concept to completion using digital technologies such as Building Information Modelling, extended reality and AI. Students gain guaranteed industry projects and skills in managing people, processes and resources. Graduates work as digital construction and project managers. Indicative international tuition is around 43,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 118324M.

name: Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description: The Bachelor of Education (Primary) at Swinburne University of Technology is a four-year full-time initial teacher education degree in which students learn modern teaching methods and gain practical experience through school placements. Learning is built around genuine teaching challenges and professional practice, taught by registered, practising teachers. Graduates are prepared for registration and work as primary school teachers. Indicative international tuition is around 36,300 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Education Studies
description: The Bachelor of Education Studies at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree that prepares graduates for careers in government education policy and in corporate and non-profit training, with guaranteed industry-based experience. Students learn to plan and implement effective teaching and learning in diverse contexts and tailor electives to a range of education environments. Graduates work in education policy, training and learning design roles. Indicative international tuition is around 39,800 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
Swinburne runs two versions of this degree side by side: the standard Bachelor of Engineering (Honours), where a Professional Placement is optional (a 6- or 12-month placement can exempt students from the standalone Professional Experience in Engineering unit), and the Professional variant, which builds a paid 12-month industry placement directly into the course structure as a compulsory co-major worth 100 credit points. That's an unusually large chunk of the degree carved out for placement rather than coursework, and it reflects Swinburne's long-standing industry-integrated learning model, which predates most Australian universities' recent push toward more work-integrated learning.

Students choose an engineering discipline major (the university's strengths run toward mechanical, electrical, aerospace and robotics/mechatronics given Swinburne's Hawthorn campus facilities and manufacturing partnerships in Melbourne's east), and Engineers Australia accreditation means placement components are assessed specifically against the competencies that body requires for professional registration, not just generic employability skills.

Graduates of the Professional stream leave with a full year of documented, assessed industry experience already on their CV, which functions as a meaningful head start over graduates whose only industry exposure was a short vacation placement.
curriculum:
Engineering core units (10-11 units): mathematics, mechanics, thermodynamics, materials, electrical fundamentals, engineering design and professional practice
Engineering discipline major (17 units): discipline-specific technical units building toward the chosen specialisation
Professional Placement Co-Major (4 units, Professional stream only): includes a 12-month paid industry placement, assessed against Engineers Australia competency standards
Elective units (2-3 units)
Final Year Capstone Project (1 and 2)
Total: 475 credit points (Professional stream); standard stream substitutes optional Professional Placement for the co-major
admission_requirements: ATAR ~70+ with Units 3/4 Maths Methods recommended
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Engineering Technology
description: The Bachelor of Engineering Technology at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree that teaches broad engineering skills to work as a para-professional engineer, including six industry projects. Students study core concepts of mechanics, kinematics, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics and energy through industry-based projects and workshops, across mechanical, electronics and software engineering. Graduates work as engineering technologists. Indicative international tuition is around 48,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 116130D.

name: Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science
description: The Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree that develops the skills to manage and improve the health, fitness and performance of individuals and teams through training, coaching and advice. Students learn to work in an increasingly digitised industry with access to laboratories and technology including wearable sensors. Graduates work in exercise science, strength and conditioning, and sport performance roles. Indicative international tuition is around 45,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 097922M.

name: Bachelor of Film and Television (Honours)
description:
The defining feature of this degree is its two-part final capstone: Major Project: Production, followed by Major Project: Post-Production and Distribution, both built in consultation with industry partners rather than assessed purely as a student exercise. Splitting the capstone across production and post/distribution phases mirrors how an actual film project moves through a professional pipeline, and it means graduating students leave with a finished, distributable piece of work rather than just raw footage.

Swinburne's film program draws on Melbourne's screen industry base, and the honours structure (an extra fourth year layered onto what would otherwise be a three-year degree) gives students more time inside that production pipeline than a standard bachelor's would allow, plus a research component that pushes toward critical and theoretical engagement with the medium alongside the practical filmmaking.

Students typically specialise informally across the degree (directing, cinematography, editing, sound, producing) while still working across every stage of the pipeline in group productions, which is standard practice for film schools that want graduates who understand the whole set rather than just their own department.
curriculum:
Foundation units: screenwriting, cinematography, sound design, editing, film and television history and theory
Mid-course production units: documentary practice, narrative fiction production, television production, producing and budgeting
Honours research component: critical and theoretical study of screen media, integrated across the fourth year
Capstone: Major Project: Production (FTV40010) followed by Major Project: Post-Production and Distribution (FTV40011), developed in consultation with industry partners
Total: 400 credit points across four years
admission_requirements: ATAR plus folio/selection task submission and interview
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Forensic Psychological Science
description: The Bachelor of Forensic Psychological Science at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree, described by the university as Australia's first undergraduate forensic psychology degree. Grounded in developmental psychology, neuroscience and mental health, students learn about the intersection of psychology and the law. Graduates work in corrections, youth justice and related settings, and can continue to postgraduate psychology study. Indicative international tuition is around 43,900 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 119097J.

name: Bachelor of Games and Interactivity (Professional)
description: The Bachelor of Games and Interactivity (Professional) at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-and-a-half-year full-time degree combining game design, creative research and media studies, with a professional placement. Students examine the role of games in society and undertake projects focused on analog and digital games in a games lab environment. Graduates work in game design, production and the wider interactive media industry. Indicative international tuition is around 40,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 088399M.

name: Bachelor of Health Science
description: The Bachelor of Health Science at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree that provides work-integrated training for a career in the health industry, with a choice of seven majors including digital health, biomedical science and others. Students learn using interactive technology to understand the body across health and disease states. Graduates work in health services, health promotion and allied health support roles. Indicative international tuition is around 43,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 077669G.

name: Bachelor of Information and Communication Technology
description: The Bachelor of Information and Communication Technology at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree teaching network configuration, web and app programming and database design, with six industry projects. Students gain expertise in advanced web development, data visualisation, business systems design and requirements analysis, and work on real projects through work-integrated learning. Graduates work as software developers, systems analysts and ICT infrastructure specialists. The course holds CRICOS registration 088401M.

name: Bachelor of Innovation and Design
description: The Bachelor of Innovation and Design at Swinburne University of Technology, offered as the combined Bachelor of Design and Bachelor of Applied Innovation, is a three-year full-time double degree for designers who want an innovation edge. Students learn in multidisciplinary innovation labs through hackathons, industry projects and innovation sprints, creating work across typography, digital media, brand and identity design and spatial experiences. Graduates work as designers and design innovators. Indicative international tuition is around 34,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 108353M.

name: Bachelor of Laws
description: The Bachelor of Laws at Swinburne University of Technology is a full-time degree, described by the university as the only law degree in Victoria with a focus on commercial law emphasising intellectual property law and legal technology. Students study trademarks, patents, designs, copyright and competition law, develop skills in legal technology, and complete 60 days of law-related professional experience placements. Graduates progress toward admission to practise. Indicative international tuition is around 46,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 119074E.

name: Bachelor of Laws Graduate Entry
description: The Bachelor of Laws Graduate Entry at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time pathway of the Bachelor of Laws for students who have completed prior tertiary study. The degree focuses on commercial law with an emphasis on intellectual property and legal technology, and includes study of trademarks, patents, copyright and competition law plus 60 days of professional experience placements. Graduates progress toward admission to practise. Indicative international tuition is around 45,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 119074E.

name: Bachelor of Laws Standard Entry
description: The Bachelor of Laws Standard Entry at Swinburne University of Technology is a four-year full-time degree, described by the university as the only law degree in Victoria with a focus on commercial law emphasising intellectual property law and legal technology. Students study trademarks, patents, designs, copyright and competition law, and complete 60 days of law-related professional experience placements. Graduates progress toward admission to practise. Indicative international tuition is around 46,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 119074E.

name: Bachelor of Media and Communication
description: The Bachelor of Media and Communication at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree offering seven majors, giving students real-world skills in current communication technologies and media industry practice across advertising, film and television, and popular culture. Students benefit from industry links with leading screen and media organisations. Graduates work in media production, communications, advertising and content roles. Indicative international tuition is around 42,500 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 088390J.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Swinburne's nursing students train first in dedicated clinical learning laboratories capped at a 12-to-1 student-academic ratio before they're sent into real placements. It's a deliberately small simulation group size that gives students more individual correction time on technique before it matters with an actual patient. From there, students accumulate over 800 hours of supervised Professional Experience Placement across hospitals, community health, aged care and mental health settings, the threshold required to register as a nurse.

Specialty study areas built into the degree include high acuity nursing, mental health, aged and palliative care, rural and Indigenous health care, and family/paediatric and primary health care, a broader specialty spread than some competing nursing degrees that concentrate mainly on acute hospital care. The rural and Indigenous health content in particular signals an intent to prepare graduates for placements and eventual practice outside metropolitan Melbourne, not just within it.

The degree sits alongside Swinburne's TAFE-level Diploma of Nursing, giving the university an internal pathway for enrolled nurses wanting to upgrade to registered nurse qualifications.
curriculum:
Foundation units: anatomy and physiology, health assessment, foundations of nursing practice, pharmacology
Specialty study units: high acuity nursing, mental health nursing, aged and palliative care, rural and Indigenous health care, family, paediatric and primary health care
Clinical learning laboratory simulation training (capped at 12 students per group) preceding placement blocks
Over 800 hours of supervised Professional Experience Placement across hospital, community, aged care and mental health settings
Total: 300 credit points across three years
admission_requirements: ATAR ~60+ (or equivalent Year 12), plus health/immunisation and police checks
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0 (nursing registration requirement)

name: Bachelor of Nutrition
description: The Bachelor of Nutrition at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree in which students study progressive food trends, sustainable nutrition and food's impact on health and wellbeing in a lab-based environment. It offers hands-on learning in laboratory spaces with clear pathways to postgraduate study. Graduates work in community and public health nutrition, food industry and health promotion roles. Indicative international tuition is around 43,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 116518F.

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours)
description:
This is Swinburne's APAC-accredited fourth year, the honours qualification students need after an accredited three-year psychology degree if they want to move on to provisional registration and postgraduate training in clinical, organisational or sports psychology, or into psychology research more broadly. Entry is genuinely competitive rather than automatic: Swinburne requires a Distinction average (70%) across third-year core psychology units and at least credit-level results across second and third-year core and major units, with only one unit exception allowed, a real filter rather than a formality.

At 100 credit points it's a single intensive year built around an accredited research thesis alongside advanced coursework, and because the year functions as the gateway into every specialist psychology career path (clinical, forensic, organisational, sport and exercise), Swinburne treats it less as a general capstone and more as a professional screening year.

Graduates who complete it are positioned for the 4+2 or 4+1+1 postgraduate/supervised practice pathways toward psychologist registration with AHPRA, or direct entry into competitive APAC-accredited master's and doctoral programs.
curriculum:
Advanced coursework units: advanced research methods and statistics, psychological assessment, advanced topics across clinical, organisational, developmental and cognitive psychology
Honours research thesis, supervised, conducted across the year
Entry requirement: Distinction average (70%) in third-year core psychology units; credit or higher in second- and third-year core/major units (maximum one exception)
APAC-accredited sequence, required for progression to postgraduate psychology training and eventual AHPRA registration
Total: 100 credit points, one year full-time
admission_requirements: ATAR ~70+ (or equivalent Year 12)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Psychological Sciences (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Psychological Sciences (Honours) at Swinburne University of Technology is a one-year full-time program for students who have completed an accredited Australian psychology undergraduate degree. Students develop advanced research skills and the qualification prepares them for postgraduate study in specialist areas such as clinical, organisational or sports psychology, or for a research career. Graduates continue toward registration as psychologists or into research. Indicative international tuition is around 49,200 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Psychology (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Psychology (Honours) at Swinburne University of Technology is an integrated four-year full-time program accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council, and the first step toward becoming a professional psychologist. Swinburne is ranked among the top universities globally for psychology and highly for graduate employment. Graduates continue to postgraduate study in specialist areas on the path to registration. Indicative international tuition is around 45,600 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 088386E.

name: Bachelor of Psychology and Cognitive Neuroscience
description: The Bachelor of Psychology and Cognitive Neuroscience at Swinburne University of Technology is a three-year full-time degree purpose-built for students interested in the brain-behaviour connection. name: Master of Business Administration
description:
The signature unit in Swinburne's MBA is the Organisational Growth and Innovation Capstone Project, which puts the final assessment squarely on solving a genuine organisational problem rather than sitting a comprehensive exam, a design choice consistent with Swinburne's broader house style of industry-linked capstones across its business, IT and engineering degrees. Students work through core units covering strategic management, finance, marketing and leadership before landing on that project, where prior coursework gets applied against a live business challenge rather than a hypothetical one.

Swinburne's MBA also draws on the university's identity as a technology-focused institution rather than a pure business school: expect more emphasis on digital transformation and data-driven decision making than at MBAs housed in universities without Swinburne's engineering and computing base.

The degree suits mid-career professionals looking to move into general management or executive roles, and the capstone project format gives students a tangible deliverable they can discuss directly in job interviews or promotion conversations, rather than an abstract description of "an MBA project."
curriculum:
Core units: Strategic Management, Managerial Finance and Accounting, Marketing Management, Leadership and Organisational Behaviour, Business Analytics for Decision Making, Economics for Managers, Digital Transformation and Innovation
Elective units in an area of specialisation (subject to availability)
Capstone: Organisational Growth and Innovation Capstone Project (BUS60017), applying prior coursework to a live organisational challenge
Delivered across trimesters/semesters depending on study mode; total credit points and duration vary with prior credit granted
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree plus at least 2 years professional work experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Data Science
description:
Swinburne's Master of Data Science makes the industry-based capstone mandatory rather than optional: every student works with an external client on a real business problem before graduating, not just those who opt into an industry track. High-performing students (Credit average or better) can go further and apply for the internship unit (ICT80004), which places them directly inside a company for the duration rather than working client problems from campus.

The course is structured with a graduate-certificate exit point after 8 core units, so students who need to stop partway (a job offer, a visa change, a change of plans) leave with a genuine, transcript-backed credential rather than nothing. That's a more forgiving structure than degrees where the only recognised outcome is the full masters.

Given Swinburne's engineering and computing strengths, the data science degree tends to lean toward applied, production-oriented data science, building and deploying models for real organisational use, over a purely theoretical statistics-heavy curriculum, which suits students aiming at industry data science and machine learning engineering roles rather than academic research.
curriculum:
8 core units (graduate certificate exit point): programming for data science, statistical modelling, machine learning, big data systems, data visualisation, data ethics and governance
Additional core and elective units toward the full masters (2 further core units plus 1 elective, subject to specific course version)
Optional: Internship Project (ICT80004) for students with a Credit average or higher
Capstone: mandatory Industry Capstone Project, delivered for an external client organisation
Total award requirements vary by entry pathway and credit granted; typical full-time load is 8 units/year
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a quantitative or IT-related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

Students specialise in an engineering area such as network systems and telecommunications. Graduates work in specialist engineering and research roles. Indicative international tuition is around 35,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 097335G.

name: Master of Finance
description: The Master of Finance at Swinburne University of Technology is a two-year full-time degree that deepens understanding of financial markets, investment strategies and risk management, alongside leadership and management capability. Graduates work in financial analysis, investment, corporate finance and advisory roles across banking, funds management and corporate treasury. Indicative international tuition is around 50,400 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 102233A.

name: Master of Finance and Banking (Global Leadership Program)
description: The Master of Finance and Banking (Global Leadership Program) at Swinburne University of Technology is delivered through the Master of Finance, a two-year full-time degree that deepens understanding of financial markets, investment strategies and risk management, with an added global leadership focus. Graduates work in banking, financial analysis, investment and advisory roles internationally. Indicative international tuition is around 40,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 102233A.

name: Master of Health Sciences (Research)
description: The Master of Health Sciences (Research) at Swinburne University of Technology is a two-year full-time research degree focused on advanced health sciences research. It fosters independent research skills and is ideal preparation for PhD study or a research career. Graduates continue to doctoral study or work in health research roles. Indicative international tuition is around 47,100 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 082697E.

name: Master of Human Resource Management
description: The Master of Human Resource Management at Swinburne University of Technology is an eighteen-month full-time degree that develops strategic insight to lead in dynamic workplaces, with strong links to industry partners and professional bodies. Students choose specialisations to align the degree with their goals. Graduates work in HR management, business partnering and organisational development roles. Indicative international tuition is around 40,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 102651E.

name: Master of Information and Communication Technologies (Research)
description: The Master of Information and Communication Technologies (Research) at Swinburne University of Technology is a two-year full-time research degree in which students undertake supervised research in an ICT discipline such as cloud computing or data management. It fosters independent research skills and is ideal preparation for PhD study or a research career. Graduates continue to doctoral study or work in ICT research roles. Indicative international tuition is around 47,600 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 082696F.

name: Master of Information Systems Management
description: The Master of Information Systems Management at Swinburne University of Technology is delivered through the Master of Business Information Systems, a two-year full-time degree that develops expertise in leveraging technology for organisational success. Students choose specialisations such as business analytics, working with strong links to industry partners. Graduates work as information systems managers, business analysts and IT consultants. Indicative international tuition is around 27,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 092700K.

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
Swinburne's Master of Information Technology closes with a capstone that puts students in front of an actual external client rather than a simulated case study. Teams spend their final semester delivering a working solution to a real organisation's problem, which is a heavier industry-facing finish than the research-essay capstone many IT master's degrees default to. Students who keep a Credit average across the degree can additionally apply for a 12-week professional internship that counts toward the qualification itself, rather than sitting outside it as an optional add-on.

At 200 credit points across roughly two years of full-time study, the degree gives students room to specialise (an Information Systems stream is one of the named pathways) while still anchoring everyone in a shared core. Swinburne's Hawthorn campus sits inside Melbourne's tech and startup corridor, and the capstone client pool tends to draw on that local industry base rather than generic case studies licensed from a textbook publisher.

For career changers without an IT background, the degree is commonly taken as a genuine retraining pathway into software, data or systems roles, with the capstone project doubling as the first real Australian industry reference a graduate can put on a resume.
curriculum:
Core units across data structures and algorithms, systems analysis and design, database systems, IT project management, cloud computing and enterprise architecture
Specialisation stream (e.g. Information Systems) or elective units depending on prior background
Optional: 12-week Professional Masters Internship (available to students maintaining a Credit average), credited toward the degree
Final semester: Capstone Project, delivered for an external industry client or business
14 units (200 credit points) total; typical full-time load is 8 units/100 credit points per year
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline) or higher, or Graduate Certificate/Diploma of Information Technology; Postgraduate Qualifying Program available for international applicants who don't meet direct entry.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (Swinburne standard for MIT and other general postgraduate degrees).

name: Master of Information Technology Project Management
description: The Master of Information Technology Project Management at Swinburne University of Technology is delivered through the Master of Information Technology, a two-year full-time degree teaching advanced skills and theory in the design, construction, operation and maintenance of IT solutions, with an added project management focus. Students can also specialise in areas such as data analytics or information systems. Graduates work as IT project managers and technology leads. Indicative international tuition is around 27,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 001742J.

name: Master of Law (Research)
description: The Master of Law (Research) at Swinburne University of Technology is a two-year full-time research degree in which students undertake supervised research in a legal discipline of their choice. Candidates develop independent thinking, project management, data analysis, critical thinking and communication skills, and the degree is ideal preparation for PhD study or a research career. Graduates work in legal research, policy and academia. Indicative international tuition is around 42,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 096402K.

name: Master of Marketing - Advanced
description: The Master of Marketing - Advanced at Swinburne University of Technology, delivered through the Master of Marketing, prepares students for marketing leadership with a choice of specialisations, work on live projects with real clients, and a fast-track study option. The advanced pathway adds further study depth. Graduates work in marketing management, brand and digital strategy roles. Indicative international tuition is around 39,500 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 102652D.

name: Master of Marketing (Global Leadership Program)
description: The Master of Marketing (Global Leadership Program) at Swinburne University of Technology, delivered through the Master of Marketing, prepares students for marketing leadership with a choice of specialisations and work on live projects with real clients, with an added global leadership focus. Graduates work in marketing management, brand and digital strategy roles internationally. Indicative international tuition is around 40,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 102652D.

name: Master of Media and Communication
description: The Master of Media and Communication at Swinburne University of Technology is a two-year full-time degree that develops expertise in digital media, journalism and strategic communication. Students choose specialisations such as strategic communication or social media, learning to manage communications plans, handle public relations and drive audience engagement. Graduates work in communications, content, public relations and digital media roles. Indicative international tuition is around 39,500 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 093362D.

name: Master of Occupational Therapy
description: The Master of Occupational Therapy at Swinburne University of Technology is a two-year full-time degree that prepares students to work with clients who have neurological, musculoskeletal or mental health conditions. The program combines coursework with supervised clinical placements. Graduates are prepared for professional recognition and work as occupational therapists across health, disability and community settings. Indicative international tuition is around 49,900 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 089748J.

name: Master of Physiotherapy
description: The Master of Physiotherapy at Swinburne University of Technology is a two-year full-time degree that provides the digital health, technology, business and leadership skills to practise as a confident and innovative physiotherapist. The program combines coursework with supervised clinical placements. Graduates are prepared for registration and work as physiotherapists across clinical settings. Indicative international tuition is around 57,700 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 098499B.

name: Master of Practising Accounting
description: The Master of Practising Accounting at Swinburne University of Technology is delivered through the Master of Professional Accounting, which provides specialised skills for senior accounting roles, a FinTech specialisation, an intensive fast-track option, and a partnership with Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand. Graduates work in accounting, advisory and finance roles. Indicative international tuition is around 36,500 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 116706B.

name: Master of Professional Accounting (Graduate Entry)
description: The Master of Professional Accounting (Graduate Entry) at Swinburne University of Technology is an eighteen-month pathway of the Master of Professional Accounting, which provides specialised skills for senior accounting roles, a FinTech specialisation and a partnership with Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand. Graduates work in accounting, advisory and finance roles. Indicative international tuition is around 44,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 116706B.

name: Master of Professional Engineering
description: The Master of Professional Engineering at Swinburne University of Technology is a two-year full-time degree that strengthens management and communication skills in engineering while students undertake industry-related research and project work in a chosen specialisation. It is designed for graduates seeking an accredited professional engineering qualification. Graduates work in professional engineering practice. Indicative international tuition is around 53,500 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 085866B.

name: Master of Project Management
description: The Master of Project Management at Swinburne University of Technology is an eighteen-month full-time degree that develops advanced skills and knowledge to lead projects effectively, with strong links to industry partners and professional bodies and a choice of specialisations. Graduates work as project and program managers across sectors. Indicative international tuition is around 38,700 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 102653C.

name: Master of Research
description: The Master of Research at Swinburne University of Technology is a two-year full-time research degree in which students undertake supervised research in a discipline of their choice across the humanities, arts, social sciences and other fields. It fosters independent research skills and is ideal preparation for PhD study or a research career. Graduates continue to doctoral study or work in research roles. Indicative international tuition is around 42,400 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 046751C.

name: Master of Science (Research)
description: The Master of Science (Research) at Swinburne University of Technology is a two-year full-time research degree in which students advance their scientific knowledge and research skills through supervised research on real-world challenges. It fosters independent research capability and is ideal preparation for PhD study or a research career. Graduates continue to doctoral study or work in scientific research roles. Indicative international tuition is around 47,100 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 008343A.

name: Master of Science in Biotechnology
description: The Master of Science in Biotechnology at Swinburne University of Technology, offered as the Master of Science (Biotechnology), is a two-year full-time degree covering the fundamental principles of biotechnology. Graduates pursue careers in medical, industrial, forensic, agricultural, pharmaceutical and environmental biotechnology, and in research. Indicative international tuition is around 48,900 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 055216G.

name: Master of Social Impact
description: The Master of Social Impact at Swinburne University of Technology is an eighteen-month program, delivered through the university's social impact postgraduate suite, for professionals seeking advancement in philanthropy, not-for-profit, social enterprise and social innovation. Students learn to lead people effectively in a changing social economy and develop innovative responses to complex social and business problems. Graduates work in social enterprise, purpose-driven business and community leadership roles. Indicative international tuition is around 50,400 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 095160J.

name: Master of Social Investment and Philanthropy
Master of Supply Chain Innovation
description: The Master of Supply Chain Innovation at Swinburne University of Technology is an eighteen-month full-time degree that prepares students to drive business change by designing innovative supply chains. Study combines design thinking, analytics and lean management with strong links to industry partners and professional bodies. Graduates work in procurement, logistics, operations and supply chain strategy roles. Indicative international tuition is around 40,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 102654B.

name: Master of Teaching (Secondary)
description: The Master of Teaching (Secondary) at Swinburne University of Technology is a two-year full-time initial teacher education degree with hybrid study and the opportunity to complete a paid internship in partnership with the Victorian Department of Education. Course content, produced with industry partners, focuses on classroom management, learning and responsive teaching. Graduates are prepared for registration and work as secondary school teachers. Indicative international tuition is around 39,000 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Urban Design
description: The Master of Urban Design at Swinburne University of Technology is delivered through the Master of Architecture and Urban Design, a two-year full-time degree in which students learn to create urban designs that help modern cities thrive, studying principles of modelling, theory and research. Graduates work in urban design, planning and architecture practice. Indicative international tuition is around 43,900 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 098496E.

name: Advanced Diploma of Civil Construction Design
Associate Degree of 3D Art and Animation
Bachelor of 3D Art and Animation
description:
TAFE NSW frames this degree explicitly around commercial production pipelines rather than pure fine-arts animation theory. Students work in deadline-driven environments meant to mimic actual studio conditions in feature film, games, television, advertising and visualisation work, and graduate with a bachelor's degree plus a showreel built for client and employer review rather than just an academic portfolio. That production-pipeline framing runs through the whole course: students don't just learn individual 3D and animation skills in isolation, they practice working with others across a production pipeline to deliver a finished result against a brief, the way an actual studio team would.

Run out of Design Centre Enmore, one of TAFE NSW's specialist creative campuses, the degree blends theoretical grounding in art and animation principles with the technical software skills the games and VFX industries actually use day to day.

Graduates aim at roles across feature filmmaking, game production, television and online content, and advertising and visualisation, a broader placement than a games-only or film-only animation degree, useful for students who aren't yet sure which specific corner of the visual effects and animation industry they want to land in.
curriculum:
Core subjects: animation principles, 3D modelling and texturing, rigging and character animation, visual effects and compositing, lighting and rendering, art and design theory
Production-pipeline studio projects simulating deadline-driven commercial briefs
21 core subjects, 3 elective subjects (24 total, 240 credit points)
Final-year capstone: client-brief production project, delivered as part of a team, contributing to a graduate showreel
Delivered at Design Centre Enmore; total three-year bachelor's degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant Diploma pathway, portfolio may be requested
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

name: Bachelor of Applied Commerce
description:
TAFE NSW's Bachelor of Applied Commerce carries triple professional-body accreditation: CPA Australia, Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand (CAANZ), and the Financial Advice Association Australia (FAAA). That's a heavier accreditation load than most standalone accounting or financial planning degrees carry individually, since it's built to satisfy the education requirements of both the accounting and financial planning professions at once. Students choose a major in accounting or financial planning, or take a double major covering both, a genuinely unusual combination given how differently those two professions are regulated and how rarely degrees try to service both simultaneously.

A third-year industry placement is built into the structure, developed in consultation with industry so the practical component reflects what employers in accounting and financial services firms are actually looking for rather than a generic business internship.

Coursework runs beyond pure numbers into client psychology and communication, reflecting how much of financial planning practice in particular depends on advising real people through decisions rather than just producing correct calculations.
curriculum:
Core units: accounting principles, financial planning fundamentals, marketing, client psychology and communication, management, economics, business law, taxation
Major (choose one or both): Accounting / Financial Planning
Third-year industry placement, developed in consultation with accounting and financial services employers
Accreditation alignment: CPA Australia, CAANZ, and FAAA education requirements built into course design
Total: three-year bachelor's degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant VET Diploma/Advanced Diploma pathway
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
TAFE NSW's Bachelor of Business builds toward three named specialisations: marketing, management, or hospitality and hotel management. The placement requirement is deliberately scaled to match: 60 hours minimum for marketing and management students, but a much heavier 300 hours for the hospitality and hotel management stream, reflecting how much that industry expects hands-on shift experience before graduation. Students commit to a specialisation from second year, choosing four relevant electives in year two and another four in year three that build toward it, rather than declaring a major on day one and locking it in.

Coursework spans management, economics, finance, marketing, communications technologies, business statistics, law and people management, a broad general-business foundation before the specialisation electives narrow things down. Being a TAFE NSW degree rather than a university one, the course leans into applied, workplace-facing content and built-in professional placement as differentiators, consistent with the sector's practical training reputation.

Graduates come out with both a bachelor's qualification and documented, assessed workplace hours in their chosen specialisation, which matters particularly for the hospitality stream where employers routinely want to see real service-floor or front-of-house experience.
curriculum:
Core units: business theory and practice, management principles, economics, finance, marketing fundamentals, communications technologies, business statistics, business law, people management
Year 2: 4 specialisation electives (marketing, management, or hospitality and hotel management)
Year 3: 4 further specialisation electives, building toward the chosen stream
Work placement: minimum 60 hours (marketing/management) or minimum 300 hours (hospitality and hotel management)
Total: three-year bachelor's degree, specialisation confirmed through elective selection rather than a separate application
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (ATAR not required; portfolio/mature-age and VET pathway entry accepted) or a relevant Diploma/Advanced Diploma
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

name: Bachelor of Business (Hospitality and Hotel Management)
description:
This is the hospitality and hotel management specialisation of TAFE NSW's broader Bachelor of Business, and the placement load makes the distinction obvious: 300 hours minimum, five times the 60-hour minimum set for the marketing and management streams of the same base degree. That reflects how hospitality employers hire, since a degree without extensive documented shift and service-floor experience carries a lot less weight in that industry than one that does.

Students share the same core business foundation as other Bachelor of Business students (management, economics, finance, marketing, business law, communications technologies, statistics) before specialising into hospitality and hotel-specific electives from second year onward, so graduates leave with both general business competence and hotel/hospitality-specific operational knowledge rather than one at the expense of the other.

Given TAFE NSW's long history running vocational hospitality training (commercial cookery, hotel operations, tourism) alongside this degree, students in this stream often have access to industry connections and placement employers built up through the organisation's much larger hospitality training footprint, rather than a placement office that's improvising industry contacts from scratch.
curriculum:
Core business units: management principles, economics, finance, marketing fundamentals, business law, communications technologies, business statistics, people management
Year 2 hospitality and hotel management electives: front office and rooms division operations, food and beverage management, event and conference operations
Year 3 hospitality and hotel management electives: revenue management, hotel operations strategy, tourism and hospitality marketing
Work placement: minimum 300 hours in a hospitality or hotel setting
Total: three-year bachelor's degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant VET Diploma/Advanced Diploma pathway
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

name: Bachelor of Creative Practice (Music Production and Performance)
description:
This degree is the top tier of a deliberately staged three-year pathway: a one-year Diploma of Music first, in a student's choice of Sound Production, Performance, or Creation and Composition specialisation, followed by the two-year Bachelor of Creative Practice (Music Production and Performance) itself. That staged structure means students test their specialisation choice at diploma level before committing to the longer bachelor's stage, and it gives TAFE NSW a natural exit point for students who want a shorter, standalone qualification rather than the full degree.

Unlike a conservatorium-style performance degree that concentrates heavily on classical technique and repertoire, this program is built for working across performance, production and composition simultaneously, reflecting how contemporary music careers rarely stay confined to just one of those roles. The Sound Production diploma track, for instance, is explicitly aimed at assistant sound engineer and sound designer roles in the entertainment industry, while Creation and Composition leans toward electronic production, sound design and music distribution.

Students come out with both technical production skills and performance capability, positioned for careers as recording artists, producers, composers or session musicians rather than a single narrow professional track.
curriculum:
Year 1: Diploma of Music, one specialisation chosen — Sound Production, Performance, or Creation and Composition
Years 2-3: Bachelor of Creative Practice (Music Production and Performance) core units — music production techniques, live performance practice, composition and arrangement, music business and industry practice, studio recording and mixing
Elective units aligned to the student's diploma specialisation background
Final-year capstone: original creative project (performance, production, or composition portfolio)
Total: three-year packaged pathway (1-year diploma + 2-year bachelor's)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant Diploma pathway, audition/portfolio may be requested
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

name: Bachelor of Early Childhood Education and Care (Birth-5 years)
description:
This ACECQA-approved degree qualifies graduates as early childhood teachers, not just educators, which puts it in the same regulatory category as equivalent university early childhood teaching degrees despite being delivered by TAFE NSW. The four-year structure carries 805 hours (115 days) of work placement, a substantial practicum load that's woven through the degree rather than concentrated in a single final-year block, giving students repeated, staged exposure to real early learning settings as their coursework deepens.

Curriculum content runs across children's development, language and literacies, STEM, Indigenous education, leadership, inclusive and gifted education, health and wellbeing, and the arts in the early years: a broader spread than a narrower early childhood care qualification, reflecting the birth-to-five age range the degree is built to cover rather than splitting infant/toddler care from preschool teaching into separate credentials.

Because it's delivered through TAFE NSW's applied learning model, students combine contemporary early-childhood research with heavily practice-oriented coursework, which the university positions as a direct pathway into preschool and long day care teaching roles as well as broader children's and family services positions.
curriculum:
Core units across children's development and learning theory, language and literacies, STEM in the early years, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives, inclusive and gifted education, leadership and service management, health, safety and wellbeing, creative arts pedagogy
805 hours (115 days) of supervised work placement, staged progressively across the four years
ACECQA-approved sequence, required for recognition as a qualified early childhood teacher
Final-year capstone integrating leadership and service management with an extended placement block
Total: four-year bachelor's degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care, plus a Working with Children Check
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Fashion Design
description:
Delivered through TAFE NSW's Fashion Design Studio, a name in Australian fashion education dating back to 1955, this three-year degree ends with the sort of milestone most fashion schools treat as the whole point: in third year, students design and present their own collection and graduate holding a portfolio of realised, physical garments rather than just a folio of sketches and coursework grades. Two separate work placements are built into the structure, positioned by the university as much for building professional networks in the industry as for skill development.

The course is taught through what TAFE NSW calls a global fashion business lens, meaning students aren't just learning pattern-making and construction but also studying the industry side: trend forecasting, international market awareness, and the commercial context a design has to survive in once it leaves the studio.

As a TAFE NSW degree rather than a standalone art school program, students get access to the technical machinery and production facilities the vocational fashion program uses, which tends to mean more hands-on garment construction time than programs run purely as academic design theory courses.
curriculum:
Core subjects: pattern making and garment construction, textile and fabric knowledge, design fundamentals, fashion illustration, fashion history and trend analysis, global fashion business and market awareness
21 core subjects and 3 elective subjects (24 total, 240 credit points)
Two industry work placements across the degree
Third-year capstone: design, construct and present an original fashion collection, submitted alongside a portfolio of realised work
Total: three-year bachelor's degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant Diploma of Fashion Design, portfolio may be requested
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

name: Bachelor of Information Technology (Cyber & Network Security)
description:
TAFE NSW's own bachelor's degree in cyber and network security is a genuinely different animal from its VET certificates in the same subject area. This is a 24-subject, 240-credit-point higher education award, assessed and structured as a degree rather than a training package. What sets it apart from an equivalent university IT degree is where it sits inside the organisation: TAFE NSW runs vocational cyber security qualifications right up to diploma level at the same campuses, so students move through Certificate/Diploma pathways into the bachelor's without changing institutions, and staff teaching the degree often come out of hands-on industry security roles rather than purely academic backgrounds.

The curriculum covers network design, administration and security, with a deliberate emphasis on critical analysis of security risk and applying real mitigation policies rather than treating security as a bolt-on topic within a general IT degree. Cybercrime protection and the use of emerging technologies to manage security threats sit at the centre of the coursework, not the periphery.

For students who want practical, industry-facing training with a straight line to network security and cyber operations roles, without the more theoretical computer science load a traditional university IT degree might carry, this is one of the more targeted options available in NSW.
curriculum:
21 core subjects covering network design and administration, security architecture, cybercrime prevention, data protection, risk analysis and threat management
3 elective subjects, chosen according to specialisation interest and campus availability
Progressive practical labs building toward applied network security projects rather than a single end-of-course assessment
Total: 24 subjects, 240 credit points, delivered as a stand-alone bachelor's degree or via Diploma-to-Bachelor packaged pathway
Not all elective subjects run at every TAFE NSW location each semester
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (TAFE NSW's own published bachelor-entry bar)

name: Bachelor of Information Technology (Data Engineering)
description:
This is TAFE NSW's data engineering bachelor's, delivered out of the Meadowbank campus, and it's built specifically around the infrastructure and pipeline side of data work: designing, implementing and managing big data systems, rather than the more analysis-and-modelling focus a typical data science degree takes. Students work across data security, cloud computing on both AWS and Microsoft Azure, and emerging database technologies, with the course explicitly designed around industry certification pathways from Cisco, AWS, Microsoft, Red Hat and CompTIA rather than treating certification as an optional extra.

At 24 subjects and 240 credit points over three years, the structure mirrors TAFE NSW's other IT bachelor's degrees, with 21 core subjects and 3 electives, and the practical partnerships with vendors like Palo Alto, Juniper and Oracle mean students are training on tools those companies actually use in production, not generic teaching environments.

Graduates go on to roles like data engineer, SQL developer, cloud data engineer, big data analyst and data warehouse engineer, a more infrastructure-and-pipeline-focused set of outcomes than the model-building and analytics roles a pure data science degree tends to produce.
curriculum:
21 core subjects: data analysis foundations, machine learning fundamentals, AI engineering, data security, networking and infrastructure, cloud computing (AWS and Microsoft Azure), database design and administration, emerging data technologies
3 elective subjects
Industry certification alignment built into coursework (Cisco CCNA, AWS, CompTIA and related vendor pathways)
Total: 24 subjects, 240 credit points, three-year degree, delivered at Meadowbank campus
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant VET Diploma/Advanced Diploma pathway in IT
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

name: Bachelor of Interior Design
description:
TAFE NSW structures the practical component of this interior design degree in two distinct stages: 70 hours of mandatory work placement earlier in the course, then a compulsory final-year internship in a professional interior design practice that's assessed as its own subject rather than treated as a pass/fail add-on. Students already working in the industry, or those for whom a suitable internship placement can't be found, can substitute one of three alternative electives (sustainability design, total experience design, or lighting interior environments), which is a more flexible arrangement than degrees that make the internship a hard, non-negotiable gate.

Coursework builds from generating original design concepts through to the spatial, structural and material analysis of real interior environments, and the degree deliberately folds in project management and business development skills alongside the creative content, reflecting that most interior designers eventually run or work inside small practices where those business skills matter as much as design talent.

Run through TAFE NSW's Design Centre Enmore, the course emphasises future-focused digital design tools alongside the traditional colour, furniture and fixture specification skills the profession has always required.
curriculum:
Core subjects: design concept generation, spatial and structural analysis, materials and finishes, colour theory and application, furniture and fixture specification, digital design tools and visualisation, project management and business development for designers
70 hours mandatory work placement
Final-year professional internship (compulsory subject) in an interior design practice, or an alternative elective (sustainability design / total experience design / lighting interior environments) where an internship isn't available
Delivered at Design Centre Enmore; total three-year bachelor's degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant Diploma of Interior Design, portfolio may be requested
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

name: Bachelor of Property Valuation
description:
TAFE NSW makes a specific, verifiable claim about this degree: it's the only specialist valuation degree in Australia, rather than valuation being taught as a subset within a broader property or business degree elsewhere. It's accredited by the Australian Property Institute (API) for Associate Membership, and graduates with two years of subsequent professional experience become eligible for Certified Practising Valuer (CPV), Certified Property Practitioner (CPP) or Certified Development Practitioner (CDP) status: the actual professional credentials the valuation industry requires for signing off on formal valuations.

At 24 subjects across residential, commercial and specialist valuation areas, the degree is narrower and more technically concentrated than a general property or real estate degree, training students specifically in the methodology, legal frameworks and market analysis techniques a working valuer applies rather than the broader property development, agency or funds-management content a property degree elsewhere might carry.

Given how tightly this program tracks to a single professional credential, it suits students who already know valuation is the specific career they want, rather than those looking for a general property qualification with several possible career exits.
curriculum:
Core subjects: valuation theory and methodology, residential valuation, commercial and industrial valuation, specialist valuation (rural, plant and machinery), property law, real estate economics, statutory valuation and compensation
21 core subjects, 3 elective subjects (24 total, 240 credit points)
Capstone valuation practice project, applying methodology across mixed property types
Graduates eligible for API Associate Membership; CPV/CPP/CDP eligibility after two years' professional experience
Total: three-year bachelor's degree, the only specialist valuation degree offered in Australia
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant VET Diploma/Advanced Diploma pathway
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

Bachelor of Business
description:
TAFE Queensland's Bachelor of Business runs through the same University of Canberra partnership arrangement that underpins its creative-industries degrees, giving students access to a metropolitan business curriculum without leaving Brisbane's South Bank, Mt Gravatt or Coomera campuses. Class sizes are smaller than at a standard university business school, and a lot of the assessment is built around applied projects with real local businesses rather than case studies written for a textbook.

The core is conventional business fundamentals: accounting, marketing, management, economics and business law, but students choose a major partway through, with options that track Queensland's actual employment mix: management, marketing, human resource management and event/tourism-adjacent majors show up more than a generic finance-only track would. Because the degree sits inside a TAFE campus rather than a university one, students doing a business major alongside, say, a hospitality or IT diploma at the same site can cross-enrol in electives from those areas, which isn't something a standalone university business degree typically allows.

Graduates go into generalist business, management-trainee, marketing coordinator and small-business roles across Queensland, and the degree also functions as a credentialing step for TAFE Queensland students moving up from a business-related diploma.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting Principles, Introduction to Management, Marketing Fundamentals, Business Economics, Business Law, Business Communication
Year 2: Organisational Behaviour, Financial Management, major-specific units begin (Management, Marketing or Human Resource Management stream), Business Analytics, Business Ethics and Sustainability
Year 3: Strategic Management, major capstone units, Applied Business Project (client-based consulting project), electives from cross-campus TAFE Queensland offerings
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Creative Industries (Drama and Performance)
description:
Run out of TAFE Queensland's South Bank campus in partnership with the University of Canberra, this degree trains performers alongside the people who will end up producing, facilitating and managing the work around them. The course explicitly covers the role of arts facilitators, educators, producers and project managers in creating socially engaged performance work, not just acting technique.

It's built to take students at very different starting points: TAFE Queensland describes it as suited to complete beginners as much as emerging or already-working performers who want to formalise their practice, sit alongside performance theory and pick up professional and entrepreneurial skills they may not have needed for community or amateur work. South Bank's location gives the cohort proximity to Brisbane's professional theatre scene, and the course draws on that for industry contact and, per TAFE Queensland's own program materials, an active on-campus theatre community.

It's a three-year, Commonwealth Supported Place degree with entry based on an entrance rank and typical alternate pathway and admission scheme options.
