Graduates move into performance work, but the producer/facilitator strand of the curriculum also opens out into arts administration, community arts and theatre-in-education roles that a pure acting degree wouldn't prepare students for as directly.
curriculum:
Year 1: Performance Foundations, Voice and Movement, Introduction to Devising, Theatre History and Theory, Ensemble Practice
Year 2: Text-Based Performance, Physical Theatre, Performance for Social Change, Arts Facilitation and Community Practice, production placement
Year 3: Directing and Dramaturgy, Producing and Project Management for the Arts, Entrepreneurship for Performing Artists, capstone performance season (devised or directed public production)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); audition/interview may be requested
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Creative Industries (Visual Arts)
description:
Like the Visual Communication Design degree, this is a combined qualification: a TAFE Queensland Diploma of Visual Arts feeds into the University of Canberra's Bachelor of Creative Industries (Visual Arts) award. The structure suits students who aren't certain yet whether they want a strictly technical art practice or a broader creative-industries career, since the diploma phase is studio-heavy and the degree phase opens out into curating, arts administration and public art.

Studio practice spans drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking and increasingly digital and mixed media, with the later degree units pushing students toward professional contexts such as exhibition planning, artist statements, grant writing, and gallery relationships that a purely technical diploma wouldn't cover. Brisbane's South Bank campus sits a short walk from the Queensland Art Gallery and GOMA, and the course leans on that proximity for guest critiques and exhibition opportunities rather than treating it as incidental.

Career outcomes are deliberately broad: gallery and museum work, arts education, arts administration, curating, exhibition and display design and public art commissions all show up as destinations, which reflects the creative-industries framing more than a narrower "fine artist" pathway would.
curriculum:
Diploma phase: Drawing and Visual Language, Painting Studio, Printmaking, Sculpture and 3D Practice, Materials and Processes, diploma exhibition project
Degree phase (University of Canberra): Contemporary Art Theory, Curatorial Practice, Arts Administration and Grant Writing, Exhibition and Display Design, Professional Studio Practice, capstone body of work and public exhibition
Credit pathway: TAFE Queensland diploma credit transfers up to 24 credit points into the bachelor's
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); folio may be requested
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Dental Prosthetics
description:
This AQF Level 7 degree is accredited by the Australian Dental Council and approved by the Dental Board of Australia, and it trains one of the few allied dental professions that can treat patients directly rather than only supporting a dentist. Dental prosthetists issue, maintain and examine dentures, insert and try in prosthetics, take impressions and carry out the technical laboratory work themselves, a scope of practice that's genuinely unusual in dentistry, where most non-dentist roles are lab-only or chairside-assist-only.

Coursework covers not just full and partial dentures but more specialised appliances: sleep apnoea and anti-snoring devices, splints, and immediate dentures fitted the same day as extractions. Training happens in TAFE Queensland's working denture clinic, where students treat real patients under supervision using the same lab equipment they'll use professionally, rather than working exclusively on models.

The entry requirement that gets flagged repeatedly by TAFE Queensland itself is manual dexterity: it's assessed at admission and has to be maintained throughout enrolment, which says something about how hands-on the daily work actually is. Graduates are eligible to register as dental prosthetists with the Dental Board of Australia and can go into private practice, dental laboratories or continue into further postgraduate dental study.
curriculum:
Year 1: Oral Anatomy and Physiology, Dental Materials Science, Introduction to Denture Construction, Infection Control and Clinical Practice, Impression Taking and Casting
Year 2: Complete Denture Prosthetics, Partial Denture Design, Occlusion and Articulation, Clinical Practice I (working denture clinic, supervised patient treatment)
Year 3: Immediate Dentures and Same-Day Prosthetics, Sleep Apnoea and Splint Devices, Removable Prosthodontic Complications, Clinical Practice II, Professional and Regulatory Practice for Dental Prosthetists
Clinical training: supervised patient treatment throughout in TAFE Queensland's on-site working denture clinic and dental laboratory
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent) plus relevant work placement component; accredited by the Australian Dental Council
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Design (Visual Communication Design)
description:
Delivered by TAFE Queensland in partnership with the University of Canberra, this is a dual-award structure: students complete a TAFE Queensland Diploma of Graphic Design en route to the University of Canberra's Bachelor of Digital Design (Visual Communication Design) testamur, which is the actual degree name that appears on the parchment despite the program being commonly listed under the broader title. The arrangement means students get a vocational, portfolio-heavy first phase before the degree work broadens into strategy and theory.

Studio work covers typography, logotype and identity design, publication layout, packaging, environmental graphics and digital design, taught by working designers rather than exclusively by academic staff. Class sizes at the South Bank and Coomera studios are kept small enough that students get direct one-on-one critique, which matters in a discipline where the difference between a portfolio that gets a graduate an interview and one that doesn't often comes down to individual feedback rather than course content.

Graduates leave with an industry-ready portfolio and typically move into junior graphic design, brand identity, digital design or in-house studio roles; the credit-transfer arrangement (any one-year TAFE Queensland diploma articulates with 24 credit points, equivalent to a full year of the bachelor's) also makes this a common re-entry point for students who started a diploma elsewhere and want to upgrade to a degree.
curriculum:
Diploma phase: Design Fundamentals, Typography 1 & 2, Digital Imaging, Layout and Publication Design, Branding and Identity, Packaging Design, industry-based diploma project
Degree phase (University of Canberra): Design Theory and Criticism, Environmental and Wayfinding Design, Interactive and Motion Design, Design for Social Impact, Professional Practice, capstone design project and portfolio exhibition
Credit pathway: completed TAFE Queensland diplomas can transfer up to 24 credit points (one year) into the bachelor's component
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); delivered in partnership with the University of Canberra
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Information Technology (Cyber Security)
description:
This degree sits inside TAFE Queensland's broader IT offering at the Coomera campus, where students share lab space (the IT, Immersive Technology and Cyber Security Labs) with games design and network engineering cohorts rather than working in isolation. That cross-pollination matters more than it sounds: a lot of the practical cyber security work students end up doing (penetration testing a web app, hardening a small business network) touches the same infrastructure other students are building.

The course covers programming, networking and database management before narrowing into security-specific work: threat modelling, intrusion detection, digital forensics and governance frameworks. Queensland's cyber security workforce shortfall is cited constantly in TAFE Queensland's own marketing for this course, and it isn't exaggerated. Demand spans banking, healthcare, retail, defence contractors and state government simultaneously, which gives graduates more geographic flexibility within Queensland than a narrower specialisation would.

Graduates typically land entry-level security analyst, SOC analyst or junior penetration tester roles, and the degree articulates directly into TAFE Queensland's Graduate Diploma and Master of Cyber Security for anyone who wants to keep going.
curriculum:
Year 1: Programming Fundamentals, Network Fundamentals, Database Design and Management, IT Systems and Infrastructure, Introduction to Cyber Security, Professional Practice in IT
Year 2: Network Security and Defence, Operating Systems Security, Web Application Development and Security, Ethical Hacking Fundamentals, Cloud Computing, Systems Analysis and Design
Year 3: Digital Forensics, Cyber Security Governance and Risk, Incident Response and Threat Intelligence, Secure Software Development, capstone industry project (client-based security assessment), electives in IoT security or cryptography
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
TAFE Queensland's Bachelor of Nursing is built around clinical hours rather than lecture hours. The course schedules 840 hours of Professional Experience Placement across the three years, which clears the 800-hour minimum the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia sets for registration eligibility, and placement blocks are threaded through every year of study instead of stacked at the end.

Before students set foot in a ward, they work through scenarios in TAFE Queensland's simulated hospital wards, which run mock handovers, deteriorating-patient drills and medication rounds under the same documentation standards used in Queensland Health facilities. The course markets itself as "designed by nurses for nurses," and the teaching staff are practising or recently practising RNs rather than career academics, which shows up in how much time is spent on the unglamorous procedural detail of real ward work.

Graduates are eligible to apply for registration as a Registered Nurse with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (subject to AHPRA requirements) and typically move into acute care, aged care, community health or mental health settings across the Queensland public and private hospital systems.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology A & B, Introduction to Health Assessment, Psychology for Health Professionals, Professional Communication in Health, first Professional Experience Placement block (aged care/sub-acute)
Year 2: Pathophysiology and Pharmacology, Acute Care Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Nursing Older Persons, Primary Health Care, Research and Evidence-Based Practice, second and third PEP blocks (medical/surgical wards)
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing, Perioperative and Critical Care Nursing, Child and Family Health, Leadership and Transition to Professional Practice, one elective unit, final PEP blocks including a graduate transition placement
Clinical placement: 840 hours total across acute, sub-acute, mental health, community and aged care settings, exceeding the 800-hour AHPRA/NMBA minimum
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, plus health/immunisation checks (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall (typical registration-body bar for nursing programs, approximate)

name: Bachelor of the Built Environment (Architecture)
description:
Delivered with the University of Canberra, this degree is part of an Architects Accreditation Council of Australia-accredited pathway that continues into the Master of Architecture, meaning it's structured from year one as the first half of a longer registration pathway rather than a terminal qualification, which matters for students weighing it against a straight university architecture degree.

Work-integrated learning is built into every stage rather than bolted on as a single placement unit: TAFE Queensland promotes a series of "live" projects run with practising architects and design firms, plus internship placements at local, national and international practices. Studio culture leans into critique from working professionals rather than purely academic staff, and coursework is framed around developing "informed critique" of architecture as both creative and professional practice. The ethical and environmental responsibilities of the profession get explicit attention alongside design skill.

Entry is based on entrance rank, and it's a Commonwealth Supported Place, which keeps the cost profile closer to a standard university architecture degree than to a private design school. Graduates continue to the Master of Architecture for registration eligibility, or move into design, drafting and project roles in the built environment sector without completing the full registration pathway.
curriculum:
Year 1: Architectural Design Studio 1 & 2, History and Theory of Architecture, Construction Technology 1, Digital Representation and CAD, Environmental Design Principles
Year 2: Architectural Design Studio 3 & 4, Structures and Materials, Construction Technology 2, Urban Design and Context, live industry project 1
Year 3: Architectural Design Studio 5 & 6, Professional Practice and Ethics, Sustainable Design, live industry project 2, internship placement, portfolio for progression to Master of Architecture
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); accredited by the Architects Accreditation Council of Australia
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Diploma of Anaesthetic Technology and Practice
Diploma of Apparel, Fashion and Textiles
Diploma of Conservation and Ecosystem Management
Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care
Diploma of Photography and Digital Imaging
Diploma of Travel and Tourism Management
Graduate Diploma in Cyber Security
description:
This is TAFE Queensland's bridging qualification for people who already have IT or related experience but need a formal, accredited cyber security credential fast, and its own marketing is explicit that the intended endpoint is the Master of Cyber Security (Advanced), with graduates able to fast-track straight in rather than starting a master's from scratch. As a standalone qualification it also stands on its own for anyone not planning to continue to postgraduate level.

Content splits fairly evenly between technical security work (system security, digital forensics, ethical hacking and defensive techniques) and governance: cyber policy, compliance and organisational risk. That combination is deliberate; TAFE Queensland is explicit that the course is meant to produce people who understand both the attack surface and the regulatory environment around it, rather than pure penetration testers.

Entry accepts a relevant AQF 5 qualification plus two years' relevant work experience, a relevant bachelor's degree completed within six years, or three years of directly relevant work experience with no formal qualification, which makes this a realistic option for experienced IT staff without a cyber-specific degree.
curriculum:
Core units: System Security and Hardening, Digital Forensics Fundamentals, Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing, Cyber Policy and Governance, Risk Management and Compliance, Network Defence Techniques
Capstone: applied security assessment project
Progression: graduates can fast-track into the Master of Cyber Security (Advanced) with credit for equivalent units
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in any discipline (or relevant industry experience considered)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Cyber Security
description:
TAFE Queensland pitches this degree specifically at people who don't want to choose between the technical and policy sides of cyber security. The course is built to produce graduates who can both run an incident response and sit across the table from a board explaining what happened and why the organisation's governance failed. That dual framing is unusual for a technical postgraduate degree in this space, where most competitors lean hard into one side or the other.

Entry is flexible by design: applicants can come in via a relevant AQF 5 qualification plus two years' work experience, a relevant bachelor's degree, or three years of straight industry experience with no formal cyber credential at all, which makes it a realistic upgrade path for IT professionals who moved into security informally. Students who complete the Graduate Diploma in Cyber Security first (offered at the same campus) can fast-track directly into this Master's, and TAFE Queensland also runs a "Master of Cyber Security (Advanced)" variant with an extended research or industry project component for those wanting a deeper technical specialisation.

The course leans on Queensland's acute cyber workforce shortage (the state's banking, health, legal, retail, defence and government sectors are all short-staffed at once), and graduates move into security architecture, GRC (governance, risk and compliance), and senior analyst roles rather than purely entry-level positions given the postgraduate entry bar.
curriculum:
Core: Advanced Network Security, Cyber Security Policy and Governance, Digital Forensics and Incident Response, Security Risk Management, Applied Cryptography, Cyber Law and Ethics
Advanced/capstone stream: Enterprise Security Architecture, Threat Intelligence and Analytics, industry-based capstone project (real client security assessment or research thesis for the Advanced stream)
Delivery: coursework plus an industry-linked capstone; fast-track entry available for Graduate Diploma in Cyber Security completers, who receive credit for foundational units
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in IT or a related discipline (or relevant industry experience considered)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Advanced Diploma of Game Design and Development
description: The Advanced Diploma of Game Design and Development at Torrens University Australia builds the core skills needed to start a career in the gaming industry, built on three pillars: asset production, game ideation and design, and game project management. Students explore the principles and practices of professional asset production while gaining hands-on experience with industry-standard tools and game engines, supported by studio-based learning, theory and critical discussion. Students work in team-based studio environments using agile project management, and collaborate with game programming students on cross-disciplinary briefs.

name: Advanced Diploma of Game Programming
description: The Advanced Diploma of Game Programming at Torrens University Australia develops the technical, analytical and problem-solving expertise required to build modern games and interactive experiences across PC, mobile and console platforms. Students build their command of the mathematics, logic and software engineering skills that make gameplay possible, gaining hands-on experience with algorithms, C++, data structures, computer architecture, mathematics, physics and communication networks, and learning how these components integrate to produce responsive, immersive game systems. Learning takes place in collaborative, studio-style environments shaped by experienced educators and an industry-informed curriculum.

name: Advanced Diploma of Interior Design and Decoration
description: The Advanced Diploma of Interior Design and Decoration at Torrens University Australia is built in response to changing industry standards and prepares students for a career as a professional interior designer creating innovative spaces. Students learn to work on projects from the ground up, revamp residential spaces, and take on commercial projects, fusing style, comfort and sustainability. They develop decorative schemes for a range of interiors, learning how to select furnishings and finishes, and gain real-world experience documenting designs and bringing them to life, with projects focused on sustainability.

name: Advanced Diploma of Photography and Content Creation
Associate Degree of 3D Design and Animation
Associate Degree of Branded Fashion Design
Associate Degree of Business (International Hotel and Resort Management)
Associate Degree of Fashion Marketing and Enterprise
Associate Degree of Film and Video
Associate Degree of Software Engineering (Artificial Intelligence)
Associate Degree of UX and Web Design
Bachelor of 3D Design and Animation
description: The Bachelor of 3D Design and Animation at Torrens University Australia provides the technical skills, creative development and practical experience for a career in 3D design and animation. Students master 3D modelling, animation and interactive design for the games industry and gain an understanding of emerging areas of the field along with niche skills in a specialist area. Students work on live client projects, learn from industry professionals, and undertake internships that develop their skills in real-world professional settings.

name: Bachelor of Architectural Technology
description: The Bachelor of Architectural Technology at Torrens University Australia prepares students to work in the built environment industry using digital tools, and is described as the first course of its kind in Australia. Students focus on computer-aided design and building information modelling, learning the fundamentals of designing high-performance buildings from concept development to digital modelling and construction documentation, and master the core principles of materials, structure and energy efficiency for sustainable and socially conscious design. Mentored by industry leaders, students tackle live client briefs and gain practical experience in professional design environments.

name: Bachelor of Branded Fashion Design
description: The Bachelor of Branded Fashion Design at Torrens University Australia is about creating, producing and managing a fashion brand from the ground up. Students learn to design collections, bring them to life with industry-standard software, and market them, with guidance from industry experts on garment construction techniques, brand strategy analysis and fashion trends. The course explores how to produce collections that meet industry standards, stay on budget and meet deadlines, and how to manage brand integrity and positioning. Graduates can take a role at an existing label or launch their own.

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
The degree runs 15 core subjects against 9 electives, a heavier core-to-elective ratio than a lot of comparable business degrees, which front-loads shared fundamentals (business communication, understanding people and organisations, customer experience management, marketing fundamentals) before students branch into electives across marketing, public relations, event management, tourism and hospitality.

Two features do most of the work distinguishing this from a generic business degree: a mandatory 300 hours of industry-relevant experience built across the course rather than a single placement block, and a compulsory Industry Consulting Project subject where students work on an actual business problem for a real organisation rather than a simulated case study. That project is usually the first thing graduates put on a resume.

240 credit points, three years full-time standard, with part-time and accelerated study options and delivery across Torrens' Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Adelaide campuses as well as online.
curriculum:
Core subjects: Business Communications, Understanding People and Organisations, Marketing Fundamentals, Business Environment, Accounting Principles, Customer Experience Management, Industry Skills Projects, Business Law, Economics for Business
Electives (choose from): Marketing, Public Relations, Event Management, Tourism and Hospitality streams
Capstone: Industry Consulting Project (client-based applied business project)
Work experience: 300 hours of industry-relevant experience integrated across the degree
Total: 240 credit points across 24 subjects
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); no prerequisite subjects
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Communication Design
description: The Bachelor of Communication Design at Torrens University Australia teaches students to share information visually using contemporary techniques, tools and technology from across disciplines, guided by industry experts such as brand consultants, graphic designers and creative directors. The course covers the theory and practice of information design from initial concepts through to finished visuals, including print and digital design, strategic thinking, brand strategy, packaging design, storytelling, customer experience design and service design, along with sustainability in design and UI and UX design. Students develop a cross-disciplinary design skillset and choose electives aligned with their interests.

name: Bachelor of Community Services
description: The Bachelor of Community Services at Torrens University Australia equips students with the theory and skills for a career in the community and public sectors, covering counselling, social justice, advocacy and welfare, with practical experience working with individuals and communities. The course focuses on practical training while providing a grounding in communication, counselling and policy theory, and includes an extensive range of elective subjects and fieldwork placements. The course is not currently accredited and is awaiting the outcome of accreditation by the industry peak body.

name: Bachelor of Cybersecurity
description: The Bachelor of Cybersecurity at Torrens University Australia prepares students for a career fighting cybercrime in in-demand roles. Designed and delivered by industry, the course covers the ethical use of emerging and smart technologies and how to defend them, across subjects including cybersecurity principles, ethical hacking and penetration testing, human-centric cybersecurity in a smart society, and enterprise cybersecurity governance and applications, along with work-integrated learning. Graduates can analyse and recommend innovative cybersecurity solutions using design thinking and problem-solving skills. The course was co-developed with industry-leading ICT practitioners and academics.

name: Bachelor of Design (Graphic and Communication Design)
description:
This runs under Torrens' Billy Blue design school brand, and the course content pushes well past traditional graphic design into service design and CX: alongside brand strategy, packaging and storytelling, students work through UI/UX design and design thinking methodologies aimed at digital product work, not just print and identity design.

The signature subject is Design Studio, which is run deliberately like a working creative agency: students respond to briefs in small teams and are expected to defend design decisions to a "client" rather than simply submit finished artwork for grading. Sustainability in design also gets explicit curriculum time, which is a newer addition reflecting where the industry itself has moved.

Delivered across Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane campuses plus online, full-time, part-time or accelerated. Graduates go into art direction, UX design, graphic design, web and exhibition design, and branding/advertising/marketing specialist roles, a wider spread than "graphic designer" alone, reflecting how much of the later curriculum is aimed at digital and strategic design work.
curriculum:
Foundational: Design Fundamentals, Typography, Visual Communication, Design History and Theory
Core studio sequence: Design Studio (agency-style collaborative briefs, run across multiple trimesters at increasing complexity), Brand Strategy, Packaging Design, Storytelling and Visual Narrative
Digital/UX stream: UI/UX Design, Design Thinking, Service Design and CX
Sustainability and professional practice: Design for Sustainability, Professional Practice and Portfolio
Capstone: industry-briefed final major project and portfolio presentation
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); portfolio may be requested
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Fashion Marketing and Enterprise
description: The Bachelor of Fashion Marketing and Enterprise at Torrens University Australia, co-developed with industry, gives students creative and business skills, hands-on experience with leading brands and networking opportunities. Students experiment with building, marketing and managing fashion businesses, working with business models, digital strategies, fashion buying, brand development, consumer insights and the principles of entrepreneurship, and complete a double Capstone project in their final year. The degree prepares graduates to join and shape the future of the fashion industry.

name: Bachelor of Game Design and Development
description: The Bachelor of Game Design and Development at Torrens University Australia explores the fundamentals of game design, ideation and production, teaching students to transform ideas into playable experiences through creativity, critical thinking and problem-solving. Students develop advanced technical and artistic skills with a strong understanding of production pipelines, design principles and games culture, built on three pillars: asset production, game ideation and design, and game project management. Students create games from the ground up through work-integrated learning and a capstone project that culminates in a polished portfolio piece.

name: Bachelor of Game Programming
description: The Bachelor of Game Programming at Torrens University Australia is a specialised degree that develops game programmers for the PC, mobile and console games sector. Developed with industry and delivered by experienced educators, the course combines theory with hands-on practice. Students design and build the systems that power interactive experiences, from gameplay mechanics and artificial intelligence to graphics, physics and networking, grounded in core areas including C++, algorithms, data structures, mathematics, computer architecture and software engineering, with the technical depth to engineer high-performance, real-time game systems from concept to production.

name: Bachelor of Hospitality Management
description:
Structured as 8 common business core subjects, 10 specialised hospitality subjects and 6 electives across 240 credit points, this degree keeps a genuine business core rather than treating hospitality as a purely vocational add-on. Students graduate able to speak the language of a hotel group's finance and marketing teams, not just its floor operations.

The defining feature is two separate Industry Practicum placements rather than one, totalling a minimum of 800 hours of industry placement concentrated in second year. That's a substantial chunk of the degree spent working in the field partway through rather than only at the end, which means students get a second placement to apply what the first one taught them before they graduate.

Torrens also runs a related Bachelor of Business (Hospitality and Tourism Management) with a slightly different subject mix (20 core, 4 electives) for students wanting a broader tourism focus rather than a hospitality-management-specific one; the two are commonly confused because of overlapping subject names.
curriculum:
Business core (8 subjects): Business Communications, Accounting Principles, Marketing Fundamentals, Economics, Business Law, Understanding People and Organisations, Customer Experience Management, Business Analytics
Hospitality specialisation (10 subjects): Rooms Division Management, Food and Beverage Operations, Hospitality Financial Management, Revenue Management, Event and Conference Management, Hospitality Marketing, Hospitality Law, Sustainable Hospitality Operations, Human Resources in Hospitality, Hospitality Strategy
Industry placement: two Industry Practicum subjects totalling a minimum of 800 hours, concentrated in second year
Electives: 6 subjects from the broader business or hospitality/tourism elective pool
Total: 240 credit points across 24 subjects
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
22 subjects, 240 credit points, with one outsized final subject, ATW306 Advanced Tech: Work Integrated Learning, worth 30 credit points instead of the standard 10, effectively a triple-weighted capstone that anchors the whole degree around a substantial applied project rather than treating work-integrated learning as a token add-on.

Coverage spans programming, web development, data management and cybersecurity broadly enough that graduates aren't locked into one specialisation on paper, and Torrens frames the outcome explicitly around software engineering, cloud computing and cyber security demand, three areas where Australian employer demand has consistently outstripped supply. Delivery is online or on campus.

The single heavily-weighted capstone subject is the structural detail worth knowing if comparing this against other providers' IT degrees. Most spread work-integrated learning across two or three smaller subjects rather than concentrating it into one triple-credit unit near the end.
curriculum:
Core: Programming Fundamentals, Web Development, Database Systems, Network Fundamentals, Data Structures and Algorithms, Systems Analysis and Design, Cybersecurity Fundamentals, Cloud Computing
Electives: chosen across software engineering, cyber security or data-focused streams depending on trimester offering
Capstone: ATW306 Advanced Tech: Work Integrated Learning (30 credit points — triple the standard subject weight)
Total: 240 credit points across 22 subjects
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Interior Design (Commercial)
description: The Bachelor of Interior Design (Commercial) at Torrens University Australia gives students the skills and experience to design commercial environments such as retail stores, hotels, nightclubs, restaurants and workspaces. Students explore the practical elements of designing commercial interiors, including branding, lighting, sustainability and materiality, and learn how interior design strategies are developed and executed along with industry essentials such as contract management, cross-disciplinary teamwork and professional design practice. Using contemporary software and 3D modelling, students learn to take design ideas from costing to construction.

name: Bachelor of Media Production and Communication
description: The Bachelor of Media Production and Communication at Torrens University Australia develops creative, technical and strategic capabilities in media production, storytelling, content creation and digital communication. The course combines theory, practice and professional connection through hands-on, project-based learning and industry-led briefs, with students collaborating across creative and design disciplines while building expertise in narrative production, audience engagement, media influence and ethical, globally informed practice. From the first year, students engage with emerging technologies including generative AI and automation.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Torrens' Bachelor of Nursing carries the standard 800-hour clinical placement requirement across hospitals, aged care facilities, community health centres and other industry settings, but it's paired with an on-campus simulation hospital built to mirror real clinical environments before students ever go out on placement: assessment and clinical decision-making, person-centred care and professional communication get practised in a controlled setting first.

One thing Torrens does that's genuinely useful for students rather than just a marketing line: its Clinical Placement Program (CPP) provides paid clinical placements, addressing the unpaid-placement problem that's a live financial issue for nursing students nationally (most Australian nursing degrees still run placements unpaid). It's a relatively recent addition and worth noting because it changes the real cost of doing this degree compared to competitors that haven't moved on it.

Three years full-time, evidence-based curriculum, and graduates are eligible to apply for registration as a Registered Nurse with AHPRA on completion.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing, Anatomy and Physiology, Health Assessment, Professional Communication in Health, first simulation-hospital placements
Year 2: Pathophysiology and Pharmacology, Mental Health Nursing, Acute Care Nursing, Nursing the Older Person, clinical placements in hospital and aged care settings
Year 3: Complex and Critical Care Nursing, Primary Health Care, Research and Evidence-Based Practice, Transition to Professional Practice, final clinical placement block
Clinical placement: minimum 800 hours across hospital, aged care, community health and industry settings, with paid placement available through Torrens' Clinical Placement Program (CPP)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent), plus health/immunisation and police checks
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0 (nursing registration requirement)

name: Bachelor of Nutrition
description: The Bachelor of Nutrition at Torrens University Australia prepares students to assess the determinants of health and the nutritional needs of communities and broader populations. The course includes an industry-led group nutrition project supported by an industry partner, giving students practical experience. Students gain a solid understanding of health science, biology and physiology, learn about nutrition in the context of public health, pathology and improving health and wellness, and develop skills to critically analyse, develop and implement nutrition intervention programs, along with specialist subjects such as First peoples culture, history and healthcare, and public health nutrition.

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
This degree carries full APAC (Australian Psychology Accreditation Council) accreditation, backdated to Trimester 1 2024 so that every enrolled cohort is covered rather than only students who started after a given date. That detail matters because APAC accreditation is the non-negotiable first step toward registering as a psychologist in Australia, and a degree without it simply doesn't count toward that pathway regardless of course content quality.

Structurally this is Torrens' entry point into the standard Australian psychology registration pipeline: a three-year accredited undergraduate degree, followed by further accredited postgraduate study (typically an Honours year or Master's) and supervised practice before registration with the Psychology Board of Australia. Students who complete this degree without continuing to postgraduate psychology study still graduate with a solid grounding in research methods, statistics and behavioural science applicable to allied-health-adjacent and human-services roles.

Delivered across Torrens' health-focused campuses with the standard mix of research methods, biological and cognitive psychology, developmental and social psychology coursework that APAC's accreditation standard requires.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Psychology, Research Methods 1, Social Psychology, Developmental Psychology
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Research Methods 2 and Statistics, Abnormal Psychology, Psychological Assessment, Personality and Individual Differences
Year 3: Health Psychology, Research Methods 3 (empirical thesis/project), Professional Ethics in Psychology, electives, capstone research project
Accreditation: APAC-accredited (backdated to Trimester 1 2024), first stage of the Australian psychologist registration pathway
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of UX and Web Design
description: The Bachelor of UX and Web Design at Torrens University Australia develops the user experience and web design skills needed to work in the digital economy. Through industry-driven briefs, real client projects, industry mentors and internships, students learn practical coding and digital media alongside the psychology behind user behaviour, human-computer interaction and user experience. Students also study professional practice, graduating ready to work in the UX and web design industry with a strong portfolio.

name: Diploma of Beauty and Spa Practice
description: The Diploma of Beauty and Spa Practice at Torrens University Australia delivers the foundational knowledge and skills to apply a range of beauty therapy treatments and techniques, with graduates able to use up-to-date technologies and innovations in professional practice. Students gain a thorough understanding of beauty and spa technologies, treatments and practices and hands-on experience in the University's student-run clinic, The Practice Wellbeing Centre, under the supervision of practising aestheticians, in a collaborative learning environment that prepares them to begin working in the beauty industry.

name: Diploma of Branded Fashion Design
description: The Diploma of Branded Fashion Design at Torrens University Australia is an introduction to the fashion world and the business of what we wear, teaching students to create designs and take them from sketchbook to shop floor with an emphasis on creative, strategic, sustainable and cost-effective solutions. Guided by industry professionals, students study the theories of design and marketing, analyse communication and brand strategies, and examine fashion trends from historical, social and political angles, mastering the craft of turning ideas into market-ready fashion, working with form, shape and colour, materials, and technical drawing.

name: Diploma of Business (International Hotel and Resort Management)
Diploma of Cybersecurity
description: The Diploma of Cybersecurity at Torrens University Australia equips students with the practical, technical and theoretical skills in demand amid a global rise in cybercrime. Designed, developed and delivered by industry, the course develops IT skills across subjects including programming, data and networking, cloud computing, software engineering and cybersecurity principles. Its human-centric design focus is distinctive, and graduates can apply cybersecurity principles to developing ICT solutions that consider ethical and social responsibilities. The course is structured to meet the Australian Computer Society's Core Body of Knowledge and Cybersecurity Body of Knowledge.

name: Diploma of Design
description: The Diploma of Design at Torrens University Australia builds a foundation of design principles in one year, working alongside other students and supported by industry professionals. In studios and hands-on environments, students collaborate on real design briefs. Designed for people new to design as well as those with some experience, the diploma provides a broad taste of the industry, with electives that let students explore Branded Fashion Design, Fashion Marketing and Enterprise, Communication Design, Interior Design or Architectural Technology, and a pick-and-mix option for the undecided.

name: Diploma of Fashion Marketing and Enterprise
description: The Diploma of Fashion Marketing and Enterprise at Torrens University Australia focuses on the business side of fashion, covering the creation and management of fashion businesses. Students study fashion marketing, operations and retail, explore fashion business models, craft digital communication strategies, and learn the processes of fashion buying, merchandise planning and brand building, along with consumer research and entrepreneurship. On completion, graduates are ready to enter industry or continue to the Bachelor of Fashion Marketing and Enterprise.

name: Diploma of Game Design and Development
Diploma of Graphic Design
description: The Diploma of Graphic Design at Torrens University Australia covers the theory and practice of graphic design, with students crafting original solutions for digital signage, social media, websites and more. The course explores brand development, typography, UX and web design principles, and the Adobe Creative Suite, with students graduating with a portfolio. Guided by industry professionals, students develop design principles, research skills, ideas generation and brand identity, creating and workshopping their own brand, and tackle real-world projects and briefs. Study is available online or on campus.

name: Diploma of Health Science
description: The Diploma of Health Science at Torrens University Australia is a one-year diploma offering foundational knowledge in biological and social sciences, with electives and specialisations available in public health, naturopathy, nutrition and Chinese medicine so students can tailor their study. Students learn how the human body functions and core concepts in chemistry and evidence-based practice, and can enter the workforce or pursue further study in natural therapies or public health through the pathways program.

name: Diploma of Interior Design and Decoration
description: The Diploma of Interior Design and Decoration at Torrens University Australia gives students a foundation in the technical skills, industry knowledge and design processes that shape residential and commercial spaces. Guided by industry professionals, students explore design processes, materials and finishes, and gain practical experience working on live briefs, tackling real-world sustainability challenges and learning to design for a range of clients. Every piece of work created during the course builds the student's professional portfolio. It sets students up for further study or a career in the industry.

name: Diploma of Media Production
description: The Diploma of Media Production at Torrens University Australia is an entry point into storytelling, media, digital and content production. The hands-on, career-focused course builds foundational skills that students can take into the workforce or use as a pathway into a bachelor's degree. Aligned with today's media landscape, it explores a broad range of media and content disciplines, developing an understanding of media studies, the fundamentals of content creation, practical skills in motion design, and professional media practice, using industry-standard tools and workflows.

name: Diploma of Photography and Content Creation
Diploma of Photography and Photo Imaging
description: The Diploma of Photography and Photo Imaging at Torrens University Australia focuses on technical skills and hands-on experience in camera work, lighting, image manipulation and studio management. Students become confident with industry-standard software such as Adobe Photoshop, Lightroom and Premiere, and work with DSLR cameras, studio lighting and video rigs, handling projects from concept to completion across still images and video. Real-world exercises and access to studio spaces let students refine their skills, with guidance from professional photographers.

name: Diploma of UX and Web Design
description: The Diploma of UX and Web Design at Torrens University Australia blends practical coding and digital media skills with user interaction principles to help students design digital experiences. Students work hands-on with contemporary digital design software, UX and UI practices, and the psychological considerations that drive digital interaction and decision-making. The course shares subjects with other diplomas and bachelor programs, giving a clear pathway to further study or the credentials to enter the industry after graduation.

name: Doctor of Philosophy
description: The Doctor of Philosophy at Torrens University Australia is a research degree in which candidates conduct independent research under the supervision and guidance of experts in their field. The PhD requires completion of a thesis that demonstrates original thought and academic rigour and makes a significant contribution to existing knowledge. It is available on campus in Sydney, Adelaide, Melbourne and Brisbane, offshore and online. Candidates develop research skills to be work-ready in academic and industry contexts, conducting original research and communicating the impact of their findings to stakeholders in real-world applications.

name: Graduate Certificate in Counselling
description: The Graduate Certificate of Counselling at Torrens University Australia enhances counselling and interpersonal communication skills and builds an understanding of the human psyche, counselling theories and barriers to wellbeing. It is valuable for extending skills in fields such as nursing, social work and teaching. Students develop knowledge of the theoretical and ethical underpinnings of counselling, delivery methods such as telehealth, working with suicidality and common mental health conditions, and the importance of effective boundaries and self-care. The course can start or advance a career in the counselling and wellbeing industry and is delivered online.

name: Graduate Certificate in Learning and Teaching
description: The Graduate Certificate in Higher Education (Learning and Teaching) at Torrens University Australia is a professional development program designed to improve teaching practices in tertiary, vocational and higher education. It is aimed at academics with subject-specialist expertise, experienced educators, and those considering a career teaching in VET and higher education. Students develop the knowledge and skills to address teaching challenges in their discipline, with action-based research informing best practice, and have the chance to apply and test their strategies in adult educational settings with opportunities for reflective practice.

name: Graduate Certificate of Analytics
description: The Graduate Certificate of Analytics at Torrens University Australia develops the knowledge and skills for a career in a data-centric world, meeting the demand for professionals who can convert data into insights and solutions. Through experiential learning, students develop practical knowledge of the analytical lifecycle and fundamental skills in key areas such as artificial intelligence, data and programming, learning to prepare data from multiple sources and work with programming languages to support analytics processes. The certificate provides a pathway into further study, including the Master of Business Analytics.

name: Graduate Certificate of Business Administration
description: The Graduate Certificate of Business Administration at Torrens University Australia provides a foundation in leadership, marketing and business management, teaching students to make effective decisions in a global context and develop business acumen and leadership ability that can be applied in a current workplace or a new venture. The course comprises four core subjects: Business Environment, Business Communications, Marketing, and Financial Management, and is a pathway toward the MBA.

name: Graduate Certificate of Business Analytics
description: The Graduate Certificate of Business Analytics at Torrens University Australia equips students with the knowledge and practical skills to work in a data-centric world, covering foundational areas such as data analysis and modelling and the tools to turn raw information into actionable insights. Students examine contemporary technologies and communication techniques to build their data and analytical capabilities and their ability to converse with expert and non-expert stakeholders, and the course provides a pathway into further study including the Master of Business Analytics.

name: Graduate Certificate of Cybersecurity
description: The Graduate Certificate of Cybersecurity at Torrens University Australia provides fundamental IT skills and an understanding of the field of cybersecurity, developing knowledge of software and data security along with a foundation of cybersecurity principles applied within the Industry 4.0 environment. The course teaches the in-demand human-centric problem-solving skills employers seek and an understanding of ethical and professional decision making in a cybersecurity context. It was co-developed with industry-leading ICT practitioners and academics and is structured to meet the Australian Computer Society's Core Body of Knowledge and Cybersecurity Body of Knowledge.

name: Graduate Certificate of Design
description: The Graduate Certificate of Design at Torrens University Australia sharpens skills in design and problem-solving, using contemporary technology and methodologies to tackle business and societal challenges through design thinking and critical analysis. Core subjects include Professional Identity, Design Methods and Design Communication, plus an elective in UX Design or Project Management. It suits people with no design background who want an entry point into the field, as well as those already working in design who want to develop their practice, and prepares graduates to work across global creative industries.

name: Graduate Certificate of Education
description: The Graduate Certificate of Education at Torrens University Australia prepares students for leadership roles across the broad field of education, developing key skills and knowledge to expand and enhance their practice. Taking a design-thinking approach to educational issues, the course provides a foundation in the research of inclusion, leadership and social justice and empowers students to enact change in program, policy and project design through case study analysis and research. It is a standalone qualification and a pathway into the Graduate Diploma and Master of Education.

name: Graduate Certificate of Global Project Management
Graduate Certificate of Higher Education
description: The Graduate Certificate in Higher Education (Learning and Teaching) at Torrens University Australia is a professional development program designed to improve teaching practices in tertiary, vocational and higher education. It is aimed at academics with subject-specialist expertise, experienced educators, and those considering a career teaching in VET and higher education. Students develop the knowledge and skills to address teaching challenges in their discipline, with action-based research informing best practice, and apply and test their strategies in adult educational settings with opportunities for reflective practice.

name: Graduate Certificate of Information Technology
description: The Graduate Certificate of Information Technology at Torrens University Australia expands existing knowledge of fundamental IT skills, providing creative application, cognitive and technical skills for a career in the ICT industry. Students cover key IT areas including programming, environmental security, software engineering and software development, learning to design and develop secure, innovative ICT solutions to business problems. The course can be completed full time over one trimester or part time over three, and was co-developed with industry-leading ICT practitioners and academics.

name: Graduate Certificate of International Hotel Management
Graduate Certificate of Public Health
description: The Graduate Certificate of Public Health at Torrens University Australia focuses on health and the prevention of illness, disease, injury and death, covering social, cultural and behavioural factors in public health, health policy and advocacy, health systems and economics, and epidemiology. This online certificate develops an understanding of current global and environmental health issues along with the social, behavioural and cultural determinants of health, with a strong focus on ethical practice and communicating health information to diverse audiences. It is a standalone qualification and a pathway to the Graduate Diploma or Master of Public Health.

name: Graduate Certificate of Research Studies
description: The Graduate Certificate of Research Studies at Torrens University Australia offers foundational theoretical and technical knowledge and skills in research. Students undertake four research training units and gain an understanding of literature review, future research requirements and research proposal writing, along with the analytical and communication skills required for future research. On completion, graduates are equipped to work in research-related fields and support researchers with foundation research skills, having advanced theoretical and technical knowledge in one or more disciplines and advanced cognitive, technical and communication skills.

name: Graduate Diploma of Business Administration
description: The Graduate Diploma of Business Administration at Torrens University Australia expands on business knowledge with a global leadership perspective, teaching students to develop strategies to guide business development and to employ dynamic leadership skills. Designed by industry academics for ambitious individuals, the course covers four core and four elective subjects and is a pathway to a full MBA or MBA (Advanced), as well as a standalone qualification. The core units of the Graduate Certificate of Business Administration are required for the exit pathway.

name: Graduate Diploma of Business Analytics
description: The Graduate Diploma of Business Analytics at Torrens University Australia offers advanced skills across business analysis, data modelling, statistical analysis and visual analytics, with a practical focus on driving data-driven solutions in a commercial setting. Students examine contemporary technologies and communication techniques to build their data and analytical capabilities and their ability to converse with stakeholders, and learn to elicit business requirements and recommend analytical solutions that embed within business flows. It provides a pathway into further study including the Master of Business Analytics.

name: Graduate Diploma of Business Information Systems
Graduate Diploma of Counselling
description: The Graduate Diploma of Counselling at Torrens University Australia is a postgraduate qualification that enhances skills in counselling and interpersonal communication. This online course focuses on the theories and practices of counselling and offers practical experience through supervised work placement. Students learn about personal self-care while caring for others, the effects of vicarious trauma, and how to provide services through telehealth, graduating with professional counselling experience and skills to enable further lifelong learning and effective interpersonal communication across business, community, education and wellbeing settings.

name: Graduate Diploma of Education (Leadership & Innovation)
description: The Graduate Diploma of Education at Torrens University Australia allows current teachers, education practitioners and professionals to enhance their skills, research capabilities and expertise in specific areas of educational theory and practice, choosing from specialisation streams including Leadership and Innovation and Inclusive Literacies. The Leadership and Innovation stream develops theoretical and practical insights to identify challenges and opportunities in education, devise effective strategies, and critically assess contemporary educational innovations. Grounded in research on inclusion, leadership and social justice, the course equips students to effect change in program, policy and project design.

name: Graduate Diploma of Global Project Management
Graduate Diploma of Information Technology
description: The Graduate Diploma of Information Technology at Torrens University Australia equips IT professionals with a diverse skillset for the ICT landscape, establishing a foundation in software development, cloud computing and AI principles beyond fundamental IT competencies. Students cultivate creative application, cognitive and technical abilities and learn to manage complex IT projects by analysing problems and developing solutions. The course serves as a standalone qualification or a pathway into the Master of Information Technology and Master of Information Technology (Advanced).

name: Graduate Diploma of Public Health
description: The Graduate Diploma of Public Health at Torrens University Australia provides advanced knowledge to prepare health professionals to address public health challenges and improve health and wellbeing, emphasising the social determinants of health and equipping students to address inequalities for vulnerable populations. Students gain an understanding of global and environmental health issues, health policy, systems and economics, and develop skills in planning, implementing and evaluating public health programs, health promotion and disease prevention, advocacy, statistics and epidemiology. It can lead to further study with the Master of Public Health.

name: Graduate Diploma of Research Studies
description: The Graduate Diploma of Research Studies at Torrens University Australia offers advanced theoretical and technical knowledge and skills in research. Students undertake eight core subjects including a Preliminary Research Thesis, with a strong foundation in research skills and research project planning and implementation that provides the analytical and communication skills required for future research. On completion, graduates are equipped to work in research-related fields and support researchers, having gained advanced cognitive, technical and communication skills to analyse, evaluate and transform information and generate solutions to complex problems.

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Torrens' MBA is built around six core leadership subjects and then hands most of the customisation over to the student: elective streams run through Marketing Management, Business Analytics and Insight, Project Management, Engineering Management, Technology and Digital Innovation, Strategy and Entrepreneurship, Health Leadership, CX and Service Design, and Finance, and students aren't locked into picking just one: electives can be mixed across streams rather than treated as a fixed specialisation.

The exit-point structure is the more unusual design choice: a student who needs to stop partway through can leave with a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma of Business Administration rather than nothing, which matters for working professionals whose circumstances change mid-degree. Full-time completion runs 1.5 years standard or one year accelerated, with part-time and blended online/on-campus options across Torrens' city campuses.

Given the elective spread, this MBA tends to attract people already mid-career who want to redirect rather than restart, someone moving from operations into digital strategy, or a clinician moving into health leadership, more than fresh graduates.
curriculum:
Core (6 subjects): Leading and Managing People, Strategic Marketing, Financial Management for Decision Making, Business Analytics, Global Business Environment, Leadership and Ethics
Elective streams (choose one or combine): Marketing Management, Business Analytics and Insight, Project Management, Engineering Management, Technology and Digital Innovation, Strategy and Entrepreneurship, Health Leadership, CX and Service Design, Finance
Capstone: applied strategy project
Exit points: Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma of Business Administration available before full MBA completion
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline), professional experience considered favourably (typical MBA entry bar, approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Master of Business Analytics (Advanced)
description: The Master of Business Analytics (Advanced) at Torrens University Australia advances students' ability to convert data into insights and solutions, mastering the analytical lifecycle in a multidisciplinary course. Students develop fundamental knowledge and skills in key analytical areas such as artificial intelligence, data, optimisation, and visualisation and storytelling, and examine contemporary technologies and communication techniques to build their capabilities and their ability to converse with expert and non-expert stakeholders. Students learn to elicit business requirements and recommend analytical solutions that embed within business flows. The Advanced version extends the course with additional study.

name: Master of Counselling
description: The Master of Counselling at Torrens University Australia is a postgraduate qualification that enhances counselling skills and equips students to advance their career in the field. This online course focuses on the advanced theories and practices of counselling and offers practical experience through supervised work placement, preparing students to offer counselling services and facilitate effective interpersonal communication across business, community, education and wellbeing settings. The accredited degree is described as the highest level of counselling training available in Australia and provides a supervised environment to develop hands-on counselling skills.

name: Master of Cybersecurity (Advanced)
description: The Master of Cybersecurity (Advanced) at Torrens University Australia meets the growing need for professionals equipped to protect against cybersecurity threats. Students develop extensive knowledge and skills in software and network security, human-centric cybersecurity solutions and enterprise computing systems, with a thorough understanding of the ethical use of technology in designing and implementing innovative cybersecurity solutions. Students complete work-integrated learning subjects to put their learning into practice. The course was co-developed with industry-leading ICT practitioners and academics and is structured to meet the Australian Computer Society's Core Body of Knowledge and Cybersecurity Body of Knowledge.

name: Master of Design
description:
Torrens' postgraduate design offering (delivered through the Billy Blue design school) is built for people who already have design experience or an undergraduate design qualification and want to move into strategic or leadership-level creative roles, such as creative direction, design strategy, or service design leadership, rather than a from-scratch design conversion degree.

The curriculum extends the same strategic and service-design emphasis that runs through Torrens' undergraduate design courses: brand strategy, CX and service design, and design thinking applied at a systems level rather than a single-artefact level, with a major independent research or industry project forming the spine of the degree.

Delivered on campus in Sydney, Melbourne or Brisbane, or online/blended, typically over 1.5 to 2 years full-time depending on advanced standing granted for prior design study.
curriculum:
Core: Design Strategy and Leadership, Advanced Design Research Methods, Service Design and CX at Scale, Design Management
Electives: brand strategy, UX/UI leadership, sustainable design practice (subject to trimester offering)
Capstone: major independent design research or industry-partnered project
Entry: undergraduate design qualification or significant industry design experience, with advanced standing assessed individually
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in design or a related field; portfolio may be requested
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Engineering Management
description: The Master of Engineering Management at Torrens University Australia enhances management, innovation and sustainability practices, focusing on effective engineering management in technical organisations and drawing on the University's network of industry partners. Students develop cognitive, technical and creative skills to solve problems, manage risks and develop strategies in an organisational context, studying 10 core subjects and six electives to tailor the qualification to their career goals. Graduates are equipped for leadership roles in technical organisations.

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
Torrens offers both a standard Master of Information Technology and an "Advanced" variant; the Advanced stream runs 160 credit points over 13 subjects, including a 20-credit-point capstone (ITW601) and a 30-credit-point advanced project (ITA602), which is a noticeably heavier project load than most coursework master's degrees carry.

Content mixes core software and systems units, including Principles of Programming, Secure by Design, and Software Engineering Principles, with electives in cloud computing, artificial intelligence and data modelling, letting students weight the degree toward development, security or data depending on where they're headed. Entry expects an existing IT-adjacent bachelor's degree covering programming, networks, databases and web development, so this isn't designed as a from-scratch career-change degree the way some competitor "IT conversion" master's programs are.

Delivered online or on campus, with the Advanced version taking around two years full-time for international students.
curriculum:
Core: Principles of Programming, Secure by Design, Software Engineering Principles, Cloud Computing, Data Modelling, Systems Analysis and Design
Advanced stream extras: extended capstone (ITW601, 20 credit points) and advanced industry project (ITA602, 30 credit points)
Electives: artificial intelligence, advanced cloud architecture, cybersecurity, data analytics (subject to trimester offering)
Entry: relevant IT-related bachelor's degree required (programming, networks, databases, web development)
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Information Technology Advanced
description: The Master of Information Technology (Advanced) at Torrens University Australia builds on students' current knowledge to create new opportunities and explore different career paths across a range of IT topics, providing advanced capability with existing and emerging technologies. Students choose electives aligned with their goals, including big data and analytics, user experience design, management of people and teams, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence, with a focus on the infrastructure aspect of IT such as designing and implementing cloud computing solutions. The course is structured to align with the guidelines of the Australian Computer Society.

name: Master of International Hotel Management
description: The Master of International Hotel Management at Torrens University Australia prepares students to lead and manage hotel operations in the global hospitality industry while building connections with leading hotel brands around the world. Students explore core business concepts such as management, marketing, revenue generation, research, critical analysis and leadership through the specialised lens of hotel management and the wider hospitality sector. In the second year, students complete a professional placement of 600 hours with a hotel organisation, applying their knowledge and skills in a real-world setting.

name: Master of Philosophy
description: The Master of Philosophy at Torrens University Australia is a postgraduate qualification for those seeking to enhance their research skills. It provides research training through coursework and a research project, culminating in a minor thesis, with a structure designed around adult learning theory to promote collaboration and critical thinking. Graduates gain an advanced and integrated understanding of a complex body of knowledge in one or more disciplines, along with knowledge and skills for research, professional practice and further learning.

name: Master of Professional Accounting (Advanced)
description: The Master of Professional Accounting (Advanced) at Torrens University Australia covers accounting, auditing, finance, economics, information systems and tax law, and is accredited by CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand. Students learn from industry-experienced academics through practical and work-integrated learning and gain hands-on experience with industry-leading software. Graduates are prepared for a career in global accounting and financial organisations, able to apply ethical, legal, social and environmental responsibilities and interpret and apply rules, regulations and theories to complex accounting situations. The Advanced version extends the course with additional study.

name: Master of Public Health
description:
Torrens runs both a standard Master of Public Health (1.5 years full-time, one year accelerated) and a Master of Public Health (Advanced), a two-year version aimed at health professionals who want deeper grounding in the social determinants of health rather than a faster generalist qualification. The Advanced stream is explicitly framed as building on existing clinical or health-sector experience rather than being a from-scratch entry point.

Torrens also offers combined degrees pairing an MPH with a Master of Global Project Management or a Master of Business Administration, aimed at students who want public health content married to leadership or project-delivery credentials, a combination that's more common among students already working in health system management or NGO/government health roles than clinicians heading toward direct patient care.

Delivered on campus at Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Adelaide as well as online, with core public health methods (epidemiology, biostatistics, health policy) underpinning both the standard and Advanced streams.
curriculum:
Core: Foundations of Public Health, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Health Policy and Systems, Health Promotion, Research Methods in Public Health
Advanced stream extras: Social Determinants of Health (extended), Health Systems Leadership, additional applied research project
Electives: global health, environmental health, health program evaluation (subject to trimester offering)
Capstone: applied public health project or research thesis
Combined degree options: available with Master of Global Project Management or Master of Business Administration
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in health science, nursing, or a related field
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Public Health Advanced
description: The Master of Public Health (Advanced) at Torrens University Australia builds on existing knowledge and skills to equip health professionals to address public health issues, emphasising the social determinants of health and preparing students to address inequalities for vulnerable populations. This extended degree gives professionals from a broad range of health backgrounds the advanced knowledge and skills to address public health challenges locally and around the world, enhancing understanding of global and environmental health issues, ethical practice, health policy, systems and economics, and the social, behavioural and cultural determinants of health. As an extended degree it is well suited to international students.

name: Master of Research Studies
description: The Master of Research Studies at Torrens University Australia offers advanced theoretical and technical skills in research management. Students learn how to contribute to new knowledge through research and to improve professional practice in research proposal writing, ethics, data collection and method choices to support projects in advanced professional practice. Graduates gain advanced cognitive, technical and communication skills, learning to analyse, critically evaluate and transform information to solve complex business, social or environmental problems, and to demonstrate autonomy, adaptability and responsibility as a research practitioner.

name: Master of Software Engineering (Artificial Intelligence, Advanced)
Professional Doctorate (Research)
description: The Professional Doctorate (Research) at Torrens University Australia embeds research training through coursework and reflective practice, resulting in new discipline knowledge through research. Graduates require a systematic and critical understanding of a complex field of learning and specialised research skills for the advancement of new knowledge. Students collaborate with industry, government and community partners to find innovative solutions that benefit business and community at a local, national and global level, and are positioned for career advancement across a diverse range of industry sectors. The course suits students with previous work experience.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
A three-year, 72 credit point arts degree built around a core major in Arts plus one specialist major chosen from about ten options, including Creative Writing, Digital Media, Film Production, Game Development, Journalism, Global Studies, Marketing Communication, Culture and Heritage, Literary Studies and Sports Media. The rest of the degree is open electives, so students can add a second major or spread across disciplines.

Teaching is project-based, and work integrated learning through internships, mentorships and placements is a required part of the structure rather than an add-on. Applicants can enter on academic results or through a portfolio that demonstrates creative potential. Graduates move into content and copywriting, production, curatorial and heritage work, communications and policy roles, with the exact path shaped by the major chosen. It suits students who want a flexible humanities and creative-industries degree with a clear practical and industry-facing emphasis.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Arts and Design (Honours)
description: A one-year honours year following the Bachelor of Arts and Design or a related degree at the University of Canberra. It combines advanced coursework with a substantial supervised research project or creative work in a chosen area of the arts, design, media or humanities. Entry requires a completed bachelor's degree with a strong grade average in the relevant field and an available supervisor. The honours result is classified, and a first or upper second class is the standard requirement for PhD entry and many scholarships.
