description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in international development, covering development theory, aid and program practice, and the political and economic context of development work. It sits within UC's governance and policy offering and articulates into related graduate diploma and master's study. Entry is open to graduates and to people working in aid, NGOs or government. It suits people entering or working in international development who want a formal qualification, or a first step toward a master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); open to people working in government, advocacy, research or the community sector, with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Law
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate for non-law graduates who want working legal knowledge, delivered fully online and part-time over about eight months. It is not a qualification to practise law. Students take two foundation units, Legal Methods and Skills and Legal Systems, plus two electives such as Contract Law, Constitutional Law or Intellectual Property Law. Entry requires a bachelor's degree in a non-law field with a sound grade average and IELTS 6.5. Graduates can progress into UC's Graduate Diploma in Law or the Juris Doctor, which does lead toward admission to practise. It suits professionals in compliance, policy, government relations and business who need to understand the law without becoming a lawyer.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in a non-law field with a sound grade average; IELTS 6.5 overall (6.0 in each band) for international applicants.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in LGBTQIA+ Policy
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in LGBTQIA+ policy, covering how law and public policy affect LGBTQIA+ communities, policy analysis and the evidence base for reform. It sits within UC's public policy suite and articulates into related graduate diploma and master's study. Entry is open to graduates and to people working in government, advocacy or community organisations. It suits policy officers and advocates who want a focused qualification in LGBTQIA+ inclusive policy.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); open to people working in government, advocacy, research or the community sector, with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Policy and Data
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate that pairs public policy with data skills, covering policy analysis alongside data handling, visualisation and evidence use for decision-making. It sits within UC's policy and governance offering and articulates into related graduate diploma and master's study. Entry is open to graduates and to people working in government or research. It suits policy and program staff who want to work more confidently with data, or a short qualification before a fuller policy master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); open to people working in government, advocacy, research or the community sector, with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Policy Evaluation
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in policy evaluation, covering evaluation design, methods, and using findings to improve programs and inform decisions. It sits within UC's public policy suite, which is a natural fit in Canberra given the concentration of federal agencies, and articulates into related graduate diploma and master's study. Entry is open to graduates and to people working in government or the community sector. It suits program and policy staff who want formal training in evaluating what works.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); open to people working in government, advocacy, research or the community sector, with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Public Administration
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in public administration, covering how government works: policy processes, public sector management, governance and accountability. It articulates with full credit into UC's Graduate Diploma and Master of Public Administration, a suite well suited to Canberra's public service. Entry is open to graduates and to people working in government. It suits public servants and people entering the sector who want a formal qualification, or a staged route into the master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); open to people working in government, advocacy, research or the community sector, with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Public Policy
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in public policy, covering the policy cycle, policy analysis and the political and institutional context of policymaking. It articulates with full credit into UC's Graduate Diploma and Master of Public Policy. Entry is open to graduates and to people working in government, advocacy or research. It suits people entering or working in policy roles who want a formal grounding, or a first step toward the master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); open to people working in government, advocacy, research or the community sector, with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in STEM Education
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in STEM education for people who already work in education, taken fully online. Units cover STEM pedagogy, integrated project-based learning and assessment, and are credited in full toward UC's Master of Education with a STEM focus. It is not an initial teaching qualification. It suits practising teachers and school leaders who want to strengthen and formalise their STEM teaching, or a short step toward the master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in a STEM field or education (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL) and Foreign Language Teaching (FLT)
Graduate Certificate in TESOL and Foreign Language Teaching (FLT)
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in teaching English to speakers of other languages and foreign language teaching, covering second language acquisition and language teaching methodology. The units are credited in full toward UC's Graduate Diploma and the two-year Master of TESOL and Foreign Language Teaching. It is an introductory qualification: registration to teach in Australian schools is a separate process. It suits people exploring a move into language teaching, or professionals who want a short TESOL credential.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in a related field (relevant for practising or aspiring language educators) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Ultrasound Studies
description: The University of Canberra's Graduate Certificate in Ultrasound Studies is a 12 credit point course and the first step toward a career in sonography, developing foundational knowledge and practical skills in medical ultrasound over about a year part-time in blended mode. On its own it does not confer accreditation: graduates must complete the Graduate Diploma in Medical Ultrasound to become an Australian Sonographer Accreditation Registry accredited sonographer. Applicants do not need to already work in a clinical role, but entry requires a bachelor's degree in medical radiation science, or a bachelor's in any field plus completed anatomy and physiology study. It suits people moving into sonography who want to start with a shorter qualification.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in medical radiation science; or a bachelor's degree in any field plus completed degree-level anatomy and physiology study. Prior clinical work is not required.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Graduate Certificate: Country as Teacher
description: The University of Canberra's Graduate Certificate Country as Teacher is a specialist 12 credit point course, three units delivered part-time over about eighteen months, that helps registered teachers embed First Nations knowledge and Country-based pedagogy in their classrooms. The units move from relating with Country practice, to co-designing units of work, to implementing and evaluating them, using a both-ways approach that combines Western and Aboriginal ways of knowing and teaching. Entry requires current teacher registration at proficient level or equivalent, and enrolment is generally on a cohort basis through partnerships rather than individual application. It suits practising teachers and school leaders who want to embed Indigenous perspectives authentically.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in education or a related field, with a focus on Indigenous ways of teaching and learning (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Building and Construction Information Management
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma, the middle stage of the University of Canberra's Building Information Modelling pathway. It builds on the graduate certificate with further study in BIM technology, procurement and project management, and articulates with full credit into the two-year Master of Building and Construction Information Management, which uses UC's BIM Hub facilities. Entry normally requires an undergraduate qualification in a built-environment field, with recognition of prior learning for experienced applicants. It suits construction and design professionals building toward the full master's in stages.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in construction management, architecture, engineering or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Business Informatics
description: The University of Canberra's Graduate Diploma in Business Informatics is a 24 credit point course sitting between the graduate certificate and the two-year Master of Business Informatics. It covers systems analysis, IT security and business-technology alignment, with the option to work toward a specialisation in Cybersecurity, Data Science or Project Management. No prior IT or informatics background is assumed. All units are credited in full toward the master's. It suits people bridging business and IT who want a substantial qualification with the option to complete the master's later.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); no prior IT or informatics background is assumed.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Communication
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in professional communication, sitting between UC's Graduate Certificate and Master of Communication. It extends the certificate with further study in communication strategy, digital media, research and a professional or applied component. All units are credited in full toward the master's. It suits people working in or moving into communication, marketing and public relations who want a substantial qualification and the flexibility to finish the master's later.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in communication, media or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Counselling
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in counselling, the middle stage of UC's counselling pathway, building on the graduate certificate with further theory, skills and the start of supervised practice. It articulates with full credit into the Master of Counselling, which is accredited by the Australian Counselling Association and includes 200 hours of placement and a five-day intensive. The diploma is an intermediate qualification and not a route to independent practice on its own. It suits people moving into counselling who want a substantial qualification and a staged path to the master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in psychology, social science or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Creative Industries
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in the creative industries, sitting between UC's Graduate Certificate and Master of Creative Industries. It extends the certificate with further discipline study, professional practice and project work. All units are credited in full toward the master's. It suits practising creatives and people entering the sector who want a substantial postgraduate qualification with the option to complete the master's later.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in a creative or related discipline (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Information Technology
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in information technology for graduates from any field, sitting between UC's Graduate Certificate and Master of Information Technology. It covers programming, systems, databases, networks and a project component, with no prior IT study assumed. All units are credited in full toward the master's. It suits career changers who want a substantial IT qualification and a staged, lower-commitment route to the master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (extended IT conversion program) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Law
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in law for non-law graduates, sitting between UC's Graduate Certificate in Law and the Juris Doctor. It covers foundational legal subjects and legal method in more depth than the certificate. It is not a qualification to practise law: that requires the Juris Doctor and admission. Units are credited toward the JD for students who continue. It suits professionals in policy, compliance, government and business who want substantial legal knowledge, or a staged path toward qualifying as a lawyer.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in a non-law field (or the Graduate Certificate in Law); IELTS 6.5 overall (6.0 in each band) for international applicants.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Medical Ultrasound
description: The University of Canberra's Graduate Diploma in Medical Ultrasound is a 24 credit point course, taken part-time over about two years in blended mode, that builds clinical sonography competence through coursework and supervised clinical practice. Completing it is the qualification that makes graduates eligible for accreditation with the Australian Sonographer Accreditation Registry as an accredited medical sonographer, following on from the Graduate Certificate in Ultrasound Studies. Students generally need access to a clinical placement site. It suits people committed to a career in sonography who have completed the entry-level certificate.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in medical radiation science, nursing, medicine or a related field, with relevant clinical experience (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Graduate Diploma in Nutritional Science
description: The University of Canberra's Graduate Diploma in Nutritional Science is a 24 credit point course covering nutrition through the lifespan, public health nutrition, and the evidence base for dietary advice. It is a science and public health qualification rather than a clinical dietetics degree, so it does not lead to registration as a dietitian. It can articulate into further postgraduate nutrition study. Entry normally requires a bachelor's degree with some biological science. It suits health, fitness and food-industry professionals who want a solid grounding in nutrition science.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in science, health science or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Public Policy
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in public policy, sitting between UC's Graduate Certificate and Master of Public Policy. It extends the certificate with further study in policy analysis, evaluation and the institutional context of government. All units are credited in full toward the master's. It suits people working in or moving into policy roles, particularly in and around the Canberra public service, who want a substantial qualification with the option to finish the master's later.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); open to people working in government, advocacy, research or the community sector, with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Diploma in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL) and Foreign Language Teaching (FLT)
Graduate Diploma in TESOL and Foreign Language Teaching (FLT)
description: A 24 credit point graduate diploma in teaching English to speakers of other languages and foreign language teaching, sitting between UC's Graduate Certificate and the two-year Master of TESOL and Foreign Language Teaching. It covers second language acquisition, methodology, curriculum and assessment in more depth than the certificate. All units are credited in full toward the master's. Registration to teach in Australian schools is a separate process. It suits people moving into language teaching who want a substantial qualification and a staged route to the master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in a related field (relevant for practising or aspiring language educators) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Honours in Science and Technology
description: A one-year science and technology honours year at the University of Canberra, taken after a relevant bachelor's degree in the sciences, mathematics or technology. It pairs advanced research-methods coursework with a supervised research project and thesis in a discipline matched to a supervisor, such as biology, environmental science, chemistry, physics, data science or IT. Entry requires a completed bachelor's degree with a strong grade average in the relevant area. The honours result is classified, and a first or upper second class is the standard requirement for PhD entry and research scholarships. It suits science and technology graduates who want a research year before committing to a doctorate or moving into a research role.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 70-75 (or equivalent); Mathematics at a senior secondary level recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Juris Doctor
description:
UC's Juris Doctor is a graduate-entry law degree for people who already hold a bachelor's degree in a non-law field, delivered fully online across 24 units, each run in a seven-week block rather than a traditional semester. With six intakes a year, students can start almost whenever life allows rather than waiting for a February or July opening.

To graduate, students must complete the foundation units, all Priestley 11 units (the national core required for admission to legal practice in Australia), the program's additional core units, and at least one of three Research and Internship Stream units, filling out the rest with electives.

Those electives lean toward technology, innovation and dispute resolution, which fits UC's broader positioning as a public-policy and government-adjacent university; several electives sit at the intersection of law and public administration, useful for JD students already working in or heading toward Commonwealth legal or policy roles based in Canberra.
curriculum:
Foundation units: Introduction to Law and Legal Reasoning; Legal Research and Writing
Priestley 11 core units: Contracts; Torts; Criminal Law; Property Law; Equity; Company Law; Administrative Law; Federal and State Constitutional Law; Civil and Criminal Procedure; Evidence; Professional Conduct (Ethics)
Additional core units: Public International Law; Legal Theory
Research and Internship Stream (complete at least 1): Legal Internship; Directed Research Project; Law Reform Project
Electives (remaining units to reach 24 total): drawn from technology and law, alternative dispute resolution, and public-sector/government law offerings
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (or equivalent); this is a graduate-entry law qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Applied Arts and Humanities (Research)
Master of Architecture
description:
A two-year graduate-entry master's for people who hold a Bachelor of Architecture or an equivalent design degree with a credit average in studio work; a strong portfolio can support an application with lower grades. It is accredited by the Architects Accreditation Council of Australia, and completing it after an accredited bachelor's degree covers the qualifying steps toward registration as an architect.

Four major design studios sit at the core, several taught with practising architects and built around live projects, with electives in areas such as heritage, technology and research. Canberra itself, a planned capital, is used as a design case study. It suits architecture graduates who need the accredited master's to register and want a focus on contemporary urban architecture.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in architecture or a related built-environment field (typically following an accredited bachelor's degree) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Building and Construction Information Management
description: A two-year, 48 credit point postgraduate degree in Building Information Modelling and digital construction management, taught on campus at the Bruce campus. The structure runs from an introduction to BIM and BIM technology through procurement, project management and research methods to a 12 credit point professional thesis, with graduate certificate and graduate diploma exit points along the way. Students use the University of Canberra BIM Hub, which has VR and AR facilities, 3D laser scanners and industry modelling software. Entry normally requires an undergraduate qualification in architecture, construction, engineering or a related field, with recognition of prior learning available for applicants with several years of relevant work experience. Graduates work as BIM managers and coordinators, digital engineers, project managers and design managers across architecture, construction and infrastructure. It suits built-environment professionals moving into the coordination and data side of projects.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in construction management, architecture, engineering or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
UC frames its MBA around the fact that Canberra is the seat of national government as much as a business centre, pitching the degree at professionals moving into executive roles across corporate, government and not-for-profit sectors alike. The core 12-unit structure covers strategy, finance, marketing, economics and people management, and finishes with a substantive research or consulting project rather than a conventional exam.

An MBA (Plus) variant is available for students who want to go deeper in one functional area (human resource management, marketing, or international business) by adding four specialised units on top of the core program.

Work Integrated Learning is built into the online delivery model too: rather than a single internship, students work through applied projects set by real organisations, which UC positions as giving graduates a portfolio of demonstrated outcomes for job interviews rather than just a transcript.
curriculum:
Core units: Managing People and Organisations; Accounting for Managers; Economics for Managers; Marketing Management; Strategic Management; Business Law and Ethics; Financial Management; Operations and Supply Chain Management; Managing in a Global Environment; Business Analytics
Applied component: Work Integrated Learning consulting project with an external organisation
Capstone: MBA Research Project or Strategic Management capstone
MBA (Plus) pathway: additional four specialisation units chosen from Human Resource Management, Marketing, or International Business streams
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree plus at least 2-3 years of relevant professional work experience (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Business Informatics
description: The University of Canberra's Master of Business Informatics is a two-year, 48 credit point conversion degree that sits across business and information technology, for graduates from any field: no prior IT or business informatics study is assumed. The core covers systems analysis, IT security, aligning technology with business needs and a capstone research project, and students choose one focus from no specialisation, Cybersecurity, Data Science or Project Management. Applicants with relevant work experience can enter through the Professional Pathway. The qualification is recognised by the Australian Computer Society at Professional level, which supports ICT career mobility including overseas. Graduates work as business analysts, IT security analysts, data scientists, systems architects and IT project managers. It suits career changers and recent graduates who want a technology qualification that stays connected to how organisations actually use IT, rather than a pure computer science degree.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); no prior IT or business informatics study is assumed, with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Clinical Psychology
description:
A highly selective two-year master's (48 credit points) covering the Level 3 and 4 graduate competencies set by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council, combining coursework, 1,000 hours of supervised placement across four rotations, and a three-part research project ending in a capstone.

Early placements run in UC's student-led health clinic, later ones across the lifespan in external services. Graduates are eligible for general registration as a psychologist and entry to the registrar program for clinical endorsement through AHPRA. Entry requires a four-year APAC-accredited psychology sequence, usually honours, completed within the last decade with at least 75 percent in the final year, plus eligibility for provisional registration. Shortlisted applicants are interviewed, and Commonwealth-supported places are limited and awarded on merit.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in psychology (typically an APAC-accredited honours degree), highly competitive limited-entry program (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Master of Communication
description:
A two-year master's (48 credit points) with seven core units on politics, communication trends and research methods, a restricted set of electives, and one specialisation of five units in strategic communication, marketing, journalism, or digital marketing.

It is open to graduates of any discipline, and applicants with a related degree can receive up to 12 credit points of advanced standing, shortening the program to about 18 months. A 180-hour internship is built into the curriculum, with placements in agencies, PR firms, government departments and non-profits, in Australia or overseas, which is a real advantage given Canberra's concentration of government communication and public affairs work. It suits people moving toward senior roles in strategic communication, brand and marketing, or journalism.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); a related degree attracts up to 12 credit points of advanced standing.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Counselling
description: The University of Canberra's Master of Counselling is a part-time, 36 credit point degree delivered mostly online over about two years, with 12 study blocks. It combines counselling theory and skills with supervised practice: 200 hours of placement in an approved agency plus a compulsory five-day in-person intensive. Students should expect to travel for placement, and regional students may need to relocate if they cannot secure one locally. Entry is open to graduates from any discipline. The course is accredited by the Australian Counselling Association, so it supports the pathway toward professional registration and membership as a counsellor. Graduates work in mental health services, community organisations, employee assistance programs, schools and private practice. It suits people moving into counselling from another career who want a recognised qualification with a substantial supervised practice component.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Creative Industries
description:
The University of Canberra's Master of Creative Industries is a deliberately flexible two-year degree (48 credit points) that students shape around their own goals, with core units, a specialisation in digital marketing, creative leadership, design, or heritage materials conservation, a wide elective pool spanning marketing, UX, entrepreneurship and creative business finance, and a work-integrated learning or research component.

The industry element can be an internship, a research project or a work-based project done with a partner or at the student's own workplace. Entry is a bachelor's degree in any field, with credit for relevant graduate certificates and a professional pathway for experienced applicants. It runs on campus, online or blended, and suits people moving into leadership and business roles across the creative and cultural sector.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any field (or equivalent); credit for relevant graduate certificates and a professional pathway for experienced applicants.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Data Science
description:
The Master of Data Science is a two-year, full-time program built around a flexible 12-credit-point core rather than a rigid unit list: students can mix and match from units like Business Intelligence Systems, Database Systems, Artificial Intelligence Techniques, Soft Computing, Data Analytics and Business Intelligence, and Computer Vision and Image Analysis, unless they want a named specialisation printed on their testamur.

Three specialisation tracks are on offer: Sports Analytics, Business Intelligence, and Artificial Intelligence and Computational Modelling. Sports Analytics is a distinctly UC offering, drawing on the same AIS and elite-sport connections that shape the university's exercise science program, applied here to performance data rather than physiology.

Work Integrated Learning is again a required element rather than an optional extra, with students applying data science methods to a real industry problem before graduating. UC pitches this as the point of difference against more theory-heavy data science masters elsewhere.
curriculum:
Foundation units: Database Systems (PG); Statistics for Data Science; Programming for Data Science
Core/elective pool (12cp, mix per specialisation): Business Intelligence Systems; Artificial Intelligence Techniques; Soft Computing; Data Analytics and Business Intelligence; Computer Vision and Image Analysis; Data Science Technology and Systems; Econometrics
Specialisation tracks (optional, for testamur notation): Sports Analytics; Business Intelligence; Artificial Intelligence and Computational Modelling
Applied component: Work Integrated Learning industry data project
Capstone: Data Science Research Project or Industry Project
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in a quantitative discipline (or equivalent); some programming or statistics background expected.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Education
description: The University of Canberra's Master of Education is a 24 credit point degree for people who already work in education, completed fully online over about 17 months with intakes every two months and one unit at a time. It is not an initial teaching qualification: entry requires current teacher registration, or a three-year education degree plus three years of professional experience. Students take a generalist path or specialise in STEM Education or Educational Leadership, with graduate certificate exit points in either. The coursework centres on analysing education theory, policy and curriculum and building reflective practice. Graduates move into roles such as curriculum coordinator, head of department, instructional leader, student wellbeing lead and deputy principal. It suits practising teachers and school leaders who want a flexible research-informed qualification to support progression, rather than a route into the classroom.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in education or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Education Studies
description: The University of Canberra's Master of Education Studies is a two-year, 48 credit point degree for people who want to work on policy, curriculum and leadership rather than classroom teaching. One thing to be clear on: it is not externally accredited and is not recognised as a teaching qualification in Australia, so it does not lead to teacher registration. The structure is five core units, 27 credit points of electives and a 6 credit point capstone project, with work integrated learning and authentic assessment built through the degree. Study covers research methods, international policy trends and evidence-based program design. Entry is open to people with a three-year education degree, a bachelor's plus an education diploma, or equivalent professional experience. Graduates work as curriculum developers, policy advisers, educational researchers and senior school and sector leaders. It suits education professionals building toward leadership and policy roles.
admission_requirements: A three-year education degree, a bachelor's degree plus an education diploma, or equivalent professional experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Educational Leadership and Management
description: The University of Canberra's Master of Educational Leadership and Management is a one-year, 24 credit point degree, available on campus or blended, made up of eight units covering leadership and management theory, organisational change, comparative education and educational futures, and ending with a research project. Entry requires a bachelor's degree plus at least three years of relevant experience in education or public administration, and IELTS 6.5 for international applicants. It is aimed squarely at people already working in education who are moving toward formal leadership: aspiring and current principals, deputy principals, education officers and administrators. Graduates work as school and system leaders, district and sector administrators and early childhood directors. It suits mid-career educators who want a focused, one-year leadership qualification rather than a broader two-year master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in education, with relevant teaching/leadership experience (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Engineering
description:
A two-year graduate-entry master's (48 credit points) with a network engineering focus, covering the design, development and operation of networking systems. Entry requires a four-year engineering degree, a three-year Engineers Australia accredited technologist degree, or a UC degree in IT, software engineering or a relevant science major, with assumed knowledge in ICT and basic programming.

The course includes 450 hours of work-integrated learning and a two-part capstone that delivers a real engineering solution for a business, government or community client. UC states it will pursue accreditation with Engineers Australia at professional engineer level and with the Australian Computer Society, so applicants should confirm the current accreditation status before enrolling. It suits engineering and computing graduates moving into network engineering, ICT security engineering, IoT or IT project roles.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in engineering or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Information Sciences (Research)
description: A research master's in the information sciences at the University of Canberra, two years full-time (up to six years maximum), worth 48 credit points: a 30 credit point thesis, 6 credit points of research methodology and proposal work, and 12 credit points of approved coursework. Research spans statistics, mathematics, information systems, business informatics, network and software engineering and artificial intelligence, supervised by academics in those areas. Entry requires a bachelor's degree in information sciences at credit level or equivalent, plus evidence of research capacity. Domestic students are typically covered by a Research Training Program fee offset. Graduates continue to doctoral study or move into research and specialist technical roles. It suits computing and IT graduates who want a research qualification or a route into a PhD.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree with honours (or equivalent) in a related field, and an approved research proposal with confirmed supervisor availability.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Information Technology
description: The University of Canberra Master of Information Technology and Systems is a transition master for graduates from any discipline, assuming no prior IT knowledge. It runs two years full-time, to a maximum of six years, with specialisations in Cybersecurity and in AI and Machine Learning, each 18 credit points, plus flexible unit choice and exit awards of a graduate certificate or graduate diploma. Work-integrated learning is built in, giving students real or work-like placements and professional connections. Entry requires an Australian bachelor degree in any field or equivalent, confident desktop-computer use, and strong spoken and written English. Indicative international tuition is around A$38,000 per year. Graduates enter information technology roles across industry, government and research.

name: Master of Information Technology and Systems
description:
A two-year master's (48 credit points) that takes graduates from any field into IT, so no prior computing study is assumed. Thirty credit points of core cover introductory IT, systems analysis and modelling, professional practice, research methods and a technology capstone research project; the remaining 18 form one specialisation from cybersecurity, AI and machine learning, cloud computing and IoT, data science, or a general track.

It is fully accredited at professional level by the Australian Computer Society, and work-integrated learning places students with organisations, which matters in Canberra given the size of the federal government technology workforce. Delivery is flexible across weekday, evening, blended and online options. It suits career changers moving into roles such as systems analyst, cybersecurity specialist, data analyst or IT manager.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (extended IT conversion program for non-cognate graduates) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of International Development
description:
A two-year master's (48 credit points: 30 required, 12 restricted-choice, 6 elective) covering sustainable development, gender and development, humanitarian intervention, global health, and the planning, monitoring and evaluation of development projects.

The nine-credit-point Development Research Project lets students investigate a real initiative, often tied to their current job, with past work examining programs in Papua New Guinea, Indonesia, Mexico and Pakistan. Entry is a bachelor's degree in any field, with a professional pathway for people with relevant experience, and holders of a graduate certificate or diploma in the field receive credit. Being in Canberra puts students near DFAT and the aid and NGO sector. It suits people heading into roles as program managers, monitoring and evaluation officers, gender advisers or development consultants.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any field (or equivalent), with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience; holders of a graduate certificate or diploma in the field receive credit.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Medical Imaging
description:
The University of Canberra's Master of Medical Imaging is an accelerated graduate-entry degree that compresses a normal three-year radiography qualification into 2.5 years. Entry is a bachelor's degree in any field with a credit average plus at least two degree-level units of anatomy and physiology, with introductory physics, psychology and statistics assumed, and IELTS 7.0 in every band.

It is an approved program of study with the Medical Radiation Practice Board of Australia, so graduates can apply for registration as a diagnostic radiographer. Clinical training is substantial: four five-week placement blocks and two 13-week residencies across general radiography, CT, MRI, mammography and ultrasound, after practising on campus equipment first. It suits graduates changing career into diagnostic imaging who want the fastest registrable route.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in any discipline with a credit average, including at least two degree-level units in anatomy and physiology; introductory physics, psychology and statistics are assumed knowledge. IELTS 7.0 with no band below 7.0.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Master of Nursing Practice (Graduate Entry)
description:
A two-year graduate-entry nursing degree for people who already hold a bachelor's degree in any discipline and want to become a registered nurse. It is taught in intensive theory blocks supported by online content and interspersed with clinical placements.

Students complete 800 hours of supervised clinical practice across settings including medical and surgical wards, emergency, intensive care, paediatrics and aged care, at Canberra Hospital and regional NSW facilities. The course is accredited by ANMAC and approved by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, so graduates are eligible to apply for registration as a nurse through AHPRA. Entry requires a completed degree with a credit average finished within the last ten years, IELTS 7.0, and the usual immunisation, police and first-aid clearances. It suits career changers committed to clinical nursing.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (graduate-entry pathway to nursing registration) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 with no band below 7.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL), reflecting the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia English requirement.

name: Master of Nutrition and Dietetics
description:
A two-year master's (48 credit points) that qualifies graduates as an Accredited Practising Dietitian through Dietitians Australia, a credential recognised internationally. Year one is eight units of clinical, community and research content; year two is almost entirely placement.

Students complete up to 24 weeks of full-time workplace education across hospitals, community health services and food service settings, plus an additional four-week internship that UC builds in for networking and job-seeking. Entry is demanding: a bachelor's degree in human nutrition plus specific degree-level study in chemistry, human biology and physiology, biochemistry, and food and nutrition science, and IELTS 7.0 with no band below 7.0. It suits nutrition graduates set on clinical and community dietetics practice, with a stated emphasis on ageing populations.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree with specific degree-level study in chemistry, human biology and physiology, biochemistry, and food and nutrition science. Highly competitive limited-entry program. IELTS 7.0 with no band below 7.0.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Master of Occupational Therapy
description:
The University of Canberra's Master of Occupational Therapy is a two-year graduate-entry degree, starting in Semester 2, open to graduates of any discipline with a credit average. Students complete 1,000 hours of practical education in hospitals, clinics, community organisations, schools and aged care, locally and interstate, with placements run full-time and travel and accommodation at the student's expense.

The degree is accredited by the Occupational Therapy Council of Australia and approved by the World Federation of Occupational Therapists, so graduates can apply for registration with the Occupational Therapy Board of Australia and have their qualification recognised in many other countries. Entry requires IELTS 7.0 with no band below 7.0, a police check, Working with Vulnerable People registration, immunisation records, and first aid and CPR. It suits graduates committed to enabling people with disability, injury or age-related limitation to take part in daily life.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in any discipline with a credit (65%) or higher average (or equivalent). Limited-entry program; places are offered on academic merit and meeting the requirements does not guarantee a place. Anatomy and physiology are taught within the course.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Master of Optometry
description:
A two-year graduate-entry master's open specifically to graduates of UC's Bachelor of Vision Science. It is accredited by the Optometry Council of Australia and New Zealand, and completing both degrees makes graduates eligible to apply for registration as an optometrist with the Optometry Board of Australia, including autonomous prescribing of ocular therapeutics.

Clinical placements are full-time and generally involve interstate travel at the student's own cost, and students buy a set of specialist equipment (around A$5,000) before placement. It suits Vision Science students continuing straight through to clinical qualification, with graduates working in private practice, hospitals, community eye care and research.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in vision science or a related field, highly competitive limited-entry program (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Master of Pharmacy
description:
The University of Canberra's Master of Pharmacy is a two-year graduate-entry degree for people who already hold a bachelor's degree in any field with a credit average and have completed one unit in five of six sciences: chemistry, biochemistry, microbiology, anatomy, physiology and pharmacology.

It is fully accredited by the Australian Pharmacy Council, so graduates can go on to the supervised internship year that leads to registration as a pharmacist. Placements include two-week blocks in community and hospital pharmacies over the winter periods plus shorter placements through each teaching semester, with the usual police, immunisation and Working with Vulnerable People clearances. It suits career changers who want to become pharmacists without repeating a four-year undergraduate degree.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in any discipline with a credit or higher average, including at least one degree-level unit in five of the six disciplines: chemistry, biochemistry, microbiology, anatomy, physiology and pharmacology. Limited-entry program offered on academic merit.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Master of Physiotherapy
description:
The University of Canberra's Master of Physiotherapy is a two-year graduate-entry degree (48 credit points) for people who hold a health science bachelor's degree with a credit average and prior study in musculoskeletal and functional anatomy, exercise physiology and biomechanics.

Clinical education is four five-week full-time placements spanning acute care, rehabilitation and aged care. Placements are full-time only and typically require interstate travel at the student's own cost. The course is accredited by the Australian Physiotherapy Council, and graduates are eligible to apply for registration as a physiotherapist through AHPRA. It suits health graduates, often from exercise or sport science, who want the fastest accredited route into physiotherapy practice rather than a four-year undergraduate degree.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in exercise science, health science or a related field, highly competitive limited-entry program (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Master of Primary Teaching
description:
A two-year graduate-entry teaching degree for people whose bachelor's degree includes at least one year of full-time study relevant to a primary curriculum learning area. It is registered by the ACT Teacher Quality Institute and recognised as a teaching qualification across Australia.

Students complete 60 days of supervised professional experience in Canberra partner schools and must pass a moderated Teaching Performance Assessment to graduate, as well as both parts of the LANTITE literacy and numeracy test. All applicants attend a suitability interview (CASPI). The English requirement for entry and for later registration is high: IELTS 7.5 overall with 8.0 in speaking and listening. It suits graduates moving into primary teaching who can evidence relevant prior study.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (graduate-entry pathway to primary teaching registration) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.5 with 8.0 in speaking and listening and no band below 7.0 (or equivalent), reflecting the teacher-registration English requirement.

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description:
The University of Canberra's Master of Professional Accounting is a two-year conversion degree (48 credit points) taught on the Bruce campus, accredited by both CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, so graduates meet the academic entry requirement for the CPA and CA ANZ professional programs.

Thirteen core units cover accounting systems, corporate and management accounting, business finance and auditing, with electives in areas such as risk management, entrepreneurship and revenue law, plus a capstone that can be a research project, an industry project or an internship. It is built for career changers with a non-accounting degree and for internationally trained accountants seeking Australian recognition; applicants who already hold an accounting major from an Australian university are not eligible. No prior accounting study or work experience is required to enter.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); no prior accounting study is required.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Public Health
description:
An 18-month master's (36 credit points), with 27 points of required study covering epidemiology, biostatistics, health economics, health promotion, ecological public health, policy, and a research project, and 9 points of electives in areas such as communicable disease control, global health, Indigenous health and program evaluation.

Work placements and applied research projects are available through the elective units, with students working alongside UC Health Research Institute staff and partners in government, NGOs and community organisations. Being based in Canberra puts students close to the federal health department and national agencies. Entry is a completed bachelor's degree, with admission on academic merit and some basic biostatistics knowledge assumed. It suits clinical and non-clinical health workers moving into public health officer, policy, health promotion or community health roles.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in health science, medicine, nursing or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Public Policy
description:
UC's Master of Public Policy is delivered fully online and built from 12 core units, each running on a compressed seven-week cycle rather than a standard semester; the university advises 15-20 hours of study per week, which lets motivated students finish in as little as two years while working full time.

The content is explicitly applied rather than theoretical: policy analysis, economic modelling, data analytics and program evaluation sit alongside more traditional units on the machinery of government. Being based in the national capital gives UC's politics and public policy staff direct lines into Commonwealth departments and agencies, which shows up in guest contributions and case material drawn from actual ACT and federal policy processes rather than generic international examples.

The degree sits within a nested suite (Graduate Certificate, Graduate Diploma and Master), so students can exit early with a lower award or step up into the full Master of Public Policy depending on how their circumstances change during study.
curriculum:
Core units (12 x 7-week blocks): Foundations of Public Policy; The Policy Process; Public Sector Economics; Policy Analysis and Evaluation; Government and Governance; Data Analytics for Policy; Program Evaluation; Public Finance and Budgeting; Regulation and Policy Instruments; Comparative Public Policy; Strategic Policy Leadership; Applied Policy Project
Exit points: Graduate Certificate in Public Policy (4 units); Graduate Diploma in Public Policy (8 units); Master of Public Policy (12 units)
Capstone: Applied Policy Project addressing a real government or public-sector problem
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (or equivalent); relevant government/public-sector experience well regarded.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Research
description: A research master's at the University of Canberra, 18 months full-time (up to three years part-time), worth 36 credit points: 27 on the thesis and 9 on coursework in research methodology, ethics and data analysis. It is available across disciplines through the Graduate Research School and is explicitly designed as preparation for a PhD, while also standing alone as a qualification. Entry is open to holders of a bachelor's, honours or graduate qualification in any field, subject to supervision being available for the topic. Graduates move into research roles in academia, government, industry and the not-for-profit sector, or continue to doctoral study. It suits graduates who want supervised research training and a completed thesis before committing to a PhD.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree with honours (or equivalent), and an approved research proposal with confirmed supervisor availability.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Secondary Teaching
description:
A two-year graduate-entry secondary teaching degree. Entry requires a bachelor's degree with a major in a school teaching area such as English, mathematics, science, a language, humanities and social sciences, health and physical education, technologies, or creative and performing arts, with a second teaching area preferred.

Students complete 60 days of supervised placement in Canberra region secondary schools, pass a Teaching Performance Assessment, and pass both components of the LANTITE test. All applicants sit a suitability interview (CASPI), and the English requirement is IELTS 7.5 with 8.0 in speaking and listening. The course is registered by the ACT Teacher Quality Institute and recognised nationally. It suits graduates with a strong discipline background who want to teach years 7 to 12.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in a discipline relevant to a secondary teaching specialisation (graduate-entry pathway to secondary teaching registration) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.5 with 8.0 in speaking and listening and no band below 7.0 (or equivalent), reflecting the teacher-registration English requirement.

name: Master of Social Work (Qualifying)
description:
The University of Canberra's Master of Social Work (Qualifying) is a three-year qualifying degree (16 study blocks) for graduates who hold a bachelor's degree in a related field such as psychology, allied health, counselling, education or sociology, with prior study in social science and human behaviour. It is delivered online, with in-person attendance required only for placement.

Students complete 1,000 hours of field education across two supervised placements. The program is undergoing provisional accreditation with the Australian Association of Social Workers rather than holding full accreditation, which applicants should weigh, since AASW eligibility is what allows practice as an accredited social worker. Recognition of prior learning of up to 25 percent is available to social welfare and community services graduates. It suits career changers moving into aged care, disability, child and family, mental health, justice or policy work.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (qualifying pathway to social work registration) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Speech Pathology
description:
A two-year graduate-entry master's for people who already hold a bachelor's or postgraduate degree in any field with a credit average. It has full accreditation from Speech Pathology Australia, so graduates are eligible for practising membership and can work as speech pathologists across Australia.

Clinical placements run four days a week at health and education sites including the UC Health Precinct and regional and remote locations. The course is framed around producing researcher-practitioners and builds in substantial research training alongside clinical work in speech, language, swallowing and communication disorders across all age groups. The English requirement is unusually high at IELTS 8.0 with no band below 8.0, alongside police, immunisation and Working with Vulnerable People checks.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline, highly competitive limited-entry program (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 8.0 with no band below 8.0 (or equivalent), reflecting the Speech Pathology Australia English requirement.

name: Master of Sport and Exercise Science (Research)
Master of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL) & Foreign Language Teaching (FLT)
description: The University of Canberra's Master of TESOL and Foreign Language Teaching is a two-year, 48 credit point degree in teaching English to speakers of other languages and foreign language teaching, delivered in blended mode. The coursework covers second language acquisition, TESOL and language teaching methodology, curriculum and assessment, and includes a work integrated learning component of at least 60 hours with Working with Vulnerable People registration required for the practice unit. No prior teaching qualification or experience is required to enter, only a completed bachelor's degree. Note that registration to teach in Australian schools is a separate process and applicants who want school registration should confirm the current requirements with the ACT Teacher Quality Institute. Graduates work as English language teachers, language teachers, adult and community educators, curriculum advisers and in international education. It suits people moving into language teaching from another background.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in a related field (relevant for practising or aspiring language educators) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Professional Doctorate in Business Administration (Research)
description: A professional doctorate in business at the University of Canberra, four years full-time (up to eight years part-time), worth 96 credit points: 24 of coursework in research fundamentals, literature review and research design in year one, then a 72 credit point thesis. It differs from a PhD by building in work-integrated learning and centring on professional practice, with candidates using their existing workplace expertise to investigate a real business problem. Entry requires about five years of senior professional practice plus a relevant master's or honours qualification at credit level. Research can sit in accounting, management, economics, human resource development or organisational behaviour. Graduates move into executive and senior advisory roles. It suits experienced managers who want a doctorate focused on applied, workplace-relevant research.
admission_requirements: A relevant master's degree (e.g. MBA) plus substantial senior management/professional experience and an approved research proposal.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: UC Connect
description: A short enabling pathway for people who have recently finished Year 12 in Australia or completed a Certificate III but do not quite meet the entry requirements for their preferred University of Canberra degree. It runs about 16 teaching weeks (18 weeks including exams and a break) at roughly nine hours a week, building academic writing, research and study skills. Australian and New Zealand citizens and permanent residents are eligible for a Commonwealth Supported enabling place, meaning the government covers the program fee. On successful completion, students gain a pathway into a UC undergraduate degree. It suits recent school leavers who just missed direct entry.
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 11 (or equivalent secondary schooling); designed as an alternative entry pathway into UC bachelor's degrees for students who do not yet meet direct-entry ATAR requirements.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.0-5.5 (no band below 5.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 35-46, PTE 30-42), depending on the specific stream.
intake_dates: February, July (rolling entry also available for some streams)

name: UC Preparation Scheme
description: A part-time enabling pathway delivered by UC College for mature-age people who finished school more than two years ago, have been away from study, or want to retrain or move into para-professional work. Classes run about four hours a week across two sessions at the Bruce campus, building the academic writing, reading and study skills needed for university. Applicants must be Australian or New Zealand citizens or permanent residents and aged over 19. On successful completion it provides a pathway into a University of Canberra undergraduate degree. It suits adult learners returning to formal study who want a supported, low-intensity start.
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 11 (or equivalent secondary schooling); designed as an alternative entry pathway into UC bachelor's degrees for students who do not yet meet direct-entry ATAR requirements.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.0-5.5 (no band below 5.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 35-46, PTE 30-42), depending on the specific stream.
intake_dates: February, July (rolling entry also available for some streams)

name: Undergraduate Certificate in Education
description: The University of Canberra's Undergraduate Certificate in Education is a short qualification worth a year of study, aimed at education support staff and people considering a teaching career who want a formal entry point. It covers foundational ideas in learning, child development and classroom practice. It is not a teaching qualification and does not lead to registration; graduates who want to teach go on to a full initial teacher education degree, into which this certificate can provide credit and a pathway. It suits teacher aides and career explorers who want a supported, credentialled first step.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); satisfactory National Police Certificate required prior to professional placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: University of Canberra International Foundation Studies
description: A one-year pre-university course delivered by UC College at the Bruce campus for international students who have completed the equivalent of Year 11 but do not meet direct entry to a University of Canberra bachelor's degree. The curriculum is pitched at Australian Year 12 level: 12 units across English, mathematics, technology and humanities and society, worth 36 credit points over three terms, developing both English proficiency and university study skills. Entry requires IELTS 5.5 with no band below 5.0 and a minimum age of 17. On successful completion, students gain entry into the first year of most UC undergraduate degrees. It suits international students who need a recognised foundation year before starting university in Australia.
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 11 (or equivalent secondary schooling) for international students seeking an alternative pathway into a UC bachelor's degree.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.5 (no band below 5.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 46, PTE 42).
intake_dates: February, July (multiple intakes for some streams)

name: Advanced Diploma in Theology and Ministry
Bachelor of Counselling
description:
The Bachelor of Counselling sits a little apart from the rest of the University of Divinity's catalogue, which is otherwise almost entirely theology and ministry. This is a professional counselling degree, though it's taught within a university whose identity and college network are explicitly Christian, and several of its member colleges (Whitley College, Eastern College Australia among them) fold a pastoral or values-based counselling orientation into the training rather than treating it as incidental.

Students complete core counselling theory, ethics and practice units alongside supervised placement hours, working toward eligibility for professional counselling registration in Australia (typically ACA or PACFA-aligned pathways depending on the specific college and cohort). The counselling degree exists partly because chaplaincy, pastoral care and church-based welfare work are common destinations for University of Divinity graduates broadly, and a dedicated counselling qualification lets students formalise that pastoral instinct into a registrable clinical skill set.

Graduates go into private practice, community and church-based counselling services, and pastoral care roles in hospitals, schools and aged care, often building on a values framework that's more explicit here than in a secular counselling degree elsewhere.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Counselling Theory, Human Development, Communication Skills, Ethics in Counselling
Year 2: Counselling Practice and Techniques, Family and Relationship Counselling, Trauma-Informed Practice, supervised placement I
Year 3: Group Work and Facilitation, Counselling in Faith and Community Contexts, advanced supervised placement, capstone case study portfolio
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Ministry
description:
The Bachelor of Ministry is the more vocationally focused sibling of the Bachelor of Theology: same three-year, four-field structure (Humanities, Biblical Studies, Christian Thought and History, and Theology: Mission and Ministry), but weighted harder toward the Mission and Ministry strand and toward practical placement, aimed squarely at students heading into lay ministry, youth or community ministry, or pastoral leadership roles that don't require the extended academic and language training built into a Master of Divinity.

Students complete it through one of the University of Divinity's member colleges, and many are already working in a church or parachurch role while studying part-time, which the degree structure accommodates: it can stretch to nine years part-time, the same maximum as the Bachelor of Theology.

It functions as a practical entry point into vocational ministry for people who know their calling is hands-on pastoral and community work rather than academic theology, without foreclosing the option of moving on to a Master of Divinity or Master of Theology later.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Old Testament, Introduction to New Testament, Foundations of Christian Ministry, Humanities elective
Year 2: Pastoral Care and Ministry Practice, Christian Thought and History unit, supervised ministry placement I
Year 3: Leadership in Ministry Contexts, advanced Mission and Ministry electives, capstone ministry placement and reflective portfolio
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); typically undertaken alongside a church/ministry placement
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Theology
description:
The Bachelor of Theology is the University of Divinity's foundational undergraduate degree, but "the university" here is a loose word for what's actually a federation: students enrol through one of the constituent colleges (Catholic Theological College, Pilgrim Theological College, Ridley College, Whitley College and others spanning Anglican, Baptist, Catholic, Lutheran, Uniting Church and Salvation Army traditions) rather than a single central campus, and take classes structured around four fields: Humanities, Biblical Studies, Christian Thought and History, and Theology: Mission and Ministry.

That federated structure is the actual selling point, not a bureaucratic quirk. A Bachelor of Theology student can end up studying alongside seminarians from a different denomination entirely, taught by faculty formed in a different tradition, in a way that a single-denomination bible college simply can't replicate. The university has described itself as one of the more sustained ecumenical experiments in Australian higher education, going back over a century to its 1910 founding as the Melbourne College of Divinity.

The three-year, full-time degree suits people heading toward ministry, chaplaincy, religious education or further postgraduate theological study, and it can be completed over as long as nine years part-time, which matters given how many students are already working in parish or pastoral roles while they study.
curriculum:
Field of study across the degree: Biblical Studies (Old and New Testament units), Christian Thought and History (patristics through to modern theology), Theology: Mission and Ministry, Humanities electives
Year 1: Introduction to Old Testament, Introduction to New Testament, Introduction to Christian Thought, foundational Humanities unit
Year 2: further Biblical Studies units, Church History, Ethics, a Mission and Ministry practicum unit
Year 3: advanced electives across the four fields, capstone unit chosen in consultation with the student's college
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Diploma in Theology
description:
The Diploma in Theology is the University of Divinity's entry-level credential, shorter than the three-year bachelor degrees and pitched at students testing whether formal theological study suits them, those wanting a foundational qualification for a church or parachurch role without a full degree commitment, or students planning to build credit toward a Bachelor of Theology or Bachelor of Ministry later; completed units typically count toward the bachelor's degree if a student decides to continue.

It draws on the same four-field structure as the university's bachelor degrees (Humanities, Biblical Studies, Christian Thought and History, and Mission and Ministry), just compressed into a shorter, more introductory sequence, and like the rest of the university's offerings it's delivered through one of the constituent colleges rather than a single central faculty.

Graduates commonly move into entry-level church ministry support roles, or use the diploma as a stepping stone into a full bachelor's program once they've confirmed the direction suits them.
curriculum: Introduction to Old Testament, Introduction to New Testament, Introduction to Christian Thought, Foundations of Christian Ministry, one Humanities elective, one further elective chosen from Biblical Studies or Mission and Ministry
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); no prior theological study required
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Doctor of Philosophy (Theology)
description:
The Doctor of Philosophy (Theology) is the University of Divinity's highest research degree and, unlike the coursework-heavy Master of Divinity, it's almost entirely independent research: a substantial thesis supervised by a scholar drawn from one of the constituent colleges, examined externally in the standard Australian PhD model. Candidates work across the university's full theological range: biblical studies, systematic and historical theology, ethics, liturgical studies and practical theology, and supervision is matched to a candidate's specific research question rather than assigned by a single central department, since expertise is distributed across the college network.

What makes doctoral study here distinctive is the ecumenical breadth of supervisory expertise available under one doctoral framework: a candidate researching, say, Catholic sacramental theology and one researching Uniting Church ecclesiology can both be supervised and examined within the same PhD program, drawing on faculty across traditions the university has spent over a century bringing together.

Graduates go into academic theology, senior denominational leadership, and specialist research and teaching roles at seminaries and universities, both in Australia and internationally.
curriculum: Candidature milestones rather than semester units: confirmation of candidature (research proposal and literature review, typically within the first year), annual progress review, thesis writing across candidature (nominally three to four years full-time, longer part-time), final thesis submission and oral or written examination by external examiners
admission_requirements: Master's degree with a strong research component (Honours or equivalent); admission by School of Graduate Research Committee
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 6.5

name: Graduate Diploma in Divinity
description:
The Graduate Diploma in Divinity is a shorter postgraduate credential for students who already hold a bachelor's degree, often but not always in theology, and want structured graduate-level theological formation without committing to the full length of a Master of Divinity. It's a common pathway for people converting a degree in an unrelated field into theological qualification ahead of ministry candidacy, or for graduates of a Bachelor of Theology or Bachelor of Ministry wanting to add a postgraduate credential before deciding whether to pursue the full Master of Divinity.
