Like everything else at the University of Divinity, it's delivered through a specific member college, so the exact mix of units, and how much practical ministry formation is built in versus purely academic content, depends on which college a student enrols with, whether that's a Catholic, Anglican, Uniting Church, Baptist or other tradition-specific institution within the federation.

Many students use it as a stepping stone: credit typically transfers into the Master of Divinity for those who go on to complete it, so the diploma isn't a dead end so much as a shorter first commitment.
curriculum: Core postgraduate units in Biblical Studies and Systematic Theology, Church History, an introductory Pastoral Ministry unit, electives chosen according to the student's college and intended pathway (often credit-bearing toward the Master of Divinity)
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in any discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Divinity
description:
The Master of Divinity is the professional ministry-formation degree at the University of Divinity, and its scale reflects that: 432 points across 18 units, a three-year full-time load that most students actually take considerably longer than three years to finish, since it's the standard qualifying degree for ordained ministry across several of the denominations that make up the university's college federation. It combines academic theological study (biblical languages, systematics, church history) with practical formation units in preaching, pastoral care, liturgy and mission that a purely academic theology degree wouldn't include.

Because students enrol through a specific college rather than a generic university faculty, the Master of Divinity looks noticeably different depending on whether it's taken at, say, a Catholic seminary college or a Baptist or Uniting Church college: denominational formation requirements, placement structures and even which biblical languages are compulsory can vary, even though the degree title and the awarding university are the same.

Graduates are typically heading toward ordination, chaplaincy or vocational ministry leadership, and the degree is usually a prerequisite step in a denomination's own candidacy and formation process rather than a stand-alone academic credential.
curriculum:
Year 1: Biblical Languages (Greek and/or Hebrew), Old and New Testament Studies, Introduction to Systematic Theology, Foundations of Pastoral Ministry
Year 2: Church History, Christian Ethics, Homiletics and Preaching, supervised field education placement
Year 3: Advanced Systematic Theology, Liturgy and Sacramental Theology, Mission and Ministry Practicum, integrative capstone unit tied to denominational formation requirements
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline); designed as professional preparation for ministry
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Theology
description:
The Master of Theology is the university's two-year (240-point, ten-unit) postgraduate research-leaning degree, sitting a level above coursework masters like the Master of Divinity in the amount of independent scholarly work it asks for. Students take it through one of the University of Divinity's member colleges, and the choice of college matters more than it would at a conventional university, since each carries its own denominational library, faculty specialisation and theological emphasis. A student drawn to Catholic sacramental theology and one drawn to Reformed biblical hermeneutics will often end up doing genuinely different degrees under the same university name.

The course typically combines advanced coursework units with a substantial research component, often a minor thesis, and it's commonly taken by clergy and religious professionals seeking to deepen expertise in a specific area: biblical languages, systematic theology, church history, rather than a general theological education, which the Bachelor of Theology or Master of Divinity already cover.

Graduates go on to doctoral study, teaching roles in theological colleges, or senior ministry and denominational leadership positions where advanced theological training is expected.
curriculum:
Year 1: advanced coursework units in the student's chosen specialisation (e.g. Biblical Studies, Systematic Theology, Church History), research methods unit
Year 2: further specialised coursework, minor thesis or major research project, oral presentation of research to college faculty
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in theology or a related field (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall (typical bar for postgrad at private AU providers, approximate)

name: Bachelor of Agriculture
description:
The Bachelor of Agriculture at the University of Melbourne, co-designed with industry, builds a foundation in agricultural science across biology, natural environments and agricultural production, starting with Agriculture Discovery Week at the University's Dookie campus. Students complete 24 subjects over three years, combining eight core subjects with major and elective subjects, along with labs, fieldwork and hands-on experience.
The degree connects to careers spanning farms, finance, fieldwork, policy, business, science and environment, preparing graduates for roles across the agricultural sector and beyond.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
The Bachelor of Arts at the University of Melbourne, ranked first in Australia for arts and humanities, offers a flexible approach to studying the humanities, social sciences and languages. Students choose from more than 40 majors spanning languages, psychology, economics and media and communication, with a multidisciplinary first year building a strong foundation for further study.
Graduates develop career-ready skills in creative and analytical thinking, communication and leadership, with opportunities to build an international perspective through language study and exchange.
curriculum:
Year 1: introductory subjects across two intended majors, plus one breadth subject from outside the arts faculty
Year 2: major sequence subjects deepen (choose from majors including History, Philosophy, English, Politics and International Relations, Psychology, Media and Communications, and area studies), continued breadth requirement
Year 3: capstone subject within the major, remaining major electives, final breadth subject
Breadth subjects (roughly a quarter of the degree) must be taken outside the Faculty of Arts
No formal honours year built in — a separate fourth-year Honours program is available by application for high-achieving students
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 80-90 typically competitive (no specific prerequisites beyond English).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Biomedicine
description:
The Bachelor of Biomedicine at the University of Melbourne immerses students in the Southern hemisphere's largest biomedical precinct, home to more than 40 hospitals, research institutes and biotechnology organisations. Students choose from 16 majors across biomedical disciplines, building knowledge of the body's normal structure and function alongside critical thinking, problem-solving and evidence analysis skills.
Melbourne is ranked first in Australia for life sciences and medicine and for graduate employability. Graduates move into medicine, health sciences and biomedical research careers.
curriculum:
Year 1: Biomolecules and Cells, Genetics and the Evolution of Life, Human Structure and Function, Chemistry for Biomedicine
Year 2: major selection (Cell and Developmental Biology, Human Structure and Function, Immunology, Pathology, Pharmacology, Neuroscience, or others), Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
Year 3: advanced major subjects, research-methods subject, capstone research or laboratory project
Breadth subjects required outside the science faculty, consistent with the wider Melbourne Model structure
Strong emphasis throughout on preparation for graduate-entry professional degrees (MD, Doctor of Dental Surgery, Doctor of Physiotherapy)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 92-97, a common pathway toward Medicine/Dentistry postgraduate entry; prerequisite Units 3/4 Chemistry and Mathematical Methods recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (writing 6.5); PTE Academic 65. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description:
The Bachelor of Commerce at the University of Melbourne, Australia's number one ranked university for business and management, builds a strong foundation in first year through a curated pool of subjects and a compulsory quantitative requirement. Students complete 24 subjects across three years, choosing majors and electives to deepen their commerce knowledge alongside breadth subjects from across the University.
Melbourne commerce graduates are known for their strong understanding of business issues and processes, their resourcefulness, and their problem-solving and leadership skills, moving into challenging and rewarding careers in Australia and overseas.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introductory Microeconomics, Introductory Macroeconomics, Accounting Reports and Analysis, Quantitative Methods, Business Statistics
Year 2: major selection (Accounting, Actuarial Studies, Econometrics, Economics, Finance, Management, Marketing), core major subjects begin
Year 3: advanced major subjects, capstone subject within major, one elective outside the major
Actuarial Studies major carries direct accreditation recognition from the Actuaries Institute
Breadth subjects required outside the Faculty of Business and Economics, per the Melbourne Model structure
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 90-95 typically competitive, plus prerequisite Units 3/4 Mathematics (Any).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Dance (Degree with Honours)
description:
The Bachelor of Fine Arts (Dance) at the Victorian College of the Arts, University of Melbourne, builds on the College's reputation for performance-focused dance education, developing kinetically strong, culturally and conceptually aware dance artists. The three-year, full-time degree centres on studio practice, expanded dance thinking and performance, covering contemporary dance practices, dance science, somatics, critical dance studies and choreography.
New works by professional Australian and international choreographers and repertory studies provide performance experience. Graduates move into careers as performers, choreographers, dance leaders and cultural partners across performance, community and arts management sectors.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Design
description:
The Bachelor of Design at the University of Melbourne develops practical skills and theoretical expertise across cities, buildings, transport networks, furniture, websites and landscapes, with Design Studio classes that mirror real workplace practice from the first semester. Students complete 23 to 24 subjects across 300 credit points, producing their own designs and learning a range of design techniques and thinking approaches.
Graduates apply design thinking across technology, architecture, business and other industries, in a job market where demand for creativity skills has risen sharply in recent years.
curriculum:
Year 1: Design Thinking and Ideas, Visual Communication, Digital Design Tools, common studio project across all design majors
Year 2: major selection (Architecture, Landscape Architecture, Construction Management, Property, Urban Design), studio-based major subjects begin
Year 3: advanced design studios within major, Sustainability in the Built Environment, capstone design project
Studio-based assessment (physical and digital models, design juries) dominates from second year onward
Pathway degree into Melbourne's Master of Architecture or other graduate professional design qualifications
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 80-88; pathway toward Master of Architecture, Landscape Architecture, Urban Planning or Construction Management.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Engineering
description: The University of Melbourne does not offer an undergraduate Bachelor of Engineering. Under the Melbourne Model, students who want to become engineers first complete a three-year bachelor's degree, usually the Bachelor of Science taking an engineering systems major (or the Bachelor of Design for some disciplines), then complete the two- to three-year Master of Engineering, which carries professional accreditation from Engineers Australia. The Bachelor of Science plus Master of Engineering pathway takes about five to six years in total. Prospective engineering students should apply for the Bachelor of Science and choose an engineering-focused major, or the Bachelor of Design. This page is kept for reference because a Bachelor of Engineering still appears in the CRICOS register. International tuition for the Bachelor of Science is around A$50,000 per year.

name: Bachelor of Film and Television (Degree with Honours)
description:
The Bachelor of Fine Arts (Film and Television) at the Victorian College of the Arts, University of Melbourne, develops writer-directors with distinctive creative voices and detailed practical knowledge of all stages of film and television production. The three-year, full-time degree offers production-based, practical filmmaking and screen-based storytelling, with students initiating, developing and realising short film projects in studio and production environments.
Students and graduates win industry awards at festivals including Berlin International, Cannes and the Academy Awards. Graduates move into cinematographer, director, editor, producer and screenwriter roles.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Fine Arts (Honours)
description:
The Bachelor of Fine Arts (Honours) at the University of Melbourne is a one-year program introducing candidates of proven ability to research training, developing critical thinking, creative drive and the capacity to manage a major creative research project. Visual Art students work from The Stables, a contemporary arts research hub, producing work under individual supervision that enters the annual VCA Graduate Exhibition.
Graduates continue into advanced practice or pathways into graduate research programs such as the Master of Fine Arts by Research or Doctor of Philosophy (Fine Arts and Music).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Medical Science (Degree with Honours)
description:
The Bachelor of Medical Science (Degree with Honours) at the University of Melbourne develops skills in interpreting and applying scientific evidence to clinical practice, exploring the design, recording and ethical reporting of clinical research. Students complete 100 credit points across three compulsory subjects: Introduction to Medical Research, Advanced Medical Research, and a Project in Medical Research.
Graduates develop analytical reasoning and problem-solving skills to critically evaluate scholarly evidence, meeting entry requirements for a master's degree or PhD in a relevant discipline.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (writing 6.5); PTE Academic 65. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Music
description:
The Bachelor of Music (Honours) at the University of Melbourne is an intensive, one-year program rounding off undergraduate music study, with specialisations in composition, interactive composition, jazz and improvisation, musicology or ethnomusicology, and performance. Under a supervisor's guidance, students produce a major creative work or series of works and related research, building on and deepening the skills of their chosen specialisation.
The program creates a direct pathway to graduate coursework and research opportunities, including the Master of Music (Research) and Doctor of Philosophy (Fine Arts and Music), or a career as a professional practising artist.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Oral Health
description:
The Bachelor of Oral Health at the University of Melbourne prepares students to register as an oral health therapist, qualified to practise as both a dental therapist and dental hygienist, taught alongside dental students at the Melbourne Dental School. The three-year degree comprises eight compulsory year-long subjects spanning oral health sciences, social sciences and health promotion, and community oral health studies, with hands-on clinical experience in metropolitan and rural placements.
Graduates gain the practical skills to examine, diagnose and treat patients and qualify for registration as a dental practitioner with AHPRA upon graduation.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
The Bachelor of Science at the University of Melbourne offers more than 40 majors across science, engineering, IT and mathematics, with a flexible first year letting students explore before specialising. Students complete 24 subjects over three years, including the discovery subject Today's Science, Tomorrow's World in their first semester, building analytical, technical, practical and theoretical skills.
Graduates move into careers across science, engineering, health and technology, with the flexibility to add a specialisation building complementary expertise.
curriculum:
Year 1: common core across Chemistry, Biology, Physics, and Mathematics, plus breadth subject requirement
Year 2: major selection from a wide list (Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, Genetics, Microbiology and Immunology, Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics and Statistics, Environmental Science, Computing and Software Systems, and others), major core subjects begin
Year 3: advanced major electives, capstone Science Research Project embedded in an active research group
Fourth-year Honours available by application for high-achieving students, often a prerequisite for research higher degrees
Breadth requirement (outside the science faculty) runs across all three years
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 85-93 typically competitive, plus prerequisite Units 3/4 Mathematical Methods.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Science Advanced (Honours)
description: The University of Melbourne's Bachelor of Science Advanced (Honours) is a four-year undergraduate degree with a flexible, student-directed structure supported by the Melbourne curriculum. Students build core scientific knowledge and practical skills across a wide range of fields and specialise once they are ready, with an embedded honours research year. Graduates work across science, research, industry and further study.

name: Diploma in Computing
description:
The Diploma in Computing at the University of Melbourne, open only to students already admitted to another University of Melbourne degree, teaches programming, online solution design and web application development alongside a primary undergraduate degree. Students complete 100 points of specified study, with up to 50 points cross-credited between the diploma and their bachelor's degree, completing two compulsory subjects including COMP10001.
The diploma equips students with IT knowledge valued across finance, economics, biology, engineering, health and communications industries.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Diploma in Languages
description:
The Diploma in Languages at the University of Melbourne, one of five concurrent diplomas available to bachelor's degree students, lets students study one of 12 languages alongside their primary degree, with or without prior language training. Students complete a 100-point program through a proficiency-based progression sequence across three levels, with a mix of compulsory and elective subjects at each stage.
Melbourne is ranked 19th in the world for language study. Graduates gain oral, aural, writing and reading mastery comparable to a language major, alongside cultural understanding of the societies associated with their chosen language.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Diploma in Mathematical Sciences
description:
The Diploma in Mathematical Sciences at the University of Melbourne, open only to students already admitted to another University of Melbourne degree, gives students a mathematics qualification alongside their undergraduate studies. Students specialise in applied mathematics, operations research, pure mathematics, or statistics and stochastic processes, completing up to 50 points of mathematics and statistics subjects alongside their primary degree.
Graduates gain numerical and modelling skills applicable across almost every area of employment, engaging in mathematical discourse across science, industry, technology and commerce.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Diploma in Music (Practical)
description:
The Diploma in Music (Practical) at the University of Melbourne, open only to students already admitted to another University of Melbourne degree, gives students access to the full curriculum at the Melbourne Conservatorium of Music alongside their main studies. Students focus on practical music training with individual instrumental or vocal tuition over a minimum three-year sequence, or complete the equivalent of a major in musicology or ethnomusicology.
Students study alongside Bachelor of Music students, building networks and friendships, and graduate with a music qualification that complements their primary degree or leads toward a music-focused career in education or performance.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Clinical Dentistry
description:
The Doctor of Clinical Dentistry at the University of Melbourne lets general dentists become specialists in a chosen dental field, fully accredited by the Australian Dental Council. Students complete 300 points, with 75 points of core research subjects and 225 points in their chosen specialisation, split roughly 50 per cent clinical training, 20 per cent coursework and 30 per cent research.
Melbourne is ranked first in Australia and 41st in the world for dentistry. Graduates specialise across seven clinical dentistry fields including endodontics, oral medicine, orthodontics, paediatric dentistry, periodontics, prosthodontics and special needs dentistry.
admission_requirements: To be considered for entry into this course, you must: Have completed a bachelor degree (AQF7) or equivalent in a cognate (relevant) discipline. Cognate (relevant) disciplines include: Dentistry or equivalent that qualifies the applicant to register and practice as a Dentist (in their country of origin or residence). And Have two years of documented relevant clinical work experience. And Have demonstrated proof of current dental registration (AHPRA or international equivalent). The University of Melbourne is committed to maintaining a transparent admissions policy by clearly communicating all entry scores to prospective students. Entry requirements to the University of Melbourne are regularly reviewed to ensure they align with the University's Selection and Admissions Policy . The entry requirements published for this course will apply from the start year 2027 intake onwards.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 91; PTE Academic 72. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Dental Surgery
description:
The Doctor of Dental Surgery at the University of Melbourne is a four-year, full-time program preparing students for registration as a general dentist in Australia and New Zealand, with eligibility to apply for certification in Canada. The curriculum integrates foundational scientific knowledge with progressively increasing clinical experience, culminating in a final year predominantly spent in clinical settings.
Melbourne is ranked first in Australia and 41st in the world for dentistry. Graduates are equipped to provide comprehensive oral health care across a variety of settings, supported by modern clinical facilities.
admission_requirements: To be considered for entry into this course, you must have: An undergraduate degree (or equivalent) in any discipline, with studies completed within 10 years of 1 January of the year in which you intend to commence this degree, OR An undergraduate degree (or equivalent) in any discipline AND a graduate diploma, master's degree or PhD (or equivalent) completed within 10 years of 1 January of the year in which you intend to commence this degree. AND Passed prerequisite university subjects * in anatomy, biochemistry and physiology at second year level (or equivalent), with prerequisite subjects to have been taken within 10 years of 1 January of the year in which you intend to commence this degree, AND either: The Graduate Australian Medical School Admissions Test ( GAMSAT ), OR For international students who are located overseas only, one of the following: The United States Dental Admission
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (writing 6.5); PTE Academic 65. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Education
description:
The Doctor of Education at the University of Melbourne is a research doctorate for experienced professionals with educational responsibilities, combining a tailored coursework program with research directly relevant to their professional role. Candidates complete 100 credit points of coursework across four doctoral-level subjects in research design and methodology, plus a 55,000-word thesis comprising a substantial piece of original research, over four years full-time or eight years part-time.
Melbourne's Faculty of Education is ranked first in Australia and 15th in the world, and candidates demonstrate academic leadership and originality in their contribution to knowledge.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Medicine
description:
The Doctor of Medicine at the University of Melbourne is a four-year, full-time course externally accredited by the Australian Medical Council, comprising a year of integrated bioscience and clinical learning, two core clinical training years, discovery subjects for exploring particular interests, and a capstone semester rehearsing the skills needed for safe clinical practice. Students can also complete an immersive research experience.
Melbourne is ranked first in Australia and 20th in the world for medicine. Graduates are eligible to apply for registration with the Medical Board of Australia and move into clinical practice, research, health leadership and education roles.
admission_requirements: To be considered for entry into the Doctor of Medicine via the standard pathway , as an international applicant you must: Have completed a bachelor degree (AQF7) or equivalent in any discipline with studies to have been completed within 10 years of 1 January in the year in which you intend to commence the Doctor of Medicine. Or Have completed a bachelor degree (AQF7) or equivalent in any discipline completed 10 or more years before 1 January of the year in which you intend to commence the Doctor of Medicine. And Have completed a graduate diploma (AQF8) or equivalent in any discipline completed within 10 years before 1 January of the year in which you intend to commence the Doctor of Medicine. And Complete the Graduate Australian Medical Schools Admission Test (GAMSAT) with a minimum of 50 in each section. For international students who are located overseas only, either complete the GAMSA
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 91; PTE Academic 72. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Optometry
description:
The Doctor of Optometry at the University of Melbourne, the first course of its kind in the southern hemisphere, covers the basic and applied optical, visual and biomedical sciences underpinning optometry, fully accredited by the Optometry Council of Australia and New Zealand. Students complete 400 credit points across four years, including a clinically relevant research project and clinical training at metropolitan, rural and overseas sites in the final year.
Melbourne is ranked 14th in the world for life sciences and medicine. Graduates access high employment rates across diverse optometry career pathways.
admission_requirements: To be considered for entry into this course, you must have: an undergraduate degree (or equivalent) with studies to have been completed within 10 years of commencing this degree OR An undergraduate degree (or equivalent) in any discipline completed more than 10 years ago, AND a graduate diploma, master's degree or PhD (or equivalent) completed within 10 years of commencing this degree. Learn more about prerequisite subjects for the Doctor of Optometry . You must also have completed: Three subjects at level two or level three (or equivalent) from one or more relevant biological science disciplines, with subjects to have been completed within 10 years of commencing this degree. Weighted average mark (WAM) While there is no minimum WAM for this course, applicants with a WAM of 65+ are encouraged to apply. The performance of applicants in their previous studies will be assessed using a WAM c
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (writing 6.5); PTE Academic 65. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Agricultural Sciences
description:
The Doctor of Philosophy in Agricultural Sciences at the University of Melbourne requires an 80,000 word thesis under academic supervision, examining a specific problem across soil and plant health, animal health, animal production and welfare, food sciences or agribusiness. Candidates access specialist support including lectures, seminars, writing bootcamps and workshops while making a significant, original contribution to their field.
Melbourne is ranked third in Australia for agriculture and forestry. A PhD is an essential qualification for a research career in agricultural science, with graduates moving into postdoctoral research, academia and industry.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Architecture, Building and Planning
description:
The Doctor of Philosophy (Architecture, Building and Planning) at the Melbourne School of Design is a higher-level research degree for outstanding local and international graduates investigating a specific built environment problem or issue, undertaken as a full dissertation or combined with a creative project. Working under academic supervisors and an advisory committee, candidates progress through structured milestones toward a thesis making a significant contribution to existing knowledge.
Graduates gain an internationally recognised research qualification, with many going on to leading built environment practices in Australia and around the world.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Arts
description:
The Doctor of Philosophy in Arts at the University of Melbourne is the highest arts degree offered by the University, requiring an 80,000 to 100,000 word thesis of independent research that makes a significant, original contribution to an existing area of knowledge. Candidates complete four subjects in their first year, including the Arts PhD Research Intensive and Research Workshop, and access specialist support including three-minute thesis competitions and research leadership programs.
Candidates can specialise across the Graduate School of Humanities and Social Sciences and the Asia Institute. Graduates pursue roles as researchers, academics and subject matter experts.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Business and Economics
Doctor of Philosophy - Education
description:
The Doctor of Philosophy in Education at the University of Melbourne gives doctoral candidates outstanding research training at Australia's leading faculty of education, producing a substantial piece of original research of around 80,000 words with the potential to shape education practice. Candidates present their research findings at a public completion seminar attended by their Advisory Committee, over four years full-time or eight years part-time.
Melbourne's Faculty of Education is ranked first in Australia and 15th in the world. Graduates pursue academia and research leadership as part of the international education scholarly community.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Engineering and IT
description:
The Doctor of Philosophy (Engineering and IT) at the University of Melbourne lets candidates make an original research contribution over four years full-time, supported by experienced supervisors and advisory committees. Candidates complete a thesis of 80,000 to 100,000 words, choosing research projects across biomedical engineering, chemical engineering, computing and information systems, electrical and electronic engineering, infrastructure engineering, or mechanical engineering and mechatronics.
Graduates move into academia and industry, applying specialist knowledge and transferable skills, with access to the Melbourne Accelerator Program for students wanting to commercialise their research.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Fine Arts and Music
description:
The Doctor of Philosophy (Fine Arts and Music) at the University of Melbourne signifies a substantial piece of original research conducted under academic supervision, demonstrating authority in the candidate's field and a thorough grasp of appropriate methodology. Candidates are enrolled in the PhD Research subject for the duration of their candidature, submitting a final project as a written thesis or a combination of creative and written work depending on their discipline, and participating in research seminars and intensive research weekends.
Completion can be a pathway to a career as an academic or professional researcher, developing research skills at the highest level in the candidate's chosen discipline.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Indigenous Knowledge
description:
The Doctor of Philosophy (Indigenous Knowledge) at the University of Melbourne is the first program in Australia to offer studies in Indigenous knowledge as an explicit, interdisciplinary subject area, recognising insights, innovations and practices Indigenous peoples have developed across generations. Candidates complete an innovative research project over 3.5 years full-time, choosing from four thesis formats ranging from an 80,000-word thesis to a 20,000-word thesis with a major folio of work.
The degree deepens engagement and reciprocal learning with Indigenous communities. Graduates go on to postdoctoral research and academic careers, competitive for research funding that benefits Indigenous communities.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Law
description:
The Doctor of Philosophy in Law at the University of Melbourne gives doctoral candidates outstanding research training at Australia's leading law school, supported by an experienced supervisor and Advisory Committee. Candidates produce a thesis demonstrating authority in their field, a thorough grasp of relevant methodology, and the potential to change legal understanding and practice.
Melbourne Law School is ranked first in Australia and eighth globally, home to internationally recognised scholars. Graduates pursue careers in academia, research leadership and legal scholarship.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Medicine, Health Sciences
description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Medicine, Dentistry and Health Sciences at the University of Melbourne is a higher research degree in which candidates undertake a substantial piece of original research reported through a thesis. The submission must be a careful, rigorous and sustained piece of scholarship demonstrating authority in the candidate's field, conducted under academic supervision within a supportive research environment. Research areas span clinical and biomedical disciplines, and the degree takes four years full-time or eight years part-time.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Melbourne Business School
Doctor of Philosophy - Music
description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Music at the University of Melbourne, offered through the Faculty of Fine Arts and Music, signifies that the holder has undertaken a substantial piece of original research conducted and reported under academic supervision in a research environment. The thesis demonstrates authority in the candidate's field and command of knowledge in relevant fields, and may incorporate creative and performance-based research. Candidates study at the Southbank campus over four years full-time or eight years part-time.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Science
description:
The Doctor of Philosophy (Science) at the University of Melbourne lets candidates join one of the University's world-renowned research groups across agriculture, biosciences, chemistry, geography, mathematics, physics and veterinary science, working with more than 500 academic researchers. Candidates complete an 80,000-word thesis over 3.5 years full-time, with regular progress reviews and the option of joint PhD opportunities with partner institutions.
A PhD is an essential qualification for a research career in science and a ticket to international research opportunities. Graduates move into postdoctoral research, academia and industry roles.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Veterinary Science
description:
The Doctor of Philosophy in Veterinary Science at the University of Melbourne requires an 80,000 word thesis under academic supervision, examining a specific problem in veterinary biosciences, animal health and welfare, or infectious diseases and public health biosecurity, making a significant original contribution to the field. Candidates demonstrate command of knowledge, rigorous methodology and the ability to communicate research findings in a professional and international context.
Melbourne is ranked 20th in the world for veterinary science. A PhD is an essential qualification for a research career in science, and many graduates go on to postdoctoral research and academic careers.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Philosophy - Victorian College of the Arts
description:
The Doctor of Philosophy at the Victorian College of the Arts, University of Melbourne, signifies a substantial piece of original research conducted under academic supervision, demonstrating authority in the candidate's field and a thorough grasp of appropriate methodology. Candidates are enrolled in the PhD Research subject for the duration of their candidature, submitting a final project as a written thesis or a combination of creative and written work depending on their discipline.
Candidates participate in research seminars and intensive research weekends, developing research skills at the highest level in their chosen artistic discipline, with completion a pathway to academia or professional research.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Philosophy (Medicine, Dentistry & Health Sciences)
description:
The Doctor of Philosophy (Medicine, Dentistry and Health Sciences) at the University of Melbourne marks a student's admission to the University's community of medicine, dentistry and health sciences scholars, requiring a substantial piece of original research reported via thesis. The normal candidature is three years full-time, with a minimum of 12 months of full-time research completed at the University under academic supervision.
The degree develops academic leadership, independence, creativity and innovation in research work, with the thesis judged on originality and its distinct contribution to knowledge.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (writing 6.5); PTE Academic 65. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Physiotherapy
description:
The Doctor of Physiotherapy at the University of Melbourne builds on the University's history in physiotherapy education and research, developing advanced skills in leadership, pharmacology and management alongside clinical practice. Students gain hands-on experience across major hospitals, community settings and international placements, with graduate attributes mapped across self-knowledge, patient care, the physiotherapy profession, health systems and society.
Melbourne is ranked first in Australia and 13th in the world for anatomy and physiology. Graduates are work-ready and prepared to deliver person-centred care to children, older adults and other priority groups.

name: Doctor of Veterinary Medicine
description:
The Doctor of Veterinary Medicine at the University of Melbourne, Australia's first DVM, gives students hands-on training in purpose-built facilities from day one, with graduates eligible to register in every Australian state and territory, New Zealand and the UK, and to sit the North American licensing exam. The curriculum is built around five learning domains: the scientific basis of clinical practice, ethics and animal welfare, biosecurity and population health, clinical skills, and personal and professional development, with an optional Tracks program for building expertise in a chosen clinical interest.
Melbourne is ranked 20th in the world for veterinary science. Graduates move into private practice, animal welfare and public health roles.

name: Executive Master of Arts
description:
The Executive Master of Arts at the University of Melbourne combines practical career development skills with critical and creative thinking drawn from the humanities, developed in consultation with arts, government, corporate and community sectors. Students choose a 200-point, two-year program of eight compulsory subjects plus capstone and electives, or a 150-point, 1.5-year program for Bachelor of Arts graduates, focused on project management, leadership and people management.
Graduates move into roles including arts program director, business analyst, communications manager, foreign affairs officer, management consultant and public relations manager.

name: Graduate Certificate in Agricultural Sciences
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Agricultural Sciences at the University of Melbourne covers the fundamental and applied science behind sustainable, profitable food and fibre production, preparing graduates for Australia's $61 billion agricultural sector or an international career. Students choose from five specialisations, including agribusiness, animal breeding and welfare, and crop production, developing scientific research literacy alongside written, verbal and visual communication skills.
More than 90 per cent of graduates find employment after completing the course, working across global agricultural boundaries.

name: Graduate Certificate in Arts
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Arts at the University of Melbourne builds a foundation for further study and research, developing the analytical and critical capacities to understand key issues and conceptual frameworks across areas including linguistics, media and communications, and applied research technologies. Students apply these skills to contemporary issues within their chosen area of specialisation.
The course prepares graduates for further postgraduate study or research within the arts and social sciences, building the scholarly foundation used across the Faculty's graduate programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Bushfire Planning and Management
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Bushfire Planning and Management at the University of Melbourne extends existing knowledge of fire's role in the Australian environment, developed alongside industry with two streams: bushfire planning and fire management. Students complete four core subjects across 50 points, combining weekly online lectures with two five-day residentials at the Creswick campus, applying concepts in the field and fire laboratory.
The course is not available to international students requiring a student visa. Graduates move into bushfire risk management, land management, and planning and urban design roles across public and private sectors.

description:
The Graduate Certificate in Educational Research at the University of Melbourne lets students explore educational research methodology and design an educational research project over six months full-time or one year part-time. Two compulsory subjects cover research methodology and a research project, preparing graduates to progress into a Master of Education (Research) with advanced standing, subject to competitive entry.
Melbourne's Faculty of Education is ranked first in Australia and 15th in the world, recognised as a leader in Australian and international education research, with strong professional and industry connections built through the course.

name: Graduate Certificate in Entrepreneurship
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Entrepreneurship at the University of Melbourne is a boutique program taught by academic experts in entrepreneurship and experienced industry entrepreneurs, connecting students with mentors, speakers, investors and incubators. Students complete four compulsory subjects covering entrepreneurial practice, entrepreneurial organisation, managing innovation and building entrepreneurial ventures, including an intensive Winter subject, and can take it full-time or alongside a different master's course.
Graduates build the competence to analyse and evaluate social and business problems and establish their own entrepreneurial venture. Melbourne is ranked first in Australia for business and economics.

name: Graduate Certificate in Environment
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Environment at the University of Melbourne explores the full breadth of environmental disciplines, spanning cities, wilderness, agricultural lands and oceans, over six months full-time or equivalent part-time. Students complete a 50-point program with a core subject in Environmental Sustainability plus electives that can include an applied research project, industry internship or overseas field trip.
Graduates move into roles as strategy and policy advisors, environmental planners, sustainability specialists and environmental scientists across government and private consultancies.

The Graduate Certificate in Evaluation at the University of Melbourne, developed by the Assessment and Evaluation Research Centre, gives professionals a rare online qualification in evaluation theory and practice, covering the nature, purpose and types of evaluation. Students learn to plan, engage stakeholders and report on evaluations, developing the responsibilities and ethical principles of evaluation leadership, with credit available toward the Master of Evaluation.
The course suits professionals across international development, health, education, corporate and community sectors moving into evaluation specialist and leadership roles.

The Graduate Certificate in Food Science at the University of Melbourne prepares students for a career in food and associated industries through advanced subjects in food chemistry, processing, food safety and microbiology. Students choose electives in food policy and governance, sustainability, management and business, with full credit toward the Graduate Diploma in Food Science for those who continue.
Melbourne is ranked first in Australia for life sciences and medicine. Graduates gain the foundational skills to move into food manufacturing and quality assurance roles.

description:
The Graduate Certificate in Genomics and Health at the University of Melbourne was the first of its kind in Australia, giving clinical, health, education and research professionals the skills to apply genomics knowledge in practice and policy. Students complete a 50-point program introducing human genetics and its clinical and research applications, taught by research and education leaders from prestigious Melbourne hospitals and research institutes in a flexible, blended learning model.
Graduates build a pathway into genomics-related roles across healthcare, research and law, with access to organisations including the Parkville Children's Campus.

The Graduate Certificate in Journalism (Advanced) at the University of Melbourne is associated with the Master of Journalism, developing critical and technical journalistic skills through three compulsory subjects over six months full-time or part-time. The course covers integral journalism understandings with the option to study further advanced subjects.
Graduates move into roles across all media platforms, including TV, print or radio journalist and reporter, editor and subeditor, and blogger and copywriter.

The Graduate Certificate in Language and Cultural Literacy at the University of Melbourne gives students flexibility to study one or more of 14 languages, from Arabic and Chinese to Russian and Spanish, as a beginner or to consolidate existing knowledge. Melbourne is ranked first in Australia for modern languages. Graduates build language and intercultural communication skills valuable across international relations, education and business.

Four specialist core subjects cover second language teaching methodology, grammar for language teachers, language acquisition and supervised teaching, with 50 credit points toward the Master of Modern Languages Education for students who continue.
Graduates with Victorian Institute of Teaching registration become eligible for language teaching positions in Victorian schools, with the skills to critique and manage culturally and linguistically appropriate curricula.

The Graduate Certificate in Public Health at the University of Melbourne gives current health sector professionals fundamental public health skills applicable to practice, policy and management, with full credit toward the Master of Public Health for students who continue. Students learn public health conceptual foundations, current global health challenges, and the population-based strategies used to address them, alongside skills in analysing and synthesising public health evidence.
Melbourne is ranked second in Australia and 17th in the world for public health. The course strengthens career prospects across the health sector and provides a direct pathway into the full master's degree.

Graduates move into professional editing, print and online publications, communications and stakeholder management, and copywriting and website content roles.

description:
The Graduate Certificate in Science at the University of Melbourne lets students with a bachelor's degree in one science major complete the equivalent of a major in a second area, chosen from 14 streams including botany, chemistry and physics. Students complete 62.5 points, combining 50 points of third-year-equivalent study with 12.5 points at master's level.
This course is no longer accepting new applications. Graduates are well placed to continue into the related Master of Science stream or enter the workforce with a broadened scientific skillset.

Graduate Certificate in TESOL

name: Master of Architecture
description:
The Master of Architecture at the University of Melbourne builds expertise in contemporary design and sustainable buildings, taught in studio-based classes that mirror real design practice by over 30 full-time academics and leading architectural practitioners. Students develop creative and critical thinking skills to push the boundaries of architectural design and critique its technical, aesthetic, social and environmental performance, with a research subject option available.
Completing a three-year architecture bachelor's degree plus the two-year entry point of this master's, or the three-year entry point on its own, meets the academic requirements for registration as an architect with the Architects Registration Board of Victoria.
admission_requirements: The Master of Architecture is a 300-point (3-year) course, however if you have completed previous study in this discipline, you may be eligible for up to 100 points of credit (2-year course option). To be considered for entry into the 200-point (2-year) course option, you must: Have a bachelor degree (AQF7) with a major in architecture or architectural studies with a weighted average mark of at least 65%, or equivalent. If you are a University of Melbourne undergraduate student, see below 'Additional information' for details on guaranteed pathways.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 81; PTE Academic 64. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Master of Art Curatorship
description:
The Master of Art Curatorship at the University of Melbourne, taught for nearly 30 years, combines theoretical, historical and practical study of the changing role of art museums and arts organisations in collecting, interpreting and exhibiting art. Leading professionals from the Australian art world contribute to teaching alongside staff from the University's cultural collections and the Grimwade Centre for Cultural Materials Conservation.
Students choose a 200-point, two-year program or a 150-point, 1.5-year program for relevant graduates. Graduates move into art auctioneering, arts policy and law, collection and exhibition management, and freelance curating roles.

OR Have a bachelor degree (AQF7) in a cognate (relevant) discipline with a weighted average mark (WAM) of at least 65%, or equivalent, and at least two years of documented relevant work and/or professional experience. name: Master of Arts and Community Practice
Master of Arts and Cultural Management
description:
The Master of Arts and Cultural Management at the University of Melbourne develops transferable management skills across film, theatre, dance, music and the visual arts, with an optional internship placement and a practical understanding of cultural policy. Students choose a 200-point, two-year program with foundation, compulsory, capstone and elective subjects, or a 150-point, 1.5-year program for graduates of a relevant discipline.
Graduates move into roles across screen production and distribution, festivals, galleries and museums, community arts, theatre and dance, cultural policy development, and art marketing and philanthropy.

name: Master of Banking and Finance Law
description:
The Master of Banking and Finance Law at the University of Melbourne gives law and non-law graduates a sophisticated understanding of the legal and regulatory framework governing the Australian and international financial sector. Students complete 100 credit points, including Fundamentals of the Common Law for those without a common law degree, choosing from subjects covering banking, funds management, finance transactions, superannuation and capital markets.
The course is part of the Melbourne Law Masters program. Melbourne Law School is ranked first in Australia and eighth globally, and graduates build the legal expertise needed for banking, finance and regulatory roles.

name: Master of Biomedical Engineering
description:
The Master of Biomedical Engineering at the University of Melbourne works at the intersection of engineering and biology to solve problems in medicine and human disease, blending biomedical science with engineering techniques. Students with a relevant undergraduate major complete the degree in two years, starting in second year with credit for foundation subjects, and can pursue a Business specialisation or continue unspecialised.
Graduates work across biotechnology, government, health services, medical devices and pharmaceuticals, designing medical devices, solving clinical problems and developing imaging algorithms or engineered tissues.
admission_requirements: To be considered for entry into the 200-point (2-year) course option, you must: Have completed a bachelor degree (AQF7) from the University of Melbourne majoring in Biomedical Engineering Systems with a weighted average mark of at least 65% or equivalent. Or Have completed a Bachelor of Engineering, or equivalent as recognised by the Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, in a cognate (relevant) discipline with a weighted average mark (WAM) of at least 65% or equivalent. Cognate (relevant) disciplines include: Biomedical Engineering. And Have completed below prerequisite subject(s): 25 points of appropriate tertiary-level mathematics subjects, equivalent to MAST10006 Calculus 2 and MAST10007 Linear Algebra . And 25 points of appropriate tertiary-level Biology. Or 25 points of appropriate tertiary-level Chemistry. Or 12.5 points of second year Engineering Mathematics, equivale

name: Master of Biomedical Science
description:
The Master of Biomedical Science at the University of Melbourne advances human health through research, letting students choose coursework from discipline, industry and professional skills electives. Students complete 200 credit points comprising core subjects including Introduction to Biomedical Research, elective subjects, and a 125-point research project undertaken alongside academics, researchers and industry partners.
Graduates build technical know-how and industry skills for a career in biomedical science or pursue further research through a PhD, in a field dedicated to advancing human health and technology.
admission_requirements: To be considered for entry into this course, you must: Have completed a bachelor degree (AQF7) in a cognate (relevant) discipline with a weighted average mark (WAM) of 65%, or equivalent. Cognate (relevant) disciplines include (but are not limited to): A major in anatomy, biochemistry and molecular biology, biotechnology, cell and developmental biology, chemistry, data science, genetics, immunology, microbiology, neuroscience, pathology, pharmacology, physiology, psychology. name: Master of Biostatistics
description:
The Master of Biostatistics at the University of Melbourne teaches students to design and analyse health studies and communicate findings to other health professionals, applying computational analysis to real health datasets. Students choose between five core subjects, five electives and a biostatistics research project, or a capstone selective with a shorter research project, studied full-time or part-time, face-to-face or online.
Graduates can become accredited with the Statistical Society of Australia, working in Australia or internationally on questions from disease prevention to patient treatment.

name: Master of Biotechnology
description:
The Master of Biotechnology at the University of Melbourne combines biological and medical knowledge with business acumen to bring emerging technologies and therapeutics to market, studied within Melbourne's Biomedical Precinct. Students complete a 200-point program with core subjects in science, commercialisation and professional skills, an Industry or Business Project, and electives spanning finance, bioethics and law.
Graduates move into pharmaceuticals and biotechnology roles, often with their industry placement company, or pursue further study through a PhD.
admission_requirements: To be considered for entry into this course, you must: Have completed a bachelor degree (AQF7) in a cognate (relevant) discipline with a weighted average mark (WAM) of 65%, or equivalent. name: Master of Business Administration
description:
The Melbourne MBA at Melbourne Business School has a long record of producing senior executives able to lead across private, public and government organisations, with an integrated, skills-focused curriculum built for career impact. Students apply their learning to real business problems through internships, capstone projects and an Innovation Bootcamp shark-tank scenario, choosing to study over one or two years.
Melbourne Business School's global alumni community exceeds 17,000 people in senior positions at organisations including World Vision, BHP and Bain and Company. The Melbourne MBA is ranked first in Australia and 32nd in the world.
curriculum:
Core year: Financial Accounting, Managerial Economics, Marketing Management, Organisational Behaviour, Corporate Finance, Operations Management, Strategy
Core continued: Business Analytics, Leadership, Negotiation
Electives (second half of program): choose a concentration from Finance, Strategy, Marketing, or Entrepreneurship and Innovation
Capstone: Strategic Consulting Project with a real partner organisation
Optional international study tour or exchange component depending on cohort year
admission_requirements: Completed bachelor degree in any discipline plus a minimum of two to three years relevant full-time work experience; GMAT/GRE may strengthen an application. No Commonwealth Supported Places available (full fee-paying, offered via Melbourne Business School).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Master of Business Analytics
description:
The Full-time Master of Business Analytics at Melbourne Business School is a one-year, advanced degree developing the computational, analytical and business skills to extract value from data as a strategic asset. Five modules take students from the analytics problems businesses face through foundational and advanced techniques, applied to a real business in the Analytics Lab, finishing with analytics applications in finance, marketing and supply chain contexts.
Melbourne Business School's global alumni community exceeds 17,000 people at organisations including ANZ Bank, Medibank, Suncorp and Morgan Stanley.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Master of Chemical Engineering
description:
The Master of Chemical Engineering at the University of Melbourne develops the skills to design and implement industrial-scale processes that convert raw materials into everyday products, with specialisations in Business, Materials and Minerals, or Sustainability and Environment. Students with a relevant undergraduate major complete the degree in two years, starting in second year with credit for foundation subjects, guided by experts in nanotechnology and carbon capture.
Graduates work across petrochemicals, minerals processing, mining, pharmaceuticals, chemical manufacturing, natural gas and environmental consulting, with a skillset also valued in management consulting and finance.
admission_requirements: To be considered for the 200 point (2-year) course option, you must: Have completed a bachelor degree (AQF7) from the University of Melbourne majoring in Chemical Engineering Systems with a weighted average mark of 65% or equivalent. Or Have completed a Bachelor of Engineering (AQF7), or equivalent as recognised by the Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, in a cognate (relevant) discipline with a weighted average mark (WAM) of 65% or equivalent. Cognate (relevant) disciplines include: Chemical Engineering, Biochemical Engineering. And Have completed below prerequisite subject(s): At least 25 points of tertiary-level Mathematics, equivalent to MAST10006 Calculus 2 and MAST10007 Linear Algebra And At least 25 points of appropriate tertiary-level Chemistry, equivalent to CHEM10003 Chemistry 1 and CHEM10004 Chemistry 2 . Exact credit can only be determined on application.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 81; PTE Academic 64. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Master of Civil Engineering
description:
The Master of Civil Engineering at the University of Melbourne prepares students to design, construct, maintain and operate the built and natural environment, spanning structural, geotechnical, water resources, transport, energy and project management, with specialisations in Business, Energy or Structural engineering. Students with a relevant undergraduate major complete the degree in two years, starting in second year with credit for foundation subjects.
Graduates work across aerospace, construction, oil and gas, transport and water resources at organisations including AECOM, BHP Billiton and Melbourne Metro Rail Authority.

name: Master of Climate Science
description:
The Master of Climate Science at the University of Melbourne, delivered through the Office for Environmental Programs with 20 years of environmental excellence, develops climate system expertise with pathways focused on policy or climate science. Students complete a 200-point program with foundational core, discipline core, discipline electives and professional skills subjects, with an optional internship connecting study to industry.
Graduates work in climate risk and environmental consulting roles, helping government, industry and society adapt to a changing climate.
admission_requirements: To be considered for entry into this course, you must: Have completed a bachelor degree (AQF7) in a cognate (relevant) discipline with a weighted average mark (WAM) of 65%, or equivalent. Cognate (relevant) disciplines include: Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering, Environmental Science, or equivalent. And Have completed below prerequisite subject(s): MAST10005 (Calculus 1) or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 81; PTE Academic 64. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Master of Clinical Audiology
description:
The Master of Clinical Audiology at the University of Melbourne trains graduates to assess, diagnose and manage hearing and balance disorders, learning from clinicians and researchers through lectures, tutorials and supervised practicals with hands-on patient experience from day one. Students complete an independent research project alongside comprehensive clinical training, developing critical thinking and the ability to apply theory in novel clinical situations.
The professionally accredited program supports eligibility for registration as an audiologist. Graduates move into hospitals, private clinics, community health services and research roles.
admission_requirements: To be considered for entry into this course, you must: Have completed a bachelor degree (AQF7) or equivalent in a cognate (relevant) discipline. Cognate (relevant) disciplines include: Science, health sciences, biomedicine, linguistics, phonetics, psychology, music. We encourage all applicants with a WAM of 65 or above to apply. This WAM is an indication only and may vary year to year depending on the applicant pool, achieving this WAM does not guarantee entry. Domestic applicants who have special circumstances are encouraged to apply through Graduate Access Melbourne to increase their eligibility.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 91; PTE Academic 72. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Master of Clinical Dentistry
description:
The Master of Clinical Dentistry at the University of Melbourne gives general dentists a solid foundation in prosthodontics and restorative dentistry, clinical skills, patient management and ethical considerations, delivered full-time over 12 months or part-time over 24 months. Students access modern dental practice facilities and the Royal Melbourne Hospital, supervised by University faculty, completing an introduction to research methods alongside advanced clinical subjects.
Melbourne is ranked first in Australia and 41st in the world for dentistry. Graduates apply new skills immediately in general practice, increasing both the procedures they can perform and their clinical confidence.
admission_requirements: In order to be considered for entry, applicants must have completed: An undergraduate degree in Dentistry or equivalent degree that qualifies the applicant to register and practice as a Dentist (in their country of origin or residence); and Minimum two years of documented relevant clinical work experience (including nomination of three referees) and demonstrated proof of current dental registration (AHPRA or international equivalent); and Personal statement (1-2 pages) detailing why they wish to undertake the program; and One or more of a test, interview, workshop, or presentation, for the stream to which entry is sought; and Referees of shortlisted applicants will be requested to provide a referee report prior to an interview taking place.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Master of Clinical Research (by Coursework)
description:
The Master of Clinical Research at the University of Melbourne is the University's premier clinical research course for medical, biomedical, nursing, allied health and health science professionals who want to formalise their research skills or start a career in the field. Students learn the fundamentals of clinical research, plan and implement a research program, and translate research into clinical practice through small classes and an applied research or industry project.
The course is driven by industry needs and highly regarded by employers, meeting entry requirements for further study including a PhD pathway.
admission_requirements: To be considered for entry into this course, you must: Have completed a bachelor degree (AQF7) or equivalent in a cognate (relevant) discipline. Cognate (relevant) disciplines include: Medicine, an allied health profession, science or social science. name: Master of Commerce
description: The University of Melbourne's Master of Commerce is not a general coursework master's degree. It is a two-year research-training program that forms years one and two of the University's five-year doctoral programs, offered as Master of Commerce in Management, Economics, Marketing, Accounting, Finance, or Decision, Risk and Financial Sciences. Students take advanced disciplinary and research-methods subjects and a research report, and progress into the PhD only if they meet high grade thresholds, generally a 75 to 80 per cent average. Entry is highly competitive and aimed at students planning an academic or research career, with scholarships including fee waivers and a stipend for strong applicants. Graduates who want a professional coursework qualification should instead look at Melbourne's Master of Management, Master of Finance, or the Master of Commerce specialisation coursework alternatives.

name: Master of Commercial Law
description:
The Master of Commercial Law at the University of Melbourne is available only to legal graduates, covering finance, competition law, dispute resolution, tax, intellectual property, construction, energy and resources law, and core questions of private law. Students complete 100 credit points with a minor thesis option available for those interested in independent research, delivered flexibly to fit around working professionals' schedules.
The course is part of the Melbourne Law Masters program. Melbourne Law School is ranked first in Australia and eighth globally, and graduates build an employable mix of commercial law knowledge, research and analytical skills.

name: Master of Computer Science
description:
The Master of Computer Science at the University of Melbourne gives students a broad base of high-level computing knowledge with specialist skills in at least one area including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, programming languages and distributed computing, or spatial information science. Students complete 200 credit points, including a research methods subject, foundational and elective computer science subjects, and a compulsory 100-point research project.
Graduates work as software developers and engineers, systems and cybersecurity analysts, and data scientists at organisations including IBM, Microsoft, Google, Deloitte and major banks.
curriculum:
Foundational stream (for non-CS entrants): Programming and Software Development, Algorithms and Data Structures, Computer Systems
Core (all students): Software Processes and Management, Distributed Systems, Database Systems, Elements of Data Processing
Specialisation electives: Artificial Intelligence, Cloud Computing, Cybersecurity, Computer Graphics, or Programming Language Implementation
Capstone: Project subject (research-oriented or industry-partnered) in final year
Research-strand students may take an extended thesis component as an alternative to the standard project
admission_requirements: To be considered for entry into this course, you must: Have completed a bachelor degree (AQF7) in a cognate (relevant) discipline with a weighted average mark (WAM) of 75%, or equivalent. name: Master of Construction Law
description:
The Master of Construction Law at the University of Melbourne gives construction and related industry professionals in-depth knowledge of construction law and its interaction with industry commerce and practice. Students complete 100 credit points, with at least 62.5 credit points from the Construction Law subject list, and a minor thesis option available for independent research.
The course is part of the Melbourne Law Masters program. Melbourne Law School is ranked first in Australia and eighth globally, and graduates build a highly employable mix of construction law knowledge and practical skills.

name: Master of Construction Management
description:
The Master of Construction Management at the University of Melbourne gives students the theoretical knowledge and practical skills to manage the social, technological, financial and environmental challenges facing the construction industry, with specialisation options across building, project management and related areas. The course runs as a two or three-year degree depending on prior qualifications, with the three-year stream for non-construction backgrounds including foundation construction subjects.
The course meets the requirements of professional bodies including the Australian Institute of Building, the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors and the Australian Institute of Quantity Surveyors.
