name: Graduate Certificate in Laboratory Medicine
description: The Graduate Certificate in Laboratory Medicine at the University of Newcastle introduces laboratory medicine with an emphasis on practical laboratory skills that transfer to a modern pathology laboratory. It is designed for graduates of biology, biotechnology, biomedical science or related degrees interested in a career in diagnostic pathology. Students gain practical experience with the latest advances in diagnostic medicine and can progress into the graduate diploma or master degree.

name: Graduate Certificate in Marketing and Digital Strategy
description: The Graduate Certificate in Marketing and Digital Strategy at the University of Newcastle enhances students' strategic capabilities in the marketing field, a fast-changing and demanding business function. The program equips students with essential skills for evolving business sectors, blending marketing principles with advanced digital strategies and providing a foundation in marketing theory covering strategy, consumer psychology and behaviour, and digital marketing.

name: Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting
description: The Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting at the University of Newcastle is a pathway to a career in accounting for students with a degree in a field other than accounting. A career in accounting offers challenging, rewarding and versatile opportunities, and businesses value the superior analytical skills that accounting develops. The program provides an introduction to accounting concepts and procedures and can lead into the graduate diploma or master degree.

name: Graduate Certificate in Social Change and Development
description: The Graduate Certificate in Social Change and Development at the University of Newcastle equips students with foundational knowledge to work in social change and development. It suits people who want to work in the professional service of others. Students learn about the key areas of social change through theoretical and practical coursework, and develop an understanding of the implications of social and political changes at a global level, preparing them for careers in community and international development.

name: Graduate Certificate in Sports Analytics
description: The Graduate Certificate in Sports Analytics at the University of Newcastle provides the skills and knowledge essential to measuring and evaluating sport performance through data analysis. Focusing on practical applications and case studies from the sports industry, students learn how to effectively and ethically use data to make informed decisions, building a foundation for careers in performance analysis and sports business or for further study.

name: Graduate Diploma in Psychological Science
description: The Graduate Diploma in Psychological Science at the University of Newcastle is an alternative pathway into psychology, designed for graduates from any discipline and requiring no prior background in the field. Students can study full-time and complete the program in as little as one year, developing foundational skills in key areas of psychology. It suits people looking to change careers, build psychological knowledge to support their current role, or pursue further study in psychology.

name: Juris Doctor
description:
Newcastle's JD is the standard graduate-entry law degree for people with a non-law bachelor's wanting to qualify for legal practice, and the program's selling point is scale: small cohorts mean JD students get taught by the same academics teaching the undergraduate combined degrees, not a separated graduate-only faculty, and the Newcastle Legal Centre clinical placement option is open to JD students as well as undergrads.

Most JD students are career-changers in their late twenties to forties, and Newcastle's JD timetabling (with some units offered in intensive or evening formats) reflects that. It's noticeably more accommodating of students working full time than a lot of the fully daytime-timetabled JDs at bigger city law schools. The program covers the full set of "Priestley 11" core subjects required for admission in Australia, plus electives in areas like environmental and resources law where Newcastle's research strength is genuine given the Hunter region's mining and energy industry.

Graduates still need to complete Practical Legal Training before seeking admission as a solicitor, and the JD itself typically runs three years full-time.
curriculum:
Year 1: Legal Method and Reasoning, Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law, Property Law, Legal Research and Writing
Year 2: Equity and Trusts, Constitutional Law, Administrative Law, Corporations Law, Evidence, electives
Year 3: Civil and Criminal Procedure, Professional Responsibility and Ethics, capstone units, electives (options include Environmental and Resources Law, given regional relevance)
Covers Priestley 11 core subjects required for admission to legal practice in Australia; Practical Legal Training required post-graduation
admission_requirements: Completed bachelors degree in any discipline; non-law backgrounds welcome
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 6.5

name: Master of Architecture
description: The Master of Architecture at the University of Newcastle is grounded and future-focused, preparing students for professional practice and the next step towards becoming a registered architect. The program is shaped by a commitment to Caring for Country and a focus on social and ecological responsibility. Students develop their own approach to architecture through design-led studio learning that engages with real-world challenges and communities, spending more time in the studio than any other NSW program.

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Newcastle's MBA runs through the AACSB-accredited Newcastle Business School and is pitched squarely at working professionals. Most units are delivered in intensive block or evening/weekend format rather than assuming students can attend daytime classes, and the cohort skews toward regional NSW managers and public sector employees rather than the international-student-heavy MBA cohorts common at city business schools.

The program includes a capstone strategy consulting project where student teams work with a real regional organisation on an actual business problem, often drawing on the Hunter region's mix of health, mining services, manufacturing, and increasingly renewable energy employers for project partners, a genuinely local flavour compared to generic case-study capstones. Students can also tailor the degree with electives toward specific interests like health management, given the strong health-sector presence in the region through Hunter New England Health and the university's own medical faculty.

Entry typically requires several years of professional work experience alongside an undergraduate degree, consistent with most AACSB MBA admission standards, and the program can be completed part-time over a longer period for students not wanting to step away from full-time work.
curriculum:
Core units: Accounting for Managers, Managerial Economics, Marketing Management, Organisational Behaviour and Leadership, Strategic Management, Corporate Finance, Operations and Supply Chain Management, Business Analytics
Electives: choose from streams including Health Management, Human Resource Management, International Business, Innovation and Entrepreneurship
Capstone: Strategic Management Consulting Project (team-based, real client brief, often with a Hunter region organisation)
Delivery: intensive block and evening/weekend formats to suit working professionals; part-time completion available
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in any discipline plus 2+ years relevant work experience preferred
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Business Psychology
description: The Master of Business Psychology at the University of Newcastle is for graduates seeking to advance their leadership and management skills using insights from psychological science. Designed for graduates from a wide range of backgrounds, not limited to psychology qualifications, the program enhances understanding of human psychology across workplace contexts and provides novel, evidence-based leadership skills and insights for understanding, working within, and leading organisations.

name: Master of Clinical Epidemiology
description: The Master of Clinical Epidemiology at the University of Newcastle teaches students how to use epidemiologic methods to conduct health care research. Students learn to apply the principles of epidemiology and biostatistics, apply theoretical frameworks and develop a research study protocol. Graduates are ready to work in clinical epidemiology and healthcare, and studies count towards continuing professional development points for clinicians, with credit available for prior learning.

name: Master of Clinical Psychology
description: The Master of Clinical Psychology at the University of Newcastle is a professional qualification for those who wish to practise as a clinical psychologist. The program offers expert supervision in the university psychology clinic and in local health care and community settings, giving students the skills to work in the assessment, diagnosis and treatment of a wide range of psychological disorders across the lifespan, and to apply advanced knowledge, principles and methods to practice.

name: Master of Cyber Security
description: The University of Newcastle Master of Cyber Security offers two specialisations, including a Cyber Security Analyst stream that emphasises the human dimensions of cyber security, cyber crime and the consequences of security breaches. Coursework spans data, system and network security, security attack analysis and mitigation, human factors, and elements of law, psychology and criminology. Students complete a hands-on industry project across two semesters, using industry-leading cyber security labs and taking part in hackathons and real application development in a controlled environment. A Graduate Certificate in Cyber Security is available as a pathway into the masters. International students must meet the University English proficiency requirement. Indicative international tuition is around A$49,400 per year. Graduates work as cyber security analysts and ICT security specialists across many sectors.

name: Master of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
description: The University of Newcastle's Master of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence is a two-year degree designed for both experienced professionals and people new to the field. It merges data science fundamentals, including data processing, visualisation and predictive modelling, with machine learning and Big Data technologies for storing and analysing large structured and unstructured datasets. Students choose one of two specialisations, Computational Intelligence or Health Data Analysis, and complete an industry or research project. Graduates work as data scientists, machine learning engineers, data analysts and analytics consultants across health, finance, government and technology. Indicative international tuition is around A$47,700 per year.

name: Master of Disaster Resilience and Sustainable Development
Master of Disaster Risk and Resilience
description: The Master of Disaster Risk and Resilience at the University of Newcastle equips graduates from diverse backgrounds with resilience and sustainable development skills to help build a more resilient future. Students learn to anticipate and reduce disaster risks and to handle the impacts of extreme events, so that organisations can mitigate disaster risks while protecting lives and revenue. Graduates work in disaster management, policy development and community resilience roles.

name: Master of Education
description: The Master of Education at the University of Newcastle is for practising educators looking to retrain in an additional teaching area or advance their professional skills. Students deepen their understanding of educational theory and practice, stay updated with industry trends and research, and apply a proven, evidence-supported teaching framework. The program lets students deepen their curriculum knowledge in specialised areas to enhance their teaching effectiveness and career prospects.

name: Master of Environmental Law
description: The Master of Environmental Law at the University of Newcastle provides legal and non-legal professionals with a deeper knowledge of environmental law in Australia and beyond. Students study a range of discipline areas taught by international industry experts, including environmental and life sciences, business, and architecture and built environment. It is the only postgraduate legal program in Australia offering the opportunity to obtain certification by the United Nations Institute for Training and Research.

name: Master of Fintech
description: The Master of Fintech at the University of Newcastle equips students with a comprehensive understanding of emerging financial technologies, along with advanced financial theory, principles and practices, to build a successful career in the finance sector in the digital era. The program provides a nexus between traditional financial knowledge and transformative financial technologies, and is offered through an AACSB and EQUIS accredited business school.

name: Master of Food Science and Technology
description: The Master of Food Science and Technology at the University of Newcastle provides advanced knowledge, skills and opportunities to work across the food industry as the world faces evolving challenges in food production, sustainability and nutrition. Food is a cornerstone of culture, global health and innovation, and demand for forward-thinking professionals in food science has never been greater. Graduates work in product development, food safety, quality assurance and research.

name: Master of Health Economics, Management and Policy
Master of Health Management and Policy
description: The Master of Health Management and Policy at the University of Newcastle prepares graduates to become leaders in the health sector, where effective leadership and a strong understanding of healthcare organisations and policy are crucial to navigating complex challenges. This multidisciplinary program meets the growing demand for expertise in healthcare leadership and management roles, and students learn directly from international industry experts about policy and governance.

name: Master of Human Resource Management
description: The Master of Human Resource Management at the University of Newcastle provides the skills and knowledge to manage people and efficient work practices within an organisation, and to develop and lead high-performing teams and workforces within complex organisational environments. It suits people looking to advance their career in human resource management, employment relations or consulting, and develops a deep, nuanced understanding of strategic human resource management.

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
Newcastle's Master of IT sits inside a school that grew out of the university's original computing and engineering strength rather than being bolted on as a later cash-generator, and it shows in the elective spread: alongside the expected software engineering and networking units there are dedicated strands in cybersecurity and data science that draw on the same research groups producing NURVsim and IoT security work out of Callaghan. Most cohorts run heavy with international students converting from other bachelor's degrees, so the program includes conversion-style foundation units in the first session for anyone without a CS undergrad background, then lets students specialise from session two.

Teaching is a mix of Callaghan campus and, for some intakes, Sydney's CBD campus at 350 George Street, which matters for students weighing proximity to internships at Sydney-based tech employers against lower living costs in Newcastle. The capstone is an industry project rather than a pure research thesis for most students, done in small teams with a real client brief: recent ones have included local government data dashboards and health-sector app prototypes tied to the Hunter New England health precinct next to the university.
curriculum:
Session 1: Programming Fundamentals, Database Systems, Networking Fundamentals, Systems Analysis and Design
Session 2: Software Engineering, Advanced Database Systems, Elective (Cybersecurity or Data Science stream)
Session 3: Cloud Computing, Elective, Elective, IT Project Management
Session 4: IT Capstone Project (industry-sponsored team project), Elective
Specialisation streams: Cybersecurity, Data Science, Software Engineering, Networking
Entry pathway: Graduate Certificate in IT available for students needing foundation coursework before full enrolment

name: Master of International Business
description: The Master of International Business at the University of Newcastle helps students deepen their understanding of international business and develop the strategic decision-making knowledge and skills required to be a successful manager for organisations with an international focus. Students learn to form and implement strategic decisions in the global business environment. The program is hosted at NUspace in the heart of the Newcastle CBD.

name: Master of International Sports Business
description: The Master of International Sports Business at the University of Newcastle is an interdisciplinary program that equips students with the advanced knowledge and skills to excel in the global sports industry. It prioritises the development of problem-solving skills, ethical decision-making and strategic perspectives, preparing students for diverse careers in sport business. The program is delivered on campus in Sydney in partnership with the Global Institute of Sport, using the Allianz Stadium and Sydney Cricket Ground precinct.

name: Master of Laboratory Medicine
description: The Master of Laboratory Medicine at the University of Newcastle prepares job-ready graduates with advanced expertise in diagnostic pathology and medical research, real clinical laboratory experience, and strong pathways into hospital, pathology and regional laboratories. Designed to meet Australia's growing demand for skilled laboratory professionals, it is ideal for graduates of biomedical science, biology, biotechnology or closely related disciplines. Students undertake supervised placements in clinical laboratories, gaining practical experience with current diagnostic techniques before entering the workforce.

name: Master of Laws
description: The Master of Laws at the University of Newcastle is for people who want to specialise in a specific area of law, with flexible study options tailored to career needs. Students choose from Dispute Resolution, Environmental Law, Employment and Labour Relations Law and International Law, engaging in advanced studies with a strong research focus and developing critical thinking skills to analyse complex legal issues. Classes are held at NUspace in the Newcastle CBD.

name: Master of Leadership and Management in Education
Master of Marketing and Digital Strategy
description: The Master of Marketing and Digital Strategy at the University of Newcastle is a comprehensive, contemporary and practical program that equips students with digital transformation skills and data-driven insights to promote socially responsible marketing and foster a strategic and entrepreneurial mindset. The program can be studied face-to-face at the Newcastle City Precinct, online, or a combination of the two, allowing students to balance professional and personal life.

name: Master of Materials Science and Engineering
description: The Master of Materials Science and Engineering at the University of Newcastle combines coursework and research, with access to specialised infrastructure at the Global Innovative Centre for Advanced Nanomaterials. Students undertake research related to the design and discovery of new materials, including advanced materials, nanomaterials, functional materials, drug carriers, photovoltaics and soft materials, preparing them for careers in materials research and engineering.

name: Master of Midwifery Studies
description: The Master of Midwifery Studies at the University of Newcastle offers registered midwives a pathway to broaden their scope beyond bedside care and move into leadership, education or specialist roles such as primary care and research. Today's midwives work in increasingly complex environments with growing workload pressures, and the program is designed with these realities in mind, supporting midwives who are balancing shift work and career development.

name: Master of Nursing
description: The University of Newcastle Master of Nursing is built for working registered nurses who want to progress into senior, specialist, leadership, educator or researcher roles without stepping away from practice, with flexible online learning and recognition of existing experience. It offers specialisations such as Advanced Practice and Leadership and Management, and develops the knowledge to lead teams, manage complex care and deliver evidence-based care. Entry requires registration as a registered nurse in the applicant own country, plus a postgraduate qualification at AQF level 8 or higher or at least one year of work experience as a registered nurse, evidenced by a CV and statement of service. Indicative international tuition is around A$47,600 per year. With a projected national shortfall of around 79,000 nurses by 2035, demand for advanced-practice nurses is strong.

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description: The University of Newcastle Master of Professional Accounting is a two-year conversion degree for graduates whose qualifications are in a field other than accounting, covering financial and management accounting, finance, taxation, business law and auditing. It is structured to satisfy the joint accreditation guidelines of CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, so graduates can take up associate membership of CPA Australia and enrol in the CPA Program or the CA Program. Entry requires a bachelor degree in any discipline, or at least seven years of relevant organisational experience including two years in management, plus the University English proficiency requirement. Indicative international tuition is around A$42,600 per year. Graduates work in accounting, finance, tax and audit roles across commerce, professional practice and government.

name: Master of Professional Engineering (Geospatial Engineering and Surveying)
Master of Professional Psychology
description: The Master of Professional Psychology at the University of Newcastle is designed for those interested in a career as a registered psychologist. Students develop core counselling skills and competencies appropriate for an early career psychologist, and graduates are ready to commence their internship as part of the 5+1 pathway to general psychology registration. Students learn to assess, develop a case formulation and apply best practice with people who have a range of psychological presentations.

name: Master of Public Health
description: The University of Newcastle's Master of Public Health is an 80-unit degree, one year full-time or two years part-time, available on campus or online. It is built from 40 units of core courses and 40 units chosen from a wide course list, so students can focus on areas such as epidemiology, biostatistics, health promotion or health services management. The program gives a broad grounding in identifying, evaluating and responding to public health problems at both local and global scale, and can also be taken as a double degree with health management and policy or with social change and development. Graduates work in government health agencies, non-government organisations, community health and research. Indicative international tuition is around A$46,400 per year.

name: Master of Social Change and Development
description: The Master of Social Change and Development at the University of Newcastle teaches students to undertake projects in collaboration with community members and to influence positive outcomes through theoretical and applied knowledge. The global environment is rapidly changing, and students make immediate impact through hands-on learning opportunities. The program provides an opportunity to create original research work as part of study and to shape a career in local and international development.

name: Master of Social Work (Qualifying)
description: The Master of Social Work (Qualifying) at the University of Newcastle prepares graduates from unrelated fields to become qualified social workers, a profession in high demand. The program is practice-led and industry-engaged, with embedded fieldwork placements to prepare students for professional practice. Students can study full-time or part-time, with a flexible night-school approach to class times to suit work and home responsibilities.

name: Master of Special and Inclusive Education
description: The Master of Special and Inclusive Education at the University of Newcastle builds on students' existing education or health qualifications, blending theory, research, practice, reflection and innovation with an emphasis on applying best-practice, evidence-based approaches to support the learning and development of people with disability or additional needs. It is designed for educators working in inclusive and specialist settings, including practising and accredited teachers seeking additional qualifications.

name: Master of Sports Analytics
description: The Master of Sports Analytics at the University of Newcastle is delivered in partnership with the Global Institute of Sport and is a future-focused degree for data-driven students with aspirations towards careers in sports business or performance analysis. Both growth areas require evidence-based decision-making and research skills, which are fundamental learning outcomes of the degree. Students study at the heart of Sydney's business and sports precinct.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
Notre Dame's BA covers the usual humanities spread (history, English, philosophy, politics), but the university's smaller scale and Catholic mission mean genuinely small tutorial groups and a values and ethics thread running through core units, framed differently than at a secular university. Available across the Fremantle and Sydney campuses, with slightly different elective offerings depending on location.

It's commonly taken as a combined degree (Arts/Law, Arts/Education) rather than standalone, and the degree's smaller enrolment numbers mean students get real access to academic staff rather than being one of several hundred in a lecture theatre.
curriculum:
Year 1: two introductory subjects across chosen majors, Core Curriculum unit (a university-wide requirement covering ethics and philosophy foundations)
Years 2-3: major sequences (8 subjects per major), electives
Typical majors: History, English, Philosophy, Politics and International Relations, Theology
Capstone: independent research essay or internship subject, final year
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with an ATAR of approximately 65-70 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Biomedical Science (Assured Pathway to Medicine)
description:
This is Notre Dame's dedicated feeder degree into its own Doctor of Medicine program. Students who maintain the required GPA through the three years get a guaranteed interview and, on passing that, a confirmed place in the MD without sitting GAMSAT, which is largely why students choose this over a generic biomedical science degree elsewhere. It runs out of the Fremantle campus, sharing teaching space and some staff with the medical school itself.

Class sizes are genuinely small by Australian university standards. Notre Dame markets itself on this, and in the science labs it means more direct instructor time than at the larger biomedical cohorts nearby. The degree still stands on its own for anyone who doesn't proceed to medicine, but the assured pathway is the headline feature and shapes the entire cohort's expectations.
curriculum:
Year 1: Human Biology, Chemistry, Foundations of Anatomy, Introduction to Medical Sciences
Year 2: Physiology, Biochemistry, Pathophysiology, Pharmacology Foundations
Year 3: Advanced Systems Physiology, Research Project, electives, MD entry interview process
Pathway requirement: minimum cumulative GPA maintained through all three years, interview in final year
admission_requirements: Minimum ATAR of 92 (or IB/equivalent) for international school leavers; maintain GPA of 2.5+ each semester to remain on assured pathway to MD
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description:
A standard business generalist degree through Notre Dame's School of Law and Business, offering majors across accounting, finance, management, and marketing, with the accounting major carrying professional accreditation relevant to CPA and CAANZ pathways. Class sizes are notably smaller than at the larger Perth or Sydney business schools, and the degree's Core Curriculum requirement (shared across all Notre Dame undergraduate degrees) means commerce students also take ethics and philosophy units alongside their business coursework, a genuine point of difference from a purely vocational business degree.

Placement and internship opportunities lean on Notre Dame's local business community ties in Fremantle and Perth, or Sydney depending on campus.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting Fundamentals, Economics, Business Statistics, Core Curriculum unit
Year 2: Corporate Finance, Marketing Principles, Management, first major subjects
Year 3: major specialisation, Business Law, Strategic Management, capstone/internship option
Majors: Accounting, Finance, Management, Marketing
Capstone: work-integrated learning or business project, final year
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with an ATAR of approximately 65-75 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description:
Leads to registration as a primary school teacher in Australia, with a strong practicum emphasis: students are typically in schools on placement from first year, not just in a token block near the end, which the university uses as a selling point against programs that front-load theory before classroom exposure. The Catholic education sector across WA and NSW is a major employer of Notre Dame education graduates, and the degree includes specific preparation for teaching in faith-based schools alongside the standard curriculum and pedagogy content required for any teaching role.

Literacy and numeracy pedagogy get heavy emphasis given AITSL's national teaching standards, and students sit the mandatory literacy and numeracy test (LANTITE) during the degree, not as an afterthought at the end.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Education, Child Development, Introduction to Curriculum, early school placement block
Year 2: Literacy Pedagogy, Numeracy Pedagogy, Classroom Management, school placement
Year 3: curriculum specialisations (science, HASS, arts, health/PE), Inclusive Education, extended placement
Year 4: Professional Experience (extended final placement), capstone teaching portfolio, LANTITE completion
Registration: leads to provisional teacher registration in the relevant state or territory
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with an ATAR of approximately 65-75 or equivalent; interview and personal statement often required for teaching entry
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0 (professional teacher registration requirement)

name: Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science
Bachelor of Health and Physical Education (Primary) (Honours)
Bachelor of Laws
description:
Notre Dame's standard-entry undergraduate LLB, distinct from the graduate-entry JD, is usually taken as a combined degree (Arts/Law and Commerce/Law are the common pairings) across four to five years depending on the combination. It covers the same Priestley 11 core required for practice, delivered in smaller classes than the large capital-city law schools, with the same values-based ethics emphasis that runs through Notre Dame's law teaching generally.

Clinical legal education and mooting programs give students supervised practical exposure before graduation, and the smaller cohort size means more direct access to teaching staff for mooting coaching and clinic supervision than at higher-enrolment law schools.
curriculum:
Core (Priestley 11): Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law, Property Law, Equity, Constitutional Law, Administrative Law, Evidence, Civil Procedure, Corporations Law, Professional Conduct
Electives: minimum 6-8 subjects depending on combined degree structure
Clinical option: supervised legal clinic placement
Capstone: moot or research subject, final year
Leads to: eligibility for Practical Legal Training and admission as a legal practitioner
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with an ATAR of approximately 80-85 or equivalent, or mature-age entry with relevant experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Marketing and Public Relations
Bachelor of Nursing
description:
The University of Notre Dame Australia's Bachelor of Nursing leads to registration eligibility with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, taught with a strong clinical placement structure across Fremantle-area hospitals and health services, and Sydney placements for that campus's cohort. The degree's Catholic institutional character shows up specifically in mandatory units on ethics and pastoral care within a health context, sitting alongside the standard clinical science curriculum required for any nursing accreditation.

Simulation-based learning happens on campus in dedicated clinical skills labs before students progress to live hospital and community placements, with placement blocks increasing in complexity and autonomy each year.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Health Assessment, Ethics and Pastoral Care in Health
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Pharmacology, clinical placement blocks
Year 3: Acute and Critical Care, Community and Primary Health Care, Aged Care Nursing, final capstone placement
Placement: clinical hours across acute, community, aged care, and mental health settings, AHPRA-aligned
admission_requirements: Indicative ATAR of 70 with a minimum score of 50 in ATAR English/Literature/EALD, or equivalent; interview may be required
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 6.5 (higher requirement due to clinical placements)

name: Bachelor of Philosophy
description:
A distinctive offering shaped by Notre Dame's Catholic identity: unlike a standard philosophy major bolted onto a BA, this is a dedicated degree with a strong grounding in the history of philosophy, from ancient through medieval to modern, alongside contemporary ethics, metaphysics, and philosophy of religion. The faculty includes specialists in Thomistic and Catholic intellectual tradition scholarship structured in a way you won't find at a secular university.

It draws a genuinely small cohort (this isn't a high-enrolment degree), but that means seminar-style teaching rather than lectures for most of the degree, and students get close engagement with staff on primary texts rather than survey-level treatment.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Philosophy, Ancient Philosophy, Logic and Critical Thinking, Ethics
Year 2: Medieval Philosophy, Modern Philosophy, Philosophy of Religion, Metaphysics
Year 3: Contemporary Philosophy, Political Philosophy, independent research essay, electives
Capstone: extended research essay or thesis, final year
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with an ATAR of approximately 65-70 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Physiotherapy
description:
A four-year professional degree accredited by the Australian Physiotherapy Council, leading to registration eligibility with AHPRA. Notre Dame runs this out of its Fremantle health sciences facilities, with clinical placement hours spread across public hospital, private practice, aged care, and sports settings. The degree emphasises hands-on clinical skills training in on-campus labs well before students go into placement, using the same anatomy and clinical skills facilities shared with the university's medical and nursing programs.

Given Notre Dame's smaller cohort compared to the bigger physiotherapy schools in the region, students get more individual attention in practical skills classes, which the school markets directly to prospective students.
curriculum:
Year 1: Anatomy, Physiology, Biomechanics, Introduction to Physiotherapy Practice
Year 2: Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy, Neurological Physiotherapy, Cardiorespiratory Physiotherapy, clinical skills labs
Year 3: clinical placements begin (hospital, private practice), Exercise Physiology, Pain Science
Year 4: extended clinical placements (aged care, paediatrics, sports, community), Professional Practice, capstone case-based assessment
Placement: clinical hours across acute, community, private practice, and sports settings, AHPRA-aligned
admission_requirements: Indicative ATAR of approximately 85-90 or equivalent; interview and/or portfolio may be required due to clinical placements
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 6.5

name: Bachelor of Sport and Recreation Management
Doctor of Medicine
description:
Notre Dame's MD is a four-year graduate-entry program taught at the Fremantle campus (Sydney also runs the degree), accredited by the Australian Medical Council. The first two years use problem-based learning as the backbone rather than traditional lecture-heavy pre-clinical teaching: small tutorial groups work through clinical cases collaboratively with a facilitator rather than being taught anatomy and physiology in isolation from clinical context.

The distinguishing feature is the rural and community health emphasis: third year is run jointly with UWA through the Rural Clinical School of Western Australia, and around a quarter of each cohort can opt into a full year-long placement in a rural WA clinical site instead of the standard rotation structure. Clinical years also include a compulsory rural or remote general practice placement for everyone, not just those on the extended rural track, a genuine point of difference from more metro-focused medical schools.
curriculum:
Years 1-2: Problem-Based Learning case tutorials, basic clinical sciences, population and preventive health, bioethics, therapeutics, clinical skills training
Year 3: clinical rotations at Perth teaching hospitals, or Rural Clinical School of WA year-long placement for selected students
Year 4: discipline-based clinical rotations (medicine, surgery, paediatrics, psychiatry, obstetrics and gynaecology), rural/remote general practice placement, translational research or clinical audit project
Accreditation: AMC-accredited, leads to provisional registration and internship
admission_requirements: Completed bachelor degree in any discipline; GAMSAT average 52+ (min 50 per section) or equivalent, GPA 5.2+, CASPer situational judgement test, and interview
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0

name: Graduate Certificate in Medical Sciences
description:
A short postgraduate certificate aimed at graduates from non-medical backgrounds wanting a structured bridge into medical science postgraduate study, or as a standalone credential for allied health and science professionals wanting formal grounding in human biomedical sciences. It's not a pathway into Notre Dame's MD in the way the Assured Pathway biomedical degree is. It functions more as targeted upskilling or a stepping stone toward further postgraduate study.

Coursework compresses core biomedical science content (physiology, pathophysiology, pharmacology basics) into an intensive format, often taken part-time by people already working in health-adjacent fields.
curriculum:
Core subjects: Human Physiology, Pathophysiology, Pharmacology Foundations, Research Methods in Health Sciences
Structure: typically 4 subjects, completable in one semester full-time or across two part-time
Assessment: coursework-based, no thesis component
Progression: can articulate into further postgraduate medical science or health study for eligible students
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor degree in science or health-related field
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Juris Doctor
description:
Notre Dame's JD is a graduate-entry law degree run through the School of Law, built for people with an existing non-law bachelor's degree wanting to qualify for legal practice. It covers the full Priestley 11 core subjects required for admission in an accelerated postgraduate format, with practical legal skills, mooting, negotiation, a supervised legal clinic placement, woven through rather than left entirely to post-degree Practical Legal Training.

Notre Dame's law cohort is smaller than the big Sydney law schools, and the school leans into a values-based framing consistent with the university's Catholic character, which shows up in dedicated subjects on legal ethics and social justice rather than treating those as an afterthought elective.
curriculum:
Core (Priestley 11): Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law, Property Law, Equity and Trusts, Constitutional Law, Administrative Law, Evidence, Civil Procedure, Corporations Law, Professional Conduct and Ethics
Electives: minimum 4-6 subjects, options include international law, family law, employment law
Clinical option: supervised legal clinic placement (credit-bearing)
Capstone: research subject or moot, final semester
Leads to: eligibility for Practical Legal Training and admission as a legal practitioner
admission_requirements: Completed bachelor degree in any discipline (or equivalent); relevant work experience viewed favourably
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Notre Dame's MBA is a smaller, values-oriented program compared to the large AACSB-branded MBAs at bigger business schools: positioned toward professionals wanting leadership and management skills grounded in ethical decision-making, consistent with the university's mission, rather than competing primarily on rankings or alumni network size. Delivered in flexible formats aimed at working professionals, with core subjects in finance, strategy, and marketing alongside a distinctive emphasis on ethical leadership.

Cohorts are small, and the program leans on case-based and applied project work over large-lecture delivery, reflecting Notre Dame's teaching style across its postgraduate business offerings generally.
curriculum:
Core: Financial Management, Strategic Management, Marketing Management, Ethical Leadership, Organisational Behaviour, Business Analytics
Electives: choose from entrepreneurship, human resource management, international business
Capstone: applied business project or strategy report, final term
Delivery: part-time/flexible options for working professionals
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline), professional experience considered favourably (typical MBA entry bar, approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Master of Education (Leadership and Management)
description:
Aimed at practising teachers moving into or already in school leadership roles (deputy principal, principal, head of department), this is a part-time-friendly postgraduate degree with an emphasis on Catholic and independent school sector leadership specifically, reflecting Notre Dame's institutional base, though the content applies across government schools too. Assessment leans on applied projects tied to students' own school contexts rather than purely theoretical coursework, on the assumption most students are working full-time in schools while studying.

Coursework covers educational leadership theory, school improvement and change management, and financial and human resource management within schools, with a research project or dissertation option for students wanting a pathway toward doctoral study afterward.
curriculum:
Core: Educational Leadership Theory, Managing Change in Schools, School Improvement and Data-Informed Practice, Human Resource Management in Schools
Electives: financial management in schools, curriculum leadership, pastoral care leadership, Catholic school leadership and mission
Capstone: applied leadership project based in the student's own school context, or research dissertation option
Delivery: part-time, intensive/block format common for working teachers
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor degree in education or related field, typically with teaching experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Advanced Business (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Advanced Business (Honours) is the University of Queensland Business School's flagship four-year undergraduate degree, built for high-achieving students aiming at leadership careers in business, strategy or consulting. Honours is embedded in the degree rather than added on afterwards, and students choose two majors from six options, including accounting, finance and marketing, or opt for a research pathway that leads toward postgraduate study. Core courses in information systems for strategic advantage and business analytics and artificial intelligence sit alongside major-specific study such as auditing, behavioural finance or applied market research, and a capstone project closes out the degree. Cohort-exclusive courses and structured networking are built into the program to help students build lasting professional connections, and graduates who complete the accounting major with an extra elective can work toward CAANZ or CPA accreditation. Typical destinations include investment analyst, operations manager and analytics project manager roles.
curriculum: UQ calls subjects "courses" within this program. A sample of what you study includes: Information Systems for Strategic Advantage [Core course], Business Analytics and Artificial Intelligence [Core course], Auditing & Public Practice [part of Accounting major], Behavioural Finance [part of Finance major], Applied Market Research [part of Marketing major], Business Industry Consultancy Project [Elective], Business Industry Placement [Elective], Operations manager. The exact core versus elective structure depends on the major, specialisation or study plan chosen, and is confirmed in UQ's official program and course list at enrolment.

name: Bachelor of Advanced Finance and Economics (Honours)

The degree was developed in close collaboration with Australia's agricultural and business sectors, so the transferable business skills it builds are recognised well beyond farming specifically. name: Bachelor of Agricultural Science
description:
Agriculture at UQ runs primarily out of the Gatton campus, a genuine working farm and research station about an hour west of Brisbane rather than a token rural annex, and the Bachelor of Agricultural Science leans on that hard: students get direct access to livestock and cropping systems, UQ's own research farms, and industry connections into Queensland's cattle, grain, and horticulture sectors that are simply larger and more varied than what a metro-based agriculture program can offer.

The degree covers plant and animal production systems, agribusiness, and increasingly precision agriculture and sustainability units, reflecting real shifts in the industry toward data-driven farm management, and UQ's agricultural research strength (particularly in areas like plant breeding genetics and tropical agriculture, given Queensland's subtropical and tropical growing regions) feeds directly into elective and capstone project offerings.

Most students complete a substantial industry placement or work-integrated learning component, often with agribusiness employers, government agencies like the Department of Agriculture and Fisheries, or research organisations, and Gatton's genuinely rural setting (compared to a program run entirely from a capital-city campus) means students graduate having actually worked with production systems rather than only studying them in theory.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Agricultural Science, Soil Science, Plant Biology, Animal Biology, Agricultural Economics
Year 2: Crop Production Systems, Livestock Production Systems, Agricultural Business Management, Pest and Disease Management
Year 3: Precision Agriculture, Agribusiness and Marketing, Sustainable Farming Systems, work-integrated learning placement
Year 4: Capstone Agricultural Systems Project, electives (options include tropical agriculture, plant breeding, agricultural technology), industry placement
Delivered primarily at UQ Gatton campus
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with ATAR of approximately 78+

Core courses include sustainability for global citizenship and foundation design studios, and the degree includes field trips and study tours to locations such as Japan and India. Teaching staff are a mix of academics and practising architects, so classroom projects stay connected to real practice. Graduates leave with an industry-ready design portfolio and typically move into roles such as architect, interior designer or urban designer.

A student who exits with the Bachelor of Behavioural Science still has a recognised university qualification covering the first 3 years of that coursework, useful for roles in human resources, community services, research support and further study in a related field, but without the honours research component or the direct line into psychologist registration that completing the full 4 year program provides.

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description:
UQ Business School holds the "triple crown" of business accreditations (AACSB, EQUIS, AMBA), a distinction only a handful of Australian business schools carry, and the Bachelor of Commerce is the school's flagship undergraduate degree: majors span accounting, finance, economics, and business analytics through to more specialised options like actuarial studies, one of the few undergraduate actuarial programs in the country accredited toward the Actuaries Institute pathway.

The degree draws a genuinely large international cohort, which shapes the classroom experience in group project units especially, and UQ Business School runs its own careers and mentoring programs that connect students directly to Brisbane's finance and professional services sector as well as national graduate programs at the big four accounting firms and major banks. Students can combine the Commerce degree with another (law, engineering, IT) as a dual degree, a common path for students wanting a technical-plus-business skill set.

Class delivery mixes large first and second-year lectures with smaller major-specific seminars from third year, and a capstone consulting-style project unit in most majors gives students a real client brief to work through in their final semester rather than a purely theoretical assessment.

Students are awarded the Bachelor of Criminal Justice after completing 48 units of that program's core and elective coursework in Level 2 and Level 3, before the dedicated honours year of Honours Research Thesis and Research Design courses.
admission_requirements: There is no direct entry pathway for this award. Students reach it only by first being admitted to and enrolling in UQ's Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice (or its Arts double-degree variant), and completing 48 units of Level 2 and Level 3 core courses with a grade point average (GPA) of 5.0.

Core courses include the honours research thesis and research design across the humanities, arts and social sciences, building analytical and evidence-evaluation skills that go well beyond a standard undergraduate criminology degree. It suits students who have completed an undergraduate criminology or criminal justice degree and want to strengthen their research credentials before applying for postgraduate study or research-focused roles. Typical graduate roles include policy adviser, intelligence analyst, cyber crime investigator and criminology tutor.

Coursework covers general dentistry alongside specialty areas including periodontics, paediatric dentistry, endodontics, prosthodontics and oral and maxillofacial surgery, with small cohort sizes giving students close contact with specialist teaching staff. Graduates register as dentists and can pursue further specialisation later through UQ's Doctor of Clinical Dentistry.

description: The Bachelor of Design at the University of Queensland is a 3-year interdisciplinary degree that trains students to design products, services, systems and experiences rather than specialising narrowly in one design field. Teaching moves from foundational design processes, visual communication and fabrication into hands-on studio projects, with access to UQ Innovate for prototyping and UQ Ventures for students interested in entrepreneurship. Core courses include design for a better world, design for the circular economy and design for complex systems, and the program is formally recognised by the Design Institute of Australia, the national peak body for the profession. Students graduate with a professional portfolio documenting their design thinking and process rather than only finished pieces. Typical graduate roles span design manager, user experience designer, product designer and service designer across health, business, technology and social innovation sectors.

Core courses in introductory microeconomics, macroeconomics and tools of economic analysis build a foundation before students specialise in up to two majors and choose electives aligned with their career interests, whether in banking, government policy, health, technology or the environment. A professional placement builds practical work experience into the degree, and many students combine it into dual programs with law or business management. Because the degree teaches transferable statistical and analytical skills rather than a single fixed career path, graduates move into varied roles including economic consultant, investment analyst, regulatory affairs officer and business development manager.

name: Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description: UQ's Bachelor of Education (Primary) trains students to teach across the full range of primary school subjects, from English and mathematics to science, the arts and humanities. Supervised school placements start from first year, building from observation and support work toward a final placement where students take substantial responsibility for a whole class. Core courses cover child development, inclusive classroom practice, Indigenous knowledge and education, and the Australian Curriculum, and students choose one of four minors, in English and literacy, humanities and social sciences, mathematics and numeracy, or science, to deepen their subject knowledge. Small cohort sizes are a deliberate feature of the degree, helping students build a support network alongside their studies. Because Queensland teacher registration requires a higher IELTS band than most UQ degrees, the program suits students who already have strong English proficiency. name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
UQ Engineering carries real weight in mining, minerals processing, and chemical engineering specifically. The Sustainable Minerals Institute is a globally recognised research centre, and it's not unusual for chemical and mining engineering students to end up working on SMI-affiliated research projects for their thesis, something a lot of comparable engineering schools around the country can't offer at the same depth given Queensland's genuine resources industry base.

The Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) is a four-year, Engineers Australia accredited degree covering the standard range of majors (civil, mechanical, electrical, chemical, mining, software, and others), with all students completing a common first year before choosing a major, giving some flexibility to switch specialisations early without losing time. A mandatory professional practice component (minimum weeks of industry experience) is built into the degree, and UQ's engineering placement office benefits from strong ties to Queensland's resources and infrastructure sectors as well as multinational engineering firms with Brisbane offices.

Final-year thesis projects are individually supervised and, for students in minerals, energy, or water-related majors, frequently connect to one of UQ's larger applied research centres rather than being a purely academic exercise, which gives some graduates a direct route into industry-sponsored postgraduate research if they want it.
curriculum:
Year 1 (common to all majors): Engineering Mathematics, Engineering Mechanics, Engineering Modelling and Problem Solving, Chemistry and Materials for Engineers
Year 2: Major-specific core units begin (Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, Chemical, Mining, Software, or other majors), Engineering Design, Thermodynamics/Fluid Mechanics (major-dependent)
Year 3: Advanced major units, Professional Practice (industry placement component), Engineering Management, Sustainability in Engineering
Year 4 (Honours): Advanced design units, Engineering Thesis (individual research project, often SMI-affiliated for minerals/resources-related majors), technical electives
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with ATAR of approximately 85+, prerequisite Mathematical Methods and Chemistry or Physics
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

The degree combines natural sciences with social and economic disciplines, decision-making and policy analysis, and includes a full semester of placement and practical experience alongside hands-on field and lab-based learning across Queensland's biodiversity hotspots, from coral reefs to World Heritage rainforests. Core courses include cultural heritage management, environmental impact assessment and conservation planning and management, with the embedded honours component adding a research dimension. Graduates typically move into roles such as environmental management consultant, sustainability adviser, natural resources manager or environmental planner in government or private consultancies.

Students planning careers helping elite athletes optimise performance, supporting community health and fitness, or working in rehabilitation and research settings use this degree to build both the science background and the practical hours accreditation bodies expect. Graduates go on to roles across sports academies and institutes, rehabilitation clinics, hospitals and research centres, applying biomechanics, physiology and psychology to turn research into training and recovery plans for individuals and teams across Australia and internationally.

name: Bachelor of Laws (Honours)
description:
UQ Law School is consistently rated among the top two or three in the country, and the LLB (Honours) benefits from that reputation in ways that show up in specific programs: its Pro Bono Centre places students in real supervised legal work with community legal centres and Legal Aid Queensland, and the law school runs one of the more active international mooting programs in Australia, regularly sending teams to competitions like the Willem C. Vis arbitration moot in Vienna.

Students take the LLB combined with another degree (arts, commerce, science, and others are common pairings), which stretches the program to five years but means graduates leave with genuine breadth rather than a law-only credential. UQ also has particular research strength in areas like international law and human rights, taught by academics with real practice or UN-adjacent backgrounds, and third and fourth-year elective offerings reflect that rather than sticking to a generic elective list.

Brisbane's legal market is smaller than Sydney's or Melbourne's, but UQ graduates dominate hiring at the state's top-tier firms and at the Queensland Bar, and the law school's clerkship placement rates into those firms are a large part of why the program remains competitive to enter despite Queensland having several other law schools to choose from.
curriculum:
Years 1-2: Legal Method and Reasoning, Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law, Property Law, plus first two years of paired degree (Arts, Commerce, Science, or other)
Years 3-4: Equity, Constitutional Law, Administrative Law, Corporations Law, Evidence, Civil and Criminal Procedure, continued paired degree units
Year 5 (honours): Advanced electives (options include International Law, Human Rights Law, Competition Law), honours thesis or advanced coursework, Professional Responsibility
Co-curricular: Pro Bono Centre placements, international mooting competitions
Practical Legal Training required post-graduation for admission as a solicitor
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with ATAR of approximately 95+
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0

name: Bachelor of Mathematics
description: The Bachelor of Mathematics at the University of Queensland offers more than 60 mathematics and statistics courses, more than any other university in the state, letting students specialise in areas such as mathematical artificial intelligence, optimisation and operations research, mathematical physics or pure mathematics. The Mathematical Artificial Intelligence major covers machine learning, data science and algorithm development, while Optimisation and Operations Research focuses on solving real logistical and efficiency problems for industry. Students can gain practical, real-world experience through UQ's Summer Industry Experience Program, working on live projects rather than only theoretical coursework. Core courses include calculus and linear algebra, methods and models of applied mathematics, and abstract algebra and number theory. Graduates typically move into roles such as data scientist, statistician, quantitative analyst or bioinformatician across finance, technology, healthcare and government.
curriculum: UQ calls subjects "courses" within this program. A sample of what you study includes: Calculus & Linear Algebra II [Core course], Methods & Models of Applied Mathematics [part of Applied Mathematics major], Operations Research & Mathematical Planning [part of Optimisation and Operations Research major], Algebraic Methods of Mathematical Physics [part of Mathematical Physics major], Deep Learning [part of Mathematical Artificial Intelligence major], Abstract Algebra & Number Theory [part of Pure Mathematics major], Problems & Applications in Modern Statistics [part of Statistics and Mathematical Data Science major], Bachelors of Music / Mathematics. The exact core versus elective structure depends on the major, specialisation or study plan chosen, and is confirmed in UQ's official program and course list at enrolment.

name: Bachelor of Medical Science (Exit award)
description: The Bachelor of Medical Science (Exit award) is granted at the University of Queensland to students enrolled in the Bachelor of Medical Science / Doctor of Medicine dual degree who complete the 2 year pre-medicine component, and typically a further stage of the Doctor of Medicine, before choosing or needing to leave the combined program early, since UQ approves an early exit after 3 years of this pathway. The full dual degree lets students graduate as a doctor at least a year earlier than traditional postgraduate medicine pathways, combining tailored pre-medicine study with a 4 year Doctor of Medicine, and covers traditional science and biomedical science alongside public health, humanities and computer science or information technology. A student exiting with the Bachelor of Medical Science keeps a recognised science degree covering that coursework, useful for roles in biomedical research, health administration, science communication or further postgraduate study, without the clinical training and registration pathway that completing the full Doctor of Medicine provides.
curriculum: This is an exit award from UQ's Bachelor of Medical Science / Doctor of Medicine dual degree, not a program with its own separate course list. The first 2 years (pre-medicine) cover 8 core foundational courses in Year 1 and 5 core courses plus 3 electives in Year 2, spanning traditional science, biomedical science, public health, humanities and computer science or information technology, before transitioning into Doctor of Medicine clinical coursework in later years.
admission_requirements: There is no direct entry pathway for this award. Students reach it only by first being admitted to and enrolling in UQ's Bachelor of Medical Science / Doctor of Medicine, which for domestic school leavers requires an adjusted ATAR of 95 or equivalent, Queensland Year 12 General English and Mathematical Methods (Units 3 and 4, C), a competitive UCAT ANZ score, and a multiple mini-interview.
english_requirements: As an exit award, English language requirements match UQ's Bachelor of Medical Science / Doctor of Medicine: IELTS Academic overall 7.0, with 7.0 in each of reading, writing, speaking and listening. PTE Academic overall 72, with a minimum of 72 in each communicative skill.

name: Bachelor of Midwifery
description: UQ's Bachelor of Midwifery is a 3-year program developed with midwifery academics, industry partners and parents themselves, training students to support women through pregnancy, labour, birth and the postpartum period. Clinical placement rostered shifts and simulated learning begin in first year, building toward extended clinical placements in the final year that manage the transition from student to practising midwife. Core courses include introduction to midwifery practice and clinical midwifery practice, and students who want to also qualify as a registered nurse can complete UQ's combined Bachelor of Nursing/Midwifery dual degree with just one extra year of study. Graduates typically move into hospital midwifery, community midwifery, antenatal care or international aid work, in a profession facing sustained demand across Australia's health system.
curriculum: UQ calls subjects "courses" within this program. A sample of what you study includes: Introduction to Midwifery Practice, Professional Practice 1, Bachelors of Nursing / Midwifery, Midwife, Community midwife, Antenatal midwife. name: Bachelor of Music (Honours)
description: UQ's Bachelor of Music (Honours) is a research-focused year for musicians who want to explore a specialist area of music in depth before moving into a professional or academic music career. Students combine advanced coursework with planning and completing a substantial research or creative project, developing independent investigation skills alongside performance, analysis and research work under close academic supervision. Core courses include research design in arts and culture, and the honours research thesis itself, taught by nationally and internationally recognised music academics and performers. The program is designed as a direct pathway into postgraduate music study and research as much as into performance careers. Typical graduate roles include music researcher, music critic, music tutor and music producer, alongside performance and composition careers.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description: The Bachelor of Nursing at the University of Queensland prepares students to become registered nurses through 880 hours of supervised clinical practice in real hospitals and healthcare facilities across Australia. The program was developed with healthcare professionals, industry partners and patients, and uses a narrative and inquiry-based teaching approach that integrates evidence-based theory with clinical practice from the first year, when students begin rostered clinical placement shifts and skills simulation. Core courses cover health across the lifespan, clinical nursing practice, older adults' health and acute care nursing, and students can pursue a combined Bachelor of Nursing/Midwifery dual qualification. Registered nurse graduates from UQ move into diverse settings including paediatric, critical care, mental health, rural health and aged care nursing, a profession with strong ongoing demand in Australia.

The embedded honours qualification is internationally recognised and can lead into further research or postgraduate study. Graduates typically register as occupational therapists, working in injury rehabilitation, disability services, aged care or paediatric settings.

name: Bachelor of Pharmaceutics and Therapeutic Science (exit award only)
description: The Bachelor of Pharmaceutics and Therapeutic Science (exit award only) is granted at the University of Queensland to students enrolled in the Bachelor of Pharmaceutics and Therapeutic Science / Doctor of Pharmacy dual degree who complete 48 units in years 1 to 3 but choose, or need, to leave before the Doctor of Pharmacy stage. The full 5 year dual degree trains students to work as registered pharmacists, with over 700 hours of supervised clinical placement across community pharmacy, hospital pharmacy and aged care beginning in year 2, and an optional major in Clinical and Experimental Therapeutics for students interested in a research project in areas like drug discovery. Honours is not available for this exit award. A student exiting after the bachelor stage keeps a recognised science qualification covering pharmaceutical and therapeutic science coursework and placement hours, useful for roles in pharmaceutical companies, laboratories or further study, but without the clinical training and registration that completing the full Doctor of Pharmacy provides.
curriculum: This is an exit award from UQ's Bachelor of Pharmaceutics and Therapeutic Science / Doctor of Pharmacy dual degree, not a program with its own separate course list. Students are awarded it after completing 48 units drawn from years 1 to 3 of that program, which include roughly 165 hours of supervised placement across community pharmacy, hospital pharmacy and aged care settings, before the Doctor of Pharmacy stage begins.
admission_requirements: There is no direct entry pathway for this award. Students reach it only by first being admitted to and enrolling in UQ's Bachelor of Pharmaceutics and Therapeutic Science / Doctor of Pharmacy, which requires Queensland Year 12 General English, General Mathematics, Mathematical Methods or Specialist Mathematics, and Chemistry (all Units 3 and 4, C), with Biology recommended.

name: Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours) at the University of Queensland trains students to become registered pharmacists, teaching safe, effective, patient-centred use of medicines alongside the technical knowledge needed to work as a medicines expert. Teaching happens in UQ's roughly $100 million biomedical science centre at Dutton Park, purpose-built with laboratories, mock dispensaries and simulated pharmacies, and includes two 6-week clinical placements plus an interprofessional education program with other health disciplines. Core courses include pharmacy practice and medicines management, pharmaceutical sciences, and pharmacokinetics and medicines management, building toward registration as a community, hospital or industrial pharmacist. The honours component gives the degree a research dimension beyond standard pharmacy registration training, and graduates describe the program's cohort as a close-knit professional community rather than a large lecture-only degree.

name: Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours)
description: UQ's Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours) trains students in the diagnostic and clinical skills needed to help patients recover from injury, manage chronic conditions and restore movement and function. The embedded honours qualification is internationally recognised and gives graduates the option of continuing into physiotherapy research after they finish. Typical graduate destinations include general physiotherapy practice, sports physiotherapy, community health physiotherapy or further clinical research.

name: Bachelor of Politics, Philosophy and Economics (Honours)
description: UQ's Bachelor of Politics, Philosophy and Economics (Honours) combines all three disciplines to prepare students for leadership careers in business, politics, the not-for-profit sector or academia. Core courses across introductory microeconomics, introduction to Australian politics, critical reasoning and introduction to ethics build a common foundation before students specialise in one area or continue across all three as a general path. A Work-Integrated Learning course lets students apply their theoretical knowledge to real business problems, and small, high-achieving cohorts create close academic relationships with teaching staff who hold a significant share of Australia's competitive research grants. A global study experience is built into the degree to give students an international network before they graduate. Typical graduate roles include economic policy adviser, political adviser, public commentator and diplomat.

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours)
description:
UQ's psychology school is one of the largest and most research-active in the country, with active labs in areas ranging from clinical and cognitive psychology to social identity research, the latter a genuine UQ specialty, given the school is home to some of the researchers behind widely cited social identity and group processes theory that gets taught internationally. The Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours) is a four-year embedded honours degree rather than a separate bolt-on year, meaning honours entry (competitive, GPA-gated) is built into the program's structure from the start rather than treated as an optional extra.

Because the school is so large, students get access to a wide spread of research areas for their honours thesis, supervised individually, and the school's own on-campus clinics (including for things like the treatment of anxiety and other clinical presentations) give some students supervised client-facing experience during their degree, a step up from purely coursework-based training.

The degree is APAC accredited, positioning graduates for further postgraduate training: provisional psychologist registration, and eventually a masters or doctorate in clinical, forensic, or organisational psychology, areas where UQ's own postgraduate programs are strong and where honours graduates get a genuine leg up in admission.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Bases of Behaviour, Social and Developmental Psychology, Statistics for Psychology
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Personality and Individual Differences, Research Methods, Abnormal Psychology
Year 3: Advanced Research Design and Statistics, Psychological Assessment, electives across clinical, social, and cognitive streams
Year 4 (Honours, competitive entry): Supervised empirical thesis, advanced seminars, research placement options
APAC accredited — pathway to provisional registration and postgraduate clinical, forensic, or organisational training
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with ATAR of approximately 88+
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Rehabilitation Studies (exit award only)
description: The Bachelor of Rehabilitation Studies (exit award only) is granted at the University of Queensland to students enrolled in either the Bachelor of Occupational Therapy (Honours) or the Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours) who complete 48 units drawn from years 1 to 3 of those programs but choose, or need, to leave before finishing the full honours qualification. Both parent degrees train students for allied health careers through more than 1,000 hours of supervised clinical practice across hospitals, schools and private practice, accredited by their respective national boards so that graduates can register with AHPRA. A student exiting with the Bachelor of Rehabilitation Studies keeps a recognised qualification covering the shared foundational coursework in anatomy, professional skills and client centred practice from either pathway, useful for allied health support roles or further study, but without the clinical placement hours or accreditation needed to register as an occupational therapist or physiotherapist.
curriculum: This is an exit award from UQ's Bachelor of Occupational Therapy (Honours) or Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours), not a program with its own separate course list. Students are awarded it after completing 48 units drawn from years 1 to 3 of either parent program, which include courses such as Systematic and Applied Anatomy, Introduction to Professional Skills in Occupational Therapy, and Promoting Participation through Occupation and the Environment, before the honours clinical year.
admission_requirements: There is no direct entry pathway for this award. Students reach it only by first being admitted to and enrolling in UQ's Bachelor of Occupational Therapy (Honours) or Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours), which require Queensland Year 12 General English and one of Biology, Chemistry or Physics (Units 3 and 4, C), with a minimum adjusted ATAR of 95.5 for occupational therapy in recent intakes.
