PTE Academic overall 72, with a minimum of 72 in each communicative skill.

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
UQ's Bachelor of Science is a broad, major-driven degree, and the range of majors on offer reflects some genuinely distinctive UQ research strengths: marine biology students get access to the Moreton Bay Research Station on Stradbroke Island for fieldwork, and students interested in genetics or molecular biology sit close to major research institutes like the Institute for Molecular Bioscience and the Australian Institute for Bioengineering and Nanotechnology, both based on the St Lucia campus, giving undergraduates a rare chance to see (and sometimes join) frontier research as an elective or vacation project.

Students choose one or two majors from a long list spanning the physical, life, earth, and mathematical sciences, and the flexibility to combine, say, ecology with data science, or physics with a second science major, is a genuine structural feature rather than marketing language. The degree's unit planner is built around combinability. A capstone science project or thesis in third year is common across most majors, giving students a taste of independent research before deciding whether to pursue honours.

Because UQ's science faculty is large and spread across many buildings and even campuses (Gatton for agriculture-adjacent majors, St Lucia for most others), the actual day-to-day experience varies a lot depending on chosen major. That's a fairly typical feature of large comprehensive science degrees at big research universities, but worth knowing rather than assuming a single unified experience.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundational units across chosen majors (Chemistry, Biology, Physics, Mathematics, Earth Sciences typically among first-year choices), Introduction to Scientific Practice
Year 2: Major-specific core units (one or two majors selected from options including Marine Biology, Genetics, Ecology, Physics, Data Science, Geology, Chemistry), Research Methods
Year 3: Advanced major units, Capstone Science Project, electives
Optional Year 4: Honours year with individual research thesis (competitive entry based on GPA)
Distinctive majors: Marine Biology (fieldwork at Moreton Bay Research Station), Genetics/Molecular Biology (research institute proximity)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with ATAR of approximately 80+, prerequisite Mathematical Methods
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Social Science
description: The Bachelor of Social Science at the University of Queensland examines social systems, inequality and human behaviour through disciplines including sociology, policy and community development, with strong links kept between theory and real-world practice throughout. Early courses cover social structures and policy before students specialise in one of three majors aligned with their career interests, and a supervised, year-long research project gives students hands-on experience conducting original social research. Core courses include introduction to the social sciences, political problems and public policy, and introduction to social research, and the degree can be combined with a Bachelor of Arts as a dual program. Teaching builds skills in policymaking, advocacy, public communication and project management that employers in the social and government sectors actively look for. Typical graduate roles include community development officer, social and government researcher, and community planning and policy adviser.

name: Bachelor of Social Work
description: UQ's Bachelor of Social Work qualifies graduates as registered social workers, training them to support individuals, families, groups and communities facing social exclusion or distress. Students complete 1,000 hours of supervised placement across settings including hospitals and public and private agencies, with the option to apply for a rural, interstate or international placement. Core courses include human development and social work, working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, and the moral and ethical foundations of social work, and teaching uses simulated client encounters so students can practise real-world responses before working with actual clients. Because the profession requires a higher IELTS band than most UQ undergraduate degrees, it is aimed at students with strong English proficiency. Graduates typically move into roles such as counsellor, child welfare worker, family therapist or community worker.

name: Bachelor of Speech Pathology (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Speech Pathology (Honours) at the University of Queensland trains students to assess, diagnose and treat communication and swallowing disorders across all ages, building on a program that has been training speech pathologists since 1962. From first year, students learn through inquiry-based and simulated learning experiences in UQ's purpose-built simulated hospital ward, working toward a tailored clinical placement program that covers settings from health promotion through to mental health and youth justice. Core courses include communication and swallowing across the lifespan, disability across the lifespan, and anatomy and neuroanatomy for speech pathologists, taught by internationally recognised researchers in the field. The honours qualification supports further clinical specialisation or research after graduation. Graduates commonly work as paediatric, disability, rehabilitation or private practice speech pathologists.

A sample of what you study includes: Communication and Swallowing Across the Lifespan, Disability Across the Lifespan, Mental Health and Justice, Anatomy and Neuroanatomy Fundamentals for Speech Pathologists, Private practice speech pathologist, Paediatric speech pathologist, Disability speech pathologist, Rehabilitation speech pathologist. The exact core versus elective structure depends on the major, specialisation or study plan chosen, and is confirmed in UQ's official program and course list at enrolment.

name: Bachelor of Tourism, Hospitality and Event Management
description: UQ's Bachelor of Tourism, Hospitality and Event Management prepares students for management careers across hotels, tourism operators and events, based in Brisbane, one of Australia's major tourist gateways. Students choose between a hotel and hospitality management major or a tourism and event management major, or combine both as a dual major, with core courses in sustainability in tourism and hospitality, visitor experience and marketing, and business information systems. The degree is built around practical exposure rather than classroom theory alone, including work placements, industry site visits, behind-the-scenes tours, and international internship opportunities such as a placement with Disney World Florida. Teaching staff bring current industry research and global sector trends into the classroom, and graduates typically move into roles such as hotel and resort manager, events producer, or food and beverage manager across the hospitality and tourism industry.

name: Bachelor of Urban Planning
description: UQ's Bachelor of Urban Planning is a 3-year degree that trains students to plan cities, towns and regions around challenges such as climate change, housing affordability, transport and population growth. From first semester, students work through design studios, field trips and community projects, and complete an industry placement working directly with government, community and industry partners. The curriculum covers land use, urban design, transport and infrastructure planning, heritage and conservation, environmental planning and planning law, grounded in culturally responsive and First Nations approaches to planning. Students can also get involved in UQ's student-run Organisation of Planning Students society to build leadership and networking skills alongside coursework. Graduates typically move into roles such as town planner, urban designer, regional development manager or spatial data specialist in government or private planning consultancies.

name: Bachelor of Veterinary Science (Honours)
description:
UQ's vet school is the oldest and one of the most internationally recognised in Australia, holding accreditation from the Australasian, American (AVMA), European, and Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons bodies simultaneously, a rare combination that lets graduates practice in a wider range of countries without extra certification than most other vet degrees allow. Most of the clinical years happen at the Gatton campus, about an hour west of Brisbane, where UQ operates its own teaching hospital plus large-animal and equine facilities that give students hands-on experience with production animals most city-based programs can't offer at the same scale.

The six-year Bachelor of Veterinary Science (Honours) folds a science-heavy first two years into increasingly clinical training, with extramural studies (externally supervised placements at private practices, zoos, and specialist referral hospitals) building up across the degree so students graduate with genuine caseload experience rather than only university clinic exposure. UQ's teaching hospital handles a real mixed caseload of companion animals, equine patients, and production animals, and students rotate through all three streams rather than specialising early.

Places are extremely competitive (among the hardest to gain entry to of any UQ program), and the honours research component in the final years gives students who want to go on to specialist veterinary residencies or research careers a genuine head start.
curriculum:
Years 1-2: Animal Biology, Biochemistry, Anatomy, Physiology, Animal Husbandry, Veterinary Pathology foundations (largely St Lucia campus)
Years 3-4: Clinical Sciences (companion animal, equine, production animal streams), Veterinary Pharmacology, Diagnostic Imaging, Surgery foundations (transition to Gatton campus)
Years 5-6: Clinical rotations through UQ Veterinary Medical Centre (small animal, equine, production animal), extramural studies placements at external practices, Honours research project
Extramural studies (externally supervised clinical placement weeks) required throughout later years
Accredited by AVBC, AVMA, EAEVE, and RCVS
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with ATAR of approximately 99+, prerequisite Chemistry
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0

name: Bachelor of Veterinary Technology
description: UQ's Bachelor of Veterinary Technology trains students as para-veterinary healthcare specialists, based at UQ's Gatton campus alongside its Small Animal Hospital and Equine Hospital. Core study covers basic sciences such as chemistry and biochemistry, animal handling, welfare and behaviour, applied and clinical nutrition, and diagnostic techniques for animal disease, with electives available in agribusiness, wildlife science and animal production. Students complete 14 weeks of clinical rotation and placement in third year, learning surgical and medical nursing principles and veterinary practice management alongside the small and large animal health curriculum. The program is taught by internationally regarded animal health academics and prepares graduates for a broad range of roles across clinical, commercial, research and diagnostic settings. Typical destinations include veterinary technician, veterinary nurse, laboratory technician and biosecurity officer roles.

name: Bachelor of Wildlife Science
description: The Bachelor of Wildlife Science at the University of Queensland combines zoology, ecology, conservation biology and animal husbandry to train students in protecting species, managing ecosystems and caring for animals in captivity. The first year is based at UQ's St Lucia campus, building a foundation in ecology and animal science, before students move between St Lucia and the Gatton campus in later years depending on their chosen major, such as Captive Wildlife Management. Field experience is built throughout the degree, drawing on Queensland's biodiversity and industry partnerships with Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary, Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary and Hidden Vale Research Station. A dedicated work-integrated learning course prepares students for the realities of wildlife careers rather than only classroom study. Typical graduate roles include environmental biologist, wildlife scientist, conservation officer and ecotourism guide.

name: Doctor of Clinical Dentistry
description: The Doctor of Clinical Dentistry at the University of Queensland is a 3-year postgraduate specialist training program for qualified general dentists working toward specialist registration in fields such as orthodontics, periodontics, prosthodontics, oral medicine or dento-maxillofacial radiology. Teaching and clinical placement take place at UQ's Oral Health Centre, a purpose-built $138 million facility on the Herston campus, with interdisciplinary patient care built into training from the first week. The periodontics stream is accredited by the European Federation of Periodontology, and the degree keeps a research focus running alongside clinical practice under academics with international standing in their specialty. Graduates move directly into specialist dental practice, working as orthodontists, periodontists, prosthodontists or dento-maxillofacial radiologists rather than as general dentists.
curriculum: UQ calls subjects "courses" within this program. A sample of what you will study includes: Clinical Science, Advanced clinical practice, Data Collection & Analyses, Research Completion & Report. The exact course list and any core versus elective structure depends on the specialisation and study plan you choose, and is confirmed in the program's official course list at enrolment.

Hold general or limited registration with the Dental Board of Australia. You must have a grade point average (GPA) of 4.0 on a 7-point scale in your previous qualification. name: Doctor of Medicine (MD)
description:
UQ's MD is one of the largest medical programs in Australia by enrolment, which comes with a genuinely unusual feature: a long-running dual accreditation partnership that lets a portion of the cohort complete significant clinical training at Ochsner Health in New Orleans, a legacy of UQ's original push into US-facing medical education in the early 2000s. Most students, though, train through Queensland's own network: Brisbane's major tertiary hospitals (Royal Brisbane and Women's, Princess Alexandra) plus an extensive regional and rural clinical school system stretching to Toowoomba, Rockhampton, Bundaberg, and further afield, reflecting Queensland's genuinely dispersed population and UQ's role in training doctors who will actually work outside the southeast corner.

The four-year graduate-entry MD (after a relevant bachelor's, GAMSAT, and interview) replaced the old MBBS structure, and its first eighteen months are organ-systems based with early clinical exposure through longitudinal GP placements, before students move into full hospital-based clinical rotations for the remainder of the degree.

Because so much of the clinical training happens in regional and rural settings, and because of the Ochsner option for eligible students, the actual training experience varies more between UQ MD students than at a program that keeps everyone in one metropolitan teaching hospital, something prospective applicants should factor in rather than assuming a single uniform experience.
curriculum:
Years 1-2 (pre-clinical/early clinical): Foundations of Medicine (organ systems-based), Clinical Skills, Population and Social Health, longitudinal general practice placements
Years 3-4 (clinical): Core rotations in medicine, surgery, psychiatry, obstetrics and gynaecology, paediatrics, general practice, emergency medicine — delivered through metropolitan teaching hospitals, regional clinical schools (Toowoomba, Rockhampton, Bundaberg), and rural placements
Ochsner Clinical School pathway: eligible students complete extended clinical rotations in New Orleans, USA
Electives and selectives in later clinical years; final-year preparation for internship
Entry: relevant bachelor's degree, GAMSAT, interview (MMI format)
admission_requirements: Completed bachelor degree in any discipline with a competitive GPA, plus GAMSAT and MMI interview
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0

name: Doctor of Philosophy (Architecture, creative arts, education, health, information technology, management and commerce, mathematical sciences, social and cultural studies)
description: This Doctor of Philosophy listing groups several broad University of Queensland research fields, including architecture, creative arts, education, health, information technology, business and commerce, mathematical sciences, and social and cultural studies. In practice UQ runs one PhD research degree and admits candidates by field and school rather than through separate program pages for each discipline group. A PhD at UQ is an internationally recognised research degree in which a candidate works independently, guided by an advisory team, to produce original research and an 80,000 word thesis, defended through an oral examination, typically over 3 to 4 years full-time. UQ enrols around 1,000 PhD candidates a year across its schools, with access to a Career Development Framework for building transferable research and professional skills alongside the thesis. Before applying, a prospective candidate needs to identify a research topic and either secure a supervisor or apply to join an existing project, since admission is assessed against that specific research proposal rather than a generic entry test.
curriculum: The Doctor of Philosophy is a research only degree with no set course list. Candidates work independently, guided by an advisory team, on an original research project in their chosen field, drawing on UQ's library, laboratory and research infrastructure, and complete an 80,000 word thesis plus an oral examination over roughly 3 to 4 years full-time. UQ also offers professional development through its Career Development Framework alongside the research itself.
admission_requirements: You need an approved university degree completed within the last 10 years, demonstrating research experience and capability. Acceptable qualifications include a Master of Philosophy or other research master's degree, a bachelor's degree with at least honours class IIA or equivalent, or a coursework master's degree with an overall grade point average (GPA) of 5.65 on UQ's 7-point scale.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5, with a minimum of 6.0 in each sub band, for most research fields; clinical research projects require an overall score of 7.0 with 7.0 in every sub band. See UQ's English language requirements page for accepted alternative tests.

name: Doctor of Veterinary Clinical Science
description: UQ's Doctor of Veterinary Clinical Science is a 3.5-year veterinary residency and doctoral program for already-qualified veterinarians working toward specialist certification. It combines clinical training in UQ's roughly $100 million veterinary facilities, including a small animal hospital, an equine specialist hospital and a diagnostic laboratory, with a research-based thesis of about 50,000 words. Coursework and supervised clinical work in a diagnostic laboratory or teaching hospital build specialist-level skills in areas such as case management, epidemiology and research methods, and count toward the degree alongside the thesis. UQ's veterinary program is accredited by the Australasian Veterinary Boards Council, the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons and the American Veterinary Medical Association, which supports international recognition of the qualification. Graduates typically become specialist veterinarians in fields such as anatomical pathology, anaesthesiology or equine surgery, in clinical practice, public health agencies or university research.
curriculum: This is UQ's veterinary residency doctorate: a 3.5-year, 56-unit program based at the Gatton campus combining supervised clinical training in an approved veterinary diagnostic laboratory or referral hospital with a research-based thesis of around 50,000 words. Coursework requirements are built around your clinical residency rather than a standard subject list, and the exact structure is confirmed with your supervisor and the UQ Graduate School before you enrol.
admission_requirements: Postgraduate degree in Veterinary Science of at least one year full-time equivalent including relevant experience and an overall GPA of 5; OR BVSc or equivalent plus two years relevant experience, or one year internship under the supervision of a registered veterinary specialist. Applicants must satisfy the Head of School and Dean of the Graduate School that they are qualified for admission, and may be required to attend an interview. Applicants must be eligible for registration with the Veterinary Surgeons Board of Queensland. Prerequisites BVSc(Hons) with honours class IIB or higher; OR Postgraduate degree in Veterinary Science of at least one year full-time equivalent including relevant experience and an overall GPA of 5; OR BVSc or equivalent plus two years relevant experience, or one year internship under the supervision of a registered veterinary specialist.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0; PTE Academic overall 72; TOEFL iBT overall 100. UQ also accepts Cambridge C1 Advanced, C2 Proficiency, OET and other approved English tests; see UQ's English language requirements page for the full sub band breakdown and alternative pathways.

name: Graduate Certificate in Agribusiness
description: The Graduate Certificate in Agribusiness is a half-year postgraduate program at UQ's St Lucia campus designed for recent business, agricultural or rural science graduates, and for established professionals moving into agribusiness. Over the program students gain specialised knowledge of agribusiness management alongside business and communication skills, taught by academics and industry experts who cover contemporary issues such as sustainability, globalisation, food security and international trade. Students learn how agribusinesses in different contexts can respond to global opportunities and challenges. It can serve as a standalone qualification or a pathway into the Graduate Diploma or Master of Agribusiness. Graduates work in agribusiness management, agricultural supply chains, trade and marketing, agri-finance and rural policy.

The program can be studied alone or as a pathway to the Graduate Diploma or Master of Agricultural Science. Graduates work in government, commercial, community and research roles across agronomy, crop and soil science, animal production and natural resource management.

Students select from more than 20 courses across genetics, breeding, nutrition, biosecurity, agronomy, agribusiness and human-wildlife interaction, along with business electives that build management ability. The program develops leadership, research and problem-solving skills aimed at the global challenges of feeding the world and maintaining the environment, and can lead into further study. It suits educators, language professionals and people working across cultures, starting with language structure, communication and language learning, then moving into multilingualism, language teaching and language use in different settings. Learning combines research-based study with practical analysis tasks. The program can be a standalone qualification or a pathway into the Master of Applied Linguistics. Graduates work in language teaching and curriculum, TESOL, editing and communication, language policy, and language-related research.

Because the program assumes no prior business training, it works well for career-changers moving from engineering, health, science or the arts into commercial roles such as digital marketing manager, campaign manager or change manager. Students explore the four core areas of the discipline: international theory, the development of the international system, international security and international political economy, along with diplomacy, international cooperation and global governance. name: Graduate Certificate in Learning Studies (Primary)
description: The Graduate Certificate in Learning Studies (Primary) is an exit award at the University of Queensland rather than a program you apply for directly. It is granted to students enrolled in UQ's Master of Teaching (Primary) who complete at least 8 units of that program's coursework and then choose, or need, to withdraw before finishing the full qualification. The certificate recognises the education theory and classroom foundations covered in the early part of the Master of Teaching (Primary), including child development, literacy and numeracy teaching and inclusive classroom practice, but it is not approved for teacher registration in Australia because it falls short of a full initial teacher education qualification. Students who want to teach in a Queensland primary school need to complete the full Master of Teaching (Primary) or an equivalent accredited program instead. Entry, coursework and English language requirements all mirror the parent Master of Teaching (Primary) program at the point a student is enrolled in it.
curriculum: This is an exit award from UQ's Master of Teaching (Primary), not a program with its own course list. Students are awarded the Graduate Certificate in Learning Studies (Primary) if they withdraw from the Master of Teaching (Primary) after successfully completing at least 8 units drawn from that program's course list, which covers areas such as contemporary theories of development and learning, introduction to teaching mathematics, building inclusive primary classrooms and teaching science. The certificate is not approved for teacher registration in Australia.

english_requirements: As an exit award, English language requirements match UQ's Master of Teaching (Primary): IELTS Academic overall 7.5, with a minimum of 8 in speaking and listening and 7 in reading and writing. PTE Academic, TOEFL iBT and several other tests are not accepted for this teaching qualification; see UQ's English language requirements page for the accepted test list.

Students learn in a multidisciplinary environment from radiographers, medical practitioners, medical physicists, chemists and engineers, with access to an advanced range of magnetic resonance instrumentation. Graduates work as MRI technologists and applications specialists in hospitals, imaging practices and industry.

name: Graduate Certificate in Molecular Biology

Students master techniques such as electrophoresis, polymerase chain reaction, endonuclease mapping and expression vectors, and develop advanced knowledge of genes and proteins, genome sequencing, recombinant DNA technology and macromolecular structure, with training in bioinformatics, molecular genetics and immunology. Work placements and practical training run alongside the theory. Graduates move into roles as in-house or freelance translators and interpreters, translation project managers, and interpreters in tourism, hospitality, health and legal settings, with local salary data for interpreters sitting in the 75,000 to 90,000 Australian dollar range.

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
UQ's MBA runs through the triple-accredited UQ Business School, which puts it in the same accreditation tier as a small number of the most established MBA programs in the Asia-Pacific, and the program leans on that reputation with a genuinely international student mix and an emphasis on global business context in its core case studies rather than a purely domestic Australian focus.

The full-time MBA includes an international study tour as a core component in most cohorts. Students travel as a group to a partner region (destinations have included parts of Asia and Europe in past cohorts) for a short but intensive period of company visits and comparative business study, which is a more substantial global-exposure element than a lot of competing Australian MBAs offer as standard. A capstone consulting project, done in teams for a real client organisation, functions as the practical culmination of the degree.

The program can be completed full-time or part-time, and UQ's career development team runs dedicated MBA-specific coaching and employer engagement events, reflecting the fact that most MBA students are mid-career professionals looking for a deliberate career pivot or acceleration rather than a first postgraduate qualification.

Core units: Financial Management, Strategic Marketing, Managerial Economics, Leadership and Organisational Behaviour, Operations Management, Business Analytics and Decision Making
International component: Global Business Study Tour (company visits and comparative study in a partner region)
Electives: choose from streams including entrepreneurship, finance, marketing, health management
Capstone: Strategy Consulting Project (team-based, real client organisation)
Full-time (approx. 1.5 years) or part-time delivery available

name: Master of Computer Science
description:
UQ's computer science research sits inside the School of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering, and the Master of Computer Science draws directly on ITEE's active groups in machine learning, computer vision, and data science rather than existing as a standalone teaching-only degree. Students in the AI-heavy specialisations regularly cross paths with PhD candidates and postdocs in shared labs, which is a genuinely different experience from a pure coursework master's.

The degree is designed as a professional entry qualification for computing, split into an extended (for students without a computing background) and standard pathway (for those with a relevant bachelor's), a structure UQ uses to funnel students from unrelated undergrad degrees, engineering, science, even arts, into software careers without demanding they redo an entire CS bachelor's. Specialisations include artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and software engineering, and the capstone project unit typically pairs students with either an academic research group or, less often, an industry partner sourced through UQ's employability programs.

St Lucia's tech employer proximity is modest compared to Sydney or Melbourne, but Brisbane's tech sector (particularly in gov-tech and health-tech, given Queensland Health's large IT footprint) has grown enough that local placement and graduate hiring pipelines are reasonably active for students who don't want to relocate after finishing.
curriculum:
Extended pathway (no computing background): foundation units in programming, data structures, and discrete mathematics before core coursework
Core coursework: Algorithms and Data Structures, Software Engineering Practice, Programming Languages, Database Systems, Computer Systems
Specialisation (choose one): Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Software Engineering, Data Science
Capstone: Master's Project (research-group or industry-partnered, one to two semesters depending on specialisation)
Standard pathway (relevant bachelor's): condensed core plus specialisation and capstone, typically 1.5 to 2 years
admission_requirements: GPA 5.0/7.0 in a bachelor's degree in computer science or software engineering (1.5-year track), or a bachelor honours degree with broader CS/IT discipline content (1-year track).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall; 6.0 minimum in each of reading, writing, speaking, listening.

description: UQ's Master of Cyber Security is designed for students who want to lead cyber security strategy at a technological, organisational or policy level, not only work as a technical specialist. The program covers cryptography, cyber criminology, cyber defence and leadership, developed in partnership with industry and government experts in response to Australia's projected shortfall of roughly 18,000 cyber security professionals by 2026. Students study alongside a cohort from diverse backgrounds spanning technology, business, mathematics, social science and law, then complete an industry or research-based project to build workforce-ready experience. It is one of the first Australian programs built around this deliberately interdisciplinary approach to cyber security rather than a purely technical curriculum. Typical graduate roles include cyber security analyst, security consultant, chief information security officer pathway roles and cyber policy adviser.

name: Master of Data Science
description:
UQ's Master of Data Science is a joint offering between the School of Mathematics and Physics and ITEE, which in practice means the curriculum leans more heavily on statistical theory and mathematical foundations than a lot of competing data science master's programs that are essentially applied-CS degrees with a statistics unit bolted on: students spend real time on probability theory and statistical inference before getting to the machine learning and big-data-systems units.

The program is designed to take students from varied undergraduate backgrounds (maths, science, commerce, engineering) through to job-ready data science skills, with an extended pathway for students needing foundational programming or statistics coursework first. UQ's genuine research strength in areas like computational biology and bioinformatics (there's a large research presence in these fields at UQ, including at the Institute for Molecular Bioscience) means some students end up doing capstone projects with an unusually strong life-sciences data flavour compared to the finance- or tech-heavy capstones typical elsewhere.

Brisbane's data science job market is smaller than Sydney's or Melbourne's, but Queensland Health, mining and agribusiness analytics, and a growing gov-tech sector provide a reasonably steady set of local capstone and graduate employer partners for students who complete the program.

Foundation units (extended pathway only): Programming Fundamentals, Introductory Statistics

Capstone: Data Science Project (industry or research-group partnered, one to two semesters)

description: This Master of Philosophy listing groups several broad University of Queensland research fields, including architecture, creative arts, education, health, information technology, business and commerce, mathematical sciences, and social and cultural studies. In practice UQ runs one Master of Philosophy research degree and admits candidates by field and school rather than through separate program pages for each discipline group. An MPhil is a research only postgraduate degree in which a candidate works with an advisory team on an original research project, culminating in a 40,000 word thesis and an oral examination, typically over 1.5 to 2 years full-time. UQ enrols around 500 MPhil candidates a year, and many go on to convert into a PhD once their research is underway. Before applying, a prospective student needs to identify a research topic and a confirmed thesis supervisor within the relevant school, since admission is assessed against that specific proposal rather than a generic entry test.
curriculum: The Master of Philosophy is a research only degree with no set course list. name: Master of Public Health
description:
UQ's School of Public Health is one of the largest and most research-active in Australia, and the Master of Public Health draws on that scale to offer a genuinely wide set of specialisation streams, including epidemiology, health policy, global health, and environmental health, rather than the generic single-track MPH some smaller schools offer. A meaningful share of the cohort each year is international, often mid-career health professionals from across Asia and the Pacific, which shapes case discussions toward genuinely global health system comparisons rather than an Australia-only lens.

The program includes a substantial applied component: most students complete either a supervised field placement with a health organisation (government health departments, NGOs, or research units) or a research-based project, and UQ's public health research strength in areas like infectious disease modelling and Indigenous health gives some students access to genuinely active research groups for their placement or project supervision.

Because the degree can be tailored heavily through electives, two MPH graduates can come out with quite different skill profiles: one epidemiology and biostatistics-heavy, another policy and health systems-focused. That's a deliberate design feature for a workforce that includes clinicians, policy analysts, and program managers all under the one degree title.
curriculum:
Core units: Foundations of Public Health, Biostatistics, Epidemiology, Health Policy and Systems, Global Health
Specialisation streams (choose one or combine electives): Epidemiology, Health Promotion, Environmental Health, Global Health, Health Economics
Applied component: Field Placement (supervised with a health organisation) or Research Project
Capstone: Public Health Project or Practicum, integrating specialisation coursework
Delivered over 1.5 to 2 years full-time equivalent, part-time options available
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in any discipline plus 1 year relevant healthcare work experience, or graduate certificate/diploma in a relevant discipline, GPA 4.0/7.0

name: Master of Speech Pathology Studies
description: The Master of Speech Pathology Studies is an accelerated two-year postgraduate program at UQ's St Lucia campus for students who have completed an undergraduate degree, qualifying them as speech pathologists. Students build on their existing qualifications, expanding theoretical knowledge and professional attributes while gaining the clinical and research skills to graduate with confidence. Graduates work as speech pathologists in hospitals, community and aged care, schools, private practice, disability services and research.

name: Master of Sustainable Energy
description: The Master of Sustainable Energy is a 1.5-year postgraduate program at UQ's St Lucia campus that builds the skills to tackle global energy challenges and the shift to a low-carbon future. Students learn from academics, researchers and industry practitioners about energy generation, distribution and supply, and the transition to sustainable energy, in a flexible structure designed to fit around work. Graduates work in energy policy and planning, renewable energy projects, energy analytics and management across utilities, industry, consulting and government.

name: Master of Teaching (Primary)
description: The Master of Teaching (Primary) at the University of Queensland is a 4-semester graduate-entry qualification for students who already hold an undergraduate degree and want to become registered primary school teachers. Early study covers child development, curriculum design and contemporary theories of learning, before extended professional placements, 60 days of supervised classroom experience in total, let students apply teaching approaches in real Queensland schools. Core courses include introduction to teaching mathematics, building inclusive primary classrooms and teaching science, taught by lecturers with national and international teaching awards. The program is accredited for teacher registration in Queensland and other Australian states, with the option to teach internationally afterwards. Because Queensland teacher registration requires a higher English band than most UQ postgraduate programs, applicants need stronger IELTS scores than a typical master's degree. Graduates typically register as primary school teachers or move into curriculum leadership roles.
curriculum: UQ calls subjects "courses" within this program. The exact course list and any core versus elective structure depends on the specialisation and study plan you choose, and is confirmed in the program's official course list at enrolment.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for entry, you'll need: a bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in any discipline, which includes one year of full-time equivalent study in areas relevant to one or more learning areas of the primary school curriculum in Australian schools (see below). You must have a grade point average (GPA) of 4.0 on a 7-point scale in your previous qualification. Please refer to the School of Education website for further information on entry requirements and becoming a teacher.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.5. UQ also accepts Cambridge C1 Advanced, C2 Proficiency, OET and other approved English tests; see UQ's English language requirements page for the full sub band breakdown and alternative pathways.

name: Master of Tourism, Hotel and Event Management
description: The Master of Tourism, Hotel and Event Management is a postgraduate program at UQ's St Lucia campus that builds the business acumen and professional skills to create exceptional customer and visitor experiences. Students tailor their studies through a choice of specialisation and electives and take part in industry engagement opportunities, in an internationally recognised qualification. Graduates work in destination and hotel management, event planning and production, tourism marketing, and visitor experience roles in Australia and internationally.
curriculum: UQ calls subjects "courses" within this program. The exact course list and any core versus elective structure depends on the specialisation and study plan you choose, and is confirmed in the program's official course list at enrolment.

name: Master of Urban Development and Design
description: UQ's Master of Urban Development and Design trains students to approach cities strategically and holistically, treating urban design as its own discipline rather than a specialism borrowed from architecture or planning. Core courses include urban design: urban futures, contemporary urbanism theory and practice, and urban design: responsive environments, alongside a course in managing organisational behaviour for students who will lead urban projects. The program is aimed at addressing growing global demand for urban designers who can respond to limited resources, population growth and climate change with a strategic view of how cities work rather than one-off design solutions. It suits both working professionals and graduates from architecture, planning or related fields who want to specialise further. Typical graduate roles include urban designer, urban strategist, community engagement consultant and landscape architect.
curriculum: UQ calls subjects "courses" within this program. A sample of what you will study includes: Urban Design: Urban Futures, Contemporary Urbanism Theory and Practice, Urban Design: Responsive Environments, Managing Organisational Behaviour. The exact course list and any core versus elective structure depends on the specialisation and study plan you choose, and is confirmed in the program's official course list at enrolment.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for entry, you'll need a bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in a relevant discipline such as architecture, architectural design, design, landscape architecture, planning, regional and town planning, or urban planning, or a graduate certificate, graduate diploma or master's degree in a relevant discipline (GPA 4.5 on a 7-point scale), or a relevant bachelor's degree plus 6 months full-time equivalent relevant postgraduate work experience in an urban design environment (GPA 4.0). Relevant work experience must be supported by a signed employer letter detailing your role, duties and length of employment.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5; TOEFL iBT overall 87. UQ also accepts Cambridge C1 Advanced, C2 Proficiency, OET and other approved English tests; see UQ's English language requirements page for the full sub band breakdown and alternative pathways.

name: Master of Urban Planning
description: The Master of Urban Planning at the University of Queensland is an accredited qualification from the Planning Institute of Australia, aimed at professionals or graduates ready to move into leadership and advisory roles in city planning. Students choose a field of study in Environment and Sustainability, Urban Analytics, or Research in Urbanism, and build advanced expertise across transport and infrastructure planning, environmental planning, statutory planning and community engagement. Coursework is built around authentic planning challenges worked through with industry, government and community stakeholders rather than only theoretical case studies, taught by academics who are also practising planners. It suits graduates of the Bachelor of Urban Planning or a related discipline who want formal accreditation and advanced skills rather than an entry-level qualification. Typical graduate roles include urban planner, strategic planner, urban strategist and research analyst in government planning departments or consultancies.
curriculum: This 32-unit program (2-year full pathway, or a 1.5-year pathway with 8 units of recognised prior learning) combines foundation courses such as Applied Demography, Urban Innovations, Urban Law and Regulation, and Transport Planning with core courses including Planning Systems and Governance, Planning for Social Change, Urban Infrastructure Transitions, Data Science and Technology for Planners, Urban Policy Impact Lab, and Urban Design: Urban Futures. Students then choose a Field of Study such as Environment and Sustainability, Research in Urbanism, or Urban Analytics, plus program or general electives.
admission_requirements: This program has two entry pathways. For the 2-year, 32-unit degree you need a bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in any discipline, except qualifications accredited by the Planning Institute of Australia, with a GPA of 4.5 on a 7-point scale. For the accelerated 1.5-year, 24-unit degree (using recognised prior learning) you need a bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline such as urban or regional planning, architecture, urban design, environment, design, engineering or geography, or a bachelor's degree in a non-relevant discipline plus 2 years full-time equivalent relevant work experience in urban and regional planning, again with a GPA of 4.5.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5; TOEFL iBT overall 87. UQ also accepts Cambridge C1 Advanced, C2 Proficiency, OET and other approved English tests; see UQ's English language requirements page for the full sub band breakdown and alternative pathways.

name: Master of Urban Water Engineering (Professional)
description: The Master of Urban Water Engineering (Professional) at the University of Queensland is an Engineers Australia accredited degree that trains engineers to manage the whole urban water cycle, from drinking water supply through to wastewater treatment. Core courses cover drinking water supply source, treatment and distribution, and sewer network design, operation and maintenance, addressing a global shortage of engineers who understand how the different parts of the urban water system interact. The program responds directly to growing water stress in dense, urbanising cities, a trend UQ expects to continue rather than reverse. Students can select electives to complement their existing engineering background, and the degree suits civil or environmental engineers moving into water-specific specialisation. Typical graduate roles include wastewater treatment engineer, urban engineer and water infrastructure consultant.
curriculum: UQ calls subjects "courses" within this program. The exact course list and any core versus elective structure depends on the specialisation and study plan you choose, and is confirmed in the program's official course list at enrolment.

english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5; TOEFL iBT overall 87. UQ also accepts Cambridge C1 Advanced, C2 Proficiency, OET and other approved English tests; see UQ's English language requirements page for the full sub band breakdown and alternative pathways.

name: Master of Writing, Editing and Publishing
description: The Master of Writing, Editing and Publishing is a postgraduate program at UQ's St Lucia campus covering the full writing and publishing process, from creative writing and publishing to workplace communication and digital content. Students learn from award-winning authors and publishing professionals, including UQ Press and Corella Press, building a foundation across publishing practice, workplace writing, editing techniques and digital storytelling before shaping their studies around creative or professional interests. Graduates work in publishing, editing, content, communications and freelance writing.

name: Associate Degree of Medical Laboratory Science
Bachelor of Agricultural Technology and Management
description:
UniSQ describes this as Queensland's first dedicated degree in agricultural technology and management, and the pitch is specific: it sits between traditional agricultural science and straight agribusiness, training students to apply precision-ag and digital technology to farm systems rather than just studying plant and animal science in the abstract or business theory divorced from paddock reality. Students based at Toowoomba get direct access to the working farming and agtech industries of the Darling Downs, one of Australia's most productive agricultural regions, and the course can also be completed externally for students already working in the sector.

At 24 units it's a leaner degree than most three-year bachelor's programs, built around agricultural science fundamentals (plant and animal production systems), the technology layer (precision agriculture, remote sensing, farm data systems), and the management side (agribusiness, supply chains, farm business decision-making). Work-integrated learning and industry placement units are built into the structure, which matters in a discipline where employers routinely rate practical exposure above classroom theory.

Graduates are aimed at roles in agronomy support, farm technology and precision-ag consulting, agribusiness management, and agricultural data analysis, a narrower but more targeted set of outcomes than a general agricultural science degree, reflecting the technology-and-management framing the course was actually built around.
curriculum:
Year 1: Plant production systems, animal production systems, introduction to agricultural technology, farm business fundamentals
Year 2: Precision agriculture and remote sensing, soil and water management, agribusiness and supply chains, agricultural data systems
Year 3: Farm business management and decision-making, industry placement/work-integrated learning, capstone agricultural technology project, elective units in a chosen specialisation
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, no specific ATAR cut-off; suited to students from rural and regional backgrounds, with articulation pathways from the Diploma of Agriculture and Environmental Science Studies.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0, or equivalent.

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
UniSQ's Bachelor of Business follows the standard flexible-major structure most Australian business schools use now: a shared first-year core across accounting, economics, marketing, and management, then students pick a major: accounting, marketing, management, human resource management, tourism, or a handful of others, and build the back two years around it. What sets the delivery apart is less the content than the mode: a large share of the cohort studies wholly online, and the university has built its systems around that being the default rather than an add-on for people who can't make it to campus.

The degree carries professional accreditation pathways relevant to its majors, the accounting major is designed to meet the academic requirements for CPA Australia and CA ANZ membership, for instance, so students with a specific professional body in mind can check their major choice against that requirement early rather than discovering a gap in final year.

A capstone business project or internship unit toward the end of the degree gives students a chance to apply what they've studied to an actual organisational problem, and the university's regional business networks around Toowoomba and southeast Queensland feed a reasonable number of those placements.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting principles, economics, marketing fundamentals, management and organisational behaviour, business law, business statistics
Year 2: Major core units (accounting, marketing, management, HR, or tourism strand), business analytics, financial management
Year 3: Advanced major units, strategic management, capstone business project or industry placement, elective units
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Queensland Certificate of Education) or equivalent, ATAR of approximately 60-65 or equivalent; no prerequisite subjects required.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0, or equivalent.

name: Bachelor of Design and Interactive Technologies
Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description:
Primary teaching at UniSQ is a four-year initial teacher education degree accredited against the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers, and it leads to registration as a primary school teacher on graduation. That's the standard shape for this qualification nationally, but UniSQ's version leans on its regional footprint for placement variety, with school partnerships across the Darling Downs, Ipswich, and wider southeast Queensland giving students a mix of regional and larger-town classroom experience rather than an exclusively metropolitan one.

Curriculum studies units cover the primary learning areas (literacy, numeracy, science, HASS, health and PE, the arts) alongside professional units in child development, inclusive education, and classroom management, with supervised professional experience placements building in length and responsibility each year, from observation-heavy early placements to a substantial final-year internship where students effectively run a classroom under a mentor teacher's supervision.

A sizeable share of the cohort studies externally, particularly students already working as teacher aides or in regional schools, and the degree is structured so placement blocks can be arranged around a student's existing location rather than requiring relocation to a university city.
curriculum:
Year 1: Child development, introduction to teaching and learning, foundations of literacy and numeracy, first professional experience placement
Year 2: Curriculum studies (English, mathematics, science), inclusive education, classroom management, professional experience placement
Year 3: Curriculum studies (HASS, the arts, health and PE), assessment and reporting, Indigenous perspectives in education, extended professional experience placement
Year 4: Advanced pedagogy, professional capstone unit, final internship placement (extended, near-autonomous teaching)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, ATAR of approximately 60-65 or equivalent, plus satisfactory completion of the Literacy and Numeracy Test for Initial Teacher Education (LANTITE) prior to final-year professional experience placement.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with no band below 7.0 (or equivalent), reflecting Queensland teacher registration standards.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
Ask most Queensland engineering academics who teaches the most students by distance and UniSQ's name comes up first: the university has run distance-education engineering programs for more than four decades and is Australia's largest provider of engineering degrees delivered off-campus. The Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) is the degree that carries that reputation, and it shows in how the labs are built: UniSQ's Remote Access Laboratories let external students run real instrumentation and measurement experiments over the internet rather than substituting simulations for hands-on work.

Students choose a major from the usual spread (civil, electrical and electronic, mechanical, mechatronic, power, and others) and the degree is accredited by Engineers Australia, so graduates sit the same accreditation bar as anyone from a metro sandstone university. A supervised professional placement is built into the course, which matters more than it sounds for a program with a large external cohort: it's the mechanism that gets distance students onto an actual work site before graduation, not just into a classroom.

The university has also been ranked Australia's number one for graduate starting salary by the Good Universities Guide, a data point UniSQ leans on in its own marketing but which is at least consistent with an engineering-heavy graduate profile. Whether a given student is based in Toowoomba, Springfield, or studying entirely online from a mine site or a regional town, the course structure and assessment are designed to be identical, which is unusual enough among Australian engineering schools to be worth naming directly.
curriculum:
Years 1-2: Engineering mathematics and mechanics, engineering materials, engineering computing, professional engineering practice, discipline foundation units (statics, thermofluids, circuits depending on major)
Year 3: Major-specific core units (e.g. structural analysis for civil, power systems for electrical, machine design for mechanical), engineering management, project management
Year 4: Capstone engineering project (two-part), professional placement/work-integrated learning, advanced major electives, engineering law and ethics
Throughout: Remote Access Laboratory sessions and residential schools for practical/lab components
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with sound achievement in English and Mathematics (Methods or equivalent recommended), ATAR of approximately 70-75 or equivalent; a Preparatory year is available for students who do not meet prerequisites.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0, or equivalent.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
This is the entry-level computing degree UniSQ builds its whole postgraduate IT pipeline around. Finish it and the university explicitly points graduates toward its Master of Information Technology, Master of Data Science, or Master of Cyber Security as the next step, which tells you something about how the undergraduate course is structured: broad enough in first year to let students discover which specialisation actually interests them, then increasingly focused from second year on.

Majors run through the usual spread for a modern IT degree, including software development, cyber security, networking, data science and analytics, and programming-heavy units are backed by UniSQ's long-running remote/online lab infrastructure, the same systems that support its distance engineering cohort, so external students aren't working with a lesser version of the practical content.

A professional placement or capstone project unit near the end of the course gives students something concrete to point to in job interviews beyond a transcript, and the degree's accreditation alignment with the Australian Computer Society matters for students planning to chase ACS-recognised professional status after graduation.
curriculum:
Year 1: Programming fundamentals, computer systems, database fundamentals, web technologies, IT professional practice
Year 2: Major core units (software development, cyber security, networking, or data science strand), systems analysis and design, data structures and algorithms
Year 3: Advanced major electives, IT project management, capstone IT project or industry placement, emerging technologies elective
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, ATAR of approximately 60-65 or equivalent; no specific prerequisite subjects, though Mathematics is recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0, or equivalent.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Nursing at UniSQ is delivered from a regional base (Toowoomba and Ipswich rather than inner-city Brisbane), which shapes where a lot of its clinical placements happen: students get real exposure to rural and regional health settings that metro-heavy nursing schools often can't offer as standard, alongside placements in larger hospital systems. The degree is accredited by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, and graduates sit for AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse on completion.

The course structure follows the pattern most Australian nursing degrees use: foundational anatomy, physiology, and pharmacology units in first year, building toward specialty clinical units (mental health, paediatrics, aged care, acute care) in second and third year, with supervised clinical placement hours threaded through every year rather than saved for the end. UniSQ's placement network covers regional Queensland health services as well as metropolitan hospitals, which is a genuine point of difference for students who want experience in under-served health systems before they graduate into them.

Students who want to keep studying can move directly into UniSQ's Master of Nursing for a postgraduate specialisation, and the university markets a fairly direct undergraduate-to-postgraduate nursing pipeline for exactly that reason.
curriculum:
Year 1: Anatomy and physiology, foundations of nursing practice, pharmacology basics, communication in health care, introductory clinical placement
Year 2: Mental health nursing, medical-surgical nursing, pathophysiology, health assessment, clinical placement blocks
Year 3: Acute and critical care nursing, aged care and chronic illness, paediatric and family nursing, transition to professional practice, capstone clinical placement
Throughout: Supervised clinical placements across regional and metropolitan health settings, professional experience portfolio
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (Queensland Certificate of Education) or equivalent, no specific ATAR cut-off, plus a Health Undertaking and National Police Check; relevant recognition of prior learning available for enrolled nurses.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with no band below 6.5, or equivalent (higher than most UniSQ programs due to nursing registration requirements).

name: Bachelor of Psychology (Honours)
description:
UniSQ's Bachelor of Psychology (Honours) is a four-year, APAC-accredited sequence built for students who already know they want provisional registration at the end of it, not just a psychology-adjacent arts degree. The first three years share a common set of foundational units with the university's other psych-flavoured degrees, so students who start here and change their mind about the honours pathway aren't locked in early. The divergence happens later, once the fourth-year research component kicks in.

That fourth year is where the degree earns its name. Students complete an honours research project (PSY4000) alongside units in advanced research methods, ethical and professional practice, and applied assessment and intervention skills, working under the supervision of academic staff who are themselves practising or research psychologists. Because a large share of UniSQ's cohort studies externally, the clinical and assessment skills components are built around structured on-campus intensives and simulated client work rather than assuming everyone is walking past a psych clinic on campus daily.

Graduates come out eligible for provisional registration as a psychologist with AHPRA, which is the real value proposition of choosing the Honours pathway over a plain Bachelor's: it's the entry ticket to supervised practice or further postgraduate study toward general or clinical registration. UniSQ explicitly positions this degree as a pipeline into its own Master of Professional Psychology, so students planning that far ahead can map out a five-plus-one style progression from day one.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Psychology, Lifespan Development, Social Psychology, foundational research methods and statistics units
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Psychological Measurement, Abnormal Psychology, Personality Theory, intermediate quantitative and qualitative research methods
Year 3: Health Psychology, Psychology of Learning, Applied research design, discipline elective units, work-integrated learning options
Year 4 (Honours): PSY4111 Advanced Research Approaches, PSY4020 Ethical and Professional Practice, PSY4040 Psychological Interventions, PSY4070 Assessment and Interview Skills, PSY4000 Psychology Honours Project (thesis)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, ATAR of approximately 65-70 or equivalent; competitive entry into the honours component based on GPA in earlier years.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0, or equivalent.

name: Graduate Certificate of Sport and Exercise
Master of Business Administration
description:
UniSQ's MBA follows the generalist model most Australian MBAs use: core units across strategy, finance, marketing, leadership, and organisational behaviour, aimed at experienced professionals moving into or already working in management roles rather than fresh graduates. Where it departs from the metro-university MBA template is delivery: it's built primarily for students studying externally while working full-time, which shapes the assessment design around applied, workplace-relevant projects rather than assuming students have time for extended residential intensives.

Students typically bring several years of workplace experience into the cohort, and case studies and group assignments lean on that mix of industries and seniority levels rather than assuming a uniform corporate background. A capstone strategic management project toward the end of the degree asks students to apply the accumulated coursework to a real organisational problem, often drawn from their own workplace.

The degree doesn't chase the specific big-name accreditations (AACSB, EQUIS) that the most prestige-focused Australian MBAs market heavily, and is positioned instead as an accessible, flexible option for regional and remote professionals who need postgraduate business credentials without relocating or taking time off work.
curriculum:
Core units: Strategic management, managerial finance, marketing management, organisational behaviour and leadership, business economics, operations management
Elective units: Selected from specialisations such as project management, human resource management, or international business
Capstone: Strategic management project (applied, often workplace-based)
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree plus at least two years of professional work experience, or a graduate certificate/diploma in a related discipline; delivered fully online.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0, or equivalent.
intake_dates: February, April, July, September, November (online, multiple study periods)

name: Master of Data Science
description:
The Master of Data Science runs on twelve core ICT and analytics units rather than a long menu of loosely related electives, which keeps the degree tight: statistics, machine learning, big data systems, and data visualisation are treated as the spine of the course rather than optional add-ons bolted onto a generic IT masters. Students coming in with an undergraduate background outside computing typically pick up a set of foundation units first to bring their programming and stats up to postgraduate speed before moving into the specialist content.

What distinguishes it from a lot of similarly-named degrees elsewhere is that it's taught by a university that has spent decades building distance-delivery infrastructure, so the heavily technical, lab-based components (model building, data pipeline work, visualisation projects) are designed from the ground up for students working through them off-campus, often while employed full-time. A capstone project lets students apply the full analytics pipeline to a real or realistic dataset, which is the piece employers tend to ask about at interview.

Graduates leave positioned for data analyst, data engineer, or junior data scientist roles, and the degree sits alongside UniSQ's Master of Information Technology and Master of Cyber Security as one of three postgraduate computing options the university actively cross-promotes to its own IT undergraduates.
curriculum:
Foundation units (where required): Programming fundamentals, database systems, introductory statistics
Core: Data wrangling and management, statistical modelling, machine learning, big data technologies, data visualisation, data ethics and governance, cloud computing for data science
Capstone: Data science project (industry or research-based)
Maximum candidature: six years part-time, allowing for concurrent full-time work
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant or any discipline (typical Australian postgrad IT/CS entry bar used as approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Master of Education
description:
UniSQ's Master of Education is aimed at people already teaching, not career-changers looking for an initial qualification. It's a postgraduate degree for practising educators who want to specialise or move into leadership, and the course design assumes students are working full-time in schools while they study. Specialisation strands typically cover areas like educational leadership, TESOL, inclusive education, and curriculum studies, and students can usually shape a chunk of the degree around whichever of those matches their actual career direction.

Because the degree sits within a university whose delivery model has been built around distance and online study for decades, assessment is structured around what a working teacher can realistically produce alongside a full timetable: applied projects and research tied to the student's own school context rather than requiring long stretches of campus attendance.

A research-focused exit option (often a minor thesis or major project) exists for teachers considering a later move into doctoral study or educational research roles, alongside the more common coursework-only completion for those staying in the classroom or moving into middle leadership.
curriculum:
Core units: Educational research methods, contemporary issues in education, leading learning and teaching
Specialisation units (select strand): Educational leadership, TESOL, inclusive and special education, or curriculum and pedagogy
Elective units: Drawn from education specialisations or cross-disciplinary options
Exit options: Coursework-only completion, or research project/minor thesis pathway for those considering further postgraduate research
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, normally in education or a related field, or a bachelor degree plus relevant professional teaching experience; designed for practising teachers seeking specialisation or career progression.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0, or equivalent (reflecting teacher registration requirements).

name: Master of Nursing
description:
This is UniSQ's postgraduate specialisation route for registered nurses who've finished their undergraduate degree and want to move into advanced clinical practice, education, or leadership rather than staying at generalist RN level indefinitely. It's built for working nurses: the majority of the cohort studies externally while holding down clinical shifts. Specialisation strands typically include areas like nurse practitioner preparation, clinical leadership, or nurse education, depending on which stream a student enrols in.

Coursework covers advanced clinical assessment, evidence-based practice, and health systems leadership, with a research or applied project component that lets students investigate a genuine clinical or workplace issue rather than a hypothetical one. Given UniSQ's Bachelor of Nursing graduates are steered toward this degree as the next step, there's a reasonably well-worn pathway from RN registration through to postgraduate specialisation within the one institution.

Students pursuing the nurse practitioner stream complete additional advanced practice and prescribing units alongside supervised clinical hours, positioning them for endorsement as nurse practitioners, a role with growing demand in the regional and rural health services UniSQ's own placement network already covers.
curriculum:
Core units: Advanced health assessment, evidence-based practice, health systems and leadership, research methods for nursing
Specialisation strand: Nurse practitioner preparation (advanced pharmacology, diagnostics, prescribing) or clinical leadership/education strand
Applied/research component: Clinical project or minor research thesis
For NP stream: Supervised advanced clinical practice placements
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in a health-related discipline (a non-nursing entry pathway is available), or a Bachelor of Nursing for registered nurses seeking advanced standing; current registration or eligibility for registration with AHPRA required for the nursing-entry stream.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with no band below 6.5, or equivalent, consistent with nursing registration standards.

name: Master of Professional Psychology
description:
This is the degree UniSQ points its own Bachelor of Psychology (Honours) graduates toward, and it functions as the next rung on the registration ladder for students who've done the four-year undergraduate sequence and want to keep moving toward broader practice rights rather than stopping at provisional registration. The course combines advanced coursework in assessment, intervention, and professional ethics with a substantial supervised practicum placement: the applied hours are the actual point of the degree, not a formality attached to it.

Students work with clients under supervision as part of the practicum component, building the direct-practice hours AHPRA expects to see before general registration, and the coursework side covers assessment techniques, evidence-based interventions, and the professional and ethical frameworks that govern psychological practice in Australia.

Because UniSQ runs a large distance cohort, the placement component is coordinated across a wider geographic spread of supervising psychologists and services than a metro-only program would need, which in practice means students in regional Queensland aren't stuck waiting for a city-based placement to open up.
curriculum:
Core coursework: Advanced psychological assessment, evidence-based interventions, professional ethics and practice standards, psychopathology
Applied component: Supervised practicum placement (staged across the degree, building client contact hours)
Research component: Applied research project or case-based research unit
Professional development: Practice management and supervision seminars
admission_requirements: An Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC) accredited four-year psychology qualification (e.g. Bachelor of Psychology Honours) with a credit average or better; competitive entry due to limited places.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0, or equivalent.

name: Bachelor of Advanced Computing
description:
The Bachelor of Advanced Computing at the University of Sydney is accredited by the Australian Computer Society and lets students specialise in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Software Development or Computational Data Science, combined with a shared pool of more than 100 majors. Core units build the design principles and programming skills behind technologies from intelligent drones and virtual reality to cybersecurity and the Internet of Things, alongside an Advanced Computing major and elective units.
Students can add a minor or second major from the disciplinary pool or elsewhere in the University. Graduates move into roles such as big data analyst, computer programmer, cybersecurity analyst, software architect and software project manager. Sydney is ranked first in Australia for computer science and information systems.

description:
The Bachelor of Agricultural Economics at the University of Sydney, delivered through the Bachelor of Agricultural Science, builds skills in crop production, animal production, soil science, food science and agricultural economics at Australia's first university for agricultural science. The University of Sydney is ranked 18th globally in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Graduates move into roles including agricultural business manager, agricultural policy maker, consulting agronomist and food scientist.

Students work closely with academic supervisors to design, implement and write up their research as a thesis, developing specialist knowledge and research skills that extend career options beyond the pass degree. Sydney is ranked fourth in the world for sports-related subjects.
