admission_requirements: To be considered for admission, an applicant is required to have: Australian bachelor's degree or higher (minimum 60 percent average) or equivalent qualification, or Australian bachelor's degree or higher with a pass average (minimum 50 percent) or equivalent qualification, and satisfactory performance in the GMAT (for guidance, the class average score is 590) or equivalent Business School approved admissions test.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Diploma in Professional Studies (Education)
description: The Graduate Diploma in Professional Studies (Education) at the University of Sydney, now offered as the Graduate Diploma in Educational Studies, is a one-year full-time program that develops and supports the careers of trained teachers, educational administrators, researchers and policymakers. Students choose units to suit their interests or specialise in areas such as educational leadership, educational psychology, international education, special and inclusive education, sports coaching, or teaching English to speakers of other languages. Graduates advance in education roles. Indicative international tuition is around 54,100 Australian dollars per year.

name: Graduate Diploma in Project Management
description:
The Graduate Diploma in Project Management at the University of Sydney's Faculty of Engineering builds on the graduate certificate with a fuller set of technical skills for managing complex projects, combining core units, project management competency units and diploma-level electives. It complements on-the-job training with the fundamental methodologies, modelling and analytical skills used in project design and delivery.
The course is accredited by the Project Management Institute and draws on the University's John Grill Institute for Project Leadership. Graduates work in project management roles across event management, manufacturing, construction, IT, finance and environmental consultancy, locally and internationally.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: an Australian bachelor's degree in any discipline with a minimum 60 percent or a University of Sydney Graduate Certificate in Project Management with a minimum 60 percent.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Diploma in Public Health
description:
The Graduate Diploma in Public Health at the University of Sydney covers the prevention of illness and the promotion of health across populations, over 48 credit points of core and elective units. Core units in epidemiology, biostatistics, qualitative health research, health promotion and public health ethics are offered face-to-face or online, mostly in first semester.
Graduates take on hands-on and research-oriented public health roles, including government health department officer, health promotion officer and health researcher. Sydney is ranked first in Australia and tenth globally for public health in the ShanghaiRanking Global Rankings of Academic Subjects.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Graduate Diploma in Public Health requires a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Diploma in Public Policy
description:
The Graduate Diploma in Public Policy at the University of Sydney gives students a critical, multidisciplinary perspective on public policy at the global, national and local level, with the opportunity to examine specialist dimensions such as social, economic or international policy. Core units cover the fundamentals of public policy and public administration, with selective units and electives from related disciplines, and the course can serve as a pathway to the full Master of Public Policy.
The course suits people working in or aiming for government and the public sector, as well as those in non-government and private organisations who want to understand government's role in policymaking. Graduates move into policy analyst, government adviser and strategic planning roles.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Graduate Diploma in Public Policy requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney with a minimum 60% average, calculated over the whole degree, and a major in a cognate discipline, or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the Graduate Certificate in Public Policy with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Diploma in Publishing
description:
The Graduate Diploma in Publishing at the University of Sydney gives students the skills needed for book, magazine, digital and online publishing, combining professional training with a scholarly understanding of publishing's history, cultural significance and changing directions. Students complete a minimum of 24 credit points of core units and up to 24 credit points of electives, drawn from the Arts and Social Sciences Publishing program.
The Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences supports research of national and international standing across the publishing field. Graduates establish careers in publishing houses, as magazine editorial staff, and as social media editors.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Graduate Diploma in Publishing requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum 60% average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, including a major in the humanities or social sciences, or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the Graduate Certificate in Publishing with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Diploma in Science (Research)
description: The Graduate Diploma in Science (Research) at the University of Sydney is offered within the Master of Philosophy (Science), a research degree in which candidates pursue supervised research across the faculty's fields of expertise, completing a thesis over one to two years. Students build critical analysis, problem-solving and project management skills. Graduates continue to doctoral research or research roles in industry and government. Indicative international tuition is around 58,800 Australian dollars per year.

name: Graduate Diploma in Science in Medicine
description:
The Graduate Diploma in Science in Medicine at the University of Sydney is a research-methods qualification for health professionals and clinical researchers who want to generate and interpret high-quality clinical research. Delivered fully online with optional face-to-face components, it sits within the same clinical epidemiology teaching used across Sydney's graduate certificate, diploma and masters in the field.
Students build skills in study design, biostatistics and evidence-based practice that translate directly into clinical and health-service research roles. Sydney is ranked first in Australia and tenth globally for public health.
admission_requirements: Admission to the course requires: a medical degree from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification; or a bachelors degree in a health-related discipline with first or second class honours from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification; or a pass bachelors degree in a health-related discipline from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification. Applicants must have completed work equivalent to a first or second class honours bachelors degree or pass a preliminary examination(s) as prescribed by the Faculty; or completion of the first 4 years of an undergraduate medical degree that is accredited by the Australian Medical Council, and a letter of recommendation from the head of clinical school/medical program supporting concurrent enrolment while completing degree requirements. All students entering the program are expected to have some clinical experience.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Diploma in Social Work
description:
The Graduate Diploma in Social Work at the University of Sydney builds toward the University's Master of Social Work (Qualifying), developing the values and practices needed for professional social work in health, community services or the non-government sector. Core units cover practice with Indigenous Australians, mental health, child protection, violence against women and social exclusion, addressing the key priority areas identified by the AASW accreditation process.
The course suits students aiming to work in mental health, women's services, corrections, disability support, child and family services, migrant and refugee services or international development, with a pathway to progress into the full master's degree.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Master of Social Work (Qualifying) requires: a relevant Australian bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification; and evidence of the ability to meet the required prerequisite knowledge in relation to human development and of society; and evidence of relevant employment history in human and community services industry (generally evidence of at least 2 years is required). In exceptional circumstances, the Dean may admit applicants without a bachelor's degree who, in the opinion of the faculty, have qualifications and evidence of experience and achievement sufficient to successfully undertake the award. This may include evidence through publications or authorship of official documents.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.5 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 105; PTE Academic 78 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Diploma in Strategic Public Relations
description:
The Graduate Diploma in Strategic Public Relations at the University of Sydney draws on organisational communication, social theory and political studies to examine how public relations shapes identities, disperses power and creates knowledge. Students complete 48 credit points across core and elective units, developing the critical and strategic thinking needed to engage stakeholders in a complex media environment.
The course is taught within a media and communications program at the forefront of research into an evolving media landscape. Graduates move into public relations, media and communications officer, and digital communications strategist roles.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Graduate Diploma in Strategic Public Relations requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum 60% average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the Graduate Certificate in Strategic Public Relations with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Diploma in Sustainability
description:
The Graduate Diploma in Sustainability at the University of Sydney tackles key global sustainability challenges, building a foundation across health and population, energy and resources, food and water security, policy and governance, and social change. Students tailor electives to their background and career interests, spanning environmental science, finance, law, urban planning and sustainable building design.
The course suits professionals across all industries as organisations invest in sustainable practices and seek staff who can measure, report on and solve sustainability challenges. Graduates work in the built environment, business and public sector sustainability roles.
admission_requirements: Admission to this course requires: a Bachelor degree from any discipline. Applicants who do not meet the requirements for admission into this degree may wish to consider applying for entry into the Graduate Certificate in Sustainability .
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Diploma in Taxation
description:
The Graduate Diploma in Taxation at the University of Sydney Law School is a specialist qualification in Australian tax law, drawing on the Law School's internationally respected taxation program. Students complete four units of study, building toward a high level of specialist tax expertise.
The course meets the needs of lawyers, accountants, public administrators and academics working in the Australian tax profession, taught by acclaimed legal educators and practitioners in the field.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Graduate Diploma in Taxation requires a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney; or an equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Diploma in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
description:
The Graduate Diploma in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages at the University of Sydney draws on the latest research to examine the theoretical basis of key issues in the sociocultural contexts of second language education. Students complete 48 credit points across core, selective and optional elective units, gaining insights that apply directly to daily teaching practice.
The course suits teaching professionals, education leaders, researchers and policymakers building TESOL expertise, though it does not itself lead to a recognised teaching qualification. It sits within the University's broader postgraduate educational studies program.
admission_requirements: A successful applicant for admission to the Graduate Diploma in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages will: hold a bachelor degree or higher in a cognate discipline from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification, and professional experience equivalent to one year full-time in English language teaching; or a bachelor honours degree or postgraduate qualification in a non-cognate discipline from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification, and professional experience equivalent to one year full-time in English language teaching.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Diploma in Transport
description:
The Graduate Diploma in Transport at the University of Sydney develops critical understanding of transport systems, covering their prevalence, identification, analysis and design alongside broad interdisciplinary analytical skills. Students complete core units from the transport discipline along with electives, drawing on the University's Institute of Transport and Logistics.
The course suits graduates entering the growing global transport sector as well as professionals already in the field who want to upskill, with a pathway to progress into the full Master of Transport. Sydney is ranked first in Australia and eighth in the world for transport-related research.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: an Australian bachelor's degree or higher in a cognate discipline
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Diploma in Urban & Regional Planning (Heritage Conservation/Housing Studies)
description:
The Graduate Diploma in Urban and Regional Planning (Heritage Conservation/Housing Studies) at the University of Sydney builds toward the Planning Institute of Australia-accredited Master of Urban and Regional Planning, developing an understanding of how cities and sites are constructed physically, socially and environmentally. Core units in urban and regional planning are combined with electives focused on design and current urban issues.
The course suits graduates with a background in human geography, design or a related field, or graduates of Sydney's Bachelor of Architecture and Environments, seeking a professional education in planning. Graduates work in the public, private and not-for-profit sectors guiding urban and regional change.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Master of Urban and Regional Planning requires: a bachelor's degree in design, human geography or related field from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification with a credit average mark across all units; or completion of the requirements of the embedded graduate diploma with an average mark of at least 70.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Diploma in Urban Design
description:
The Graduate Diploma in Urban Design at the University of Sydney builds toward the University's Master of Urban Design, developing skills and knowledge in urban design and urbanism with a strong emphasis on sustainability, quantification and implementation. Coursework covers the historical and theoretical dimensions of urbanism and expands design skills at suburban and metropolitan scale, refining spatial thinking and visual communication.
Graduates are sought after by private consulting firms, development organisations, and local and state governments to prepare and evaluate urban design policies, strategies, frameworks and master plans.
admission_requirements: Admission to this course requires: an undergraduate degree in architecture, landscape architecture, urban planning, town planning, urbanism, geography or a related field; or completion of the requirements of the embedded Graduate Certificate with an average mark of at least 65 Based on the applicant's undergraduate performance, the Program Director reserves the right to require a portfolio of work indicating relevant design interests and capabilities for admission. A portfolio should only be provided if requested by the Program Director.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Diploma in Veterinary Studies
description:
The Graduate Diploma in Veterinary Studies at the University of Sydney is the coursework component of a combined clinical residency program in veterinary science, taken alongside the Master of Veterinary Clinical Studies. Students complete 48 credit points of supervised elective units within a designated clinical stream, such as small animal medicine, equine surgery, ruminant medicine or veterinary anaesthesia.
Places are limited to postgraduate veterinarians who have already been offered a spot in one of the designated clinical streams after an advertised vacancy. Sydney's veterinary science program is ranked first in Australia and among the few outside North America accredited by the American Veterinary Medical Association.
admission_requirements: Available places will be offered to qualified applicants based on academic merit and relevant professional experience, according to the following admissions criteria: A Bachelor of Veterinary Science with Honours or equivalent, such as a masters degree which is recognised by the NSW Veterinary Practitioners Board (relevant professional experience in the relevant stream is desirable). Full registration, or Registration with conditions, or Limited Registration with the NSW Veterinary Practitioners Board for the entire duration of the candidature. Admission to candidature will be conditional upon the appointment of an appropriate clinical supervisor and associate supervisor. Merit factors and professional experience required include: Grade point average (GPA) or Weighted Average Mean Average (WAM) of veterinary degree (essential). Honours mark or equivalent (essential). Membership of Australian and New Zealand College of Veterinary Scientists is equivalent to Hons I. ‘Accepted’ or published papers in Web of Knowledge listed journals or respected open access on-line journals (not essential, but desirable). Presentations/abstracts at national and international veterinary conferences (not essential, but desirable). Other esteem factors e.g. awards, veterinary positions held since graduation (not essential, but desirable). A minimum experience of a one year rotating internship or equivalent practice experience (essential). Two referees’ reports (essential). Applications will be ranked (in the same manner as for all USYD applicants applying for Australian Postgraduate Awards) within each of the disciplines seeking residents at that time. The highest ranked applicants within each of the disciplines seeking residents at that time, will be requested to attend an interview with the Faculty Academics that oversee this program. Final selection will be made after the interview.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.5 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 64 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Diploma of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics
description:
The Graduate Diploma of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics at the University of Sydney examines the forms and functions of spoken and written language and how it connects with visual and digital contexts, applying linguistics and cross-cultural research to professional practice. Students complete four core units, including Structure and Function of Language, Language, Society and Power, and Discourse, building a foundation for higher research degrees.
The course suits students seeking professional practice skills in crosscultural linguistics or a pathway into further research. Graduates move into roles spanning public relations, multilingual education, community engagement, TESOL teaching and doctor-patient communication in health settings.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Graduate Diploma in Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics requires: a bachelor’s degree or higher award from the University of Sydney, or a qualification deemed by the faculty to be equivalent; or completion of the requirements of the embedded graduate certificate in this discipline or qualifications deemed by the faculty to be equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Diploma of Social Justice
description: The Graduate Diploma of Social Justice at the University of Sydney is a compact, flexible program that lets students explore pressing social justice issues alongside peers studying human rights, peace and conflict, and development studies. It suits people trying out postgraduate study or broadening their expertise. Graduates work in advocacy, community, policy and research roles. Indicative international tuition is around 51,300 Australian dollars per year.

name: Grauate Diploma in Design Science (Audio and Acoustics)
description:
The Graduate Diploma in Design Science (Audio and Acoustics) at the University of Sydney specialises students in interactive sound and audio design for entertainment, buildings and public spaces, building on the University's human-centred interaction design program. Students design across platforms and scales, from wearable computing and mobile applications to interactive architecture and responsive environments, through collaborative design studios and technical workshops.
The course lets students take electives from other faculties and build a portfolio combining design skill with technical audio and acoustics knowledge. Graduates work in the emerging field of interactive sound across entertainment, architecture and public space design.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Master of Interaction Design and Electronic Arts requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification with a credit average mark across all units; or completion of the requirements of the embedded graduate diploma; or completion of the requirements of the embedded graduate certificate with an average mark of at least 70.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Joint Doctor of Philosophy (Arts and Social Sciences)
description:
The Joint Doctor of Philosophy (Arts and Social Sciences) at the University of Sydney lets candidates complete their PhD under joint supervision with a partner institution, researching and writing a thesis on an approved topic across the faculty's six schools, spanning economics, languages and cultures, art, communication and English, humanities, social and political sciences, and education and social work. Candidates typically hold first or second class honours, a research master's, or a coursework master's with a strong research component.
The joint arrangement gives candidates access to supervision, resources and networks at both institutions. Graduates pursue careers in industry, the public sector, education and research organisations.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Doctor of Philosophy (Arts and Social Sciences), you must have completed the equivalent of one of the following in a subject area related to your proposed research area: bachelor’s degree with first class honours or, master’s degree by research; or master’s degree by coursework with a substantial independent research component such as a thesis, dissertation or research project, with a minimum overall pass average of 75% or above; or demonstrated appropriate experience and alternative qualifications at a high level of excellence in the proposed field of research. Applicants who are close to completing an entry requirement, such as honours or a masters degree, may apply and my receive a conditional offer of admission. Transfer from Master of Philosophy Outstanding candidates in the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences who successfully complete up to one year full-time or equivalent part-time of the Master of Philosophy (Arts and Social Sciences) or Master of Fine Arts may apply for transfer into the Doctor of Philosophy (Arts and Social Sciences) and be granted credit for work already completed. You must provide evidence that your research is of a sufficient scope and depth for a doctoral thesis. This transfer may be applied for with the support of your supervisor, Progress Evaluation panel, and School Postgraduate Coordinator. You must also have met all higher degree by research progression requirements and have completed at least 20,000 words of a thesis (or practice-led equivalent) to the satisfaction of the School Postgraduate Coordinator. Meeting these minimum requirements for eligibility does not guarantee admission in the PhD, which is always subject to the approval of the Associate Dean (Research Education). The University must certify that there are sufficient supervisory and other resources and facilities available to enable your candidature to be completed successfully.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Juris Doctor
description:
The Juris Doctor at the University of Sydney Law School is a graduate-entry professional law degree providing a pathway into legal practice for graduates from non-law disciplines or with an overseas law degree. The program develops cultural competency to work with clients and colleagues from diverse backgrounds including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, legal research and technology skills including statutory interpretation and generative AI, and the ability to collaborate ethically with professional peers.
Graduates work across the legal profession and beyond, including as solicitor, barrister, corporate counsel, judge, business strategist, government policy adviser and diplomat, in organisations ranging from international bodies such as the United Nations to small community practices.
curriculum:
Year 1: Legal Reasoning and the Common Law Tradition, Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law, Public Law
Year 2: Property, Equity, Corporations Law, Evidence, Administrative Law, electives
Year 3: Civil and Criminal Procedure, Professional Responsibility, Clinical Legal Education placement option, advanced electives (options include International Law, Competition Law, Intellectual Property)
Covers Priestley 11 subjects required for admission to legal practice in NSW; Practical Legal Training required post-graduation
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for this course required: a bachelor's degree from any discipline other than Law. We also welcome applications from law graduates with a degree from a non-common law jurisdiction. These applicants may receive credit for some of their previous studies toward the JD. Domestic students Domestic students are assessed on the better of a combination of a secondary school leaving qualification such as the NSW Higher School Certificate and completed tertiary study or completed tertiary study by itself. Applicants are ranked by merit and offers for available places are issued according to the ranking. Where students have completed more than one degree, results from the best degree will be used. Applicants who identify as Australian Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander may be eligible for an admissions pathway. After submitting your course application, please email your confirmation of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander identity documentation to indigenous.recruitment@sydney.edu.au for assessment. International students International students are assessed on completed tertiary study. They are assessed using a minimum rank and offers are made according to this minimum standard.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.5 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 105; PTE Academic 78 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master in Policy Studies
description:
The Master in Policy Studies at the University of Sydney gives students a critical, multidisciplinary perspective on public policy at the global, national and local level, amid growing public scrutiny, shrinking resources and new cross-border challenges. Core units cover the fundamentals of public policy and administration, with optional specialisations in economic policy, political economy or social policy, finishing with a capstone research project or supervised dissertation.
Certain units can be completed intensively over four days rather than across a full semester. Graduates move into policy analyst, government adviser and strategic planning roles across administration, research and education.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Master of Public Policy requires: a bachelor’s degree from the University of Sydney with a minimum credit (65%) average, calculated over the whole degree, or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Public Policy with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s, you may be able to enter via the Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Administrative Law and Policy
description:
The Master of Administrative Law and Policy at the University of Sydney lets public administrators, lawyers and policy analysts study together across law, government and social policy. Students complete compulsory units in administrative law and the politics of policy making, with students who lack a law degree also completing a foundational legal reasoning unit, before choosing remaining electives from across the Law School.
The course suits professionals in law, economics, government or social work who want to upgrade their qualifications for career advancement, complementing law studies with content from the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences.
admission_requirements: Admission to the degree requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit average from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; or a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; and evidence of two years of relevant professional experience
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Advanced Nursing Practice
description:
The Master of Advanced Nursing Practice at the University of Sydney is designed for experienced registered nurses who want to extend their advanced practice capability, critical thinking and leadership in complex clinical environments. Over three years of part-time study across 11 units, students complete core foundation units, specialisation project units, nurse prescribing units and a research capstone, along with self-directed learning components that connect coursework to their own clinical practice.
Graduates move into advanced clinical, leadership and specialist roles such as advanced practice registered nurse, nurse unit manager, nurse educator and clinical nurse consultant across hospital, community and primary care settings.
admission_requirements: A successful applicant for admission to the Master of Advanced Nursing Practice will hold: Current general registration with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) as a (Division 1) Registered Nurse and proof of current employment in this capacity at an appropriate health facility. A minimum of three years full-time equivalent experience as a registered nurse. A pre-registration nursing degree at bachelor level or higher with a credit average.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Agriculture and Environment
description:
The Master of Agriculture and Environment at the University of Sydney trains students to address food security, climate change, and the management of carbon, water and the environment, combining lab and field experience. Students complete core units and a chosen specialisation, along with capstone research units and compulsory fieldwork before the start of semester, developing cross-disciplinary thinking and project management skills.
The course suits science, economics or related-experience graduates moving into agriculture and environmental careers. Sydney is Australia's first institution for agricultural science, and graduates work in carbon and water trading, food security, ecohydrology, sustainability and catchment management.
admission_requirements: Admission to this course requires: bachelor’s degree with a credit average (65 percent) in agriculture, science, economics, or an equivalent qualification, or have completed the requirements for the award of the Graduate Certificate in Agriculture and Environment from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Applied Linguistics
description: The Master of Applied Linguistics at the University of Sydney, offered as the Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics, is a one-year full-time degree covering core concepts of language and culture and their application across marketing, education, teaching English to speakers of other languages, community relations, media, medicine and business. Graduates work across language services, education, communications and research. Indicative international tuition is around 51,300 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Applied Science (Health Sciences)
description:
The Master of Applied Science (Health Sciences) at the University of Sydney gives health professionals and career changers a practical, applied-research grounding in a chosen area of health sciences practice. Students combine coursework with an applied project, working with academic supervisors to connect theory to a real health-service problem in their area of interest.
The degree suits practitioners who want postgraduate qualifications without a full research masters, and prepares graduates for advanced clinical, project and policy roles across the health system. It sits within the University of Sydney's Faculty of Medicine and Health.
admission_requirements: Admission to this course requires: a bachelor's degree with first or second class honours from the University of Sydney, or equivalent qualification and a minimum of 1 year of work experience in a health or policy related field; or completion of the requirements of the embedded graduate certificate; or completion of the requirements of the embedded graduate diploma, or equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Architectural Science (One Stream)
description:
The Master of Architectural Science (One Stream) at the University of Sydney is part of the University's Building Performance and Sustainable Design program, developing advanced technical, collaborative and cultural competencies to drive environmental outcomes for a low-carbon built environment. Core foundational and advanced units mix theory and practice, preparing graduates for careers as environmentally sustainable design consultants or in other building science-focused roles.
The course suits graduates aiming for a career in sustainability consulting as well as built environment professionals seeking formal sustainable design qualifications. Graduates move into environmentally sustainable design consulting, property development, construction management and urban planning roles.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Master of Building Performance and Sustainable Design requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the requirement of the graduate certificate with an average mark of at least 70; or completion of a recognised undergraduate program in architecture, engineering, project management or a related field from another institution with a credit average mark (equivalent to 65%) over the final two years of study.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Architecture
description:
The Master of Architecture at the University of Sydney is a studio-based postgraduate degree for graduates and professionals who want to become a registered architect, blending interdisciplinary theory and practice under the guidance of leading experts and practitioners. Students complete core studio-based units, a capstone and electives, developing a customisable design philosophy adaptive to environmental and societal challenges in practice.
Sydney School of Architecture, Design and Planning alumni go on to diverse careers as project architects, studio directors, government architects and founders of their own practices, as well as consultants across the public and private sectors.
admission_requirements: For admission to the Master of Architecture, you need to hold a Bachelor of Design in Architecture, or a Bachelor of Architecture and Environments or an equivalent from another university. Bachelor of Design in Architecture Students who have completed the Bachelor of Design in Architecture at the University of Sydney need to have completed the Master of Architecture prerequisite unit of study BDES3025 (Architectural Professional Practice) and have an average mark of 65. Bachelor of Architecture and Environments Students who have completed the Bachelor of Architecture and Environments at the University of Sydney need to have completed the Master of Architecture prerequisite unit of study BDES3025 (Architectural Professional Practice), have an average mark of 65, and are required to submit a portfolio. Equivalent undergraduate architecture degree Students who have completed an equivalent undergraduate architecture degree at another university will need a credit average (65 percent or equivalent) over the final two years of their degree, and must submit a portfolio of work to the school and/or demonstrate practical experience.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Art Curating
description:
The Master of Art Curating at the University of Sydney is taught in collaboration with leading galleries, museums and art spaces, training future art sector leaders in the cultural, theoretical, social, political and economic forces shaping gallery and museum systems. Students complete 72 credit points, including core units such as Working with Art, The Art Museum, and Contemporary Curating, alongside core and general electives and a capstone experience.
The course suits recent graduates and arts and cultural workers accelerating their careers. Graduates move into roles including curator, exhibition or collection manager, and arts administrator across museums, galleries, auction houses and contemporary art spaces globally.
admission_requirements: Entry in the 1 year or 1.5 year degree program is determined by the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) criteria below: Admission to candidature for the Master of Art Curating (1.5 year full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree with a major in Anthropology, Archaeology, Art History, Cultural Geography, Cultural Studies, Education, English, Gender Studies, History, Indigenous Studies or related field, and a minimum credit (65%) average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification Admission to candidature for the Master of Art Curating (1 year full-time) requires: completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Art Curating with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or an Honours degree in a relevant discipline; or relevant professional work experience and a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average or an equivalent qualification If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s degree, you may be able to enter via a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in the same subject area and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Arts (Research)
description:
The Master of Arts (Research) at the University of Sydney's Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences lets students research and write a thesis on an approved topic under one-on-one supervision, combining a 20,000 to 40,000 word thesis with at least one postgraduate coursework unit. The degree spans disciplines including visual arts and art history, archaeology and classics, languages and their cultures, economics, English literature, history, philosophy, global political economy, sociology, media and communications, and social work.
Students typically hold a bachelor's or master's degree and want to advance their expertise, strengthen career prospects, or prepare for a PhD. The degree offers a recognised pathway into the University's Doctor of Philosophy.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission to the MA (Research) you must have completed the equivalent of one of the following in a subject area related to your proposed research area: bachelor’s degree or equivalent; or master’s degree by coursework These constitute the minimum requirements for eligibility and do not guarantee admission. This remains at the discretion of the relevant supervisors and departments. The University must certify that there are sufficient supervisory and other resources and facilities available to enable your candidature to be completed successfully.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Bioethics
description:
The Master of Bioethics at the University of Sydney examines the ethical challenges arising in health care, public health and the life sciences, taught by scholars at Sydney Health Ethics spanning sociology, pharmacy, public health, philosophy, history and medicine. Students choose from units including Methods of Bioethics, Clinical Ethics, Moral Theory and Philosophy of Health, taught by leading researchers in the field.
Students come from backgrounds including philosophy, humanities, social science, law, science, medicine, nursing and allied health, with no medical background required. Sydney is ranked first in Australia and tenth globally for public health, and graduates move into roles across medicine, nursing, pharmacy, health law and health policy.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Master of Bioethics requires: a bachelor's degree with a credit average from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification in the field of science, medicine, nursing, allied health sciences, philosophy/ethics, sociology, anthropology, history, law or other relevant fields; or completion of the requirements of an embedded graduate certificate or graduate diploma or equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.5 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 64 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Biomedical Science (Infection and Immunity)
description:
The Master of Biomedical Science (Infection and Immunity) at the University of Sydney trains graduates in advanced clinical laboratory techniques used to understand and translate infectious disease research into clinical practice. Students complete core and selective units in clinical laboratory science, immunology, clinical immunology, immunotherapy, virology and bacteriology, alongside an elective unit and a research or industry-related capstone project.
The course suits recent science and health graduates as well as established scientists or clinicians advancing their careers in infectious disease prevention, diagnosis and treatment. Graduates become well versed in the research literature and laboratory techniques used across clinical and research laboratories.
admission_requirements: Admission to this course requires: A bachelor’s degree with honours in science, medical or veterinary science, biomedical science, health science or a health-related discipline, or qualifications deemed by the faculty to be equivalent; Or a bachelor plus a postgraduate degree in a science, medical or veterinary science, biomedical science, health science, or a health-related discipline with a minimum average mark of 65% in each degree; Or a bachelor's degree in a science, medical or veterinary science, biomedical science, health science or a health-related discipline with a minimum average mark of 65% plus a minimum of 24 months relevant work experience; Or completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma with a minimum average mark of 65% in either degree.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.5 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 64 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Brain and Mind Sciences
description:
The Master of Brain and Mind Sciences at the University of Sydney prepares neuroscience, mental health, medical, nursing, psychiatry and psychology professionals to meet the needs of people with disorders of the brain and mind. Core units link the fundamentals of neuroscience to clinical applications and interventions, alongside specialised elective units and a capstone project, directed through the Brain and Mind Centre.
The course suits students from science, psychology, health or education backgrounds, as well as general practitioners and nurses caring for patients with mental illness. Graduates move into research and industry roles across biotech, pharmaceutical and government organisations.
admission_requirements: A successful applicant for admission to the Master of Brain and Mind Sciences will: have completed the requirements of the embedded graduate certificate or graduate diploma in this discipline, without graduating, from the University of Sydney, or equivalent qualification; or hold a bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification; and satisfactorily perform at an interview where required.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Building Performance and Sustainable Design
description:
The Master of Building Performance and Sustainable Design at the University of Sydney develops advanced technical, collaborative and cultural competencies to drive world-leading environmental outcomes for a low-carbon built environment. Core foundational and advanced units mix theory-based and practice-based study, equipping graduates for careers as environmentally sustainable design consultants or in other sustainability and building science-focused roles.
The course suits graduates aspiring to a sustainability-focused career in the built environment, as well as professionals already working in the sector who want formal qualifications. Graduates move into environmentally sustainable design consulting, property development, construction management and urban planning.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Master of Building Performance and Sustainable Design requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the requirement of the graduate certificate with an average mark of at least 70; or completion of a recognised undergraduate program in architecture, engineering, project management or a related field from another institution with a credit average mark (equivalent to 65%) over the final two years of study.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Business Administration (Leadership and Enterprise)
description:
The Master of Business Administration (Leadership and Enterprise) at the University of Sydney Business School is an 18-month, full-time MBA for professionals with at least three years of experience who want to accelerate into senior roles. Delivered intensively in small classes of 50 students or fewer, two units at a time over nine-week blocks, the program builds digital leadership, big data analytics, creative problem-solving and complex systems thinking across 12 units.
The first four units build personal and interpersonal leadership skills, before students move into core business knowledge and skills development. University of Sydney MBA graduates are in high demand with multinational employers, moving into roles such as management consultant, business development manager and operations manager.
admission_requirements: To be eligible to apply for the full-time MBA, you need to have: a minimum of three years of relevant work experience; and a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 65 or equivalent in your undergraduate degree; provide a statement of motivation outlining what will be achieved professionally and personally by completing the course; and pass a selection interview (typically takes place a month following the application deadline). Admission pathways If your academic record does not meet the above criteria, a GMAT (Graduate Management Admission Test) score of 600+ may be required. Candidates with no first degree but with substantial managerial experience will be assessed on a case by case basis and are advised that GMAT may be required. We consider each case holistically and on an individual basis. We look for evidence of communication skills; interpersonal skills; leadership skills; team-building skills; integrity and ethics; initiative; cross-cultural sensitivity; motivation and commitment. Graduate Management Admission Test (GMAT) While GMAT is not a specific requirement for candidates who meet our other admission criteria, students with GMAT scores within the target range will be more likely to receive an offer for entry into the program. You need to have a balanced score on all parts of the GMAT. You should aim for a score of 600+. Although we do not specify a minimum, we are highly unlikely to admit a candidate with a score below 500.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Business Law
description:
The Master of Business Law at the University of Sydney Law School gives business professionals specialist legal knowledge without requiring them to practise law, drawing on units across commercial, corporate, securities, finance and international business and taxation law. Students complete one core unit and choose electives matching their interests, with an option to complete an independent research project.
The degree suits professionals who need to understand the legal issues that arise in business, finance and corporate environments, including those who already hold a professional accounting qualification. Graduates work across business, accounting, finance and corporate roles.
admission_requirements: Admission to the degree requires: a bachelor's degree with a credit average (65 percent) from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification.; or a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; and the applicant provides evidence of two years of relevant professional experience.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Cancer and Haematology Nursing
description:
The Master of Cancer and Haematology Nursing is a specialisation stream within the University of Sydney's Master of Nursing, for registered nurses and graduate-entry students who want to specialise in oncology and blood disorder care. It builds on the Master of Nursing's core units in anatomy, pathophysiology, pharmacology and culturally safe, person-centred practice, with a concentration in cancer and haematology nursing.
The program is accredited by the Australian Nursing and Midwifery Accreditation Council. Graduates work in cancer centres, haematology units and oncology services across metropolitan, regional and international health systems.
admission_requirements: You must have: a previous Australian level bachelor degree (or equivalent) in any discipline other than nursing, AND this qualification has been completed within 10 years prior to applying Overseas nursing qualifications are acceptable. See our Master of Nursing Admissions Guide (pdf, 1.00MB) for more information.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Clinical Psychology
description:
The Master of Clinical Psychology at the University of Sydney gives psychology graduates the knowledge and practical experience to work as a professional clinical psychologist, including full registration as a psychologist in Australia. Students complete core units in the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of psychological disorders, alongside 1,200 hours of supervised clinical placements in clinics, teaching hospitals and community settings, and a research project.
Sydney established Australia's first psychology department in 1927, and clinical training begins at the University's Brain and Mind Centre. Graduates work as clinical, forensic, organisational or sports psychologists across clinical and community settings.
admission_requirements: Completion of an Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC) accredited four year bachelors degree with honours in psychology from a higher education provider, gaining at least first class honours or equivalent. The bachelors degree with honours must include a major research project and thesis as an essential part of the degree. You must satisfy the Head of the School of Psychology (or delegate) of your personal suitability for the practice of clinical psychology through your application, references and selection interview. Applicants for the MCP/PhD must additionally meet the PhD admission requirements. Gadigal Program applicant qualifications Please note that Gadigal Program applicants have different qualification requirements, please see detailed information below. Non-Australian qualifications (if relevant) The Australian Psychological Accreditation Council (APAC) provides information on APAC accredited psychology qualifications in Australia. The Australian Psychological Society (APS) assesses non-Australian qualifications for APAC equivalence. All qualifications obtained from a non-Australian Higher Education Provider must be assessed as equivalent by the Australian Psychological Society (APS) before an application may be submitted.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Commerce
description:
The Master of Commerce at the University of Sydney Business School is an 18-month postgraduate degree for graduates with prior business study or relevant professional experience who want advanced, industry-relevant expertise in a focused commerce discipline. Students build a foundation in core business areas in their first year, then specialise in one of eight commerce disciplines, add breadth through selective units, and complete a capstone project applying their learning to a real business situation.
Graduates move into advanced positions across private, public and non-profit organisations, including accounting, marketing and other specialist fields. Students can transfer between the Master of Commerce and its extension variant depending on how their study progresses.
curriculum:
Core units: Managerial Economics, Accounting for Managers, Quantitative Methods for Business, Business Ethics and Sustainability
Major coursework (choose one): Finance, Accounting, Marketing, Business Analytics, International Business, Human Resource Management
Electives within chosen major, plus cross-disciplinary electives
Capstone: Business Project or Internship unit (final semester)
Duration: 1.5 to 2 years full-time depending on prior qualifications
admission_requirements: To be considered for admission, an applicant is required to have: an Australian bachelor's degree in commerce, business or related discipline with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification, or an Australian bachelor's degree or higher in commerce, business or related discipline (minimum 50 percent average) or equivalent qualification, and satisfactory performance in the GMAT (for guidance, the class average score is 630) or GMAT Focus Edition (for guidance, the class average score is 585), or an Australian bachelor's degree in any discipline with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification and a minimum of one-year relevant work experience, or an Australian bachelor's degree with honours or higher in any discipline with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification, or the University of Sydney Graduate Diploma or Graduate Certificate in Commerce with a credit average (65 percent).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Computer Science
description:
The Master of Computer Science at the University of Sydney gives students the expertise to address challenges in generative AI, cybersecurity, programming, software engineering and network systems, from foundational knowledge through to specialised skills. Students complete foundation subjects, computing professional core subjects, specialist computing subjects and a professional capstone or research project, with an advanced-entry pathway available for applicants who already hold a computing qualification.
Graduates take on roles designing, implementing and evaluating computer science solutions across IT companies, consulting firms and financial services. Sydney is ranked first in Australia and 36th in the world for computer science and information systems.
curriculum:
Foundation units (extended pathway only): Introduction to Programming, Data Structures and Algorithms, Discrete Mathematics for Computing
Core coursework: Software Construction and Design, Computer Networks, Database Systems, Machine Learning Fundamentals
Specialisation streams: Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Software Development
Capstone: choose between Industry Project, Research Project (with academic supervisor), or Coursework Capstone Project
Standard pathway (relevant bachelor's): approximately 1.5 years; extended pathway: approximately 2 years
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have an Australian bachelor’s degree in any discipline with a credit average (65 percent), or an equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Contemporary Art
description: The Master of Contemporary Art at the University of Sydney is now offered through the Master of Fine Arts by research, delivered by Sydney College of the Arts as a supervised independent program of written work and studio research. Students develop their art practice through advanced research in one or more discipline areas. It suits visual arts graduates who want to elevate their practice through research-driven exploration. Graduates work as practising artists and pursue further research. Indicative international tuition is around 50,200 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Creative Writing
description:
The Master of Creative Writing at the University of Sydney develops core skills in fiction, creative nonfiction, poetry and other forms of writing through multi-genre workshops, alongside practice-based research methods and industry knowledge. Students complete core units in creative writing research and practice, specialist writing workshops, electives from across the University, and a capstone creative dissertation or project.
The course suits writers seeking expert guidance toward publication or further study, as well as teachers building their workshop skills and pedagogy. Sydney describes its program as Australia's most research-intensive in creative writing.
admission_requirements: Entry in the 1 year or 1.5 year degree program is determined by the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) criteria below: Admission to candidature for the Master of Creative Writing (1.5 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, including a major in a relevant subject area in the humanities or social sciences, or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the requirements for the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Creative Writing with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification. Admission to candidature for the Master of Creative Writing (1 year full-time) requires: an Honours degree in a relevant discipline; or relevant professional work experience and a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average or an equivalent qualification. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s degree, you may be able to enter via a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in the same subject area and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course with the relevant minimum average mark.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 64. The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Criminology
description:
The Master of Criminology at the University of Sydney examines contemporary questions about crime and social control in policy, theory and practice, comparing Australian and global perspectives, taught by leading Australian criminologists. Students complete eight units of study covering crime theories, psychology, public policy, social research and legal theory, building the knowledge to work with criminal justice and social welfare agencies.
The course welcomes students from backgrounds including social policy, psychology, public health, media and policing. Graduates work across criminal justice agencies, government policy, border protection and research institutions.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Master of Criminology requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit average from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; or a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; and the applicant provides evidence of two years of relevant professional experience.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics
description:
The Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics at the University of Sydney examines the forms and functions of spoken and written language and how it connects with visual and digital contexts, applying linguistics and cross-cultural research to professional and social engagement. Core units build critical awareness of the connections between language, culture and society, finishing with a capstone professional practice unit.
The course suits students seeking to deepen their knowledge of linguistics and cross-cultural communication or pursue further research. Graduates move into roles spanning public relations, multilingual education, community engagement, TESOL teaching and doctor-patient communication in health settings.
admission_requirements: Entry in the 1 year or 2 year degree program is determined by the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) criteria below: Admission to candidature for the Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics (2 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification. Admission to candidature for the Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics (1.5 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average in a relevant discipline, calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate in Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or relevant professional work experience. Admission to candidature for the Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics (1 year full-time) requires: completion of the embedded Graduate Diploma in Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or an Honours degree in a relevant discipline; or relevant professional work experience and a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average or an equivalent qualification. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s degree, you may be able to enter via a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in the same subject area and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Crosscultural Communication
description:
The Master of Crosscultural Communication at the University of Sydney, known as the Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics, gives students the concepts and methods of linguistics and cross-cultural research and applies them to marketing, education, TESOL, community relations, media, medicine and business. Core units build foundational knowledge of language, culture and society, finishing with a capstone professional practice unit and electives chosen from across the University.
Graduates work across public relations, multilingual education, community engagement, TESOL teaching, media and doctor-patient communication in health settings.
admission_requirements: Entry in the 1 year or 2 year degree program is determined by the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) criteria below: Admission to candidature for the Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics (2 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification. Admission to candidature for the Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics (1.5 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average in a relevant discipline, calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate in Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or relevant professional work experience. Admission to candidature for the Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics (1 year full-time) requires: completion of the embedded Graduate Diploma in Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or an Honours degree in a relevant discipline; or relevant professional work experience and a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average or an equivalent qualification. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s degree, you may be able to enter via a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in the same subject area and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Cultural Studies
description:
The Master of Cultural Studies at the University of Sydney examines popular culture, media, gender, sexuality, globalisation and consumer culture, using real-world examples to analyse cultural expressions and their significance within socio-historical frameworks. Core units build conceptual and methodological skills, complemented by electives matched to the student's interests and a capstone research project.
The course suits students seeking to apply a deep understanding of cultural processes to their industry. Graduates move into government, community, arts, education and communication roles.
admission_requirements: Entry in the 1 year or 1.5 year degree program is determined by the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) criteria below: Admission to candidature for the Master of Cultural Studies (1.5 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney including a major in a relevant subject area in the humanities or social sciences, or an equivalent qualification. Admission to candidature for the Master of Cultural Studies (1 year full-time) requires: completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Cultural Studies with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or an Honours degree in a relevant discipline; or relevant professional work experience and a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average or an equivalent qualification. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s degree, you may be able to enter via a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in the same subject area and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Cybersecurity
description:
The Master of Cybersecurity at the University of Sydney gives professionals an expert-level understanding of leading attack and defence techniques, network security assessment, and organisational cybersecurity strategy. Students complete cybersecurity and computing professional core subjects, cybersecurity specialist electives, and a capstone or research project, with optional specialisations in cloud security, cryptography and blockchains, or data and information security.
The course is designed for professionals aiming to become leaders and technical experts in an industry projected to need 17,000 additional cybersecurity professionals in Australia within five years. Sydney is ranked first in Australia for computer science and information systems.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: a three year Australian bachelor's degree in a cognate discipline with a minimum credit average (65 percent), or the University of Sydney Graduate Diploma in Cybersecurity with a minimum credit average (65 percent), or a qualification deemed to be equivalent; or completed 24 credit points of the University of Sydney Graduate Diploma in Cybersecurity or Graduate Certificate in Cybersecurity with a minimum credit average (65 percent). The 24 credit points must include 12 credit points of Cybersecurity Core units and 12 credit points of Cybersecurity specialist elective units, and a major or minor in information technologies (IT) or computer science, or equivalent in volume of learning as determined by the program directors is required for this discipline
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Data Science
description:
The Master of Data Science at the University of Sydney develops the analytical and technical skills professionals with a strong mathematical or quantitative background need to use data science for strategic decision making. Students complete data science core subjects, computing professional core subjects, data science specialist electives, and a capstone project or research project, with optional specialisations in data engineering or machine learning.
