description: The Bachelor of Medical Research with Honours at the University of Tasmania provides students with a firm foundation for postgraduate study in medical research. For students not wishing to progress further, an in-depth research project provides an important understanding of the processes of medical research. Alongside the major research project, students investigate and present on an area unrelated to their main project. The one-year program is offered in Hobart, Launceston, Sydney and online.

name: Bachelor of Medical Science and Doctor of Medicine
description:
The Bachelor of Medical Science and Doctor of Medicine is Tasmania's combined medical pathway: three years of medical science foundations followed by the four-year MD, rather than a separate graduate-entry MD alone. Its defining feature is where students end up training: the university runs rural clinical schools across Tasmania (including Launceston and rural placement sites), reflecting a deliberate policy push, shared with several Australian medical schools, to train doctors in the kind of regional and rural settings they're most needed in rather than concentrating clinical training entirely in one metropolitan teaching hospital.

The medical science years build the standard preclinical foundation (anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, pathology) before students move into the MD's clinical years, which are built around extended rural and rotational placements across Tasmania's hospital network rather than a single fixed hospital site, giving graduates broader exposure to generalist practice than a purely metropolitan clinical school typically offers.

Graduates emerge with provisional registration and move into internship and residency, with Tasmania's own health system, persistently short of doctors in regional areas, a common and immediate destination, alongside interstate and, for some graduates, international training pathways.
curriculum:
Years 1–3 (Bachelor of Medical Science): Human Anatomy and Physiology, Biochemistry and Cell Biology, Pathology and Pharmacology, Population Health and Epidemiology, clinical skills foundation units
Years 4–7 (Doctor of Medicine): core clinical rotations (medicine, surgery, paediatrics, obstetrics and gynaecology, psychiatry, general practice), extended rural clinical placement year, elective specialty rotation, final-year internship-preparation clinical placement
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with high ATAR (approximately 90+), UCAT score, and interview; competitive selection
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0, no band below 7.0 (or equivalent)

name: Bachelor of Medical Science with Honours
description: The Bachelor of Medical Science with Honours at the University of Tasmania is designed to provide students with a firm foundation for further study in medicine and future vocational career pathways. An in-depth research project gives students an important understanding of the processes of medical research in laboratory, community and clinical settings, and students also investigate and communicate analysis on a second topic. The one-year program is offered at the Hobart, Launceston and Cradle Coast campuses.

name: Bachelor of Music
description: The Bachelor of Music at the University of Tasmania immerses students in a vibrant concert and events program from first year, exploring diverse musical styles and genres through performance and creation. Students can use their elective zone to build skills in another area, consider a double degree to broaden their career possibilities, or undertake an overseas exchange. The degree takes a minimum of three years full-time and is based in Hobart at the School of Creative Arts and Media.

name: Bachelor of Natural Environment & Wilderness Studies (Honours)
Bachelor of Natural Environment and Wilderness
Bachelor of Natural Environments and Conservation
description: The Bachelor of Natural Environments and Conservation at the University of Tasmania is grounded in a state that is a living laboratory, with around 23 per cent of Tasmania recognised as world heritage and 42 per cent as protected areas, accessible from campus. Students learn to understand the issues facing the planet and how to help build a better future, connecting with the rich culture of the conservation movement in Tasmania. The degree takes a minimum of three years full-time and is based in Hobart.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
The Bachelor of Nursing trains students for clinical placement across a state where rural and remote healthcare delivery isn't a special elective topic but the default context most graduates will actually work in. Tasmania's population is spread across small regional centres as much as Hobart and Launceston, and the degree's placement structure reflects that, sending students into rural hospitals and community health settings as a matter of course rather than as an optional rural health unit bolted onto a metropolitan-focused course.

Clinical placement hours meet the national accreditation standard required for registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, and the course combines campus-based simulation and skills labs with hospital and community placements building progressively across the degree, from observation-heavy first-year placements to near-independent practice in the final year.

Graduates register as nurses and typically go into acute care, aged care, community and rural health roles, with Tasmania's own public health system, spread thin across a small population, a common and immediate employer for local graduates.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Health Assessment, introductory clinical placement
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Pharmacology, expanded clinical placement including rural rotation
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing, Aged Care and Chronic Disease Management, Leadership in Nursing Practice, final capstone clinical placement
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent) with satisfactory results in English; ATAR of approximately 65 recommended
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0, no band below 7.0 (registration requirement for nursing)

name: Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours) at the University of Tasmania prepares students to work as pharmacists, the medication experts within collaborative health care teams working alongside doctors and nurses. The degree suits people who enjoy chemistry and biology and want to step straight into a career, and draws on extensive relationships with leading pharmacists and service providers in Tasmania for placements. It takes a minimum of three years full-time and is available at the Hobart, Launceston and Cradle Coast campuses.

name: Bachelor of Pharmacy with Honours
description: The Bachelor of Pharmacy with Honours at the University of Tasmania trains students to become pharmacists, the medication experts in collaborative healthcare teams who help people manage their health alongside doctors, nurses and other professionals. The degree combines chemistry and biology with clinical practice and placements arranged through the university's extensive relationships with Tasmanian pharmacists and service providers. It takes a minimum of three years full-time and is offered at the Hobart, Launceston and Cradle Coast campuses.

name: Bachelor of Philosophy
description: The Bachelor of Philosophy at the University of Tasmania is a companion degree for high-achieving students who are critical and creative thinkers and want to become the thought and action leaders of the future. It lets students expand their university experience to include multidisciplinary perspectives and effect positive change in their future careers. The degree is built around the student's own choices, is studied online, and takes a minimum of 1.5 years, generally alongside another degree.

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
The Bachelor of Psychological Science is the accredited undergraduate entry point into psychology in Australia, built to the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council standard that any student aiming for provisional registration and eventual practice needs. At Tasmania it's taught through a psychology department with a long research profile in areas like cognitive neuroscience and mental health, and undergraduates get exposure to active research labs earlier than at some larger universities simply because cohort sizes are smaller and staff-to-student contact is closer.

The degree covers the core content areas APAC mandates (biological bases of behaviour, cognition, developmental and social psychology, statistics and research methods), building toward fourth-year Honours as the next required step for anyone pursuing registration as a psychologist, which the bachelor's degree alone doesn't confer.

Graduates who don't continue into Honours and postgraduate training still leave with a strong quantitative research skill set that transfers into human resources, market research, policy and community services work, which is where a meaningful share of psychology bachelor graduates nationally actually end up.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Research Methods and Statistics I, Biological Bases of Behaviour
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology, Research Methods and Statistics II
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology, Personality, Advanced Research Methods, capstone research project (required for APAC-accredited sequence, pathway to Honours)
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 70 recommended
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent)

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science with Honours
description: The Bachelor of Psychological Science with Honours at the University of Tasmania is a one-year full-time or part-time program for high-achieving students ready to deepen their expertise through research. It provides students with the opportunity to learn the ethical principles and content areas of psychology as a scientific discipline, combining advanced coursework with a significant research project. It is offered in Hobart and Launceston and completes an accredited sequence in psychology.

name: Bachelor of Science
description: The Bachelor of Science at the University of Tasmania is a gateway to a wide range of rewarding careers for students who enjoy pursuing their curiosity and understanding the world around them. Set in Tasmania's living laboratory, the degree lets students explore scientific disciplines and can be combined into a double degree to accelerate a career. It takes a minimum of three years full-time and is offered in Hobart and Launceston, with a broad choice of majors.

name: Bachelor of Social Work with Honours
description: The Bachelor of Social Work with Honours at the University of Tasmania has been designed with direct industry input to reflect current and emerging practice trends in the profession. Students learn how to respond to social justice, human rights and socio-environmental challenges, recognising that compassion and support are key to improving social, financial, environmental and cultural wellbeing. The accredited degree takes a minimum of four years full-time and is available at the Hobart, Launceston and Cradle Coast campuses.

name: Bachelor of Surveying and Spatial Science with Honours
Diploma of Arts
description: The Diploma of Arts at the University of Tasmania gives students the opportunity to interpret human culture and behaviour from different perspectives and periods, explore contemporary questions about society, and engage with creativity, performance and innovation. The course can serve as the first year of a Bachelor of Arts or as a standalone qualification. It takes a minimum of one year full-time and is available at the Hobart, Launceston and Cradle Coast campuses and online.

name: Diploma of Fine Arts
description: The Diploma of Fine Arts at the University of Tasmania develops skills in self-expression and creative problem-solving to generate artwork. Students are encouraged to participate in contemporary culture, engaging directly with Tasmania's internationally acclaimed arts culture through ongoing partnerships with festivals and arts institutions across the state, and to contribute to the cultural life of the community. It takes a minimum of one year full-time and is offered in Hobart and Launceston, and can serve as a pathway into the Bachelor of Fine Arts.

name: Diploma of Global Logistics and Maritime Management
description: The Diploma of Global Logistics and Maritime Management at the University of Tasmania, offered through the Australian Maritime College, equips students with up-to-date business knowledge for roles in management and administration within the maritime and logistics industries. It provides a practical and comprehensive understanding of how global trade operates and is an ideal stepping stone into the associate degree or bachelor degree. It takes a minimum of one year full-time and is offered in Launceston and online.

name: Diploma of Legal Studies
description: The Diploma of Legal Studies at the University of Tasmania provides exposure to the study of law without a full commitment to a law degree. It suits people planning a role that would benefit from legal knowledge, as well as those who already use legal knowledge in their career. Alongside introductory units covering the foundations of law and legal reasoning, students choose units targeting one or more specialist areas. It takes a minimum of one year full-time and is offered in Hobart, Launceston and online.

name: Diploma of Music
description: The Diploma of Music at the University of Tasmania is for students who want a greater understanding and knowledge of the discipline of music. Its structure allows students to improve skills in one or more broad areas of interest, including ensemble skills, music history, music literacy, and audio design and music technology. It permits a year of dedicated pre-Bachelor of Music study for students wishing to improve their performance or composition, and takes a minimum of one year full-time in Hobart.

name: Doctor of Philosophy (Quantitative Marine Science) and Graduate Diploma of Marine and Antarctic Science
Doctor of Philosophy (Quantitative Marine Science) and Graduate Diploma of Quantitative Marine and Antarctic Science
Foundation Studies Program (Standard)
description: The Foundation Studies Program (Standard) at the University of Tasmania is a direct academic pathway to first-year undergraduate degree study. It acts as a bridging course for international students who wish to study a university undergraduate degree but do not yet meet the academic requirements or English language skills for tertiary study. To complete the program, students must achieve a pass in all units. It runs over a minimum of 36 weeks and is based in Hobart.

name: Graduate Certificate in Global Logistics and Supply Chain Management
description: The Graduate Certificate in Global Logistics and Supply Chain Management at the University of Tasmania, offered through the Australian Maritime College, helps professionals understand how to develop and implement sustainable, effective and efficient logistics and supply chain management strategies as global supply chains evolve and expand. It suits those seeking a competitive advantage in any industry and can serve as a pathway into the graduate diploma or master degree. It takes a minimum of half a year full-time, in Launceston or online.

name: Graduate Certificate in Maritime Engineering
description: The Graduate Certificate in Maritime Engineering at the University of Tasmania, delivered through the Australian Maritime College, gives engineering graduates in-depth exposure to a range of subjects relevant to maritime engineering systems. It is tailored for engineering professionals already in the workforce but with limited exposure to the maritime engineering sector, and can serve as a pathway to a master degree. It takes a minimum of half a year full-time and is offered in Launceston and online.

name: Graduate Certificate in Maritime Management
description: The Graduate Certificate in Maritime Management at the University of Tasmania, offered through the Australian Maritime College, equips students with the ability to develop solutions for complex problems faced by the maritime industry. It suits professional development and can serve as a pathway to a master degree. It takes a minimum of half a year full-time and is offered in Launceston and online.

name: Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting
description: The Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting at the University of Tasmania is an entry point into accounting and an ideal first step for those considering further qualifications in the field. Designed for people seeking foundational knowledge, it introduces key accounting principles and practices while incorporating contemporary perspectives such as sustainability and ethical decision-making. It takes a minimum of half a year full-time and is offered in Hobart and online.

name: Graduate Certificate in Social Care (International Pathway)
Graduate Certificate in Tourism, Environmental and Cultural Heritage
Graduate Diploma of Environmental Geospatial Analysis
description: The Graduate Diploma of Environmental Geospatial Analysis at the University of Tasmania teaches students to integrate geospatial and environmental knowledge to make practical recommendations as environmental challenges become increasingly complex. Students learn to map, monitor and measure environmental change and to analyse a variety of information, including mapped data, to help respond to current environmental crises. It takes a minimum of one year full-time and is based in Hobart.

name: Graduate Diploma of Environmental Planning
description: The Graduate Diploma of Environmental Planning at the University of Tasmania develops knowledge and skills in maintaining and building sustainable places. Learning is grounded in Tasmania's rich heritage of environmental and social issues, including meaningful participation in decision-making and the equitable distribution of environmental benefits and risks, with a focus on planning for diverse communities and future generations. It takes a minimum of one year full-time and is offered in Hobart and online.

name: Graduate Diploma of Global Logistics and Supply Chain Management
description: The Graduate Diploma of Global Logistics and Supply Chain Management at the University of Tasmania, offered through the Australian Maritime College, develops the knowledge to design and implement sustainable, effective and efficient logistics and supply chain management strategies as global supply chains constantly evolve and expand. It builds on the graduate certificate and can lead into the master degree. It takes a minimum of one year full-time and is offered in Launceston and online.

name: Graduate Diploma of Information and Communication Technology
Graduate Diploma of Land Surveying
description: The Graduate Diploma of Land Surveying at the University of Tasmania, together with the Bachelor of Surveying and Spatial Sciences or its equivalent, provides the qualifications needed for registration with the Tasmanian Land Surveyors Accreditation Board for the purposes of the Surveyors Act, and for reciprocal registration in other Australian states. It builds advanced cadastral surveying knowledge and professional practice skills, takes a minimum of one year full-time, is based in Hobart, and runs subject to minimum enrolment numbers.

name: Graduate Diploma of Legal Practice
description: The Graduate Diploma of Legal Practice at the University of Tasmania, also known as the Tasmanian Legal Practice Course, is a 24-week full-time professional and practical training course conducted by the Centre for Legal Studies in Hobart. Running on campus and in person from February to July each year, it prepares law graduates for the conduct of legal practice and admission as a legal practitioner, and is an approved course of practical legal training.

name: Graduate Diploma of Marine and Antarctic Science
description: The Graduate Diploma of Marine and Antarctic Science at the University of Tasmania provides a solid coursework foundation in a chosen area of specialisation and serves as a pathway to the Master of Marine and Antarctic Science. As a gateway to Antarctica with a natural marine laboratory on its doorstep, the university is an ideal base for a career in marine biology and the fisheries and aquaculture industries. It takes a minimum of one year full-time and is based in Hobart.

name: Graduate Diploma of Maritime Engineering
description: The Graduate Diploma of Maritime Engineering at the University of Tasmania, delivered through the Australian Maritime College, provides engineering graduates with comprehensive exposure to a wide range of subjects relevant to maritime engineering systems, along with management skills. It is aimed at engineering professionals already in the workforce but with limited exposure to the maritime engineering sector. It takes a minimum of one year full-time and is offered in Launceston and online.

name: Graduate Diploma of Maritime Management
description: The Graduate Diploma of Maritime Management at the University of Tasmania, offered through the Australian Maritime College, provides the extensive knowledge and analytical skills needed to meet the challenges facing the maritime industry and to enhance career opportunities in management positions. It suits professional development or can serve as a pathway to a master degree. It takes a minimum of one year full-time and is offered in Launceston and online.

name: Graduate Diploma of Pharmaceutical Science
description: The Graduate Diploma of Pharmaceutical Science at the University of Tasmania is a one-year course (part-time over two years) for health and science graduates who want to build a career in the pharmaceutical industry or regulatory organisations. Students gain a strong foundation in pharmaceutical science through practical, hands-on laboratory sessions focused on techniques used around the world, and develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills. It is offered in Hobart.

name: Graduate Diploma of Professional Accounting
description: The Graduate Diploma of Professional Accounting at the University of Tasmania is a 12-month course with flexible full-time or part-time options, designed for those without an accounting background who want to start a new career or boost their current skills. Students gain a strong foundation in accounting fundamentals, and completing the diploma sets them on a path towards becoming a certified accountant with opportunities to advance further. It is offered in Hobart and online.

name: Graduate Diploma of Protected Area Conservation
description: The Graduate Diploma of Protected Area Conservation at the University of Tasmania trains students in the fundamental aspects of governance, planning and management needed for effective conservation of nature as environmental challenges such as bushfires and climate change become increasingly complex. Students learn how the protected area estate can effectively conserve nature and deliver its benefits. It takes a minimum of one year full-time and is offered in Hobart and online.

name: Graduate Diploma of Tourism, Environmental and Cultural Heritage
Master of Agriculture and Food Sciences (Specialisation)
description: The Master of Agriculture and Food Sciences (Specialisation) at the University of Tasmania provides graduates with advanced contemporary knowledge in agricultural and food sciences. Students apply their skills and knowledge to address contemporary challenges and support sustainable agricultural growth and innovative food production, choosing a specialisation within the field. The degree takes a minimum of two years full-time and is based in Hobart.

name: Master of Applied Science in Aquaculture
Master of Architecture
description: The Master of Architecture at the University of Tasmania is an accredited professional course that provides advanced education in architecture and serves as the principal pathway to becoming a practising architect. Building on the Bachelor of Architecture and Built Environments, it draws on a rich heritage of teaching traditions, community partnerships, technical capabilities, design excellence and pioneering research. The degree takes a minimum of two years full-time and is based in Launceston.

name: Master of Business Administration in Maritime Management
description: The Master of Business Administration in Maritime Management at the University of Tasmania, delivered through the Australian Maritime College, is designed for those seeking management skills and knowledge appropriate for the maritime industry. It provides a high level of understanding of the maritime industry and the foundation to undertake middle and senior management positions after graduating. The degree takes a minimum of two years full-time and is offered in Launceston and online.

name: Master of Chemistry
description: The Master of Chemistry at the University of Tasmania helps students gain advanced skills and knowledge for a wide range of chemistry-related careers, whether they want to specialise in a new area or update their qualifications. Students learn in an active research environment guided by experts, and the course includes a research thesis that develops strong communication skills. The degree takes a minimum of two years full-time and is based in Hobart.

name: Master of Economic Geology (C/W)
description: The Master of Economic Geology at the University of Tasmania is a specialised degree tailored for industry and government geologists. It is the nucleus of the postgraduate teaching program at the ARC Centre of Excellence in Ore Deposits (CODES) and an integral part of the National Minerals Geoscience Master's Program. The course is typically offered part-time and externally, with full-time admission reserved for students demonstrating financial and other support. It is based in Hobart, with online study.

name: Master of Education
description: The Master of Education at the University of Tasmania is designed for experienced educators seeking professional learning, personal and professional enquiry and intellectual engagement within a specialist area or across a range of specialisations. This coursework degree is based on principles of active learning and practice-oriented enquiry, informed by professional standards, contemporary theoretical perspectives and research in teaching. It takes a minimum of 1.5 years and is studied online.

name: Master of Environmental Geospatial Science
description: The Master of Environmental Geospatial Science at the University of Tasmania prepares highly skilled professionals to analyse a variety of information, including mapped data, to help respond to increasingly complex environmental challenges such as bushfire management and climate change. Students draw on Tasmania's Land Information System and other geospatial resources to map, monitor and measure environmental change. The degree takes a minimum of two years full-time and is based in Hobart.

name: Master of Global Logistics and Supply Chain Management
description: The Master of Global Logistics and Supply Chain Management at the University of Tasmania, offered through the Australian Maritime College, develops the knowledge to design and implement sustainable, effective and efficient logistics and supply chain management strategies as global supply chains constantly evolve and expand. It builds advanced analytical and management capability for careers across many industries. The degree takes a minimum of two years full-time and is offered in Launceston and online.

name: Master of Health Service Management
description: The Master of Health Service Management at the University of Tasmania is designed for aspiring management professionals ready to take the next step in their careers. The course content is aligned to the health sector's current and emerging issues and opportunities, and has been developed in collaboration with, and for some classes delivered by, Australia's leading senior health service executives. It takes a minimum of two years full-time and is taught at the Melbourne and Sydney (Ultimo) study centres.

name: Master of Information Technology and Systems
description:
The Master of Information Technology and Systems is a conversion-friendly postgraduate IT degree, aimed as much at graduates moving into tech from an unrelated undergraduate background as at computer science graduates deepening their qualification, with core units in programming, systems analysis, databases and networking alongside specialisation options in areas like cybersecurity, data analytics or enterprise systems depending on current course structure and student interest.

Being based in Hobart rather than a larger tech hub means the degree leans on Tasmania's smaller but genuinely growing digital economy: state government IT, agtech and data-driven agriculture given Tasmania's agricultural base, and a modest but real local software and services sector, rather than assuming graduates will inevitably relocate to Sydney or Melbourne, though many do.

Graduates move into systems analysis, software development, IT project management and business analysis roles, with the degree commonly chosen by international students and career-changers specifically because it doesn't assume an undergraduate computing background, unlike a straight Master of Computer Science.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Programming Fundamentals, Systems Analysis and Design, Database Systems
Semester 2: Networking and Security, Enterprise Systems, IT Project Management
Semester 3: specialisation electives (cybersecurity, data analytics, or software engineering stream), Research Methods in IT
Semester 4: capstone IT project or industry-based project, professional practice unit
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant or any discipline (typical Australian postgrad IT/CS entry bar used as approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Master of Laboratory Medicine
description: The Master of Laboratory Medicine at the University of Tasmania prepares students to join a field at the heart of modern healthcare, where almost every diagnosis depends on accurate laboratory results. The practical, industry-focused course combines theory with hands-on experience, covering clinical disciplines within laboratory medicine. The degree takes a minimum of two years full-time and is based in Launceston.

name: Master of Marine and Antarctic Science
description: The Master of Marine and Antarctic Science at the University of Tasmania is the only master's degree in the world that uniquely combines marine science with a focus on the Southern Ocean and Antarctica. Students have access to industry-leading facilities at the Institute for Marine and Antarctic Studies and prepare for careers in marine biology, fisheries and aquaculture. The degree takes a minimum of two years full-time and is based in Hobart.

name: Master of Maritime Engineering (Professional)
description: The Master of Maritime Engineering (Professional) at the University of Tasmania, delivered through the Australian Maritime College, is designed for qualified engineers who want to build specialist knowledge in the maritime sector. Professional engineers with a four-year bachelor degree in any engineering discipline can use the program to change the course of their career, gaining expertise in areas including naval architecture. The degree takes a minimum of two years full-time and is offered in Launceston and online.

name: Master of Occupational Therapy
description: The Master of Occupational Therapy at the University of Tasmania prepares students to work as occupational therapists, supporting people who experience challenges to live a meaningful life. Students learn to help people engage in the occupations they need, want or are expected to perform and to participate in their communities, adopting a strength-based approach. The accredited degree takes a minimum of two years full-time and is based in Launceston.

name: Master of Pharmaceutical Science
description: The Master of Pharmaceutical Science at the University of Tasmania is a two-year course taught over four semesters in Hobart. Teaching is primarily based on hands-on training through individualised laboratory-based interactive sessions, with the goal of equipping students with the basic and advanced laboratory and analytical skills commonly used in pharmaceutical industries and research laboratories. The course prepares graduates for real-world roles in pharmaceutical research and manufacturing.

name: Master of Physiotherapy
description: The Master of Physiotherapy at the University of Tasmania gives students the qualifications and skills to become a practising physiotherapist in Australia. Developed in collaboration with health professionals, industry leaders and professional bodies, the course equips graduates with the future-facing capabilities needed to adapt and respond to rapidly occurring changes in health. The degree takes a minimum of two years full-time and is based in Launceston.

name: Master of Planning
description: The Master of Planning at the University of Tasmania is a professionally accredited course in which students learn the theoretical, technical and communication skills required by planning professionals. Students develop a range of essential planning competencies, from the legal to the strategic, and these two sides combine to enable planners to envision and action more sustainable futures. The degree takes a minimum of two years full-time and is offered in Hobart and online.

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description: The Master of Professional Accounting at the University of Tasmania is designed for people who want to enter accounting without formal qualifications or who are professionals looking to upskill. Students gain practical experience through internships and work with Tasmanian industries, including opportunities at the Tax Clinic, building valuable connections for their future career. The degree takes a minimum of two years full-time and is offered in Hobart and online.

name: Master of Professional Psychology
description: The Master of Professional Psychology at the University of Tasmania is taught primarily by practising psychologists focused on preparing students to step into the profession with confidence. Students build relationships with teachers and peers, developing professional networks before graduation, within a community-focused approach. The one-year program is offered in Hobart and Launceston and forms part of the pathway to registration as a psychologist.

name: Master of Protected Area Conservation
description: The Master of Protected Area Conservation at the University of Tasmania builds the knowledge and practical skills needed to work in protected area governance, planning and management. Protected areas cover more than 15 per cent of global land, 20 per cent of Australia and 40 per cent of Tasmania, and effectively managing these landscapes is critical to global conservation and sustainable development goals. Students explore how protected areas are managed across government, private and community settings. The degree takes a minimum of two years full-time and is offered in Hobart and online.

name: Master of Psychology (Clinical)(Coursework)
description: The Master of Psychology (Clinical) at the University of Tasmania is built around a community-focused, scientist-practitioner model, with an ungraded-pass methodology that focuses on collegiality, competency development and depth and breadth of learning. It prepares students for a career as a clinical psychologist helping individuals and communities. The degree takes a minimum of two years full-time and is offered in Hobart and Launceston.

name: Master of Public Health
description: The Master of Public Health at the University of Tasmania provides students with the tools to make a difference in their community and to tackle contemporary and emerging public health challenges. Students learn to be systems thinkers, to confidently navigate the research, policy and practice interface, and to design, implement and evaluate complex public health interventions. The degree takes a minimum of two years full-time and is offered in Hobart and online.

name: Master of Speech Pathology
description: The Master of Speech Pathology at the University of Tasmania develops the knowledge, skills and confidence to work as an autonomous speech pathologist, responding to the needs of individuals and communities who experience difficulties with communication and swallowing. Students develop the tools to provide safe, ethical and quality person, family and community-centred practice in complex and changing environments. The degree takes a minimum of two years full-time and is based in Launceston.

name: Master of Teaching
description: The Master of Teaching at the University of Tasmania transforms an existing bachelor degree into a teaching qualification, allowing students to use their existing expertise to inspire and engage the next generation. It suits people seeking a more fulfilling career, greater work-life balance or the opportunity to make a lasting impact. The degree takes a minimum of two years full-time and is offered in Hobart and online, and leads to teacher registration.

name: Master of Tourism, Environmental and Cultural Heritage
Bachelor of Advanced Science
description: The Bachelor of Advanced Science at UTS is designed for students aiming for careers in medicine, pharmaceuticals, or physics and quantum sciences, joining a science faculty known for its contribution to STEM education and research. Students specialise in one of three majors: Pre-medicine, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or Physics and Quantum Technology. Each major blends theoretical knowledge with practical experience, with opportunities to work with high-quality specimens, engage in advanced research, and develop communication skills, giving students a deep understanding of their chosen discipline from human anatomy and drug impacts to quantum devices.

name: Bachelor of Animation Production
description:
The Bachelor of Animation Production at the University of Technology Sydney (UTS) is a hands-on degree in 2D and 3D character animation. Core subjects cover sound and the moving image, ethical creative practice and entrepreneurship, and the animation stream develops skills in animation performance and short film production across multiple modes. In the final year, students work with industry partners to design and pitch an animated series and complete a capstone short film.
Study takes three years full-time. Graduates work in animation, film, television and games. English requirements are IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 in writing.
admission_requirements: Applicants must have completed an Australian Year 12 qualification, Australian Qualifications Framework Diploma, or equivalent Australian or overseas qualification at the required level.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); TOEFL iBT 79 (writing 21); PTE Academic 58 (writing 50). UTS also accepts its UTS College academic English courses.

name: Bachelor of Artificial Intelligence
description:
The Bachelor of Artificial Intelligence at the University of Technology Sydney (UTS) teaches students to design, build and evaluate AI solutions, covering deep learning, reinforcement learning, image processing, computer vision and natural language processing, on a foundation of mathematics, statistics and software development.
The degree can be taken as the standard program or through the UTS Industry Degree Academy. City campus graduates are eligible to apply for Australian Computer Society professional membership. Study takes three years full-time. English requirements are IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 in writing.
curriculum: Core subjects — 31265 Communication for IT Professionals; 43030 Professional Practice in Computing; 31268 Web Systems; 31269 Business Requirements Modelling; 41092 Network Fundamentals; 31271 Database Fundamentals; 31272 Project Management and the Professional.
admission_requirements: Applicants must have completed an Australian Year 12 qualification, Australian Qualifications Framework Diploma, or equivalent Australian or overseas qualification at the required level. Additional application and selection procedures apply for the IDeA version of this course. Assumed knowledge: HSC Mathematics Advanced and any two units of English. Mathematics Extension 1 and English Advanced are recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); TOEFL iBT 79 (writing 21); PTE Academic 58 (writing 50). UTS also accepts its UTS College academic English courses.

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
The Bachelor of Business at the University of Technology Sydney (UTS) is one of the most popular business degrees in New South Wales. A foundational first year covers core subjects such as Accounting and Accountability, Economics for Business, People and Organisations, and Marketing and Customer Value, after which students choose a major from areas including accounting, finance, marketing, human resource management and management.
Students can add a second major or sub-major, take electives from other UTS faculties, and complete workplace internships. Study takes three years full-time. English requirements are IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 in writing, and assumed knowledge is mathematics and any two units of English.
curriculum: Core subjects — 22108 Accounting and Accountability; 23115 Economics for Business; 21212 People and Organisations; 26134 Responsible Evidence-Based Decisions; 24109 Marketing and Customer Value; 25400 Financial Literacy; 21214 Business and Social Impact.
admission_requirements: Applicants must have completed an Australian Year 12 qualification, Australian Qualifications Framework Diploma, or equivalent Australian or overseas qualification at the required level. Assumed knowledge: Mathematics and any two units of English.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); TOEFL iBT 79 (writing 21); PTE Academic 58 (writing 50). UTS also accepts its UTS College academic English courses.

name: Bachelor of Communication (Honours)
description:
The Bachelor of Communication (Honours) at the University of Technology Sydney (UTS) is a fourth year of study for communication students, covering advanced work in social sciences, cultural studies and creative arts. Students develop critical thinking, creativity and project management through advanced coursework and a research project, with the specific path shaped by their discipline.
The honours year builds a foundation for postgraduate research or a research career, and supports work in digital media, public relations, journalism, policy and advocacy. English requirements are IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 in writing.
curriculum: Core subjects — 55993 Honours Research Design; 55994 Honours Project; 55990 Honours Theoretical Frameworks.
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR approximately 85-90, competitive entry across communication majors
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); TOEFL iBT 79 (writing 21); PTE Academic 58 (writing 50). UTS also accepts its UTS College academic English courses.

name: Bachelor of Communication in Creative Writing
description:
The Bachelor of Communication in Creative Writing at the University of Technology Sydney (UTS) pairs core communication subjects with a Creative Writing stream covering narrative, writing and editing, and publishing practice. Disciplinary electives include media law and ethics, digital audiences and creative advertising, and students can add a second stream in journalism, media business or strategic communication.
Graduates build a portfolio across fiction, creative non-fiction, poetry and screenwriting. Study takes three years full-time. English requirements are IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 in writing.
curriculum: Core subjects — 52600 Communication and Society; 52601 Communication and Technology; 52602 Communication and Work Futures; 52690 Narrative in Theory and Practice; 52691 Creative Writing Foundations; 52692 Imagining the Real; 52603 Writing Through Form and Genre.
admission_requirements: Applicants must have completed an Australian Year 12 qualification, Australian Qualifications Framework Diploma, or equivalent Australian or overseas qualification at the required level.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); TOEFL iBT 79 (writing 21); PTE Academic 58 (writing 50). UTS also accepts its UTS College academic English courses.

name: Bachelor of Communication in Digital and Social Media
description:
The Bachelor of Communication in Digital and Social Media at the University of Technology Sydney (UTS) was one of the first Australian degrees focused on this field. Alongside core communication subjects, the Digital and Social Media stream covers media metrics, digital audiences, user experience, UI design and app prototyping, with the option of a second stream or an industry internship.
Graduates work as social media managers, UX and UI designers, and digital campaign managers. Study takes three years full-time. English requirements are IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 in writing.
curriculum: Core subjects — 52600 Communication and Society; 52601 Communication and Technology; 52602 Communication and Work Futures; 52680 Digital Media Industries; 52681 Understanding Digital Audiences; 52682 Digital Media Metrics; 52683 User Experience Research.
admission_requirements: Applicants must have completed an Australian Year 12 qualification, Australian Qualifications Framework Diploma, or equivalent Australian or overseas qualification at the required level.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); TOEFL iBT 79 (writing 21); PTE Academic 58 (writing 50). UTS also accepts its UTS College academic English courses.

name: Bachelor of Communication in Journalism
description:
The Bachelor of Communication in Journalism at the University of Technology Sydney (UTS) combines core communication subjects, such as Communication and Society and Communication and Technology, with a Journalism stream covering news, reporting in the age of social media, media law and ethics, and multimedia reporting.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description: UTS Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) prepares students for professional engineering practice with complex systems and large-scale projects. Majors include biomedical, civil, civil and environmental, data science, electrical, electronic, mechanical, mechanical and mechatronic, mechatronic and software engineering, with a Flexible option that lets students explore in first year before choosing; the fully accredited majors are recognised internationally under the Washington Accord. The degree is four years full-time or eight part-time. Entry is based on a selection rank that varies by major, and applicants need HSC Mathematics Extension 1, Physics and English (English Advanced recommended) or equivalents. Indicative international tuition is around A$54,800 per year. Career paths follow the chosen major across biomedical, civil and environmental, electrical and electronic, and mechanical and mechatronic engineering.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) Diploma in Professional Engineering Practice
Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) in Software Engineering
description:
Software Engineering at UTS sits inside the Bachelor of Engineering (Honours), which means students get the full four-year accredited engineering treatment rather than a computer-science-adjacent degree with "engineering" in the name for marketing purposes. It's accredited by Engineers Australia and recognised under the Washington Accord, so the qualification travels internationally.

What distinguishes it from a straight CS degree is the amount of systems-level and professional-practice content: subjects on requirements engineering, software architecture and formal engineering practice sit alongside the expected programming, algorithms and databases sequence. Many students take the course through UTS's Diploma in Professional Engineering Practice pathway, which embeds paid industry placements into the degree. UTS has one of the larger cooperative-education programs among Australian engineering schools, with placement partners across Sydney's finance, defence and telecommunications sectors.

Fourth year centres on a substantial capstone engineering project, usually with an external client or research supervisor, which functions as the honours thesis component. Engineers Australia accreditation also means the degree satisfies a chartered engineer pathway later on, something worth knowing if a student's ambitions run past their first graduate job.
curriculum:
Duration: 4 years full-time (or 5 years with Diploma in Professional Engineering Practice / industry placement)
Year 1: Engineering Study and Professional Practice, Programming Fundamentals, Mathematical Modelling for Engineers, Introduction to Electrical Engineering
Year 2: Data Structures and Algorithms, Object-Oriented Software Development, Software Architecture, Discrete Mathematics, Systems Analysis
Year 3: Requirements Engineering, Database Systems, Software Construction and Testing, Engineering Elective, Industry-focused Professional Practice subjects
Year 4: Capstone Engineering Project (thesis-equivalent, 2 sessions), Software Engineering electives, Professional Engineering Practice
Optional: paid industry placement (Diploma in Professional Engineering Practice) adds roughly 12 months across the degree

Students can take electives across science or from other faculties such as business and law. Study takes three years full-time. English requirements are IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 in writing.
