The course is highly multidisciplinary, covering development policy and practice, the intellectual history of development, and internal debates within the field, with units ranging from development economics to environmental sciences, food and agriculture, governance, public health, and law and policy. Graduates work with aid agencies, NGOs, government and international organisations.

name: Master of International Law
description: The Master of International Law at the University of Western Australia helps students advance their knowledge of international law and open up career opportunities in government, non-government and private institutions where international law is relevant. Taught by a team of international experts with backgrounds in practice, the course develops a sound understanding of the theory and practice of international law and how international institutions work. It is available to law and non-law graduates. Graduates work in legal, policy, diplomacy and advisory roles.

name: Master of International Relations
description: The Master of International Relations at the University of Western Australia is a professionally oriented postgraduate course studied over three or four semesters full-time equivalent. It offers deep expertise in international relations with a particular focus on the dynamic Indo-Pacific and Indian Ocean regions, and provides the knowledge, skills and networks for a career in foreign affairs and diplomacy, government, international and non-governmental organisations, the media and education. Graduates work across diplomacy, government, international organisations and research.

name: Master of Landscape Architecture
description: The Master of Landscape Architecture at the University of Western Australia provides an education in the design, management and resilience of natural and built landscapes for the benefit of communities and to improve the quality of the environment. Students gain the knowledge and skills to respond to complex issues such as climate change and biodiversity loss by applying systems thinking and creative practice to develop long-term, multi-scale solutions. Graduates work in landscape architecture practice, urban design, and environmental planning toward professional registration.

name: Master of Law Policy and Government
description: The Master of Law, Policy and Government at the University of Western Australia is available to law and non-law graduates seeking an advanced understanding of socio-legal theory, policy development and the skills required to work in or with government. Combining theory and practically oriented units, the course suits those building a career in the public sector as legal practitioners, or in private industry where it intersects with government approval, regulation and compliance. Graduates work in policy, regulatory, governance and legal roles.

name: Master of Laws
description: The Master of Laws at the University of Western Australia is designed to equip practising lawyers and law graduates with an advanced understanding of the law to meet the challenges of the dynamic workplace. Students learn from experienced teaching staff, including current and former lawyers and former judges, and study alongside the next generation of leaders in legal practice, government, business and the not-for-profit sector. Graduates deepen their specialist expertise and advance their legal careers.

name: Master of Management (Coursework)
description: The Master of Management at the University of Western Australia is ideal for graduates seeking further business expertise and to boost their employment opportunities around the world. Experienced academics and industry partners ensure students are exposed to current theory and practice, alongside extracurricular activities from career fairs and networking events to student groups, professional development workshops and guest lectures from senior executives. Graduates move into management and leadership roles across sectors.

name: Master of Marine Biology (coursework or coursework and dissertation)
description: The Master of Marine Biology at the University of Western Australia is designed to prepare students for a meaningful marine biology career in industry or as a researcher, addressing an unmet need in Western Australia to generate graduates who can contribute to marine and coastal science and management. The course focuses on both the quantitative elements of marine biology and processes in marine environments, and the application and translation of marine science into industry practice and management. Graduates work in marine research, conservation, consulting and management.

name: Master of Marketing
description: The Master of Marketing at the University of Western Australia focuses on making and keeping customers by finding, communicating and sustaining the competitive advantage that makes a company successful. Topics covered include advertising, company strategy, competitive analysis and value creation, and students have the opportunity to undertake projects for real organisations, having previously worked with companies including Coles, Google, Microsoft and Rio Tinto. Graduates work in marketing strategy, brand, analytics and communication roles.

name: Master of Medical Physics (coursework and dissertation)
description: The Master of Medical Physics at the University of Western Australia develops the knowledge and skills to combine physics principles with engineering methods and techniques in the clinical environment and in research, for the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of human diseases. The course is designed to meet the requirements of international students. Graduates work as medical physicists in hospitals, radiation oncology, diagnostic imaging and research, on the pathway to clinical certification.

name: Master of Mining and Energy Law
description: The Master of Mining and Energy Law at the University of Western Australia is designed to give legal and non-legal professionals the expertise to pursue careers in the mining and energy industries. Subject areas include the exploration and production of minerals and petroleum in Australia, native title, concepts of sustainability and social licence to operate, and broader policy objectives, alongside the technical knowledge of how petroleum is produced and how iron ore is mined. Graduates work in legal, compliance, policy and advisory roles across the resources sector.

name: Master of Music (Research)
description: The Master of Music at the University of Western Australia extends existing skills in music, both as a professional-level degree and as a platform for doctoral study. It can be taken in composition, performance or musicology and consists of a combination of thesis and creative work, with all candidates producing independent research under the guidance of a supervisor. Graduates pursue performance, composition, research and teaching careers across the music and creative arts sector.

name: Master of Ocean Leadership
description: The Master of Ocean Leadership at the University of Western Australia provides graduates from any field with ocean-related leadership skills and expertise across marine science, engineering, law, resource economics and environmental management. This enables graduates to strategically address human challenges in ocean systems and implement solutions for the future of coasts and seas, working in multidisciplinary contexts to lead and contribute to effective teams. The highly interactive program suits professionals and recent graduates alike.

name: Master of Oceanography (coursework or coursework and dissertation)
description: The Master of Oceanography at the University of Western Australia develops a sound understanding of dynamic marine and coastal systems and the skills to tackle ocean challenges. The oceans provide food, act as a conduit for global trade, provide renewable energy and drive coastal economies, and graduates are in demand who can support sustainable ocean use, mitigate climate change impacts and drive the Blue Economy. Western Australia's location on the Indian Ocean rim provides an excellent living laboratory. Graduates work in oceanography, coastal engineering, environmental and research roles.

name: Master of Offshore and Coastal Engineering
description: The Master of Offshore and Coastal Engineering at the University of Western Australia prepares graduates from engineering backgrounds with the knowledge and practical skills to lead innovation in offshore and coastal engineering. The course integrates disciplinary knowledge across the whole water column, from oceanography and hydrodynamics to structural and geotechnical engineering and data science, to analyse and design ocean engineering solutions for ocean energy infrastructure, aquaculture, shipping and coastal development. Graduates work across the offshore, marine and coastal engineering sectors.

name: Master of Ore Deposit Geology
description: The Master of Ore Deposit Geology at the University of Western Australia provides a high-quality, advanced education in the geology and evaluation of ore deposits, designed for geologists with different levels of professional experience. Building on UWA's international reputation in economic geology and strong collaboration with the minerals industry, the course focuses on the formation, exploration and evaluation of ore deposits, including data integration and modelling approaches. Graduates work in mineral exploration, mining geology and resource evaluation.

name: Master of Pathology (Thesis and Coursework)
description: The Master of Pathology at the University of Western Australia initially focuses on a student-designed research project proposal, after which students implement the project, carrying out, evaluating and presenting a discrete body of applied research relevant to pathology. Students present their findings to a forum of scientific peers or at scientific meetings. The course comprises a 36-point research project and 12 points of supporting research coursework. Graduates work in laboratory research, diagnostic pathology and academic roles.

name: Master of Physics
description: The Master of Physics at the University of Western Australia develops a combination of high-level research, analytical and problem-solving skills that are highly valued by industry and government employers. The course can be undertaken in specialisations including Astronomy and Astrophysics or Computational Physics, covering areas such as astro-statistics, galactic dynamics, plasma astrophysics, high-energy astrophysics, numerical methods and high-performance computing. Graduates work in research, data science, defence, and technical and analytical roles.

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description: The University of Western Australia's Master of Professional Accounting runs 1.5 to 2 years and is aimed squarely at graduates without an accounting background; applicants who already hold an accounting major are not eligible. Entry is a bachelor degree with a weighted average of at least 60 percent, or two years of relevant professional experience, or a UWA Graduate Certificate in Commerce, with IELTS 6.5 and no band below 6.0. The Accounting Practice specialisation satisfies the requirements of both Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand and CPA Australia; an Accounting Research specialisation with a dissertation is also offered. Graduates work in audit, advisory, financial reporting, management accounting and corporate finance. Indicative international tuition is around A$52,700 per year.

name: Master of Professional Engineering
description: The Master of Professional Engineering at the University of Western Australia is for students who have completed undergraduate studies in engineering and want to become a professionally accredited engineer. Students specialise in one of nine engineering disciplines and undertake advanced engineering technical units, professional units, design and research projects, and a 12-week professional practicum. Graduates practise as professional engineers or pursue further research, and find employment across a wide range of engineering sectors.

name: Master of Public Health
description: The University of Western Australia's Master of Public Health is a 1.5-year degree. Entry is a bachelor degree with a weighted average of at least 60 percent and IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. A 36-point core builds a foundation in epidemiology, biostatistics, qualitative research methods, health economics and health promotion, and electives include Aboriginal health, environmental and occupational health, clinical epidemiology, and health leadership and management. Students choose one of three pathways: coursework only, coursework with a dissertation, or coursework with a practicum placement. Graduates work in government health departments, non-government organisations, research and health service management. Indicative international tuition is around A$47,800 per year.

name: Master of Public Policy
description: The Master of Public Policy at the University of Western Australia gives students a multidisciplinary understanding of the role of government in economic activity and public administration and governance, focusing on how government interacts with the economy, law and society. Topics include economic growth and stability, taxation, infrastructure, regulation, health, defence, education, comparative law, theories of justice and punishment, public international law and social security. The course integrates theory and practice, with a choice of specialisations. Graduates work in policy, government and advisory roles.

name: Master of Renewable and Future Energy
description: The Master of Renewable and Future Energy at the University of Western Australia responds to the energy industry's transition by providing engineering professionals with relevant renewable energy skills for a growing market. The course draws on research expertise in both traditional and renewable energy and strong connections with local industry partners, and takes advantage of the growing role of renewables in remote and small communities of Western Australia. Renewable energy expertise cuts across many disciplines. Graduates work in renewable energy engineering, project development and consulting.

name: Master of Resources and International Commercial Law
description: The Master of Resources and International Commercial Law at the University of Western Australia gives students specialised legal knowledge for a career in the highly regulated mining, energy and natural resources sector. Students learn about a wide range of legal considerations across the sector as well as the technical knowledge behind it, such as how petroleum is produced and how iron ore is mined, gaining a comprehensive and multifaceted understanding of the industry. The course is available for law and non-law graduates. Graduates work in legal, compliance and commercial roles across resources and energy.

name: Master of Rural and Remote Medicine (Thesis and Coursework)
description: The Master of Rural and Remote Medicine at the University of Western Australia allows students to tackle the questions important to those who live in the bush, questions best explored in a local context, with Indigenous health a special focus. As rural and remote medicine is a generalist discipline, the range of research topics is wide, from large-scale epidemiological studies to educational, qualitative and clinical studies. Graduates work in rural and remote clinical practice, teaching and research.

name: Master of Science (thesis and coursework)
description: The Master of Science (Thesis and Coursework) at the University of Western Australia is a research degree with students selecting one discipline area from Agriculture and Environment, Biological Sciences, Earth Sciences, Human Sciences, Molecular Sciences or Psychological Science. Students gain advanced knowledge in their chosen area through independent research and coursework units that include a literature review and proposal unit and an advanced coursework unit, working with internationally recognised researchers. Graduates progress to doctoral study or to research and technical roles.

name: Master of Science Communication
description: The Master of Science Communication at the University of Western Australia teaches the principles of effective science communication and the practical skills needed to communicate with audiences ranging from children to scientists. Students develop strategies that address the communication needs of groups such as government organisations, museums, science centres and research centres, and gain experience in new media, written, oral and visual presentations, science performance and working with industry experts. Graduates work in science communication, media, outreach and engagement roles.

name: Master of Social Work (Coursework)
description: The Master of Social Work at the University of Western Australia prepares beginning social work practitioners for employment in local, state and international human services agencies. Led by qualified, experienced and research-active experts with strong ties to the profession and community services, the course benefits from research-led teaching based on up-to-date data, allowing students to apply the most relevant theory to practice. Social work has been taught at UWA since 1965. Graduates work in child protection, health, mental health, community development and policy.

name: Master of Strategic Communication
description: The Master of Strategic Communication at the University of Western Australia develops expertise and highly sought-after skills in designing and managing communication strategies, projects and campaigns across a range of media platforms and professional contexts. As digital media grows in importance, organisations of all sizes need communication experts. The course advances students' capacity to succeed in a range of media and communication roles and to provide effective strategy and leadership for industry, government and community. Graduates work in communication, public relations and campaign roles.

name: Master of Studies
description: The Master of Studies at the University of Western Australia lets students create their own course, selecting a unique combination of postgraduate units from different schools and faculties across the University to achieve their academic, professional or personal goals. Many of the world's major problems and areas of current research are multidisciplinary, and this course enables students to draw on a broad range of postgraduate units, subject to their previous study. Graduates gain a flexible, tailored qualification aligned to their career direction.

name: Master of Taxation Law
description: The Master of Taxation Law at the University of Western Australia is an advanced program designed to give tax professionals the expertise necessary to specialise in the complex and varied field of taxation law. Tax law impacts the outcomes of all business and work activities, and students develop an advanced understanding of the technicalities of tax law across a range of specialist areas. Graduates work as tax specialists in law and accounting firms, corporations and government.

name: Master of Teaching-Secondary
description: The Master of Teaching (Secondary) at the University of Western Australia is a teacher preparation program for university graduates who seek to begin a rewarding career in secondary education. The course ensures students have an in-depth knowledge of the theory and the practical skills required for secondary teaching, combining subject-area expertise with supervised professional placements. Graduates are qualified to register and teach in secondary schools in their subject areas.

name: Master of Translation Studies
description: The Master of Translation Studies at the University of Western Australia provides specialised translation training between English and one of ten Asian and European languages, at the home to the largest selection of language study options in Western Australia. The course is accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters, and is taught by practitioners and translation researchers to help students develop a competitive edge in an increasingly globalised job market. Graduates work as translators across government, business and the language services industry.

name: Master of Urban Design
description: The Master of Urban Design at the University of Western Australia, delivered by the Australian Urban Design Research Centre, prepares students to participate at all levels of the urban design profession. Students develop an in-depth understanding of urban design theories and issues, techniques of urban analysis, and skills for the design and development of cities and urban places, through a first year of focused studies in history, theory, implementation strategy and studio-based learning and a second year of advanced work. Graduates work in urban design, planning and city-shaping roles.

name: Masters of Commerce (Coursework) and Masters of Translation Studies (Coursework or Coursework and Dissertation)
Bachelor of Arts
description:
A fairly standard humanities generalist degree, whose distinguishing feature is breadth. UOW's BA covers majors from history and English literatures through creative writing, politics, sociology, and Asian studies, and it's genuinely flexible about double majors and combining with education, law, or science. It runs through the Faculty of the Arts, Social Sciences and Humanities.

Because Wollongong's cohort is smaller than the capital-city sandstones, tutorials tend to run at a size where students get to know staff by name. The creative writing major in particular has built a local reputation through a student anthology the program publishes each year.
curriculum:
Year 1: two introductory subjects in each of two chosen majors, plus electives
Years 2-3: minimum 8 subjects per major, increasing specialisation, research methods subject in at least one major
Typical majors: English Literatures, History, Creative Writing, Politics and International Relations, Sociology, Asian Studies, Philosophy
Capstone: independent research project or internship subject in final year, depending on major
admission_requirements: ATAR 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Arts in Western Civilisation
description: The Bachelor of Arts in Western Civilisation at the University of Wollongong focuses on close reading, peer dialogue and sustained engagement with great works in small-group settings. Students engage directly with major works of art, literature, philosophy, politics, religion and science from across the ages, studied in live conversation with one another. The degree embeds a Liberal Arts major centred on perennial questions about truth, knowledge, virtue, the self and what it means to lead a good life, responding to contemporary challenges. Graduates pursue careers in policy, education, media, law and the public sector.

name: Bachelor of Business
description: The University of Wollongong Bachelor of Business lets students try study areas before choosing a major in second year from Marketing, Management or Accounting. Students build practical skills alongside the core disciplines of business through project work and a Business Internship program that places them with industry partners such as KPMG, Mercer, NAB and Accor Hotels. A UOW College Diploma of Business provides entry into second year, and the degree is also offered online with scheduled classes. Indicative international tuition is around A$36,000 per year. UOW reports that over 90 per cent of its business students find employment after graduating. Graduates work in marketing, management and accounting roles across the private and public sectors.

name: Bachelor of Business Analytics
description: The Bachelor of Business Analytics at the University of Wollongong provides the skills to become a strategic business problem solver and an essential part of decisions made across the entire business lifecycle, an area of increased graduate demand. Students study a combination of business and computer science, learning how to analyse large volumes of data to support decision making across all areas of business, and gain an understanding of data management concepts and processing relational data with SQL. Internship opportunities and a fast-track to a master's degree are available. Graduates work as business and data analysts.

name: Bachelor of Business Information Systems
description: The Bachelor of Business Information Systems at the University of Wollongong prepares students to analyse business problems and find IT solutions, from running efficiency audits on information systems to analysing file management systems and designing business software applications. Students study the fundamentals of computer science and IT, including programming, problem-solving, networks and communications, web technology, data management, systems analysis, human-computer interaction and project management. The degree is designed to prepare students for a career as a systems analyst or information systems specialist. Graduates work across business and technology roles.

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description:
UOW's business generalist degree, run out of the Faculty of Business and Law. Majors span accounting, finance, marketing, management, and international business, with the accounting major accredited by CPA Australia and CAANZ, which is relevant for anyone planning to go into public practice.

The degree leans on UOW's industry links in the Illawarra (BlueScope, Port Kembla logistics firms, regional financial services) for internship placements, and there's a business analytics elective stream that's grown in enrolment as demand for data-literate commerce graduates has increased.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting Fundamentals, Economics for Business, Business Statistics, Marketing Principles
Year 2: Corporate Finance, Management and Organisational Behaviour, first major subjects
Year 3: second major or elective deepening, Business Law, Strategic Management
Major options: Accounting, Finance, Marketing, Management, International Business, Human Resource Management
Capstone: work-integrated learning subject or business strategy capstone, final year
admission_requirements: ATAR 75 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Communication and Media
description:
Run through the School of the Arts, English and Media, this degree covers journalism, digital media production, public relations, and media studies as combinable strands rather than forcing an early major choice. UOW has invested in student-run media output, a digital publication and campus radio-adjacent projects, that functions as informal work experience alongside the formal internship subject.

It's a smaller program than the media schools at bigger metro universities, which in practice means more hands-on time per student on the video and podcast equipment rather than queueing for bookings.
curriculum:
Year 1: Media and Communication, Introduction to Journalism, Digital Media Production, Communication Theory
Year 2: Public Relations Principles, Media Law and Ethics, Video and Audio Production, Social Media Strategy
Year 3: specialisation electives (journalism, PR, digital production), Media Industries and Policy, Internship (WIL)
Capstone: portfolio or major media production project, final year
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Computer Science
description:
The undergraduate sibling of UOW's Master of Computer Science, this degree covers programming fundamentals through software engineering practice, security, and a choice of specialisation streams: the school offers strands touching games and interactive media, data-adjacent electives, and networks and cybersecurity. UOW's CS undergrad has an established internship option that a meaningful slice of students take up, usually with regional employers or Sydney firms willing to take on Illawarra-based interns.

First year is common across CS, IT and related degrees, so switching majors early is low-friction. The degree is accredited with the Australian Computer Society, which matters for anyone aiming at visa-sponsored roles later.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Programming, Data Structures and Algorithms, Discrete Mathematics, Computer Systems
Year 2: Object-Oriented Design, Database Systems, Operating Systems, Software Engineering
Year 3: Networking, specialisation electives (security, AI/ML, interactive media), Professional Practice
Optional: Professional and Community Engagement (WIL/internship) subject in place of an elective
Capstone: team-based major project, Year 3
admission_requirements: ATAR 75 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Creative Arts
description: The Bachelor of Creative Arts at the University of Wollongong develops confident, adaptable thinkers through hands-on learning, alongside study of each discipline's historical and theoretical contexts to prepare students for the changing world of contemporary arts and culture. In first year students choose a major from Creative Writing, Music, Performance and Theatre, Visual Arts, or Visual Arts and Design, studying in purpose-built facilities including industry-standard music recording studios, painting and textile studios, art galleries and performance theatres. Graduates pursue practice, production and creative industry careers.

name: Bachelor of Criminology
description: The Bachelor of Criminology at the University of Wollongong helps students explore crime trends, offending, victimisation, prevention and policy from individual, social and structural perspectives, examining why people commit crime and how societies respond through policing, courts, prisons and alternative justice approaches. The degree emphasises evidence-based thinking, helping students develop skills in analysing data, questioning misinformation and clearly communicating complex ideas, and students learn from internationally recognised academics. Graduates work in criminal justice, policy, research, corrections, policing and community roles.

name: Bachelor of Data Science and Analytics
Bachelor of Data Science and Decisions
description:
The University of Wollongong's Bachelor of Data Science and Decisions is a newer-generation degree pairing statistics and computing with decision science and business analytics, pitched at the gap between a pure CS degree and a pure statistics degree, aimed at students who want to work as analysts or data scientists rather than software engineers or statisticians specifically. Taught jointly by the business faculty and computing school, which shows up in units combining optimisation and decision theory with programming and machine learning.

Because it's a relatively new offering, cohort sizes are still modest, and the school has used that to keep project work genuinely individualised rather than templated group assignments.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Programming, Statistics for Data Science, Business Decision Making, Mathematics for Data Science
Year 2: Databases, Machine Learning Fundamentals, Optimisation and Decision Analysis, Data Visualisation
Year 3: Big Data Analytics, Applied Business Analytics, Capstone Data Science Project, electives
Capstone: applied project with an industry or research dataset, final year
admission_requirements: ATAR 80 or equivalent, Mathematics recommended
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Economics and Finance
description: The Bachelor of Economics and Finance at the University of Wollongong offers an integrated understanding of two interrelated fields, blending economic theories with financial practices to give students a comprehensive view of global markets. The degree covers economic analysis, monetary systems and investment strategies, fostering critical thinking and financial decision-making skills, and covers microeconomics and macroeconomics, corporate finance, investment analysis, portfolio management, statistics and econometrics. Graduates work in banking, investment, economic analysis, policy and financial services roles.

name: Bachelor of Education - The Early Years
Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description: The University of Wollongong Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) lets students try all study areas before choosing a major in second year from biomedical, civil, computer and autonomous systems, electrical and electronics, environmental, materials, mechanical, mechatronic, mining, or telecommunications engineering and internet of things. A single major requires at least 192 credit points and normally takes four years; a double major requires 240 credit points and takes five, as do double degrees. Entry is based on an ATAR or equivalent at the level UOW sets each year. Indicative international tuition is around A$44,300 per year. Graduates work as professional engineers in their chosen discipline across construction, resources, manufacturing, energy and technology.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) - Civil Engineering
description:
The University of Wollongong's Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) in Civil Engineering is a four-year Engineers Australia-accredited degree run through the School of Civil, Mining and Environmental Engineering. Students get access to the SMART Infrastructure Facility's transport and infrastructure modelling research, and the degree includes a mandatory minimum 12 weeks of industrial experience, which the school helps place, often with Illawarra-region firms doing heavy industry, port, or rail infrastructure work given the area's industrial history around the steelworks and Port Kembla.

Structural, geotechnical, water, and transport engineering are the core specialisation threads, and the thesis project in the final year is usually tied to a live industry or research problem rather than a hypothetical brief.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Mechanics, Mathematics for Engineers 1 & 2, Materials Science, Engineering Design
Year 2: Structural Analysis, Fluid Mechanics, Geotechnical Engineering 1, Surveying
Year 3: Structural Design (steel and concrete), Water Engineering, Transport Engineering, Construction Management
Year 4: Capstone Engineering Design Project (thesis), advanced electives, Professional Practice
Mandatory: minimum 12 weeks industrial experience
admission_requirements: ATAR 80 or equivalent, completion of Year 12 with Mathematics
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Engineering Technology
description: The Bachelor of Engineering Technology at the University of Wollongong is for innovators and problem-solvers interested in developing in-demand skills across broad areas of engineering, enabling graduates to work alongside engineers on real-world projects in all engineering fields. Students study foundation subjects in mathematics and physics combined with options in programming, electrical systems, sustainable design, materials selection and mechanics, and can shape the degree around their interests. Graduates work in engineering support, technical and project roles across industry.

name: Bachelor of Environmental Science
description:
Sits within the Faculty of Science, Medicine and Health and makes practical use of Wollongong's geography: the Illawarra escarpment, coastal wetlands, and nearby national parks are used as actual field sites rather than being theoretical case studies. Fieldwork is a genuine differentiator here; students spend blocks of time out of the classroom on ecological surveys, water quality monitoring, and soil sampling from early in the degree.

Graduates go into environmental consulting and local or state government environmental roles. The degree includes a professional practice subject aimed specifically at that job market, and there's crossover with the university's earth and environmental sciences research groups for students wanting an honours pathway.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Environmental Science, Ecology, Earth Systems, Chemistry for Environmental Science
Year 2: Environmental Monitoring and Assessment, Soil Science, Hydrology, GIS and Remote Sensing
Year 3: Environmental Management and Policy, Conservation Biology, field research project, Professional Practice
Fieldwork: recurring field-based subjects using Illawarra escarpment, coastal and wetland sites
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Exercise Science
description: The Bachelor of Exercise Science at the University of Wollongong prepares students to apply the science of exercise to improve human health, fitness and performance, designing, implementing and evaluating exercise and physical activity programs for a wide range of people. The degree covers anatomy, physiology, exercise physiology, exercise prescription, nutrition, psychology, neuromechanics and biomechanics, and prepares students for careers in sporting organisations, education, community and corporate health units, and gymnasiums, or for further study in clinical exercise physiology.

name: Bachelor of Exercise Science and Rehabilitation
description: The Bachelor of Exercise Science and Rehabilitation at the University of Wollongong prepares students to become exercise physiologists, specialised allied health professionals who use exercise strategies to enhance health, aid recovery and foster independence among people with chronic health conditions, disabilities or injuries. Students study anatomy, physiology, clinical exercise physiology, exercise prescription, biomechanics and neuromechanics, working across settings including private clinics, hospitals, community health centres, aged care, workplace rehabilitation and research. Graduates work as accredited exercise physiologists.

name: Bachelor of Health and Physical Education
Bachelor of Information Technology
description: The Bachelor of Information Technology at the University of Wollongong builds knowledge across the underlying sciences, IT, engineering and mathematical methodologies used to create and manage computer-based applications, systems and networks. Students study the fundamentals of computer science and IT, including programming, problem-solving, network and communications, web technology, data management, systems analysis, human-computer interaction and project management, and gain foundation knowledge of organisational areas such as database management and information systems analysis and design. Graduates work as developers, systems analysts, network specialists and IT managers.

name: Bachelor of International Studies
description: The Bachelor of International Studies at the University of Wollongong equips students with the tools to respond to global challenges by understanding how political, social, cultural and economic forces intersect at local, national and international levels, and how they influence what comes next. Students are encouraged to question how they see the world and to recognise how their perspectives are shaped by experience, history and culture, building understanding of today's globalised world through the study of nations, power and global connections. Graduates work in government, international organisations, NGOs, business and research.

name: Bachelor of Journalism
description: Journalism at the University of Wollongong is offered within the Bachelor of Communication and Media, which builds students' creative and critical thinking around communication, how it works and why it matters. As media, rapid technological change and artificial intelligence reshape content creation, the degree develops human-centred communication with clarity, empathy and purpose, covering media production, journalism, strategic communication and communication research. Graduates work as journalists, producers, content creators and communication professionals across news, media and organisations.

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
UOW's LLB is taught out of the School of Law on the main campus and is accredited for admission purposes in NSW. It can be taken standalone but most students do a combined degree: Laws/Arts, Laws/Commerce, Laws/Science are the common pairings. The law school runs a clinical legal education program through the Illawarra Legal Centre, giving students real client contact under supervision before they graduate, a differentiator from programs that stay purely classroom-based until Practical Legal Training.

Wollongong isn't a huge legal market compared to Sydney, so a lot of graduates end up doing PLT and early career work there, but the local legal aid and community legal centre placements give students exposure most city-campus students don't get until much later in their careers.
curriculum:
Core (Priestley 11 subjects): Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law, Property, Equity, Constitutional Law, Administrative Law, Evidence, Civil Procedure, Company Law, Professional Conduct
Electives: minimum 8 subjects from areas including IP law, family law, international law, employment law
Clinical option: supervised placement at Illawarra Legal Centre (credit-bearing)
Capstone: research subject or moot competition, final year
admission_requirements: ATAR 90 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Marine Science
description: The Bachelor of Marine Science at the University of Wollongong prepares students to investigate the physical and biological nature of oceans, their conservation and environmental management, and their impact on human society. Students learn how to understand, observe and define oceanographic and coastal processes, ocean biodiversity, governance and management, and use emerging technologies in marine science. The degree benefits from proximity to the diverse New South Wales South Coast environment, providing substantial fieldwork opportunities. Graduates work in marine research, conservation, environmental management and government roles.

name: Bachelor of Mathematics (Honours)
description: Mathematics at the University of Wollongong is the language of data and the basis for successful decision-making and problem-solving across all sectors and industries, with mathematical and statistical models used to analyse information and forecast results in economics, finance, medicine and industrial processes. The mathematics degree teaches highly transferable skills in problem-solving, data analysis, probability and variability, modelling, logistics and logic, and students tackle authentic real-world problems drawn from industry, science and government. Graduates work as mathematicians, statisticians, data analysts and modellers, or progress to research.

name: Bachelor of Mathematics Advanced
description: The Bachelor of Mathematics Advanced at the University of Wollongong is an elite degree available to students who have achieved outstanding results at the highest level of mathematics in high school or have equivalent knowledge on entry. It offers an accelerated program of studies for high-achieving students with a passion for mathematics, and a unique feature is that students undertake supervised undergraduate research projects, working closely with active researchers to develop independent learning, critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Graduates work as mathematicians, data scientists, statisticians and analysts, or progress to research.

name: Bachelor of Medical and Health Sciences
description:
This one is UOW's on-ramp into its own Graduate School of Medicine. Most students taking it are aiming at the Doctor of Medicine, and the course is built around that transition: a defined number of places carry a guaranteed pathway into the MD for students who hit the GPA and interview bar, rather than everyone having to sit GAMSAT cold. It sits in the Faculty of Science, Medicine and Health and shares anatomy and physiology teaching space with the medical school next door.

First year is standard biomedical science: anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, cell biology, shared with other health science cohorts. From second year it narrows into pathophysiology, pharmacology, and population health, with an honours research year in fourth year that pairs students with active medical research groups, several connected to the Illawarra Health and Medical Research Institute on campus. Not everyone ends up in medicine; it's a legitimate finishing degree for people heading into health policy, medical research, or postgraduate allied health study, but the MD pathway is the reason most people enrol.
curriculum:
Year 1: Human Biology, Chemistry for Health Sciences, Foundations of Anatomy and Physiology, Introduction to Health and Medical Sciences
Year 2: Systems Physiology, Biochemistry, Microbiology and Immunology, Pathophysiology
Year 3: Pharmacology, Population and Global Health, Research Methods, discipline electives
Year 4 (Honours): independent research thesis with a medical/health research supervisor, advanced seminar subjects
MD pathway: GPA threshold assessed progressively, guaranteed interview and provisional entry confirmed by end of Year 3
admission_requirements: ATAR 85 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Medical and Radiation Physics
Bachelor of Medical and Radiation Physics Advanced (Honours)
Bachelor of Nursing
description:
UOW's nursing degree leads to registration eligibility with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. It carries a heavy clinical placement load: well over 800 hours spread across acute, aged care, community, and mental health settings, mostly within Illawarra Shoalhaven Local Health District facilities given the university's location next to Wollongong Hospital.

Simulation labs on campus get heavy use in first and second year before students move to live placements, and the school runs a specific rural and remote placement stream for students willing to travel, which some take up for the different clinical exposure it offers.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Health Assessment, first clinical placement block
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Pharmacology, Aged Care placement
Year 3: Acute and Critical Care Nursing, Community and Primary Health Care, Paediatric and Maternal Nursing, final capstone placement
Placement hours: 800+ across the degree, mix of acute, community, aged care and mental health settings
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 or equivalent, National Police Check and Working with Children Check required
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 7.0)

name: Bachelor of Nutrition and Dietetics (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Nutrition and Dietetics (Honours) at the University of Wollongong prepares graduates to become specialist nutritionists who apply the science of food and nutrition to promote health, prevent and treat disease, and optimise the health of individuals, groups and communities. Students study the building blocks of nutrition, including biochemistry, nutritional epidemiology, public health nutrition and pathophysiology, alongside medical nutrition therapy and supervised professional practice. Graduates are accredited to work in community and public health nutrition, clinical dietetics, food service management and research.

name: Bachelor of Nutrition Science
description: The Bachelor of Nutrition Science at the University of Wollongong provides a strong foundation in nutritional science, including nutrition and exercise, community health nutrition, food chemistry, biochemistry and metabolism, along with training in nutrition research, health promotion and food innovation. Students build real-world skills for a wide range of careers in health, wellness, the food industry and beyond, and the final year includes elective subjects designed to broaden knowledge and experience. Graduates work in public health nutrition, food industry, community health and research roles.

name: Bachelor of Politics, Philosophy and Economics
Bachelor of Pre-Medicine, Science and Health
description: The Bachelor of Pre-Medicine, Science and Health at the University of Wollongong is a three-year degree designed to provide a strong foundation for students aspiring to enter medicine or other health and science-related fields. The course prepares students to be competitive for entry into medical school and exposes them to a range of pathways across the health and life sciences, with foundational subjects in anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, pharmacology, public health and medical ethics delivered through lectures, tutorials and hands-on practical sessions. Graduates progress to postgraduate medicine, allied health or research study.

name: Bachelor of Primary Education
description: The Bachelor of Primary Education at the University of Wollongong is a nationally accredited qualification for employment as a Kindergarten to Year 6 teacher in the public and independent school systems. The degree focuses on educating the whole child and promotes lifelong learning, with students undertaking a school placement from second year to learn by observation and apply their skills in the classroom early. Students also have opportunities for rural and international professional experiences. Graduates are qualified to teach across primary schools.

name: Bachelor of Professional Accounting
description: The Bachelor of Professional Accounting at the University of Wollongong focuses on supplying dependable, timely and precise information for decision-makers, with accountants playing a central part in advising senior management on organisational financial performance and direction. Students undertake a foundation year covering the core disciplines of business, then in second year study professional accounting subjects including financial reporting, auditing, management accounting, and information systems in accounting. Graduates work in accounting, audit, financial analysis and advisory roles across corporations, government and public practice.

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
An APAC-accredited undergraduate psychology degree, the standard first step toward provisional and eventual general registration in Australia. Taught within the School of Psychology, which has research groups in areas such as early childhood development and clinical neuropsychology that feed into elective options and honours placements.

The degree is explicitly the first three years of the accreditation sequence: students who want to practise go on to a competitive, GPA-gated Honours year and then postgraduate clinical training. UOW's cohort size means the practicals (running small real research studies as coursework) happen in genuinely small groups rather than being simulated at scale.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Psychology, Research Methods 1
Year 2: Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology, Cognition, Research Methods 2 (statistics)
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology, Personality, Psychological Assessment, Research Methods 3 (independent project)
Honours (separate, competitive entry): thesis plus advanced coursework, required for the provisional registration pathway
admission_requirements: ATAR 75 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Psychology (Honours)
description: Psychology at the University of Wollongong is the scientific study of the human mind and its functions and how this influences behaviour, with psychologists using research findings to help understand who we are and how we think, feel, act and change, and to promote wellbeing and understand psychological problems. The undergraduate psychology degree is the first stage of the qualification required to work as a professional psychologist, though this degree alone does not qualify graduates to practise. Graduates continue to accredited postgraduate study or work in research, human resources, health and community roles.

name: Bachelor of Public Health
description: The Bachelor of Public Health at the University of Wollongong teaches the art and science of promoting population health. Students learn to improve living standards by preventing infectious diseases and poor health caused by unhealthy lifestyles and other societal factors, and by enabling positive mental wellbeing based on scientific evidence. The degree develops skills in understanding research questions, investigating them and applying evidence to promote health and wellbeing in communities. Graduates work in health promotion, policy, epidemiology and program roles across government and non-government organisations.

name: Bachelor of Secondary Education
description: The Bachelor of Secondary Education at the University of Wollongong is a four-year degree that allows students to become high school teachers in their chosen discipline. The degree develops deep content and pedagogical knowledge, what to teach and how to teach it, within a globalised society, with students studying subjects aligned with their major discipline alongside professional knowledge about how the brain works, psychology and adolescent development, classroom management, Aboriginal education, inclusion, special education, technology and pedagogy. Graduates are qualified to teach in secondary schools.

name: Bachelor of Social Science
description: The Bachelor of Social Science at the University of Wollongong equips students with the skills to investigate complex issues and design practical, evidence-based solutions. Students explore challenges shaping communities today, such as housing affordability, food insecurity, racism and discrimination, community health and wellbeing, and social injustice and inequality, and learn how the policies that shape everyday life are developed, applied and improved through interdisciplinary study and majors. Graduates work in policy, community services, research, advocacy and government roles.

name: Bachelor of Social Work
description: The Bachelor of Social Work at the University of Wollongong prepares students to step confidently into a profession in high demand across Australia and globally, working in hospitals, schools, community services, justice systems and emerging digital and policy settings. Taught by academics who are active social work practitioners, this four-year accredited degree develops skills in advocacy, counselling, community development and case management through immersive, simulation-based classes and supervised field education. Graduates work across health, child protection, community services and policy, and are eligible for Australian Association of Social Workers membership.

name: Diploma of Arts, Social Science and Humanities
Doctor of Medicine
description: The Doctor of Medicine at the University of Wollongong aims to produce knowledgeable, caring and competent graduates who are well prepared to commence vocational training in any area of medicine. The MD is a four-year full-time degree, with each academic year approximately 42 weeks long, using a combination of face-to-face teaching, clinical placements, blended and online learning, and self-directed learning. Teaching takes place at the Wollongong, Shoalhaven and Southern Highlands campuses and one of eight rural hubs, giving the program a strong community and rural health emphasis. Graduates enter internship and prevocational training toward registration as a medical practitioner.

name: Graduate Certificate in Applied Finance
description: The Graduate Certificate in Applied Finance at the University of Wollongong is an introductory course providing a general understanding of areas in applied finance such as financial statement analysis, managerial finance, statistics and corporate governance. The course values prior learning and work experience, and mature-age working professionals without an undergraduate degree can still apply and have their relevant qualifications or substantial professional experience assessed. Domestic students can study on campus or by distance. Graduates use it to formalise finance skills and progress toward further postgraduate study or finance roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Business
description: The Graduate Certificate in Business at the University of Wollongong is for those who want to advance their career, formalise their industry experience or move into a business-focused role within their field. The course covers key business areas including accounting, financial management, organisational behaviour and marketing management. It caters for professional and lifestyle commitments by offering study on campus at Wollongong or Sydney CBD, or online through distance or fully online delivery modes. Graduates use it to build business knowledge and progress toward management roles or further master's study.

name: Graduate Certificate in Business Administration (Executive)
description: The Graduate Certificate in Business Administration at the University of Wollongong is designed for professionals ready to sharpen their strategic capabilities and lead with purpose in complex business environments. Fully embedded within the MBA, the course focuses on diagnosing real organisational challenges through the disciplines that drive business performance, developing the analytical rigour and ethical framework needed to make decisions that matter. Learning is grounded in practical real-world examples, industry input and collaborative assessment. Graduates advance into management and leadership roles or continue into the MBA.

name: Graduate Certificate in Computing
description: The Graduate Certificate in Computing at the University of Wollongong provides a postgraduate introduction to computing for students without prior knowledge of IT and computing. As occupations in data science, cyber security, IT management, health informatics and software engineering grow in demand, the course allows graduates and professionals from a non-IT background to add a recognised computing qualification to their skill set. It includes a selection of core computing and information technology subjects related to programming and systems. Graduates progress into IT roles or into further postgraduate computing study.

name: Graduate Certificate in Education
description: The Graduate Certificate in Education at the University of Wollongong is designed for educators seeking a short, flexible degree that can be tailored to their needs and interests. It suits graduates and professionals looking to diversify or change career direction into fields such as staff training and development or policy and planning. The course has one core subject and three electives chosen from the Master of Education specialisations, including educational leadership, digital technologies for learning, and TESOL, and can articulate into the Master of Education. Graduates apply it across teaching, training and education support roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Engineering
description: The Graduate Certificate in Engineering at the University of Wollongong is designed to train and enhance professional practice, advance technical and specialist skills, and provide the opportunity to apply theory through applied projects. It provides a foundation for the more intensive theoretical and practical work of the graduate diploma and master's degrees. The course consists of four subjects: engineering research methods plus three technical subjects in a specialisation such as civil, mining and environmental; electrical, computer and telecommunications; or mechanical, materials and mechatronic engineering. Graduates advance their engineering careers or continue to further study.

name: Graduate Certificate in Financial Technology
description: The Graduate Certificate in Financial Technology at the University of Wollongong is built on the intersection of finance and information technology, a field growing exponentially and transforming the future of business. The course is aimed at students seeking to upgrade existing finance skills or aspiring to a career in the growing FinTech field. Students learn to consider the impact of technology on banking and global payment systems, the insurance industry and trading in financial markets, and how blockchain technology facilitates more transparent transactions. Graduates work in FinTech, banking, payments and financial services roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Fisheries Policy
description: The Graduate Certificate in Fisheries Policy at the University of Wollongong is tailored for individuals seeking to specialise in fisheries policy, management or representation within the fisheries sector, including fisheries policy officers, junior managers and government enforcement officers, as well as industry and non-government organisation representatives. The course provides a broad understanding of the international legal and policy framework within which fisheries resources are managed, conserved and developed, and examines the principles of fisheries management. Graduates work in fisheries and marine resource management, policy and compliance roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Indigenous Trauma and Recovery Practice
description: The Graduate Certificate in Indigenous Trauma and Recovery Practice at the University of Wollongong responds to issues of particular relevance in Australian Indigenous communities. It is a multidisciplinary program in which students apply critical thinking, collaborative practice and judgement when working with individuals who have experienced trauma. The course focuses on applying Indigenous social and emotional wellbeing principles, practices and healing frameworks, using both Aboriginal and Western concepts of trauma and considering the historical and cumulative impact of trauma. Graduates work in health, community, social and emotional wellbeing, and healing roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in International Relations
description: The Graduate Certificate in International Relations at the University of Wollongong offers a focused introduction to international relations for graduates from any discipline. Students build in-demand skills in critical thinking, policy analysis and professional communication that transfer across industries, deepening their understanding of complex global systems and how to respond to real-world international issues. The course prepares students to contribute across government, business and the not-for-profit sector, and can articulate into further international relations study.

name: Graduate Certificate in Law of the Sea
description: The Graduate Certificate in Law of the Sea at the University of Wollongong covers the international law governing the rights and duties of stakeholders in maritime environments, including the rights and obligations of coastal states, navigational rights and responsibilities, conservation and use of marine resources, and maritime security. It is designed to meet the early and mid-career education requirements of legally qualified professionals working in a maritime policy or operational context. Graduates work in maritime law, ocean governance, policy and enforcement roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Maritime Studies
description: The Graduate Certificate in Maritime Studies at the University of Wollongong deals with policy, law and security issues related to the world's oceans, including maritime trade routes, the ocean as a natural habitat, and its role as a source of both international tension and cooperation. Students gain an understanding of maritime enforcement, maritime security threats and solutions, marine environmental law, regulation of shipping and marine resources management, and learn to analyse the legal, political and operational factors that shape the law of the sea and maritime policy. Graduates work in maritime policy, security and governance roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting
description: The Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting at the University of Wollongong is an introductory course providing a general understanding of accounting and related areas in business, including accounting, finance, economics and business law. Successful completion provides a pathway to the Master of Professional Accounting or Master of Professional Accounting Advanced with credit for four subjects, and progression to other master's degrees including the MBA may also be possible. Graduates use it to enter the accounting profession or to build toward a professional accounting qualification.

name: Graduate Certificate in Public Health
description: The Graduate Certificate in Public Health at the University of Wollongong is a flexible program providing a broad introduction to public health, enabling graduates to work with communities to contribute to effective and sustainable public health practices nationally and internationally. Students gain insight into the challenges of improving the health of vulnerable communities and the range of career opportunities in public health, studying two core public health subjects plus two electives. The course can articulate into the Master of Public Health. Graduates work in health promotion, policy and program roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Science and Management
Graduate Certificate in TESOL
description: The Graduate Certificate in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages at the University of Wollongong is a specialist qualification for people who want to teach English to speakers of other languages in Australia or overseas, and for current primary or high school teachers who want additional ESL qualifications. The course offers sound theoretical and empirical foundations and extensive practical skills, including exploring teaching methods and common grammar issues and undertaking a supervised professional experience placement in an ESL classroom. Graduates teach English across language schools, secondary and vocational settings, and overseas.

name: Graduate Diploma in Business Administration (Executive)
description: The Graduate Diploma in Business Administration at the University of Wollongong is designed to build responsible, strategic leaders who can make confident decisions and drive meaningful change in complex global business environments. The course grounds students in the fundamentals that matter, from economics and finance to marketing, artificial intelligence, supply chain, and people and culture. Through case studies drawn from contemporary organisations and input from industry experts, students develop the strategic thinking and ethical framework required to lead organisations that are commercially successful and socially responsible. Graduates advance into management roles or continue into the MBA.

name: Graduate Diploma in Occupational Health and Safety
description: The Graduate Diploma in Occupational Health and Safety at the University of Wollongong is for students holding an undergraduate degree or graduate certificate in occupational health and safety or occupational hygiene. Developed with industry to address the complex nature of workplace health and safety, the course covers advanced WHS risk management, applied human factors and ergonomics, industrial epidemiology and toxicology, occupational health and safety theories and systems, work health and safety law, and workplace hazards and hygiene. Graduates work as WHS advisers, managers and consultants across industry and government.

name: Graduate Diploma in TESOL
description: The Graduate Diploma in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages at the University of Wollongong is designed for TAFE or vocational education teachers whose employers require an in-depth qualification, and for experienced educators seeking a higher specialist qualification in ESL teaching. The course offers sound theoretical and empirical foundations and extensive practical skills, providing the skills to teach English with a focus on international and local contexts and catering for diversity in the classroom. Graduates teach English across vocational, secondary and adult education settings in Australia and overseas.

name: Master of Applied Finance
description: The Master of Applied Finance at the University of Wollongong builds advanced understanding of applied finance for careers in financial statement analysis, managerial finance, corporate governance and related areas. The course values prior learning and professional experience, and develops the analytical and decision-making skills finance professionals need across corporate finance, investment and risk. Graduates work in banking, corporate finance, investment and financial analysis roles.

name: Master of Business
description: The Master of Business at the University of Wollongong allows students to choose subjects that are of most interest to them and their career, building fundamental business knowledge and skills through core subjects and completing a research capstone. It can be combined with another business master's degree through the double master's program, earning two master's degrees in two years and building expertise in two in-demand areas. Graduates gain knowledge across a broad range of business areas and move into a variety of business careers.

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
UOW's MBA runs through the Faculty of Business and Law and is AACSB-accredited. It targets working professionals: most units are offered in intensive or evening/weekend formats so people can study alongside full-time jobs, and the cohort skews toward students with several years' work experience rather than fresh graduates.

Core coverage is standard MBA territory (strategy, finance, marketing, leadership), but the elective structure lets students build a concentration: options have included international business and innovation/technology management, reflecting the region's manufacturing and steel industry links. A consulting-style capstone project replaces a traditional thesis for most students, usually done with a real host organisation.
curriculum:
Core: Managerial Economics, Financial Management, Strategic Management, Marketing Management, Organisational Leadership, Business Analytics for Decision Making
Electives: choose 4, options include International Business, Innovation Management, Human Resource Strategy, Entrepreneurship
Capstone: applied strategy/consulting project with a partner organisation, final session
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree plus 2 years relevant work experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Master of Business Administration Advanced
description: The Master of Business Administration (MBA) Advanced at the University of Wollongong is designed to shape responsible, strategic leaders who can navigate complexity, drive innovation and make confident data-informed decisions in rapidly evolving organisations. The advanced course allows students to specialise in an area of interest by completing additional subjects, and is grounded in the Principles of Responsible Management Education so that graduates lead ethically and sustainably. Students study economics, accounting, marketing, finance, people and culture, artificial intelligence, project management and supply chain management. Graduates progress into senior management and leadership roles.

name: Master of Business Analytics
description: The University of Wollongong Master of Business Analytics builds skills in descriptive, predictive and prescriptive analytics for working with large volumes of business data. Foundation subjects are completed in the first two sessions, followed by Advanced Business Analytics and a Business Analytics Research Capstone in the final sessions, with two 900-level electives chosen from across the Faculty of Business and Law. On completion, students receive the SAS Joint Certificate and the Advanced SAS Joint Certificate. The course is offered on campus and by distance. Overseas qualifications must be assessed as equivalent to an Australian bachelor degree, and international students must show English proficiency. Indicative international tuition is around A$37,100 per year. Graduates apply analytics and the associated tools and technologies to support business decision-making.

name: Master of Clinical Exercise Physiology
description: The Master of Clinical Exercise Physiology at the University of Wollongong is for graduates of exercise science who want to upgrade their qualifications and work with individuals with chronic diseases and disabilities. On completion, students have the technical expertise to restore good health and physical capability to people after illness or injury, and develop their skillset in data gathering and analysis as it applies to human movement, physiological systems integration and the processes underpinning unhealthy individuals. Graduates work as accredited exercise physiologists in clinical, hospital and community settings.

name: Master of Computer Science
description:
UOW's Master of Computer Science runs out of the School of Computing and Information Technology, based across the main Wollongong campus and the SMART Infrastructure Facility building on the eastern side of campus. It's built for people switching into computing from another background as much as CS graduates topping up their qualification: there's a foundation stream covering programming and data structures for anyone without a CS undergrad, then the degree proper moves into data management systems, network design, and software architecture. Wollongong's CS group has a long-standing research strength in wireless networking, and that shows up in elective options around network and system security.

Class sizes are smaller than at the Group of Eight campuses in Sydney, and a fair chunk of the cohort is international, drawn partly by post-study work rights and partly by regional-campus fee settings that undercut the big Sydney universities. The degree finishes with an individual capstone project, supervised one-on-one, which functions as a portfolio piece students bring to interviews with Illawarra-region and Sydney tech employers.
curriculum:
Foundation session (waived with a relevant CS background): Programming and Data Structures, Data Management Systems
Core: Software Construction and Design, Advanced Database Systems, Strategic Network Design, Security, Ethics and Professionalism
Electives: choose from cloud computing, machine learning, mobile application development, distributed systems
Capstone: individual major project, supervised by CSIT faculty, final session
Optional: internship/WIL subject in place of one elective for eligible students
Duration: 24 months full-time or 48 months part-time
admission_requirements: A recognised bachelor's degree in any field with a weighted average mark (WAM) of 60% or above; applicants with other qualifications plus relevant professional experience may also be considered.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, minimum 6.0 in each band.

name: Master of Computing
description: The Master of Computing at the University of Wollongong develops the next generation of computing professionals with broad knowledge and a deep understanding of the technical, managerial and ethical aspects of computing practice. The data analytics specialisation focuses on applying current technologies to deliver data-driven insights and intelligence. The degree suits graduates with a computing background who wish to upskill and graduates without a computing background who wish to enter the field, and incorporates academic learning with practical application. Graduates work as computing and data professionals across industry.

name: Master of Data Science
description:
Housed in the School of Computing and Information Technology, this is a conversion-friendly degree: people with a quantitative but non-CS background (maths, engineering, science, even some commerce graduates) can enter through the foundation stream. Coursework runs through statistics, machine learning, big data systems, and data visualisation, with more weight put on applied projects using real or realistic datasets than on pure theory.

UOW markets this partly on Wollongong's growing data-analytics employer base and partly on affordability relative to Sydney's data science masters programs, a genuine consideration for the international cohort making up a large share of enrolments.
curriculum:
Foundation session (background-dependent): Programming for Data Science, Statistics for Data Science
Core: Machine Learning, Big Data Management, Data Visualisation, Data Mining
Electives: deep learning, natural language processing, business analytics (varies by session offering)
Capstone: applied data science project, industry or research-based, final session
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Master of Earth and Environmental Sciences
description: The Master of Earth and Environmental Sciences at the University of Wollongong is for students who wish to extend their knowledge and diversify their skills across sub-disciplines of the earth and environmental sciences, including environmental science, earth science, life sciences and conservation. The degree emphasises the interconnectedness of these sub-disciplines through common core subjects, and is designed through the lens of global perspectives in science, with students using drones, artificial intelligence and coding. Graduates work in environmental science, conservation, consulting and research roles.

name: Master of Education
description: The Master of Education at the University of Wollongong is a higher degree for teachers and educators wishing to pursue advanced studies in their area of interest. Many subjects require the application of research and theoretical insights to actual practice, and it is desirable that students have some workplace or teaching experience. Specialisations include digital technologies for learning, educational leadership, interdisciplinary studies and TESOL. Graduates advance into leadership, curriculum, policy and specialist roles across the education sector.

name: Master of Education Extension
description: The Master of Education Extension at the University of Wollongong is a higher degree for professional educators and for those interested in a career in teaching English to speakers of other languages or in educational leadership. The two-year program extends the learning outcomes of the Master of Education and offers candidates the opportunity to specialise in either TESOL or educational leadership, introducing contemporary trends and issues in research, theory and practice, with flexible online or classroom study. Graduates advance into specialist, leadership and TESOL teaching roles.

name: Master of Engineering
description: The Master of Engineering at the University of Wollongong delivers the expert skills and applied competencies required for the professional engineer. Designed to train and enhance professional practice and advance technical and specialist skills, the degree provides the opportunity to put theory into practice through applied projects and research, while building communication, strategic and project management skills.
