Because the program deliberately straddles two related but distinct industries, graduates leave with genuinely dual expertise rather than a construction qualification with a token property module or vice versa. It suits people who want career flexibility across both construction delivery and property investment and development, rather than committing to a narrower single-discipline postgraduate qualification.

name: Master of Curating and Cultural Leadership
description: UNSW's Master of Curating and Cultural Leadership builds connections between curating, audience engagement, policy, management, critical writing, promotion and production, treating contemporary curating as a dynamic profession that sets cultural agendas rather than a purely administrative gallery function. Built on more than 20 years of UNSW Art & Design postgraduate experience in this field, the program is delivered in close collaboration with UNSW Galleries and a broad range of Australian and international industry partners, giving students genuine professional networks alongside academic training. Fully online study is available, though only for domestic students not on an international student visa. It suits both people with existing backgrounds in museums, galleries, arts organisations or art practice, and career-changers entering curating or cultural leadership from other professional backgrounds, preparing graduates as independent professionals able to lead across curating, exhibition, arts policy and management contexts.

name: Master of Cyber Security (Research)
description: UNSW's Master of Cyber Security (Research) lets students contribute new knowledge within cyber security through a genuine research project, developing critical research skills and methodologies alongside original scientific insight rather than following a purely taught curriculum. The program builds the experience and expert knowledge needed to confidently approach a research career in cyber security, distinguishing it from taught cyber security master's degrees focused on applied professional skills. It suits computer science, engineering or related graduates with a genuine cyber security research question who want a formal research credential, often as a pathway toward a PhD or a specialised research role in security research institutions, government cyber agencies, or industry security research and development teams, rather than students seeking a taught professional cyber security qualification.

name: Master of Data Science and Decisions
description: UNSW's Master of Data Science and Decisions trains current and future data scientists and analysts to meet strong workforce demand, building broad, advanced knowledge across mathematics and statistics, computer science, and economics before students specialise more deeply in one of four available areas. Two pathways accommodate different statistics backgrounds: Option 1 covers foundational probability and statistical theory for students with limited prior exposure, while Option 2 assumes existing knowledge of probability, hypothesis testing and estimation methods, letting students skip straight to more advanced coursework. Research and communication skills are developed through genuine project work rather than only classroom instruction, reflecting how data science actually gets applied in industry settings. It suits graduates from any quantitative background who want genuinely interdisciplinary data science training, with the flexible statistics pathway accommodating both newcomers to formal statistical theory and those who've already studied it.

name: Master of Design

name: Master of Development Studies

Unlike the broader Master of Applied Economics, this program leans more theoretically rigorous, suiting students who want deep economic theory training rather than a more practically oriented economics qualification. It suits economics or related quantitative graduates who want genuinely advanced economic theory and econometric technique, positioning graduates for roles in economic research, policy analysis, financial institutions or further doctoral study in economics. The specialist framing distinguishes it from generalist business or commerce postgraduate degrees that touch on economics as one component among several.

name: Master of Environmental Management
description: UNSW's Master of Environmental Management trains reflexive leaders, change-agents and advocates who understand not just the ecological dimensions of environmental issues but their social, cultural and structural drivers and impacts at local and global scales. The transdisciplinary program bridges social sciences, humanities, natural sciences, creative arts and participatory community approaches, building both conceptual tools and practical, experiential skills for ethical, restorative sustainability leadership in professional and change-making contexts. Its flexible format, taught primarily face-to-face or blended with distance options outside field-based courses, suits both environmental specialists and newcomers from unrelated disciplines. It suits people who want to lead environmental change in organisations or communities, taking seriously the social and political dimensions of environmental problems rather than treating them as purely technical or scientific issues.

name: Master of Finance
description: UNSW's Master of Finance is a specialist degree developed in close consultation with the finance sector, built to expose students to current research and advanced finance topics well beyond an undergraduate finance major. Applied learning activities both in and outside the classroom keep the theory grounded in practice, and the program's length flexes based on background: graduates with an undergraduate finance major can complete it in one year, while others need two years full-time, with part-time study also available at a proportionally longer duration. It suits finance graduates who want deeper technical specialisation as well as graduates from adjacent quantitative or business disciplines who've decided finance is their next career step, provided they meet UNSW's credit-average entry bar. The close industry consultation behind the program's design means the curriculum tends to track current finance sector thinking rather than staying purely academic.

name: Master of Financial Analysis
description: UNSW's Master of Financial Analysis is a specialist degree that builds on an existing accounting or finance background, drawing on both the School of Accounting and the School of Banking and Finance to create a genuinely targeted financial analysis qualification rather than a general business master's. Students develop high-level skills in strategy, risk analysis and management, valuation and project development, positioning them for careers in investment analysis, funds management, CFO-track roles or broader business analysis work. The program's flexible course structure lets students tailor their studies to specific career aspirations within financial analysis, drawing on a wide range of offerings across both contributing schools. Entry requires a credit average and a major in accounting or finance within a recognised bachelor's degree, meaning this is a genuine next step for accounting and finance graduates rather than an entry point for career-changers without that background.

The program was designed to supply the financial sector with highly trained quantitative finance specialists, while also preparing students for further research in mathematical finance if they choose to continue academically. It suits mathematics, statistics or related quantitative graduates who want to specialise specifically in quantitative finance rather than a general finance master's degree, positioning graduates for roles as quantitative analysts, risk modellers or derivatives specialists in banking and financial services. The program's genuine mathematical depth distinguishes it from business-school finance degrees that treat quantitative technique as a secondary skill.

name: Master of Global Health
description: UNSW's Master of Global Health takes an interdisciplinary approach to complex population health issues across local and global settings, grounded in public health but extending into comparative analysis of global health systems, health policy, and the politics and philosophy underpinning global health debates. The program tackles genuinely difficult questions around globalisation and health, decolonisation, health and human rights, environmental change and urban population growth, taught by a multidisciplinary team of research-active academics working across the Asia-Pacific and sub-Saharan Africa. Graduates typically move into roles with bilateral and multilateral aid organisations, UN agencies, civil society and NGOs, private foundations, health departments and academia. It suits students who want to work on population health challenges that cross national borders and jurisdictions, rather than domestic public health practice alone, and who are prepared to engage with the political and philosophical dimensions of global health as much as the epidemiological ones.

name: Master of Health Leadership and Management
description: UNSW's Master of Health Leadership and Management is designed for current and aspiring health system leaders, both in Australia and internationally, building the theoretical understanding and practical skills needed for strategic planning, policy development, change management, quality enhancement and decision-making in healthcare specifically. The program broadens students' understanding of current and emerging influences on the health sector, including consumer-centred care models, aiming to produce work-ready leaders who can drive meaningful change in the health systems they work within. Two main entry pathways require a three-year undergraduate degree in any field plus two years of full-time professional or volunteer experience in a relevant health-adjacent role, with a third exceptional pathway for other applicants. It suits health professionals ready for a full postgraduate leadership qualification, building on the shorter Graduate Certificate and Graduate Diploma versions of the same program for those who've already completed one of those first.

name: Master of Health Professions Education (Research)
description: UNSW's Master of Health Professions Education (Research) is designed for teachers and educational administrators working within the health professions who want to build genuine research skills, requiring an original investigation under supervision for a minimum of three academic sessions full-time or four sessions part-time or external, culminating in a thesis. Candidates can enrol as internal students at a campus or teaching hospital, or as external students spending a minimum of 14 weeks in the School during the program, with external research work requiring a co-supervisor at the host institution where necessary. Because the degree is entirely research-driven, the specific health education research question depends on the individual candidate's interests and available supervision. It suits health professions educators with a genuine research question about how health professionals are taught and trained, who want a formal research credential rather than a taught postgraduate education qualification.

In exceptional cases an applicant who submits evidence of such other academic and professional qualifications as may be approved by the Committee may be permitted to enrol for the degree. name: Master of Health Sciences (Research)
description: UNSW's Master of Health Sciences (Research) lets postgraduate students undertake supervised research aligned with the School of Health Sciences' professional programs, spanning dietetics, pharmacy, physiotherapy and exercise physiology. Because the degree is entirely research-driven, the specific focus and content depend on the individual student's chosen discipline and research question within these four areas, working under a dedicated supervisor rather than following a fixed taught curriculum. It suits health science graduates from one of these four disciplines who have a genuine research question they want to pursue, often as a pathway toward further research study or a research-focused role in clinical practice, health policy or academia. The degree gives graduates a formal research credential that complements their existing clinical training, rather than replacing it with purely theoretical coursework.

Graduates typically move into roles at health ministries and departments, government organisations, NGOs, and public and private healthcare services. It suits public health professionals who want deep specialisation in infectious disease response specifically, rather than general public health practice, particularly relevant given how central infectious disease preparedness has become to health system planning globally.

The program provides broad-based IT education with the option to specialise in up to two areas, letting graduates work across a genuinely wide range of IT industry positions rather than one narrow technical niche. It suits career-changers moving into IT from an unrelated background, IT professionals wanting broader technical grounding, and computing graduates wanting deeper specialisation, all within the same flexible program structure that adapts to each student's starting point and goals.

Entry requires a recognised undergraduate degree with a credit average, with credit available for applicants who've completed relevant prior bachelor's-level or higher study. Students examine current concerns including regional conflicts, great power rivalry, economic uncertainty, environmental threats, humanitarian crises and terrorism, extending existing knowledge with advanced research and analytical thinking skills. It suits graduates and professionals aiming for careers in diplomacy, international organisations, government foreign policy roles, think tanks or international NGOs, as well as those who want deeper theoretical grounding in world politics to complement an existing career touching international affairs.

name: Master of Journalism and Communication
description: UNSW's Master of Journalism and Communication builds a professionally relevant and academically rigorous portfolio of media practice skills spanning print, radio, television, online media, media relations and corporate communication, grounded in interdisciplinary understanding of the social, economic and political role of media locally and internationally. Community engagement is built into both coursework and assessment, with some tasks involving genuine cooperative partnerships with NGOs and industry organisations. It suits graduates and working professionals who want comprehensive journalism and communication training with real emphasis on the research-practice connection, positioning them for careers across journalism, corporate communication and media production.

The program culminates in a final-year capstone studio sequence where students undertake an independent, research-based design project. Course availability varies year to year depending on student interest and teacher availability, so not every course runs annually. It suits practising lawyers wanting to specialise further in a particular area of law, as well as law graduates from other jurisdictions wanting genuine exposure to Australian and comparative legal perspectives.

name: Master of Medicine - research
description: UNSW's Master of Medicine (Research) is the Faculty of Medicine's main postgraduate research degree, requiring candidates to submit a thesis based on original investigation under the direction of a UNSW-appointed supervisor. Candidates can enrol full-time, part-time, or as external students working at an affiliated teaching hospital or research facility, with annual progress reviews by the faculty's Higher Degree Committee and the possibility of a co-supervisor at an external institution where research is based outside UNSW itself. Because the degree is entirely research-driven, the specific medical field and research question depend on the individual candidate's interests and available supervision, spanning the full breadth of medical research the Faculty of Medicine supports. It suits medical or science graduates with a genuine research question who want a formal research credential, often as a pathway toward a PhD or a specialised medical research career, rather than students seeking a taught postgraduate medical qualification.

It suits engineering graduates who want a taste of independent research and thesis writing without committing to a full PhD, either as a standalone research credential or as a stepping stone toward doctoral study. It particularly suits people with an undergraduate degree who want to return from the workforce and develop research skills, with successful completion potentially qualifying graduates for doctoral-level research admission. It works well for career-changers moving into research-oriented roles as well as those testing whether doctoral study suits them before committing to a full PhD.

The program suits science, engineering or environmental graduates who want to specialise specifically in climate science rather than treating it as one topic within a broader environmental science degree, building the quantitative and analytical skills climate research and climate risk assessment genuinely require. It positions graduates for roles across climate research institutions, government environmental agencies, and industries increasingly needing in-house climate expertise to manage physical climate risk. Applicants should confirm current program structure and entry requirements directly with UNSW given ongoing curriculum development in this fast-evolving field.
curriculum: Research Course: HDAT9900 Health Data Science: Dissertation (6 Units of Credit), HDAT9901 Health Data Science: Dissertation (12 Units of Credit), HDAT9902 Health Data Science: Dissertation (18 Units of Credit), HDAT9910 Health Data Science: Capstone.

name: Master of Science in Vision Science (Research)
Master of Simulation and Immersive Technologies
description: UNSW's Master of Simulation and Immersive Technologies takes a human-centric, design-led approach to virtual, augmented and mixed reality, combining industry and academic perspectives with practical assignments and real industry demonstrations across media and creative arts, health, defence, business, education and manufacturing sectors. The program develops global leaders with a genuinely immersive design mindset, capable of applying simulation and immersive practices to real-world problems rather than treating VR and AR as purely technical novelties, culminating in a capstone studio applying learning to actual industry domains. Flexible delivery, full-time or part-time, fully online or with campus access for Sydney-based students, suits working professionals bringing existing domain expertise from any sector, since core courses offer only a limited technical software introduction and students are encouraged to build deeper technical skills through electives. It suits professionals with existing industry expertise who want a broadening, human-centred foundation in simulation and immersive technology relevant to their field.

name: Master of Statistics - by coursework
description: UNSW's Master of Statistics is the longest-running program of its kind in Australia, covering a wide range of statistical theory and practice to provide advanced training for practising or aspiring statisticians. Beyond preparing graduates for professional statistical careers, the program also provides genuine preparation for further statistics research at the PhD level for students who want to continue academically. Its long track record means the program has a well-established reputation and alumni network within Australian statistical practice, spanning industries from government statistics agencies to pharmaceutical research and financial services. It suits mathematics or statistics graduates who want deep, comprehensive statistical training, whether aiming for a career as a practising statistician or preparing for doctoral-level statistical research.

name: Master of Surgery
description: UNSW's Master of Surgery (Research) requires candidates to make an original contribution to knowledge in a field related to surgery, generally requiring at least three years of prior surgical training and a minimum five-year gap since completing an undergraduate medical degree before submitting the thesis. Candidates can enrol full-time, part-time or externally at an affiliated teaching hospital or research facility, with annual progress reviews by the faculty's Higher Degree Committee. Because the degree is entirely research-driven, the specific surgical research question depends on the individual candidate's clinical experience and research interests. It suits experienced surgical trainees or practising surgeons with a genuine research question in their surgical specialty who want a formal research credential, often as a pathway toward an academic surgical career or a leadership role in surgical practice improvement.
curriculum: Students must complete 96 UOC when taken as a standalone program.

name: Master of Taxation
description: UNSW's Master of Taxation is a specialist program for taxation professionals dealing with complex tax issues in business decisions and transactions, taught by leading tax academics with exposure to complex aspects of the discipline and critical understanding of the Australian taxation system. Three compulsory core courses and a compulsory capstone in tax policy form the backbone of the degree, with four elective courses letting students tailor the program toward personal tax and financial planning, indirect taxes, corporate and commercial tax, or international tax depending on career interests. Assessment emphasises sustained analytical writing on current problem areas, encouraging genuine contributions to professional debate on key tax issues rather than only reproducing existing knowledge. All courses are offered in online distance learning or hybrid mode, and the program can be studied full-time or part-time, suiting working tax professionals who need flexible delivery around existing employment.

name: Master of Teaching (Secondary)
description: UNSW's Master of Teaching (Secondary) is an accelerated, two-year equivalent postgraduate secondary teaching qualification recognised across NSW, other Australian states and widely overseas, completable full-time in four terms (1.3 years) or part-time in 2.3 years. After completing the first full-time-equivalent year, which follows a fixed, intensive structure of four courses per term, graduates become eligible to apply for jobs in NSW schools while the second year offers greater flexibility, including a part-time option that still allows teaching eligibility after the second year. It suits graduates from any discipline who've decided on secondary teaching as a career and want the fastest accredited route into the classroom, rather than an undergraduate teaching degree, with the compressed first-year structure demanding genuine full-time commitment from students who choose that pathway.

name: Master of Translation
description: UNSW's Master of Translation is endorsed by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters, preparing students for the Certified Translator certification exam and, with additional coursework, the specialist Certified Advanced Translator exam. Offered in a 48-credit-point, one-year plan or a 72-credit-point, 1.7-year plan depending on prior qualifications, the program covers translation specialisations spanning multimedia, business, legal, medical, scientific, technical, subtitling and captioning, translation technology and community translation. Real professional practice experience complements academic content, taught by leading translation and linguistics researchers and practitioners. Language combinations, offered subject to demand, span Chinese (Mandarin and Cantonese), French, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Serbian, Spanish and Turkish, with fully online study available only to domestic students not on an international student visa.

name: Master of Translation and Interpreting
description: UNSW's Master of Translation and Interpreting is a 96-credit-point program endorsed by NAATI, preparing students for certification as Certified Provisional Interpreter, Certified Interpreter and Certified Translator, with additional coursework enabling specialist certification as Certified Advanced Translator or Certified Specialist Interpreter in health, legal or conference settings. The program combines interpreting specialisations in legal, medical, business, community and conference settings with translation specialisations spanning multimedia, business, legal, medical, scientific, technical, subtitling and translation technology, giving graduates genuinely dual expertise rather than one discipline alone. Language combinations, offered subject to demand, span Chinese (Mandarin and Cantonese), French, Greek, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Serbian, Spanish and Turkish, with fully online study available only to domestic students not on an international student visa. It suits bilingual professionals who want both interpreting and translation qualifications in one combined program rather than choosing between the two.

name: Master of Urban Development and Design
Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Management
description: The Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Management (SIT60322) at Victoria University TAFE qualifies graduates for senior management positions in the hospitality industry. Students learn and apply skills in VU's fully equipped hospitality training centre under industry experts, developing advanced skills in hospitality operations and leadership including human resource management, financial management, marketing strategies and business planning. Students also learn to manage hotel front office operations, including creating reservations, managing accounts and check-out. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Associate Degree in Hospitality and Hotel Management
description: The Associate Degree in Hospitality and Hotel Management at Victoria University develops management and leadership capabilities to improve prospects of securing a senior position in the industry. Students build business management potential, gain hands-on experience in VU's hospitality training centre, and develop an understanding of industry trends and issues, learning from teachers directly involved in the industry. Skills developed include hotel operations management, food, wine and catering operations, accounting principles for management, marketing and business communications, contracts, risk and business law, resort management, and rooms division management. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Accounting
description: The Bachelor of Accounting at Victoria University produces career-ready graduates with technical and professional skills and a strong knowledge of global trends in accounting. Based at VU's City Tower in the Melbourne CBD, students develop the skills to qualify for accreditation with CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand. The degree develops the ability to execute case studies and business plans, complete evidence-based projects with real clients, and adapt cross-disciplinary knowledge in accounting, data analytics and finance, along with professional skills in critical thinking, problem solving, teamwork and communication.

name: Bachelor of Applied Music
description: The Bachelor of Applied Music at Victoria University blends creativity with real-world application, preparing students for careers in music teaching, production, performance, mixed-media arts and community projects, and setting them up for further study in music education, music therapy, community development, youth work and social work. The course focuses on four interconnected areas: music teaching, creative digital music production including video, streaming and AI music, music for life and music for change covering wellbeing and social change, and performance skills. It explores the power of music to support emotional, cultural and social wellbeing and to engage with Indigenous and social-justice issues. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Architectural Design
description: The Bachelor of Architectural Design at Victoria University focuses on sustainable building design that responds to community needs, incorporating circular-economy ideas such as reusing, repurposing, refurbishing, recycling and repairing to reduce waste. Students apply these methods to real projects, visiting sites, taking measurements and collaborating with local communities, and participate in design studio classes focused on real-world challenges in architecture and construction. Graduates have the skills to work as building designers in government and private planning and construction sectors, and can continue into a Master of Architecture to become a registered architect. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description: The Bachelor of Arts at Victoria University offers broad flexibility, letting students choose their area of focus based on their interests and career goals. After a first-year introduction to the humanities, students study one or two majors from communication studies, digital media, history, literary studies, psychology, sociology, visual art and writing, and can choose from 14 minors including Aboriginal Yulendj (Knowledge) and Community. The degree develops sought-after employability skills such as communication, problem solving, teamwork and analytical thinking. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Biomedical and Exercise Science
description: The Bachelor of Biomedical and Exercise Science at Victoria University is a dual-disciplinary degree that integrates biomedical science and exercise science in the contexts of physical activity, sport and health research. Students study the fundamentals of anatomy and physiology, pathophysiology, biochemistry, biomechanics, kinesiology and psychology, and how the structure and function of the body are influenced by exercise and impacted by disease. They apply theoretical knowledge in practical and clinical scenarios and develop research skills through active participation in research teams, using VU's medical research facilities at Sunshine Hospital. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Biomedical Science
description: The Bachelor of Biomedical Science at Victoria University develops a strong foundation in the medical sciences and advanced laboratory skills, preparing graduates for careers in biomedical research or entry into postgraduate health courses. Combining hands-on experimentation with interactive online learning, students gain in-depth knowledge of how the human body works, covering physiology, anatomy and cell biology and the causes, diagnosis and treatment of disease at molecular, cellular and system levels. Study areas include anatomy and physiology, nutrition, biochemistry, cell biology, medical microbiology, immunology, molecular biology, human genetics and pharmacology. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Biomedicine
description: The Bachelor of Biomedicine at Victoria University provides a strong foundation for a career in medicine or allied health and prepares students for entry into postgraduate medicine and courses such as physiotherapy, pharmacy and dietetics, including essential physiology, anatomy and biochemistry prerequisites. The course has a particular focus on the role of exercise and nutrition in medicine, and students design and analyse research methods and undertake a research project that can be a platform for a research degree. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Building Surveying
description: The Bachelor of Building Surveying at Victoria University is the only degree of its kind in Victoria and prepares students for roles improving the safety and quality of the built environment. Study is delivered online and in real time without traditional classrooms or labs. Graduates are ready to work as registered building surveyors accredited by the Victorian Building Authority and the Australian Institute of Building Surveyors, and with three years of relevant experience can work on buildings of any size and height. Students specialise in building and construction legislation and auditing, inspection procedures, building codes and regulations, professional practice standards, building safety and fire safety, and sustainable construction techniques.

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
VU's general business degree lets students pick a major (accounting, marketing, human resource management, management or international business among them) after a common first-year foundation, and like the rest of VU's undergraduate offering it's delivered block-mode, one unit over four weeks rather than a full timetable of subjects running in parallel.

The course is aimed squarely at Melbourne's west: a large share of VU's business students are first-in-family university attendees or came through pathway diplomas, and the degree includes built-in study support and a Professional Year option that matters to the substantial number of international students in the cohort chasing skilled migration points after graduation. There's also a work-integrated learning unit in most majors, connecting students with local employers rather than leaving placement entirely up to students to arrange.

It's not a prestige-brand business degree in the way a Melbourne or Monash commerce degree might be, and VU doesn't pretend otherwise: its pitch is accessibility and a direct line into local industry rather than an elite cohort experience.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting for Business, Economic Principles, Marketing Fundamentals, Business Communication
Year 2: Business Law, Quantitative Methods, Major units begin (Accounting, Marketing, HRM, Management, or International Business), Work-Integrated Learning unit
Year 3: Advanced major units, Strategic Management, Business Capstone Project
admission_requirements: ATAR 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Community Development
description: The Bachelor of Community Development at Victoria University gives students the skills and knowledge for roles in local community development, with units focused on practical skills to become an effective community worker and an advocate for change. Students benefit from extensive placements in community development organisations, with opportunities to travel overseas, and from university partnerships that enable study abroad and help build capacity to work in diverse communities. This combination of knowledge and practical experience prepares graduates for a rewarding and ethical career. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Construction Management (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Construction Management (Honours) at Victoria University prepares graduates to take a leading role in large-scale building and civil-engineering projects, managing residential, commercial and industrial construction from design through development, construction and operation. Students gain skills in planning and managing the construction process, assessing documents for compliance with codes and standards, assessing plans for constructability, communicating with architects and engineers, formulating project cashflows and budgets, preparing tender documents and contracts, and supervising sites and personnel. Students can add a minor in building compliance or quantity surveying. The degree is closely connected to industry and offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Criminal Justice
description: The Bachelor of Criminal Justice at Victoria University equips students with the knowledge, skills and hands-on experience to make an impact on community safety and social justice. Students examine how crime, law and inequality intersect, including the role of mental health, trauma, substance use, poverty and systemic disadvantage, and study criminal justice theories, human rights and ethical frameworks, exploring how policing, courts and prisons operate and how policy, practice and reform can shape fairer outcomes. In the final year, students complete an industry placement preparing them for careers in law enforcement, corrections, courts and legal services, youth justice, and community support. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Criminal Justice and Psychological Studies
description: The Bachelor of Criminal Justice and Psychological Studies at Victoria University combines a deep understanding of criminal behaviour with study of the systems that respond to it. Students examine the social, political and psychological factors that shape behaviour, including trauma, inequality and mental health, while developing knowledge in counselling theory, family dynamics, research and ethics. This interdisciplinary course prepares graduates for work across justice, welfare and community sectors, including victim support and advocacy, child protection and family services, corrections and rehabilitation, mental health and wellbeing, and policy development. In the final year students complete an industry placement. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Criminology
description: The Bachelor of Criminology at Victoria University develops the knowledge and practical skills to critically examine crime, justice and the operation of the criminal justice system. Students explore why people commit crime by examining social, political, cultural, psychological and economic factors, and through practical learning and real-world case studies gain experience identifying crime-related problems and developing evidence-based policy reform recommendations. Specialist subjects include crime and inequality, policing and offending, victimology, digital criminology, transnational and international crime, early intervention and crime prevention, corporate crime, environmental crime, and justice policy and reform. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Cyber Security
description: The Bachelor of Cyber Security at Victoria University builds in-demand skills to protect data and information systems. Students first study information technology, preparing for careers in software development or networking, then focus on specialised cyber security units. They learn cyber-threat detection and risk management, cyber security technologies such as digital signatures, public key infrastructure, VPNs, firewalls, intrusion detection and encryption, ethical hacking and digital forensics, vulnerability analysis and control, enterprise security, and cyber security regulation, policy and law, along with software development and network design. The degree is internationally recognised. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Data Science
description: The Bachelor of Data Science at Victoria University teaches students to identify, organise and analyse big data using specialised computational and statistical techniques to generate insights for complex problems. With industry-focused practices, real-world datasets and hands-on tools, students build an in-depth understanding of deep learning, data management, data mining and decision making, and learn to wrangle, analyse, visualise and predict from data. Targeted expertise includes machine learning, deep learning, big data management, data mining, predictive and prescriptive analysis, data visualisation, and business- and cyber security-oriented data analytics. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Dermal Sciences
description: The Bachelor of Dermal Sciences at Victoria University qualifies graduates for a career performing evidence-based skin treatments in the growing dermal therapies industry. Students get hands-on experience in VU's Dermal Clinic at the City Campus in Melbourne, learning under expert dermal clinicians to safely perform laser and light-based treatments, resurfacing procedures and lymphatic procedures. Designed with industry and the Australian Society of Dermal Clinicians, the degree is the only one of its kind in Australia and provides comprehensive knowledge across all areas of dermal science.

name: Bachelor of Early Childhood Education
description: The Bachelor of Early Childhood Education at Victoria University prepares students to become in-demand early childhood teachers, with strong projected job growth in the sector and Victorian Government scholarships and incentives available. The degree prepares graduates for a career nurturing the development and wellbeing of children from birth to five years, teaching students to support young children's foundations for success, involve families as contributors to learning, and support effective transitions to school. Students build a strong sense of social justice and ethical, inclusive teaching practice. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Early Childhood Education and Leadership
description: The Bachelor of Early Childhood Education and Leadership at Victoria University is the only course of its kind that dedicates four years of study to early childhood education with a focus on leadership, setting graduates up for advanced career opportunities. Students prepare for a career nurturing the development and wellbeing of children from birth to five years, learning to support young children's foundations for success, involve families as contributors to learning, and support transitions to school, while developing leadership capability, an understanding of child development, and ethical professional teaching practice that includes Indigenous perspectives. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood and Primary)
description:
This is a dual-qualification degree: graduates come out eligible for registration to teach both early childhood settings and primary school classrooms, which broadens job options in a way a single-sector teaching degree doesn't. VU runs the course through its College of Sport, Health, Engineering (education sits within VU's broader teaching college structure) with mandatory professional experience placements spread across multiple year levels rather than backloaded into the final year.

Students complete placements in both long day care/kindergarten settings and primary classrooms, which means the practical component runs longer in total than a primary-only degree, offset by the broader employment scope it opens up afterward. VU has increasingly focused its teaching pathways on the acute teacher shortages in Melbourne's growth corridors to the west, and a fair number of placement partnerships sit in those newer school communities rather than established inner-city schools.

Coursework covers child development, literacy and numeracy pedagogy, curriculum planning, and inclusive education, with a research or capstone project in the final year addressing a self-chosen classroom practice question.
curriculum:
Year 1: Child Development, Introduction to Early Childhood Education, Literacy Foundations, Numeracy Foundations
Year 2: Curriculum and Pedagogy (Early Childhood), Curriculum and Pedagogy (Primary), Professional Experience Placement 1
Year 3: Inclusive Education, Assessment and Reporting, Professional Experience Placement 2
Year 4: Professional Experience Placement 3 (extended), Research Project in Teaching Practice, Professional Studies Capstone
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent, Working with Children Check required
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 (no band below 7.0)

name: Bachelor of Education Studies
description: The Bachelor of Education Studies at Victoria University develops the skills to lead learning programs outside the traditional classroom and is also an alternative path into teaching. Graduates can work in mentoring and tutoring programs, community programs, public and welfare services, after-school care and teacher aide positions. Students can steer their career toward an area of interest with a major or minor in options including physical education, arts, community, English and teaching English as an additional language, humanities, ICT, maths, outdoor education and science. This course does not provide the prerequisites for teacher registration. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
Engineering at VU runs on problem-based learning rather than the standard lecture-then-lab format: students in the College of Engineering and Science are handed open-ended engineering problems from early in the course and work through them in teams, with staff acting more as facilitators than lecturers delivering content. It's accredited by Engineers Australia across its specialisations (civil, mechanical, electrical and electronic, and architectural engineering are the usual streams), so graduates come out eligible for graduate membership straight away.

The four-year honours degree includes a substantial industry placement component, and VU's location in Melbourne's west, close to manufacturing, construction and infrastructure projects rather than the CBD, shapes a lot of the applied project work students get assigned. It's a smaller, less internationally ranked engineering school than the sandstone universities, but the trade-off VU offers is smaller class sizes in the specialist years and a teaching style built around solving real problems rather than sitting exams on theory alone.

Students choose their specialisation after a shared first year of core mathematics, physics and engineering fundamentals, then move into discipline-specific design and project units.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Mathematics, Engineering Physics, Introduction to Engineering Design, Engineering Mechanics
Year 2: Specialisation core units begin (Civil, Mechanical, Electrical and Electronic, or Architectural Engineering), Materials Science, Thermodynamics or Structures
Year 3: Advanced specialisation units, Industry Placement, Engineering Project Management
Year 4: Capstone Engineering Design Project (Honours thesis-equivalent), Professional Practice, Advanced electives
admission_requirements: ATAR 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science
description: The Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science at Victoria University is a hands-on, science-based degree that equips students to support health and wellbeing, enhance athletic performance, and prevent or manage injury and chronic conditions. Students gain experience working with diverse populations and can tailor their studies toward clinical health or sport performance. Through classroom learning, laboratory work and industry placements, students explore movement and performance screening, exercise prescription and delivery, injury prevention and rehabilitation, and coaching for skill development. Accreditation pathways and industry connections prepare graduates for careers in exercise science, fitness and health promotion. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Health Science
description: The Bachelor of Health Science at Victoria University focuses on improving the health of populations and prepares students for a range of health and science careers. Through VU's collaborations with health institutes, universities and community organisations, students gain real-world experience and graduate ready to work on government health programs, private-practice initiatives and with NGOs. Students study core bioscience, research and public-health topics with a major in Public Health, and from second year choose areas of interest, graduating with expertise in disease and injury prevention, health research, health promotion and epidemiology. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Human Nutrition
description: The Bachelor of Human Nutrition at Victoria University gives students a solid foundation in nutrition, food and related science subjects, beginning with eight core units before progressing to targeted study. In the second and third years, students choose a specialisation from Biomedical Nutrition, Public Health Nutrition, or Exercise and Nutrition, broadening their learning and employment opportunities in the community nutrition and public health sector or as preparation for postgraduate study. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
A three-year degree taught entirely in VU's block format, so students take one IT subject at a time for four weeks before moving to the next, rather than the usual four-subjects-at-once semester grind. VU has published its own research on this model and reports pass rates climbing from 77% to nearly 87% after it was introduced, which the university leans on heavily in how it markets the course to first-in-family students who might otherwise struggle with a traditional course load.

Students choose a major partway through (options typically include software development, cybersecurity, networking or data analytics), and the degree includes an industry-based learning placement in the final year, giving graduates workplace experience before they finish. VU's IT program has a large international cohort, and the block structure was partly designed with exactly that group in mind: intensive, single-subject study is easier to follow for students still building English academic fluency than four simultaneous subjects.

Graduates commonly go into junior developer, systems administrator or support analyst roles across Melbourne's west, an area VU has deliberately positioned itself to serve given its Footscray and Sunshine campus locations sit closer to industrial and logistics employers than the CBD-focused universities.
curriculum:
Year 1: Programming Fundamentals, Web Development, Database Design, Networking Essentials
Year 2: Data Structures and Algorithms, Systems Analysis, Cybersecurity Principles, Major elective units begin
Year 3: Advanced major units (Software Development, Networking, or Data Analytics stream), Industry-Based Learning placement, IT Capstone Project
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent, VU Block Model entry
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
VU's law degree requires 384 credit points across four years: 96 points of first-year core study, 132 points of professional core law units (the ones needed for admission), 108 points of law electives and 48 points of non-law electives, and is taught out of VU's City campus, which the university markets as sitting inside Melbourne's legal precinct near the courts and major firms.

Students who perform strongly early (a distinction average across the first 192 credit points) can apply to transfer into the honours version of the degree, assessed against their top 12 law units, so the honours distinction isn't set from day one the way it is at some universities. It's earned partway through. Core areas covered are the ones required for admission to legal practice everywhere in Australia: contracts, torts, property, constitutional, criminal and corporate law.

Because VU draws heavily from Melbourne's west, a lot of the clinical and community legal placement options connect students with legal aid and community legal centres in that catchment rather than corporate firm internships, which shapes the kind of practical legal experience students tend to graduate with.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Law, Contracts, Torts, Legal Research and Writing
Year 2: Criminal Law, Property Law, Constitutional Law, Law elective
Year 3: Corporate Law, Administrative Law, Evidence, Law electives
Year 4: Professional Responsibility, Advanced law electives, Non-law electives, Clinical Legal Practice option
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
VU's nursing degree runs out of the St Albans campus and requires 288 credit points of core study plus roughly 800 hours of clinical placement and around 140 hours of simulation training at the Sunshine Clinical School, which sits alongside a working hospital precinct in Melbourne's west. The clinical simulation load is concentrated in third year, after students have built up foundational anatomy, physiology and nursing practice units in years one and two.

The course leads to registration eligibility with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, and VU's placement partnerships lean on the public hospitals across Melbourne's western and northern suburbs, with Western Health and its network featuring heavily, rather than a spread across the whole city, which means graduates often end up working close to where they trained.

A combined Bachelor of Midwifery/Bachelor of Nursing pathway also exists at VU for students who know from the outset they want registration in both areas, though the standalone nursing degree is the more common entry point.
curriculum:
Year 1: Anatomy and Physiology, Foundations of Nursing Practice, Health Assessment, Pharmacology Basics
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Clinical Placement Block 1
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing, Simulation-based clinical training (Sunshine Clinical School), Clinical Placement Blocks 2 and 3
Year 4: Specialty placements (paediatrics, aged care, community health), Transition to Professional Practice, Capstone
admission_requirements: ATAR 65 or equivalent, National Police Check and Working with Children Check required
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 7.0)

name: Bachelor of Outdoor Leadership
description: The Bachelor of Outdoor Leadership at Victoria University is designed to meet the needs of the outdoor education and recreation sectors. Students apply on-campus study through activities in VU's outdoor labs, combining knowledge of the natural environment, group leadership and planning to open career possibilities in adventure tourism, environmental education, outdoor recreation and nature tourism. The course includes a paid internship with The Outdoor Education Group designed to run alongside study, and explores its themes through adventure-based activities such as bushwalking, canoeing, cycling, white-water rafting, alpine activities and rock climbing.

name: Bachelor of Paramedicine
description: The Bachelor of Paramedicine at Victoria University develops the skills to work as a registered paramedic in ambulance, primary healthcare and community healthcare settings. While studying, students are registered with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency. Students study paramedicine theory in the classroom and put it into practice in high-fidelity simulation clinics, clinical-practice labs and during work-integrated learning, working with experienced registered health professionals and academics to graduate confident and job-ready. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Physical Education and Sport Science
description: The Bachelor of Physical Education and Sport Science at Victoria University covers subjects across games and sports, skill acquisition and motor development, inclusive physical activity, anatomy, kinesiology, health and nutrition, exercise physiology and biomechanics, and individual fitness activities, aquatics and athletics. Students can expand their career options with a minor in another discipline, and access to strong industry partners means graduates are ready to progress a career in the sport industry or continue to further study. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
An APAC-accredited undergraduate psychology sequence, which matters because it's the accreditation students need if they want to progress to honours and eventually provisional registration as a psychologist. A non-accredited psych degree closes that path off entirely. VU delivers the core sequence (research methods, cognition, developmental, social and biological psychology, and statistics) in its block format, meaning students spend four weeks immersed in, say, statistics before moving to the next unit rather than splitting attention across a semester.

Students needing the accredited sequence typically go on to VU's honours year or transfer into postgraduate psychology elsewhere, since the three-year bachelor alone isn't sufficient for registration. The course also serves students who don't intend to become psychologists at all: human resources, market research and community services graduates make up a meaningful share of the cohort, using the degree as a behavioural-science foundation rather than a clinical pathway.

VU's psych program is smaller than the large metropolitan universities' offerings, which in practice means smaller tutorial groups in the statistics and research methods units that trip a lot of students up elsewhere.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Psychology, Statistics for Psychology, Research Methods 1
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology, Research Methods 2
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology, Psychological Assessment, Research Methods 3, Applied Psychology electives
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Psychology (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Psychology (Honours) at Victoria University covers human behaviour, motivation and relationships and prepares students to apply for registration as a provisional psychologist and to take up further study options. The first three years focus on psychology and social research methods, including a work placement in the third year, and the fourth honours year covers advanced quantitative and qualitative research methods, professional practice units and a research thesis. Graduates have an in-depth knowledge of human emotion and behaviour. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Science (Honours) (Biomedical Science)
description: The Bachelor of Science (Honours) at Victoria University builds on a bachelor degree with a fourth year focused on a specialist research thesis, in areas including biomedicine, environmental sciences, food sciences, nursing, midwifery, sport science and exercise science. The honours year develops skills in independent research, critical analysis, problem solving, and devising, designing and conducting experimental work, along with written and spoken communication and research ethics, and prepares graduates for postgraduate research and a competitive job market.

name: Bachelor of Screen Media
description: The Bachelor of Screen Media at Victoria University develops skills in using media to tell stories across film, television, radio, screen culture, and online and mobile media production. Through practical and theoretical learning, students develop new media production skills, techniques and knowledge, including intellectual property, with a contemporary focus on delivering content for online distribution, video-on-demand and streaming platforms as well as television and radio. Students learn from teachers involved in the industry and produce cross-platform projects, motion graphics and visual effects, narrative and non-fiction film, documentaries, podcasts, and television and radio programs. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Social Work
description:
A four-year professionally accredited degree (Australian Association of Social Workers accreditation applies) that trains students for statutory and community-sector practice across Melbourne's west, a region with some of the highest need for social services in the state. VU built the course around two substantial field placements (typically around 1,000 hours combined across the degree), placing students in child protection, community health, mental health and family services settings rather than leaving fieldwork to a single capstone block.

Like the rest of VU's course offering, theory units run block-mode, one subject over four weeks, though placement blocks necessarily run on the employer's schedule rather than the university's. The curriculum spends real time on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander social work perspectives and on Melbourne's west specifically as a case study in structural disadvantage, which reflects VU's own catchment: a large share of its students come from the same low-SES postcodes the degree is training them to work in.

Graduates go on to registration-eligible roles in child and family services, community mental health and case management, with VU's local reputation among Melbourne's west community organisations doing a lot of the placement-to-job pipeline work.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Social Work, Human Development, Sociology for Practice, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Perspectives
Year 2: Social Work Theory and Methods, Field Placement 1, Mental Health and Wellbeing
Year 3: Social Policy, Community Development, Field Placement 2
Year 4: Advanced Practice Methods, Research Project, Professional Ethics and Law
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent, National Police Check required
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 7.0)

name: Bachelor of Sport Management
description: The Bachelor of Sport Management at Victoria University teaches management techniques and their application to the sport and physical recreation industries, including planning, human resource management, finance, leadership, marketing and performance evaluation. Graduates are prepared to manage professional sport organisations, major sporting events and facilities, as well as community sport programs, social development projects, outdoor adventure activities and active recreation. VU is a leading sport university, and classroom activities are blended with online and practical learning, including work placements. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Sport Science
description:
This is where VU's biggest research reputation actually lives: the university's Institute for Health and Sport was ranked #6 in the world for sport science by ShanghaiRanking in 2025, and undergraduates in this course get taught out of the same $68 million exercise physiology, biomechanics and motor-learning facility at Footscray Park that the institute's 100-plus researchers and postgrad cohort use.

Students work through core units in exercise physiology, biomechanics, motor learning and skill acquisition before specialising toward strength and conditioning, clinical exercise or high-performance sport pathways, and the degree includes practical placement hours with sporting organisations. VU has longstanding research partnerships with elite clubs that occasionally translate into student placement opportunities, though those aren't guaranteed for everyone.

Compared to sport science programs that lean heavily on classroom theory, VU's course puts students in the lab early: first-year students are running basic physiological testing protocols rather than only reading about them, which is a deliberate consequence of the block model letting each subject go deep on one topic without competing for lab time against three other units.
curriculum:
Year 1: Human Anatomy, Exercise Physiology Fundamentals, Functional Anatomy, Introduction to Biomechanics
Year 2: Motor Learning and Skill Acquisition, Strength and Conditioning Principles, Research Methods, Nutrition for Performance
Year 3: Specialisation units (Clinical Exercise, High Performance Sport, or Strength and Conditioning), Practicum Placement, Sport Science Capstone Project
admission_requirements: ATAR 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Youth Work
description: The Bachelor of Youth Work at Victoria University teaches students to help young people develop resilience through activities that are enjoyable, challenging and educational. Graduates gain a professional foundation for working with young people, specialist knowledge to support disadvantaged groups, and practical management and leadership skills. VU's program is the largest of its kind in Australia and is delivered by youth-work specialists, sociologists and experienced workers from disability, legal care, community development and social work. Students undertake substantial professional work placements. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Diploma of Beauty Therapy
description: The Diploma of Beauty Therapy (SHB50121) at Victoria University TAFE advances beauty-treatment skills and prepares students for management positions in salons and spas. Students develop knowledge of the theory and science behind beauty treatments and gain extensive hands-on experience, including a practical placement in a salon of their choice and learning in VU's beauty salon. Training covers facial treatments, lash and brow treatments, manicures and pedicures, make-up, waxing, body massage and treatments, spa treatments, and retail skin care and cosmetics, along with business and management skills for running a salon.

name: Diploma of Building and Construction (Building)
description: The Diploma of Building and Construction (Building) (CPC50220) at Victoria University prepares students to work as building project managers and to run a construction business in the residential, industrial or commercial sectors. Learning is linked to real-world practice, from industry-standard knowledge to on-site projects, and covers quantity surveying, planning and scheduling of labour and materials, selecting contractors, managing project risk and quality, supervising work sites, construction technology, workplace safety, business codes and standards, structural principles, interpreting plans and specifications, and small business finance. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Diploma of Business (Enterprise)
description: The Diploma of Business (Enterprise) at Victoria University prepares students for university study in the Bachelor of Business or for an entry-level business role. It provides a broad introduction to the industry and foundation skills relevant to working in the business sector, including accounting, management, marketing, economics, communications and information technology. Students who complete the diploma can articulate into the first or second year of a related VU bachelor degree with credit. It is offered at VU in Melbourne, and is also suited to students who want a shorter standalone business qualification.

name: Diploma of Criminal Justice and Psychological Studies
Diploma of Cyber Security
description: The Diploma of Cyber Security at Victoria University provides the foundational skills and knowledge to identify, prevent and respond to cyber threats, with hands-on experience in security technologies and practices including ethical hacking, digital forensics, network security, threat analysis, vulnerability assessment and incident response. Graduates are prepared for secure, entry-level roles, and completing the diploma provides a pathway into VU's related bachelor degrees. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care
description: The Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care (CHC50125) at Victoria University equips students to work at a high level in children's services, planning activities and caring for children with an emphasis on play-based learning that enables children to achieve developmental outcomes. The practical course includes five work placements and a first aid course, and covers childhood development, planning for children with additional needs, networking and family partnerships, and health and safety. Graduates are qualified early childhood educators. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Diploma of Education Studies
description: The Diploma of Education Studies at Victoria University prepares students to enter the second year of a teaching degree and is designed for those who did not meet the entry requirements for the Bachelor of Education through VTAC or direct selection. This Victorian Institute of Teaching accredited pathway builds the skills needed for a career in education, and successful completion earns a place in the second year of the Bachelor of Education Studies, Bachelor of Early Childhood Education or Bachelor of Arts, with further requirements opening pathways into the Bachelor of Education. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Diploma of Hospitality Management
description: The Diploma of Hospitality Management (SIT50422) at Victoria University provides the knowledge and training to become a skilled manager in the hospitality industry, with practical skills tailored to restaurants, cafes, pubs, hotels and other hospitality settings. Students learn and apply skills in VU's fully equipped hospitality training centre under industry experts, covering staff management, strategic business operations, food and beverage service, safety and business marketing, and learn to manage hotel front office operations. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Diploma of Information Technology
description: The Diploma of Information Technology at Victoria University is a practical program leading into the second year of the Bachelor of Information Technology, designed for students taking a first step toward the bachelor degree and professionals building IT knowledge and skills. Students learn networking with CISCO, database design, programming in Python, connecting databases to dynamic websites, ICT project scheduling with Microsoft Project, and Linux, along with professional communication and academic writing. Successful completion provides a guaranteed place in the second year of the Bachelor of Information Technology, Bachelor of Cyber Security or Bachelor of Data Science.

name: Diploma of Physical Education and Sport Science Studies
Diploma of Youth Work
description: The Diploma of Youth Work (CHC50425) at Victoria University develops the skills to build trusting, effective relationships with young people and to create engaging programs for children, teenagers and young adults. Students develop knowledge and skills in needs assessment, service delivery and case management, advocacy and empowerment, child protection and legal and ethical frameworks, community education and group activities, and workplace safety. A placement lets students put their learning into practice under a qualified supervisor. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Graduate Certificate in Artificial Intelligence
description: The Graduate Certificate in Artificial Intelligence at Victoria University builds a foundation in AI technologies and skills for application development, covering modern programming, data mining, data analytics, neural networks, deep learning and natural language processing. As AI drives digital transformation across industry sectors, employers face a global shortage of AI expertise, and this postgraduate course helps graduates and working professionals build capability in the field. On completion, students can critically review AI applications, appraise the components of AI system architectures, and design and implement AI applications systematically. It is taught by active researchers and can serve as a pathway into further postgraduate IT study at VU's City Campus in Melbourne.

name: Graduate Certificate in Business Administration
description: The Graduate Certificate in Business Administration at Victoria University updates business and management skills and knowledge, and is suited to business graduates and to managers qualified in other disciplines. It offers a pathway into the Master of Business Administration. The course contains four foundational units: financial analysis, marketing management, business ethics and sustainability, and strategic management and business policy. Students can study at VU's Melbourne city campus or complete the course fully online.

name: Graduate Certificate in Business Analytics
description: The Graduate Certificate in Business Analytics at Victoria University is a practical, business-focused course that builds a foundation in data-driven decision making. Through a hands-on approach using open-source environments such as R and Python, cloud platforms including AWS and GitHub, and a global partnership with SAP, students learn the principles of data science, data visualisation, machine learning and artificial intelligence, and how to apply them to real business problems. The course covers data wrangling and visualisation and predictive analytics, and units completed can be credited toward the Master of Business Analytics. It is taught at VU's City Campus in Melbourne.

name: Graduate Certificate in Construction Management
description: The Graduate Certificate in Construction Management at Victoria University is designed for people already working in construction who want to enhance their professional skills over a six-month period of full-time study. Students learn the fundamental principles of project management, including scoping, scheduling, costing and planning large-scale projects, while accounting for environmental and social considerations. The course also introduces the practical application of artificial intelligence and machine learning in analysing datasets, predicting project costs and optimising resource allocation. It provides a pathway into further postgraduate study in construction management at VU in Melbourne.

name: Graduate Certificate in Cyber Security
description: The Graduate Certificate in Cyber Security at Victoria University covers the essential areas of cyber security, from proactive threat detection and risk management to cyber law and regulation. Students learn from academic staff with a strong research record in cyber security and from industry experts, and gain expertise in cyber security fundamentals and architecture, technologies such as digital signatures, public key infrastructure, VPNs, firewalls, intrusion detection and encryption, cloud and enterprise security, and cyber security regulation, policy and law. The course is a pathway into further postgraduate IT study and is taught at VU's City Campus in Melbourne.

name: Graduate Certificate in Early Childhood Education
description: The Graduate Certificate in Early Childhood Education at Victoria University introduces key concepts for teaching young children from birth to five years in early childhood education settings. Across four units, students develop expertise in responsive teaching, focusing on different ways of knowing, being and doing in the Australian context, and learn to create rich and varied learning opportunities grounded in sound ethical principles and reciprocal relationships with children and families. Those seeking registration as an early childhood teacher can pathway from this certificate into the Graduate Diploma in Early Childhood Education. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Graduate Certificate in Education
description: The Graduate Certificate in Education at Victoria University is the first step in VU's graduate program in education, tailored to trainers and teachers in education, community, government and industry. Students gain an overview of current high-level education theory and contemporary techniques in approaches to learning, educational leadership for social justice, innovation in education, and vocational education and training policy and practice, and conduct their own workplace research. Successful completion gains admission to the Graduate Diploma in Education, which leads into the Master of Education. This course does not provide registration to teach in Australia. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Graduate Certificate in Enterprise and Resource Planning Systems
description: The Graduate Certificate in Enterprise and Resource Planning Systems at Victoria University prepares graduates for a career in SAP solutions through what VU describes as the most comprehensive postgraduate ERP program in Australia, with strong industry connections and 24-hour online access to SAP. The course covers SAP process and module delivery, technical and configuration development, and SAP/ERP application packages, along with process engineering and SAP reporting through business analytics and the main SAP processes including production planning, materials management, sales and distribution, accounting and human resources. It is the first step in VU's graduate ERP program and is offered in Melbourne.

name: Graduate Certificate in Global Public Health
description: The Graduate Certificate in Global Public Health at Victoria University establishes a knowledge base in health policy and programs in under six months. Students learn to evaluate current and emerging health challenges, appraise public health evidence, and contribute to collaborative health programs and policies, and graduate understanding how public health solutions contribute to sustainable development and inclusive practice, including ensuring Indigenous views are heard. The certificate suits recent graduates aiming to work in health policy and programs and health professionals enhancing their practice, and students may progress to the Master of Global Public Health. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Graduate Certificate in Industrial Relations and Human Resource Management
Graduate Certificate in Information Technology Project Management
description: The Graduate Certificate in Information Technology Project Management at Victoria University introduces the fundamentals of project management with specific application to IT projects, based on the international Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK) and addressing contemporary issues in managing IT projects. On completion, students can apply key project management frameworks and processes to a range of scenarios, understand the roles and responsibilities of a project manager, and communicate with specialist and non-specialist stakeholders. It suits people preparing for IT project management roles or building skills for a current position, and is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Graduate Certificate in International Community Development
description: The Graduate Certificate in International Community Development at Victoria University is a practical postgraduate program, including workplace training, for a career in community development in local and international settings. Key study areas include community development theories and practices, project design, planning and management, advocacy of gender and human rights, and conflict resolution in groups and communities, with the course critically engaging with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. It is the first of three courses that make up VU's Master of International Community Development, and graduates are eligible to continue into the Graduate Diploma. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Graduate Certificate in Marketing
description: The Graduate Certificate in Marketing at Victoria University teaches applied marketing principles along with techniques and frameworks for analysing marketplace strategies and developing integrated strategic marketing plans. Topics include marketing communication, consumer behaviour, digital marketing, and business ethics and sustainability.
