Before students can undertake Professional Experience subjects, they need Working with Children clearance and Child Protection Awareness training, and the National Literacy and Numeracy Test for Initial Teacher Education students has to be cleared before the final placement subject, both NESA requirements rather than university-specific hurdles.

WSU trains a very large share of NSW's primary teaching workforce, particularly for schools across Greater Western Sydney, and the program's placement network reflects that. A meaningful number of graduates end up placed, and later employed, in the same public school systems across Western Sydney where the university itself draws much of its student body from.

The degree is NESA-accredited and meets the national Australian Professional Standards for Graduate Teachers, qualifying graduates to teach Kindergarten to Year 6 in NSW government and non-government schools.
curriculum:
Duration: 4 years full-time, 320 credit points
Year 1: Foundations of Teaching and Learning, Child Development, Literacy Education 1, Numeracy Education 1, early Professional Experience placement
Year 2: Curriculum studies (English, Mathematics, Science, HASS), Inclusive Education, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Education, ongoing placements
Year 3: Advanced curriculum and pedagogy subjects, Classroom Management, Assessment and Reporting, Professional Experience block
Year 4: Capstone Professional Experience (extended placement), Professional Practice seminar
Requirements: Working with Children Check, Child Protection Awareness training, NESA Literacy and Numeracy Test (before final placement)
NESA-accredited; meets Australian Professional Standards for Graduate Teachers
admission_requirements: ATAR 65 or equivalent, Working with Children Check required
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 (no band below 7.0)

name: Bachelor of Tourism and Event Management
description: The Bachelor of Tourism and Event Management at Western Sydney University is a three-year full-time degree combining tourism, event management, social science, business and marketing to prepare graduates for roles in tourism, events and the visitor economy. It is co-designed with partners including Destination NSW and the Australian Federation of Travel Agents, and students choose from a suite of majors. Graduates work in event management, destination marketing and tourism operations. Indicative international tuition is around 32,500 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 109243J.

name: Bachelor of Traditional Chinese Medicine
description: The Bachelor of Traditional Chinese Medicine at Western Sydney University is a four-year full-time degree that equips practitioners with the knowledge and professional competencies for a career in acupuncture, Chinese herbal medicine and herb dispensing. It builds a broad understanding of biomedicine and health sciences to support interdisciplinary practice and client advice on treatment options. Graduates work as registered Chinese medicine practitioners. Indicative international tuition is around 37,800 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 089195D.

name: Bachelor of Youth Work
description: The Bachelor of Youth Work at Western Sydney University is a three-year full-time degree developed with industry partners that trains professional youth workers. It draws on the humanities and social sciences to understand the challenges young people face and how to respond, working with young people as people who face barriers rather than as a problem. Graduates work in youth services, community organisations and government programs. Indicative international tuition is around 31,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 114846F.

name: Diploma in Business Fast Track
description: The Diploma in Business Fast Track at Western Sydney University is an accelerated program of around eight months that prepares students for careers across accounting, finance, economics, international business, marketing, sports management, human resources and management. Using modular learning, one subject at a time, it provides a pathway to the second year of multiple business bachelor degrees without losing time. Graduates continue into a bachelor degree or enter business support roles. Indicative international tuition is around 37,900 Australian dollars per year.

name: Diploma in Criminal and Community Justice (Exit Only)
description: The Diploma in Criminal and Community Justice at Western Sydney University is a one-year qualification offered as an exit award within the Bachelor of Criminal and Community Justice, a degree developed with Brush Farm, the training academy of Corrective Services NSW, for people working in or entering corrections, probation and parole. Graduates use the diploma in community corrections and justice support roles or as credit toward completing the bachelor. Indicative international tuition is around 32,500 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 083030G.

name: Diploma in Education (Primary) (Exit Only)
description: The Diploma in Education (Primary) at Western Sydney University is a one-year qualification offered as an exit award within the Bachelor of Education (Primary), an initial teacher education degree with school experience from the first year that prepares graduates to teach Kindergarten to Year 6. Graduates use the diploma in education support roles or as credit toward completing the bachelor. Indicative international tuition is around 32,500 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 103728C.

name: Diploma in Educational Studies (Secondary) (Exit Only)
description: The Diploma in Educational Studies (Secondary) at Western Sydney University is a one-year qualification offered as an exit award within the Master of Teaching (Secondary), which combines on-campus theory with school-based placements to prepare specialist graduates as secondary teachers. Graduates use the diploma as recognition of partial study or as a foundation for further education study. Indicative international tuition is around 32,500 Australian dollars per year.

name: Diploma in General Science (exit only)
description: The Diploma in General Science at Western Sydney University is a one-year program, offered as the Diploma in Science, that uses modular learning, one subject at a time, to build the skills needed for further science study. It provides a pathway to the second year of multiple science bachelor degrees without losing time. Graduates continue into a bachelor degree or enter science support roles. Indicative international tuition is around 39,600 Australian dollars per year.

name: Diploma in Health Support (exit only)
description: The Diploma in Health Support at Western Sydney University is a one-year qualification offered as an exit award within the Bachelor of Health Science. The parent degree combines study with hands-on experience and majors in public health, health promotion, health services management, recreational therapy and clinical sciences. Graduates use the diploma in health support roles or as credit toward completing the bachelor. Indicative international tuition is around 34,800 Australian dollars per year.

name: Diploma in Laws (exit only)
description: The Diploma in Laws at Western Sydney University is a one-year qualification offered as an exit award within the Bachelor of Laws, a degree taught by practitioners and academics with internships in law firms and not-for-profits and clinical experience in the university's Justice Clinic. Graduates use the diploma as recognition of substantial legal study or as credit toward completing the bachelor. Indicative international tuition is around 38,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 041112G.

name: Diploma in Social Science (Humanitarian and Development Studies) (exit only)
description: The Diploma in Social Science (Humanitarian and Development Studies) at Western Sydney University is a one-year qualification offered as an exit award within the Bachelor of Humanitarian and Development Studies, described by the university as the only degree of its kind in Australia and developed with non-government organisations. Graduates use the diploma in humanitarian and development support roles or as credit toward completing the bachelor. Indicative international tuition is around 32,500 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 088714E.

name: Diploma in Social Science Studies (Exit Only)
description: The Diploma in Social Science Studies at Western Sydney University is a one-year program, offered as the Diploma in Social Sciences, for students interested in social sciences, policing or humanitarian and development studies. Using modular learning, one subject at a time, it provides a pathway to the second year of multiple bachelor degrees without losing time. Graduates continue into a bachelor degree or enter community and social service roles. Indicative international tuition is around 32,500 Australian dollars per year.

description: The Graduate Diploma in TESOL at Western Sydney University is a one-year full-time professional qualification for teaching English to speakers of other languages. It suits teachers from other education fields and graduates from any discipline wanting a long-term TESOL career in Australia or overseas, and values bilingualism and multilingualism. Graduates teach English in schools, colleges and language centres. Indicative international tuition is around 34,800 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 059714A.

name: Graduate Diploma in Translation
description: The Graduate Diploma in Translation at Western Sydney University is a one-year full-time qualification within the Master of Translation and TESOL, which prepares students to work as qualified translators or English language teachers as global demand for both continues to grow. Students build practical language transfer and teaching skills. Graduates work in translation, localisation and English language teaching. Indicative international tuition is around 39,600 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 088716C.

name: Graduate Diploma in Translation Studies - exit only
description: The Graduate Diploma in Translation Studies at Western Sydney University is a one-year full-time qualification offered as an exit award within the Master of Translation and TESOL. The parent program prepares students to work as qualified translators or English language teachers, building practical language transfer and teaching skills. Graduates work in translation, localisation and English language teaching. Indicative international tuition is around 39,600 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 088716C.

name: Juris Doctor
description: The Juris Doctor at Western Sydney University is a three-year full-time professional-entry masters degree that satisfies the academic requirements for admission to practise as a lawyer in Australia. It combines accredited legal education with technology, real-world experience and contemporary legal practice, building legal knowledge, practical skills and professional confidence. Graduates enter legal practice and law-related careers. Indicative international tuition is around 47,100 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 101997K.

name: Master of Applied Finance
description: The Master of Applied Finance at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree that prepares students for executive careers in finance, banking, funds management, property investment and corporate treasury. Students choose subjects aligned to their career goals and acquire the technical knowledge to work in an evolving and increasingly sophisticated financial environment. Graduates work in financial analysis, investment, treasury and advisory roles. Indicative international tuition is around 39,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 079262C.

name: Master of Applied Neuromorphic Engineering
description: The Master of Applied Neuromorphic Engineering at Western Sydney University is an eighteen-month full-time degree in an interdisciplinary field spanning electrical engineering, computer science, neuroscience, signal processing and mathematics. Students partner with industry on an applied or research project mentored by researchers at the International Centre for Neuromorphic Systems. Graduates work in bio-inspired sensing, edge computing and brain-inspired hardware. Indicative international tuition is around 41,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 106434D.

name: Master of Architecture (Urban Transformation)
description: The Master of Architecture (Urban Transformation) at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree for students who have completed undergraduate architecture study and need the professional degree required for registration as an architect in Australia. It also prepares graduates for doctoral study. The program focuses on architecture in the context of urban change and transformation. Graduates progress toward registration and work in architectural practice. Indicative international tuition is around 41,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 099363K.

name: Master of Art Therapy
description: The Master of Art Therapy at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time clinical training program, described by the university as the only program of its kind in New South Wales and one of only three in Australia. Students learn to use visual art media within a therapeutic relationship to support people in distress, graduating with the theoretical knowledge and practical experience to work as art therapists. Graduates work across health, mental health, education and community settings. Indicative international tuition is around 33,100 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 013543F.

name: Master of Artificial Intelligence
description: The Master of Artificial Intelligence at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree covering AI from foundations to current technologies and applications, including knowledge representation and reasoning, machine learning, and natural language understanding. Students learn how AI is driving digital disruption and how to work in a fast-evolving field. Graduates work as AI developers, machine learning engineers and technology consultants. Indicative international tuition is around 41,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 101783M.

name: Master of Arts in Literature and Creative Writing
description: The Master of Arts in Literature and Creative Writing at Western Sydney University is an eighteen-month full-time degree that connects creative writing practice with ideas and creative work from the arts and sciences. Students think across creative, critical and disciplinary categories and produce works of scholarship or creative writing, including work that crosses into music, art, performance and film, taught through the university's Writing and Research Centre. Graduates work in writing, editing, publishing, teaching and the arts. Indicative international tuition is around 34,800 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 092783B.

name: Master of Arts in TESOL
description: The Master of Arts in TESOL at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree, offered through the Master of Translation and TESOL, that prepares students to teach English to speakers of other languages and to work across language services. Students build teaching methodology and practical language skills as global demand for qualified English language teachers continues to grow. Graduates teach English in schools, universities and language colleges in Australia and overseas. Indicative international tuition is around 39,600 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 088716C.

name: Master of Arts Translation and Interpreting Studies
description: The Master of Arts Translation and Interpreting Studies at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree, offered through the Master of Interpreting and Translation, that builds the skills to work as a qualified interpreter and translator as global business and social interactions cross borders. Students develop practical language transfer skills and prepare toward professional accreditation. Graduates work as interpreters and translators across community, legal, health and conference settings. Indicative international tuition is around 39,600 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 084736J.

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Western Sydney University's MBA runs out of the Parramatta City campus and is pitched deliberately at working professionals across Greater Western Sydney's public sector, health, education and logistics employers rather than assuming a Sydney CBD finance-and-consulting cohort. Case material and guest teaching draw heavily on the region's own major employers. Western Sydney has become a genuine economic centre in its own right, particularly with the new Western Sydney Airport precinct under construction and the associated business and government investment that's followed it.

The core spine covers strategy, finance, marketing and leadership as any MBA would, but WSU frames its differentiator as a stronger focus on public sector and not-for-profit management alongside standard corporate strategy, reflecting the composition of its actual student cohort more than it does at some private-sector-oriented MBA programs.

Most students complete the degree part-time while working, with evening and block-intensive delivery options, and the capstone is typically an applied strategy project connected to the student's own workplace or a partner organisation rather than a purely theoretical case study exercise.
curriculum:
Duration: 1.5–2 years part-time, or accelerated full-time option
Core subjects: Strategic Management, Financial Management, Marketing Management, Leading People and Organisations, Business Analytics, Public Sector and Not-for-Profit Management
Elective block: Finance, Marketing, Health Management, or Entrepreneurship streams
Capstone: applied strategy project, often based in student's own workplace or partner organisation
Delivery: evening and block-intensive options for part-time cohort
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree plus relevant work experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Master of Business Analytics
description: The Master of Business Analytics at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree focused on business analytics rather than data analytics alone. Students study the nature of data, including big and unstructured data, and learn to run data-driven investigations and visual and computational analytics for business decision making. Graduates work as business analysts, insight specialists and analytics consultants. Indicative international tuition is around 39,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 098262A.

name: Master of Chinese Medicine
description: The Master of Chinese Medicine at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree for Chinese medicine practitioners strengthening their knowledge and skills to work autonomously within health systems, and for graduates seeking a research pathway. The program includes a clinical placement undertaken either at the Beijing University of Chinese Medicine or in Sydney. Graduates advance their practice and pursue research in Chinese medicine. Indicative international tuition is around 34,800 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 109098B.

name: Master of Clinical Psychology
description: The Master of Clinical Psychology at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree that provides education and supervised training toward practice as a clinical psychologist. Provisionally registered students are supported by an experienced clinical teaching team and gain real-life experience through the university's psychology clinics. Graduates progress toward registration and endorsement as clinical psychologists. Indicative international tuition is around 47,600 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 042101C.

name: Master of Construction Law
description: The Master of Construction Law at Western Sydney University is a one-year full-time industry-endorsed degree for construction lawyers and professionals working in construction, engineering and associated industries. Taught by leaders in the field, it develops advanced knowledge of construction law and its application for Australian and overseas practitioners. Graduates advance in construction law, contract administration and dispute resolution roles. Indicative international tuition is around 41,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 108750J.

name: Master of Creative Music Therapy
description: The Master of Creative Music Therapy at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree that prepares students for professional practice as registered music therapists. It integrates creative practice, extensive work-integrated learning and research capability, with a curriculum focused on developing music therapy practice. Graduates work as music therapists across health, disability, aged care, mental health and community settings. Indicative international tuition is around 35,400 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Data Science
description: Western Sydney University's Master of Data Science is a 160-credit-point degree, two years full-time or four years part-time, with a strong applications focus. Core subjects include Programming for Data Science, The Nature of Data, Big Data, Visualisation, Advanced Statistical Methods and Predictive Analytics, and students complete two self-guided master's projects that produce actionable insights and metrics. Entry requires a completed undergraduate degree in any discipline; prior statistics or programming is an advantage but not essential. An alternative pathway accepts a data science undergraduate degree plus two years of relevant full-time professional experience in roles such as data analyst, statistician or machine learning. Indicative international tuition is around A$41,200 per year. Graduates are equipped to work effectively in data-driven organisations.

name: Master of Educational Studies (exit only)
description: The Master of Educational Studies at Western Sydney University is a two-year fully online degree offered within the Master of Education, for educators who want to deepen their knowledge, extend their professional expertise and advance their careers. It covers contemporary approaches to education applied to real-world challenges across early childhood, primary, secondary, tertiary, community and professional education. Graduates move into specialist and leadership roles in education. Indicative international tuition is around 35,100 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Engineering
description: The Master of Engineering at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time fully accredited professional program for practising engineers and recent graduates. Taught at the Parramatta City campus, it lets students upgrade their skills and qualify sooner across a range of majors including civil, environmental, electrical, mechanical, mechatronic and telecommunications engineering. Graduates advance in professional engineering practice. Indicative international tuition is around 41,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 042034J.

name: Master of Epidemiology
description: The Master of Epidemiology at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree that builds the skills to find solutions to epidemics, improve global health and establish effective public health policy. Delivered through the university's medical school, it combines rigorous method with active involvement in the field. Graduates work in epidemiology, disease surveillance, public health units and research. Indicative international tuition is around 37,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 088189K.

name: Master of Finance
description: The Master of Finance at Western Sydney University is an eighteen-month full-time degree, offered as the Master of Applied Finance, that prepares students for executive careers in finance, banking, funds management, property investment and corporate treasury. Students choose subjects aligned to their goals and acquire the technical knowledge to work in an evolving financial environment. Graduates work in financial analysis, investment, treasury and advisory roles. Indicative international tuition is around 39,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 079262C.

name: Master of Global Security and Justice
description: The Master of Global Security and Justice at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree with a distinctive emphasis on human security and social justice. It is interdisciplinary and covers domestic and international issues including transnational crime, cybercrime and security, and comparative international politics, building critical thinking and ethical problem-solving skills. Graduates work in security, justice, policy, government and international organisations. Indicative international tuition is around 34,800 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 113137K.

name: Master of Health Science
description: The Master of Health Science at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree that prepares aspiring and mid-career health service practitioners, planners and managers to lead in the strategic and operational management of health services and facilities. Students choose a focus in health services management, occupational health and safety, or digital health, developing skills in managing people, resources, systems and processes. Graduates work in health service leadership and management roles. Indicative international tuition is around 37,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 064020M.

name: Master of Human Resource Management
description: The Master of Human Resource Management at Western Sydney University is a one-year full-time degree that builds the knowledge base for working in human resources and employment relations, with an emphasis on knowledge in action informed by the Australian HR Institute's professional capabilities. Key functional areas are considered within a strategic and contextualised framework. Graduates work in HR advisory, business partnering and people management roles. Indicative international tuition is around 39,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 093560J.

name: Master of Humanitarian and Development Studies
description: The Master of Humanitarian and Development Studies at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree, described by the university as the only degree of its kind in Australia. It responds to the ongoing need for qualified workers in disaster relief and development across government and non-government agencies, preparing students to deliver specialist humanitarian aid and development practice. Graduates work in humanitarian response, aid coordination, development programs and policy. Indicative international tuition is around 34,800 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 109090K.

name: Master of Information and Communications Technology
description:
Western Sydney University's Master of ICT is aimed squarely at career-changers and international graduates entering the tech workforce through Sydney's western suburbs corridor, an area that's absorbed a lot of the city's newer data centre and logistics-tech investment as space in the inner city has run out. The course structure typically opens with foundation subjects for students without a computing background, then narrows into a specialisation (software development, networking, data analytics or cybersecurity are common options) before a final applied project.

WSU's tech teaching happens across its Parramatta and Kingswood campuses, and the university has been building out partnerships with western Sydney's expanding business park tenants (logistics, health tech, government shared-services) as placement and project partners, which gives the program's industry project component a genuinely regional flavour rather than defaulting to CBD finance-sector case studies the way an inner-Sydney university's ICT masters might.

Graduates commonly move into systems analyst, network administrator, or junior software developer roles, with the degree also functioning as a stepping stone toward permanent residency pathways for many international students given its alignment with the skilled occupation list.
curriculum:
Duration: 1.5–2 years full-time, depending on entry background
Foundation subjects (non-IT entrants): Programming Fundamentals, Database Systems, Networking Basics
Core subjects: Systems Analysis and Design, IT Project Management, Enterprise Architecture
Specialisation (choose one): Software Development, Networking and Security, Data Analytics, Cybersecurity
Capstone: industry-based ICT project or research subject in final term
Electives drawn from cross-faculty computing subjects
admission_requirements: Undergraduate degree (any discipline); duration/pathway (1.5-3 years) depends on prior study and relevant work experience.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (Western Sydney postgraduate standard).

name: Master of Interpreting and Translation
description: The Master of Interpreting and Translation at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree for fluent bilingual graduates who want to work as qualified interpreters and translators as business and social interactions cross global borders. Students build practical language transfer skills and prepare toward professional accreditation. Graduates work as interpreters and translators across community, legal, health and conference settings. Indicative international tuition is around 39,600 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 084736J.

name: Master of Laws (2)
description: The Master of Laws at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time flexible postgraduate degree for law and non-law graduates who want advanced, integrated and contemporary knowledge in one or more areas of legal study. It gives substantial consideration to professional and transdisciplinary aspects of the law to enhance career expertise and prospects. Graduates advance in legal practice, policy, compliance and academia. Indicative international tuition is around 39,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 101782J.

name: Master of Neuromorphic Engineering
description: The Master of Neuromorphic Engineering at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree in an interdisciplinary field spanning electrical engineering, computer science, neuroscience, signal processing and mathematics. Students partner with industry on a research project mentored by researchers at the International Centre for Neuromorphic Systems at the MARCS Institute, addressing demand for bio-inspired sensing, smart edge devices and brain-inspired computing. Graduates work in neuromorphic hardware, sensing and AI research roles. Indicative international tuition is around 41,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 106435C.

name: Master of Nursing
description: Western Sydney University Master of Nursing gives registered nurses the theoretical knowledge and critical-thinking skills for advanced clinical practice, with a major in clinical leadership, clinical teaching or tuberculosis management. In the final sessions students apply what they have learned through a project or research experience relevant to their goals. A one-year, 80 credit point pathway requires current registration as a registered nurse, or eligibility, or registration within the last five years; a 1.5-year, 120 credit point pathway also requires two years of full-time-equivalent registered-nurse experience within the last five years. Full-time and part-time study are both available. Indicative international tuition is around A$38,700 per year. Graduates progress into clinical leadership, education and specialist roles.

name: Master of Nursing Practice (Preregistration)
description: The Master of Nursing Practice (Preregistration) at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree that lets graduates of any discipline become registered nurses. It combines simulated education on campus with hands-on industry placements and is built around public safety and contemporary nursing, digital health and education practice. Graduates are eligible to apply for registration as a Registered Nurse (Division 1) with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. Indicative international tuition is around 42,100 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 108310M.

name: Master of Philosophy (Engineering)
description: The Master of Philosophy (Engineering) at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time supervised research degree in engineering. It suits candidates with some research training and experience who do not yet meet the criteria for direct entry to a PhD, and can be used as a pathway to upgrade to a doctorate. Candidates complete an original research project and thesis. Graduates pursue research and specialist technical roles or continue to doctoral study. Indicative international tuition is around 36,300 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Planning
description: The Master of Planning at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree in urban and regional planning, accredited by the Planning Institute of Australia. It prepares students for leadership roles in statutory town planning practice and policy development, using the Parramatta City campus in Sydney's growth corridor as an urban laboratory. Graduates work as urban and regional planners in government and consulting. Indicative international tuition is around 34,800 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 080224K.

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description: Western Sydney University Master of Professional Accounting is an accredited graduate conversion program for holders of a bachelor degree in any discipline other than an accredited accounting major, letting them complete the pre-entry education requirements for CPA Australia, Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand and the Institute of Public Accountants. It runs 1.5 years full-time or three years part-time and requires 160 credit points: twelve postgraduate accounting core subjects and four electives. The degree is also internationally accredited with the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants, giving graduates exemptions from 11 ACCA papers. Entry requires a completed undergraduate degree or a graduate certificate. Indicative international tuition is around A$39,300 per year. Graduates work as accountants, auditors, tax advisers and financial analysts.

name: Master of Professional Psychology
description: The Master of Professional Psychology at Western Sydney University is a one-year full-time fifth-year qualification that provides education and training to prepare provisionally registered psychologists for their internship. Students are supported by an experienced clinical teaching team and the university's professional partnerships for placements. Graduates progress through the internship pathway toward general registration as a psychologist. Indicative international tuition is around 47,600 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 088715D.

name: Master of Project Management
description: The Master of Project Management at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree that prepares students to apply key project management concepts and practices across a range of professions. Students learn to customise a project management life cycle, develop project plans with cost and quality control, manage risk and stakeholders, build efficient schedules and communicate effectively in team settings. Graduates work as project and program managers across industries. Indicative international tuition is around 41,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 111857E.

name: Master of Property Investment and Development
description: The Master of Property Investment and Development at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree offering advanced study in property investment and development. Students learn to understand the multidisciplinary nature of the field and develop the analytical and decision-making skills needed by property professionals, in a program with a strong reputation in the industry. Graduates work in property investment, development, funds management and valuation roles. Indicative international tuition is around 39,300 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 097590D.

name: Master of Psychotherapy and Counselling
description: The Master of Psychotherapy and Counselling at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree that brings together theory and practice to prepare graduates to work in psychotherapy and counselling. Students learn under the guidance of experienced clinical practitioners and internationally recognised psychotherapy educators, refining their capacity to support people through self-understanding and healthy change. Graduates work as counsellors and psychotherapists across health, community and private practice settings. Indicative international tuition is around 34,800 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 088713F.

name: Master of Public Health
description: The Master of Public Health at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree focused on the comprehensive assessment of all determinants of health, including social and environmental factors alongside physical risk factors. Students develop the knowledge and skills to assess and respond to emerging public health issues, evaluate programs, and plan for disasters, with flexible on-campus and online study. Graduates work in public health units, government, non-government organisations and research. Indicative international tuition is around 37,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 014002E.

name: Master of Research (High Cost)
description: The Master of Research at Western Sydney University combines advanced research training with an independent research project, allowing students to build expertise in a chosen discipline across arts, business, education, health, science and technology. It develops the skills to make an original contribution to knowledge and prepares candidates for doctoral study. Graduates pursue research careers or continue to a PhD. Indicative international tuition is around 42,400 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Science
description: The Master of Science at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree that builds on prior study and professional experience to develop advanced expertise in science. Students choose a major such as public health nutrition, food science, greenhouse horticulture, agriculture, or sustainable water futures. Graduates find senior roles in government, universities, research organisations, and the food and agriculture sectors. Indicative international tuition is around 41,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 098472B.

name: Master of Social Work (Qualifying)
description: The Master of Social Work (Qualifying) at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree for graduates of social sciences or human services programs who want a professional social work qualification. Students study applied social sciences topics including ageing, alcohol and drug use, community empowerment, person-centred practice, and therapeutic and community interventions, with substantial field education. Graduates are eligible for professional recognition and work as social workers across health, community and government settings. Indicative international tuition is around 34,800 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 088712G.

name: Master of Sustainable Tourism, Hospitality and Event Management
description: The Master of Sustainable Tourism, Hospitality and Event Management at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree that provides specialist knowledge and skills to shape the future of the tourism, hospitality and event sectors in Australia and overseas. Students can complete majors in themes such as human resource management and innovation, and graduate ready to deliver sustainability and innovation outcomes. Graduates work in managerial, operational, policy, planning and research roles across the sector. Indicative international tuition is around 34,800 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 110871D.

name: Master of Teaching (Secondary)
description: The Master of Teaching (Secondary) at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time initial teacher education degree that turns a specialist undergraduate degree into a secondary teaching career. It combines on-campus theory with school-based placements, giving graduates practical tools to teach and support high-school students. Graduates are prepared for registration and work as secondary school teachers. Indicative international tuition is around 35,100 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 057369G.

name: Master of Teaching (Secondary) STEM
description: The Master of Teaching (Secondary) STEM at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time initial teacher education degree focused on teaching science, technology, engineering and mathematics subjects. Western is one of only three providers of STEM teacher education in Australia, combining on-campus and online learning with hands-on experience in schools. Graduates are prepared for registration and work as secondary STEM teachers. Indicative international tuition is around 35,100 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 095774A.

name: Master of Translation and TESOL
description: The Master of Translation and TESOL at Western Sydney University is a two-year full-time degree that prepares students to work as qualified translators or English language teachers as global demand for both continues to grow. Students build practical translation skills alongside language teaching methodology. Graduates work in translation, localisation and English language teaching in Australia and overseas. Indicative international tuition is around 39,600 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 088716C.

name: Master of Urban Management and Planning
description: The Master of Urban Management and Planning at Western Sydney University is a one-year full-time degree that provides the education, skills and real-world knowledge to help shape how cities grow and function. Based at the Parramatta City campus in the centre of Sydney's growth area, students learn from internationally recognised scholars about the challenges of planning and urban living. Graduates work in urban planning, policy and development roles. Indicative international tuition is around 34,800 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 067913E.

name: Advanced Diploma of Travel and Tourism Management
Associate Degree in Resort and Hotel Management
Associate Degree in Tourism and Hospitality Management
Bachelor of Culinary Management
description:
This degree sits on top of Angliss's core reputation: the institute has trained generations of Melbourne's professional chefs, and its commercial kitchens run as genuine working production and training spaces rather than teaching-only mockups, supplying the institute's own training restaurant and bakery outlets that serve the public. Culinary Management students aren't just cooking in class; they're working alongside vocational chef apprentices and trainees in kitchens that operate under real commercial kitchen conditions and food safety obligations.

The degree is built for students aiming at kitchen leadership and food business management roles rather than a pure culinary arts (hands-on cooking) qualification. It layers business management, food cost control, and menu engineering on top of solid practical culinary skills, positioning graduates for head chef, food and beverage manager, or hospitality business owner pathways rather than line-cook roles. Angliss's placement network into Melbourne's restaurant, hotel, and catering scene (a city with a genuinely dense and competitive food industry) gives students access to kitchens ranging from high-volume hotel operations to smaller chef-driven restaurants.

Because Angliss's culinary teaching culture is built by working chefs as much as academics, expect assessment that includes live food production under time pressure and real cost-control exercises, not only written business case assignments.
curriculum:
Year 1: Culinary Fundamentals and Kitchen Operations, Food Safety and Hygiene, Introduction to Menu Planning, Hospitality Business Fundamentals, kitchen placement (short block)
Year 2: Advanced Culinary Techniques, Food and Beverage Cost Control, Menu Engineering, Kitchen Team Leadership, extended kitchen/restaurant placement
Year 3: Culinary Business Management, Supply Chain and Procurement for Food Service, Sustainable and Ethical Food Practices, Capstone Culinary Business Project, final industry placement
Practical training delivered in William Angliss's working commercial kitchens and training restaurant
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent; prior culinary certificate preferred
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Event Management (Diploma to Degree Pathway)
description:
This is a stacked pathway degree: students complete a diploma-level qualification first (Angliss's diploma in event management is itself a well-regarded vocational credential in the Victorian events industry) before articulating into the bachelor's degree, which means graduates come out with both a completed diploma and a full bachelor's, a structure aimed at students who want a recognised qualification milestone partway through rather than a single long commitment.

Melbourne's genuine events economy, with major sporting events (the Australian Open, Melbourne Cup Carnival, AFL grand final), large conventions, and a dense festival calendar, gives Angliss event management students access to real, large-scale event placements that a lot of smaller event management programs elsewhere in the country simply can't offer. The diploma stage focuses heavily on operational event delivery skills (run sheets, vendor coordination, on-the-day logistics), and the degree stage builds on that with strategic event business management, marketing, and larger-scale project planning.

Because the pathway structure means students transition from a TAFE-style diploma delivery model into more strategic degree-level units partway through, the shift in workload and assessment style between the two stages is genuinely noticeable. Angliss's course advisors flag this directly to students moving between the diploma and degree components rather than treating it as a seamless continuation.
curriculum:
Diploma stage: Event Operations and Logistics, Event Marketing and Promotion, Risk Management for Events, Vendor and Stakeholder Coordination, supervised event placements
Degree stage Year 1 (post-diploma articulation): Strategic Event Management, Event Business Planning, Sponsorship and Partnership Management, Financial Management for Events
Degree stage Year 2: Large-Scale Event Project Management, Sustainable and Ethical Event Practice, Capstone Event Project (often tied to a real Melbourne event), final industry placement
Graduates receive both the diploma and bachelor's qualification through the articulated pathway
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent; first year delivered as Diploma of Event Management
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Resort and Hotel Management
description:
Angliss built this degree specifically around hotel and resort operations rather than the broader tourism-industry framing of some of its sister degrees, and the practical bent shows in the assessment style: students work through actual front office, housekeeping, and food and beverage operational scenarios using the institute's on-campus training facilities, which include a working commercial kitchen, bakery, and bar rather than only lecture-based case studies.

Placement is heavily weighted in this degree, and Angliss's long-standing relationships with major international hotel brands operating in Australia (a legacy of the institute's decades as the primary trainer for Melbourne and Victoria's hospitality workforce) mean students typically get placed into genuine hotel operations roles rather than administrative shadowing. Resort management units draw on case material from both Australian coastal and regional resort operators and international examples, reflecting graduates' genuine spread of career destinations: some go into city hotel management, others into regional or international resort operations.

Because Angliss's teaching culture leans so heavily on people who've worked the industry themselves, students should expect assessment that mirrors real operational pressure (rostering problems, service recovery scenarios, revenue management under real seasonal demand curves) rather than purely theoretical management frameworks.
curriculum:
Year 1: Hotel and Resort Operations, Front Office Management, Food and Beverage Service Operations, Customer Experience Management, industry placement (short block)
Year 2: Rooms Division Management, Resort Facilities and Recreation Management, Financial Management for Hospitality, Human Resource Management, extended industry placement

name: Bachelor of Tourism
description:
Angliss's Bachelor of Tourism leans toward destination management, tourism marketing, and sustainable tourism planning rather than the operations-heavy hospitality focus of the institute's hotel and resort degrees. It suits students aiming at roles with tourism boards, destination marketing organisations, tour operators, or the travel sector rather than on-property hotel management.

Victoria's tourism industry (Melbourne's major-events calendar, regional tourism across the Great Ocean Road and wine regions, and Victoria's state tourism agency presence) gives Angliss tourism students placement and project opportunities genuinely grounded in a real, active state tourism economy rather than abstract global tourism theory. The degree includes units on sustainable and responsible tourism, reflecting increasing industry and government focus on managing tourism's environmental and community impact, particularly relevant given Victoria's push on regional and nature-based tourism.

Because Angliss is fundamentally an industry-training institute rather than a research university, the tourism degree's teaching staff mix includes people who've worked in destination marketing organisations and tour operations, and assessment tends toward applied projects, such as actual destination marketing plans and tourism product development pitches, rather than purely theoretical tourism studies essays.

name: Bachelor of Tourism and Hospitality Management
description:
This degree runs through the same campus that trains Angliss's chefs and baristas, which means tourism and hospitality management students aren't learning service standards purely from textbooks. The institute's commercial training restaurant, bakery, and bar operate as real, publicly trading venues, and management students do rotations through front-of-house operations there alongside the vocational trainees, giving them direct exposure to how a service business actually runs on a given shift rather than only studying it in case format.

Angliss has decades-deep relationships with Victoria's tourism and hospitality employers, and industry placement is a substantial, credit-bearing part of the degree rather than an optional add-on: students typically complete placements with hotel groups, tourism operators, or event companies across multiple points in the degree, building a genuine employment track record before graduating. The institute's location in Melbourne, a city with a real convention, major-events, and hospitality economy, gives students access to large-scale operations (major hotel chains, the Melbourne Convention and Exhibition Centre precinct, and a dense CBD hospitality strip) that a regional or suburban-based hospitality school couldn't match.

The degree covers both the tourism-destination-management side and hands-on hospitality operations management, and Angliss's teaching staff mix includes industry veterans as much as academics, which shows up in how practically the coursework is pitched: a lot of assessment is scenario and operations-based rather than purely essay-driven.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Tourism and Hospitality Industries, Hospitality Operations, Customer Service Management, Tourism Destination Studies, industry placement (short block)
Year 2: Rooms Division and Hotel Operations Management, Food and Beverage Management, Tourism Marketing, Human Resource Management for Hospitality, extended industry placement
Year 3: Revenue Management, Strategic Management in Tourism and Hospitality, Sustainable Tourism, Capstone Industry Project, final industry placement
Delivered with direct access to William Angliss's own training restaurant, bakery, and bar operations

name: Master of International Hospitality Entrepreneurship
description:
William Angliss doesn't run this as an academic hospitality-theory degree. It's built for people who already have some industry background and want to launch or scale their own venture, whether that's a restaurant group, a boutique accommodation brand, or a food and beverage startup. Classes are small and run out of the institute's Melbourne CBD campus, which has its own working training restaurant, bars, and bakery on site, so the teaching staff are frequently people who've actually run venues rather than career academics, and guest lecturers tend to be working hospitality operators and investors from Melbourne's genuinely dense hospitality scene.

The degree centres on a business venture project: students develop an actual business plan or concept across the program, often one they intend to launch for real, and it gets pressure-tested against real costing, supply chain, and staffing constraints rather than treated as a hypothetical case study. Angliss's industry placement network (built over decades of supplying trained chefs, managers, and baristas to Melbourne hospitality) gives students access to venue owners and hospitality investors most standalone business schools can't offer.

Because the cohort is small and heavily practitioner-taught, the pace and flavour of each intake varies with who's enrolled and who's teaching that trimester. This isn't a large standardised MBA-style program, and Angliss is upfront that a lot of the value comes from the industry network and mentorship as much as from the coursework itself.

name: Master of International Hotel Leadership
description:
This is Angliss's senior credential for hotel industry professionals, longer and more research-oriented than the Graduate Diploma of International Hotel Leadership, and it's pitched at people aiming for general manager or regional leadership roles within international hotel brands rather than a first entry into hospitality management. The program draws on Angliss's genuinely deep international hotel industry relationships, built over decades of training staff who go on to work across branded hotel groups throughout the Asia-Pacific region.

Coursework moves from operational hotel leadership topics into higher-level strategic and international business content: cross-cultural management, international hotel branding and franchise models, and hospitality investment and asset management, reflecting the reality that senior hotel leaders increasingly need to understand ownership and brand-management structures, not just day-to-day operations. The capstone research or applied project typically has students examining a real strategic problem in international hotel operations, often connected to their own employer or a target market.

Given the practitioner-heavy cohort (most students are already working in hotel management), Angliss runs the degree with flexible block and intensive delivery options, and it's common for students to be sponsored or part-supported by their current employer as part of a leadership development plan, which shapes both the applied focus of assessments and the seniority of typical classroom discussion.
curriculum:
Core units: International Hotel Leadership and Strategy, Cross-Cultural Management in Hospitality, Hotel Branding and Franchise Models, Financial and Asset Management for Hotels
Advanced units: Hospitality Investment and Development, Global Hotel Operations Standards, Strategic Human Resource Leadership
Capstone: Applied Research Project or Strategic Business Project (often connected to the student's own employer or target market)
Delivered in block/intensive format for working international hotel industry professionals
